body:
[Theorem 57 ({\cite[Theorem 4) of arXiv:2608.05931, 'Effective Lagrangian regularity and the uniqueness threshold for random H\"older velocity '] {gotze_bounds_2008}}]

    Let $n,d \in \N$ and $p > 2$. Let $(D_j)_{1 \leq j \leq n}$ be independent $\R^d$ valued random variables. We suppose that there exists $\lambda,\Lambda >0$ such that the following holds for all $1 \leq j \leq n$:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $\E D_j =0$.
        \item For all $v \in \R^d$, $\E (v \cdot D_j)^2 \geq \lambda |v|^2$.
        \item $\E |D_j|^p \leq \Lambda^{p/2}$.
    \end{enumerate}
    Then there exists $C(p,d, \Lambda/\lambda)>0$ and (on perhaps a larger probability space) mutually independent $\R^d$-valued Gaussian random variables $(Z_j)_{1 \leq j \leq n}$ (though \textit{not independent of the $D_j$}) so that
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $\E Z_j =0$,
        \item $\E Z_j \otimes Z_j = \E D_j \otimes D_j$,
    \end{enumerate}
    and we have the approximation bound
    \[\E\bigg[\sup_{1\leq k\leq n} \Big|\sum_{j=1}^k (D_j-Z_j)\Big|^p\bigg]^{1/p}\leq C \Lambda^{1/2} n^{1/p}.\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma 9 of arXiv:2506.10522, 'On the Law of the Iterated Logarithm for $m$-dependent stationary random variables under s'] Suppose $X\in \mathcal{H}$.
\begin{description}
  \item[\rm (i)]
 For any $\delta>0$,
$$ \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \V\big(|X|\ge \delta \sqrt{n\log\log n} \big)<\infty \;\; \Longleftrightarrow C_{\V}\left[\frac{X^2}{\log\log|X|}\right]<\infty.
$$
 \item[\rm (ii)]
   If $C_{\V}\left[\frac{X^2}{\log\log|X|}\right]<\infty$, then for any $\delta>0$ and $p>2$,
$$ \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{\mbE\big[\big(|X|\wedge (\delta \sqrt{n\log\log n})\big)^p\big]}{(n\log\log n)^{p/2}}<\infty. $$
 \item[\rm (iii)] $C_{\V}\left[\frac{X^2}{\log\log|X|}\right]<\infty$, then for any $\delta>0$,
 $$ \mbE[X^2\wedge (2\delta n\log\log n)]=o(\log \log n) $$
 and $$ \breve{\mathbb E}[(|X|-\delta \sqrt{2  n\log\log n})^+]=o(\sqrt{\log\log n/n}).\;\;  $$
\end{description} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Let N>=1 and d_0,...,d_N be positive integers, with d_j>=min(d_0,d_N) for 1<=j<N. Let Phi be a real d_N-by-d_0 matrix of full rank min(d_0,d_N). For real matrices W_j of size d_j-by-d_{j-1}, write P=W_N...W_1 and L(W_1,...,W_N)=||P-Phi||_F^2/2. All layers are updated simultaneously by W_j(t+1)=W_j(t)-eta grad_{W_j} L(W_1(t),...,W_N(t)). Assume c>0 and ||P(0)-Phi||_F<=sigma_min(Phi)-c, where sigma_min denotes the min(d_0,d_N)-th singular value. Put delta=c^2/(256 N^3 ||Phi||_F^{2(N-1)/N}). Assume ||W_{j+1}(0)^T W_{j+1}(0)-W_j(0) W_j(0)^T||_F<=delta for all 1<=j<N. Choose 0<eta<=c^{(4N-2)/N}/(6144 N^3 ||Phi||_F^{(6N-4)/N}). For every integer t>=0, ell(t)<=ell(0) exp(-eta c^{2(N-1)/N} t). Consequently, if ell(0)>0 and epsilon>0, any integer T>=max(0,ceil(log(ell(0)/epsilon)/(eta c^{2(N-1)/N}))) satisfies ell(T)<=epsilon. If ell(0)=0 the loss remains zero. This is a conditional deterministic convergence theorem: it does not assert that independently Gaussian-initialized layers satisfy both initialization conditions with high probability.
positive integer depth and layer dimensions; no hidden bottleneck
real full-rank target Phi
loss is one half squared Frobenius error of the end-to-end product (equivalently the whitened-data objective after dropping its constant)
positive deficiency margin c at initialization
adjacent-layer Gram imbalance at most delta=c^2/(256 N^3 ||Phi||_F^{2(N-1)/N})
simultaneous gradient descent with the stated positive step-size upper bound

body: [Lem hpcabc of arXiv:2412.09535, 'Local limit theorem for joint subgraph counts'] A necessary condition for $n$ to be $(p, \pm)$-HPC is that $\frac{1}{b}(h_\pm+a\binom{n}{2})$ is an integer and $b^8 \mid 2h_\pm(n-2)$. A sufficient condition for $n$ to be $(p, \pm)$-HPC is that $\frac{1}{b}(h_\pm+a\binom{n}{2})$ is an integer and $b^{12} \mid n-2$.

Own-work draft; proof (unaudited); D0010-C003 v1; audits w668:PASS. For n>=3 and 0<=lambda<=1, the density f(x)=lambda*(n-1)*(1-x)^(n-2)+(1-lambda)*(2n-1)*(2n-2)*x*(1-x)^(2n-3) on [0,1] is unimodal, has mean 1/n, and is n-CM. It is the common-center mixture of Beta(1,n-1) and Beta(2,2n-2) simplex marginals. Its mode lies inside (0,1) when lambda<C/[C+(n-1)(n-2)], C=(2n-1)(2n-2); otherwise the density is nonincreasing. This is a special sufficient family; novelty is not asserted.
n integer >=3
lambda in [0,1]

Status: proof (unaudited). Known Dirichlet/Beta construction plus an elementary mixture calculation; novelty not asserted.

For n>=3 and 0<=lambda<=1, the density on [0,1]

 f_lambda(x)=lambda*(n-1)*(1-x)^(n-2)
       +(1-lambda)*(2n-1)*(2n-2)*x*(1-x)^(2n-3)

is continuous, unimodal, has mean 1/n, and is n-CM. When

 lambda < (2n-1)*(2n-2) / [(2n-1)*(2n-2)+(n-1)*(n-2)],

its mode is strictly inside (0,1), so it is not monotone (the mode is 1/(2n-2) when lambda=0). Otherwise it is nonincreasing. Thus it gives concrete extra sufficient structure in the D0010 boundary regime, without invoking the density-floor theorem.

1. Gamma/Dirichlet construction. For alpha>0 draw n independent positive variables G_i with density g^(alpha-1) exp(-g)/Gamma(alpha). Put T=sum G_i and Z_i=G_i/T. By changing coordinates from the G_i to (T,Z_1,...,Z_{n-1}), with Z_n=1-sum_{i<n}Z_i, the Jacobian is T^(n-1). The joint density becomes

 T^(n alpha-1) exp(-T) product_i Z_i^(alpha-1) / Gamma(alpha)^n.

Integration over T gives density Gamma(n alpha)/Gamma(alpha)^n times the product on the simplex. In particular the vector is invariant under coordinate permutations and sums to one, so the common marginal is n-CM with mean 1/n.

2. Marginal formula. Fix Z_1=x. On the remaining (n-2)-dimensional simplex write Z_i=(1-x)V_i for i>=2. The resulting power of (1-x) is (n-1)(alpha-1)+(n-2)=(n-1)alpha-1. Applying the normalization formula from Step 1 for n-1 coordinates gives marginal

 Gamma(n alpha)/[Gamma(alpha)Gamma((n-1)alpha)]
          * x^(alpha-1)*(1-x)^((n-1)alpha-1).

For alpha=1 this is (n-1)(1-x)^(n-2). For alpha=2 it is (2n-1)(2n-2)x(1-x)^(2n-3). Each is n-CM, has total mass one and mean 1/n, since its coupling sums to one and has identical marginals.

3. Choose an independent Bernoulli label, selecting the alpha=1 vector with probability lambda and the alpha=2 vector otherwise. Every outcome still has sum one, and each marginal has f_lambda. Thus f_lambda is n-CM and has boundary mean 1/n.

4. Unimodality. For x in (0,1), divide the derivative by the positive factor (1-x)^(n-3), and put C=(2n-1)(2n-2). Its sign is the sign of

 D(x)= -lambda*(n-1)*(n-2)
       +(1-lambda)*C*(1-x)^(n-1)*(1-(2n-2)x).

On [0,1/(2n-2)] the second factor R(x) is strictly decreasing, because

 R'(x)=(n-1)*(1-x)^(n-2)*(-3+2n*x)<0

there for n>=3. Beyond that interval R(x) is nonpositive, so D(x)<=0. For lambda below the threshold, D(0)>0 and D(1/(2n-2))<=0, with a unique crossing in the open interval (including lambda=0, where the crossing is at the endpoint 1/(2n-2), see correction immediately below). For lambda at or above the threshold, D(0)<=0 and the density is nonincreasing.

Endpoint clarification: for lambda=0 the mode is exactly 1/(2n-2). Accordingly the precise interior-mode statement is: when 0<lambda<threshold the mode is in (0,1/(2n-2)); when lambda=0 the mode is at 1/(2n-2). All below-threshold cases have a mode strictly inside (0,1).

The construction is sufficient for this explicit family, not a necessary condition for general unimodal laws. [Prop 11 of arXiv:2605.26664, 'Mixing times for Glauber dynamics of lozenge tilings of the hexagon'] Given two
floors $H_-,H'_-:D\mapsto \mathbb R$ with $ H_-\le H'_-$, two ceilings $H_+,H'_+:D\mapsto \mathbb R$ with $H_+\le H'_+$ and two
initial conditions $\eta_0,\eta'_0\in\Omega_D$ satisfying $ \eta_0\le \eta'_0$, ${\eta_0}\in\Omega_{H_\pm}, {\eta'_0}\in\Omega_{H'_\pm}$, the Glauber  dynamic $\eta_t$ in $D$ constrained between $H_\pm$ and the dynamic $\eta'_t$ constrained between $H'_\pm$
can be coupled in such a way that $\eta_t\le \eta_t'$ for all times $t$, with probability $1$.
{In particular, it holds that $\pi_{H_\pm}\preceq \pi_{H'_\pm}$}.
title: Prop 11 of arXiv:2605.26664

[Theorem te:protection of arXiv:2606.15339, 'Uniform integrability of the distance to the nearest leaf in random trees'] Let $v_n$ be a uniformly chosen vertex of $\mathcal{T}_n$. As $n\to\infty$ along those $n$
for which $\mathcal{T}_n$ is defined,
\[
\partial_{\mathrm{p}}(\mathcal{T}_n,v_n) \xrightarrow{d} \partial(\mathcal{T}),
\qquad
\mathbf{E}\bigl[\partial_{\mathrm{p}}(\mathcal{T}_n,v_n)^p\bigr] \to \mathbf{E}\bigl[\partial(\mathcal{T})^p\bigr]
\quad(p\ge 1),
\]
where $\mathcal{T}$ is a Bienaym\'e--Galton--Watson tree with a specific offspring distribution $\xi$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Protection number of a random vertex

body:
[Proposition Prop:finite-horizon-lower-bound of arXiv:2608.19643, 'Time-Uniform Self-Normalized Concentration for Discounted Least Squares: Limits and Correc'] Consider the same scalar Gaussian process as in (Eq:counterexample-recursion of the paper). Fix \(T\geq1\) and \(\delta\in(0,1)\). Let \(C_T(\delta)\) be any deterministic boundary satisfying
\[
\mathbb P\left(
\max_{1\leq t\leq T}
\frac{\lvert S_t^\gamma\rvert}{\sqrt{\widetilde V_t^\gamma}}
\leq C_T(\delta)
\right)\geq1-\delta .
\]
Then
\[
C_T(\delta)
\geq
\frac{R}{(1+\gamma)\sqrt{\lambda+(1-\gamma^2)^{-1}}}
\,
\Phi^{-1}\left(\frac{1+(1-\delta)^{1/T}}{2}\right),
\]
where \(\Phi\) is the standard normal distribution function. In particular, for fixed \(\gamma\) and \(\lambda\), there are positive constants \(c_{\gamma,\lambda}\) and \(x_0\) such that, for \(\delta\in(0,1/2]\) and \(T/\delta\geq x_0\),
\[
C_T(\delta)\geq c_{\gamma,\lambda}R\sqrt{\log\frac{T}{\delta}}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Finite-horizon lower bound

body: [Abstract of arXiv:2609.03924, 'Beyond normal fluctuations in local laws for Wigner matrices'] We identify non-Gaussian corrections to the central limit theorem for the global and local laws, i.e. for Stieltjes transform of the empirical eigenvalue distribution of a large real symmetric or complex Hermitian Wigner matrix. We find that in the real case the rate of convergence in this CLT is substantially slower than in the complex case. For the proofs, we develop new static and dynamic hierarchies of extended cumulants up to any order that can be analysed by a refinement of the zigzag strategy.
title: Abstract of arXiv:2609.03924: Beyond normal fluctuations in local laws for Wigner matrices

body: A non-degenerate distribution function G is called max-stable (or an extreme value distribution) if for every integer n \ge 2, there exist constants a_n > 0 and b_n \in \mathbb{R} such that G(x)^n = G(a_n x + b_n) for all x \in \mathbb{R}. That is, the maximum of n i.i.d. random variables with distribution G has the same distribution as G up to an affine rescaling.
title: Extreme Value (Max-Stable) Distribution

body: Ergodic theory is a branch of mathematics that studies statistical properties of deterministic dynamical systems; it is the study of ergodicity. In this context, "statistical properties" refers to properties which are expressed through the behavior of time averages of various functions along trajectories of dynamical systems. The notion of deterministic dynamical systems assumes that the equations determining the dynamics do not contain any random perturbations, noise, etc. Thus, the statistics with which we are concerned are properties of the dynamics.
title: Ergodic theory

\[
    f(x)=\sum_{r=1}^K(a_r+b_rx)e^{\alpha_rx}

is not identically zero, then $f$ has at most $2K-1$ real zeros counted with multiplicity.

[Thm 7 ($L^1$-stability and uniqueness) of arXiv:2607.28238, 'Well-posedness and large deviations for the obstacle problem of first-order stochastic con'] Let \textbf{Hypotheses (H1) and (H2)$'$} hold.
Let $(u_1,\nu_1)$ and $(u_2,\nu_2)$ be two kinetic solutions of the lower obstacle problem for \eqref{eq:intro-reflected-model} in the sense of Definition \ref{def:dfn-1},
with corresponding initial values satisfying
\[
u^0_{1},u^0_{2}\in L^\infty(\mathbb{T}^N),
\qquad
u^0_{i}\geq \psi(\cdot,0)\quad\text{a.e. on }\mathbb{T}^N.
\]
Then, for almost every $t\in[0,T]$,
\begin{equation}
\E\Vert u_1(t)-u_2(t)\Vert _{L^1(\mathbb{T}^N)}
\leq
\Vert u^0_{1}-u^0_{2}\Vert _{L^1(\mathbb{T}^N)}.
\end{equation}
In particular, if $u^0_{1}=u^0_{2}$ a.e. on $\mathbb{T}^N$, then
\[
u_1=u_2
\quad\text{in }L^1(\Omega\times\mathbb{T}^N\times[0,T]),
\]
and the reflection measures coincide:
\[
\nu_1=\nu_2
\quad\text{as Radon measures on }\mathbb{T}^N\times[0,T),
\quad \mathbb{P}\text{-a.s.}
\]
Thus, the kinetic solution pair $(u,\nu)$ is unique.

the function $x \mapsto x \cdot f(x)$ for $x \in [1, \infty)$

[campaign result 2026-09-14, author_checked_criterion_controlled_against_the_papers_own_deterministic_benchmark] This is the broader partial answer reported for both cases of the open question in Remark 5.3(ii) of arXiv:2607.07410. Let V be a two-sided (r_0,alpha)-semi-selfsimilar Levy process with alpha in (0,2), whose value at time one has positive probability of each sign, and let nu be its Levy measure. For delta > 0 consider the two diffusion forms with reference densities exp(-|x|^delta - V(x)) and exp(|x|^delta - V(x)), each with energy (1/2) integral |f'|^2 times the corresponding density. The record claims noncompactness, with essential-spectrum bottom zero, for every delta, when nu has negative jumps in the first case or positive jumps in the second. The written quiet-window proof covers delta > 1; the paper's Proposition 5.2 covers 0 < delta <= 1/alpha. Together these give all delta when alpha <= 1, which includes alpha < 1, where nu must charge both half-lines. For alpha in (1,2) and 1/alpha < delta <= 1 the claim is not established by the written argument. For alpha > 1, delta > 1 and no negative jumps, the record also sketches compactness at the +infinity end of the first diffusion via the bound B_l(x) <= C^2 x^(2-2delta). Here B_l is the integral of the reciprocal density from a fixed positive x_0 to x times the integral of the density from x to infinity, and C is a finite path-dependent constant. The record explicitly leaves the uniform near-field estimate unwritten, so this converse is a sketch. Compactness at one end does not by itself establish compactness of the full two-sided operator. This is an unrefereed campaign result.
The converse is explicitly a sketch, with a missing uniform estimate.
The claimed converse concerns the positive-infinity end only.

body: Cantor's diagonal argument is a mathematical proof that there are infinite sets which cannot be put into one-to-one correspondence with the infinite set of natural numbers – informally, that there are sets which in some sense contain more elements than there are positive integers. Such sets are now called uncountable sets, and the size of infinite sets is treated by the theory of cardinal numbers, which Cantor began.

[Corollary 13 (Bridge to the Gaussian-base factor of Dytso et al.) of arXiv:2606.18458, 'Stable size-biasing and the positive scale-mixture order of generalized Gaussian laws'] Let $0<r\le2$, and let $V_{G,r}$ denote the Gaussian-base factor of \citet{Dytso2018}, defined by
\[
X_r\stackrel{d}{=}V_{G,r}X_2,
\qquad
V_{G,r}>0,\qquad V_{G,r}\perp X_2 .
\]
Then
\[
V_{G,r}\stackrel{d}{=}V_{r,2},
\]
and
\[
V_{G,r}\ \text{is Stieltjes moment-determinate}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
r\ge \frac25 .
\]
Equivalently,
\[
V_{G,r}\ \text{is Stieltjes moment-indeterminate}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
0<r<\frac25 .
\]
Thus \citet[Proposition~8]{Dytso2018} is recovered and sharpened: their sufficient condition $r\ge2/5$ is the exact Gaussian-base threshold.

body:
Let X be a compact metric space and T : X -> X a continuous surjection. T is TOPOLOGICALLY EXACT, also called locally eventually onto, if for every nonempty open set U there is an integer n >= 1 with T^n(U) = X. Two consequences are what proofs actually use. (a) UNIFORMITY IN n: if T^n(U) = X then T^m(U) = X for every m >= n, because T is onto; hence for each nonempty open U there is N with T^n(U) = X for ALL n >= N. (b) DENSE BACKWARD ORBITS WITH ALL LARGE PERIODS: for every x in X and every nonempty open U there is N with U intersect T^{-n}(x) nonempty for every n >= N; in particular the full backward orbit of any point is dense. Property (b) is a genuine aperiodicity statement that topological transitivity does not give and that even topological mixing of an invertible system cannot give. Relations: topological exactness implies topological mixing, which implies topological transitivity; the converses are false. An invertible map is never topologically exact unless X is a single point, since T^n(U) = X forces U = X for a homeomorphism, so exactness is a hypothesis reserved for genuinely non-invertible maps: expanding maps of the circle or of a compact manifold, one-sided mixing subshifts of finite type, and Chebyshev-like interval maps are the standard examples.
X is a compact metric space
T : X -> X is continuous and surjective

[Theorem 2 (Eichelsbacher \cite{eichelsbacher2024stein}) of arXiv:2506.17061, 'Non-uniform bounds for non-normal approximation via Stein's method with applications to th'] Let $k$ be a positive integer and let $Y_k$ be a random variable distributed according to $p_k$ as given in \eqref{b1}. 
		Let $(W, W')$ be an exchangeable pair of random variables satisfying \eqref{nonlinear2}, and let $\Delta := W - W'$. 
		Assume that $\E|\psi(W)|^{2} < \infty$ and $|\Delta| \le a$ for some $a>0$. Then for any $z \in \mathbb{R}$, we have
		\begin{equation}		\left| \mathbb{P}(W \le z) - \mathbb{P}(Y_k \le z) \right| \le 
			\dfrac{C}{\left( 1 + |z|^{2k-1} \right)}  
			\left(\left| \mathbb{E} \left( 1 - \frac{1}{2\lambda}\mathbb{E}(\Delta^2|W) \right) \right| + \dfrac{\mathbb{E}|R|}{\lambda} + 3a\right),
		\end{equation}
		where $C$ is a constant depending only on $p_k$ and $\E|\psi(W)|^2$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2608.27372, 'Universality and sharp thresholds for ellipsoid fitting'] Let $(x_i)_{1\leq i\leq n}\in \R^d$ be i.i.d. random vectors such that $x_1=(x_{1j})_{1\leq j\leq d}$ has indpenedent coordinates satisfying
	\begin{equation}
		\E[x_{1j}]=0,\qquad \E \left[x_{1j}^2\right]=1,\qquad
		\E \left[x_{1j}^4\right]=\kappa,\qquad \sup_{j\le d}\|x_{1j}\|_{\psitwo}\le K_x,
	\end{equation}
    where $\kappa>1$ and $K_x>0$ do not depend on $n,d$. Let
	$n,d\to\infty$ with $n/d^2\to\alpha\in(0,\infty)$.  There is an explicit
	threshold $\alpha_\star(\kappa)$, defined in Eq.~\eqref{eq:alpha-star-def},
	which depends only on $\kappa$, such that the following holds.
	\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
		\item If $\alpha<\alpha_\star(\kappa)$, then with probability tending to one, there exists an ellipsoid fitting all $(x_i)_{1\leq i\leq n}$:
		\[
		\exists R\succ 0,\quad\textnormal{such that}\quad x_i^{\top}R x_i=1\quad \textnormal{for all}\quad 1\leq i\leq n.
		\]
		Moreover, such $R\in \R^{d\times d}$ can be chosen to be well-conditioned: $\lambda_{\max}(R)/\lambda_{\min}(R)=O(1)$. 
		\item If $\alpha>\alpha_\star(\kappa)$, then with probability tending to one
		there is no $R\succeq0$ such that $x_i^\top R x_i=1$ for all $1\leq i\leq n$. Moreover, the optimal squared fitting error converges in probability:
		\begin{equation}
			\Gamma_X:=\inf_{R\succeq0, \operatorname{Tr}R=d}\,\inf_{r\geq 0}\,
			\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n\left(\frac{x_i^\top Rx_i}{\sqrt{d}}-r\right)^2
			\pto e_\star(\alpha,\kappa),
		\end{equation}
        where $e_\star(\alpha,\kappa)$ is defined in Eq.~\eqref{eq:optimal-fitting-error-main}. For $\alpha>\alpha_\star(\kappa)$, $e_\star(\alpha,\kappa)>0$ holds, thus an approximate ellipsoid fitting is not possible with any $R\succeq 0$ with $\Tr R=d$.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 2 of arXiv:2608.27372

[Lem 11 of arXiv:2607.22414, 'Asymptotic fluctuations in supercritical multi-type Crump--Mode--Jagers processes'] Assume that~\ref{assumpt:Malthusian alpha} through~\ref{assumpt:hreprMoments} hold. 
	Let $\theta \geq 0$ and $f : [0,\infty) \to [0,\infty)^p$ be a continuous function
	such that $f(x) = O(x^\theta)$ as $x \to \infty$ and $x^{-\theta}f(x)$ is uniformly continuous on $[1,\infty)$. Suppose that the limit
	$$ \lim_{t\to\infty, t\in\G} \frac1{t^{\theta+1}} \int_{[0,t]} \bu^\trans f(s) \, \ell(\dd s) \eqqcolon c \in (0,\infty)	$$
	exists. Let $\varphi(t) = e^{\alpha t} f(t) \1_{[0,\infty)}(t)$, $t \in \R$. Then

[Lem measure_2arm of arXiv:2604.14122, 'The scaling limit of random walk and\\ the intrinsic metric on planar critical percolation'] Fix an annulus $A$ and $r>0$. For each $\delta > 0$, let $X_\delta$ be the set of points $x \in A^{\inn}$ such that there are two disjoint (open or closed) arms crossing $B(x,r)\setminus B(x,\delta)$. Then
    \[
    \lim_{\delta\searrow 0} \mathbf{E}[\mu^A(X_\delta)] = 0 .
    \]
    In particular, the set of points with two disjoint arms to distance $r$ has measure $0$ almost surely.
title: Lem measure_2arm of arXiv:2604.14122

Let K ⊂ ℝⁿ be nonempty and closed and let d(x) := dist(x, K) = min_{y ∈ K} |x − y| (the minimum is attained because K is closed). Then: (a) d is 1-Lipschitz, d ≥ 0, and d(x) = 0 exactly when x ∈ K. (b) [minimal-time / control representation] d(x) = inf { T ≥ 0 : there is an absolutely continuous ξ: [0,T] → ℝⁿ with |ξ'(s)| ≤ 1 for a.e. s, ξ(0) = x, ξ(T) ∈ K } = inf { ∫_0^T |ξ'(s)| ds : ξ absolutely continuous, ξ(0) = x, ξ(T) ∈ K, T ≥ 0 } — the distance is the value function of the minimal-time problem for the control system ξ' = α, |α| ≤ 1, with target K, and the straight segment from x to a nearest point of K is an optimal trajectory. (c) [variational characterization] d is the largest 1-Lipschitz function that is ≤ 0 on K: if u: ℝⁿ → ℝ is 1-Lipschitz and u ≤ 0 on K then u ≤ d everywhere, and d itself is admissible; equivalently d(x) = max { u(x) : u 1-Lipschitz, u ≤ 0 on K }. (d) [eikonal equation] d is a viscosity solution of |Du| − 1 = 0 in the open set ℝⁿ \ K, and a viscosity subsolution of |Du| − 1 ≤ 0 on all of ℝⁿ. Sharp edges. (1) The sign convention matters: d solves |Du| − 1 = 0 but is in general NOT a viscosity solution of 1 − |Du| = 0 (for K = {−1, 1} ⊂ ℝ, d = 1 − |x| on (−1,1) has a concave kink at 0 which is admissible for the first form only). (2) Uniqueness of viscosity solutions of |Du| = 1 in ℝⁿ \ K vanishing on K FAILS without a sign or growth restriction: for K = {0}, the function u(x) = −|x| is a classical (hence viscosity) solution of |Du| − 1 = 0 in ℝⁿ \ {0} with u(0) = 0, different from d(x) = |x|. The distance is singled out among solutions by (c), or by nonnegativity/boundedness-below conditions that this lemma does not assert. (3) For K not closed the minimum in the definition of d must be replaced by an infimum and d vanishes on the closure of K, not only on K.
K ⊂ ℝⁿ is nonempty and closed
the Euclidean norm is used (for the eikonal equation |Du| = 1 the ball of the same norm is the unit speed set)
the eikonal equation is taken in the form |Du| − 1 = 0

[Definition of arXiv:2606.01683, 'Singular-value gap of nonreversible Markov processes'] For a Banach couple $(E_0, E_1)$, denote by $\mathcal{F}(E_0, E_1)$ the class 
    of functions $F: \Bar{S} \to E_0 + E_1$ satisfying
    \begin{itemize}
        \item $F$ is continuous on $\Bar{S}$ and analytic on $S$
        \item $F(it) \in E_0$ and $F(1+it) \in E_1$ for all $t \in \mathds{R}$
        \item $\|F\|_{\mathcal{F}(E_0, E_1)} \coloneqq 
        \max \Big\{ \sup_{t \in \mathds{R}} \|F(it)\|_{E_0}, \sup_{t \in \mathds{R}} \|F(1+it)\|_{E_1}           \Big\} < \infty$ 
    \end{itemize}
    Then, for $0 \leq \theta \leq 1 $, the \textbf{complex interpolation space} $[E_0, E_1]_\theta$ is the 
    Banach space defined by
    \[
        [E_0, E_1]_\theta \coloneqq \{h \in E_0 + E_1: h = F(\theta) \ \ \text{for some} \ F \in \mathcal{F}(E_0, E_1)\}
    \]
    equipped with the norm
    \[
        \|h\|_{[E_0, E_1]_\theta} \coloneqq \inf_{\substack{F \in \mathcal{F}(E_0, E_1) \\
        F(\theta) = h}} \|F\|_{\mathcal{F}(E_0, E_1)}
    \]
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2606.01683, 'Singular-value gap of nonreversible Markov processes'

[Proposition 104 (Passage of finite propagation to the cutoff limits) of arXiv:2607.10813, '2607.10813'] Let $(\chi_1,\rho_1)$ and $(\chi_2,\rho_2)$ be adapted to $(K,T_0)$, and let
$(u_\jmath,v_\jmath,\mathcal N_\jmath)$, $\jmath=1,2$, be the corresponding
limiting localized solutions with existence times $\tau_1,\tau_2$.  Fix
$T<\tau_1\wedge\tau_2$.  Choose
$\eta\in C_c^\infty(\R^3)$ such that $\eta=1$ on a neighborhood of $K$ and
$\operatorname{supp}\eta\subset K^{[1]}$.  For every sufficiently large
integer $J$, on the finite intersection of the two fixed-profile dyadic
probability-one events,
\begin{equation}
 \eta(u_1-u_2)=\eta(v_1-v_2)=0
 \quad\text{in }C_TH^{-J},
 \qquad
 \eta(\mathcal N_1-\mathcal N_2)=0
 \quad\text{in }L_T^1H^{-J}.
\end{equation}
For an arbitrary admissible cofinal cutoff sequence and deterministic
$T$, the same conclusion holds on the event
$\{T<\tau_1\wedge\tau_2\}$ in the partial convergence sense of
\cref{def:partial-probability-convergence}: the two localized approximations
converge in probability in the same Banach spaces to the common triple in
\eqref{eq:limit-localization-comparison}.

[Defn defi_kin_sol of arXiv:2608.30548, 'Finite speed of propagation and waiting time phenomena for stochastic porous media equatio'] Let $u_0\in L^1(\mathbb{T}^d)$ be non-negative and assume  (equation equation_n_m_together of the paper)  and (equation Eq_ass_B1 of the paper)--(equation Eq_ass_B3 of the paper). Then, a kinetic solution to (equation Eq_SPME_intro of the paper) is a non-negative, continuous, $\mathscr{F}$-adapted, $L^1(\mathbb{T}^d)$-valued process $u\in L^1(\Omega \times [0,T]\times \mathbb{T}^d)$, such that:
	\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
	\item mass is conserved, i.e., $\mathbb{P}$-a.s, we have  $\|u(t)\|_{L^1(\mathbb{T}^d)} = \|u_0\|_{L^1(\mathbb{T}^d)}$ for all $t\in [0,T]$,
	\item it holds $\sigma(u) \in L^2(\Omega \times [0,T]\times \mathbb{T}^d)$,
	\item  we have $((K\wedge u )\vee 1/K) \in  L^2(\Omega \times [0,T]; H^1(\mathbb{T}^d))$ for all $K\in \mathbb{N}$,
	\end{enumerate}  
and there exists  a kinetic measure $q$ with 
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
	\setcounter{enumi}{3}
	\item $\mathbb{P}$-a.s, $m\delta(v - u)v^{m-1} |\nabla u|^2 \le q $ in the sense of measures on $\mathbb{T}^d \times (0,\infty) \times [0,T]$,
	\item  $q$ vanishes at infinity in the sense that $\lim_{M\to\infty} \mathbb{E} [ q(\mathbb{T}^d \times [M,M+1] \times [0,T])] = 0$,
	\item and for every $\psi \in C_c^\infty(\mathbb{T}^d\times (0,\infty ))$, it holds $\mathbb{P}$-a.s.\ 
	\begin{align}\begin{split}&\int_{\mathbb{R}}\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}
		\mathbf{1}_{\{0<v <u(t,x)\}} \psi(x,v)
		\,\mathrm{d} x \mathrm{d} v \,=\, \int_{\mathbb{R}}\int_{\mathbb{T}^d}
		\mathbf{1}_{\{0<v <u_0(x)\}} \psi(x,v)
		\,\mathrm{d} x \mathrm{d} v\\&\qquad -\,m\int_0^t \int_{\mathbb{T}^d}
		u^{m-1}\nabla u \cdot (\nabla \psi )(x, u)
		\,
		\mathrm{d} x
		\mathrm{d} s\,-\, \frac{1}{2}\int_0^t \int_{\mathbb{T}^d}\bigl[\Psi_1 (\sigma'(u))^2 \nabla u \,+\, \sigma'(u) \sigma(u)\Psi_2 \bigr] \cdot (\nabla \psi )(x, u) \,\mathrm{d} x \mathrm{d} s

Let $D$ be a simply connected domain and $\varphi\colon \h \to D$ a conformal transformation. Let $j,k \in \N$ be such that $\abs{\varphi'(i)} \ge 2^{-j}$, and suppose that
 \[ \abs{\shortcutscales \cap \{j,\ldots,j+k\}} \ge N . \]

 \[ 
 \frac{\rmet{x}{y}{\Gamma}}{\rmett{x}{y}{\Gamma}} \le \sqrt{c_1 c_2} 
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \rmet{x}{y}{\Gamma} \ge \epsilon\,\median[2^{-j-k}]{} .
 \]
 Then
 \[ \p[ G_{D,\varphi} ] \ge p . \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let (Omega, F, mu) be a measure space and 1 <= p <= infinity. Then L^p(mu) is complete: every Cauchy sequence in the L^p norm converges in that norm to an element of L^p(mu), and a subsequence converges almost everywhere. In the Hilbert-space form: if (e_n) is an orthonormal sequence in L^2(mu) and (c_n) is a sequence of scalars, the series sum c_n e_n converges in L^2 if and only if sum |c_n|^2 < infinity, and when (e_n) is an orthonormal basis the map f |-> (<f, e_n>)_n is an isometric isomorphism of L^2(mu) onto l^2. For Fourier series on the circle this says that every square-summable coefficient sequence is the coefficient sequence of exactly one L^2 function.
(Omega, F, mu) any measure space (no sigma-finiteness needed)
1 <= p <= infinity
the Hilbert-space form: (e_n) orthonormal in L^2(mu), an orthonormal BASIS for the isomorphism statement

UNREVIEWED DRAFT, not a solution of C0056. Real symmetric finite matrices with all eigenvector squared components and IPR equal to 1/N can have local measures converging to singular-continuous Cantor measure. With N=2^k and eta=N^-1/2, the diagonal smoothing contribution is 1/(2pi sqrt(N))->0, while the full second moment is at least N^((1-log(2)/log(3))/2)/(5pi)->infinity. The abstract counterexample refutes an IPR-only inference, not the Anderson conjecture.

[Definition 11 (Signature of tfBm) of arXiv:2512.04646, '\textbf{Canonical Rough Path over Tempered Fractional Brownian Motion: Existence, Construc'] The \emph{signature} of $\mathbf{B}_{H,\lambda}$ over $[s,t]$ is
the formal power series
\[
S(\mathbf{B}_{H,\lambda})_{s,t}
= \Bigl(1,\;B_{H,\lambda}(s,t),\;
  \mathbb{B}_{H,\lambda}(s,t),\;
  \mathbb{B}^{(3)}_{H,\lambda}(s,t),\ldots\Bigr)
\in T((\mathbb{R}^d)),
\]
where $T((\mathbb{R}^d))=\prod_{k=0}^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)^{\otimes k}$
is the completed tensor algebra and $\mathbb{B}^{(k)}_{H,\lambda}$
denotes the $k$-th iterated integral, defined recursively by
Chen's relation.

Let X_1, ..., X_n be independent identically distributed random variables with E X_1 = 0, E X_1^2 = sigma^2 > 0 and rho = E |X_1|^3 < infinity. Let F_n be the distribution function of (X_1 + ... + X_n) / (sigma sqrt(n)) and Phi the standard normal distribution function. Then sup_x |F_n(x) - Phi(x)| <= C rho / (sigma^3 sqrt(n)) for an absolute constant C. The constant satisfies 0.4097 < C <= 0.4748 (the upper bound from Shevtsova, 2011). A version for independent but non-identically distributed summands holds with the third-moment ratio sum E|X_i|^3 / (sum sigma_i^2)^{3/2} and a slightly larger constant.

    \[

    \[
    B \colon \BMod_{(\sP, \sO)}(\SSeqnu(\sA, \sB)) \longrightarrow \BcoMod_{(B\sP, B\sO)}(\SSeqnu(\sA, \sB))
    \]
    on mapping categories. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 12 of arXiv:2608.30138, 'High-frequency wave propagation for the viscoelastic wave equation with singular memory'] For $k=0,1,\dots$, let $F\in C([0,T];H^k(\Omega))$, and
assume that \eqref{m-int-k} holds with $k+1$ in place of $k$. 
Then the Volterra equation 
\begin{equation}   
\Delta_{\sigma_\eps} u (t) -  \eps\nabla \cdot \int_0^t \mathfrak{m}(s,\cdot) \nabla u(t-s)\,\d s=F(t)
\end{equation}
has a unique solution $u\in C([0,T]; \, H^{k+2}(\Omega)\cap H_0^1(\Omega))$. Moreover, the norm of the solution operator $F\mapsto u$ is uniformly bounded in $\eps\in [0,\eps_0]$, for $\eps_0\ll1$ possibly depending on $m$.

[Proposition prop:q-refining-homeomorphism of arXiv:2604.05941, 'Banach spaces of continuous paths with finite $p$-th variation'] Let $q\ge2$ and let $\mathbb P=(\mathbb P^n)_{n\ge0}$ be a dense $q$-refining partition sequence. Then there exists a unique increasing homeomorphism $\phi:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ such that
    \[
        \phi(t_i^n)=\frac{i}{q^n},\qquad i=0,\dots,q^n,\ \ n\ge0.
    \]
    Equivalently, $\mathbb P^n=\phi^{-1}(\mathbb{T}_q^n)$, for $n\ge0$.

[Proposition 20 of arXiv:2605.08844, 'Signature Kernel and Schwinger-Dyson Kernel Equations as Two-Parameter Rough Differential '] For every \(n\in [1:\kappa+\zeta]\), let \(\ell=\lceil n/2\rceil\). Then the homogeneous components of the Schwinger--Dyson kernel satisfy
\begin{equation}
K_0(s,t)=1 +  \int_s^t  K_{1}(s,u) d\mathbf{X}_u du,
\qquad
K_n(s,t)
=
-\int_s^t \sigma_n\bigl(K_{\ell-1}(s, \cdot),K_{n-\ell}(\cdot, t)\bigr)_u\,d\mathbf X_u .
\end{equation}
Here, for every word \(I=i_1\cdots i_n\) over the alphabet \(\{1,\dots,d\}\), we set
\(
\tilde I:=i_1\cdots i_{\ell-1},\,
\hat I:=i_{\ell+1}\cdots i_n,
\)
and,given a basis \(e_1,\dots,e_d\) of \(V\), define
\begin{align*}
&\sigma_n:
\mathrm{Hom}\bigl(V^{\otimes(\ell-1)},\mathbb R\bigr)\boxtimes
\mathrm{Hom}\bigl(V^{\otimes(n-\ell)},\mathbb R\bigr)
\to
\mathrm{Hom}\bigl(V,\mathrm{Hom}(V^{\otimes n},\mathbb R)\bigr),\\
&\sigma_n(\eta,\xi)[e_j](e_I)
=
\sigma_n(\eta,\xi)[e_j](e_{\tilde I}\otimes e_{i_\ell}\otimes e_{\hat I})
=
\eta(e_{\tilde I})\,\delta_{i_\ell j}\,\xi(e_{\hat I}),
\end{align*}
for every word \(I\) of length \(n\), and extend linearly on \(V^{\otimes n}\).
title: Proposition 20 of arXiv:2605.08844

analytic) stratification 
$X=\bigsqcup_{\alpha \in A}X_\alpha$ of $X$ such that for any $\alpha \in A$ 
we have an isomprphism $F|_{X_\alpha}\simeq\CC_{X_\alpha}^{\oplus r_\alpha}$ 
locally on $X_\alpha$ for some $r_\alpha \geq 0$.

[Theorem thm:GP:restriction of arXiv:2605.28106, 'Gaussian Processes with Sample Paths in Reproducing Kernel Banach Spaces'] Let \( \xi : T \times \Omega \to \mathbb{R} \) be a centered Gaussian process, and suppose that there exists \( \Omega_0 \in \mathcal{A} \) with \( \mu(\Omega_0) = 1 \) such that \( \xi(\cdot,\omega) \in X \) for all \( \omega \in \Omega_0 \).
    Then the random element \( \eta : \Omega \to X \) defined by \( \xi \) is a centered Gaussian random element.

For arbitrary L/R words w in {L, R}^m and marked columns, the joint expectations of the height observables E[prod_{j=1}^k H(x_j, y_j)] under the doubly free-boundary Macdonald process are given by k-fold nested contour integrals of the form (1 / (2*pi*i)^k) * oint ... oint det[1 / (z_a - z_b)] * prod_{a=1}^k F_w(z_a; x_a, y_a) * prod_{a < b} S(z_a, z_b) dz_1 ... dz_k, where F_w contains the spectral rail-yard data and S(z_a, z_b) is the universal reflection kernel.
Contours enclose specified poles of F_w while excluding reflection poles

[Lemma lem:vertical-concatenation of arXiv:2608.12415, 'Sharp Phase Transition for Ellipsoid Fitting'] Given a backbone-dangling shape $\tau$, its deviation vector $\eta_\tau = L(\tau) \in \mathbb{R}^m $, and $w_\tau = M^{-1} \eta_\tau$, write \[ 
\mathsf{correct}(\tau) \coloneqq \frac{1}{1-\gamma} \left( \mathcal{L}^*(w_\tau ) - \gamma \cdot \mathsf{M} _\tau  \right)=   \mathsf{Proper}(\eta_\tau) + \mathsf{Error}(\eta_\tau)\,,
 \]
 where $\mathsf{Proper}(\eta_\tau)$ is a weighted linear combination of proper backbone-dangling shapes,	
 and $\mathsf{Error}$ are the remaining terms. We have
 \[ 
 \mathrm{Var}( \mathsf{Proper}(\eta_\tau))  = \frac{1}{1-\gamma}\cdot \mathrm{Var}(\eta_\eta)+o_d(1)=  \frac{\gamma}{1-\gamma}\cdot \mathrm{Var}(\tau) + o_d(1) 
 \]
 and
  \[
 \|\mathsf{ErrorShapes}\|_{sp} = o_d(1)\,.
  \]
We remind the reader that for a matrix $X$, we define its variance as $\mathrm{Var}(X)\coloneqq \frac{1}{\dim(X)} \cdot \mathbb{E}[\Tr(XX^\top)] $ and analogously for a vector. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Linearizing Deviation Attachment into Proper Shapes

[Lemma 22 (Basic Properties of Wishart Matrices) of arXiv:2609.02790, 'Full-Model Optimality for Tunable Linear Generative Priors in Compressed Sensing'] If $W\sim \mathcal W_p(\Sigma,n)$, then:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $W$ is almost surely symmetric positive semidefinite.
    \item $\mathbb{E}[W]=n\Sigma$.
    \item If $n\ge p$, then $W$ is almost surely invertible.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Basic Properties of Wishart Matrices

[Corollary 15 of arXiv:2607.17192, 'Geometric Regime--Switching Diffusions on Stratified Riemannian Spaces with an Application'] In addition to Theorem~\ref{thm:harris}, assume that there exists a measurable function $G:E \to \R$ such that $A_m^\ast V=G$ on \(O_m\) for all $m \ge 1$. If, furthermore, $X$ is aperiodic then it is $V$--uniformly geometrically ergodic:
		there exist constants $M<\infty$ and $c>0$ such that
		\[
		\|P_t(x,\cdot)-\pi\|_V
		:=\sup_{|f|\le V}\left|P_t f(x)-\pi(f)\right|
		\le M V(x)e^{-c t},
		\qquad x\in E,\ t\ge0.
		\]

body:
Let X and Y be Banach spaces. (a) The set Phi(X,Y) of Fredholm operators is open in B(X,Y) and the index ind: Phi(X,Y) -> Z is locally constant, hence continuous and constant on each connected component (in particular along norm-continuous paths of Fredholm operators). Quantitatively, if T is Fredholm with regularizer S, then T + E is Fredholm with ind(T + E) = ind T whenever ||E|| < 1/||S||. (b) If T is Fredholm and K is compact, then T + K is Fredholm and ind(T + K) = ind T. (c) The kernel dimension and the codimension of the range are upper semicontinuous: for ||E|| small enough, dim ker(T + E) <= dim ker T and dim(Y/ran(T + E)) <= dim(Y/ran T). Individually these numbers can jump down, only their difference is stable.
X and Y are Banach spaces
T in B(X,Y) is Fredholm
E in B(X,Y) with ||E|| small (explicitly ||E|| < 1/||S|| for a regularizer S) in (a) and (c)
K in B(X,Y) compact in (b)

Hence (I + S E)^{-1} S (T + E) = I - Q and (T + E) S (I + E S)^{-1} = I - Q' with Q = (I + S E)^{-1} P and Q' = P'(I + E S)^{-1} of finite rank; note (I + S E)^{-1} S = S (I + E S)^{-1}, so a single operator serves on both sides. [Pro 4 of arXiv:2605.30779, '2605.30779'] Let \(H_N\) be a GOE matrix when \(\beta=1\) and a GUE matrix when \(\beta=2\). Let
\begin{align*}
  P = \sum_{i=1}^md_ie_ie_i^\ast = \diag(d_1,\dots,d_m,0,\dots,0), \qquad d_i=1-\theta_iN^{-1/3}, \qquad i= {} 1,\dots,m,
\end{align*}
with $\theta_i \in \realR$. Write
\[
\lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_N
\]
for the eigenvalues of \(H_N+P\). Then, for each fixed \(k\ge1\),
\[
\bigl(
N^{2/3}(2-\lambda_1),\dots,N^{2/3}(2-\lambda_k)
\bigr)
\Longrightarrow
\bigl(
\Lambda_{\beta,1}^{(\theta_1,\dots,\theta_m)},\dots,
\Lambda_{\beta,k}^{(\theta_1,\dots,\theta_m)}
\bigr).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Pro 4 of arXiv:2605.30779

[Proposition 14 of arXiv:2609.02779, '2609.02779'] For the Hamiltonian \eqref{eq:twowell-H} constructed above, there exist
$C_0>0$ and $\lambda_0>0$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \|u_\lambda-u_0\|_\infty
 \ge C_0\lambda|\log\lambda|
 \qquad\text{for }0<\lambda\le\lambda_0.
\end{equation}
Consequently, Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-main} gives
\[
 \|u_\lambda-u_0\|_\infty
 \asymp\lambda|\log\lambda|.
\]

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2608.21063, '\textbf{Non-bijective scaling limits and phase transitions of planar maps}'] All limits below are taken in the Gromov--Hausdorff--Prokhorov sense as $n\to\infty$, restricted to $n\equiv0 \mod d_\omega $.
	
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item Suppose that Condition~\eqref{eq:bwfvv} holds, or that $\nu=1$ and Condition~\eqref{eq:bwregvar} holds for some $\frac{5}{4} < \alpha \le 2$. Then $\kappa < \infty$ and
		\[
			\left( \mM_n^\omega, \frac{2^{1/\alpha-1}}{\kappa}\frac{b_{n}}{n} d_{\mM_n^\omega}, \mu_{\mM_n^\omega} \right) \convd (\mathbf{T}_\alpha, d_{\mathbf{T}_\alpha}, \mu_{\mathbf{T}_\alpha}).
		\]
		\item Suppose that $\nu=1$, that Condition~\eqref{eq:bwregvar} holds with $\alpha=5/4$, and that the limit  \[
			c_\omega := \lim_{k \to \infty} L(k) \in  ]0, \infty[
		\]
		exists. Then
		\[
		   \left( \mM_n^\omega, \frac{1}{\mathfrak d_{\mathbf{M}}} \left(\frac{6}{d_\omega}\right)^{1/4} \left(\frac{5\Gamma(3/4)^4}{c_\omega}\right)^{1/5} \frac{1}{n^{1/5}\log n} d_{\mM_n^\omega}, \mu_{\mM_n^\omega} \right)
		\convd \left( \mathbf T_{5/4}, d_{\mathbf T_{5/4}}, \mu_{\mathbf T_{5/4}} \right).
		\]
		\item Suppose that $\nu=1$ and that Condition~\eqref{eq:bwregvar} holds for some $1 < \alpha < \frac{5}{4}$.	 Then
		\[
			\left( \mM_n^\omega, \left( \frac{3}{2^{2 + 1/\alpha} b_{n}} \right)^{1/4} d_{\mM_n^\omega}, \mu_{\mM_n^\omega} \right) \convd \left(\mathbf{T}^{\mathrm{dec}}_\alpha(\mathbf{M}), d_{\mathbf{T}^{\mathrm{dec}}_\alpha(\mathbf{M})}, \mu_{\mathbf{T}^{\mathrm{dec}}_\alpha(\mathbf{M})}\right).
		\]
		\item Suppose that $\nu=1$ and that Condition~\eqref{eq:bwregvar} holds with $\alpha=1$. Then
		\[ 
			\left(\mM_n^\omega, \left(\frac{3}{8 b_{n}}\right)^{1/4} d_{\mM_n^\omega}, \mu_{\mM_n^\omega} \right) \convd (\mathbf{M}, d_{\mathbf{M}},\mu_{\mathbf{M}}).
		\]
		\item Suppose that either $0<\nu<1$ and Condition~\eqref{eq:bwregvar} holds for some $\alpha\ge1$, or $\nu=0$ and Condition~\eqref{eq:bwcc14} holds. Then
		\[
			\left( \mM_n^\omega, \left( \frac{3}{8(1-\nu)n} \right)^{1/4} d_{\mM_n^\omega}, \mu_{\mM_n^\omega} \right) \convd (\mathbf{M},d_{\mathbf{M}},\mu_{\mathbf{M}}).
		\]
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 2 of arXiv:2608.21063

[Conj 8 of arXiv:2609.01413, 'Sharp Threshold for Universality of Rational Canonical Forms over a Finite Field'] Let $A_n\in\Mat_n(\F_p)$ be an $\alpha_n$-balanced random matrix
    with independent entries. If
    \begin{equation}
        
        \liminf_{n\to\infty}
        \frac{n\alpha_n}{\log n}>
        \frac{1}{d},
    \end{equation}
    then the joint distribution of partitions
    $$
    \left(\lambda^{(F_{i_1})}(A_n),\ldots,
    \lambda^{(F_{i_r})}(A_n)
    \right)
    $$
    converges pointwise to the same limiting distribution as in
    \Cref{thm:main}. (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Conjecture 8 of arXiv:2609.01413

body: [Prop rel norm in open subscheme of arXiv:2609.04023, 'Characterizing Contractions and Weighted Blowdowns'] Suppose $f : \mathcal{Y} \to \mathcal{X}$ is a finite \'etale morphism of reduced Deligne--Mumford stacks where $\mathcal{Y}$ is normal and contains an open dense subscheme $U$. Then, the normalization of $\mathcal{X}$ in $f|_U : U \to \mathcal{X}$ is precisely $f :\mathcal{Y} \to \mathcal{X}$, i.e., $\mathcal{X}^\nu_{f|_U} \simeq \mathcal{Y}.$

body:
[Definition 26 of arXiv:2608.30991, 'A block-Toeplitz approach to the spectrum of the Neumann-Poincaré operator on self-similar'] Let $a:\mathbb{T}\to\mathcal{L}(X)$. A \emph{right Wiener--Hopf factorisation} of $a$ with respect to the unit circle $\mathbb{T}$ is a representation
	\[
	a(z)=a_-(z)\Lambda(z)a_+(z),
	\qquad z\in\mathbb{T},
	\]
	in which $a_+$ and $a_+^{-1}$ extend holomorphically to the interior unit disk $\mathbb{D}$, $a_-$ and $a_-^{-1}$ extend holomorphically to the exterior domain $\mathbb{E} = \{z : |z| > 1\} \cup \{\infty\}$, all four with continuous boundary values on $\mathbb{T}$, and
	\[
	\Lambda(z)=I-\Pi+\sum_{j=1}^{J}z^{\nu_j}\Pi_j,
	\qquad
	\Pi:=\sum_{j=1}^{J}\Pi_j,
	\]
	where $\Pi_1,\dots,\Pi_J$ are rank-one idempotents with $\Pi_i\Pi_j=0$ for $i\neq j$ and $\nu_1,\dots,\nu_J\in\mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\}$ are the \emph{non-zero partial indices}, not necessarily distinct. The factorisation is \emph{canonical} if $J=0$, that is $\Lambda\equiv I$.
title: Definition 26 of arXiv:2608.30991

body:
[Definition 1 of arXiv:2608.29406, 'Partially Totally Real Submanifolds of Sasakian Manifolds'] A submanifold $M$ of a Sasakian manifold, tangent to $\xi$, is called a \emph{partially totally real (PTR) submanifold} if there exists a nonzero constant-rank totally real distribution $\Dperp\subset TM\cap\ker\eta$, i.e.
\[
 \phi\Dperp\subset\Tperp.
\]
If $\Dtilde$ denotes the orthogonal complement of $\Dperp\oplus\langle\xi\rangle$ in $TM$, then
\begin{equation}
 TM=\Dperp\oplus\Dtilde\oplus\langle\xi\rangle.
\end{equation}
Following the K\"ahler PTR terminology, $\Dtilde$ is called the
\emph{ambiguous distribution}.  The PTR structure refers to this chosen
decomposition; maximality of \(\Dperp\), when needed, is imposed later
and is not part of the definition.
title: Definition 1 of arXiv:2608.29406

[Proposition 1 of arXiv:2608.21905, '\bf Ruin theory incorporating MIPP-type jumps'] For each fixed $n\geq 2$, the sojourn times of $V_t^{(n)}$ are i.i.d. exponential random variables. More specifically,
\[
S_k^{(n)}\sim \mathrm{EXP}(\lambda q_{n-1}), \forall k\geq 1, 
\]
where $q_{n-1}=P(V_1^{(n-1)}>0)$. The sequence $q_j, j\geq 1,$ satisfy  the  recursive relation
\[
q_j=1-e^{-\lambda q_{j-1}}, \; j\geq 2,
\]
with
\[
q_1=1-e^{-\lambda}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:truth-lemma-imp-left of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] Let $L \supseteq \textbf{FIK}$, $x = (\Gamma_x, \Delta_x) \in W_L^*$, $\varphi, \psi \in \mathscr{L}_{\Box\Diamond}$.
  If $(\varphi \to \psi) \notin \Gamma_x$, then there is $x' = (\Gamma_x', \Delta_x') \in W_L^*$ such that
  $x \leq^* x'$, $\varphi \in \Gamma_x'$, and $\psi \in \Delta_x'$.
  \begin{proof}
    Suppose $(\varphi \to \psi) \notin \Gamma_x$, then $(\varphi \to \psi) \in \Delta_x$ by maximality.
    Here, $(\Gamma_x \cup \set{\varphi}, \set{\psi})$ is $L$-consistent;
    for otherwise, there is a finite $X \subseteq \Gamma_x$ such that $L \vdash \left(\bigwedge X \land \varphi\right) \to \psi$,
    then $L \vdash \bigwedge X \to (\varphi \to \psi)$, so $(\Gamma, \Delta)$ would be $L$-inconsistent since $X \subseteq \Gamma_x$ and $\varphi \to \psi \in \Delta_x$.
    Now by the Lindenbaum lemma, there is $x' = (\Gamma_x', \Delta_x') \in W_L^*$ such that $\Gamma_x \cup \set{\varphi} \subseteq \Gamma_x'$ and $\psi \in \Delta_x'$.
    Here, $x \leq^* x'$ by the definition of $\leq^*$.
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:sliceleaves_intersection of arXiv:2608.30973, 'Pseudo-Anosov flow and dynamics on guts'] Let \(a,b\) be two different slice leaves in \(\mathcal{F}^{\pm}\).
Then \(a\) and \(b\) intersects at at most one point.

Suppose that, in addition, there are two distinct points \(p,q\) in \(\partial P_{\varphi}\) such that \(\partial a\in (p,q)\) and \(\partial b\in (q,p)\).
Denote by \(R_{a},R_{b}\) the complementary regions of \(a,b\) whose boundaries avoid \(p,q\), respectively.
Then, \(R_{a}\cap R_{b}= \emptyset\).
Further, \(\overline{R}_{a}\cap \overline{R}_{b}\neq \emptyset\) if and only if \(a\cap b\) is a singular point \(p\); in this case, \(\overline{R}_{a}\cap \overline{R}_{b}=p\) and we say that \(a\) and \(b\) are \emph{tangent} at \(p\).

under energy imbalance: with class energies $E(1\pm\eta)$ it equals
$\frac E8(5-3|\eta|)$ --- a downward cusp;
(ii) for every sequence of moment systems converging to a point of
$\mathcal E$ in which some direction class genuinely splits,
\[
  \limsup\ \frac1E\inf_{|\operatorname{supp} q|\le3,\,|\mu|<1}C\ \le\ \frac12\ <\
  \frac58 .
\]
Hence no nearby ascent direction exists: $\mathcal E$ is a local maximum of
the three-point value in the stratified sense.

The rigorous determination of the Ising perceptron storage capacity (the Ding-Sun framework and its successors) is conditional on explicit numerical hypotheses: finitely many concrete inequalities about one-dimensional variational quantities attached to the Krauth-Mezard formula, stated precisely in arXiv:2607.11010. That work verifies every such condition by rigorous interval (ball) arithmetic in Arb over explicit compact domains, locating the capacity constant alpha* within [0.833078599, 0.833078600], consistent with the 1989 Krauth-Mezard prediction. The verification is computer-assisted (certificates, replays, and a Lean exact-arithmetic layer are public) and, as of this writing, not independently refereed; the exact list of verified inequalities lives in the cited paper and artifact, not in this summary node.

[Proposition prop:density_bound_2 of arXiv:2608.13452, 'Wasserstein stability of the zero cell of a Poisson hyperplane tessellation under directio'] Let $\hat{f}^{(1)}_{\gamma, n}$ and $\hat{f}^{(2)}_{\gamma, n}$ be the estimators of a density $f$ as defined in Proposition (prop:density-robust of the paper). 
    Assume that the hypotheses of Proposition (prop:density-robust of the paper) are satisfied.
    Further assume that $f$ is globally $L$-Lipschitz and $\mathrm{supp}(f) \subseteq [0,1]^d$, and that \(\phi_2\) satisfies
    \begin{align}
        W_{\mathrm{geo}}(\phi_1,\phi_2) 
        <  
        \min\biggl\{\varepsilon_0(\phi_1), \min_{u \in S^{d-1}} h(\Pi_1,u)\biggr\},
    \end{align}
    where \(\varepsilon_0(\phi_1)\) is the constant from (lem:2constant_local_holder of the paper).
    Then there exist random probability densities
    $\hat{g}_{\gamma,n}^{(1)}$ and
    $\hat{g}_{\gamma,n}^{(2)}$, defined on a common probability space,
    such that, for every fixed $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$,
    \[
    \hat{g}_{\gamma,n}^{(i)}(x)
    \overset{(d)}{=}
    \hat{f}_{\gamma,n}^{(i)}(x),
    \qquad i=1,2,
    \]
    and such that
    \begin{align*}
     \mathbb{E} \left[\int_{[0,1]^d}\left|\hat{g}^{(1)}_{\gamma, n}(x) - \hat{g}^{(2)}_{\gamma, n}(x)\right| \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} x\right]
    &\leq \frac{\|f\|_{\infty}^{1/2}\gamma^{d/2}\left(\mathrm{vol}(\Pi_1)^{1/2} + \mathrm{vol}(\Pi_2)^{1/2}\right)}{n^{1/2}} + \frac{L \tilde{C}(\phi_1, d)}{\gamma}W_{\mathrm{geo}}(\phi_1,\phi_2)^{1/d}, 
\end{align*}
for some constant $\tilde{C}(\phi_1,d)$ depending only on $\phi_1$ and $d$, where the expectation is taken with respect to the random tessellations and $\mathcal{D}_n$.
title: Proposition prop:density_bound_2 of arXiv:2608.13452

[Definition def:weakly_completely_S of arXiv:2509.20779, 'Diffusive Scaling limit of stochastic Box-Ball systems and P\MakeLowercase{ush}TASEP'] Let $R$ be a $d \times k$ matrix, $S$ be a convex polyhedron in (equation eq:def_polyhedron of the paper) 
	and $f$ be a function from $\{1,2,\dots, k\}$ to the power set  $\mathcal P(\{1,2,\dots, m\})$. Assume that, for each maximal subset $I \subseteq \{1,2,\dots, m\}$, there exists $\lambda_{I} \in \mathbb{R}^I_{> 0}$ such that $(\lambda_{I}^\top N^IR^I)_j \ge 1$ for all $j \in J_I$, where $N^I:=[n_i]_{i \in I}^\top$ is a $|I| \times d$ matrix consisting of row vectors $n_i$ with $i \in I$, $J_I := \{1 \le j \le k: f(j) \subseteq I\}$, and $R^I:=[R_j]_{f(j) \subseteq I}$ consists of column vectors $R_j$ with $f(j) \subseteq I$.
	Then $R$ is said to be weak $\mathcal S$ with respect to $S$ and $f$.

[Lemma 18 of arXiv:2608.30875, 'A Decomposition Theorem for Topological Semi-small Maps'] Let $f:X \longrightarrow [0,1]$ be a proper surjection such that the restriction $f\vert_{f^{-1}((0,1])}:f^{-1}((0,1]) \longrightarrow (0,1]$ is a trivial fiber bundle with closed stratified fibers; i.e., $f^{-1}((0,1]) \cong F_{1}\times (0,1]$,
    where $F_{1}$ is a closed stratified space. Suppose that the fiber $F_{0}:=f^{-1}(\{0\})$
    is a closed stratified space. If $X$ is a topologically stratified space, then there exists a map $g:F_{1}\longrightarrow F_{0}$ such that $X$ is homeomorphic to the mapping cylinder $\operatorname{Cyl}(g)$.

[Lem 11 of arXiv:2608.21312, 'Interface between competing random walks on a cycle'] Fix $k,m\ge1$. Let $S_n$ be the ATD walk as in~\eqref{eq:ATD walk}. Then there are universal constants $C_1$ and $C_2$ such that 
\[
  \pr\left(\exists\,1\le j\le m:k m^2<\zeta_j\le 2k m^2\right)  \ge \frac{C_1}{\sqrt{k}}
\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad
  \pr\left(\abs{ S_m^{(j)}}>\frac12 km^2\right)\le \frac{C_2}{\sqrt{k}},
\]
for each $1\le j\le m$.
title: Lem 11 of arXiv:2608.21312

body:
[Satz 6 of arXiv:2506.13661, 'Box-Covariances of Hyperuniform Point Processes'] Let $\eta$ be a stationary hyperuniform point process on $\mathbb{R}^2$ with truncated pair correlation measure $\beta.$ Suppose that $\beta$ is box-symmetric (with respect to reflection and swapping of the axes), that ${|\beta|(\mathbb{R}^2)<\infty}$, and that $F(x):=\beta(\Lambda_\infty(x))$ is non-positive (or, non-negative) for $\|x\|$ sufficiently large. 
	Assume further that both $H_\pm(y_1,y_2):= \int_0^{y_1}\int_0^{y_2}F(\pm x_1,x_2)\mathrm{d}x_1\mathrm{d}x_2$ are multivariate $(a_\pm,g_\pm)$-regularly varying, each with $a_\pm\in[0,1]$ and such that $g_-(x,y)=g_-(y,x)$. Moreover assume $K_+:=\lim_{n\to\infty}H_+(n,n)/H_-(n,n)$ exists and set $K_-=-1$.
	Then, $\mathrm{cov}(z)$ exists and can be expressed similar to \eqref{eq:Cov_non_int}. 
	
	
	More precisely, denoting $|z|:=(|z_1|,|z_2|)$ and $\tau(z)=\min(\mathrm{sign}(z_1),\mathrm{sign}(z_2))$ (i.e. $\tau(z)=-$ if and only if at least one of $z_1,z_2$ has negative sign), then for $z\in\Lambda_\infty(0)$, we have
	\begin{align*}
		\mathrm{cov}(z)= &  -K_+\|z\|^ag_+\left(\frac{z}{\|z\|}\right)+\sum_{\substack{e\in\mathbb{Z}^2\\ \|e\|=1}}\frac{K_{\tau(z+e)}}{2} \|z+e\|^ag_{\tau(z+e)}\left(\frac{|z+e|}{\|z+e\|}\right)\\
		&-\sum_{v\in\{-1,1\}^2}\frac{K_{\tau(z+v)}}{4}\|z+v\|^ag_{\tau(z+v)}\left(\frac{|z+v|}{\|z+v\|}\right)+ \ind_{\Lambda_1}(z)\frac{1}{2}\|z-\mathbf 1\|^ag_{\tau(z+v)}\left(\frac{|z-\mathbf 1|}{\|z-\mathbf 1\|}\right).
	\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Satz 6 of arXiv:2506.13661

body:
[Proposition 38 of arXiv:2608.07239, 'Unified framework for asymptotically uniform iterative construction of generalised random '] Assume that $\alpha\to\infty$, with $\ell$ fixed and $M=O(\alpha^{\sfrac12}/(\log\alpha)^2)$. Consider the following three conditions on an alternative weight function $\b':V\to\mathbb{R}$ with $\b'_{\max}:=\max\{|\b'(v)|:v\in V\}=O(M/\alpha)$.
		\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
			\item We have $\b'(v)=\b(v)$ for all $v\in V\setminus F$.
			\item We have $\b'(v)=-\log(1-\b(v))$ for all $v\in V$.
			\item The quantity $\b(S)-\b'(S)$ is the same for all MISs $S$ of $G$. 
		\end{enumerate}
		If $\b'$ satisfies any of these conditions, then for any FMIS $S$ of $G$, substituting $\b'$ for $\b$ in the definition of $\mathscr{P}(S)$ multiplies its value by a factor of $1+O(M^2/\alpha)$. It follows that the IMFIS process on $(G,F,R,\b')$ gives the same distribution on $\boldsymbol{S}_{\infty}$ as the IMFIS process on $(G,F,R,\b)$, up to a factor of $1+O(\mathscr{E}(\alpha,M))$.
		
		Furthermore, for any FIS $T$ of $G$ and vertex set $U$ satisfying the requirements of Theorem~\ref{theorem_space}, substituting $\b'$ for $\b$ in the definition of $\mathscr{Q}(T,U)$ multiplies its value by a factor of $1+O(\mathscr{E}(\alpha',M'))$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 38 of arXiv:2608.07239

body:
[Lemma 12 of arXiv:2511.06414, 'Non-uniform Edgeworth expansions for weakly dependent random variables and their applicati'] Under Assumption \ref{GrowAssum},
for all $x\in\bbR$ and $3\leq p\leq m$ we have
$$
\left|\Phi_{p,n}(x)-\Phi_{p-1,n}(x)\right|\leq C_m(1+|x|)^{-m-1}\sig_n^{-(p-2)}.
$$
As a consequence, for all $2\leq m_1<m$,
$$
\left|\Phi_{m,n}(x)-\Phi_{m_1,n}(x)\right|\leq A_m(1+|x|)^{-m-1}\sig_n^{-(m_1-1)}.
$$
Here $A_m,C_m$ are constants that do not depend on $n$ or $x$.

[Lemma 3 of arXiv:2606.14038, 'Trivariate Hypergeometric Series Formulas\\ for Pure Partition Functions of Multiple $3$-S'] Suppose $\{y_1,y_2,y_3,y_4\}=\{u_1,v_1,u_2,v_2\}$ and   $y_4<y_3<y_2<y_1$.  Then
  $$\lim_{t\to \tau^-}\frac{(g_t(y_1)-g_t(y_2))(g_t(y_3)-g_t(y_4))} {(g_t(y_1)-g_t(y_3))(g_t(y_2)-g_t(y_4))}\begin{cases}
    \in (0,1) &\text{if } \eta(\tau)\in(-\infty,y_4);\\
    \in (0,1) &\text{if } \eta(\tau)\in(y_4,y_3);\\
    =0 &\text{if } \eta(\tau)\in(y_3,y_2);\\
    \in (0,1) &\text{if } \eta(\tau)\in(y_2,y_1).\\
  \end{cases}$$
  By the elementary cross-ratio identity
\(
\frac{(a-b)(c-d)}{(a-c)(b-d)}
+
\frac{(a-d)(b-c)}{(a-c)(b-d)}
=1
\),
the complementary cross-ratio has limit equal to one minus the limit above.

[Corollary 3 of arXiv:2608.29486, 'Cabled braids and their crossing matrices'] Let $A=[a_{ij}]$ be an $n \times n$ zero-diagonal symmetric matrix. 
If $A$ satisfies that for any subset $S$ of $N= \{ 1, 2, \dots , n \}$ with $1<|S|<n$, $a_{kl}\ne a_{kl'}$ for any $k\in \overline{S}$ and any distinct $l, l'\in S$, then $A$ is the crossing matrix of a pseudo-Anosov pure $n$-braid. 
In particular, if $a_{kl}\ne a_{kl'}$ for any $k\in N$ and any distinct $l, l'\in N$, then $A$ is the crossing matrix of a pseudo-Anosov pure $n$-braid. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let (a_n) be a sequence of real numbers that is monotonically decreasing with limit 0, and let (b_n) be a sequence of real or complex numbers whose partial sums B_N = b_1 + ... + b_N are bounded, |B_N| <= K for all N. Then the series sum a_n b_n converges. Special cases: the alternating series test (b_n = (-1)^n) and the convergence of sum a_n sin(n x) and sum a_n cos(n x) for every x that is not a multiple of 2 pi, since the partial sums of sin(n x) and cos(n x) are bounded by 1/|sin(x/2)|. Abel's test is the companion: if sum b_n converges and (a_n) is monotone and bounded, then sum a_n b_n converges.
(a_n) real, decreasing, a_n -> 0

[Theoremi thm_main_undirected of arXiv:2604.04672, 'Connected components and topological ends of stationary planar forests'] With probability one, every connected component of $G$ is a tree with at most $2$ topological ends. Let $N_0, N_1$ and $N_2$ respectively denote the number of finite, one-ended and two-ended connected components of $G$, taking values in $\mathbb{Z}_+\cup\{\infty\}$. Then, $(N_0,N_1,N_2)$ is constant on a full-probability event, and the following holds almost surely:
        \begin{itemize}
            \item $N_0\in\{0,\infty\}$,
            \item $N_1\leq 2$, and
            \item $N_1=2\implies N_2<\infty$.
        \end{itemize}
    Moreover, this classification is optimal: every value for $(N_0,N_1,N_2)$ satisfying the above constraints is realized by some model on which the result applies. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theoremi thm_main_undirected of arXiv:2604.04672

body:
[Defn 5 of arXiv:2603.28702, 'Distribution of the magnetization of the critical Ising model on sparse random graphs'] \begin{itemize}
\item 
Let $G$ be a graph with vertex set $V$. The Ising model on this graph with inverse temperature $\beta$ is the probability measure $\mu$ on $\{-1,1\}^V$ satisfying
$$\mu_{\beta}(\sigma)=\dfrac{1}{Z_{\beta,G}}\exp\left(\beta\SL{u\sim v}\sigma_u\sigma_v\right).$$
\item
Fix a measure $\nu$ on $\{-1,1\}^V$. For a configuration $\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^V$ and for some $v\in V$, let $\sigma^{\oplus v}$ be the configuration $\sigma$ in which the spin at vertex $v$ is flipped. For two configurations $\sigma,\tau\in\{-1,1\}^V$, we write $\sigma\sim\tau$ if $\tau=\sigma^{\oplus v}$ for some $v\in V$. The continuous time Glauber Dynamics on $G$ for $\nu$ at rate 1 is a Markov chain with transition rates, for $\sigma\neq\tau$, equal to
$$q(\sigma,\tau)=\begin{cases}
\dfrac{\nu(\tau)}{\nu(\sigma)+\nu(\tau)},\ \ \text{if}\ \ \sigma \sim \tau
\\ \\
0,\ \ \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}$$
Informally, every vertex gets updated at rate one, and the update happens conditionally on the configuration in the rest of the vertices.
\end{itemize}
title: Definition 5 of arXiv:2603.28702

body:
[Cor 9 of arXiv:2609.03791, 'Canonical Bochner--K\"{a}hler potentials via the Sasaki--K\"{a}hler correspondence'] A Bochner--K\"{a}hler manifold $M$ is locally homogeneous if and only if the parameter $a=0$ and the eigenvalues $\tau$ of $X$ satisfy $\tau^2=-r$. 
    
    For $\tau=0$, we get the flat K\"{a}hler metric on $\mathbb C^n$.
    
    For $\tau\neq 0$, the locally defined manifold extends to a Cartesian product of a $\mathbb CP^{n_1}$ with Fubini--Study metric and a ball $\mathbb B^{n_2}$ with Bergman metric, with potential
    \begin{equation}
    v=\frac{1}{\tau}\log (1+\tau \langle z',z'\rangle)- \frac{1}{\tau}\log (1-\tau \langle z'',z''\rangle)
    \end{equation}
    where $n_1+n_2=n$ and $\tau>0$ is a real parameter. These K\"{a}hler manifolds are globally homogeneous. In this case the parameter $\beta\in \mathbb C^n$ is arbitrary and $\hBlock$ consists of two arbitrary hermitian diagonal blocks of dimensions $n_1\times n_1$ and $n_2\times n_2$, respectively, resulting in a symmetry group of dimension $2n+n_1^2+n_2^2$.

[Theorem thm:1.1 of arXiv:2607.06785, 'On the smallest singular value of the product of random and deterministic matrices'] Let \(A=(a_{ij})\) be an \(n\times n\) real-valued random matrix with independent entries satisfying for all \(i,j\),
\[
  \mathbb{E}[a_{ij}] = 0,\quad \mathbb{E}[a_{ij}^2] = 1,\quad \mathbb{E}[a_{ij}^4] \leqslant K,
  \quad \mathcal{L}(a_{ij},1)\leqslant \kappa
\]
where \(K\geqslant1\) and \(\kappa\in(0,1)\). Further, let \(M\) be a fixed real-valued invertible \(n\times n\) matrix.
Then there exist constants \(C,c>0\), depending only on \(K\) and \(\kappa\),
such that for all $\varepsilon \geqslant 0$
\begin{equation} 
   \mathbb{P}\Bigl(s_{\min}(MA) \leqslant \frac{\varepsilon}{\|M^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}}\Bigr)
  \leqslant C \varepsilon + e^{-cn}. 
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:1.1 of arXiv:2607.06785

[Proposition prop:fkg of arXiv:2412.04539, 'Counting minimal cutsets and $p_c<1$'] Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite, connected graph. Let $\mathrm P$ be a positively associated percolation  measure on $G$. Let $B \subset  V$, let $\theta,p \in (0,1]$ and suppose that  $\mathrm P(u \leftrightarrow B) \geq \theta$ for every $u \in V$, and $\mathrm P(e \text{ is open}) \geq p$ for every $e \in E$.
Then for every $o \in V$,
    \[
        \mathrm P\left( \bigcap_{b \in B} \{ o \leftrightarrow b \}  \right) \geq c^{|B|},
      \]
      where  $c := \left(\frac{p\theta}{2}\right)^{3/\theta}$.
title: Proposition prop:fkg of arXiv:2412.04539

body:
Let p and q be probability mass functions on a finite set, d = d_TV(p, q), and call a coupling (X, Y) of p and q maximal when P(X != Y) = d. Every maximal coupling has P(X = Y = x) = min(p_x, q_x) for every x, and the maximal couplings are exactly the diagonal min(p, q) plus a transport plan from (p - q)_+ to (q - p)_+. For an event A let o = sum over x in A of min(p_x, q_x), u = sum over x in A of (p_x - q_x)_+ and v = sum over x in A of (q_x - p_x)_+. Over all maximal couplings, P(X in A, Y in A) takes exactly the values in [o + max(0, u + v - d), o + min(u, v)].
p, q probability mass functions on one finite set
maximal means P(X != Y) = d_TV(p, q)

[Theo 3 of arXiv:2605.23292, 'Second-order Poincaré inequalities and localization on the Poisson space'] (rates of normal convergence for sums of $BL$-space-time localizing scores on metric spaces) 
Let $\xi:(X \times \R \times \MM) \times \mathbf{N}_{X \times \R \times \MM} \rightarrow \R$ be a score function on the marked space domain $X \times \R \times \MM$ and $\P$ a Poisson process on $X \times \R$ with intensity $\nu \otimes \mu $ and $\hat{\P}$ its marked version. Define
\[
H:=H(\hat{\P}) = \sum_{(z,t_z) \in \P \cap (W \times \R)} \xi((z,t_z, M_z),\hat{\P}).
\]
Assume that $\xi$ satisfies  $BL\big(\tfrac{1}{240}, \tfrac{1}{120}\big)$ space-time localization according to Def.~\ref{def:space-time-loc}, with $M^\xi_{5,X}<\infty$.
For $\psi$ as in Def.~\ref{def:space-time-loc} and $q>0$, put 
\[
G_{q}:=\int_{X} \psi(d(x,W))^{q} \nu(dx) = 2^q \nu(W) + \int_{X\setminus W} \psi(d(x,W))^{q} \nu(dx).
\]
If $G_{1/120}<\infty$, then there is a 
$C_K<\infty$ given by
\[
C_K:= c\cdot  {\cal I}_{\psi,X}\big(\tfrac{1}{240}\big)^{3} \cdot {\cal I}_{\phi}\big(\tfrac{1}{120}\big)^{7/2},
\]
where $c<\infty$ is a universal scalar, such that
\begin{equation} 
    \mathbf{d}_K \left(  \frac{H - \E H} {\sqrt{\Var H}}, N \right) \leq C_K \cdot (M_{5,X}^\xi)^{2/5} \cdot \frac{G_{1/120}^{1/2}}{\Var H}
\end{equation}
and there is a $C_W <\infty$ given by
\[
C_W := c \cdot  {\cal I}_{\psi,X}(\tfrac{1}{50})^{3} \cdot {\cal I}_{\phi}(\tfrac{3}{200})^{4}
\]
such that
\begin{equation} 
    \mathbf{d}_W \left(  \frac{H - \E H} {\sqrt{\Var H}}, N \right) \leq C_K \cdot (M_{5,X}^\xi)^{2/5} \cdot \frac{G_{1/120}^{1/2}}{\Var H} + C_W  \cdot (M_{5,X}^\xi)^{3/5} \cdot\frac{G_{3/200}}{(\Var H)^{3/2}}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theo 3 of arXiv:2605.23292

body:
[Lemma lem:nointersectAT of arXiv:2604.15146, 'Renormalised two-point functions of CLE$_4$ gaskets'] Let $\widetilde F_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}$ denote the event that at least two different odd CLE$_4$ gaskets of the family of CLE$_4$ gaskets constructed in Theorem (thm:twopointAT of the paper) intersect both 
$\mathbb{D}(z_1, \varepsilon_1)$ and $\mathbb{D}(z_2, \varepsilon_2)$. Then
\begin{itemize}
    \item Let $E_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}^{\rm{odd},k}(z_1,z_2)$ denote the event that the $k$-th odd nested CLE$_4$ gasket intersects 
    $\mathbb{D}(z_1,\varepsilon_1)$ and $\mathbb{D}(z_2,\varepsilon_2)$. Then there is a constant $C > 0$
    such that for all $k \geq 1$,
    $$\mathbb{P}(\widetilde F_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2} \cap E_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}^{\rm{odd},k}(z_1,z_2)) \leq C(\varepsilon_1\varepsilon_2)^{1/4}\left(\mathbb{P}(E_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}^{\rm{odd},k}) + \1_{k \geq 2}\mathbb{P}(E_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}^{\rm{odd},k-1})\right).$$
    \item Further, for some $\widetilde C > 0$, 
    for all $\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2 > 0$ sufficiently small, 
$$\sum_{k \geq 1}\mathbb{P}(E^{\rm{odd},k}_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}(z_1,z_2)) < \widetilde C\mathbb{P}(E_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}^{\rm odd}(z_1,z_2)).$$
    \item In particular, $\mathbb{P}(\widetilde F_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2})$ is bounded by $C(\varepsilon_1\varepsilon_2)^{1/4}\mathbb{P}(E_{\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2}^{\rm odd}(z_1, z_2))$ for some $C > 0$ as $\max(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2)\to 0$. 
\end{itemize}
Further, the same holds when we replace odd by even everywhere. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem:nointersectAT of arXiv:2604.15146

PROOF (UNAUDITED); novelty unverified. Let d=r+k, r>=0, k>=1, n>=1, and let X_i be iid real d-dimensional feature rows with uncentered second moment G=E[XX^T] positive definite and kappa=E[(X^TG^(-1)X)^2]<infinity. Let S=n^(-1)sum_i X_iX_i^T and B(M)=C-D^TA^+D for the first-r/last-k partition M=[[A,D],[D^T,C]], or B(M)=M if r=0. Then E||B(G)^(-1/2)B(S)B(G)^(-1/2)-I_k||op^2 <=(kappa-d)/n, including singular S. For k=1, E[(sqrt(B(S)/B(G))-1)^2]<=(kappa-d)/n as well. The mixture with conditional centered Gaussian covariance B(S) admits a coupling to N(0,B(G)) with squared cost <=tr(B(G))(kappa-d)/n. A uniform bound on kappa is an additional hypothesis. Conditional use requires conditionally iid rows and retains E[tr(B(G))(kappa-d)]/n without factoring it. This is a local covariance-step lemma, not a complete Tensor Program length theorem.
n>=1; d=r+k; r>=0; k>=1
Rows iid; G is uncentered positive-definite second moment; kappa finite
Generalized Schur complement uses Moore-Penrose inverse; empirical S may be singular
Conditional version requires conditional iid and retains E[tr(B)(kappa-d)] without factoring

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:508933338764b01c7c4d1c5df7ac72e621ab385aa0a5e762dff0ec85982252a0","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/50/508933338764b01c7c4d1c5df7ac72e621ab385aa0a5e762dff0ec85982252a0.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:a3ae660870fdea8f35c824f25dc15528839b10e28ddcb8627fdccfcc527d9ad7","bundle_entry_key":"t250_w712_c025","bundle_id":"population.w712-t250-c025-c026-relative-schur-and-rare-features","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability and Gaussian conditioning","draft":"w712/bundle_019.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.neural_networks:relative-schur-sampling-whitened-fourth-moment-gaussian-coupling","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C025 v1: relative Schur sampling bound via whitened fourth moments

Kind: moved (one restricted stochastic covariance step). Target: 4.
Status: proof (unaudited); novelty unverified. Standard Schur monotonicity and sample-moment identities are used, not claimed as new.

## Statement and scope
Let d=r+k with r>=0 and k>=1. Let X_1,...,X_n be iid real d-vectors, n>=1, with positive definite UNCENTERED second-moment matrix G=E[XX^T]. No zero-mean assumption is imposed. Suppose

kappa=E[(X^T G^(-1)X)^2]<infinity.

Set S=n^(-1) sum_i X_i X_i^T. Partition the first r and last k coordinates. Write B(M) for the generalized Schur complement of the first block of a PSD matrix M: if M=[[A,D],[D^T,C]], set B(M)=C-D^T A^+ D. For r=0, B(M)=M. Put B=B(G)>0.

Then, including singular empirical S,

E || B^(-1/2) B(S) B^(-1/2) - I_k ||_op^2 <= (kappa-d)/n.       (1)

There is a coupling, with the correct conditional Gaussian law N(0,B(S)) given S, to an unconditional N(0,B) vector, with expected squared Euclidean cost at most

tr(B) (kappa-d)/n.                                            (2)

After whitening both output vectors by B^(-1/2), the cost is at most k(kappa-d)/n. Thus the W2 distance between the Gaussian covariance mixture E[N(0,B(S))] and N(0,B) is at most sqrt(tr(B)(kappa-d)/n). Constants do not explicitly involve lambda_min(G); the distribution-dependent parameter kappa can nevertheless be large.

This addresses the covariance-noise part of source equation (4.9) for an iid feature block only. It does not prove that every reused-weight parent block is iid, control its deviation from the infinite-width population G, control the conditional mean error, or prevent accumulation over program lines. It is not a complete Target 1 or Target 4 theorem. Prior literature/novelty and independent review remain open.

## 1. Deterministic relative Schur stability
For a PSD block matrix M and every v in R^k,

v^T B(M) v = inf_{u in R^r} (u,v)^T M (u,v).                  (3)

This is the usual variational characterization of the generalized Schur complement. To see the singular case directly, PSD implies each column of D lies in range(A): for w in ker(A), positivity of (tw,v)^T M(tw,v) for all real t forces w^T Dv=0. Complete the quadratic square with u+A^+Dv; its infimum is v^T(C-D^TA^+D)v. In particular B is monotone for Loewner order and positively homogeneous on PSD matrices. This is standard matrix algebra, included to fix the rank-deficient convention of source equation (3.1).

Let delta=||G^(-1/2)(S-G)G^(-1/2)||_op, which is finite. Always S<=(1+delta)G. If delta<=1 then S>=(1-delta)G as well. Applying (3) gives

B(S)<=(1+delta)B;
B(S)>=(1-delta)B when delta<=1.

When delta>1, the trivial B(S)>=0 supplies the lower bound needed instead. Hence, for all delta>=0, all eigenvalues of

C_S=B^(-1/2)B(S)B^(-1/2)

lie in [max(0,1-delta),1+delta]. Therefore

||C_S-I||_op<=delta,
||sqrt(C_S)-I||_op<=delta.                                  (4)

The latter follows from |sqrt(t)-1|=|t-1|/(sqrt(t)+1)<=|t-1| for t>=0. No good-event cutoff, inverse sample Gram, or rank assumption on S is needed.

## 2. Exact sampling identity
Set Y_i=G^(-1/2)X_i, so E[Y_iY_i^T]=I_d. Define E_i=Y_iY_i^T-I_d. They are independent, mean-zero matrix-valued variables with finite second moment. Thus cross inner products have zero expectation and

E || n^(-1) sum_i E_i ||_F^2
= n^(-1) E ||YY^T-I||_F^2
= n^(-1) [E||Y||^4 - 2E||Y||^2+d]
= (kappa-d)/n.                                             (5)

This uses independence of distinct iid rows, not independence of a Gram matrix and its Schur complement. Since operator norm is at most Frobenius norm, (4)-(5) prove (1). Cauchy-Schwarz gives kappa>=d^2, so the displayed nonnegative bound is consistent even for n<d.

## 3. Conditional Gaussian coupling
Take Z~N(0,I_k) independent of the whole sample, and define

U=B^(1/2) sqrt(C_S) Z,    V=B^(1/2) Z.

Given S, U is centered Gaussian with covariance B^(1/2) C_S B^(1/2)=B(S), and V has the fixed target covariance B. The factor for U need not be the symmetric square root of B(S); it gives the correct conditional Gaussian law. Conditional expected squared distance equals

tr[B (sqrt(C_S)-I)^2] <= tr(B) delta^2,

using (4) and PSD trace monotonicity. Equation (5) proves (2). Whitening U and V yields sqrt(C_S)Z and Z, with cost <=k E delta^2. Taking infima gives the W2 conclusions. No assumption that B commutes with C_S is used.

## 4. Conditional version and dependence warning
The same proof applies conditionally on a sigma-field F if the rows are conditionally iid, G=E[XX^T|F] is positive definite almost surely, and kappa=E[(X^TG^(-1)X)^2|F] is finite. With an independent fresh Gaussian Z, the conditional cost is <=tr(B)(kappa-d)/n. Its unconditional expectation is

E[tr(B)(kappa-d)]/n,

provided this is finite. It is NOT replaced by a product of expectations without an additional justification. Past-measurable mean errors can be added to U and V; the mean/noise cross term then vanishes by the centered fresh Z, not by assuming means and covariance errors are independent.

## 5. Checks, literature status, and unpaid source hypotheses
For Gaussian X~N(0,G), the usual Gaussian fourth moments give kappa=d(d+2), so (2) is tr(B)d(d+1)/n regardless of conditioning of G. This is only a simple corollary and is not claimed to improve the classical Wishart Schur-complement distribution.

The full source proof still needs a bound on whitened moments for its actual nonlinear parent-feature blocks, an appropriate conditional-iid/martingale replacement where rows are dependent, population-kernel transport, mean stability, and accumulation over lines. Merely bounding coordinate fourth moments or marginal kernel variances does not supply a bound on kappa. A separate rare-feature construction tests that missing implication.

[Theorem 30 (Ma--Qing) of arXiv:2609.02267, 'Locally Conformally Flat Manifolds with Positive Scalar Curvature: Kleinian Groups, Moduli'] Let \((M^n,\bar g)\), \(n\geq3\), be a complete Riemannian manifold, and let \(S\subset M\) be compact. Let \(D\subset M\) be a bounded open neighborhood of \(S\). Suppose that
\(g=u^{\frac{4}{n-2}}\bar g\) is a conformal metric on \(D\setminus S\) that is geodesically complete near \(S\). If the scalar curvature of \(g\) is nonnegative, then
\[
\dim_{\mathcal{H}}^{\bar g}(S) \le \frac{n-2}{2}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:plurality of arXiv:2608.20480, 'When Clean Data Hurts: Learning with Monotone \\ Corruptions Beyond Binary Classification'] Assume that the adversary adds at most $b$ examples. Put $r=4b+1$ and
$t=\lfloor(n+b)/r\rfloor$. After padding to the declared final length with
correctly labeled duplicates, select $rt$ positions uniformly if necessary,
partition them randomly into $r$ groups of size $t$, run an ordinary improper
learner on every group, and output their pointwise plurality. Then
\[
    R^{\mathrm{imp}}_{\mathrm{ad},b}(n;\mathcal{H})
    <
    4 \, R^{\mathrm{imp}}_{\mathrm{iid}}(t;\mathcal{H}).
\]
Consequently, if $d_{\mathrm{DS}}(\mathcal{H})=d$, then
$R^{\mathrm{imp}}_{\mathrm{ad},b}(n;\mathcal{H})=O(d(b+1)/(n+b))$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Partition and plurality

body: [LITERATURE CHECK 09-08 10:1x, answering his novelty question] Read Solomyak's survey directly. CONFIRMED: 2/3 is open and the survey states verbatim that the only known singular parameters are reciprocals of Pisot numbers, so this session's control-set hole is real. Salem 1944 already gives muhat -> 0 at any non-Pisot parameter, so all our work concerns the RATE. Solomyak Thm 2.7(i) gives an L^2 density for a.e. lambda in (1/2, 2^-1/2), an interval CONTAINING 2/3 - so the L^2 route is the classical route and 2/3 is simply not covered as an individual point. Garsia does not apply since 3/2 is not an algebraic integer. Transversality is the named crucial idea behind the a.e. results, so our finding that Erdos-Kahane collapses at fixed lambda because transversality fails is the expected reason, not a discovery. HONEST VERDICT: no theorem; the reformulations are the subject's standard instruments; the one plausibly novel item is the parity obstruction (any relaxation dropping parity returns the trivial bound identically), which is a negative result about a criterion we built and still needs checking against the computer-assisted-bounds literature

 \leqslant  \frac{c_{\delta,s}}{ n^{ \frac{\delta}{2} - (2+\delta) s} },

[Corollary cor:tailrl-binary-recovery of arXiv:2609.02987, 'Tail Likelihood Reinforcement Learning'] Suppose $r_i\in\{0,1\}$ and let
$M:=\sum_{i=1}^N\mathbbm{1}\{r_i=1\}$. If $M>0$, then every successful
rollout receives weight $1/M$ and every unsuccessful rollout receives weight
zero. Hence the uncentered TailRL{} estimator reduces to
\begin{equation}
g_{\mathrm{TailRL}}^{(N)}(x)
=
\frac{1}{M}
\sum_{i:r_i=1}S_i,

\end{equation}
which is the MaxRL estimator. After mean-centering, successful rollouts have
weight $1/M-1/N$ and unsuccessful rollouts have weight $-1/N$. If $M=0$,
all uncentered and centered weights are zero.

[Dfn 23 (Exact lumpability and exact lumping) of arXiv:2604.12853, 'Coupling Markov Chains \\with a Common Image Chain'] Let $f:A \twoheadrightarrow B$ be a surjection between countable sets. 
    We say that $P\in\SM(A)$ is \textbf{exactly lumpable} under $f$ with respect to $(\nu_z)_{z \in B}$ if $\nu_z \in \PM(f^{-1}(z))$ for each $z \in B$ and there exists $Q \in \SM(B)$ such that for every $z,z' \in B$ and every $x' \in f^{-1}(z')$, the \emph{exact lumping equation} holds:
    \begin{equation}
    
        \sum_{x\in f^{-1}(z)} \nu_z(x) P(x,x')  = Q(z,z') \nu_{z'}(x')\,.   
    \end{equation}
    We say $P$ is exactly lumpable under $f$ to $Q$ if such a family $(\nu_b)_{b \in B}$ exists for which \eqref{eq: EL discrete} holds. 
    
    For $\upalpha \in \PM(A)$, we say that
    $\MC(\upalpha,P)$ \textbf{lumps exactly} under $f$ to the chain $\MC(f_*(\upalpha),Q)$
    if there exists a family $(\nu_z)_{z\in B}$ and a matrix $Q$, that together satisfy equation~\eqref{eq: EL discrete}, such that $\upalpha$ is a convex combination of the measures $(\nu_z)_{z \in B}$.
title: Exact lumpability and exact lumping
