body:
[Lemma le:bounds-W-l-one-step of arXiv:2411.06195, 'Restrictions of some reinforced processes to subgraphs'] \mbox{}\\
  Consider the setup of Theorem (thm:from-r-to-l of the paper). 
  For $l\in\{1,\ldots,r\}$, $\bar e\in E_{l-1}$, and $e'\in E_l$, 
  we have
  \begin{align}
    
    &{\mathbb E}[(W^{(l-1)}_{\bar e})^\alpha]\le 2^{-\alpha}{\mathbb E}[(W^{(l)}_{e'})^\alpha]
      \quad\text{for }\alpha\in[0,1],\\
    
&{\mathbb E}[(W^{(l-1)}_{\bar e})^\alpha]\le C_\alpha {\mathbb E}[(W^{(l)}_{e'})^\alpha]^2
      \quad\text{for }\alpha\in[0,\tfrac12),\\
    
    &{\mathbb E}[\log W^{(l-1)}_{\bar e}]\le\min\{{\mathbb E}[\log W^{(l)}_{e'}]-\log 2,2{\mathbb E}[\log W^{(l)}_{e'}]+{c_2}\}
  \end{align}
  with the constants $C_\alpha$ and ${c_2}$ from Theorem (thm:from-r-to-l of the paper).
  For $\alpha\in[0,\frac12)$,
  the bound  in (equation eq:bound-exp-w-l-alpha of the paper) is stronger than
  the bound in (equation eq:bound2-exp-w-l-alpha of the paper) if and only if
  ${\mathbb E}[(W^{(l)}_{e'})^\alpha]>2^{-\alpha}C_\alpha^{-1}$.
  Similarly, the minimum in bound (equation eq:bound2-exp-w-l-log of the paper) equals
  ${\mathbb E}[\log W^{(l)}_{e'}]-\log 2$ if and only if
  ${\mathbb E}[\log W^{(l)}_{e'}]\ge -\log 2-{c_2}$.
  Note that the expectations do not depend on the choice of $\bar e$ and
  $e'$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Lemma lem:intersections_times of arXiv:2411.13133, 'Connectivity of the adjacency graph of\\ complementary components of the $\SLE$ Fan'] Fix $\kappa \in (0,4)$ and let $h$ be a whole-plane GFF with values modulo a global multiple of $2\pi\chi$. Fix $\delta, p \in (0,1)$. Then,  there exists $\theta_0 \in (0,1)$ depending only on $\kappa , \delta$ an $p$ such that the following holds with probability at least $1 - p$ for any fixed $\theta \in (0, \theta_0)$. Let F be C, R or Q, r >= 3 an integer and 0 < eps <= 1, and let xi be uniform on {-1,1}^n. (Thm 1.1) There is C = C(r, eps) such that: if f in F[x_1,...,x_n] is a quadratic polynomial all of whose coefficients have absolute value <= 1 and sup_x P(f(xi) = x) >= C (log n)^{r/2} / n^{1 - 2/(r+2)}, then there is a quadratic form h of rank < r such that the sum of the absolute values of the coefficients of f - h is at most eps n^2. (Thm 1.2) If instead the degree-2 coefficients of f lie in a fixed finite set S (C = C(r, eps, S)), the same hypothesis gives h of rank < r differing from f in at most eps n^2 coefficients. With r = 3: point probabilities much larger than n^{-3/5} force f to be close to a form of rank <= 2, which over C splits into two linear factors.

Assumes: Rademacher variables; coefficients bounded by 1 (Thm 1.1) or taken from a finite set (Thm 1.2)

body:
[Prop 31 ({\cite[Proposition~3.8) of arXiv:2609.01389, 'K-stability and birational rigidity of Fano 3-fold weighted complete intersections'] {CO}}]

With the notation and assumptions as above, let $\msp \in Z \subset Y \subset X$ be a flag of type $\mathrm{IIa}$.
Then,
\[
\delta_{\msp} (X) \ge
\min \left\{ 4 l_Y, \ \frac{1}{S (V_{\bullet, \bullet}^Y; \Gamma)}, \ \frac{1}{r_{\msp} S (W_{\bullet, \bullet, \bullet}^{Y, \Gamma}; \msp)} \right\},
\]
where
\[
\begin{split}
S (V_{\bullet, \bullet}^Y; \Gamma) &= \frac{3}{(A^3)} \int_0^{\frac{1}{l_Y}} \left(\int_0^{\frac{\nu - \mu}{\nu} t (u)} \left( (2 \nu + \lambda - \mu) t (u)^2 - 2 (\nu + \lambda) t (u) v + \lambda v^2 \right) d v \right. \\
& \hspace{3cm} \left.+ \int_{\frac{\nu - \mu}{\nu} t (u)}^{t (u)} \frac{\nu^2 + \lambda \mu}{\mu} (t (u) - v)^2 d v \right) d u, \\
S (W_{\bullet, \bullet, \bullet}^{Y, \Gamma}; \msp) &= \frac{3}{(A^3)} \int_0^{l_Y} \left( \int_0^{\frac{\nu-\mu}{\nu} t (u)} ((\nu+\lambda) t(u) - \lambda v)^2 d v  \right. \\
& \left. \hspace{2cm} + \int_{\frac{\nu-\mu}{\nu} t (u)}^{t(u)} \left( \frac{\nu^2 + \lambda \mu}{\mu} \right)^2 (t(u) - v)^2 d v \right) d u + F_{\msp} (W_{\bullet, \bullet, \bullet}^{Y, \Gamma}),
\end{split}
\]
with $t (u) = (1 - l_Y u)/l_H$ and
\[
F_{\msp} (W_{\bullet, \bullet, \bullet}^{Y, \Gamma}) = \frac{1}{4 l_Y l_H^3 (A^3)} \cdot \frac{\mu(\nu^2 + \lambda \mu)}{\nu^2} \cdot \ord_{\msp} (\Delta|_{\Gamma}).
\]

Author-derived counterexample, independent review pending: let f be majority of three independent bits, mu=Bernoulli(epsilon)^3, nu=Bernoulli(1-epsilon)^3 with 0<epsilon<1/2. Each endpoint exterior makes a cell section nonconstant with probability 2 epsilon(1-epsilon), and each cell TV is 1-2 epsilon. Substituting endpoint sensitivities into a telescoping bound would give 6 epsilon(1-epsilon)(1-2 epsilon), tending to zero, whereas E_nu f-E_mu f=1-6 epsilon^2+4 epsilon^3 tends to one. For replacement order 1,2,3, the actual hybrid sensitivities are 2 epsilon(1-epsilon), (1-epsilon)^2+epsilon^2, 2 epsilon(1-epsilon); their TV-weighted sum equals the true difference. At epsilon=1/100 the false bound is 14553/250000 and the difference is 249851/250000. The valid inequality with actual hybrid laws is not refuted.

body:
[Definition 17 of arXiv:2609.02105, 'Contact fundamental forms and \\ adjoint varieties'] For $0\le r\le k$, write $\pi^k_r:J^k\to J^r$ for the natural truncation.
By convention, we set $J^r=0$ and $\pi^k_r=0$ when $r<0$.
By Theorem \ref{t.Taylor}, the vector space $J^k_h$ for $h \in \sH$ is equal to the vector space of polynomials of the form   $$ \sum_{|I| = 0}^{ k} c_I \ h^*(xyt)^I $$ with coefficients $c_I \in \C$. Thus an element $\sigma \in \sO(J^k)_h$, namely,  a local section $\sigma$ of the bundle $J^k$ near $h$, can be written as $$ \sigma(g) =  \sum_{|I| = 0}^{k} \sigma_I(g) \ g^*(xyt)^I $$ for  $\sigma_I \in \sO_{\sH, h}$, which we write simply as $$ \sigma =  \sum_{|I| = 0}^{k} \sigma_I  \ g^*(xyt)^I.$$ For each $1 \leq a \leq m$, define the differential operator $D_{X_a}$ (resp. $D_{Y_a}$)  that sends $\sigma \in \sO(J^k)_h$ to an element of  $\sO(J^{k-1})_h$ as follows. 
\begin{eqnarray*} 
D_{X_a} \sigma & := & \sum_{|I|=0}^{k-1} (X_a \sigma_I - (i_a +1) \sigma_{I^{+a}} - \frac{p+1}{2} \sigma_{I_{-a}}) g^*(xyt)^I \\
D_{Y_a} \sigma & := & \sum_{|I|=0}^{k-1} (Y_a \sigma_I - (j_a +1) \sigma_{I_{+a}} + \frac{p+1}{2} \sigma_{I^{-a}}) g^*(xyt)^I.
\end{eqnarray*}
Also define the differential operator $D_{T}$  that sends  $\sigma \in \sO(J^k)_h$ to an element of  $\sO(J^{k-2})_h$ as follows. 
$$ D_T \sigma \ = \  \sum_{|I|=0}^{k-2} (T \sigma_I - (p+1) \sigma_{I^{\sharp}}) g^*(xyt)^I.$$

[Proposition 5 of arXiv:2608.05931, 'Effective Lagrangian regularity and the uniqueness threshold for random H\"older velocity '] Let $u : \T^d \to \R^d$ be such that $u \in C^0(\T^d)$ and $y \in \T^d$. Let $X$ be \textit{any} solution to
\[\begin{cases}
    \dot X_t = u(X_t),\\
    X_0 = y,
\end{cases}\]
and $\iop u(t,x) := \int_0^t u(x+X_s)\,ds$. Then, if $\iop u \in C^\gamma([0,1], C^1(\T^d))$ for some $\gamma>1/2$, $X$ is the \textit{unique} solution to the above ODE. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 5 of arXiv:2608.05931

body:
[Theorem 3 (Small-time annealed path LDP) of arXiv:2608.26834, 'Small-time annealed large deviations principle for one-dimensional diffusions in a random '] Assume hypotheses $H_1$--$H_4$ hold. Under $P_0^{\ann}$, the family $X_\varepsilon=(X_{\varepsilon}(t))_{0\le t\le1}$ satisfies a large deviation principle on $C_0([0,1];\R)$ with speed $\varepsilon^{-1}$ and the good rate function $I$ given in \eqref{eq:rate-function}. Equivalently, for every open set $G\subset C_0([0,1];\R)$ and every closed set $F\subset C_0([0,1];\R)$,
		\begin{align}
			\liminf_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\varepsilon\log P_0^{\ann}(X_\varepsilon\in G)
			&\ge -\inf_{\varphi\in G}I(\varphi),\\
			\limsup_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\varepsilon\log P_0^{\ann}(X_\varepsilon\in F)
			&\le -\inf_{\varphi\in F}I(\varphi).
		\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Small-time annealed path LDP

body: [Definition of arXiv:2609.00978, 'Towards Categorical K\"ahler Geometry'] A norm $\|\cdot\|$ on a representation $(E,\rho)$ of $Q$ over $K$, i.e.\ a lift to $\cC(Q)$, is \textbf{harmonic} if $\operatorname{Core}(E,\rho,\|\cdot\|)\in\cC_\star(Q)$ is $\theta^\star$-semistable.\footnote{We use semistability rather than polystability in the definition, since the limiting moment-map equation may degenerate to a semistability condition on the associated graded object.}

body: [Lemma lem:spreadof2 of arXiv:2509.16541, 'Two-stage Bootstrap Percolation'] Fix a big box $B$. Assume that $B$ is successful and that it is connected by a path of successful big boxes to a $2$-ignited successful big box. Then $B$ has the property that the center box of every $q$-box in all four of the crossings of $B$ by good $q$-boxes  will eventually be completely occupied by $2$s. If, in addition, $B$ is centrally successful, then the center boxes in its path guaranteed by (CS1)--(CS2) is also completely occupied by $2$s.

body:
[Cor of arXiv:2608.25065, 'Detection of first homology via random geometric graphs in the thermodynamic regime'] Fix $\lambda \in (0, \infty)$
and let $r = (\lambda/n)^{1/d}$.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item If $\lambda > \lambda_c$,
    then with high probability as $n \to \infty$, the natural map $H_1(\mathcal{C}) \to H_1(M)$ is surjective.
    If $\lambda < \lambda_c$,
    with high probability
    it is the zero map.
    \item If $\lambda > \lambda_c$,
    there exists $1 \le Q' < \infty$
    such that $H_1(M) \cong H_1(\mathcal{C})/H_1^{Q' r|\log r|}(\mathcal{C})$
    with high probability as $n \to \infty$.
    \item For fixed $\lambda < \infty$,
    there exists $q(\lambda) > 0$
    such that, with high probability as $n \to \infty$,
    the natural map
    $H_1(\mathcal{C})/H_1^{qr|\log r|}(\mathcal{C}) \to H_1(M)$
    has nontrivial kernel (in particular, it is not an isomorphism).
    In this case, the natural map
    $H_1(\mathcal{C}) \to H_1(M)$ 
    is also not an isomorphism.\footnote{This last result also follows from Bobrowski [Bobrowski22].}

body:
[Ppn 90 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Recalling \eqref{e:sM.Lip.sym} and Definitions \ref{d:SDE.classification.sym}--\ref{d:measure.classes.sym}, we have
	\[\sM^{\Lip,\sym}(\alpha) \subseteq \sM^{\IAMP,\sym}(\alpha,0)\,.\]

\begin{proof}
Consider any $\mu \in \sM^{\Lip,\sym}(\alpha)$, as defined by \eqref{e:sM.Lip.sym}. 
    By Lemma~\ref{l:control.problems.Lip.to.Lip.sym}, we can find $\tilde\mu \in \sM^{\Lip}(\alpha)$ with $\sym(\tilde\mu) = \mu$.
It was shown in the \hyperlink{p:thm.control.problems.main}{proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:control.problems.main}} that $\sM^{\Lip}(\alpha) = \sM^{\IAMP}(\alpha,0)$, so $\tilde\mu \in \sM^{\IAMP}(\alpha,0)$.
Therefore, for any $\epsilon>0$ we can find $L>0$ and controls 
    \beq
        
        (q_*,b,\sigma,w,p,\zeta,\zeta^\Ising) \in \Adm^{\IAMP}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)
    \eeq
such that (recalling that $\sym$ is a contraction) we have
    \[
        \bbW_2\Big(\mu, \mu^{\sym}(q_*,b,\sigma,p,\zeta)\Big)
        \le\bbW_2\Big(\tilde \mu, \mu(q_*,b,\sigma,p,\zeta)\Big)
         \le \epsilon\,.
    \]
We see from Definitions~\ref{d:SDE.classification} and \ref{d:SDE.classification.sym}
that the sets of controls $\Adm^{\IAMP}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)$ and $\Adm^{\IAMP,\sym}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)$ are in fact identical, so the controls \eqref{e:Lip.general.in.IAMP.sym.controls} belong to $\Adm^{\IAMP,\sym}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)$, and 
    \[
        \mu \in \cB_\epsilon\Big(\cM^{\IAMP,\sym}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)\Big)\,.
    \]
    Since for all $\epsilon > 0$, there exists $L > 0$ so that this holds, we conclude $\mu \in \sM^{\IAMP,\sym}(\alpha,0)$.
    As this holds for all $\mu \in \sM^{\Lip,\sym}(\alpha)$, the claim follows.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Dfn 1. dfn: BTM of arXiv:2412.08236, 'Aging and sub-aging for Bouchaud trap models on resistance metric spaces'] [The Bouchaud trap model] 
  Fix an electrical network $G$.
  Let $\{\xi_{x}^{G}\}_{x \in V_{G}}$ be i.i.d.\ random variables with $\xi_{x}^{G} \stackrel{\mathrm{d}}{=} \xi$.
  Set $\nu_{G} \coloneqq \sum_{x \in V_{G}} \xi_{x}^{G} \delta_{x}$,
  which is a random measure on $V_{G}$.
  Conditional on $\nu_{G}$,
  the (symmetric) Bouchaud trap model (BTM) is defined as the continuous-time Markov chain $X_{G}^{\nu_{G}}$. 
  The random measure $\nu_{G}$ is called a \textit{trap}.

body: Let (M,g) be a Riemannian manifold with curvature tensor R. The Ricci curvature is the symmetric bilinear form Ric obtained by tracing the curvature tensor over one pair of indices: Ric(Y,Z) = trace of the linear map X |-> R(X,Y)Z. For a unit tangent vector v in T_pM, extend v to an orthonormal basis v, e_1,...,e_{n-1} of T_pM; then Ric(v,v) = sum_{i=1}^{n-1} K(sigma_i), where sigma_i is the 2-plane spanned by v and e_i, i.e. Ric(v,v) is (n-1) times the average sectional curvature of the 2-planes containing v. For general (nonzero, not necessarily unit) v, Ric(v,v) = |v|^2 Ric(v/|v|, v/|v|) by homogeneity. A further trace of Ric against the metric gives the scalar curvature.
title: Ricci Curvature

        \[\bar{y}_1 < \bar{y}_2 < \cdots < \bar{y}_N,

Then there are orthonormal systems (e_n) in H and (f_n) in K, indexed by the same set, such that T x = sum_n s_n <x, e_n> f_n for every x in H, the series converging in K; moreover the series converges in operator norm, with ||T - sum_{n <= N} s_n <., e_n> f_n|| = s_{N+1}. Here (e_n) is an orthonormal basis of (ker T)^perp, (f_n) is an orthonormal basis of the closure of ran T, T e_n = s_n f_n, T* f_n = s_n e_n, and |T| x = sum_n s_n <x, e_n> e_n. T is Hilbert-Schmidt iff sum_n s_n^2 < infinity and trace class iff sum_n s_n < infinity.

body:
[Lemma 6 (Aldous meeting-time comparison) of arXiv:2607.13183, '2607.13183'] Let $(X_t)_{t\ge0}$ be a finite irreducible reversible continuous-time chain
with stationary law $\pi$, and write $P^t$ for its transition semigroup. Let
$\tau_{\rm meet}$ be the first time two independent copies of the chain occupy
the same state. Put
\begin{equation}
        t^*_{\rm mix}:=\inf\left\{t\ge0:
        \max_x\|P^t(x,\cdot)-\pi\|_{\TV}\le \frac1{2e}\right\},
\end{equation}
and let
\[
        T_M:=\max_{x,y}\E_{x,y}\tau_{\rm meet} .
\]
If $H_i$ denotes the hitting time of state $i$ by one copy of the chain, then
there is a universal constant $K_A<\infty$ such that
\begin{equation}
        T_M
        \le
        K_A\left(\sum_i
        \frac{\pi_i}{t^*_{\rm mix}\vee \E_\pi H_i}\right)^{-1} .
\end{equation}
It follows that, for continuous-time simple random walk with jump rate $1$ on a
finite connected multigraph $G$,
\begin{equation}
        t_{\rm meet}(G)
        \le K'_A\bigl(\tmix(G)+\Kemeny(G)\bigr)
\end{equation}
for another universal constant $K'_A$.

[Prop 2. prop: atom convergence from simple measure convergence of arXiv:2412.08236, 'Aging and sub-aging for Bouchaud trap models on resistance metric spaces'] Let $\nu, \nu_{1}, \nu_{2}, \cdots$ be simple measures on $S$.
  For each compact subset $K$ of $S$,
  consider the following condition.
  \begin{enumerate} [label = (VC), leftmargin = *]
    \item 
      Write $\{x_{i}\}_{i \in I_{K}} = \At(\nu) \cap K$ for the atoms lying in $K$.
      (NB. $I_{K}$ is a finite set.)
      Then, for all sufficiently large $n$,
      we can write $\At(\nu_{n}) \cap K = \{x_{i}^{(n)} \mid i \in I_{K}\}$ 
      in such a way that $x_{i}^{(n)} \to x_{i}$ for each $i \in I_{K}$.
  \end{enumerate}
  Then, the statements below are equivalent with each other.
  \begin{enumerate} [label = (\roman*)]
    \item 
      The measures $\nu_{n}$ converge to $\nu$ vaguely.
    \item 
      Any compact subset $K$ of $S$ with $\nu(\partial K) = 0$ 
      satisfies (2. prop: characterization of vague convergence of simple measures of the paper).
    \item 
      There exists an increasing sequence $(D_{k})_{k \geq 1}$ of relatively compact open subsets of $S$ 
      such that $\bigcup_{k \geq 1} D_{k} = S$, $\mu(\partial D_{K}) = 0$ for each $k$, 
      and each $\closure(D_{k})$ satisfies (2. prop: characterization of vague convergence of simple measures of the paper).
  \end{enumerate}

$p_1,\ldots,p_{n}$ be arbitrary real polynomials in $r$ variables,
each of total degree at most $d_{\mathrm{pol}}$.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \Bigl\lvert
 \bigl\{
 \left(
  \one_{\{p_1(\bmmu)>0\}},\ldots,
  \one_{\{p_n(\bmmu)>0\}}
 \right):
 \bmmu\in\R^r
 \bigr\}
 \Bigr\rvert
 \le
 \left(\frac{4ed_{\mathrm{pol}}n}{r}\right)^r.
\end{equation}
The list may contain repeated polynomials or the zero polynomial.

body:
[Definition of arXiv:2606.21391, 'Extreme points and faces in the moment problem'] Let $\mathbf{p}\colon X\to\mathbb{R}^d$ and $f\colon X\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be arbitrary maps.
\begin{enumerate}
\item
We say that $f$ is \emph{$\mathbf{p}$-convex} if $f=h\circ\mathbf{p}$ is the composition of $\mathbf{p}$ 
followed by  a convex function $h\colon\mathbb{R}^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]$.

\item
We define the \emph{$\mathbf{p}$-convex envelope} $\env_\mathbf{p} f\colon X\to[-\infty,+\infty]$
of $f$ pointwise by 
\[
\env_\mathbf{p} f(x) := \sup\{h(x): h\leq f, \text{$h$ is $\mathbf{p}$-convex\,}\},
\qquad x\in X.
\]
As before, inequalities of functions are understood pointwise.
\end{enumerate}

[Definition eq:AMF2 of arXiv:2606.13264, 'Interference Queueing Networks: A Replica Mean-Field Approach in the Symmetric Setting'] Let \(p^\star\in[0,1]\) be a solution of the MF2 self-consistency equation: $p^\star=\mathbb P(q^{p^\star}>0)$, and let
\(\nu_{p^\star}\) denote the law of the corresponding Bernoulli random environment.
For \(i\in\{1,\dots,N\}\), define
\[
\overline\mu_i(p^\star)
:=
\mathbb E_{\nu_{p^\star}}\left[
B\log_2\left(
1+
\frac{1}{1+\sum_{m\neq i} T_{i,m} l(d(i,m))}
\right)
\right],
\]
where the random variables \((T_{i,m})_{m\neq i}\) are independent Bernoulli
random variables with parameter \(p^\star\).

The average second mean-field approximation
\[
Q^{\mathrm{AMF2}}=(q_i^{\mathrm{AMF2}})_{i=1}^N
\]
is defined, for each \(i\in\{1,\dots,N\}\), by
\begin{align}
q_i^{\mathrm{AMF2}}(t)
&=
q_i^{\mathrm{AMF2}}(0)
+
A_i[0,t]
-
\int_{\mathbb R_+}\int_0^t
\mathbf 1_{\{q_i^{\mathrm{AMF2}}(z^-)>0\}}
\mathbf 1_{\{u\leq \overline\mu_i(p^\star)\}}
\,D_i(\mathrm du,\mathrm dz).

\end{align}

Method: Polynomial small bias sufficient to fool DNF events exact calculation or structural obstruction Result: For a single conjunction C of k literals, its Fourier coefficients have magnitude2^-k on subsets of those k coordinates. An epsilon-biased distribution therefore changes E C by at most epsilon*(1-2^-k). Inclusion-exclusion for a union of s clauses gives the valid but crude error at most(2^s-1)*epsilon, since each nonempty intersection of consistent clauses is another conjunction. Check: The constant coefficient contributes no expectation difference, while all other coefficients are paired with parity biases of magnitude at most epsilon. Expanding the union into its2^s-1 nonempty clause intersections proves the stated global bound without assuming independence of clauses. Obstruction: To obtain polynomial rather than exponential bias requirements, one needs a substantially more economical approximation or cancellation argument. Small errors for individual clause probabilities do not by themselves control their union.

As $\varepsilon\to 0$, this family converges in law towards

is \textbf{independent} from
$(A,(Z_{j})_{1\leq j\leq n})$,
with an i.i.d. distribution according to the measure
$\hat{\mu}^{\rm loop}_{\text{SLE}_{4}}$.

body:
For piecewise-linear functions realized by two-layer networks in dimension at least 3, kinks supported on distinct hyperplanes cannot cancel each other locally: the realized coefficient of each kink is bounded by twice the Lipschitz constant of the function. Consequently the function class has small metric entropy regardless of how large the parameters are. The principle genuinely fails in dimension 2, where an even cycle of kink circles with alternating coefficients cancels, and it fails for smooth activations, whose discrete-derivative families need unbounded parameters.

[Corollary a7 of arXiv:2411.19926, 'Sparse Pseudospectral Shattering'] Suppose $M\in{\mathbb{C}}^{n\times n}$ satisfies $\left\|M\right\|\le1$. Let
\[
    \delta \ge \exp\left(-n^{1/7}\right), \quad \rho = \frac{\left[\log(n)\log(2/\delta+n)\right]^3}n, \quad
    \chi(n)=\left\lceil \frac{\log(n)}{(2\log\log n +2\log\log(n + 2/\delta)}\right\rceil.
\]
Then
\begin{align}
    \Pr\pare{\kappa_V(M+\delta N_g)\ge\mleft(\frac2\delta+n\mright)^{10\chi(n)}}
    &\le O\pare{n^{-\chi(n)}},\\
    \Pr\pare{\eta(M+\delta N_g)\le\delta\cdot\mleft(\frac2\delta+n\mright)^{-15\chi(n)}}
    &\le O\pare{n^{-\chi(n)}},
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary a7 of arXiv:2411.19926

[Definition 5 of arXiv:2606.10074, ''] Let $x=(\eno x n)\in \{0,1\}^n$.  Let $I$ be a set of consecutive
  integers between 1 and $n$.  If $N_{(\eno x t)}(a)>N_{(\eno x t)}(b)$
  for $t\in I$, then $I$ is called a period in $x$ where $a$ dominates
  $b$, or simply an $a$-period.  On the other hand, if
  $N_{(\eno x t)}(a) = N_{(\eno x t)}(b)$ for $t\in I$, then $I$ is
  called a neutral period (in $x$ for $a$ and $b$).  It is clear that
  \begin{align} 
    N_x(a)>N_x(b)\Iff \text{$n\in$ an $a$-period},\
    N_x(a)=N_x(b)\Iff \text{$n\in$ a neutral period}.
  \end{align}
title: Definition 5 of arXiv:2606.10074

[Lemma NEW-l:spat-mixing-diffusion of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] Under the assumptions of Lemma~(NEW-l:strong-solution-diffusion of the paper), consider
the interacting diffusions $\{M[x]\}_{x \in {\cal X }}$ on the graph $\Psi({\cal X })$ over
the time interval $t \in [0,t_0]$.
For $x\in{\cal X }$, consider a graph 
$\Psi^{[m]}_{x}({\cal X }):=\Psi(\mathfrak{B}_m(x))$  induced by  $\Psi({\cal X })$ on  the ball $\mathfrak{B}_m(x)$ of radius~$m$ centered at~$x$ in~$\Psi({\cal X })$, and consider  
the interacting diffusions $\{M^{\Psi^{[m]}_{x}({\cal X })}[y]\}_{y\in\mathfrak{B}_m(x)}$ over the interval $t\in[0,t_0]$ with the same coefficients $(b,\sigma)$, generated by the same  Brownian motions  and sharing the same initial conditions $M^{\Psi^{[m]}_{x}}(y,0)=M(y)$ as the original diffusion $\{M[x]\}_{x \in {\cal X }}$.
Then there exists a constant $C=C(L,t_0,K_{t_0})<\infty$  (not depending on the graph $\Psi({\cal X })$) such that  
for all $t\in[0,t_0]$
\begin{equation} 
\mathbb{E}  [\| M[x,t] - M^{\Psi^{[m]}_{x}({\cal X })}[x,t] \|^2]\leq 
\frac{C^m}{{m!}}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let H be a Hilbert space. A bounded operator T on H is trace class (nuclear) if it is compact and ||T||_1 := sum_n s_n(T) < infinity. Equivalently: sum_i <|T| e_i, e_i> < infinity for some (hence every) orthonormal basis (e_i), where |T| = (T*T)^{1/2}, and this sum then equals ||T||_1; equivalently, T = AB with A and B Hilbert-Schmidt operators. The trace of a trace-class T is tr T = sum_i <T e_i, e_i>; this series converges absolutely for every orthonormal basis and its sum does not depend on the basis. The trace-class operators S_1(H) form a two-sided ideal of B(H) and a Banach space under ||.||_1, with ||T|| <= ||T||_2 <= ||T||_1; finite-rank operators are ||.||_1-dense in S_1(H); under the pairing (T, B) -> tr(TB), S_1(H) is isometrically the dual of the compact operators K(H) and the predual of B(H). For a positive operator T >= 0 the sum sum_i <T e_i, e_i> in [0, infinity] is basis-independent and is finite exactly when T is trace class; for operators that are not positive, convergence (even absolute convergence) of sum_i <T e_i, e_i> in one basis does not imply trace class.
H is a Hilbert space
T is a bounded linear operator on H

body: Aldous-Fill Open Problem 4.49(ii) fails for every constant. For the cone G = K_1 v H over a connected d-regular graph H on n >= d+2 vertices with second adjacency eigenvalue mu_2: the diameter is Delta = 2; the simple-random-walk spectrum is {1, -1/(d+1)} on functions constant on H plus mu_i/(d+1) otherwise, so tau_2 = (d+1)/(d+1-mu_2); routing every unit flow through the hub gives psi = 2(d+1)(1 - pi_v), where pi_v = (d+1)/(n(d+2)) is the stationary mass of a base vertex, and the LP dual (edge lengths) gives inf psi >= 2(d+1) (r/(r+d)) (1 - (1+B_r)/n) for every r >= 1, where 1 + B_r bounds a ball of radius r-1 in H (B_r = d((d-1)^(r-1) - 1)/(d-2) for d >= 3). So inf psi < 2(d+1) on every finite cone, and inf psi -> 2(d+1) only as n -> infinity. Along Ramanujan families inf psi / (tau_2 Delta) -> d+1-mu_2 >= (sqrt(d-1)-1)^2 + 1, which is unbounded in d; on every finite cone the ratio stays below d+1-mu_2. Here psi is the book's plain congestion (Lemma 4.21), with no path-length weighting. The surviving positive bound is inf psi <= 65 tau_2 Delta log D with D the maximum degree, chained from the book's Lemmas 4.21, 4.13, 4.12 and 4.23.

body: [Lemma 25 of arXiv:2608.21663, '\bf Variance lower bounds for geometric functionals of rotationally invariant log-concave '] Let $R_N=\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ and denote by $K_N$ the convex hull of $R_N$. Let also $i \in \{1,\ldots,m\}$. Assume that exactly one point of $R_N$, say $z_i^j$ lies in $\Delta_i^j, \, j=0,\ldots,d$ and no further point lies in $\widetilde{H}_i$. If $F_i=\conv\{z_i^1,\ldots,z_i^d\}$ and $Q_i=\conv(R_N\setminus\{z_i^0\})$, then \[K_N=Q_i \cup \conv\{z_i^0,F_i\}, \quad Q_i \cap \conv\{z_i^0,F_i\}=F_i. \]

[Cor 2 of arXiv:2605.26669, '2605.26669'] Based on  Theorem \ref{thm1}, we can conclude that the sequence $(Z_n)_{n\ge 0}$, as defined in (\ref{Z-1}), meets the criteria specified in Theorem 4.1 of Shi et al. \cite{S-M}. Consequently, we can derive large deviation inequalities for $(Z_n)_{n\ge 0}$.  Specifically,  for any $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists a positive constant $a$, which is independent of $n$, such that for all sufficiently large $n$, we have
$$
\pp\left(\left|Z_{n+1}-\frac{1}{2}\right|>\varepsilon\right)\le 2 e^{-a n}.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 17 of arXiv:2609.03386, 'Twisted Gradient Flow Approach to Vegetation-Rainfall-Bushfire Interactions Model'] Let any finite time $T>0$ be prescribed and fixed.
There exists a finite time $T_{\text{{\tiny $\delta$}}} \in (0,T]$, which is independent of the approximate parameters $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$ and $\nu \in (0,1)$, 
such that the approximate initial-boundary value problem $\text{(AP)}{}_{\text{{\tiny $\delta,\!\varepsilon,\!\nu$}}}$ admits a strong solution 
$(u,v,w,z):=(u_{\text{{\tiny $\delta,\!\varepsilon,\!\nu$}}},v_{\text{{\tiny $\delta,\!\varepsilon,\!\nu$}}},w_{\text{{\tiny $\delta,\!\varepsilon,\!\nu$}}},
z_{\text{{\tiny $\delta,\!\varepsilon,\!\nu$}}})$ on $[0,T_{\text{{\tiny $\delta$}}}]$ satisfying the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}\leftskip10pt
\item[(1)] $(u,v,z,w) \in (W^{1,2}(0,T_{\text{{\tiny $\delta$}}}\,;L^2(\Omega)) \cap 
L^\infty (0,T_{\text{{\tiny $\delta$}}}\,;H^1(\Omega)) \cap L^2(0,T_{\text{{\tiny $\delta$}}}\,;H^2(\Omega)))^4$.\\[-0.3cm]
\item[(2)] The system \{(\ref{Equation-2-7})--(\ref{Equation-2-10})\} with boundary conditions (\ref{Equation-2-11}) is satisfied in the following variational sense 
for a.e. $t \in (0,T_{\text{{\tiny $\delta$}}})$:

\begin{gather}

u'(t)-D_1 \Delta_N u(t)=\beta_{\text{{\tiny $\delta$}}}(u(t))\{c_1 v(t)-c_2 w(t)\} \quad \mbox{in} \quad L^2(\Omega),\\

M_{\text{{\tiny $\delta,\!z(t)$}}} v'(t)-\nu \Delta_N v(t)+v(t)=M_{\text{{\tiny $\delta,\!z(t)$}}}g_{\text{{\tiny $\delta$}}}(u,v,w\,;t) 
\quad \mbox{in} \quad L^2(\Omega),\\

w'(t)-D_2 \Delta_N w(t)+c_5 w(t)=c_6-c_7 v(t) \beta_{\text{{\tiny $\delta$}}} (w(t)) \quad \mbox{in} \quad L^2(\Omega),\\

z'(t)-\varepsilon \Delta_N z(t)=v'(t) \quad \mbox{in} \quad L^2(\Omega).
\end{gather}

where we define $g_{\text{{\tiny $\delta$}}}(u,v,w):[0,T] \rightarrow L^2(\Omega)$ by

\begin{equation*}
g_{\text{{\tiny $\delta$}}}(u,v,w\,;t):=v(t)\{c_3 \beta_{\text{{\tiny $\delta$}}} (w(t))-c_4 \beta_{\text{{\tiny $\delta$}}} (u(t))\},\quad \forall t \in [0,T].
\end{equation*}

\item[(3)] $(u(0),v(0),z(0),w(0))=(u_0,v_0,z_0,w_0) \quad \text{in} \quad (L^2(\Omega))^4$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

 g_{q,N,R}:=g_{q,N}\mathbf 1_{\{\|n\|_\infty\le R\}},
\]
then
\[
 \|g_{q,N}-g_{q,N,R}\|_2\longrightarrow0,
\]
\[
 \mathcal E_N[g_{q,N}-g_{q,N,R}]\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \mathcal D_N[g_{q,N}-g_{q,N,R}]\longrightarrow0.
\]
The same conclusions hold for every finite linear combination of Gaussian
profiles $g_{q,N}$.

body: [Theorem 3 of arXiv:2511.05218, 'On the Color Discrepancy of Spanning Trees in Random and Randomly Perturbed Graphs'] Let $p=\frac{\log n+\omega(1)}{n}$. Then with high probability, the random graph $G(n,p)$ has the following property: for every 2-edge-coloring of $G$, there exists a spanning tree with a linear number of leaves, in which more than $\frac{1+\varepsilon}{2}n$ of its edges are assigned the same color, for some constant $\varepsilon>0$.

	\]

[Lemma lem:tree-cylinder-square-sum-branching-identity-paper of arXiv:2606.08683, 'Exact Fourier dimensions of dyadic Mandelbrot cascades under minimal integrability'] For every 
\(
m,n\ge0
\),
\begin{equation}
\Sigma_{m+n}
=
\sum_{\lvert u \rvert=m}L_u^2\Sigma^{(u)}_n.
\end{equation}
In particular, 
\[
\Sigma_{n+1}
=
X_0(\varnothing)^2\Sigma^{(0)}_n
+
X_1(\varnothing)^2\Sigma^{(1)}_n.
\]

The descendant square sums \(\Sigma^{(u)}_n\), \(
\lvert u \rvert=m\), are conditionally independent given \(\mathcal F^X_m\), have the same law as \(\Sigma_n\), and are independent of \(\mathcal F^X_m\).

body:
[Corollary cor:uniform of arXiv:2507.16188, 'The noisy voter model with general initial conditions'] Fix $\theta\in(0,1]$ and $q\geq2$. Let $G=(V,E)$ be a connected graph on $n$ vertices satisfying (equation eq:expansion of the paper) for some $\mathfrak{c}_0>0$ and $0<\upalpha<1$, and $\mathcal{U}$ be the uniform distribution on $\{0,\ldots,q-1\}^V$. Then, for every fixed $0<\varepsilon<1$, the $q$-state noisy voter model on $G$ with noise $\theta$ started from~$\mathcal{U}$ has
\begin{equation}
t_\textsc{mix}^{\mathcal{U}}(\varepsilon) = 

\frac{1+o(1)}{4\theta}\log n\,,
\end{equation}
where the $o(1)$-term is $ O\big(\log^{-\upalpha/2} n\big)
$ with a constant 

depending on $\varepsilon,\theta,q,\mathfrak{c}_0,\upalpha$ (but not $G$), and
\begin{equation} t_\textsc{mix}(\varepsilon)=\frac{1+o(1)}{2\theta}\log n\,,\end{equation}
i.e., the asymptotic worst-case mixing time (attained by the monochromatic $\mathsf{x}_0=\bf{1}$) is twice slower.
Moreover, if $G^{(n)}$ is a sequence graphs satisfying (eq:expansion of the paper) for the same $\upalpha,\mathfrak{c}_0$, then for any $\mathsf{x}_0=\mathsf{x}_0^{(n)}$,
\[
\liminf_{n \to \infty}\frac{t_\textsc{mix}^{\mathsf{x}_0}(\varepsilon)}{t_\textsc{mix}^{\mathcal{U}}(\varepsilon)} \geq 1\,,
\]
i.e., asymptotically, no deterministic initial state $\mathsf{x}_0$ is faster than the uniform initial condition $\mathcal{U}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary cor:uniform of arXiv:2507.16188

[Lem 31 of arXiv:2609.00723, 'An integral Hyodo--Kato isomorphism'] For $n\geq0$, let $B_n$ be as above. 
	Then $B_n$ is discrete, $p$-complete and $p$-torsion-free, and Frobenius on
	$B_n/p$ is surjective. Put
	\[
	B_n^\flat:=\varprojlim_{x\mapsto x^p}B_n/p,
	\qquad
	A_n:=W(B_n^\flat).
	\]
	The ring $A_n$ is $p$-complete and $p$-torsion-free, its Frobenius is an
	automorphism, and there is a natural surjective Fontaine map
	\[
	\theta_n:A_n\longrightarrow B_n.
	\]
	The constructions $B_n^\flat$, $A_n$, and $\theta_n$ are functorial in the
	cosimplicial ring $B_\bullet$; the induced maps between the $A_n$ are
	Frobenius-compatible, and $\theta_n$ is compatible with the structural maps
	$W(k)\to A_n$ and $W(k)\to B_n$.

[Lemma 3 (Measurability in the subspace variable) of arXiv:2606.25204, 'Exponential Rank Bounds for Random Matrices'] Fix \(0\leq d\leq n\), and let \(U\) be an \(\R^n\)-valued random vector.  Then
the map
\[
   V\mapsto \PP\{U\in V\},
   \qquad
   V\in\mathcal S(n,d),
\]
is Borel.  More generally, if \(U_1,\ldots,U_r\) are independent random
vectors in \(\R^n\), then
\[
   V\mapsto \PP\{U_1,\ldots,U_r\in V\}
\]
is Borel on \(\mathcal S(n,d)\).

[Lemma lem:Higgs-quotient-degree of arXiv:2609.00556, 'Higgs--Demailly System and Positivity of Higgs Bundles'] Let
\(
 \pi=\pi^{*_{h_{\rm ref}}}=\pi^2
\)
be the \(h_{\rm ref}\)-orthogonal projection onto a smooth
holomorphic Higgs subbundle \(\mathcal F\subset E\), and put
\(
 q:=\operatorname{Id}_E-\pi.
\)
Identifying the quotient bundle
\(\mathcal Q=E/\mathcal F\) with \(qE\), one has
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
 2\pi\deg\mathcal Q
 &=
 \int_M
 \operatorname{tr}\left(
  q\sqrt{-1}\Lambda_\omega R_{D_{h_{\rm ref}}}
 \right)\omega\\
 &\quad+
 \int_M|\partial^{h_{\rm ref}}\pi|^2\,\omega
 +
 \int_M|[\theta_{h_{\rm ref}}^*,\pi]|^2\,\omega.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}

[Lemma 3 (Anti-diagonal equilibria and stability) of arXiv:2607.22438, 'A deterministic scalar reduction for the phase transition in two interacting urns'] Let \(\alpha>1\). The point \(\left(\frac12,\frac12\right)\) is an equilibrium for every
\(p\in[0,1]\). 
If $0\le p<\frac{\alpha-1}{\alpha}$,
then there is a unique \(u_{\alpha,p}\in[0,1/2)\) satisfying
\begin{equation}
 u=(1-p)h(u)+\frac p2 .
\end{equation}
The corresponding off-center anti-diagonal
equilibria are exactly
\[
 (u_{\alpha,p},1-u_{\alpha,p})\text{ and }
 (1-u_{\alpha,p},u_{\alpha,p}).
\]
If $ p\ge \frac{\alpha-1}{\alpha}$,
there is no off-center equilibrium on the anti-diagonal.

Furthermore, there exists a unique number
\[
 p_{\mathrm{ad},*}=p_{\mathrm{ad},*}(\alpha)
 \in\left(0,\frac{\alpha-1}{\alpha}\right)
\]
such that, for \(0\le p<(\alpha-1)/\alpha\),
\[
 \lambda_+(u_{\alpha,p},1-u_{\alpha,p})
 \begin{cases}
 <0, & \text{if }0\le p<p_{\mathrm{ad},*},\\
 =0, & \text{if }p=p_{\mathrm{ad},*},\\
 >0, & \text{if }p_{\mathrm{ad},*}<p<\dfrac{\alpha-1}{\alpha}.
 \end{cases}
\]
Consequently, the off-center anti-diagonal equilibria are asymptotically stable for
\(0\le p<p_{\mathrm{ad},*}\) and unstable for
\(p_{\mathrm{ad},*}<p<(\alpha-1)/\alpha\).

[Definition 2 of arXiv:2603.28734, 'Free energy analyticity of the disordered XY model and Debye screening in the 2D Coulomb g'] For any $n \geq 0$ and $-t < -s < 0$, define the following coupling events.
\begin{multline*} \mathsf{C}(n,t,s) := \{ R^{\Lambda_{n}, -t, -s}(\alpha^+)_0 = R^{\Lambda_n, -t, -s}(\alpha^-)_0  \} \\ \text{ and }~\mathsf{C}(n,t,\geq s) := \bigcap_{-r \in [-s, 0]} \mathsf{C}(n,t,r), \end{multline*}
and 
\begin{multline*} \lfloor \mathsf{C}(n,t,s) \rfloor_k := \{ \lfloor R^{\Lambda_n(v), -t, -s}(\alpha^+)_0\rfloor_k = \lfloor R^{\Lambda_n(v), -t, -s}(\alpha^-)_0 \rfloor_k  \} \\ \text{ and }~\lfloor\mathsf{C}(n,t,\geq s)\rfloor_k := \bigcap_{-r \in [-s, 0]}  \lfloor\mathsf{C}(n,t,r)\rfloor_k . \end{multline*}

Finally, when $s = 0$, we remove it from the notation \emph{e.g.} we write:
\[  \mathsf{C}(n,t,0) := \mathsf{C}(n,t).  \]

Observe that those events are the ones appearing in Theorem~\ref{thm:cftp}, which explains their name of ``coupling events''.
We will also name their complementary events by replacing $\mathsf{C}$ by $\mathsf{NC}$ (``non-coupling'') for the four events just defined.
title: Definition 2 of arXiv:2603.28734

[Lemma 27 (\cite{BJMP1}, Lemma 3.4) of arXiv:2603.27940, '\Large \bf Stability of supermartingale optimal transport problems'] Let $r\ge1$. Let $\mu,\mu^k\in\mathcal M_r(X)$ and $\nu,\nu^k\in\mathcal M_r(Y)$ have equal masses, and assume that
\[
\pi^k\in\Pi(\mu^k,\nu^k)\ \xrightarrow{AW_1}\ \pi\in\Pi(\mu,\nu).
\]
Let $A\subset X$ be measurable and let $B\supset A$ be open.

\vspace{1mm}

\noindent \rm(i)\,
Let $\gamma^k\in\Pi(\mu^k,\mu)$ be an optimizer in \eqref{eq:AW_def} for $\AW(\pi^k,\pi)$ and set
\[
\tilde\mu^k:=\gamma^k(\cdot\times A),
\qquad
\varepsilon_k:=1-\frac{\tilde\mu^k(X)}{\mu(A)}.
\]
Then $\tilde\mu^k\le \mu^k|_B$ and $\varepsilon_k\ge0$. Moreover, defining
\[
\tilde\pi^k:=\tilde\mu^k\times \pi_x^k,
\]
one has
\[
AW_1\!\big(\tilde\pi^k,\ (1-\varepsilon_k)\,\pi|_{A\times Y}\big)+\varepsilon_k\longrightarrow0.
\]
\noindent \rm(ii)\,
Suppose that $\nu$ is concentrated on some $C\subset Y$.
Let $\tilde\nu^k$ and $\tilde\nu$ be the second marginals of $\tilde\pi^k$ and $\pi|_{A\times Y}$, respectively, and define
\[
\hat\mu^k=\frac{\tilde\nu^k(C)}{\tilde\mu^k(X)}\,\tilde\mu^k,
\qquad
\varepsilon_k':=1-\frac{\tilde\nu^k(C)}{\mu(A)}.
\]
Then there exist $\hat\nu^k\le\nu^k$ and $\hat\pi^k=\hat\mu^k\times\hat\pi_x^k\in\Pi(\hat\mu^k,\hat\nu^k)$
concentrated on $B\times C$ such that
\[
AW_1^r \!\big(\hat\pi^k,\ (1-\varepsilon_k')\,\pi|_{A\times Y}\big)
+\int_X W_r^r(\hat\pi_x^k,\pi_x^k)\,\hat\mu^k(dx)
+\varepsilon_k'\longrightarrow0.
\]
In particular, $1-\varepsilon_k'\le 1-\varepsilon_k$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \cite{BJMP1}, Lemma 3.4

body:
d >= 2
P(tau_e = 0) < p_c
upper tail P(T - E T >= lambda sqrt(||x||_1/log||x||_1)) <= c_1 e^{-c_2 lambda}: requires E[e^{alpha tau_e}] < infinity for some alpha > 0
lower tail P(T - E T <= -lambda sqrt(||x||_1/log||x||_1)) <= c_1 e^{-c_2 lambda}: requires only E[tau_e^2 (log tau_e)_+] < infinity
||x||_1 > 1, lambda >= 0

THE ASYMMETRY IS THE POINT: the lower-tail condition is strictly weaker than the upper-tail condition. A statement that gives both tails under one hypothesis has merged two theorems.
WHAT IT FEEDS: this is the source of exponential decay at chi = 1/2 + delta for every delta > 0, which is what the survey's own sketch uses to reach the wandering bound xi_x <= 3/4 in a direction of curvature (an alternative route to Newman-Piza's original one, which went through Kesten's and Alexander's chi' <= 1/2).
HISTORY: the first such exponential inequality was not for general distributions, only for the nearly-Gamma class.
OPEN, per the survey: whether the sqrt(||x||/log||x||) scale on the right side is optimal.
SOURCE: Damron, M., Hanson, J. and Sosoe, P., 'Subdiffusive concentration in first-passage percolation', arXiv:1401.0917. Read in Auffinger-Damron-Hanson, '50 years of first passage percolation', arXiv:1511.03262v2 (AMS University Lecture Series 68, 2017), theorem 'thm: subdiffusive', tex lines 1512-1528.
VERIFICATION STATUS: survey-claim. Lane P4 did not read arXiv:1401.0917.
title: Damron-Hanson-Sosoe subdiffusive concentration: for d >= 2 with P(tau_e = 0) < p_c, the passage time concentrates EXPONENTIALLY on the scale sqrt(||x||_1 / log ||x||_1), and the two tails need DIFFERENT hypotheses - the upper tail needs an exponential moment E[e^{alpha tau_e}] < infinity for some alpha > 0, while the lower tail needs only E[tau_e^2 (log tau_e)_+] < infinity. These are exponential, not Gaussian, inequalities.

[Theorem thm:mspacings of arXiv:2606.23547, 'The location of the largest exponential spacing and Euler’s generalized pentagonal numbers'] Let $m\geq 1$ be fixed. With probability one, there exists a unique random index
\[
R^{(m)} := \operatorname*{arg\,max}_{r\geq 1} Z_r^{(m)}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
R_n^{(m)} \stackrel{{\cal D}}{\longrightarrow} R^{(m)} \qquad\text{as } n\to\infty.
\]
The limiting distribution has full support on the positive integers. More
precisely, if
\[
q_r^{(m)} := \mathbb{P}\bigl(R^{(m)}=r\bigr), \qquad r\geq 1,
\]
then
\[
q_r^{(m)}>0 \quad\text{for every }r\geq 1, \qquad \sum_{r=1}^{\infty}q_r^{(m)}=1.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem of arXiv:2512.09308, 'On asymptotic behavior of solutions to random fractional Riesz-Bessel equations with cycli'] Let $u(t,x)$, $t > 0$, $x \in \mathbb{R}$, be the random field defined by equations~{\rm ((modch5 of the paper))} and~{\rm((modCch5 of the paper))} with the random initial condition $\xi(x),$ which covariance function satisfies Assumption~~{\rm (assumption 2ch5 of the paper)} with $A_0\neq0$. Then, for $\alpha>\kappa_0/2$, if $\varepsilon \to 0$, the finite-dimentional distributions of the random fields
\[
U^{(L)}_\varepsilon(t,x) = \frac{\varepsilon^{-\frac{\kappa_0\beta}{2\alpha}}}{L_{0}\left({\varepsilon^{-\beta/\alpha}}\right)}u\left( \frac{t}{\varepsilon}, \frac{x}{\varepsilon^{\beta/\alpha}} \right), \, t>0, \ x\in \mathbb{R},
\]
converge weakly to the finite-dimensional distributions of the zero-mean Gaussian field
\begin{equation*}
    U_0(t,x) = \sqrt{c_{2}(\kappa_0)A_{0}}\int_{\mathbb{R}} \frac{e^{i \lambda x} E_\beta(-\mu|\lambda|^\alpha t^\beta)}{|\lambda|^{(1-\kappa_0)/2}}W(d\lambda), \,
\end{equation*}

Load-bearing hypothesis: local solvability of F(Du,u,x) = 0 with u = g on Γ requires D_pF(p0,z0,x0)·ν(x0) ≠ 0, i.e. the characteristic direction must be transversal to the data surface; and the initial triple must be admissible (the tangential derivatives of g must match p0). If the surface is characteristic, existence can fail outright and uniqueness can fail catastrophically. Counterexample: the equation u_x = 0 in R^2 (F(p,z,x) = p_1, so D_pF = (1,0)) with data on Γ = { y = 0 }, whose normal is ν = (0,1): D_pF·ν = 0, so Γ is characteristic — indeed the characteristics are the horizontal lines y = const, which lie IN Γ. Every C^1 solution satisfies u(x,y) = u(0,y), so u(·,0) must be constant: if g is not constant there is NO solution in any neighbourhood of a point of Γ; if g ≡ c there are infinitely many solutions u(x,y) = h(y) with h ∈ C^1 arbitrary and h(0) = c. The same pathology occurs for u_t + u_x = 0 with data prescribed on the characteristic line { x = t }. Auditor's check: before invoking local existence by characteristics, compute D_pF·ν at the point in question; for quasilinear equations a(x,u)·Du = b this is a(x0,g(x0))·ν(x0) ≠ 0, and for the Cauchy problem u_t + H(x,Du) = 0 on { t = 0 } it is automatic (the coefficient of u_t is 1).
Counterexample: F(p,z,x) = p_1 (equation u_x = 0), Γ = {y=0}
Noncharacteristic condition: D_pF(p0,z0,x0)·ν(x0) ≠ 0
Compatibility (admissibility): F(p0,z0,x0) = 0 and p0 agrees with the tangential gradient of g on Γ
Even when the conditions hold, the conclusion is only local in a neighbourhood of the point

body:
[Theorem 1 (Main theorem) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] Let \(M\) be a closed connected three-manifold which admits a locally
homogeneous metric modeled on one of \(\RR^3\), \(\Nil\), or \(\Sol\), and let
\(g(t)\), \(0\leq t<\infty\), be any immortal Ricci flow on \(M\).  In all
three cases, for every basepoint \(\widetilde m\in\widetilde M\) in the
universal cover, the lifted blowdown flows
\((\widetilde M,\widetilde m,s^{-1}\widetilde g(s\tau))\), \(\tau>0\),
converge as \(s\to\infty\) in the pointed Cheeger--Hamilton sense to a
homogeneous expanding Ricci soliton solution.  The compact
and lifted limits are as follows.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If \(M\) has type \(\RR^3\), then, for every \(m\geq0\), \(g(t)\)
converges exponentially fast in the \(C^m\)-norm of any fixed smooth
background metric, as \(t\to\infty\), to a flat metric on \(M\).
The Gromov--Hausdorff limit of
\((M,t^{-1}g(t))\), as \(t\to\infty\), is a point.
The limit of the lifted blowdown flows is the flat expanding soliton solution
\[
        (\RR^3,0,g_{\mathrm{Euc}}(\tau)),
        \qquad
        g_{\mathrm{Euc}}(\tau)=dx^2+dy^2+dz^2,
        \quad \tau>0.
\]
\item If \(M\) has type \(\Nil\), then the Gromov--Hausdorff limit of
\((M,t^{-1}g(t))\), as \(t\to\infty\), is a point.  The limit of the lifted blowdown flows is the Nil
expanding soliton solution
\[
        \left(\RR^3,0,
        \frac{1}{3\tau^{1/3}}
        \left(dx+\frac12 y\,dz-\frac12 z\,dy\right)^2
        +\tau^{1/3}(dy^2+dz^2)
        \right).
\]
\item If \(M\) has type \(\Sol\), then the Gromov--Hausdorff limit of
\((M,t^{-1}g(t))\), as \(t\to\infty\), is a metric circle or a compact
interval of positive length.  The limit of the lifted blowdown flows is the Sol expanding soliton solution
\[
        \left(\RR^3,0,e^{-2z}dx^2+e^{2z}dy^2+4\tau\,dz^2\right).
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:general-row of arXiv:2606.27073, 'Retention Profiles and KL Contraction Bounds in Finite Markov Chains'] Let $P$ be a Markov kernel on a finite state space $S$ with $|S|\ge2$ and
stationary distribution $\pi$ of full support. Then
\[
  \eta_{\mathrm{KL}}(P)
  \;\ge\;
  \max_{x\in S}
  \frac{D_{\mathrm{KL}}\bigl(P(x,\cdot)\,\|\,\pi\bigr)}{\log\!\bigl(1/\pi(x)\bigr)}.
\]
Equivalently,
$\gamma_{\mathrm{KL}}(P)\le 1-
\max_{x\in S}
\frac{D_{\mathrm{KL}}\bigl(P(x,\cdot)\,\|\,\pi\bigr)}{\log\!\bigl(1/\pi(x)\bigr)}$.

[Proposition 9 of arXiv:2608.27450, 'Koszul duality and Morita categories'] There exists a $2$-precategory $\coMMor_+^{\mathrm{pre}}$ together with an oplax functor $U \colon \coMMor_+^{\mathrm{pre}} \to \pressymstc$ such that for every $2$-precategory $\sY$, composition with $U$ induces an equivalence of spaces
    \[
    \Oplaxunit(\sY, \coMMor_+^{\mathrm{pre}})^{\simeq} \xrightarrow{\sim} \Oplax_+(\sY, \pressymstc)^{\simeq}.
    \]
    Here $\Oplax_+(\sY, \pressymstc) \subseteq \Oplax(\sY, \pressymstc)$ is the full subcategory on those oplax functors $F \colon \sY \to \pressymstc$ for which the coalgebra $F(\id_y)$ is strongly positive for all $y \in \sY$.

body: A monad on a category C is a triple (T, eta, mu) consisting of an endofunctor T: C -> C together with two natural transformations, the unit eta: 1_C => T and the multiplication mu: T T => T (where T T denotes T composed with itself), satisfying two coherence laws. Associativity: mu o T(mu) = mu o mu_T, as natural transformations from T T T to T, meaning it does not matter whether the outer or inner pair of T's is combined by mu first. Unit laws: mu o T(eta) = mu o eta_T = 1_T, as natural transformations from T to T, so the unit acts as a two-sided identity for the multiplication.

[Lem 19 of arXiv:2604.25725, 'What is The Probability That A Random Graph With A Given Degree Sequence is Connected?'] Fix $0<\eps<\frac{1}{100}$.   Assume $H_{i-1}$ is such that  $X_{i-1}+2|E(H_{i-1})|\le 10^6$. Then  for any $(\delta^*+1)$-tuple $(s_1,\dots,s_{\delta^*+1})$, the probability conditioned on $H_{i-1}$ that $v_i$ has $s_j$ neighbours outside $H_{i-1}$ of degree $j$ for each $1\leq j\leq\delta^*+1$  is $O(\prod_{j=1}^{\delta^*+1} (\frac{n_j}{m})^{s_j})$. If $d_i(v_i) \le \delta^*+1$  then the probability that this occurs and $L_i=\ell$ is
    $O( \prod_{j=1}^{\delta^*+1} (\frac{n_j}{m})^{s_j} (\frac{1}{m})^\ell)$.

body:
[Theorem eq:bounded-block-max of arXiv:2607.27613, 'Regularized Bulk Universality versus Bounded-Disorder Nonuniversality\\for Annealed Comple'] \label[theorem]{thm:bounded-block-counterexample}
Fix \(p\ge3\) and an integer \(r\ge2\).  There is a symmetric,
compactly supported probability law \(\mu\) with a \(C^\infty\) density
such that
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2em]
\item \(\mu\) matches the standard Gaussian moments through order \(r\)
(hence is centered and has variance one);
\item for i.i.d.\ ordered-tensor entries with common law \(\mu\), there
is a compact interval \(B\subset(0,\infty)\) for which
\begin{align}
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log
 \mathbb E_\mu\operatorname{Crt}_{N,\max}^J(B)
 &>\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Crt}_{N,\max}^G(B),\\
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log
 \mathbb E_\mu\operatorname{Crt}_N^J(B)
 &>\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Crt}_N^G(B).
\end{align}
The reflected local-minimum inequality holds on \(-B\).
\end{enumerate}
In particular, for every fixed \(\varepsilon\in[0,1/2)\),
\begin{equation}
 \max_{I\in[N]^p}|J_I|\le N^{1/2-\varepsilon}
 \qquad\text{almost surely for all sufficiently large \(N\)}.
\end{equation}
Thus an \(N^{1/2-\varepsilon}\) entrywise cutoff, or even an
 \(N\)-independent entry bound, does not restore universality of the
 unregularized annealed count.  The obstruction in this theorem is a
 coherent block involving on the order of \(N^{1/p}\) coordinates,
 rather than a single quadratic-scale entry. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Bounded-disorder mesoscopic-block counterexample

[Def 3 (Small subgroups) of arXiv:2608.30990, 'Convergence of symmetries: nilpotency, dimension, and perfectness'] Let $\phi_i : G_i \to G$ be a sequence of good approximations with regular neighborhoods $A_i \subset G_i$. We say a sequence of subgroups $H_i \leq G_i$ is \emph{small} or \emph{consists of small subgroups} with respect to the pairs $(\phi_i, A_i)$  if $H_i \subset A_i$ for $i$ large enough, and $ \phi_i (h_i) \to e $ for any sequence $h_i \in H_i . $

    We say the sequence $G_i$  has the \emph{no small subgroup} (NSS) property or \emph{doesn't admit small subgroups} with respect to the pairs $(\phi_i, A_i)$ if any sequence of small subgroups $H_i \leq G_i$ with respect to the pairs $(\phi_i, A_i)$ is eventually trivial.

admits $N$ real roots $[\bs{\La}_N^{+}(\bs{\eta}_N)]_1\, < \, \cdots \, < \, [\bs{\La}_N^{+}(\bs{\eta}_N)]_N $. The map

 \mc{E} \tend \R^N \\

whose coordinates are such that

[Prop rou-inte-agr-ito of arXiv:2412.05698, 'Controlled rough SDEs, pathwise stochastic control and dynamic programming principles'] Suppose that $(Z,Z')$ defined on $[0,T] \times \Omega' \times {\mathscr{C}}^{0,\alpha}_T$ is $ {\mathfrak{C}}^{0,\alpha}_T$-optional, and satisfies $(1)$ $(Z_0, Z'_0)(\ \cdot \ ; \mathbf{W}_0) \in L_q({\mathfrak F}_0;\ensuremath{{\mathbb P}})$; $(2)$ for any $\mathbf{X}=(X,\mathbb{X}) \in {\mathscr{C}}^{0,\alpha}_T,$ $(Z,Z')^{\mathbf{X}}(\cdot):= (Z,Z')(\ \cdot \ ; \mathbf{X}) \in \mathbf{D}^{\gamma,\gamma'}_X L_{p,q}(\Omega')$, where $q \ge p \ge 2,$ 
 \(\gamma,\gamma'\in[0,1]\) such that \(\alpha+\gamma>1/2\) and \(\alpha+\min(\alpha,\gamma)+\gamma'>1\);

 $(3)$ $(Z, Z')$ is $\mathbf{X}$-{\it causal}.\
 
 
 Then for any $t\in[0,T],$ 
\[ 
\int_0^t Z^{\mathbf{W} (\omega'')}_s (\omega') d W_s (\omega'')= \Big(  \int_0^t (Z, Z')^{\mathbf{X}} (\omega') d
   \mathbf{X} \Big)   \Big|_{\mathbf{X} = \mathbf{W} (\omega'')}, \ \ \ensuremath{{\mathbb P}}\text{-a.s.}
\]
where the left-hand side is the It\^o integral.

Let f be n+1 times continuously differentiable on [a,b], and let x_0,...,x_n be n+1 distinct nodes in [a,b]. Let p be the unique polynomial of degree at most n with p(x_i) = f(x_i) for i=0,...,n (the Lagrange interpolating polynomial). Then for every x in [a,b], there exists a point xi, depending on x, in the smallest open interval containing x and all the nodes x_0,...,x_n, such that f(x) - p(x) = ( f^{(n+1)}(xi) / (n+1)! ) * prod_{i=0}^{n} (x - x_i).
f is n+1 times continuously differentiable on [a,b]
x_0,...,x_n are n+1 distinct interpolation nodes in [a,b]
p is the degree-at-most-n polynomial interpolating f at those nodes

body: In mathematical field of combinatorial geometry, the Littlewood–Offord problem is the problem of determining the number of subsums of a set of vectors that fall in a given convex set. More formally, if V is a vector space of dimension d, the problem is to determine, given a finite subset of vectors S and a convex subset A, the number of subsets of S whose summation is in A.

[Proposition 25 (Finite polyhedral Gauss-Bonnet formula) of arXiv:2608.03575, '2608.03575'] Let \(P\) be a finite trivalent hyperbolic polyhedron. Then
\[
    \sum_{f\in F(P)}L_f(P)=4\pi.
\]
Consequently, if \(f\) is chosen uniformly from \(F(P)\), then
\[
    \mathbb E[L_f(P)]
    =
    \frac{4\pi}{|F(P)|}.
\]
Moreover, if \(\rho\) is the corresponding uniformly chosen vertex of
the dual triangulation \(G(P)\), then
\[
    \mathbb E[\deg_{G(P)}(\rho)]
    =
    6-\frac{12}{|F(P)|}.
\]

body: [campaign status: candidate_full_solution - author-checked, unrefereed] Hasebe and Ueda, Large time unimodality for classical and free Brownian motions with initial distributions, ALEA 15 (2018) 353-374, Problem 3.3 asks for the optimal universal C such that mu (free additive convolution) S(0,t) is unimodal for all t >= C D_mu^2 and all compactly supported mu; the paper proves C <= 4 and prints 2 <= C <= 4. Our result (id P0174, 2026-09-08): C = 1, and it is attained. The function F_R(u) = integral d mu(x) / ((x-u)^2 + R^2) has no local minimum of value <= 1/D^2. Reweighting by dQ proportional to ((x-u)^2 + y)^-2 d mu (with y = R^2), two moment inequalities for a centred variable on an interval of length D (a <= D^2/4 and b + 3 a^2 <= D^2 a) combine with the identity 1/F_R(u) = (b + 2 a y + y^2)/(a + y) and a Jensen-derived second-derivative condition (y <= 3a) to give 1/F_R(u) - D^2 <= [(y - 3a)(y + a) + (4a - D^2) y] / (a + y) <= 0. Equality is attained at the symmetric Bernoulli law with u = 0, y = 3 = 3a and 4a = 4 = D^2, where F_R(0) = 1/4 = 1/D^2 is a strict maximum and never a local minimum. Re-deriving the printed Bernoulli threshold in the authors' own frame gives t >= 4 at D_mu = 2, but since the condition reads t >= C D_mu^2 that only forces C >= 1, not the printed 2 - flagged as either the printed constant dividing by D_mu instead of D_mu^2, or a different reading. Verification as the source words it: each step re-derived (the first moment inequality from E[(X-l)(h-X)] >= 0 with centring, the second from (X-X')^4 <= D^2 (X-X')^2 for an independent copy where E(X-X')^4 = 2b + 6a^2 and E(X-X')^2 = 2a give the coefficient 3 exactly, the second-derivative formula F_R''(u)/(2Z) = 3 - 4 y E_Q[1/((X-u)^2+y)] from scratch, and the factorisation, which expands correctly term by term); and because the prior on a refereed paper slipping is that the reader misread it, the Bernoulli threshold was re-derived inside the authors' own frame with their own criterion. Prior art not cleared. mu compactly supported with support diameter D_mu S(0,t) the semicircular law of variance t y = R^2, a and b the second and fourth centred moments under the reweighted law

[Definition def:holonomy-process of arXiv:2608.15923, 'Universality of two-dimensional Markovian holonomy fields'] A holonomy process on the pointed surface $(\Sigma,o)$ with structure group $G$ is a family $H=(H_\ell)_{\ell\in L_o(\Sigma)}$ of $G$-valued random variables on a common probability space such that, almost surely,
\[ \begin{cases}
 H_{1_o}=1_G \\
 \forall \ell_1,\ell_2\in L_o(\Sigma), H_{\ell_1\ell_2}=H_{\ell_1}H_{\ell_2} \\
 \forall \ell\in L_o(\Sigma), H_{\ell^{-1}}=H_\ell^{-1}
\end{cases}.
\]
Equivalently, it is a random element of $\mathrm{Hom}(L_o(\Sigma),G)$ equipped with the cylinder $\sigma$-field generated by the evaluation maps. If ${\mathbb{G}}$ is a topological map in $\Sigma$ containing $o$ as a vertex, a holonomy process on ${\mathbb{G}}$ is defined in the same way with $L_o({\mathbb{G}})$ in place of $L_o(\Sigma)$.
title: Definition def:holonomy-process of arXiv:2608.15923

        \item  For $\kappa \in (4, \kappa_c)$, the adjacency graph for the connected components of $\mathbb{H} \setminus \eta$ is almost surely connected.

        \item  For $\kappa \in (\kappa_c,8)$, the adjacency graph for the connected components of $\mathbb{H} \setminus \eta$ is almost surely disconnected, and moreover, the range of $\eta$ contains a topological Sierpi\'nski carpet. 
            
    \end{enumerate} (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Growth exponent for common subcladograms of random trees structural calculation Result: For the uniform model, sampling consistency gives an exact first-moment count: the expected number of agreeing k-subsets is binom(n,k)/(2k-3)!!. Thus P(C_n>=k) is at most this ratio. Stirling gives log of the ratio=k*[log n-2log k+2-log2]+o(k) when k is of order sqrt n. Consequently the elementary bound stops at order sqrt n, with threshold constant e/sqrt2. Check: The agreement probability is the collision probability of two uniform induced k-cladograms, exactly1/(2k-3)!!. Existence of a common larger subset implies existence of one of size k. The coalescent model has a nonuniform induced law, so its collision probability must instead be sum_T p_T^2; the uniform formula is not transferred to it. Obstruction: First moments overcount many strongly overlapping agreeing subsets. They cannot reach the stronger known exponent bound or prove convergence of log E C_n/log n. The source centroid recursion constructs particular matches and is not automatically optimal.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0215-growth-exponent-for-common-subcladograms-of-random-trees
No independent review
title: Attempt on Growth exponent for common subcladograms of random trees

[Definition def:TASEPcp of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] For each $\alpha>0$ and $d\in \mathbb{N}$, we defined the \textbf{$d$-coupling} of half-space TASEPs with boundary parameter $\alpha$, as follows.

        Take the Poisson process $\Pi$, and view this as a collection of Poisson clocks on $\Lambda_d$. These clocks generate half-space TASEPs as follows.
        Let $\pi:\{(x,a)\in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}\times \mathbb{Z}, x+a\in 2\mathbb{Z}\} \to \Lambda_d$ be the projection map.
        Recall that we can define half-space TASEP as a Markov process $(h_t: t\ge 0)$ on the state space $\SRW_+$ (from (equation eq:defSRW+ of the paper)). 
        We flip $h_t(i) \mapsto h_t(i) + 2$ according to the Poisson clock at the vertex $\pi(i, h_t(i))$. In words, there is a flip $h_{t}(i)= h_{t-}(i)+2$ if and only if the Poisson clock at $\pi(i, h_t(i))$ rings at times $t$, and $h_t(j)=h_{t-}(i)+1$ for $j\in \{i-1, i+1\}\cap \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$.

        By using the same set of Poisson clocks, we get a coupling of half-space TASEPs with boundary parameter $\alpha$, started from all initial configurations and all times.
title: Definition def:TASEPcp of arXiv:2604.10020

body: In real analysis, the Riemann integral is a rigorous definition of the integral of a function on an interval. It defines the integral by approximating the region under the graph of a function by finite sums of areas of vertical rectangles. For suitable functions, including every continuous function on a closed bounded interval, these Riemann sums approach a single limiting value as the partitions of the interval become finer. That limiting value defines the integral, and Riemann sums that are suitably close to the limit can be used as numerical approximations.
title: Riemann integral

[Theorem 16 (Recurrence relations) of arXiv:2608.16752, 'Absorption Probabilities for Random Convex Hulls: Distribution-Freeness via the Wall-Cross'] For every $d\geq 1$, we have
\begin{align*}
N^{\mathrm{Wend}}_{n,d}&=N^{\mathrm{Wend}}_{n-1,d}+N^{\mathrm{Wend}}_{n-1,d-1}, \qquad n\geq d+1,\\
    N^{\mathrm{walk}}_{n,d}&=(2n-1)N^{\mathrm{walk}}_{n-1,d}+N^{\mathrm{walk}}_{n-1,d-1}, \qquad n\geq d+1,\\
    N^{\mathrm{br}}_{n,d}&=(n-1)N^{\mathrm{br}}_{n-1,d}+N^{\mathrm{br}}_{n-1,d-1}, \qquad n\geq d+2.
\end{align*}
For $n\geq1$, we use the boundary conditions
$N^{\mathrm{Wend}}_{n,0}=2^n$, $N^{\mathrm{Wend}}_{n,n} = 0$,  $N^{\mathrm{walk}}_{n,0}=2^n n!$,  $N^{\mathrm{walk}}_{n,n}=0$.
For $n\geq2$, we also set $N^{\mathrm{br}}_{n,0}=n!$,
$N^{\mathrm{br}}_{n,n-1}=0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary 17 of arXiv:2506.11707, 'Fluctuations of two-dimensional determinantal processes associated with Berezin--Toeplitz '] Let $\delta>0$ and, for $j\in\{1,2\}$, let $\chi_j : \C \to[0,1]$ be smooth functions such that 
\[
\1\{V\le \mu-\delta\} \le \chi_2 \le \1\{V\le \mu-\tfrac12\delta\}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\1\{|V- \mu| \le 2\delta\}\le  \chi_1 \le \1\{|V- \mu| \le 3\delta\}.
\]
Let $f : \C \to \R$ be a smooth bounded function, and let ${\rm f}_j:= f \chi_j$ for $j\in\{1,2,3\}$ where \[\chi_3 :=(\chi_1+\chi_2-1)\1\{V<\mu\}.\] 
Then, for every $\alpha>0$,
\[\begin{aligned}
\Upsilon(f;\Pi_N) = \Upsilon({\rm f}_1;\Pi_N)+ \Upsilon({\rm f}_2;\Pi_N) - \Upsilon({\rm f}_3;\Pi_N) + \O(e^{-\alpha \sqrt{N}}). 
\end{aligned}\]
By construction, ${\rm f}_1 ,{\rm f}_3$ are smooth, supported in the bulk $\{V\le \mu-\tfrac12\delta\} $, and ${\rm f}_2$ is smooth, supported in a neighborhood of the boundary $\{|V- \mu| \le 3\delta\}$.
title: Corollary 17 of arXiv:2506.11707

[Lem tens_lb of arXiv:2411.11408, 'Multidimensional specific relative entropy between continuous martingales'] Given two multivariate continuous martingales $M= ( M^1, \dots ,M^l  )$ and $N=( N^1 , \dots , N^l )$, where  $N$ has  independent coordinates, then the specific  relative entropy between $M$ and $N$ is at least equal to the sum of the  specific relative entropy between the coordinate processes:
    \begin{equation*} \textstyle h(\mathcal{L}(M)|\mathcal{L}(N))\geq \sum _{i=1}^l h(\mathcal{L}(M^i)|\mathcal{L}(N^i)).\end{equation*}

Let G have order n>=2 and identity e. For 0<alpha<=1 let P(x,x)=1-alpha and P(x,y)=alpha/(n-1) for y!=x. Start P at e and stop at independent T with P(T=k)=p(1-p)^k, k>=0, 0<p<1. Put b=1-alpha*n/(n-1) and a=p/(1-(1-p)*b). The Metropolis kernel M with proposal P and target Law(X_T) has spectral-gap relaxation time tau(M)=tau(P)*(1+(n-1)*a), where tau(P)=(n-1)/(alpha*n). It is strictly increasing in p. With alpha=p=1/2 both kernels are lazy and tau(M)/[n*tau(P)] tends to 2/3 as n tends to infinity. This family has proposal degree n-1 and does not settle a fixed-degree variant or a differently parametrised monotonicity question.

\E[\xi_1]=0,
\qquad
\E[\xi_1^2]=\sigma^2\in(0,\infty).
\]
Set $S_0:=0$, $S_k:=\sum_{j=1}^k \xi_j$ for $k\ge1$, and define
\[
B_{n,\sigma}(t):=\frac{1}{\sigma\sqrt n}\,S_{\lfloor nt\rfloor},
\qquad t\ge0.
\]
Then, for every $T>0$,
\[
B_{n,\sigma}\big|_{[0,T]} \Rightarrow B
\qquad \text{in } D([0,T],\mathbb{R}),
\]
where $B$ is a standard Brownian motion on $[0,T]$. Moreover,
\[
B_{n,\sigma}\Rightarrow B
\qquad \text{in } D([0,\infty),\mathbb{R}).
\]

[Cor 247 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Assume that $L\ge1$ and that condition \eqref{e:deriv.p.bound} holds. Let $\vX\equiv \vX^N$ be the process defined by \eqref{e:X.decomp}
 and \eqref{e:Delta.X.Ising}, and assume that condition~\eqref{e:w2.coupling.assumption} holds. Then the process $\vX^\trstar$ of Definition~\ref{d:trunc} satisfies
	\[
	\E'\Big[\|\vX(1)-\vX^\trstar(1)\|^2\Big]
	\le O(\epsilon) + o_{\trK}(1)\,,
	\]
uniformly in $N$.

\begin{proof} 
For $\sigma\in\{\RomI,\RomII,\RomIII\}$ we have $X^{\trstar,\sigma}(1,a)=X^\sigma(\tau(a),a)$, with $\tau$ the stopping time defined by \eqref{e:trstar.stopping.time}. It follows that, for $\sigma\in\{\RomI,\RomII,\RomIII\}$, we have
	\[
	\E'\Big[( X^\sigma(1)-X^{\trstar,\sigma}(1))^2\Big]
	\le O(1)
	\E'\bigg[
	\max_{0\le d\le \dmax}
	X^\sigma(q_d)^2;\tau<1\bigg] 
	\le O(\epsilon) +o_{\trK}(1)\,,
	\]
where the last bound is by Proposition~\ref{p:max.X.process.on.trstar.stopped.event}. Similarly,
	\[
	\E'\Big[( X^\Ising(1)-X^{\trstar,\Ising}(1))^2\Big]
	\le O(1)
	\E'\bigg[
	\max_{0\le d\le \dmax}
	X^\Ising(q_d)^2;\tau^\Ising<1\bigg] 
	\le o_{\trK}(1)\,,
	\]
again by Proposition~\ref{p:max.X.process.on.trstar.stopped.event}. The conclusion follows.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:variationalForm of arXiv:2609.03094, 'Discrete Gromov--Wasserstein Duality: Algorithms and Isomorphism Testing'] Any symmetric matrix $\mathrm{M}\in\mathbb R^{k\times k}$ can be decomposed as $\mathrm{M}=\mathrm{B}_1^{\intercal}\mathrm{B}_1-\mathrm{B}_0^{\intercal}\mathrm{B}_0$ for some $\mathrm{B}_0\in\mathbb R^{r_0\times k},\mathrm{B}_1\in\mathbb R^{r_1\times k}$ with $r_0,r_1\leq k$. With this, 
\begin{equation}
    
    \inf_{u\in\mathbb R^{r_0}}\sup_{v\in\mathbb R^{r_1}}\left\{ \frac12\|u\|^2-\frac 12 \|v\|^2+\inf_{x\in\mathcal K}\left\{\left( \mathrm{B}_1^{\intercal}v-\mathrm{B}_0^{\intercal} u \right)^{\intercal}x-\varepsilon\mathsf{H}(x)  \right\} \right\}
\end{equation} is equivalent to (equation eq:entropicQP of the paper)  
in the sense that the optimal values of both problems coincide and  
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*]
    \item If $x^{\star}$ solves (equation eq:entropicQP of the paper), then $(u^{\star},v^{\star})=(\mathrm{B}_0 x^{\star},\mathrm{B}_1 x^{\star})$ solves the outer $\inf$-$\sup$ problem in (equation eq:variationalForm of the paper) and $x^{\star}\in\argmin_{x\in\mathcal K}\left\{\left( \mathrm{B}_1^{\intercal}v^{\star}-\mathrm{B}_0^{\intercal}u^{\star} \right)^{\intercal}x-\varepsilon\mathsf{H}(x)  \right\}$. 
    \item If, conversely, $(u^{\star},v^{\star})$ solves the outer $\inf$-$\sup$ problem in (equation eq:variationalForm of the paper), then there exists  
    $
    \bar x \in \argmin_{x\in\mathcal K}\left\{\left( \mathrm{B}^{\intercal}_1v^{\star}-\mathrm{B}_0^{\intercal} u^{\star} \right)^{\intercal}x-\varepsilon\mathsf{H}(x)  \right\}$ which
    solves (equation eq:entropicQP of the paper) and $(u^{\star},v^{\star})=(\mathrm{B}_0 \bar x, \mathrm{B}_1\bar x)$.  
\end{enumerate} 
Moreover, $\argmax_{v\in\mathbb R^{r_1}}\left\{ \frac12\|u\|^2-\frac 12 \|v\|^2+\inf_{x\in\mathcal K}\left\{\left( \mathrm{B}_1^{\intercal}v-\mathrm{B}_0^{\intercal} u \right)^{\intercal}x-\varepsilon\mathsf{H}(x)  \right\} \right\}\subset \mathrm{B}_1\mathcal K$ for any $u\in \mathbb R^{r_0}$. Thus, the outer $\inf$ and $\sup$ in (equation eq:variationalForm of the paper) can be restricted to $\mathrm{B_0}\mathcal K$ and $\mathrm{B_1}\mathcal K$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm 1 of arXiv:2510.22783, 'Universality of Cutoff for Riffle Shuffling'] Recalling \eqref{eq:def-Dk} and \eqref{eq:def-Vk}, let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\cD_k$ with $\mu(V_k)<1$. 
            Then any sequence of randomized $\mu$-like shuffles undergoes total variation cutoff after $\overline{C}_{\mu}\log N$ steps.
            Equivalently, for any randomized $\mu$-like shuffle with pile sizes $\bX=(\bX^{(t)})_{t\in \mathbb Z^+}$ and any $\varepsilon>0$,
		\begin{align}
			
			\lim_{N\to\infty} d_{\TV}(\bP(\bX,\lfloor(1-\varepsilon)\overline{C}_{\mu}\log(N)\rfloor),\nu_{\Unif})&=1,\\
			
			\lim_{N\to\infty} d_{\TV}(\bP(\bX,\lfloor(1+\varepsilon)\overline{C}_{\mu}\log(N)\rfloor),\nu_{\Unif})&=0.
		\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

$P_n^{\mathcal{L}_\text{inv};\{\theta^{(n)}_j\}_{j=1}^n}$-type Luce distribution with the Sukhatme weights defined in (equation Sukh of the paper)
in the case that the smallest number is  of highest rank.
Then the asymptotically optimal strategy is $\mathcal{S}^\downarrow(n,M_n^*)$, where
\begin{equation}
M_n^*\sim \left(1-(1-\frac1e)^\frac12\right)n\approx0.2049\thinspace n,
\end{equation}
and the corresponding limiting probability of success is
$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}P_n^{\mathcal{L}_\text{inv};\{\theta^{(n)}_j\}_{j=1}^n}(\mathcal{S}^\downarrow(n,M_n^*))=\frac1e.
$$
\noindent ii. Consider the secretary problem for the
$P_n^{\mathcal{L}_\text{inv};\{\theta_j\}_{j=1}^n}$-type Luce distribution with the reverse Sukhatme weights $\theta_j=j,\ j\in[n]$
in the case that the smallest number is  of highest rank.
Then the asymptotically optimal strategy is $\mathcal{S}^\downarrow(n,M_n^*)$, where
\begin{equation}
M_n^*\sim e^{-\frac12}\thinspace n\approx0.6065\thinspace n,
\end{equation}
and the corresponding limiting probability of success is
$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}P_n^{\mathcal{L}_\text{inv};\{\theta_j\}_{j=1}^n}(\mathcal{S}^\downarrow(n,M_n^*))=\frac1e.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Lemma (campaign status: audited-pass): (Lemma 5.1.) For every n >= 4 the real projective matroid on D_n is three-connected. Proof: the n fundamental relations C_i - A - B_i - B_{i+1} = 0 give a dual representation (up to column signs) by t = sum_i e_i, p_i = e_i, q_i = e_i+e_{i+1} in R^n, of rank n. No loops, coloops or singleton one-separations. For a partition (X,Y) with |X|,|Y| >= 2 and t in X, set a = #{i : p_i in X}, b = #{i : q_i in X}; a case analysis on the pinned forest components of the X- and Y-edge systems gives (n-r(X))+(n-r(Y)) <= n-2, i.e. lambda(X) = r(X)+r(Y)-n >= 2. Duality preserves the connectivity function. Notes: This is what makes the counterexample fatal to the three-connected shortcut: the obstruction is NOT produced by a hidden 1- or 2-separation. [Definition defn:no-underrun of arXiv:2601.07045, 'From Continuous to Discrete: \\ a No-U-Turn Sampler for Permutations'] Let $\mathcal{O} = (\sigma \circ \rho^k)_{k = a}^{b}$ be an orbit indexed by
consecutive integers from $a$ to $b$, and let $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$.
We say that $\mathcal{O}$ satisfies the \emph{no--underrun condition},
denoted $\textsc{Stop}(\mathcal{O},\varepsilon,w)$, if
\[
\max \!\left\{ w(\sigma \circ \rho^{a}),\, w(\sigma \circ \rho^{b}) \right\}
\;\le\;
\varepsilon \sum_{\tau \in \mathcal{O}} w(\tau).
\]
Equivalently, the combined weight at the two boundary points of the orbit
accounts for at most an $\varepsilon$ fraction of the total weight accumulated
along $\mathcal{O}$.
title: \textsc{Stop} (no--underrun condition)

For N<=M<=P with M/N->beta, P/N->alpha, 1<=beta<=alpha<infinity, take independent factor arrays U in R^(N by M), V in R^(P by M) with centered iid unit-variance entries and fixed laws with finite fourth moments. Let A=UV^T/sqrt(N) and B be the same product with standard Gaussian factor entries. For every fixed s>0, limsup [I(A;sqrt(s)A+G)-I(B;sqrt(s)B+G)]/(NP)<=0. Neither MI limit is assumed to exist for this limsup comparison. The transposed wedge P<=M<=N follows after deterministic rescaling. This does not assert an unconditional all-SNR MMSE comparison, and other aspect-ratio regions are not covered by this draft application of the cited source theorem.

metadata_json:
{"artifact_digest":"sha256:737c3890c2bdf54eec1eabbbfd6cb9b2a35da54b47da28439cbe0ed5ab8f43e1","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/73/737c3890c2bdf54eec1eabbbfd6cb9b2a35da54b47da28439cbe0ed5ab8f43e1.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:2f3275b96176775d8eb5dc40419f498be81655f87995faf6f4fc0f29ccdd72c9","bundle_entry_key":"iid-product-gaussian-mi-monotone-aspects-w718","bundle_id":"population.t287-finite-moment-and-orbit-comparison-v1","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Gaussian channels and extensive-rank matrix inference","draft":"w718/bundle_001.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.gaussian_channels:iid-product-gaussian-mi-monotone-aspects-w718","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Gaussian factors maximize limiting product mutual information on an aspect-ratio wedge

Target 2, the mutual-information comparison only. Proof draft,
unaudited; novelty is unestablished. This does not prove a formula
for the limiting mutual information, nor an unconditional all-SNR
product-MMSE comparison.

Let N<=M<=P tend to infinity with M/N->beta and P/N->alpha,
where 1<=beta<=alpha<infinity. Let U in R^(N by M) and V in
R^(P by M) be independent arrays with centered iid entries of variance
one, using fixed entry laws with finite fourth moments q_U,q_V.
The laws of U and V may differ. Let B=U_G V_G^T/sqrt(N) use
independent standard Gaussian arrays of the same dimensions, and put
A=UV^T/sqrt(N). Independent standard Gaussian observation noise is G.

The claimed comparison is, for every fixed s>0,

 limsup [ I(A;sqrt(s)A+G)-I(B;sqrt(s)B+G) ]/(NP) <=0.       (1)

Thus whenever both normalized limiting mutual informations exist,
the Gaussian-factor value is at least the value for the iid priors
above. No existence assumption is needed for the limsup difference
statement (1). Transposition and deterministic rescaling give the
corresponding wedge P<=M<=N, with 0<alpha<=beta<=1.

## 1. Primary spectral theorem and exact normalization

N. Alexeev, F. Gotze, A. Tikhomirov, arXiv:1012.2586v2,
Theorem 1.1, PDF pp.1-2, proves convergence of the EXPECTED empirical
distribution of squared singular values of a product of independent
rectangular iid-entry matrices. The source starts with a nondecreasing
dimension chain p_0=n,p_1,...,p_m and assumes n/p_l->y_l in (0,1]
and a Lindeberg condition. We impose N<=M<=P exactly; no extension
to nonmonotone dimension chains is silently used.

Use m=2, p_0=N,p_1=M,p_2=P, X^(1)=U/sqrt(M),
X^(2)=V^T/sqrt(P). The two factors are independent; each has independent
centered entries with the required unit-variance raw variables.
The Lindeberg condition holds for each fixed finite-variance entry law
because the aspect ratios are bounded and
E[|U|^2 1_{|U|>tau sqrt(N)}] tends to zero (and similarly for V).
The limit law depends only on y_1=1/beta,y_2=1/alpha, hence is the
same for the Gaussian factors.

The normalized signal S=A/sqrt(N)=UV^T/N equals
sqrt(MP)/N times X^(1)X^(2). Its expected singular-value law therefore
has a deterministic universal weak limit mu after taking the positive
square root and this deterministic rescaling. The same holds for B.

## 2. Expected spectral convergence implies convergence in probability here

The theorem's expected-measure conclusion alone is insufficient for
the coupling lemma, so the concentration step is needed. View U and V
as N+P independent row blocks. Replacing one row of U changes S in
one row, hence by a rank-one matrix. Replacing one row of V changes
S in one column, again by rank one. In either case SS^T changes by
rank at most two: if D has rank one, (S+D)(S+D)^T-SS^T has column
space contained in the span of the column of D and S times its row.

The rank inequality for Hermitian empirical distribution functions
therefore bounds the change of F_N(x), the normalized empirical
distribution function of SS^T at any fixed x, by 2/N. Efron-Stein gives

    Var F_N(x) <= (N+P)(2/N)^2/2 = 2(N+P)/N^2 ->0.

Combining with the primary theorem at continuity points and using
monotonicity of distribution functions proves weak convergence in
probability of the empirical singular-value measures to mu.

## 3. Second moments, tail control, and W2

Put d=NP and b=M/N. Write

    T_N=||A||_F^2/(NP),   E T_N=b.

The fourth joint cumulant patterns in the dossier give the exact
variance identity

 d^2 Var T_N = d [2b^2+(M/N^2)(q_U q_V-3)]
       +d(P-1)(M/N^2)(q_U-1)
       +d(N-1)(M/N^2)(q_V-1).                           (2)

Terms on distinct rows and distinct columns vanish by independence
of the factor entries used. Under the aspect ratios above, (2) is
O(N^2), so Var T_N=O(N^-2). The empirical singular second moment of
S is

    (1/N)tr SS^T = (P/N) T_N -> alpha beta

in L^2. We must also verify that mu has exactly this moment.
Let C=max(1,|q_U-1|,|q_V-1|,|q_U q_V-3|).
For the trace of (SS^T)^2, the covariance pairings have total count
NP^2+N^2P+NP. Every fourth joint cumulant has absolute value at most
C M/N^2, and there are N^2P^2 summands. Hence

 E[(1/N)tr(SS^T)^2]
 <= b^2(NP^2+N^2P+NP)/N^3 + C M P^2/N^3 = O(1).       (3)

In particular the expected empirical singular second moments have
uniformly vanishing tails, since x^2 1_{x>L}<=x^4/L^2.
Expected weak convergence and (3) imply integral x^2 dmu=alpha beta.
Weak convergence in probability together with convergence of the
second moment now yields W2 convergence in probability to mu.

It remains to upgrade to expectation, as required by the coupling.
Pointwise Jensen gives

    E T_N^2 <= E A_11^4
      =3b^2+(M/N^2)(q_U q_V-3)=O(1).

Consequently the empirical second singular moment has a bounded
second moment. The inequality

    W2(mu_S,mu)^2 <= 2 integral x^2 dmu_S+2 integral x^2 dmu

implies uniform integrability of these squared W2 distances. Their
expectations therefore tend to zero. The Gaussian products satisfy
the same bounds. By the triangle inequality and (u+v)^2<=2u^2+2v^2,

    E W2(mu_{A/sqrt(N)},mu_{B/sqrt(N)})^2 ->0.           (4)

Independent draws of the singular-value vectors suffice in (4);
no unproved alignment or independence between individual singular
values is assumed. The optimal one-dimensional empirical W2 coupling
matches their singular values in the same order.

## 4. Orbit coupling completes the mutual-information inequality

Gaussian products B are bi-orthogonally invariant. Mix A over
independent Haar left and right orthogonal matrices to obtain tilde A.
Couple the ordered singular values as in (4) and use the same Haar
matrices for the two diagonal singular-value representatives. Then

    E||tilde A-B||_F^2/(NP)
      = (N/P) E W2(mu_{A/sqrt(N)},mu_{B/sqrt(N)})^2 ->0.

The finite-size inequalities in orbit_comparison.md give

    [I(A;sqrt(s)A+G)-I(B;sqrt(s)B+G)]/(NP)
       <= sqrt(s) [E||tilde A-B||_F^2/(NP)]^(1/2) ->0.

This proves (1).

For P<=M<=N apply the direct result to VU^T/sqrt(P) and use
A^T=sqrt(P/N) [VU^T/sqrt(P)]. Its channel parameter is s P/N,
which remains bounded and tends to a positive constant. The finite-size
bound just displayed is valid at these varying parameters as well,
so the rescaling does not require uniform convergence of a limiting MI.

## Remaining target

The source theorem is used only on monotone dimension chains.
Other aspect-ratio regions require a broader primary spectral theorem
or a justified reduction. Product-MMSE comparison follows from the
abstract lemma wherever the Gaussian limiting MI exists and is
differentiable; verifying all such hypotheses remains separate work.
The finite-size low-SNR reversal in finite_size_comparison.md is
consistent with (1), since its SNR interval shrinks with dimension.

Least-trusted steps to audit: the entropy/Wasserstein bound in the
abstract lemma; the upgrade from expected spectral convergence to
expected W2 convergence; and the normalization sqrt(MP)/N in the
application of Theorem 1.1. body:
Let d>=1 and m>=1 be integers and D=[-1,1]^d. Suppose the real-valued function f admits the Fourier representation f(x)=integral_R^d exp(i x^T omega) F(f)(omega) domega and v_f,2=integral_R^d ||omega||_1^2 |F(f)(omega)| domega<infinity. Then there exists f_m(x)=b_0+a_0^T x+(v/m)sum_{k=1}^m b_k(a_k^T x-t_k)_+, where b_0=f(0), a_0=grad f(0), 0<=v<=2v_f,2, b_k in [-1,1], ||a_k||_1=1 and 0<=t_k<=1, such that sup_{x in D}|f(x)-f_m(x)|<=C v_f,2 sqrt(d+log m) m^(-1/2-1/d) for universal C. If instead the b_k are restricted to {-1,+1}, the paper supplies the weaker rate C v_f,2 sqrt(d+log m) m^(-1/2-1/(d+2)). The spectral moment uses the squared l1 norm, not the squared Euclidean norm. The affine part is explicit and is not bounded just by the displayed spectral moment. A standard one-hidden-layer ReLU realization can implement the linear term with two more neurons, since a_0^T x=(a_0^T x)_+-(-a_0^T x)_+.
f real-valued with the displayed Fourier representation
finite second absolute Fourier moment using ||omega||_1^2
d,m positive integers and cube [-1,1]^d
continuous output coefficients for the exponent 1/d; sign-only variant has exponent 1/(d+2)
affine correction f(0)+grad f(0)^T x is retained

Source-based draft, unaudited. Let Phi be a real m by n matrix of full rank min(m,n), sigma its smallest singular value, and c>0. A matrix W of the same size has deficiency margin c relative to Phi when ||W-Phi||_F<=sigma-c. Every matrix V of that size with ||V-Phi||_F<=||W-Phi||_F has smallest singular value at least c. This geometric lemma is not itself a convergence theorem and does not require whitened data or a neural-network initialization. Arora, Cohen, Golowich and Hu 1810.02281 use it in their separate whitened-data matrix-layer convergence theorem.
Finite real matrices of identical rectangular shape; Phi full rank min(m,n)
c>0 and ||W-Phi||F<=sigma_min(Phi)-c
