[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Given a sequence of Gaussian random matrices
$$Z_N\in M_N(L^\infty(X))$$
having independent $G_t$ variables as entries, for some fixed $t>0$, we have
$$M_k\left(\frac{Z_N}{\sqrt{N}}\right)\simeq t^{|k|/2}|\mathcal{NC}_2(k)|$$
for any colored integer $k=\circ\bullet\bullet\circ\ldots\,$, in the $N\to\infty$ limit.

body:
[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The orthogonal polynomials for $L^2[-1,1]$, with measure
$$d\mu(x)=(1-x)^a(1+x)^bdx$$
called Jacobi polynomials, satisfy as well a degree $2$ equation, namely
$$(1-x^2)P_k''(x)+(b-a-(a+b+2)x)P_k'(x)+k(k+a+b+1)P_k(x)=0$$
as well as an order $2$ recurrence relation, and are given by the following formula:
$$P_k(x)=\frac{(-1)^k}{2^kk!}(1-x)^{-a}(1+x)^{-b}\frac{d^k}{dx^k}\left[(1-x)^a(1+x)^b(1-x^2)^k\right]$$
At $a=b=0$ we recover the Legendre polynomials, and at $a=b=\pm\frac{1}{2}$ we recover the Chebycheff polynomials of the first and second kind, from trigonometry.

[Definition def:backoff of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix a send sequence
$\newsym{p}{send sequence, Def~(def:backoff of the paper)}{\overline{p} = (p_0,p_1,p_2,\ldots)}$  and a birth rate 
$\newsym{lambda}{birth rate, Def~(def:backoff of the paper)}{\lambda}>0$. Each~$p_k$   is  a real number in~$(0,1]$.   $W_k$   denotes~$1/p_k$.
The \emph{backoff process} $X$
with send sequence~$\overline{p}$ and birth rate~$\lambda$ is defined as follows.
For each $i\geq 0$ and $t\geq 1$, 
$\mathbf{b}^X_i(t)$~is the set of balls that  collide exactly $i$ times during steps $1,\ldots,t$. 
The process starts from the empty state, so  
for each~$i\geq 0$, 
$\mathbf{b}^X_i(0) = \emptyset$.
For each $t\geq 1$, $\mathbf{n}^X(t)$ is the set of balls that are born at time~$t$. Its size is given by $n^X(t)$,  which 
is a Poisson random variable with mean~$\lambda$.
After the births, but just
before the sends at step~$t$, the bin populations are defined as follows.
$\mathbf{B}^X_0(t) = \mathbf{n}^X(t) \cup \mathbf{b}^X_0(t-1)$. For every $i\geq 1$, $\mathbf{B}^X_i(t) = \mathbf{b}^X_i(t-1)$.  
For every $i\geq 0$, the set of balls that send from bin~$i$ at time~$t$,  {$\mathbf{s}^X_i(t)$}, is
formed by including each ball from $\mathbf{B}^X_i(t)$ independently with probability~$p_i$.  The
set of balls that escape from bin~$i$ at time~$t$,  $\mathbf{e}^X_i(t)$, is equal to $\mathbf{s}^X_i(t)$ if 
$|\mathbf{s}_i^X(t)| = |\cup_{k\geq 0} \mathbf{s}_k^X(t)| = 1$. Otherwise,
$\mathbf{e}^X_i(t) =  \emptyset$.
Finally, $\mathbf{b}_0^X(t) = \mathbf{B}_0^X(t) \setminus \mathbf{s}_0^X(t)$ and for all  $i\geq 1$,
$\mathbf{b}_i^X(t) = (\mathbf{B}_i^X(t) \setminus \mathbf{s}_i^X(t)) \cup (\mathbf{s}^X_{i-1}(t) \setminus \mathbf{e}^X_{i-1}(t))$.
For every variable $\mathbf{b}^X_i(t)$, $\mathbf{B}^X_i(t)$, $\mathbf{s}^X_i(t)$, and $\mathbf{e}^X_i(t)$, the roman (non-bold-face) version represents its size, so, for example, $b^X_i(t) = |\mathbf{b}^X_i(t)|$.
title: Definition def:backoff of arXiv:2602.21315

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2512.02538, 'On the spectral geometry of Liouville quantum gravity'] For a Borel nonnegative function $f:\Sigma \to \R$, if $\mathbf{T}_\Sigma = \inf\{ t\ge 0: Z_t \notin \Sigma\}$,

\mathbf{E}_x[ \int_0^{\mathbf{T}_\Sigma} f(Z_t) \dd t ] = \int_0^\infty g_\Sigma(x,y) f(y) \mu_\ph(\dd y).
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 16 of arXiv:2608.07365, 'A pathwise Ito formula \\for weakly differentiable functions'] Let $\pi=(\pi_n)_{n\geq 1}$ satisfy Assumptions~1 and~2 and let
\[
F\in W^{2+,p}(\mathbb{R}^d)
   \cap W^{2,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)
   \cap W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{1,2}(\mathbb{R}^d),
\qquad 1<p<\infty.
\]
Then, outside a polar set $E$ of starting points, the pathwise integral
constructed in Theorem~\ref{theorem:weakchangeofvar} agrees almost surely with the stochastic
It\^{o} integral, and
\[
\forall x\notin E,\quad 
\mathbb{P}_{x}\left( F(B(t))-F(B(0))
=
\int_0^t \nabla F(B(s))\,dB(s)
+
\frac{1}{2}[\nabla F(B),B]_{\pi}(t)\right)=1
\]
for every $t\in[0,T]$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 16 of arXiv:2608.07365

body:
[Lem holder of arXiv:2606.21049, '\textsc{Locality of rough path lifts}'] Let $H \in (0, 1/2)$ and $\gamma > 1/2 - H$.
Then the continuous inclusion $C^\gamma_0([s,t]) \subset \mathcal{H}_{s,t}$ holds with
\[
\| f \|_{\mathcal{H}_{s,t}} \lesssim_{H, \gamma} \| f \|_{\Hol\gamma} (t-s)^{\gamma + H}.
\]
For $H=1/2$, the same holds for any $\gamma \geq 0$.
title: Lem holder of arXiv:2606.21049

g_i+1:\ifrac{\psi^2}{\u}:

for $i=1,2,3$.

[Lemma l:invertibly-independence of arXiv:2510.13659, 'On the energy image density conjecture of Bouleau and Hirsch'] Let $(X,d,\mu,\mathcal{E},\mathcal{F})$ be an MMD space, also viewed as a   regular, local $2$-Dirichlet space $(X,d,\mu,\mathcal{E}_2, \mathcal{F}_2, \Gamma_2)$ as given in Lemma (lem:df-dirspace of the paper). Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$, and   $\bphi=(\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_n) \in \mathcal{F}^n$. Let $\nu$ be a minimal energy dominant measure for $(X,d,\mu,\mathcal{E},\mathcal{F})$ and let $A$ be a Borel subset of $X$. Then the following are equivalent:
		\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
			\item $\det(\gamma_\nu(\bphi))>0$ for $\mathds{1}_{\{\Tr (\gamma_\nu(\bphi))>0\}}\cdot \nu$-a.e.~$A$.
			\item $\bphi$ is $2$-linearly independent on $A$.
		\end{enumerate}
		Furthermore, $\bphi$ is $2$-linearly independent on the set $I_{\bphi}:=\{x \in X \vert \det(\gamma_\nu(\bphi)(x))>0\}$ and the measures
		$\mathds{1}_{I_{\bphi}} \cdot \nu$ and $\mathds{1}_{I_{\bphi}} \cdot \Lambda_{\bphi}$ are mutually absolutely continuous.
title: Lemma l:invertibly-independence of arXiv:2510.13659

body:
[Corollary 18 ($L^1$ and Wasserstein error estimates) of arXiv:2607.25685, 'Mimicking diffusion processes with differential equations'] Let
\[
  D_r:=2(1+r)\,e^{\|G\|_{L^1}+\|G_\theta\|_{L^1}}
\]
be the trajectory-diameter bound of Step 1. Then for every $\eta>0$,
\begin{equation}
  \big\|Z^\delta(T,\cdot)-Z^\delta_\theta(T,\cdot)\big\|_{L^1(B_r)}
  \le\eta\,|B_r|+D_r\cdot\frac{\mathcal C_p+L_\theta\sqrt{\mathcal E_v}}{\log(1+\eta\,\mathcal E_v^{-1/2})}
  \;=:\;\mathcal R(\eta,r).
\end{equation}
The  initial law is $p_\delta$, \emph{not} $p_0$, since both flows are normalised at
time $\delta$. As $p_\delta$ will in general have full support,
the tail must be estimated separately. Using Step 1 to bound
$|Z^\delta(T,x)-Z^\delta_\theta(T,x)|\le 2e^{\|G\|_{L^1}+\|G_\theta\|_{L^1}}(1+|x|)$ off
$B_r$, one gets for every $r,\eta>0$
\begin{equation}
  W_1\Big(Z^\delta(T,\cdot)_\#p_\delta,\ Z^\delta_\theta(T,\cdot)_\#p_\delta\Big)
  \;\le\;\|p_\delta\|_{L^\infty}\,\mathcal R(\eta,r)
  \;+\;2e^{\|G\|_{L^1}+\|G_\theta\|_{L^1}}\!\!\int_{|x|>r}\!\!(1+|x|)\,p_\delta(x)\,\dd x .
\end{equation}
The tail integral tends to $0$ as $r\to\infty$ because $p_\delta$ has a finite first moment
by \textup{(S1)}, so for \emph{fixed} $\theta$-dependent constants $L_\theta$, $G_\theta$ and
$\mathcal C_p$, optimising over $r$ and $\eta$ makes the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:wass}
tend to $0$ as $\mathcal E_v\to 0$. Since
$Z^\delta(T,\cdot)_\#p_\delta=p_T$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:lagrangian}\textup{(iii)} applied on
$[\delta,T]$, the left-hand side is the $W_1$ distance between $p_T$ and the output of the
deterministic sampler run from $p_\delta$ with the learned score. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: $L^1$ and Wasserstein error estimates

where $\Xi_{N,\lambda,n}:=\frac{n-N\bm{m}(\lambda)}{\sqrt{N}}$.

[Prop Xe_inverse of arXiv:2603.29711, 'Strong Feller property, irreducibility,\\ and uniqueness of the invariant measure\\ for st'] Under the assumptions of Theorem~(th:wp of the paper),
let $d=1$, let 
$\delta\in(\frac14+\sigma, \frac12+\sigma)$,
let $x\in V_{2\xi}$ for some $\xi\in[0,\frac12+\sigma)$,
and
assume one of the following settings:
\begin{itemize}
    \item $\delta\in(\frac14,\frac12)$, 
    $\gamma\geq\alpha+2$, $\xi\geq0$,
    $r:=\frac1\delta$, and
    $\mathfrak p:=\frac12+\delta$;
    \item $\delta\in[\frac12,\frac34]$, 
    $\gamma\geq\alpha+4$,
    $\xi\geq\delta$,
    $r\in(2,4)$, and
    $\mathfrak p:=\frac32+\frac1r$;
    \item  $\delta\in(\frac34,1)$, 
    $\gamma\geq\alpha+4$, 
    $\xi\geq\delta$,
    $r:=\frac2{2\delta-1}$, and
    $\mathfrak p:=1+\delta$.
\end{itemize}
Then,
for every $\ell\geq2$ and $T>0$, there exists a constant
$C>0$, 
only depending on $\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta,\sigma,\ell, T$,
such that, for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, it holds that
\begin{align*}
\|G_{\alpha, \varepsilon}^{-1}(X^x_\varepsilon)\|_{
L^\ell(\Omega; L^r(0,T;\mathscr{L}(V_{2\delta},H)))}
\le C
\left(1+\|\Psi_{\gamma}(x)\|^{\mathfrak p}_{L^1(\mathcal O)}+
  \|x\|_{V_{2\xi}}^{\mathfrak p}\right).
\end{align*}
Furthermore, the same conclusion holds also 
under any of the following stronger scenarios:
\begin{itemize}
    \item $\delta\in(\frac14,\frac12)$, 
    $\gamma>\max\{1,\frac1{4\sigma}\}(\alpha+2)+2$,
    $\xi\geq\frac12+\frac{\alpha+2}{4(\gamma-2)}$,
    $r:=\infty$, and $\mathfrak p:=\frac12+2\delta$;
    \item $\delta\in[\frac12,\frac34]$, 
    $\gamma>\max\{1,\frac1{4\sigma}\}(\alpha+4)+2$,
    $\xi\geq\max\{\delta,\frac12+\frac{\alpha+4}{4(\gamma-2)}\}$,
    $r:=\infty$, and $\mathfrak p\in(2,\frac52)$;
    \item $\delta\in(\frac34,1)$, 
    $\gamma>\max\{1,\frac1{4\sigma}\}(\alpha+4)+2$,
    $\xi\geq\max\{\delta,\frac12+\frac{\alpha+4}{4(\gamma-2)}\}$,
    $r:=\infty$, and $\mathfrak p:=\frac12+2\delta$.
\end{itemize}

[Prop nonlinear-regression-regularity of arXiv:2608.30382, 'Convergence rates for the RMSprop optimizer with full control of the hyperparameters'] Let $\mathcal V\subseteq{\mathbb R}^d$ be nonempty and compact,
let $ r \in ( 0, \nicefrac{ 1 }{ 2 } ) $, $ \delta \in (0, \infty ) $,
and suppose that there exist nonempty compact sets
$ K_Z \subseteq \mathcal Z $ and $ K_Y\subseteq {\mathbb R}^m $ and a constant
$ B \in (0,\infty) $ with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]

\item
The random variables are compactly supported in the sense that
\begin{align}\begin{split} 
  {\mathbb P}\bigl( Z \in K_Z , \, Y \in K_Y \bigr) = 1 .
 \end{split}\end{align}

\item
For $ {\mathbb P}_Z $-almost every $ z \in K_Z $, the conditional law of $ Y $
given $ Z = z $ has a Lebesgue density~$ p_z $ satisfying
\bas{

  \| p_z \|_{ L^\infty } \le B .
}

\item
The map $ ( \theta, z ) \mapsto \Gamma^{ \theta }( z ) $ and, for every
$ i \in \{ 1, \dots, d \} $,
the map
$
  ( \theta, z ) \mapsto\frac{\partial\Gamma^\theta}{\partial\theta_i}( z )
$
are continuous on $ \mathcal V \times K_Z $.

\item
The coordinate derivatives satisfy the uniform moment lower bound
\bas{

D_r
=
\inf_{ \substack{ \theta \in \mathcal V } }
\inf_{
  1 \le i \le d
}
{\mathbb E}\biggl[
\Bigl|
\frac{\partial\Gamma^\theta}{\partial\theta_i}(Z)
\Bigr|^{r}
\biggr]
\ge \delta.
}
\end{enumerate}
Choose $R\in(0,\infty)$ such that $K_Y\subseteq B(0,R)$, let
$\omega_{m-1}$ denote the volume of the unit ball in ${\mathbb R}^{m-1}$, use the
convention $\omega_0=1$, and set
\bas{
\mu_r
&=\frac{\delta^{1/r}}{2B\omega_{m-1}R^{m-1}}
\left(\frac{1-2r}{1-r}\right)^{(1-r)/r},\\
C_X
&=\max_{\substack{\theta\in\mathcal V,\ z\in K_Z,\ y\in K_Y\\1\le i\le d}}
\left|
\left\langle
\frac{\partial\Gamma^\theta}{\partial\theta_i}(z),
\Gamma^\theta(z)-y
\right\rangle
\right|.
}
Then $\mu_r,C_X\in(0,\infty)$. The innovation $(X,U)$ defined in
(equation eq:nonlinear-regression-loss-innovation of the paper) is $(c_r,q_r)$-regular on
$\mathcal V$ with
\bas{
c_r
=\frac{(1-e^{-1})\mu_r^3}{8C_X},
\qquad
q_r=\frac{(1-e^{-1})\mu_r}{2C_X}.
}

Let d and K be positive integers, let mu_1,...,mu_K be arbitrary vectors in R^d, and let X_0 have the equally weighted mixture law K^(-1) sum_i N(mu_i,I_d). For t>0 let X_t=e^(-t)X_0+sqrt(1-e^(-2t))Z with Z~N(0,I_d) independent of X_0; denote its positive density by q_t and put mu_i,t=e^(-t)mu_i. Define w_i,t(x)=exp(-||x-mu_i,t||^2/2)/sum_j exp(-||x-mu_j,t||^2/2). Then grad_x log q_t(x)=sum_i w_i,t(x)mu_i,t-x for every x in R^d. For the additional symmetric two-component hypothesis K=2, mu_1=mu and mu_2=-mu, this is mu_t tanh(mu_t^T x)-x, with mu_t=e^(-t)mu. The tanh formula requires both opposite means and equal weights. This is a spatial-density score identity, not an identity for the DDPM parameter gradient or an exact equivalence of gradient descent with EM.

body: A real symmetric (or complex Hermitian) matrix A is positive definite if x^T A x > 0 (resp. x* A x > 0) for every nonzero vector x. Equivalent conditions: all eigenvalues are positive; all leading principal minors are positive (Sylvester's criterion); A = B^T B for some invertible B (a Cholesky/Gram factorization). Positive semidefinite relaxes > to >=.
title: Positive-Definite Matrix

body: [Theorem 16 of arXiv:2609.02105, 'Contact fundamental forms and \\ adjoint varieties'] In Notation \ref{n.coordi},  for any local holomorphic function $\varphi \in \sO_{\sH,0}$, the polynomial $$ \sum_{|I|=0}^k  \frac{\big( \{\prod_{a=1}^m X_a^{i_a} Y_a^{j_a}\}T^p \varphi \big)(0)}{|I'|! \ p !} (xyt)^I $$ with $I = (i_1, \ldots, i_m, j_1, \ldots, j_m, p)$ in the sum, belongs to $ \varphi + \bm_0^{k+1}$.  Here, we regard $X_a, Y_a, T$ as left-invariant vector fields on $\sH$ and take derivative of $\varphi$ with respect to these vector fields. Similarly, for any point $h \in \sH$ and $\varphi \in \sO_{\sH,h}$,  the polynomial $$ \sum_{|I|=0}^k  \frac{\big( \{\prod_{a=1}^m X_a^{i_a} Y_a^{j_a}\}T^p \varphi \big)(h)}{|I'|!  p !} h^*(xyt)^I $$ belongs to $\varphi + \bm_h^{k+1}$, where for any function $F$ on $\sH$, we denote by $h^*F$ the function whose value at $g \in \sH$ is $h^*F(g) = F(h^{-1} g)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 16 of arXiv:2609.02105

body:
[Proposition 13 of arXiv:2606.31455, 'Discrete time-multidimensional renewal theory and applications'] Fix two distinct coordinates $u\neq v$ and times $k_u,k_v\in\mathbb{N}$.
Let $M^{[u]}(k_u)=\mathbb{E}[N^{[u]}(k_u)]$ and $M^{[v]}(k_v)=\mathbb{E}[N^{[v]}(k_v)]$.
Let $M^{[u,v]}:\mathbb{N}^2\to\mathbb{R}$ denote the \emph{bivariate} renewal function of
the projected increment vector $(X^{[u]},X^{[v]})$, i.e.
$M^{[u,v]}(k_u,k_v)=\mathbb{E}[N^{[u,v]}(k_u,k_v)]$ with
$N^{[u,v]}(k_u,k_v)=\sup\{n:(S_n^{[u]},S_n^{[v]})\le_2(k_u,k_v)\}$.

Define the univariate renewal kernels
$\psi_u:=(\ez-f^{[u]})^{(-1)}$ and $\psi_v:=(\ez-f^{[v]})^{(-1)}$ on $\mathbb{N}$, and
define $\widetilde{\psi}_{u,v}:\mathbb{N}^2\to\mathbb{R}$ by

\begin{equation}
\widetilde{\psi}_{u,v}(r_u,r_v)
=
\left\{
\begin{array}{ll}
\psi_u(r_u), & \text{if } r_u>0 \text{ and } r_v=0,\\[0.2em]
\psi_v(r_v), & \text{if } r_v>0 \text{ and } r_u=0,\\[0.2em]
\psi_u(0)+\psi_v(0)-1, & \text{if } r_u=r_v=0,\\[0.2em]
0, & \text{otherwise.}
\end{array}
\right.
\end{equation}

Then

\begin{equation}
\mathbb{E}\!\left[N^{[u]}(k_u)\,N^{[v]}(k_v)\right]
=
\big[M^{[u,v]}*\widetilde{\psi}_{u,v}\big](k_u,k_v),
\end{equation}

and consequently

\begin{equation}
\mathrm{Cov}\!\left(N^{[u]}(k_u),\,N^{[v]}(k_v)\right)
=
\big[M^{[u,v]}*\widetilde{\psi}_{u,v}\big](k_u,k_v)
-
M^{[u]}(k_u)\,M^{[v]}(k_v).
\end{equation}
title: Proposition 13 of arXiv:2606.31455

body:
[Lemma 32 of arXiv:2608.03575, '2608.03575'] There exists a constant $\delta_{\mathrm{aug}}=\delta_{\mathrm{aug}}(\varepsilon_1)>0$
such that the following holds. Suppose that $u,a,b$ are pairwise adjacent
in the RCP embedding. Let
\[
E_{a,b}(u)
=
\bigcup_{\substack{v\sim a \text{ or } v\sim b\\ v\ne u,a,b}} D_v .
\]
Then
\[
\operatorname{diam} E_{a,b}(u)
\ge
\delta_{\mathrm{aug}}\max\{r_a,r_b\}.
\]

[Proposition 18 of arXiv:2512.07202, 'Hitting Probabilities for Hypoelliptic Differential Equations Driven by Fractional Brownia'] Let \( (B_t)_{t \geqslant 0} \) be a \( d \)-dimensional fBM with Hurst parameter \( H \in (0,1) \). Then there exist  positive constants \( C_1,C_2 \), such that one has
\[
\mathbb{P}\left(\inf_{\|\phi\|_{\mathbb{R}^d}=1}\sup_{u,v\in [s,s+\delta]}\left|\langle\phi,B_{u,v}\rangle\right|\leqslant x\,\middle|\,\mathcal{F}_s^W\right)\leqslant C_1\exp\left( -C_2 \delta x^{-1/H} \right)
\]for all $\delta> 0$, $s\geqslant0$ and $ x\in(0,1)$.

body: [Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2609.00636, 'Forcing monochromatic subdivisions'] For every integers $s \ge 2$ and  $d \ge 1$ there exists an integer $D$, that depends only on $d$ and $s$, such that for every graph $P$ with maximum degree at most $ d$, there is a graph $H$ with maximum degree at most $D$ such that every $s$-coloring of $V(H)$ yields a monochromatic subdivision of $P$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 58 of arXiv:2609.02878, '2609.02878'] Let \(K\Subset Y^{\rm rv}\) admit a finite cover by Zariski-open sets
\(U_\alpha\subset Y^{\rm rv}\) such that
\[
 \pi^{-1}(U_\alpha)\longrightarrow U_\alpha
 \quad\text{is biregularly isomorphic to}\quad
 U_\alpha\times\PP^1\longrightarrow U_\alpha.
\]
Then there are constants \(0<c_K\le C_K<\infty\) such that, for every
\(q\in K\) and every \(0\le t<T\),
\begin{equation}
 c_K\sqrt{T-t}
 \le
 \operatorname{diam}_{(X,g(t))}F_q
 \le
 \operatorname{diam}_{(F_q,g(t)|_{F_q})}F_q
 \le C_K\sqrt{T-t}.
\end{equation}
The first diameter is measured by the ambient distance on \(X\), while
the last is intrinsic to the induced fibre metric.

[Lem ConstructionKernel of arXiv:2609.02882, 'A new proof that more than $2/3$ of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are simple and '] Put
\begin{equation}
C_{\mathrm{MT}}
:=
\frac12+\frac1{\sqrt2}
\cot\left(\frac1{\sqrt2}\right)
=
1.3274992963206\ldots.    
\end{equation}
Then for every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a real valued even function
$
\eta_\varepsilon\in C_c^\infty((-1/2,1/2))
$
such that, for the kernel
$
K_\varepsilon(z):=\widehat{\eta_\varepsilon^2}(z),
$
we have
$
K_\varepsilon(0)=1,
$
and
$$
\sum_{\substack{\rho,\rho'\\0<\gamma,\gamma'\leqslant T}}
K_\varepsilon\left(
i(\rho-\rho')\frac{\log T}{2\pi}
\right)^2
=
\left(
C_{\eta_\varepsilon}
+
O_{\varepsilon}\left(
\frac{1}{\sqrt{\log T}}
\right)
\right)
\frac{T}{2\pi}\log T,
$$
where
$
\left|C_{\eta_\varepsilon}-C_{\mathrm{MT}}\right|
<\varepsilon.
$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition prop:condensation of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] {bozic_models_1984}}]  \leavevmode
  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*)]
    \item Let $\mathfrak{M} = (W, \leq, \sqsubset, V)$ be a $\Box$-p model, then
          $x \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \varphi \iff x \Vdash^e_{\beta\mathfrak{M}} \varphi$
          for any $\varphi \in \mathscr{L}_\Box$ and $x \in W$.
    \item Let $\mathfrak{M} = (W, \leq, \sqsubset, V)$ be a $\Diamond$-p model, then
          $x \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \varphi \iff x \Vdash^e_{\delta\mathfrak{M}} \varphi$
          for any $\varphi \in \mathscr{L}_\Diamond$ and $x \in W$.
  \end{enumerate}
  \begin{proof}
    We first make the following claims.
    \begin{claim*}
      For any $w \in W$ and $\rho \in \mathscr{L}_\Box$, $w \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \rho \iff \forall w' \geq w\,(w' \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \rho)$.
      \begin{subproof}[Proof of claim]
        ($\Leftarrow$) Trivial.
        ($\Rightarrow$) Follows from $\Box$-persistency.
      \end{subproof}
    \end{claim*}
    \begin{claim*}
      For any $w' \in W$ and $\rho \in \mathscr{L}_\Diamond$, $w' \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \rho \iff \exists w \leq w'\,(w \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \rho)$.
      \begin{subproof}[Proof of claim]
        ($\Leftarrow$) Follows from $\Diamond$-persistency.
        ($\Rightarrow$) Trivial.
      \end{subproof}
    \end{claim*}
    Now we prove (1) and (2) separately.

    (1) Induction on the construction of $\varphi$. It suffices to consider the $\Box$ case.
    \begin{align*}
      x \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \Box \psi &\iff \forall y \sqsupset x\, (y \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \psi) & \\
                                  &\iff \forall y \sqsupset x\, \forall y' \geq y\, (y' \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \psi) & (\because \text{claim}) \\
                                  &\iff \forall y \sqsupset x\, \forall y' \geq y\, (y' \Vdash^e_{\beta \mathfrak{M}} \psi) & (\because \text{induction hypothesis})\\
                                  &\iff \forall y' \sqsupset_\beta x\, (y' \Vdash^e_{\beta \mathfrak{M}} \psi) & (\because x \sqsubset y \leq y') \\
                                  &\iff x \Vdash^e_{\beta \mathfrak{M}} \Box \psi. &
    \end{align*}

    (2) Induction on the construction of $\varphi$. It suffices to consider the $\Diamond$ case:
    \begin{align*}
      x \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \Diamond \psi &\iff \exists y' \sqsupset x\, (y' \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \psi) & \\
                                      &\iff \exists y' \sqsupset x\, \exists y \leq y'\, (y \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \psi) & (\because \text{claim}) \\
                                      &\iff \exists y' \sqsupset x\, \exists y \leq y'\, (y \Vdash^e_{\delta\mathfrak{M}} \psi) & (\because \text{induction hypothesis}) \\
                                      &\iff \exists y \sqsupset_\delta x\, (y \Vdash^e_{\delta\mathfrak{M}} \psi) & (\because x \sqsubset y' \geq y) \\
                                      &\iff x \Vdash^e_{\delta \mathfrak{M}} \Diamond \psi. & \qedhere
    \end{align*}
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lem 37 of arXiv:2608.28355, 'About the contractibility of the walking coinductive equivalence'] Let $\ell\geq0$ and $0\leq p \leq \ell+2$.
Let $S\subseteq \{0, \ldots, \ell+2\}$ such that $|S|\geq p+1$, and
\[\overline{S}\coloneqq S\setminus \{\ell+2-p+1,\ell+2-p+2, \ldots,\ell+2-p+p\}.\]
Denote by
\[\rho\colon \Delta[S]\to \Delta[\ell+2]\quad\text{ and }\quad \overline\rho\colon \Delta[\overline{S}]\to \Delta[\ell+2-p]\]
the corresponding maps.
If $\rho$ defines a non-degenerate $(|S|-1)$-simplex in $\Sigma^p\Delta[\ell+2-p]$,
then $\overline\rho$ defines a non-degenerate $(|\overline{S}|-1)$-simplex in $\Delta[\ell+2-p]$
and there is a commutative square of marked simplicial sets
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
\Delta[S]\arrow[r,two heads]\arrow[d,"\rho"swap]&
\Sigma^p\Delta[\overline{S}]
\arrow[d,"\Sigma^p\overline\rho"]\\
\Delta[\ell+2]
\arrow[r,two heads
]&\Sigma^p\Delta[\ell+2-p]
\end{tikzcd}
\]

body:
[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The moments of the beta distribution are given by
$$M_k=\frac{a(a+1)\ldots(a+k-1)}{(a+b)(a+b+1)\ldots(a+b+k-1)}$$
and in particular, the mean and variance are given by the following formulae,
$$E=\frac{a}{a+b}\quad,\quad V=\frac{ab}{(a+b)^2(a+b+1)}$$
and the skewness and kurtosis are given by the following formulae,
$$\gamma=\frac{2(b-a)\sqrt{a+b+1}}{(a+b+2)\sqrt{ab}}\quad,\quad
\kappa=3+\frac{6[(a-b)^2(a+b+1)-ab(a+b+2)]}{ab(a+b+2)(a+b+3)}$$
with $a,b>0$ being as usual the parameters.

body:
[Proposition prop:imag-spectrum of arXiv:2608.01253, 'The pseudo-quantum representation of \\finite reversible Markov chains'] Let $\lvert y_\pm\rangle:=\tfrac1{\sqrt2}(1,\pm i)^{T}$ be the eigenvectors of $\sigma^y$,
with $\sigma^y\lvert y_\pm\rangle=\pm\lvert y_\pm\rangle$. Then the $2M$ orthonormal eigenpairs of
$H_{\mathrm{NUO}}$ are

\[
H_{\mathrm{NUO}}\,\bigl(\lvert y_\pm\rangle\otimes u_j\bigr)=\mp\,\alpha_j\,
\bigl(\lvert y_\pm\rangle\otimes u_j\bigr),\qquad j=1,\dots,M,
\]

so $\operatorname{spec}(H_{\mathrm{NUO}})=\{\pm\alpha_j\}$, symmetric about $0$. The Markov relaxation modes
and the quantum energy levels are the same list of numbers. The mode with semigroup
decay $e^{s(\alpha_j-1)}$ is the pair of energy levels $\pm\alpha_j$.

body:
[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2506.11918, 'Central limit theorems for the Euler characteristic in the Random Connection Model for hig'] Let $W\in\Bf$ and $F=f(\Delta_W)$ with $\E{F}=0$, $\V{F}=1$ and $\E{F^4}<\infty$, where $f$ is a function defined for finite simplicial complexes with vertices in $\X$.
Moreover, assume that $\gamma_5,\gamma_6<\infty$.
Then it is true that
\begin{align*}
d_W(F,N) &\,\leq\, \gamma_1 + \gamma_2 + \gamma_3, \\
d_K(F,N) &\,\leq\, \gamma_1 + \gamma_2 + \gamma_3 + \gamma_4 + \gamma_5 + \gamma_6,
\end{align*}
where the quantities $\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_6$ are defined by
\begin{align*}
\gamma_1 &\,:=\, 2 \Bigg[ \beta^3 \int_{W^3} \E{ \left( \Lambda_{(x_1,U_1),(x_2,U_2)}^1F \right)^2 \left( \Lambda_{(x_2,U_2),(x_1,U_1)}^1F \right)^2}^\frac{1}{2} \\
& \qquad \enskip \times \, \E{ \left(\Lambda_{(x_1,U_1),(x_3,U_3),(x_2,U_2)}^2 F\right)^2 \left(\Lambda_{(x_2,U_2),(x_3,U_3),(x_1,U_1)}^2 F\right)^2}^\frac{1}{2}  \; \lambda^3 \, (\d {(x_1,x_2,x_3)}) \Bigg]^\frac{1}{2} \hspace{-6pt}, \\
\gamma_2 &\,:= \left[ \beta^3 \hspace{-2pt} \int_{W^3} \hspace{-2pt} \E{ \left(\Lambda_{(x_1,U_1),(x_3,U_3),(x_2,U_2)}^2 F\right)^2 \left(\Lambda_{(x_2,U_2),(x_3,U_3),(x_1,U_1)}^2 F\right)^2} \lambda^3 \, (\d {(x_1,x_2,x_3)}) \right]^\frac{1}{2}  \hspace{-6pt}, \\
\gamma_3 &\,:=\, \beta \int_W \E{ |\Lambda_{(x,U)}F|^3 } \; \lambda \, (\d x), \\
\gamma_4 &\,:=\, \frac{\beta}{2} \E{ F^4 }^\frac{1}{4} \int_W \E{ \left(\Lambda_{(x,U)}F\right)^4 }^\frac{3}{4} \; \lambda \, (\d x), \\
\gamma_5 &\,:=\, \left[ \beta \int_W \E{ \left(\Lambda_{(x,U)}F\right)^4 } \; \lambda \, (\d x) \right]^\frac{1}{2} \hspace{-6pt}, \\
\gamma_6 &\,:=\, \Bigg[ \beta^2 \int_{W^2} 6\; \E{ \left(\Lambda_{(x_1,U_1)}F\right)^4 }^\frac{1}{2} \E{ \left(\Lambda_{(x_1,U_1),(x_2,U_2)}^2 F\right)^4 }^\frac{1}{2} \\
& \qquad \qquad \enskip + 3\; \E{ \left(\Lambda_{(x_1,U_1),(x_2,U_2)}^2 F\right)^4 } \; \lambda^2 \, (\d {(x_1,x_2)}) \Bigg]^\frac{1}{2}
\end{align*}
with independent marks $U,U_1,U_2,U_3\sim\Q$, which are also independent of $\Psi$.
Furthermore, we have $\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_4<\infty$.

body:
[Definition def:standard_under of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix $\lambda \in (0,1/3)$. Let $\overline{p}$ be a send sequence with 
$p_0=1$. 
Let $U=(U^A,U^B,U^C)$ be the under-backoff process with 
birth rate $3\lambda$ and
send sequence $\overline{p}$.
Let $X$ be the backoff process with 
birth rate~$3\lambda$, send sequence~$\overline{p}$, and cohort set~$\mathcal{C}=\{A,B,C\}$ (Definition~(def:backoff-cohorts of the paper)). 
The standard coupling of $U$ and $X$ has the following invariants for every $i\geq 1$ and $t\geq 1$.
\begin{description}  
\item  [Inv-$b_i(t)$:] For each stream $D\in \{A,B,C\}$, 
$\mathbf{b}_i^{U^D}(t-1) \subseteq \mathbf{b}_i^{X^D}(t-1)$.
\item  [Inv-$B_i(t)$:] For each stream $D\in \{A,B,C\}$, $\mathbf{B}_i^{U^D}(t) \subseteq \mathbf{B}_i^{X^D}(t)$.
\item [Inv-$s_i(t)$:] 
For each stream $D\in \{A,B,C\}$, $\mathbf{s}_i^{U^D}(t) \subseteq \mathbf{s}_i^{X^D}(t)$.
\end{description}
Initially, Inv-$b_i(1)$ holds for every $i\geq 1$ since all of these sets are empty.

For any $t$ assuming Inv-$b_i(t)$, the coupling at step~$t$ proceeds as follows.
For each $D\in \{A,B,C\}$, $\mathbf{n}^{U^D}(t) = \mathbf{n}^{X^D}(t)$, so for all $i\geq 1$, 
Inv-$B_i(t)$ holds.
For every   
$D\in \{A,B,C\}$ and
$i\geq 1$, $\mathbf{S}^{X^D}_i(t)$ is formed by including each ball in 
$\mathbf{B}_i^{X^D}(t) \setminus \mathbf{B}_i^{Z^D}(t)$ 
independently with probability~$p_i$.
Then $\mathbf{s}^{X^D}_i(t) = \mathbf{S}^{X^D}_i(t) \cup \mathbf{s}^{Z^D}_i(t)$, establishing Inv-$s_i(t)$.

 
The assignments to $\mathbf{e}_i^{X^D}(t)$ 
and $\mathbf{e}_i^{U^D}(t)$ follow deterministically, using  Definitions~(def:backoffasgen of the paper) and~(def:under-backoff of the paper).

Since for all $i$ $\mathbf{s}_i^{X^D}(t) \cap \mathbf{B}_i^{U^D}(t) = \mathbf{s}_i^{U^D}(t)$,
the invariant Inv-$b_i(t+1)$ for all $i$ follows from  
$ \mathbf{s}_i^{U^D}(t) \cap \mathbf{e}_i^{X^D}(t) \subseteq \mathbf{e}_i^{U^D}(t)$, which holds: 
If a ball~$\beta$ is in $ \mathbf{s}_i^{U^D}(t) \cap \mathbf{e}_i^{X^D}(t) $ then
$\mathbf{s}^{X^A}(t) \cup \mathbf{s}^{X^B}(t) \cup s^{X^C}(t) = \{\beta\}$ so
$\mathbf{s}^{U^A}(t) \cup \mathbf{s}^{U^B}(t) \cup s^{U^C}(t) = \{\beta\}$ so 
$\mathbf{e}_i^{U^D}(t) = \{\beta\}$.

body: Let (X, Sigma, mu) be a measure space and let f_1, f_2, f_3, ... be a sequence of Sigma-measurable functions from X to [0, infinity] (nonnegative extended-real-valued, with no domination or convergence assumed). Then the integral over X of liminf_n f_n dmu is less than or equal to liminf_n of the integral over X of f_n dmu, i.e. integral(liminf f_n) <= liminf integral(f_n). The inequality can be strict, for instance when mass escapes to infinity or travels along the domain, so equality needs an extra hypothesis such as domination.

[Prop gl-flatness of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Let $X$ be any flat orthogonal $G$-spectrum. Then $X\smashp{-}$ preserves $G$-global weak equivalences. Moreover, for any $Y$, the functor ${-}\smashp Y$ preserves $G$-global weak equivalences between flat orthogonal $G$-spectra.
    \begin{proof}
        Let $f$ be a $G$-global weak equivalence. For the first statement, we have to show that $\varphi^*(X\smashp f)=\varphi^*(X)\smashp\varphi^*(f)$ is an $H$-equivariant weak equivalence for every $\varphi\colon H\to G$. As $\varphi^*(X)$ is again flat by [schwede2018global]*{Remark 3.5.8}, this follows at once from the first part of Theorem~(thm:equiv-flatness of the paper). The second part of the proposition follows in the same way from the second part of Theorem~(thm:equiv-flatness of the paper).
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). For the Erdos-Renyi random graph G(n,p) near the critical window p = 1/n + lambda n^{-4/3}, Aldous's exploration process encodes a depth-first search of the graph as a random-walk-like process Z_n(t) whose excursions above past running minima correspond exactly to the connected components, with excursion lengths equal to component sizes. After rescaling space by n^{-2/3} and time correspondingly, this process converges to a limiting process W(t) = B(t) + lambda t - t^2/2, a Brownian motion with parabolic drift, whose excursions above its running minimum encode the limiting rescaled sizes of the largest components in the critical window; the associated merging dynamics of component sizes as edges are added form the "standard multiplicative coalescent", a Markov process on sequences of masses matching the excursion structure. This gives the precise scaling limit, order n^{2/3} for the largest components with an explicit limiting joint law, for the Erdos-Renyi critical phase transition. It does not extend directly to other random graph models without re-deriving an analogous exploration or walk encoding, which may not exist in closed form, and the specific n^{2/3} spatial and n^{-1/3} time-window scaling is particular to models in the Erdos-Renyi (mean-field) universality class. Typical failure: Applying the Erdos-Renyi n^{2/3} critical scaling window and multiplicative-coalescent limit directly to a random graph model with heavy-tailed degrees, infinite third moment, or strong local clustering, where the correct scaling exponents and even the limiting process, as established for configuration models with power-law degree exponent tau in (3,4) by Bhamidi, van der Hofstad and van Leeuwaarden, differ substantially; universality of the Erdos-Renyi picture is a theorem for specific model classes, not a generic property of all critical random graphs. Canonical reference: Aldous, 1997, Annals of Probability; Aldous and Limic, 1998, Electronic Journal of Probability; Bhamidi, van der Hofstad and van Leeuwaarden, 2010, Annals of Probability.
Erdos-Renyi, or configuration-model-type with matching degree-tail conditions, random graph in the critical window p ~ 1/n + O(n^{-4/3})
a valid exploration (depth-first search) encoding of the graph as a walk whose excursions correspond to components
appropriate moment conditions, such as finite third moment of the degree for configuration models, for the walk-to-Brownian-motion scaling limit
the specific n^{2/3} spatial and n^{-1/3} time-window scaling matching the model's universality class
title: Technique: Aldous's Exploration Process and the Multiplicative Coalescent

[Definition of arXiv:2607.19651, 'Metastability and phase transition in a social network model with multiple opinions'] For any $o\in\mathcal{O}$, we call $\mathcal{S}^o$ the set of matrices $u\in\mathcal{S}$ such that there exists $r\in [0,1), n(u)\in\{1,...,N-1\}$ and a sequence of $n(u)$ different actors $a_1(u),...,a_{n(u)}(u)\in\mathcal{A}$ satisfying
        $$
            u(a_j(u),o)\geq j+r, \forall j \in\{1,...,n(u)\},\text{ and}
        $$
        $$
            u(a,p)\leq n(u)+r-\frac{1}{M-1}, \forall a\in\mathcal{A},p\in\mathcal{O}\setminus\{o\}.
        $$    
Moreover, for any initial matrix $u\in\mathcal{S}$, let
        $$
            \tau(u):=\inf\{n\geq 1, A_n\in\{A_1,...,A_{n-1}\}\}.
        $$
        This is the number of social expressions until an actor expresses an opinion for the second time. Note that $\tau(u)\in\{2, ..., N+1\}$.
title: Unnumbered definition of arXiv:2607.19651, 'Metastability and phase transition in a social network model'

body: Concept (campaign status: refuted 2026-09-01): the proposed route '|D| > r+k implies c <= 0' (which with the proved d_cb <= k would have closed Conjecture RC for all linear systems) is FALSE. Witness K(3,3): the linear system of 9 triples (each edge of the complete bipartite graph K33 plus its perfect matching's hub) has c = +0.127655 > 0 AND |D| = 36 > 18 = r+k (18 implied dual forms). Verified from scratch with the campaign's full_dual (|A| = 42). Second, mechanism-level witness: disjoint or cut-vertex unions of even tri-cycles (each c = log2(82/81) > 0, no extras) with one Pasch block (four extras, c = log2(8/9) < 0) - c is exactly additive and block extras survive into the union dual, so ten cycles plus Pasch give c > 0 with extras. Both random hunts (596 + 198 systems, zero violations) had supported the dichotomy: uniform sampling never reaches extras-with-large-fibre. Conjecture RC itself is untouched (K33 tightness 0.575).

body: [Theorem 34 of arXiv:2609.01190, 'Rough differential equations on manifolds via natural bundles'] Let $[S,T]\subseteq\Rsf$ be an interval and let $n\in\Nsf$. Let $p\in [1,3)$, let $\omega$ be a control function on interval $[S,T]$, and let $X$ be an $n$-dimensional branched rough path on interval $[S,T]$ with regularity $p$ and control $\omega$. Let $M$ be a manifold, let $f: M\to R_n^2M$ be an admissible rough velocity field, and let $Y_0\in M$. Then there exists $\varepsilon\in (0,\infty)$ and an integral curve $Y:[S,(S+\varepsilon)\wedge T]\to M$ of $f$ driven by $X$ that satisfies $Y(S)=Y_0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Let G be a connected linear algebraic group over a number field k. After enlarging a finite set S of places, G has a smooth model G/O_{k,S} with connected geometric fibres, and then H^1(O_v, G) = 1 for every finite place v not in S (Lang's theorem on the special fibre plus Hensel lifting). The local sets H^1(k_v, G) themselves need not vanish: for non-archimedean v, Kottwitz duality gives H^1(k_v, G) = Hom(Pic(G_{k_v}), Q/Z), a finite group (Proposition 2.12); accordingly the adelic set |BG(A_k^Sigma)| is the restricted product of the H^1(k_v, G), v not in Sigma, with respect to the trivial classes (Theorem 2.14).

[Dfn 4 of arXiv:2609.00719, 'On the Aleksandrov--Bakelman--Pucci estimates for the weighted $1$-Laplacian'] A function $\omega:\R^n\to\R$ is quasiconcave if $\{\omega\geq a\}$ is convex for every $a\in\R$.
For $u\in\operatorname{USC}(\R^n)$ with compact support, the quasiconcave envelope of $u^+$ is
\[
\Gamma(x):=\inf\{\omega(x):\omega\text{ is quasiconcave and }\omega\geq u^+\text{ in }\R^n\}.
\]

[Prop of arXiv:2411.09988, 'A Study in Markov Chains, Loop-Erased Random Walk and Loop Soups'] If $\mathcal{T}$ is a spanning tree of a connected graph with vertices $V = \{x_0, \ldots, x_n\}$, then the probability that $\mathcal{T}$ is chosen in Wilson's algorithm is
    \[\left[ \prod_{j=1}^{n} \deg (x_j)\right]^{-1} F(A)\]
    where $A = \{x_1, \ldots, x_n\}.$ Recall (prop3.12 of the paper), which states that $F(A) = \det G_A$. Note that the probability does not depend on how the points were ordered or on the tree $\mathcal{T}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

such that, for $T\ge T_0$, uniformly for real shifts satisfying

[Definition def:empirical_current of arXiv:2609.01581, 'Concentration of additive functionals of Stratonovich-type'] For a bounded, continuously differentiable vector field with bounded
derivatives, $U\in C^1_b(\mathbb{R}^d;\mathbb{R}^d)$, the \emph{current-type functional} (or empirical
current) is the Stratonovich integral
\begin{align}
  \overline{J}_t(U)
  \equiv \frac{1}{t}\int_0^t U(X_s)\circ\mathrm{d} X_s,
  
\end{align}
with $J_t(U)=t\overline{J}_t(U)$ the corresponding time-accumulated observable,
where $\circ$ denotes Stratonovich integration and $U(X_s)\circ\mathrm{d} X_s=\sum_i U_i(X_s)\circ\mathrm{d} X^i_s$.

body:
[Lemma 17 (coefficient calculus) of arXiv:2609.01093, 'Ideal MHD below the classical well-posedness threshold'] Let $\Psi$ be real-analytic near the origin in a finite-dimensional matrix space. There is
$\delta_\Psi=\delta_\Psi(\Psi,n,s,v_{\rm A})>0$ such that, if
$\|M_1\|_{Y^{s-1,1}}+\|M_2\|_{Y^{s-1,1}}\le\delta_\Psi$, then
\begin{equation*}\tag{P}
\|\Psi(M_1)-\Psi(M_2)\|_{Y^{s-1,1}}
\ \le\ C_\Psi\|M_1-M_2\|_{Y^{s-1,1}}.
\end{equation*}
In particular
$\|\Psi(M_1)-\Psi(0)\|_{Y^{s-1,1}}\le C_\Psi\|M_1\|_{Y^{s-1,1}}$.

In addition, suppose that the pointwise ranges of $M_1,M_2$ lie in a fixed
compact convex set $\mathscr K$ on a neighbourhood of which $\Psi$ is defined and
$C^1$.  Then, for every $1\le p\le\infty$,
\[
\|\Psi(M_1)-\Psi(M_2)\|_{L^p}\le C_{\Psi,\mathscr K}\|M_1-M_2\|_{L^p},
\]
and, separately, for every $\partial\in\{\partial_t,\partial_a\}$, $1\le a\le n$,
for which the indicated weak derivative of $M_1$ belongs to $L^1_{\rm loc}$,
\[
\partial\Psi(M_1)=\Psi'(M_1)\partial M_1\quad\text{in }\mathcal D'.
\]
Consequently, the same difference estimates hold with $C_tL^p$ in place of
$L^p$. If $M\in C_tY^{s-1,1}$, then
$\Psi(M)-\Psi(0)\in C_tY^{s-1,1}$; more generally, differences
$\Psi(M_1)-\Psi(M_2)$ are continuous there by
\eqref{eq:coeff-lipschitz}. This formulation is necessary because
$Y^{s-1,1}$ is nonunital when $\Psi(0)\ne0$.

body:
[Definition of arXiv:2609.03589, 'Correlated initialization of deep residual networks'] Let \((\banachSpace, \abs{\cdot})\) be a Banach space, and let $\alpha\in (0, 1]$.
    For a function \(f\colon [\underline{t}, \overline{t}] \to \banachSpace\)
    with \(\underline{t}, \overline{t} \in \mathbb{R}\) and  \(\underline{s}, \overline{s} \in [\underline{t},
    \overline{t}]\) we define the Hölder seminorm
    \[
        \holder{f}_{\alpha, [\underline{s},\overline{s}]} \coloneq \sup_{s\neq t \in [\underline{s}, \overline{s}]} \frac{\abs{f_t - f_s}}{\abs{t-s}^\alpha}
        \qquad\text{and}\qquad
        \holder{f}_{\alpha} \coloneq \holder{f}_{\alpha, [\underline{t}, \overline{t}]}.
    \]
    We further define the Hölder norm
    \[
        \norm{f}_{\alpha, [\underline{s}, \overline{s}]} \coloneq \norm{f}_{\infty, [\underline{s}, \overline{s}]} + \holder{f}_{\alpha, [\underline{s}, \overline{s}]}
        \qquad\text{and}\qquad
        \norm{f}_\alpha \coloneq \norm{f}_{\alpha, [\underline{t}, \overline{t}]}
    \]
    where \(\norm{f}_{\infty, [\underline{s}, \overline{s}]} = \sup_{s \in [\underline{s}, \overline{s}]} \abs{f_s}\) is the supremum norm of \(f\) on \([\underline{s}, \overline{s}]\).

body:
[Theorem CLT of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Given self-adjoint random variables $x_1,x_2,x_3,\ldots$ assumed to be i.i.d./f.i.d., centered, with variance $t>0$, we have, with $n\to\infty$, in moments,
$$\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\sum_{i=1}^nx_i\sim g_t/\gamma_t$$
where the limiting laws $g_t/\gamma_t$ are the following measures,
$$g_t=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi t}}e^{-x^2/2t}dx\quad,\quad 
\gamma_t=\frac{1}{2\pi t}\sqrt{4t^2-x^2}dx$$
which are the normal, or Gaussian, and Wigner semicircle law of parameter $t$.

$M_0=M_0(n,\lambda,\Lambda,B,D)>0$ and $\delta>0$ such that for all $a\geq1$ and $M>M_0$,
\begin{align}
\PP\left(
\norm{u^+}_{L^\infty([1,2]\times D)}>a,\,
M\norm{u^+}_{L^4(0,2;L^2(D))}\leq a

body:
[Theorem thm:transition of arXiv:2510.22778, 'Free denoising diffusion models'] Let $\rho=\tfrac12(\delta_{-a}+\delta_{a})$ and $\nu=\rho\boxplus\gamma_{v}$, $v>0$.
Then $\supp\nu$ is the union of two disjoint intervals if $v<a^{2}$ and a single
interval if $v\ge a^{2}$. The critical variance is
\begin{equation}
  v^{*}=a^{2}.
\end{equation}
In terms of the forward flow of Example~(ex:twoatom of the paper), with $a_{t}^{2}=\alpha_{t}a_{0}^{2}$
and $v_{t}=1-\alpha_{t}$, the spectrum is bimodal for
$\alpha_{t}>1/(1+a_{0}^{2})$ and unimodal thereafter.

[Proposition prop:comparison of arXiv:2607.22480, 'Distinguishability threshold for random geometric graphs'] Let $\xi \in \mathbb{R}^m$ be a vector with independent subgaussian coordinates, each with expectation $0$ and variance proxy at most $\sigma^2$, and let $g\in \mathbb{R}^m$ be a Gaussian random vector, matching $\xi$ in the first two moments. Let $M$ be a $m\times m$ symmetric matrix with zero diagonal, and let $\boldsymbol{a}\in \mathbb{R}^m$ be a fixed vector. Additionally, let $\delta_1=\max\{\sigma^2\|M\|_{op}, \sigma\|\boldsymbol{a}\|_\infty\}$ and $\delta_2=\sigma^4 \|M\|_{HS}^2+\sigma^2\|\boldsymbol{a}\|_2^2$. If $\delta_1$ is sufficiently small, then
 \[\Big|\mathbb{E}[e^{\xi^T M \xi+\boldsymbol{a}^T \xi}]-\mathbb{E}[e^{g^T M g+\boldsymbol{a}^T g}]\Big|=O\Big(e^{O(\delta_2)}\delta_1\delta_2\Big).\]

[Lem 11 of arXiv:2607.24170, '\large\bf ON NON-MONOTONICITY OF LOGARITHMIC ENERGY\\ FOR RANDOM MATRICES'] Among the Bernoulli configurations in dimension three, the following
ones have the indicated eigenvalue branches.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.2em]
\item The all-common configuration $\mathbf{U}=0$, of probability
$\qentry^9$, has two semisimple zero eigenvalues and one eigenvalue
$\mathfrak{c}\sqrt3$ after
division by $\sqrt3$.
\item Each of the nine configurations with exactly one rare entry,
of probability $\pentry\qentry^8$ each, has a simple zero eigenvalue.
\item Each of the eighteen configurations with exactly two rare
entries in one row or one column, of probability $\pentry^2\qentry^7$ each, has
a simple zero eigenvalue.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, the selected zero branches have total mass
\begin{equation}
 a_0\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}\frac23\qentry^9+3\pentry\qentry^8+6\pentry^2\qentry^7,
\end{equation}
and the selected separated outlier branch has mass
\begin{equation}
 a_1\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}\frac13\qentry^9.
\end{equation}

[Lemma 11 of arXiv:2607.19873, 'Local limit theorem for the operator norm of products of random matrices'] Let $M$ be a compact metrizable group 
and let $\eta: \wt B \to B$ be a Lipschitz $M$-principal bundle. 
Let $\rho: M \to {\rm GL}_d(\bb C)$ be a continuous linear representation for some integer $d \geq 1$. 
Then, for any continuous map $\varphi \in C^0_{\rho}(\wt B, \bb C^d)$, 
the map $s_{\varphi}$ is a continuous section of the bundle $B \times_{\rho} \bb C^d \to B$. 
Moreover, for any $\gamma \in [0, 1]$, the map 
\begin{align*}
 C^{\gamma}_{\rho}(\wt B, \bb C^d) &  \longrightarrow  \bf \Gamma^{\gamma}(B \times_{\rho} \bb C^d)  \notag\\
\varphi  &  \longmapsto s_{\varphi}
\end{align*}
is a Banach space isomorphism.

[Proposition 11 of arXiv:2607.27082, '2607.27082'] The following items hold:

\begin{enumerate}
  \item[(a)] Let \((\xi_j)_{j\ge1}\) be an i.i.d.\ sequence of symmetric, integer-valued random
variables such that
\[
\PP(|\xi_1|>x)\sim c_\xi x^{-\alpha},
\qquad x\to\infty,
\]
for some \(\alpha\in(1,2)\) and \(c_\xi>0\). Define \(Y_n(t):=\frac{S_{\lfloor n^\alpha t\rfloor}}{n},
\, t\ge0\). Then
  \[
  \frac{\tau_n^+}{n^\alpha}
  =\tau_1^+(Y_n)
  \Rightarrow \tau_1^+(X_\xi)
  \qquad\text{as }n\to\infty,
  \]
  where \(X_\xi\) is the symmetric strictly \(\alpha\)-stable Lévy process on
  \(\mathbb{R}\) with Lévy measure \(\Lambda_\xi\) given by \eqref{Levygene}.

  \item[(b)] Let $(\xi_j)_{j\geq 1}$ be an i.i.d.\ sequence of real-valued random variables such that
\[
\E[\xi_1]=0,
\qquad
\E[\xi_1^2]=\sigma^2\in(0,\infty).
\]
 Define \(Y_n(t):=\frac{S_{\lfloor n^2 t\rfloor}}{n},
\, t\ge0\). Then
  \[
  \frac{\tau_n^+}{n^2}
  =\tau_1^+(Y_n)
  \Rightarrow \tau_1^+(\sigma B)
  \qquad\text{as }n\to\infty,
  \]
  where \(B\) is a standard Brownian motion.
\end{enumerate}

[Theorem 14 of arXiv:2609.02426, 'Deformations of the $\osp(n|2)$-action on the superspace\\ of symbols of differential oper'] Let $n\geq3$ and $2d\notin\N$. Then $\Hd^1\vee\Hd^1=0$: the $\osp(n|2)$-module $\Sc^n_d$ admits no
obstructed deformation. The versal deformation of $L$ is its infinitesimal deformation
\begin{equation}

\widetilde{L}=L+\sum_{k\geq0}\tau_k f_{d-\frac k2},
\end{equation}
with $\tau_k$ even independent parameters and no relation between them; explicitly
$\widetilde{L}=\bigoplus_{k\geq0}L^{d-\frac k2+\tau_k}$ on $\bigoplus_{k\geq0}\Fc^n_{d-\frac k2}$. Any
formal deformation is equivalent to its infinitesimal part.

[Theorem 16 of arXiv:2506.11918, 'Central limit theorems for the Euler characteristic in the Random Connection Model for hig'] [Multivariate CLT for simplex counts] 
Let $(W_n)_{n\in\N}$ be a sequence in $\K^d$ with $r(W_n)\rightarrow\infty$ for $n\rightarrow\infty$.
Also, assume that $\z {\alpha+1}{\alpha+1}{\alpha+1} (\0) > 0$ and that the integrability condition (\ref{Integrabilitaet}) holds.
Furthermore, let $N_\Sigma$ denote an $(\alpha+1)$-dimensional centered normally distributed random vector with covariance matrix $\Sigma:=(\sigma_{m,l})_{1\leq m,l\leq\alpha+1}$, whose entries $\sigma_{m,l}$, $m,l\in\{1,\dots,\alpha+1\}$, are defined above.
Then $\Sigma$ is a symmetric, positive definite matrix, and we have
\begin{align*}
\frac{1}{\sqrt{|W_n|}} \left( f_0\big(\Delta_{W_n}\big)-\E{f_0\big(\Delta_{W_n}\big)},\dots,f_\alpha\big(\Delta_{W_n}\big)-\E{f_\alpha\big(\Delta_{W_n}\big)} \right) \;\xrightarrow{d}\; N_\Sigma \qquad \text{for } n \rightarrow \infty.
\end{align*}
title: Theorem 16 of arXiv:2506.11918

body:
[Prop Ahat n greater 1 of arXiv:2609.02409, 'Membranes and Maps'] For $n\in \{2,\ldots,5\}$ we have
    \begin{equation}
        \hat{\mathsf{A}}_{\mathsf{T}}\Big( \overline{M}_{0}\big(Z,[C_1]+\cdots+[C_n]\big) \Big)
        =
        \mathsf{V}(\epsvec{[n]}) \,
        \prod_{j=1}^n \hat{\mathsf{A}}_{\mathsf{T}}\Big(
            \overline{M}_{0}\big(\Tot \, N_{C_j/Z}, [C_j]\big)
        \Big) \,,
    \end{equation}
    where the function $\mathsf{V}$ is defined as in (eq: vertex function of the paper) (here, with $u = 1$):
    \begin{equation}
        \mathsf{V}(\epsvec{[n]})
        \coloneqq
        \begin{cases}
            \dfrac{\varsigma(\epsilon_3)\varsigma(\epsilon_4)\varsigma(\epsilon_5)}{\varsigma(\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2)}
            & n=2 \,, \\[0.95em]
            \varsigma(\epsilon_4)^2 \varsigma(\epsilon_5)^2
            & n=3 \,, \\[0.75em]
            \Big(\prod_{i=1}^5 \varsigma(\epsilon_i) \Big) \, \varsigma(\epsilon_5)^2 \sum_{i=1}^4 \kappa(\epsilon_i)
            & n=4 \,, \\[0.75em]
            \Big(\prod_{i=1}^5 \varsigma(\epsilon_i) \Big)^2 \Big(\big(\sum_{i=1}^5 \kappa(\epsilon_i)\big)^2 -\frac{1}{4} \Big)
            & n=5 \,,
        \end{cases}
    \end{equation}
    and we recall the notation $\varsigma(x)\coloneqq 2 \sinh \tfrac{x}{2}$ and $\kappa(x) \coloneqq \tfrac{1}{2} \coth \tfrac{x}{2}$.
title: Prop Ahat n greater 1 of arXiv:2609.02409

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The cumulative distribution function $F:\mathbb R\to[0,1]$ must be
\begin{enumerate}
\item Increasing,

\item Right continuous,

\item Such that $F(-\infty)=0$,

\item Such that $F(\infty)=1$,
\end{enumerate}
and conversely, any function satisfying these properties appears as a CDF.

[Thm chordal meander of arXiv:2506.01306, 'Asymptotic of Coulomb gas integral, Temperley-Lieb type algebras and pure partition functi'] For a fixed link pattern $\beta$, define the evaluation functional $l_\beta$ acting on Coulomb gas integrals by taking the corresponding asymptotic limit:
\[
l_{\beta}\left( \mathcal{J}^{(m,n)}_\alpha \right) := \lim_{\text{asymptotic with respect to } \beta} \mathcal{J}^{(m,n)}_\alpha.
\]
Then we have the identity:
\[
l_{\beta} \left( \mathcal{J}^{(m,n)}_\alpha \right) = \left\langle \alpha , \beta \right\rangle_{n,m},
\]
where $\delta= n(\kappa) = -2\cos\left(\frac{4\pi}{\kappa}\right)$, the right-hand side is the inner product in the standard module $V_{n,m}$ computed via the Gram (meander) matrix. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Chordal asymptotics and Gram pairing

Then, there exists a time-independent positive constant $K$ such that

[Prop decrease_free_energy of arXiv:2505.21770, 'Gradient-flow SDEs have unique transient population dynamics'] Let $(p(\cdot, t))_{t \ge T_1}$ be the marginals of a Langevin SDE (equation eq:overdamped_langevin_SDE of the paper) from the earliest possible observation time in the setting of (cor:three_points of the paper), and suppose that $\Psi \in C^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$. 

Then, the free energy $J(\rho) = \int_{\mathbb R^d} \Psi(x) \rho(x)\mathrm{d}x + \beta\int_{\mathbb R^d} \rho(x) \log \rho(x)\mathrm{d}x $, such that $\beta = \frac{\sigma^2}{2}$, strictly decreases in time, unless the process is at its stationary Gibbs distribution, $p_{\mathrm{eq}}$. Thus, $p_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the only possible marginal that can repeat at distinct times.
title: H-Theorem: marginals of gradient-flow SDEs monotonically decrease free energy

Own-work draft; proof (unaudited); T379-C030 v1, route-failure, Target1. In the paired actual-iid truth experiment take d=1,N=3,K=3,r=2,ell=0 and zero source calibration budget. One pair has one arbitrary uniform 2-support A and one all-3 systematic S, with fair orientation; the third context is known S. Sources choose context uniformly then a truth uniformly. Condition on D_u: u>=1 copies of candidate0 in the left context followed by one copy of candidate0 in the right. A genuine certificate-consistency ERM over the VC1 orientation class, breaking ties toward the larger-count A side, has posterior orientation error e_u=2^(u-1)/(3^(u-1)+2^(u-1)), tending to zero. Certificate labels S arise only when more than r distinct truths occur; no partition tags are supplied. Under the uniform-support prior, every realized output must be exactly source-calibrated at equal-score bins in ALL four compatible worlds. Its optimal conditional posterior false mass is 7/72 for every u. The supplied-orientation oracle, retaining unknown A support, has optimal conditional mean 1/12 in either orientation. Thus the disclosure penalty is 1/72 for every u: no conditional-data upper bound by C e_u for finite C, or by a modulus tending to zero with e_u, is possible. A complete exact Fraction enumeration of all 21,147 partitions of nine atoms finds 89 robust-feasible partitions; their objectives are affine in orientation posterior pi. Endpoint minima at pi=0,1 are both 7/72 while KEEPING four-world feasibility, and a common explicit partition attains both, certifying every pi. Separate two-world oracle enumeration gives 1/12. This is a conditional-data obstruction, NOT an unconditional or fixed-world minimax lower bound; D_u becomes rare. It does not refute ERM bounds involving unresolved version-space probability. Independent mathematical/priority audits pending.
Specified finite paired source and uniform world prior
Data D_u has repeated identities but no >r distinct-truth certificate
Exact source calibration in every compatible world, not posterior-average calibration

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:d409ed4f65be55c2542ddf1dc89138c070a737b4a48c03a302a2a69f695305f7","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/d4/d409ed4f65be55c2542ddf1dc89138c070a737b4a48c03a302a2a69f695305f7.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:ac3a4cf6e2ad4a5596bcd073660b0e70e2b415443ebc18f825e3c707e68bcdd3","bundle_entry_key":"erm-confidence-robust-calibration-obstruction","bundle_id":"population.t379-erm-confidence-robust-calibration-obstruction-20261020","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"calibrated generation; empirical risk minimization; robust decision; version space","draft":"w709/bundle_021.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:learning.calibration:kalai-vempala-erm-confidence-versus-robust-calibration-obstruction","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# A partition ERM can be reliable without closing the calibration penalty

T379-C030 v1. Proof (unaudited), kind route-failure, Target1.
This refutes a conditional-data classification-error bridge, not the
target's unconditional ERM minimax statement. No novelty claim.

## Statement and hardest step

Use the actual-iid paired experiment with d=1,N=3,K=3,r=2,ell=0,
zero calibration budget, and one extra known-systematic context.
Orientations are fair and the arbitrary support is a uniform 2-subset.
For every integer u>=1, condition on the ordered positive-probability
training sequence D_u consisting of u copies of candidate0 in the left
context and one copy of candidate0 in the right context.

There is a genuine certificate-consistency ERM in the VC-dimension-one
orientation class whose posterior orientation error on D_u equals

 e_u = 2^(u-1)/(3^(u-1)+2^(u-1)) -> 0,

whereas the optimal conditional posterior hallucination among outputs
exactly source-calibrated in ALL compatible worlds is

 beta(D_u)=7/72.

The oracle that is supplied the orientation, but not the unknown arbitrary
support, has conditional optimum 1/12 in either orientation. Therefore

 Delta(D_u)=beta(D_u)-O_bar(D_u)=1/72

for ALL u. No finite constant C gives Delta(D)<=C e(D) uniformly over
these data, nor does any bound Delta<=omega(e), with omega(t)->0.
The analogous statement for context classification risk uses (2/3)e_u.

Hardest step: calibration feasibility is a support-wise restriction.
Removing an orientation of small but positive posterior probability
enlarges the feasible output class discontinuously. Posterior confidence
cannot be substituted for an observable identification certificate.

## The ERM and its posterior risk

Label a context S when more than r distinct truths have been observed.
Minimize the number of certificate violations over the two orientations;
this is ordinary finite-class zero-one empirical risk minimization on
the available certified labels. As in C012, the true orientation always
has empirical risk zero. Break ties toward the orientation whose A side
has the larger factual sample count, and left if counts tie. This rule
is defined on every compatible data set, not only on D_u.

On D_u there are no labels, so both orientations minimize empirical
certificate risk. The tie rule selects left A. It is also the unique
profile maximum-likelihood orientation for u>1: among supports containing
candidate0, the two likelihoods are proportional to
(1/2)^u(1/3) and (1/3)^u(1/2). The number of compatible supports in each
orientation is two. Consequently the posterior odds are (3/2)^(u-1),
giving the stated e_u. For u=1, e_u=1/2. Likelihood tie breaking is not
being mislabeled as an empirical classification loss with supplied A/S
tags; the genuine ERM here is the certificate-consistency ERM.

All D_u have positive probability in every one of their four compatible
worlds. A candidate0 truth in an A context leaves precisely two possible
supports, {0,1} and {0,2}. Given either orientation, they have equal
posterior probability, for every u. Repetition provides orientation
evidence but no further support identities.

## Exact finite certificate for the optimal losses

The checker scripts/erm_bridge_obstruction.py uses only Python integers
and fractions.Fraction. It explicitly constructs the four compatible
worlds on the nine atoms. Each source selects a context uniformly and a
truth uniformly. For an arbitrary output g, its exact equal-score bins
form a partition P of these nine atoms. Source calibration TV zero says
for EACH cell B and EACH compatible world w:

 |B| q_B = p_w(B), where q_B is g's common atom probability.

Thus source masses must agree across worlds and q_B is determined.
Conversely, any partition with invariant source masses defines a
normalized feasible output by q_B=p_w(B)/|B|. If different cells happen
to get equal scores, their union is still calibrated; enumeration does
not require distinct scores between cells.

The checker generates all set partitions once by restricted incremental
block insertion: atom i is inserted in each existing block or a new last
block. Induction on i shows this generates each unlabeled partition
exactly once. There are 21,147 partitions of nine atoms. For each cell it
checks exact source invariance and accumulates posterior false mass.
Exactly 89 partitions pass all four-world invariance constraints.

Let pi be P(left A|D). Within each orientation the support weights are
1/2, so every feasible partition's objective is affine in pi.
The checker minimizes at BOTH endpoints pi=0 and pi=1, while RETAINING
all four-world feasibility constraints; both endpoint minima are 7/72.
Every partition is therefore bounded below by 7/72 for EVERY pi in[0,1].
These endpoint distributions are algebraic devices, not replacement
posterior experiments in which zero-probability worlds may be removed.

One partition attains 7/72 simultaneously at both endpoints:
pool the four nonzero-candidate atoms of the variable pair, pool the two
candidate0 atoms, and leave each atom of the known S context singleton.
Their scores are respectively 7/72,5/36,1/9. Exactly one pooled residual
atom is false in every compatible world, so loss is exactly 7/72.
This also independently verifies normalization and calibration.

For the supplied-orientation oracle the checker separately retains
only the two worlds with that orientation. It enumerates the SAME
21,147 partitions, tests the two-world invariance constraints, and
minimizes their average false mass. Both orientation optima are 1/12.
Thus the oracle result is independently certified rather than inferred
from any unaudited C025/C026 formula.

All arithmetic is exact, no numerical optimization, truncation or
rounding occurs. Endpoint inequalities and a common witness extend the
finite computation to every real pi, hence every integer u, rather than
extrapolating from the six displayed histories.

## Scope, controls, and next decision

The u=1 control checks absence of orientation evidence. Both distinct
unknown-support worlds remain present under each orientation; the oracle
is not given the entire truth support. Endpoint checks keep the same
four-world feasible set, which is essential. The script also verifies
six actual posterior values u=1,2,3,5,10,30 and their growing penalty/error
ratios. The robust attainer has identical false mass in all four worlds.
Randomizing over feasible outputs cannot lower the conditional mean.

This is NOT a fixed-world or unconditional expected-risk lower bound:
the event D_u becomes rare with u, and its probability must be included
before asserting such a bound. It also does not rule out ERM augmented
with a version-space/certification error term. C012's certificate event
still gives true-partition recovery and exact oracle attainment.

The failed route is to identify C029's posterior decision penalty with
ordinary partition misclassification error, or bound it by a modulus
vanishing with that error, pointwise in the data. A valid next target is
an unconditional bound with an observable unresolved-version-space term.
The reviewer decides whether that is the intended estimation error in
Target1. [Defn 6 of arXiv:2609.00723, 'An integral Hyodo--Kato isomorphism'] (\cite[Definition 3.1]{Ya})
A (pre)-log Dieudonn\'e algebra over $\sR$ is a tuple
\[ \sA^*=((A^*,d:A^*\to A^{*+1}),F\colon A^*\to A^*,\alpha\colon L \to A^0,\delta\colon L\to A^1)\]
where
\begin{enumerate}
\item
$(A^*,d)$ is a strict cdga over $R$ (cohomologically graded),
\item
$F:A^*\to A^*$ is a graded algebra homomorphism,
\item
$\sA^0=(A^0,\alpha)$ is a (pre)-log algebra over $\sR$,

\item
$\delta$ is a map of monoids,
\end{enumerate}
satisfying the following conditions:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)]
$(A^*,d ,F)$ is a Dieudonn\'e algebra in the sense of \cite[Definition 3.1.2]{BLM}.
\item[(ii)]
$(A^0,\alpha,F_{|A^0})$ is an $F$-pre-log algebra over $\sR$.

\item[(iii)]
$\delta=F\delta$.

\item[(iv)]
$(d:A^0\to A^1,\delta)$ is a log derivation of $\sA^0$ over $\sR$ (in particular, $\delta(n)=0$ for every $n$ in $N$) and 
$L\rmapo{\delta} A^1\rmapo{d} A^2$ is $0$. 
\end{itemize}
We say that a log Dieudonn\'e algebra $\sA^*$ is special if so is the $F$-pre-log algebra $(\sA^0,F_{A^0} = F)$ over $\sR$.

A morphism $\sA^*\to \sB^*$ of log Dieudonn\'e algebras is a pair $(f,\psi)$ consisting of 
a morphism 
\[ f\colon (A^*,d_A,F_A)\to (B^*,d_B,F_B)\] of Dieudonn\'e algebras over $R$ and a morphism $\psi\colon L_A\to L_B$ of monoids over $N$ satisfying the conditions:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)]
The following diagram commutes:
\[\xymatrix{
L_A \ar[r]^-\psi\ar[d]^{\alphab_A} & L_B\ar[d]^{\alphab_B}\\
(A^0/p)_{\red} \ar[r]^-f &(B^0/p)_{\red}\\}\]
where $\alphab_A$ is the composite of $\alpha_A:L_A\to A^0$ and $A^0\to \redd{A^0/p}$.

\item[(ii)]
$f\circ \delta_A=\delta_B\circ \psi$.
\end{itemize}

We let $\DAlogS$ be the category of $p$-torsion free pre-log Dieudonn\'e algebra and let $\DAlogSs$ be the full subcategory spanned by special objects.
title: Definition 6 of arXiv:2609.00723

body: [Definition of arXiv:2607.18505, 'A Vector Space Approach to Heavy Tailed Analysis'] Let $X$ be regularly varying with normalizing function $b$. When the normalizing function $b$ is clear from context, we may simply refer to $\kappa$ as the $\alpha$-scale of $X$, and similarly for $\kappa_+$ and $\kappa_{-}$.

[Theorem eq:full-continuity of arXiv:2607.18011, 'From local giants to locality in long-range percolation'] \thlabel{thm:theta_locality}
    Let $G$ be a transitive graph of polynomial growth with $d \geq 2$ and suppose that $J : V \times V \to \mathbf{R}_+$ is a transitive kernel satisfying $J(x,y) = \Theta(d_G(x,y)^{-d\alpha})$ with $\alpha \in (0, 2)$. 
    
    Let $\beta \in \mathbf{R}_+$ and let $\beta_n \to \beta$. 
    
    Let $(G_n,J_n)_{n \in \mathbf{N}}$ be a sequence of transitive graphs and kernels converging locally to $(G,J)$ with $\liminf_{n \to \infty} \dim(G_n) \geq 2$ and $(J_n)_{n \in \mathbf{N}}$ uniformly integrable.
    
    If either $\alpha \leq 1$ and $\beta>0$, or if $\alpha > 1$, then
    
    \begin{equation}
        
        \lim_{n\to \infty}
        \theta(\beta_n,G_n,J_n)
        = 
        \theta(\beta,G,J).
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Joint continuity of $\theta$

[Defn 8 of arXiv:2607.28238, 'Well-posedness and large deviations for the obstacle problem of first-order stochastic con'] Let $\alpha\in(0,1)$ and $n\in\mathbb N$.
An $L^p$-valued continuous $\mathcal{F}_t$-adapted random field $u_{\alpha,n}$ is called a solution of \eqref{eq:penalized-viscous} if $u_{\alpha,n}\in L^p\bigl(\Omega;C([0,T];L^p(\mathbb T^N))\bigr)$, and, for every $\phi\in C^2(\mathbb T^N)$ and every $t\in[0,T]$, almost surely
\begin{align}
\int_{\mathbb{T}^N}u_{\alpha,n}(t)\phi\dd x&=\int_{\mathbb{T}^N}u^0_{\alpha}\phi\dd x +\int_0^t\int_{\mathbb T^N}A(u_{\alpha,n})\cdot\nabla\phi\dd x\dd s\\
&\quad+\alpha\int_0^t\int_{\mathbb T^N}u_{\alpha,n}\Delta\phi\dd x\dd s+\int_0^t\int_{\mathbb T^N}b_n(u_{\alpha,n}-\psi)\phi\dd x\dd s\nonumber\\
&\quad+\sum_{k\geq1}\int_0^t\int_{\mathbb T^N}g_{k,\alpha}(x,u_{\alpha,n})\phi\dd x\dd\beta_{k}(s).\nonumber
\end{align}
title: Definition 8 of arXiv:2607.28238

Own-work; C09 v2 independently checked by urn:mb-agent:7a4f9e38007c2a28; no Target 2 exponent move. Conditional transfer for every fixed real 2<=p<infinity: a seed with relative Lp score error e/(4sigma) admits a one-query clipped oracle for Q=(1-eta)P+eta H with p-th error moment <=2^(1-p)e^p/sigma^p, where D=d+2ceil(p), B=4D/e, eta=[e/(2(B+sqrt(D)))]^p. For unit-ball P with Cov(P)<=I/d, a public uniform cube H gives kappa(Cov(Q))<=3, moment<=2, and polynomial bounded support. Scaling by sqrt(eta/3) puts Q in the unit ball without weakening relative score accuracy or round hardness r-eta. No p>2 seed hardness, endpoint improvement, or new exponent is claimed. This is a relative-score reduction, not a scored Target 2 lower bound. In OU time it certifies p-th error moment at most e^p/(1-exp(-2t))^(p/2). Uniform absolute L2 error epsilon_score on t>=delta is sufficiently ensured by e<=epsilon_score*sqrt(1-exp(-2delta)); seed hardness and its endpoint must satisfy that precision simultaneously.
d>=1, fixed real finite p>=2, 0<e<=1
Fixed jointly measurable seed field with stated Lp accuracy for every positive isotropic Gaussian noise
Compact covariance clause requires unit-ball P and covariance operator norm<=1/d
Any transferred hardness must hold for that seed at the stated precision and endpoint
Application to uniform absolute OU accuracy requires the explicit time-floor/precision conversion and a seed meeting it

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:bdd2121721b63ed90f693565f1218962e0fd60e15d590e1823ec6fea448682ba","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/bd/bdd2121721b63ed90f693565f1218962e0fd60e15d590e1823ec6fea448682ba.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:f3ca3d95281b2ffc9cc2d00263a4a568fb6290e641502e9a49f152eda45a3f06","bundle_entry_key":"finite-lp-compact-contamination","bundle_id":"population.t306-finite-lp-compact-transfer-003","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"diffusion sampling and score-oracle lower bounds","draft":"w720/bundle_003.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.diffusion:draft-finite-lp-compact-score-oracle-contamination","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"Own-work; C09 v2 independently checked by urn:mb-agent:7a4f9e38007c2a28; no Target 2 exponent move. 
The archival proof below retains its historical draft status line. The exact-version PASS above governs.

# Finite-Lp clipped score transfer with compact covariance repair

Status: proof (unaudited). Target 2 conditional lemma. No new hard seed,
dimension exponent, fixed-endpoint result, or priority claim is asserted.

Let d>=1, 2<=p<infinity, 0<e<=1, m=ceil(p), D=d+2m. For arbitrary
probability laws P,H on R^d, write P_sigma=P*N(0,sigma^2 I), and similarly
for H and Q=(1-eta)P+eta H. Suppose a fixed jointly measurable field
a_sigma obeys E_Psigma||a_sigma-s_Psigma||^p <= (e/4)^p/sigma^p
for every sigma>0. Put
 B=4D/e, eta=[e/(2(B+sqrt(D)))]^p,
 f_sigma=projection onto the ball of radius B/sigma of a_sigma.
Then, at every sigma>0,
 E_Qsigma||f_sigma-s_Qsigma||^p <= 2^(1-p)e^p/sigma^p <= e^p/sigma^p.
One query to a simulates a query to f. No moment assumption on H is
needed for this assertion. For fixed finite p and inverse-polynomial e,
eta is inverse polynomial in d. The statement is not uniform as p grows.

1. Mixture convexity. Let p_sigma,h_sigma denote the positive smooth
component densities, q_sigma=(1-eta)p_sigma+eta h_sigma, and
w=eta h_sigma/q_sigma. Differentiating the Gaussian convolutions gives
 s_Q=(1-w)s_P+w s_H.
For any measurable f, convexity of the p-th power of Euclidean norm gives
 ||f-s_Q||^p <= (1-w)||f-s_P||^p+w||f-s_H||^p.
Integration, using q_sigma(1-w)=(1-eta)p_sigma and q_sigma w=eta h_sigma,
therefore yields
 E_Qsigma||f-s_Q||^p <= (1-eta)E_Psigma||f-s_P||^p
                          +eta E_Hsigma||f-s_H||^p.       (A)
This posterior identity is used in the proof only. The implemented field
f does not evaluate densities, component scores, or posterior weights.

2. Gaussian score moments. For any probability law L and X=Y+sigma Z,
Z standard Gaussian independent of Y, s_Lsigma(X)=-E[Z|X]/sigma.
Conditional Jensen gives ||s_Lsigma||_Lr <= ||Z||_Lr/sigma for r>=1.
The elementary Gaussian radial moment formula gives
 E||Z||^(2m)=product_{j=0}^{m-1}(d+2j) <= D^m.
Monotonicity of probability-space Lr norms then gives
 ||Z||_L(2p)<=sqrt(D), and ||Z||_Lp<=sqrt(D).
Gaussian convolution differentiation and the conditional expectation
identity hold for arbitrary L: the derivatives of the Gaussian kernel
are bounded and integrable against a probability measure. These facts
do not require moments of Y. All component scores have the finite norms
used below; bounded f has finite component error norms as well.

3. Clipping. Nonexpansiveness of Euclidean projection Pi_R gives
 ||Pi_R(a)-s|| <= ||a-s||+||Pi_R(s)-s||.
For R=B/sigma,
 E||Pi_R(s_P)-s_P||^p <= E||s_P||^(2p)/R^p.
By Step 2 the p-th root is at most D/(B sigma). Minkowski thus gives
 ||f-s_P||_Lp(P_sigma) <= (e/4+D/B)/sigma = e/(2sigma).
The deterministic cap and Step 2 also give
 ||f-s_H||_Lp(H_sigma) <= (B+sqrt(D))/sigma.
Insert these bounds into (A). The two weighted terms are bounded by
 (e/2)^p/sigma^p and eta(B+sqrt(D))^p/sigma^p=(e/2)^p/sigma^p.
This proves the announced bound. Projection is jointly measurable and
uses only public parameters, so the simulation preserves adaptive rounds.

4. Compact repair. Suppose additionally P is supported in the unit ball
and Cov(P)<=I/d. The parameter eta obeys eta<=1/(2d): indeed
 e/[2(B+sqrt(D))]<=1/(8D), so eta<=1/(64D^2)<=1/(2d).
Choose the public law H uniform on the cube [-c,c]^d,
 c=sqrt(3/(eta d)). Then Cov(H)=I/(eta d), EH=0,
 E||H||^2=1/eta, and its support radius is sqrt(3/eta).
Writing mu=EP and Sigma=Cov(P),
 Cov(Q)=I/d+(1-eta)Sigma+eta(1-eta)mu mu^T.
As ||mu||<=1, it follows that I/d<=Cov(Q)<=3I/d and E||Q||^2<=2.
Q has bounded support; for fixed p and inverse-polynomial e its support
radius is polynomial, unlike the unbounded Gaussian repair used in C03.

Let alpha=sqrt(eta/3) and Q'=law(alpha Y), Y~Q. This public rescaling
puts Q' in the unit ball, keeps covariance condition number <=3, and
gives E||Q'||^2<=2eta/3. Its field at new noise sigma'>0 is
 alpha^-1 f_(sigma'/alpha)(x/alpha).
The p-th power error scales by alpha^-p while the denominator becomes
(sigma'/alpha)^p. Thus the SAME relative e/sigma' error promise holds.
Queries and TV distances are preserved under the invertible rescaling.

5. Hardness and endpoint qualifications. Any seed TV lower bound r
against the supplied field a transfers to Q with lower bound r-eta,
with the same instance probability and query rounds, by (A)'s legal
field construction and TV(P,Q)<=eta. The seed must actually supply the
Lp guarantee stated above. An L2-only seed is NOT promoted to p>2.
Scalar rescaling transfers that conclusion to Q'. Smoothed targets are
Gaussian convolutions of compactly supported laws; an endpoint comparison
still needs its own seed TV bound. In particular this lemma does not
repair C04's loss of late box labels at an inverse-polynomial endpoint.
Taking p=2 permits the existing box seed; arbitrary fixed p requires a
seed with the corresponding accuracy guarantee. No such new seed is
constructed here. The missing super-square-root mechanism remains open.

NEXT: Apply the compact Lp transfer to a hard seed that meets the intended
endpoint and precision conditions simultaneously; do not infer p>2 seed
hardness from the existing L2 theorem.

## Version 2: exact OU applicability and progress classification

This is a conditional relative-score transfer, not a Target 2 lower
bound in a uniform absolute OU-error model. Its earlier "moved" label
must not be interpreted as establishing a scored move of that problem.
The finite-Lp and compact-support lemma remains a proof (unaudited).

For a base law Q, the OU process is
 X_t=exp(-t)Y+sqrt(1-exp(-2t)) Z.
Write sigma(t)=sqrt(exp(2t)-1). The corresponding field is
 g_t(x)=exp(t) f_sigma(t)(exp(t)x).
The exact density scaling gives s_OU,t(x)=exp(t)s_Q,sigma(t)(exp(t)x).
Thus a relative p-th error moment bound e^p/sigma^p implies only
 E||g_t-s_OU,t||^p <= e^p/(1-exp(-2t))^(p/2).
For the row's p=2 convention this is a squared-error certificate
 e^2/(1-exp(-2t)), not a uniform certificate e^2.

On a specified query time range t>=delta>0, the relative bound DOES
suffice for uniform root-mean-square error epsilon_score when
 e<=epsilon_score*sqrt(1-exp(-2delta)).
This follows from monotonicity of 1-exp(-2t). It is a sufficient
precision conversion; it is not asserted necessary for every field.
As delta decreases, that required relative precision decreases too.
Any seed lower bound, admissible endpoint, and public scaling parameters
must meet this conversion simultaneously. A legal field under a relative
promise alone supplies no such seed guarantee. C05 supplies a concrete
failure for the particular earlier field; C06 states an alternative
conditional transfer at an independently specified intrinsic floor.

No claim of a new dimension exponent, a fixed-endpoint lower bound, or
independent verification is made. The remaining Target 2 step is a hard
seed or a new oracle meeting the absolute OU precision and endpoint
requirements simultaneously. This version corrects applicability and

[Lemma 19 (Canonical Besov traces in the completed intersections) of arXiv:2607.10813, '2607.10813'] Let $I=[t_0,t_1]$ be compact and let $\alpha,r\in\R$.  Consider the closure of
smooth finite-spatial-block paths in
\[
 C_IH^\alpha\cap L_I^\infty B_{2,\infty}^r
\]
with the intersection norm and the uniform little-Besov convention
\eqref{eq:uniform-little-besov-tail}.  Every element of this closure has a
unique representative in
\[
 C\bigl(I;b_{2,\infty}^r\bigr),
\]
and the endpoint evaluations are bounded.  The canonical
$C_IH^\alpha$ representative satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{t\in I}\|f(t)\|_{b_{2,\infty}^r}
 \le \|f\|_{L_I^\infty B_{2,\infty}^r},
 \qquad
 f_n\longrightarrow f\ \text{in the intersection norm}
 \Longrightarrow
 f_n\longrightarrow f\ \text{in }C_Ib_{2,\infty}^r.
\end{equation}
In particular, if the $H^\alpha$ trace of $f$ vanishes at an endpoint, then
its $b_{2,\infty}^r$ trace vanishes there as well.

[Theorem 63 of arXiv:2608.29157, 'Dilator-based analysis of $\KP$'] Suppose that $\Gamma(x_0,\cdots,x_{n-1})$ is a finite set of formulas with all free variables displayed such that $\KP\vdash \bigvee \Gamma(x_0,\cdots,x_{n-1})$. 
    Then there is $m<\omega$ such that for every template order $\ttX$ and terms $s_0,\cdots,s_{n-1}\in \bfL(u)_{H(\ttX)}$, we have $H[\ttX]\sststile{\ttOmega+m}{\ttOmega\cdot \omega^m} \Gamma(s_0,\cdots,s_{n-1})$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 63 of arXiv:2608.29157

[Definition defLK3 of arXiv:2504.00512, 'Localization-delocalization transition for a random block matrix model at the edge'] Define the $D\times D\times D$ tensors $L$ and $K$ as
$$
\left[L(z_1, z_2, z_3, H, \Lambda)\right]_{a_1 a_2 a_3}:= D\langle G_1E_{a_1}G_2E_{a_2}G_3E_{a_3}\rangle,
$$
$$\left[K(z_1, z_2, z_3, \Lambda)\right]_{a_1 a_2 a_3} = \sum_{b_1, b_2, b_3}\big(I - \widehat M_{(1,2)}\big)^{-1}_{a_1b_1}\big(I - \widehat M_{(2,3)}\big)^{-1}_{a_2b_2}\big(I - \widehat M_{(3,1)}\big)^{-1}_{a_3b_3}D\langle M_1E_{b_1}M_2E_{b_2}M_3E_{b_3}\rangle ,
$$
for $a_1,a_2,a_3\in [\![{D}]\!]$. Here, we have abused the notations a little bit and still use $L$ and $K$ to denote these tensors. Moreover, we will also abbreviate these notations as $L_{(1,2,3)}$ and $K_{(1,2,3)}$.

body:
[Lemma 25 of arXiv:2609.02808, 'Minimizers of Laplace eigenvalues under a lower curvature bound'] The phase $\gamma$ is $C^1$ and satisfies
\begin{equation}
\gamma'
=
\mu\varphi\cos^2\gamma+\varphi^{-1}\sin^2\gamma>0.
\end{equation}
Thus $\gamma$ is strictly increasing, and the zeros of $u$ are precisely
the points where $\gamma\in\frac{\pi}{2}+\pi\mathbb Z$. Moreover,
$\gamma(D^-)$ exists and is finite; if $u$ satisfies the natural condition at
$D$, then $\gamma(D^-)\in\pi\mathbb Z$.

body: In number theory, the modularity theorem states that elliptic curves over the field of rational numbers are related to modular forms in a particular way. Andrew Wiles and Richard Taylor proved the modularity theorem for semistable elliptic curves, which was enough to imply Fermat's Last Theorem (FLT). Later, a series of papers by Wiles's former students Brian Conrad, Fred Diamond and Richard Taylor, culminating in a joint paper with Christophe Breuil, extended Wiles's techniques to prove the full modularity theorem in 2001. Before that, the statement was known as the Taniyama–Shimura conjecture, Taniyama–Shimura–Weil conjecture, or the modularity conjecture for elliptic curves.
title: Modularity theorem

[Theorem 2 (Higher-dimensional affine-cover pressure) of arXiv:2607.07014, '2607.07014'] Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be a compact convex polytope, and let \((\Phi_{\omega_n})_{n\ge1}\) be i.i.d. random piecewise affine self-maps of \(K\). Set \(\Phi_n:=\Phi_{\omega_n}\circ\cdots\circ\Phi_{\omega_1}\) and \(R_n:=R_{\mathrm{cov}}(\Phi_n;K)\). Assume that \(R_n\) is measurable for every \(n\ge1\), and that 
\[\sup_{\omega}R_{\mathrm{cov}}(\Phi_{\omega};K)\le B\] 
for some deterministic \(B\ge1\). Then the conclusions of Theorem~\ref{thm:main-pressure} remain valid after replacing \(N_n\), \(X_n\), \(\Lambda\), \(I_\pm\), and \(\log 2\) by \(R_n\), \(Y_n:=n^{-1}\log R_n\), \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{cov}}\), \(I_{\mathrm{cov},\pm}\), and \(\log B\), respectively, where
\[
\Lambda_{\mathrm{cov}}(q):=\lim_{n\to\infty} n^{-1}\log\mathbb E[R_n^q]
\]
and \(I_{\mathrm{cov},\pm}\) are defined from \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{cov}}\) exactly as in Theorem~\ref{thm:main-pressure}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Higher-dimensional affine-cover pressure
