body:
[Lemma 12 (Harmonic dimension and directional energy) of arXiv:2608.24007, '2608.24007'] The dimension of $\mathcal V_{r,K}$ is
\[
    H_{r,K}
    =\binom{K+r-1}{r}-\binom{K+r-3}{r-2}.
\]
Let $P_{r,K}$ be orthogonal projection onto $\mathcal V_{r,K}$.  For every
unit vector $q\in\mathbb R^K$,
\[
    \left\|P_{r,K}h_r(q^\top z)\right\|_{L^2}^2
    =\alpha_{r,K},
\]
where, writing $r=2m$ or $r=2m+1$,
\[
    \alpha_{2m,K}
    =\prod_{j=0}^{m-1}
      \frac{K+2j-1}{K+2m+2j-2},
\]
and
\[
    \alpha_{2m+1,K}
    =\prod_{j=0}^{m-1}
      \frac{K+2j-1}{K+2m+2j}.
\]
For every fixed $r$, $H_{r,K}=\Theta_r(K^r)$ and
$\alpha_{r,K}\to1$ as $K\to\infty$.

body:
[Theorem thm:honest-region of arXiv:2608.20295, 'Physical-Support Confidence Sets for Highly Coherent Dictionaries'] Under Assumption~(ass:frozen-shell of the paper) and the calibration coverage condition
in Equation~(equation eq:training-rectangle of the paper), the totalized correspondence
$\widehat{\mathfrak C}_{q,r,s}^{p}$ is measurable, nonempty, and
compact-valued. Uniformly over $\mathfrak P^p_{q,r}(s)$,
\begin{equation}
\mathbb P_{p_\star,\nu_\star,D_\star}^N
\left[
\mathbb P_{\mu_\star,\sigma_\star}^T
\left\{
    \vartheta_\star
    \in
    \widehat{\mathfrak C}_{q,r,s}^{p}
    \mid Y_{1:N}
\right\}
\ge1-\alpha_T
\right]
\ge1-\alpha_D.

\end{equation}
Consequently, by independence of the calibration and deployment experiments,
with
\[
    \alpha
    =
    1-(1-\alpha_D)(1-\alpha_T),
\]
\begin{equation}
\inf_{\xi\in\mathfrak P^p_{q,r}(s)}
\mathbb P_\xi^{N,T}
\left\{
    \vartheta(\xi)
    \in
    \widehat{\mathfrak C}_{q,r,s}^{p}
\right\}
\ge1-\alpha.

\end{equation}

For $N$ above the fixed block threshold of the robust calibration-moment
construction, define
\begin{equation}
\rho_N(s)
=
C\left[
    (s\wedge\epsilon_N)
    +
    \left(s\wedge\frac{\epsilon_N}{s}\right)
    +
    \left(s\wedge\frac{\epsilon_N}{s^2}\right)
\right].

\end{equation}
Any two dictionaries retained by the same nonempty calibration region have
quotient-dictionary distance at most $\rho_N(s)$.  If
$\epsilon_N\le CN^{-1/2}$, then
\begin{equation}
    \rho_N(s)
    \le
    C\left(
        s\wedge\frac{1}{\sqrt N\,s^2}
    \right).
    
\end{equation}
Below the block threshold, retaining the full compact shell yields the same
order after adjustment of fixed constants.

For every realization,
\begin{align}
\operatorname{diam}_{\mathrm{pr}}
\left(
    \widehat{\mathfrak C}_{q,r,s}^{p}
\right)
\le{}&
C\rho_N(s)
\notag\\
&+
Cs\,
\mathbf 1
\left\{
    2\tau_{T,q}\ge m_S(\rho_N(s))
\right\}
\notag\\
&+
C\,
\mathbf 1
\left\{
    2\tau_{T,q}\ge m_G(\rho_N(s))
\right\}.

\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let P_X be an input probability law and P_F a law on measurable functions F:X->{-1,1}, with measurable evaluation. Draw F and F_prime independently from P_F. Draw X_1,...,X_m iid from P_X, independently of both functions, where m>=1 is an integer; each sampled function is held fixed throughout the batch. Define CP_infinity = E_{F,F_prime}[(E_X F(X)*F_prime(X))^2]. Define CP_m=E[((1/m) sum_{i=1}^m F(X_i)*F_prime(X_i))^2]. Then CP_m=1/m+(1-1/m)*CP_infinity. Equivalently, for K(x,x_prime)=E_F[F(x)*F(x_prime)], CP_infinity=E_{X,X_prime}[K(X,X_prime)^2], with X,X_prime independent under P_X. Thus0<=CP_infinity<=1, CP_m>=1/m and CP_1=1. No balanced-label assumption is needed for these identities.
Binary-valued functions; measurable evaluation and the stated probability laws.
The input batch is iid and independent of two iid function draws.
The same function pair is reused throughout the batch; it is not redrawn per input.

\]

[Satz thm:HigherOrderIndep of arXiv:2507.08692, 'Some notes on higher order concentration of measure'] Let $X$ be a random vector with independent components, $f: \mathcal{X} \to {\mathbb R}$ a measurable function satisfying $f = f(X) \in L^\infty(\IP)$, ${\mathbb E} f(X) = 0$ and $d \in {\mathbb N}$.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item Assuming that $\norm{\mathfrak{h}^{(j)} f}_{\mathrm{op},1} \le 1$ for all $j=1,\ldots,d-1$ and $\norm{\mathfrak{h}^{(d)} f}_{\mathrm{op},\infty} \le 1$, it holds that
        \[
        {\mathbb E} \exp\Big\{c |f(X)|^{2/d} \Big\} \le 2,
        \]
        where a possible choice of the constant $c$ is given by
        \[
        c = \frac{(\sqrt{2}-1)^2}{64 \kappa e}.
        \]
        \item For any $t\ge 0$, it holds that
        \[
        {\mathbb P}(|f(X)| \ge t)\le
        2 \exp\Big\{- \frac{C}{d^2} \min\Big(\min_{j=1, \ldots,d-1} \Big(\frac{t}{\norm{\mathfrak{h}^{(j)} f}_{\mathrm{op},1}}\Big)^{2/j}, \Big(\frac{t}{\norm{\mathfrak{h}^{(d)} f}_{\mathrm{op},\infty}}\Big)^{2/d}\Big)\Big\},
        \]
    where a possible choice of the constant $C$ is given by
    \[
    C = \frac{\log(2)}{16 \kappa e^2} > \frac{1}{217}.
    \]
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Coro 16 of arXiv:2605.23292, 'Second-order Poincaré inequalities and localization on the Poisson space'] (normal approximation for the sum of power weighted edge lengths of the $k$-nearest neighbor graph in $d$-dimensional hyperbolic space)
We work in the setup of Theorem~\ref{thm:hyperbolic}. Let $X_\la=W_\la=B(p,\la) \subset \hyp$ by a ball of radius $\la\geq2$ and $p\in\hyp$ a fixed point. Let $\mathcal{P}_\la$ be a Poisson measure of intensity $\nu$ on $W_\la$ and let $k\text{NN}(\P_\la)$ be the  undirected $k$-nearest neighbor graph on 
$\P_\la$. For $\alpha \sg 0$ we consider the sum of power weighted edge lengths
\[
H_\la^\alpha := \sum_{\text{edges } e \in k\text{NN}(\P_\la)} \text{length}(e)^\alpha.
\]
Then the functional $H_\la^\alpha$ satisfies \eqref{dKhyp} and \eqref{dWhyp} with $\nu(W_\la) \leq \Gamma_d e^{(d-1)\la}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Denote by $T'$ the copy of $T$ without the vertex $\partial$ and where the edges $\{x,\partial\}$ and $\{z,\partial\}$ have been merged into a single edge $\{x,z\}$.   \[
    \sum_{y\in\mathbb{Z}^d} p_{\varphi_y}(T) \lesssim p_\varphi(T').
  \]

[Lemma 11 (Endpoint reduction and contact identities) of arXiv:2608.06523, 'On the Gardner Transition in the Ising Pure $p$-Spin Glass II'] For the measure in \eqref{eq:mu},
\begin{equation}
 \partial_x\Phi_\mu(x,q)=\tanh x,\qquad
 \partial_{xx}\Phi_\mu(x,q)=\cosh^{-2}x.
 
\end{equation}
For every smooth test function $\varphi$ such that
$\varphi,\varphi',\varphi''$ have at most exponential growth and which
does not depend on $m$ or $\xi'(q)$,
\begin{equation}
 \E[\varphi(M(q))e^{W_\mu(q)}]
 =\frac{\E\!\left[
 \varphi(\sqrt{\xi'(q)}z)\cosh^m(\sqrt{\xi'(q)}z)\right]}
 {\E[\cosh^m(\sqrt{\xi'(q)}z)]},
 \qquad \E e^{W_\mu(q)}=1.
 
\end{equation}
At a stationary marginal point,
\begin{align}
 \Gamma_\mu(q)
 &=\E[\tanh^2(M(q))e^{W_\mu(q)}]=q,
 \\
 q&=(p-1)\xi'(q)
 \E[\cosh^{-4}(M(q))e^{W_\mu(q)}],
 \\
 \E[\cosh^{-2}(M(q))e^{W_\mu(q)}]&=1-q,
 \\
 \E[\cosh^{-4}(M(q))e^{W_\mu(q)}]
 &=\frac{q}{(p-1)\xi'(q)}.
 
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Endpoint reduction and contact identities

[Lem 24 ({See \cite[Theorem 4.33) of arXiv:2609.00723, 'An integral Hyodo--Kato isomorphism'] {Ya}}] For every $\sA=(A,L)\in \mathrm{PreLog}_{(k,N)}$,

[Definition def:vary of arXiv:2411.04773, 'Meeting of squared Bessel flow lines and application to the skew Brownian motion'] Let $\mathcal W$ be a white noise with respect to some filtration $\mathcal F$. Let $\overline{\delta}$ be a drift function with respect to $\mathcal F$. We call a collection of continuous processes $\mathcal S=(\mathcal S_{r,x}(a),\, x\ge r)_{r\in {\mathbb R},a\ge 0}$ a ${\rm BESQ}(\overline{\delta})$ flow driven by $\mathcal W$ if 
   
    (1) The restriction of $\mathcal S$ to each $A_i$ is a ${\rm BESQ}^{\delta_i}$ flow driven by $\mathcal W$.

    (2) The regularity conditions of Definition (def:BESQflow of the paper) hold.
 

If $E$ is a (possibly random) Borel set, we call $\rm BESQ(\overline{\delta})$ flow killed on $E$ the flow obtained from the $\rm BESQ(\overline{\delta})$ flow by absorbing the flow line $\mathcal S_{r,\cdot}(a)$ at $0$ at time $\inf\{x \in E\cap (r,\infty) \,:\, \mathcal S_{r,x}(a)=0\}$.

 If $E={\mathbb R}$, we will simply say that $\mathcal S$ is a killed  $\rm BESQ(\overline{\delta})$ flow. We call general  $\rm BESQ(\overline{\delta})$ flow a $\rm BESQ(\overline{\delta})$ flow or a  killed $\rm BESQ(\overline{\delta})$ flow.

body:
[Theorem 11 of arXiv:2609.03191, 'On lifting representations and actions on curves of the metacyclic groups $C_{p^s}\rtimes '] Let $V$ be a $k[H]$-module. Let $R$ be such that it contains $R_s$. Let $t\in\mathbb Z\setminus p\mathbb Z$. Let $o$ be the order of $[t]_{p^s}\in (\mathbb Z/p^s\mathbb Z)^{\times}$. Then the following properties hold.

\medskip
{\bf (1)} The following statements are equivalent.

\medskip\noindent
{\bf (1.a)} The $k[H]$-module $V$ is cyclic.

\smallskip\noindent
{\bf (1.b)} The $k[H]$-module $V$ is indecomposable.

\smallskip\noindent
{\bf (1.c)} The $k[H]$-module $V$ is strongly indecomposable.

\smallskip\noindent
{\bf (1.d)} We have $\imath_V\in\{0,1\}$.

\smallskip\noindent
{\bf (1.e)} Each lift $\mathcal V$ of $V$ to $R$ is cyclic.

\smallskip\noindent
{\bf (1.f)} Each lift $\mathcal V$ of $V$ to $R$ is cyclic and strongly indecomposable.

\medskip
{\bf (2)} The $k[H]$-module $V$ has a lift $\mathcal H$ to $R$ which is an end-hull of $V$ and a direct sum of cyclic $R[H]$-modules. Moreover, if $\jmath_V=0$, then we can also assume that $r_{\mathcal H}=0$.

\smallskip
{\bf (3)} Suppose that $V$ is cyclic. Let $\mathcal V_1$ and $\mathcal V_2$ be two lifts of $V$. Then the $R[H]$-modules $\mathcal V_1$ and $\mathcal V_2$ are isomorphic if and only if the $B[H]$-modules $\mathcal V_1\otimes_R B$ and $\mathcal V_2\otimes_R B$ are isomorphic.

\smallskip
{\bf (4)} The $k[H]$-modules $V$ and $V^{(t)}$ are isomorphic.

\smallskip
{\bf (5)} The following statements are equivalent.

\medskip\noindent
{\bf (5.a)} There exists a lift $\mathcal V$ of $V$ to $R$ which is $t$-invariant and a direct sum of cyclic $R[H]$-modules (resp.\ which is $t$-invariant and a direct sum of cyclic $R[H]$-modules with $r_{\mathcal V^H}=0$).

\smallskip\noindent
{\bf (5.b)} For each $b\in\llbracket1,p^s\rrbracket\setminus o\llbracket1,\lfloor\frac{p^s}{t}\rfloor\rrbracket$ such that $\mu_V(b)\neq 0$, $\mu_V(b)$ is a sum of cardinals of orbits of the action of $[t]_{p^s}$ on $\mathcal P_b(\Xi_s)$ (resp.\ $\mathcal P_b(\Xi_s^{\ast})$), equivalently of subsets $\Phi$ of $\mathcal P_b(\Xi_s)$ (resp.\ $\mathcal P_b(\Xi_s^{\ast})$) with $[t]_{p^s}\cdot\Phi=\Phi$.

\medskip
{\bf (6)} Suppose that $p$ is odd, $[t]_{p^s}=[p^s-1]_{p^s}$ (equivalently, $o=2$) and $\dim_k(V)$ is even. Then $V$ has a lift to $R$ which is a direct sum of cyclic $R[H]$-modules and is $t$-invariant.

\medskip
{\bf (7)} Suppose that $p$ is odd, $[t]_{p^s}=[p^s-1]_{p^s}$, $\mu_V(d)$ is even for each odd $d\in\llbracket1,p^s\rrbracket$, and $\jmath_V=0$. Then $V$ has a lift $\mathcal V$ to $R$ which is a direct sum of cyclic $R[H]$-modules and is $t$-invariant with $r_{\mathcal V}=0$.

[Lemma 18 (Ricci quadratic estimate; cf.\ Lemma A.1 of \cite{Brendle2019}, Lemma 4.7 of \cite{Chen2024}) of arXiv:2608.26598, 'Pinching cones for positive isotropic curvature in dimensions seven and eight'] Let $0\le\zeta\le1$ and $0<\varrho\le1$, and let $H$ be a symmetric two-tensor whose largest
    eigenvalue is at most $\frac12\mathrm{tr}\,H$ and whose two smallest eigenvalues have sum at
    least $\frac{2(1-\zeta)}{n}\mathrm{tr}\,H$. Then, with
    $H^0=H-\frac1n\mathrm{tr}(H)\,\mathrm{id}$, every orthonormal pair $\{e_1,e_2\}$ satisfies
    \begin{equation}
        \frac{n-2}{n}\,\mathrm{tr}(H)\,\bigl(H_{11}+H_{22}\bigr)
        -\varrho\bigl((H^0)^2_{11}+(H^0)^2_{22}\bigr)
        \ge\frac{2}{n^2}\left((n-2)(1-\zeta)-2\zeta^2\varrho\,
        \frac{n^2-2n+2}{(n-2)^2}\right)\mathrm{tr}(H)^2.
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:supp-zero-proj of arXiv:2605.10491, 'Zero-couplings of infinite measures with cyclically monotone support and multivariate regu'] Let $\gamma \in \mathrm{M}_{0}(\reals^d\times\reals^d)$ and let $\mu = \varphi_1\gamma\in\mathrm{M}_{0}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ denote its left zero-marginal. Then $\operatorname{spt}\mu \subset\operatorname{spt}\phi_1\gamma= \operatorname{cl} (\operatorname{proj}_1 (\operatorname{spt} \gamma))$. 
    
	
	As a consequence, if $\operatorname{spt} \gamma \subset T$ for some $T \subset \reals^d\times\reals^d$, then $\operatorname{spt} \mu \subset \operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{dom} T)$.
	In particular, if $T$ is maximal monotone, then $\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{spt} \mu) \subset \operatorname{dom} T$.

[Theorem thm:Unique_loop_qversion of arXiv:2603.28520, 'The Supercritical Loop O(1) and Random Current Models: Uniqueness and Mixing'] Let $q\in \mathbb{N}_{\geq 2}$, $d\geq 2$ and $x>x_{slab}$. For any Gibbs measure $\ell^q_{\mathbb{Z}^d,x}$ of the $q$-flow model, there exists a weak limit $\phi_{\mathbb{Z}^d,p,q}$ of finite-volume random-cluster measures such that 
$$
\ell^q_{\mathbb{Z}^d,x}[\;\cdot\;]=\phi_{\mathbb{Z}^d,p,q}[\operatorname{UD}_{\omega}[\;\cdot\;]].
$$
In particular, whenever $x>x_{slab},$ there is a unique Gibbs measure for the $q$-flow model if and only if $\phi^1_{\mathbb{Z}^d,p,q}=\phi^0_{\mathbb{Z}^d,p,q}$.

DRAFT, proof (unaudited), T318-C3 version 2 sections 1 and 4; no priority claim. Let p/d->psi>0, let f_j be independent uniform vectors on the sphere of radius sqrt(d), and let g~N(0,I_d) be independent. Fix a globally Lipschitz activation rho with E rho(G)=0 and v=E rho(G)^2>0 for G~N(0,1). Define W_jk=f_j^T f_k/d and C_jk=E_g rho(f_j^T g/sqrt(d))rho(f_k^T g/sqrt(d)). With b=(E G rho(G))^2 and tau=v-b, C=tau I+bW+E where E_jj=0, |E_jk|<=tau|W_jk|^2 and E||E||_F^2<=3 tau^2 p(p-1)/[d(d+2)]. The Schur product contraction gives ||C||<=v||W||. Hence C has limiting empirical law law(tau+b MP_psi), since its resolvent trace differs from that of tau I+bW by at most ||E||_F/(sqrt(p) s^2) at every s>0. Operator-norm equivalence is not asserted. For variance-one centered ReLU rho(t)=sqrt(2 pi/(pi-1))[max(t,0)-1/sqrt(2 pi)], b=pi/[2(pi-1)], tau=(pi-2)/[2(pi-1)]. Its second Hermite coefficient square is 1/[2(pi-1)]. If e is the unit all-ones vector, E e^T E e >=(p-1)/[2(pi-1)d]; the uniformly bounded second moment makes e^T E e uniformly integrable, proving that ||E|| does not converge to zero in probability. The spectral-law comparison is sufficient for the weighted sample-covariance resolvent, even though this stronger operator approximation fails. All claims remain unaudited own-work drafts.

body: The nerve of a finite collection A of nonempty sets is the simplicial complex N(A) := {sigma : nonempty sigma subset of A with intersection over B in sigma of B nonempty}. If the sets are convex subsets of R^d (in the paper, the grains x + K of the union Z_W), the union is homotopy equivalent to the nerve (a variant of the Nerve Theorem, Edelsbrunner-Harer p. 76). For general sets contractibility of the intersections is not enough; the usual hypotheses are open sets, or closed convex sets.

The planar set C={(x,y): x>0 and |y-x^2|<1} is open, connected and unbounded, but contains no straight ray with nonzero direction. A ray with negative x direction exits x>0, a vertical ray exits the bounded vertical strip at its fixed x, and a ray with positive x direction has y-x^2 tending to minus infinity quadratically. This is a geometric counterexample to an unbounded-component implies straight-visibility inference; no permitted mirror configuration or reflected-ray trapping is asserted.
All hypotheses and scope restrictions in the statement apply.

Status: proofs written; w346 KEEP pending. Neither result constructs an all-ray trapping mirror configuration.

Lemma 1. Every unbounded open convex set C in R^d contains an unbounded straight ray starting at each x in C. Therefore, if a mirror-complement component is unbounded, open and convex, an origin in it has an unobstructed escaping launch direction and cannot have every reflected ray bounded.

Proof: choose r>0 with B(x,r) contained in C and y_k in C with |y_k-x| tending to infinity. A subsequence of d_k=(y_k-x)/|y_k-x| tends to a unit direction d. For fixed t>=0 and sufficiently large k, convexity gives a ball centered at x+t*d_k with radius (1-t/|y_k-x|)*r contained in C. Eventually this radius exceeds 3r/4 and the center is within r/4 of x+t*d, so B(x+t*d,r/2) is in C. This holds for every fixed t with the same subsequential direction d, proving the entire ray stays inside C. No collision occurs along it.

Lemma 2. C={(x,y): x>0 and |y-x^2|<1} is open, connected and unbounded but contains no unbounded straight ray.

Proof: (x,u)->(x,x^2+u) is a homeomorphism from (0,infinity) times (-1,1), proving the first three properties. For a ray (a+bt,c+dt), t>=0, with nonzero direction: b<0 eventually violates x>0; b=0 and d!=0 eventually violates the strip condition; b>0 makes y-x^2 a quadratic with leading coefficient -b^2, whose magnitude diverges. Thus all possible directions leave C in finite time.

This gives an explicit algebraic version of the previous spiral-corridor obstruction: unbounded connected vacancy alone does not supply a straight ray. The corridor is not represented as a permitted mirror arrangement, and absence of straight rays does not establish trapping of reflected rays. Convexity is a sufficient special-case condition, not a necessary one.

Checks: algebraic ray exit times for a finite angle grid, openness/connectedness via the explicit parametrization, and the nonconvex midpoint pair (1,1),(3,9), whose midpoint is outside C.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:c45fd394fe262eb3894826f9741ef2253d426113863b263010b82c5401db891e","revision_digest":"sha256:8346c5ed3122a405759e1e72e48b65973dc3861780d37f5f1bf21ab01e57b363","source_id":"owner:campaign:w336:P0007:parabolic-open-corridor-contains-no-infinite-ray","source_revision":"author-proof-2026-10-10; independent audit w346 pending","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The orthogonal polynomials with respect to $\mu$ are given by
$$P_k=c_k\begin{vmatrix}
M_0&M_1&\ldots&M_k\\
M_1&M_2&\ldots&M_{k+1}\\
\vdots&\vdots&&\vdots\\
M_{k-1}&M_k&\ldots&M_{2k-1}\\
1&x&\ldots&x^k
\end{vmatrix}$$
where $M_k=\int_\mathbb Rx^kd\mu(x)$ are the moments of $\mu$, and $c_k\in\mathbb R^*$ can be any numbers.

At $k=0$ our formula is as follows, stating that the first polynomial $P_0$ must be a constant, as it should:

Method: Explicit model calculation and hypothesis obstruction Result: For simultaneously diagonal A and B on a Hilbert space, the homogeneous coordinate equation dX=-lambda*X dt+b*sqrt(lambda)*X dW gives E|X_t|^p=|X_0|^p exp{p*((p-1)*b^2/2-1)*lambda*t}. Thus positivity of A alone cannot supply a p-independent stochastic parabolicity condition. In the p=2 coercive regime b^2<2, applying Ito to ||A^(1/2)u||^2 yields control of E integral ||Au||^2 for additive input in D(A^(1/2)), after absorbing its cross term by Young inequality. Check: The moment identity follows both from the explicit stochastic exponential and from Ito applied to |X|^p. The coercive calculation uses the weighted norm A^(1/2)u, so it controls the full domain D(A), not merely the energy domain. Obstruction: A criterion handling noncommuting A,B in Banach spaces must replace scalar coercivity and preserve the correct p-dependence. No such general criterion is proved here. Brzezniak-Veraar2012 already studies this p-dependence; the diagonal calculation is a known-model rederivation.

[Prop lamclass of arXiv:2608.30031, 'Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures'] Suppose $\Lambda$ is a minimal lamination on $M$ transverse to $\partial M$. Then at least one of the following holds:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $\Lambda$ has a leaf $\lambda$ such that $\pi_1(\lambda)$ is not normally generated by boundary parallel curves.
        \item $\Lambda$ is a compact planar surface.
        \item $\Lambda$ has a leaf with a noncompact boundary component inside a Reeb, $\sharp$, or $\flat$ annulus on $\partial M$.
        \item $\Lambda$ is a $\mathbb{T}^3$-type planar lamination.
        \item $\Lambda$ is a $\mathbb{T}^2$-type planar lamination.
    \end{enumerate}

[Lemma lem:zeroes_of_omega_D of arXiv:2605.03896, 'Dimer models on astroidal zig-zag graphs'] Let \(D=\sum_{j=1}^n a_j \zeta_j\) be a degree-\(0\) real divisor such that $a_j\neq0$,
\(\zeta_j\in A_0\) for all \(j\), and index the points
\(\zeta_1,\dots,\zeta_n\) cyclically along \(A_0\). Then the differential
\(\omega_D\) satisfies:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item for each \(1\le k\le g\), the number of zeroes of \(\omega_D\) on \(A_k\) is even and at least \(2\),

    \item for each interval \((\zeta_j,\zeta_{j+1})\subset A_0\), the number of zeroes
    of \(\omega_D\) in \((\zeta_j,\zeta_{j+1})\) is odd
    if \(\res_{\zeta_j}(\omega_D)\) and \(\res_{\zeta_{j+1}}(\omega_D)\) have the same sign,
    and even if they have opposite signs. In particular, \(\omega_D\) has at least one
    zero in \((\zeta_j,\zeta_{j+1})\) whenever the residues at \(\zeta_j\) and
    \(\zeta_{j+1}\) have the same sign.
\end{enumerate}

Define the elementary factors E_0(w) = 1 - w and, for p ≥ 1, E_p(w) = (1 - w) exp(w + w^2/2 + ... + w^p/p). Let m ≥ 0 be an integer and let (a_n) be a finite or infinite sequence of nonzero complex numbers, repetitions allowed, with |a_n| → ∞ if the sequence is infinite. Choose nonnegative integers p_n such that the series Σ_n (r/|a_n|)^{p_n + 1} converges for every r > 0 (the choice p_n = n - 1 always works). Then the product P(z) = z^m Π_n E_{p_n}(z/a_n) converges absolutely and uniformly on compact subsets of C and defines an entire function whose zero set is exactly {0} (with multiplicity m, omitted if m = 0) together with the points a_n, each with multiplicity equal to the number of times it is listed. Conversely, every entire function f whose zeros are exactly these (with these multiplicities) has the form f(z) = exp(g(z)) P(z) for some entire function g. Consequently every entire function admits such a factorization, and every meromorphic function on C is a quotient of two entire functions.
the prescribed zeros form a sequence with no finite accumulation point (|a_n| → ∞ if infinite)
the integers p_n satisfy Σ_n (r/|a_n|)^{p_n+1} < ∞ for every r > 0
multiplicities are encoded by repetition in the list

body:
Let H be a complex Hilbert space. (a) If A is self-adjoint on H, then U(t) = e^{itA} (Borel functional calculus) defines a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group: U(t + s) = U(t)U(s), U(0) = I, U(t)* = U(−t), and t ↦ U(t)x is continuous on ℝ for each x. Moreover D(A) = {x ∈ H : lim_{t→0} (U(t)x − x)/t exists} and for x ∈ D(A) that limit equals iAx; D(A) is invariant under each U(t). (b) Conversely, let (U(t))_{t ∈ ℝ} be a family of unitary operators with U(t + s) = U(t)U(s), U(0) = I, and t ↦ U(t)x continuous for each x ∈ H. Then there is a unique self-adjoint operator A with U(t) = e^{itA} for all t, namely Ax = lim_{t→0} (U(t)x − x)/(it) on the set where the limit exists. (c) Weak continuity suffices in (b): if t ↦ ⟨U(t)x, y⟩ is continuous for all x, y, the group is strongly continuous, since ‖U(t)x − x‖² = 2‖x‖² − 2Re⟨U(t)x, x⟩. If H is separable, weak measurability of t ↦ ⟨U(t)x, y⟩ already implies strong continuity (von Neumann). (d) A subspace D ⊂ D(A) that is dense in H and invariant under every U(t) is a core for A (Nelson's criterion via invariant domains).
H is a complex Hilbert space
in (a): A is self-adjoint, not merely symmetric
in (b): U(t) unitary for every real t, group law on all of ℝ, and strong (or weak) continuity

[Lemma bound_on_4th_moment of arXiv:2411.07878, 'Bernstein-type and Bennett-type inequalities for unbounded matrix martingales'] Fix $\alpha > 0$. 
    Let a random matrix $\mathbf{X} \in \mathbb{H}(d)$ be such that $u \coloneqq \norm[\big]{\norm{\mathbf{X}}}_{\psi_{\alpha}} < \infty$ and $\sigma^2 \coloneqq \lambda_{\max}(\E \mathbf{X}^2)$. 
    Then for any $z > 0$ such that $\alpha z^\alpha \ge 4$
    \[
    \E \mathbf{X}^4 \preccurlyeq z^2 u^2 \lr{\E \mathbf{X}^2 + 2 z^2 u^2 e^{-z^\alpha} \mathbf{I}}.
    \]
    In particular, for $z = z(u, \sigma; \alpha)$ defined by~(equation eq:def_z of the paper),
    \[
    \lambda_{\max}(\E \mathbf{X}^4) \le \frac{5}{3} (\sigma u z)^2.
    \]
title: Lemma bound_on_4th_moment of arXiv:2411.07878

\[
  \left|
  \Cov\!\left(\Tr(AH),\Tr(BH)\right)
  \right|
  \leq
  4\sqrt{\Tr(A^2)\Tr(B^2)}.
\]

[Lemma 9 of arXiv:2512.00570, 'Makeenko--Migdal equations for lattice Yang--Mills--Higgs'] For all $e\in E_\Lambda=E_\Lambda^+\cup E_\Lambda^-$, 
we have
$\dif Q_e = \mathcal D_e \,\dif t + \dif \mathcal M_e$ where

(1)
 the drift 
$\mathcal D_e= c_\mfg Q_e +\nabla_e \cS_1+\nabla_e \cS_2$;

(2)
the martingale $\mathcal M_e$ satisfies
\begin{equs}
\text{Tr}\big(\dif \mathcal M_e \,P\, \dif \mathcal M_e \,R \big)
&=
2\Big(
\nu \text{Tr} (Q_e PQ_e R)
+\mu \text{Tr} ( P^t  R)-\lambda\text{Tr}(Q_eP)\text{Tr}(Q_eR) \Big)\dif t	
\\
\text{Tr}\big(\dif \mathcal M_e \,P\, \dif \mathcal M_{e^{-1}} \,R \big)
&=
-2\Big(
\nu \text{Tr} (Q_e PQ_e^* R)
+\mu \text{Tr} (Q_e P^t Q_e^t R)-\lambda\text{Tr}(P)\text{Tr}(R) 
\Big)\dif t						
\\
\Tr \big(\dif \mathcal M_e \,P\big) 
\Tr\big(\dif \mathcal M_e \,R \big)
&=
2\Big(\nu \Tr (Q_e P)\Tr(Q_e R)
+\mu \text{Tr} ( P R^t)-\lambda\text{Tr}(Q_ePQ_eR) \Big)\dif t		
\\
\text{Tr}\big(\dif \mathcal M_e \,P\big) \Tr\big( \dif \mathcal M_{e^{-1}} \,R \big)
&=-2
\Big(
\nu \text{Tr} (Q_e P) \Tr( RQ_e^*)
+\mu \text{Tr} (Q_e P Q_e R^t)-\lambda\text{Tr}(PR) 
\Big)\dif t						
\end{equs}
for any adapted $N$-by-$N$ matrix-valued processes $P,R$,
where $\lambda,\mu,\nu$ are as in \eqref{e:lambda-mu-nu}.

[Lemma Lyapunov-descent-riemann of arXiv:2608.29507, 'Denoising as Projection: Constrained Optimization with Gradient-Guided Diffusion'] Suppose Assumption (assump:uniform-graph of the paper) and (assump:smoothness of the paper) hold. Consider the update (equation eq:projected-gradient-guidance-relaxed of the paper). 
Let $z_t:=x_t-\eta\nabla f(x_t)$ and suppose that
   $ \|\widehat\pi_t(z_t)-\pi_\mathcal{M}(z_t)\|\le E_t .$ Assume that $\mathrm{dist}(x_t,\mathcal{M})
    \le
    \frac{r}{2}$, where $r$ is defined in (equation eq:cU of the paper). Let $p_t:=\pi_\mathcal{M}(x_t), n_t:=x_t-p_t$. If $\eta \le \min\{\frac{1}{50L},\frac{r}{4G}\}, \epsilon \le \min\{\frac{1}{512\eta(G\kappa+L)},\frac{r}{4E_t}\}$, then we have that $\mathrm{dist}(x_{t-1},\mathcal{M})
    \le
    \frac{r}{2}$, and with
\begin{align*}
    \textstyle V(x):=f(\pi_\mathcal{M}(x))+\frac{1}{160\eta}\|x-\pi_\mathcal{M}(x)\|^2,
\end{align*}
we have
\vspace{-15pt}
\begin{align*}
   \textstyle V(x_{t-1})
    \le
    V(x_t)
    -
    \frac{\epsilon\eta}{480}\|\mathrm{grad}_\mathcal{M} f(p_t)\|^2
    -
    \frac{\epsilon}{2000\eta}\|n_t\|^2
    +
    \frac{6\epsilon}{\eta}E_t^2.
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lyapunov descent with inexact projection

[Definition 5 (Conical complex) of arXiv:2609.00183, '2609.00183'] Let $(X,d)$ be an NPC space and let $O_X \in X$. For $\mu \in [0,1],$ define the mapping
\[
R_{O_X,\mu}:X \to X
\]
by letting $R_{O_X,\mu}(P)$ be the point lying a fraction $\mu$ of the way from $O_X$ to $P \in X$ along the unique geodesic joining them. We say that $X$ is {\bf conical with respect to $O_X$} if 
\begin{enumerate}
    \item for any $P,Q \in X$ and $\mu \in [0,1]$
            \[
                d\bigl(R_{O_X,\mu}(P), R_{O_X,\mu}(Q)\bigr) = \mu d(P,Q).
            \]
    \item $R_{O_X,\mu}$ is surjective for any $\mu \in (0,1].$ 
\end{enumerate}
The point $O_X$ is called the {\bf cone point} of $X.$
title: Conical complex

[Proposition prop:KW of arXiv:2506.10765, 'A General Coupling for Ising Models and Beyond'] Let $\Lambda$ be a finite cubical subcomplex of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $\mathbb{G}$ a finite abelian group, $1\leq k\leq d$, $(J_{\mathbf{c}})_{\mathbf{c}\in \Lambda^{*,k}}$ be positive coupling constants and $h:\mathbb{G}\to \mathbb{R}$ be even. Let $\Omega:=\mathrm{Im}(\partial_{d-k+1})$  and $\Sigma:=C^{k-1}$. Define $f:\Omega\to 2^{\Sigma}$ by $f(\eta) = \{\sigma \in \Sigma \mid d^k(\sigma) = \eta^* \} = (*\circ d^k)^{-1}(\eta)$ and
     $$
     \rho[\eta]\propto \prod_{\mathbf{c}\in {\Lambda_{d-k}}}\exp(J_{\mathbf{c}} h(\eta_{\mathfrak{c}})), \;\forall \eta\in \Omega, \qquad \gamma[\sigma]\propto 1,\;\forall\sigma\in\Sigma.
     $$
     Then, under the coupling measure $\mathscr{P}$ defined in Theorem (thm:generalcoupling of the paper), 
    \begin{enumerate}
		\item[(a)] The marginal of $\mathscr{P}$ on $\Sigma$ is the spin model $\mu^{*}_{\Lambda^{k-1}}$. 
        For each $\eta \in\Omega$,  the conditional measure $\mathscr{P}[\;\cdot \mid \eta]$ is the uniform measure on $f(\eta)$, that is the uniform assignment of a spin configuration consistent with the domain walls $\eta$.
		\item[(b)] The marginal of $\mathscr{P}$ on $\Omega$ is the domain wall measure $\mu_{\Lambda_{d-k}}$.  For each $\sigma \in\Sigma$, the conditional measure $\mathscr{P}[\;\cdot \mid \sigma] = \delta_{(d^k(\sigma))^*}$, the Dirac measure on the dual of the co-boundary of $\sigma$ corresponding to taking the domain walls of the spin configuration. 
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Spin Models and Domain Walls

[Conjecture of arXiv:2608.25065, 'Detection of first homology via random geometric graphs in the thermodynamic regime'] For each $d \ge 2$ and each $1 \le k \le d - 1$, there exists $0 < \lambda_{c,k}<\infty$
    such that the following holds.
    For $\lambda \in (0,\infty)$,
    let $X^n$ be a Poisson point process with intensity measure $ndM = (\lambda/r^d) dM$
    on a Riemannian manifold of $M$ of dimension $d$ and volume 1,
    and let $
    \mathcal{C} = VC_r(X^n)$
    be the associated Vietoris-Rips complex
    with radius $r$.
    Then, if $ \lambda > \lambda_{c,k}$, then
    \[
        \mathbb{P}(\mbox{the natural map }
        H_k(\mathcal{C}) \to H_k(M)
        \mbox{ is surjective})
        \to 1
    \]
    as $r \to 0$. Moreover, there exists
    some function $s_\lambda:[0,\infty) \to [0,\infty)$
    with $s_\lambda(r) = o_{r \to 0}(1), s_\lambda(r) = \omega(r)$
    such that
    \[
        \mathbb{P}(\mbox{the natural map }
        Z_k(\mathcal{C})/
        Z_k^{s_{\lambda}(r)}(\mathcal{C})
        \to H_k(M)
        \mbox{ is an isomorphism})
        \to 1
    \]
    as $r \to 0$,
    where $Z_k^{s_\lambda(r)}(\mathcal{C})$
    is the submodule
    of $Z_k(\mathcal{C})$
    generated by $k$-cycles of diameter
    at most $s_\lambda(r)$.
    \\
    On the other hand,
    if $\lambda < \lambda_{c,k}$, then
        \[
        \mathbb{P}(\mbox{the natural map }
        H_k(\mathcal{C})
        \to H_k(M)
        \mbox{ is the zero map})
        \to 1
    \]
    as $r \to 0$. (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)

Let n>=1 and y_i in {-1,+1}, and let f(w;x_i) be continuously differentiable in w in R^D. Assume global constants rho>0 and beta>0 satisfy ||grad f(w;x_i)||_2<=rho and ||grad f(w;x_i)-grad f(v;x_i)||_2<=beta||w-v||_2 for every w,v and every training index i. Define L(w)=(1/n)sum_i log(1+exp(-y_i f(w;x_i))) and w_{k+1}=w_k-eta grad L(w_k), where eta>0 denotes the source paper's eta_tilde. At any iterate w with L(w)<=1/(eta rho^2), writing g=grad L(w) and w_plus=w-eta g, one has -eta(1+beta eta L(w))||g||_2^2<=L(w_plus)-L(w)<=-eta(1-(2rho^2+beta)eta L(w))||g||_2^2. In particular L(w)<=1/[eta(2rho^2+beta)] implies L(w_plus)<=L(w). The model need not be convex or twice differentiable. Near-homogeneity and linear separability are not hypotheses of this one-step result.

body:
[Theorem thm:L of arXiv:2412.01015, 'Classical beta ensembles and related eigenvalues processes at high temperature and the Mar'] Under the moment assumption~(equation moment-assumption of the paper), it holds that 
\[
	S_n^{(N)}(t) \to m_n(t) \quad \text{as} \quad N \to \infty,
\]
in probability as random elements in $C([0, T])$. Here the limiting moment processes are recursively defined by $m_0(t) = 1,$ 
\begin{align}
	m_n(t) &= a_n + \sigma n (n+\alpha - 1)\int_0^t m_{n-1}(s)ds + \sigma {cn} \sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\int_0^t m_j(u) m_{n-1-j}(u) du,  
\end{align}
for $n \ge 1$.
If, in addition, the initial limiting moments $\{a_n\}$ satisfy a condition that
\[
	a_n \le (\Lambda n)^{2n}, \quad n \ge 0,
\]
for some constant $\Lambda > 0$. Then for any $ t \ge 0$, $\{m_n(t)\}_{n \ge 0}$ are moments of a unique probability measure $\mu_t$ on $[0, \infty)$. Moreover, the probability measure-valued process $\mu_t$ is continuous and the empirical measure process $(\mu_t^{(N)})_{0 \le t \le T}$ converges to $(\mu_t)_{0 \le t \le T}$ in probability under the topology of uniform convergence. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:L of arXiv:2412.01015

[Definition 7 of arXiv:2605.13727, 'Stochastic evolution equations\\ driven by arbitrary cylindrical Lévy processes'] A predictable process $\Psi \colon \Omega \times [0,T] \rightarrow L_2(U,H)$ is $L$-integrable if there exists a sequence $(\Psi_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of processes in $\mathcal{S}_{\rm prd}^{\rm HS}$ such that
	\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
		\item[{\rm (1)}]  $(\Psi_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ converges $P_T$-a.e. to $\Psi$;
		\item[{\rm (2)}] $\displaystyle \lim_{m,n \rightarrow \infty}d_T^{em}(I(\Psi_m),I(\Psi_n))=0.$
	\end{enumerate}
	In this case,  the stochastic integral process $(I(\Psi)(t):\, t\in [0,T])$ of $\Psi$ is defined as the limit 
	of $(I(\Psi_n))_{n\in\N}$ in $\dem_T$. The class of all $L$-integrable $L_2(U,H)$-valued predictable processes will be denoted by $\mathcal{I}_{{\rm prd},L}^{\rm HS}:=\mathcal{I}_{{\rm prd},L}^{\rm HS}(U,H)$.

body:
Let G be a finite connected undirected multigraph on n vertices, loops discarded, with Laplacian L = D - A where D is the diagonal degree matrix and A the adjacency matrix (A_{ij} the number of edges between i and j). Then the number of spanning trees of G equals every cofactor of L: deleting any row i and any column j and taking (-1)^{i+j} times the determinant gives the same value. Equivalently, if 0 = lambda_1 < lambda_2 <= ... <= lambda_n are the eigenvalues of L, the number of spanning trees is (lambda_2 lambda_3 ... lambda_n) / n.
G finite and undirected; for a disconnected graph every cofactor is 0
loops do not affect spanning trees and are removed

body:
[Lem 39 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For any constants $C,\delta > 0$, there exists a positive constant $c(C,\delta)$ such that the following holds: let $\bA$ be any $N\times N$ diagonal matrix with $\|\bA\|_{\op} \le C$, and suppose $\bg,\acute{\bg}$ are independent standard gaussian vectors in $\R^N$. Then,
    \[
        \frac{|(\bA \bg, \bg) - \Tr(\bA)|}{N}\,,
        \frac{|(\bA \bg, \acute{\bg})|}{N}
        \le \delta
    \]
    with probability at least $1-e^{- c(C,\delta) N}$.

\begin{proof}
We rewrite the random variables of interest as
    \begin{align*}
    (\bA \bg, \bg) - \Tr(\bA)
    &=
    \sum_{i=1}^N a_{i,i}
    \Big((g_i)^2-1\Big)\,,\\
    (\bA\bg,\bg')
    &=
    \sum_{i=1}^N a_{i,i}
        g_i\acute{g}_i\,.
    \end{align*}
The claim then follows by standard Chernoff bounds.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 30 of arXiv:2605.05864, 'Classification and Metrization of Classes of Smooth measures'] For \(\mu_n, \mu \in \mathcal{D}\) and their corresponding PCAFs \(A^{\mu_n}, A^{\mu}\), if \(\mu_n\) converges to \(\mu\) in \(d_\mathcal{D}\), then \(A^{\mu_n}\) converges to \(A^{\mu}\) in \(L^1(\mathbb{P}_x)\) uniformly for \(x\) with the local uniform topology for \(t\), that is, for any \(T>0\),
\[\lim_{n\to \infty} \left\|\mathbb{E}_\cdot[\sup_{0\leq t\leq T} |A^{\mu_n}_t-A^{\mu}_t|]\right\|_{\infty,q} = 0.\]

[Lm 3 of arXiv:2609.02576, 'Sharp estimates for the Jacobi and trigonometric Dunkl heat kernels'] (Parabolic minimum principle)
	Let $T=D$ or $T=D^{\rm D}$. Let $0\le t_1<t_2<\infty$ and $\Omega$ be a connected opensubset of $\RR^d$. Assume that $f \in \mathcal{C}^{2,1}(\Omega\times (t_1,t_2))\cap \mathcal{C}(\overline{\Omega}\times[t_1,t_2])$ satisfies 
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item $Tf(x,t)\geq 0$ for  $(x,t)\in \Omega\times(t_1,t_2]$,
		\item $f(x,t)\geq 0$ for $(x,t)\in\partial\Omega\times [t_1,t_2]\cup \Omega\times \{t_1\}$.
	\end{enumerate}
	Then, $f(x,t)\geq 0$ for $(x,t)\in \overline{\Omega}\times [t_1,t_2]$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem 232 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] Consider a solution $\boldsymbol{F}(z) = (F_h(z))_{h = 1}^H$ of the master Riemann--Hilbert problem with zero source, such that $\boldsymbol{F}(z) = O(z^d)$ as $z \rightarrow \infty$ for some $d \in \amsmathbb{Z}$. Then, for any non-zero $\boldsymbol{v} \in \amsmathbb{R}^H$, there exists a unique meromorphic function $F_{\boldsymbol{v}}$ on $\Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}}$ such that, for any $\boldsymbol{w} \in \mathfrak{G}.\boldsymbol{v}$ and $p \in \Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{w}}$ we have
\[
F_{\boldsymbol{v}}(p) = \big \langle \boldsymbol{w} \cdot \boldsymbol{F}(z) \big \rangle = \sum_{h = 1}^H w_h F_h(z) \qquad \textnormal{with}\quad z = Z_{\boldsymbol{v}}(p).
\]
The function $F_{\boldsymbol{v}}$ can have poles only at ramification points with order at most equal to the tameness exponent of $\boldsymbol{F}$, and at $Z^{-1}_{\boldsymbol{v}}(\{\infty\})$ with order at most $d$. If the $\mathfrak{G}$-orbit of $\boldsymbol{v}$ is finite, then $\Sigma_{\boldsymbol{v}}$ is a compact Riemann surface, and
\[
\big\{\langle \boldsymbol{w} \cdot \boldsymbol{F}(z)\rangle \,\,\big|\,\,\boldsymbol{w} \in \mathfrak{G}.\boldsymbol{v}\big\}
\]
are the various branches of an algebraic function. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 9 of arXiv:2609.03954, 'Galois representations ramified at one prime via relative deformation theory'] For every $m\in\Z$, the groups $H^i(G_{\{p\}},\Zp(m))$ are finitely generated $\Zp$-modules for $i=1,2$, and the canonical maps
\[
 H^i(G_{\{p\}},\Zp(m))\otimes_{\Zp}\Qp
 \longrightarrow
 H^i(G_{\{p\}},\Qp(m))
 \qquad \text{for}\quad i=1,2
\]
are isomorphisms.  In particular, the degree-two map
\[
 H^2(G_{\{p\}},\Zp(m))\otimes_{\Zp}\Qp
 \longrightarrow
 H^2(G_{\{p\}},\Qp(m))
\]
is an isomorphism.  Moreover
\[
 \dim_{\Qp}H^2(G_{\{p\}},\Qp(m))
 =
 \operatorname{corank}_{\Zp}
 H^2\!\left(G_{\{p\}},(\Qp/\Zp)(m)\right).
\]

[Lemma le:close_geodesic_good_eta of arXiv:2507.15589, 'Tightness of approximations to metrics on non-simple conformal loop ensemble gaskets'] There exists $c>0$ (not depending on $M,a,a_1,a_0$) such that the following is true. Fix $M,a,a_1 > 0$ such that $a,a_1$ are sufficiently small (depending on $a_0$). 
Suppose $(D,x,y)$ is $(M,a)$-good and let $\mathcal {Z}_k$ be as defined in~(equation eq:bottleneck_def of the paper). Suppose also that $\mathcal {Z}_k = \varnothing$ for $j < \log_2(\delta^{-1})$. Let $U \subseteq D_\eta$ be the $\delta^{1+a_1}$-neighborhood of $\eta$. 
Then

body:
[Theorem thm:HW of arXiv:2608.26707, 'An Exponential Lower Bound for the Permanent\\of Random Bernoulli Matrix'] Let $\varepsilon=(\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_N)$ have independent uniform sign coordinates, and let $A$ be a deterministic real symmetric $N\times N$ matrix.
Then, for every $t\geq0$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb{P}\!\left(
   \abs{\varepsilon^{\mathsf T}A\varepsilon-\operatorname{tr} A}>t
 \right)
 \leq
 2\exp\!\left[
   -c\min\!\left\{
     \frac{t^2}{\left\lVert A\right\rVert_F^2},
     \frac{t}{\left\lVert A\right\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}}
   \right\}
 \right].
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:HW of arXiv:2608.26707

body:
[Lemma 16 (From \cite{AEK2017}) of arXiv:2606.20816, 'Spectral Properties of Dense Barab\'asi--Albert Graphs'] Let $H^{(n)}$ be a centered Wigner--type matrix -- a real symmetric matrix with entries $h_{k j}$ independent for $k \leq j$ and $\E[h_{k j}] = 0$ for all $k, j$. Let the variance profile of $H^{(n)}$ satisfy assumptions \textnormal{(A)--(D)} from Proposition \ref{prop:AEK}, and let $\rho$ be the deterministic limiting density obtained from the corresponding QVE. Let $\mathrm{supp} \, \rho = \bigcup_{r = 1}^R \left[\alpha_r, \beta_r\right]$. Then, it holds asymptotically with overwhelming probability that all eigenvalues of $H^{(n)}$ lie inside $\mathrm{supp} \, \rho$. If $E_n$ denotes the stated event, then $E_n$ holds asymptotically with overwhelming probability if for every $D > 0$ there exists $N_D \in \mathbb{N}$ such that for all $n \ge N_D$,
\[
\P \left(E_n\right)
\ \ge \
1 - n^{-D}.
\]
Equivalently, $H^{(n)}$ has no outlier eigenvalues. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: From \cite{AEK2017}

[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2608.30733, 'An Operator-Theoretic Characterization of Gaussian Measure Singularity under Mean Shifts'] Assume that
$
m_{\Delta,q}\neq0
$
and let
$
\beta_q
=
\mathsf K_q^{\dagger}m_{\Delta,q}
=
\mathsf K_q^{\dagger/2}\widetilde m_{\Delta,q}
$
denote the truncated Fisher discriminant. Then
$
\beta_q
$
is an eigenfunction of the induced coordinatewise operator
$
\mathsf{\widetilde K}_{4,q}
$
if and only if there exists a constant
$
c>0
$
such that
$
\widetilde\nu_j^{\,2}=c
$
for every
$
j
$
with
$
\widetilde\nu_j\neq0.
$
In that case,
\[
\mathsf{\widetilde K}_{4,q}\beta_q=\kappa_{\Delta,q}\beta_q,
\qquad
\kappa_{\Delta,q}=3+2\rho c+\rho(1-3\rho)c^2.
\]
In particular, the condition is automatically satisfied whenever
$
\widetilde m_{\Delta,q}
$
is supported on a single Karhunen--Loève direction. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 3 of arXiv:2608.30733

body:
[Theorem thm:dependence of arXiv:2607.24705, 'Derangetropy Operators'] For $n = 2$ and $f \in \mathcal{D}_{+}(\mathbb{R}^{2})$, the Lie
		bracket of the coordinate vector fields, in the standard convention
		$[L_{1},L_{2}](f) = DL_{2}[f](L_{1}f) - DL_{1}[f](L_{2}f)$, is
		\begin{equation}
			\begin{aligned}
				[L_{1}, L_{2}]\,f
				&= \Big[w'\big(F_{2}(x_{2})\big)\,\gamma_{1}(x_{2})
				- w'\big(F_{1}(x_{1})\big)\,\gamma_{2}(x_{1})\Big]\,f,\\
				\gamma_{2}(x_{1})
				&= \operatorname{Cov}\!\big(w(F_{2}(X_{2})),\,
				\mathbf{1}\{X_{1}\le x_{1}\}\big),
			\end{aligned}
			
		\end{equation}
		and symmetrically. The bracket vanishes under independence, and the
		multiplier in square brackets depends on $f$ only through its copula,
		evaluated at the marginal ranks. Conversely, if the brackets of the
		full family $\{w_{k,\alpha}\}$ all vanish, then $X_{1}$ and $X_{2}$

[Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2608.29403, 'Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in $\boldsymbol{\Theta(n^2)}$ Steps:\\ A Proof Disco'] For every fixed
$0<\varepsilon<1$, there are constants $c_\varepsilon<\infty$ and
$n_\varepsilon$ such that for $n\ge n_\varepsilon$,
\[
  N\le t_{\mathrm{mix}}^{(n)}(\varepsilon)
  \le c_\varepsilon N.
\]
In particular,
\[
  t_{\mathrm{mix}}^{(n)}(\varepsilon)
  =\Theta_\varepsilon(n^2).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 19 (Tetrahedral analogue of Lemma 5 in \cite{GangNar}) of arXiv:2607.04138, 'Hives from deformed GUE minor processes'] \lab{lem:tet-analogue of GangNar}
Let \(\bar a,\bar b,\bar d>0\), and assume either \(\bar f>0\), or \(\bar f^2<0\) and
\[
T:=\bar a^2+\bar b^2+\bar d^2+\bar f^2<0.
\]
Define
\[
a^2=\frac{\bar a^2(\bar b^2+\bar d^2+\bar f^2)}{T},\qquad
b^2=\frac{\bar b^2(\bar a^2+\bar d^2+\bar f^2)}{T},
\]
\[
d^2=\frac{\bar d^2(\bar a^2+\bar b^2+\bar f^2)}{T},\qquad
f^2=\frac{\bar f^2(\bar a^2+\bar b^2+\bar d^2)}{T}.
\]
Then
\[
\frac{\bar a^2\bar b^2\bar d^2\bar f^2}{\bar a^2+\bar b^2+\bar d^2+\bar f^2}
=
\frac{9}{4}\diamondplus_{abdf}^2.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Tetrahedral analogue of Lemma 5 in \cite{GangNar}

Let $f\in L^1(\mathbb R^d)$ (equivalently, by the argument below, $f\in L^2(\mathbb R^d)$). If both $\{x:f(x)\ne0\}$ and $\{\xi:\hat f(\xi)\ne0\}$ have finite Lebesgue measure, then $f=0$ almost everywhere. In particular $f$ and $\hat f$ cannot both have compact support unless $f=0$, and a nonzero bandlimited function cannot vanish outside a set of finite measure. Quantitative companion (Amrein-Berthier, Nazarov in $d=1$): for sets $S,\Sigma\subset\mathbb R^d$ of finite measure there is $C=C(S,\Sigma)>0$ with $\|f\|_2\le C(\|f\|_{L^2(S^c)}+\|\hat f\|_{L^2(\Sigma^c)})$ for all $f\in L^2$.
f integrable on R^d (an L^2 function whose support has finite measure is automatically integrable)
BOTH the support of f and the support of its transform have finite Lebesgue measure
no smoothness or decay is assumed

body:
[Proposition 7 (\textsf{Graph closure of the fixed-chaos estimates}) of arXiv:2607.28742, '2607.28742'] Let $p, q\geq1$, let $F\in L^4(\Omega)\cap \bC_p$ and $G\in L^4(\Omega)\cap \bC_q$.
Let $F_n, G_n$ be the
 martingale approximants from
Theorem~\ref{thm_core}.  Then
 $ FG\in\bigoplus_{r=0}^{p+q}\bC_r.$
Let $\Gamma(F, G)$ denote the carr\'e-du-champ operator \eqref{Gamma_def}.
Then, we have
\begin{align}
  \Gamma(F_n, G_n)&\xrightarrow[\text{in }L^2(\Omega)]{n\to+\infty}\Gamma(F,G).
  
\end{align}
Moreover, the following  exact identity holds:
\begin{align}
  \frac1{2p}
  \int_\cZ\E[|D_zF|^4] \,\mu(dz)
  =\frac{3}{p}\E[F^2\Gamma(F,F)]-\E[F^4].
  
\end{align}
As a result,  the  estimates in
\cite[Lemma 3.2]{DP18} are valid under 
$F\in L^4(\Omega)\cap\bC_p$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \textsf{Graph closure of the fixed-chaos estimates}

body: For an n by n complex matrix A, the numerical range (field of values) of A is the set W(A) = {x* A x : x in C^n, x* x = 1}, a subset of the complex plane. W(A) contains every eigenvalue of A, and if A is normal (A A* = A* A), W(A) equals the convex hull of the eigenvalues of A. [standard, e.g. Horn and Johnson, Topics in Matrix Analysis]
title: Numerical Range (Field of Values) of a Matrix

[Defn def:BKS_NS+NStable of arXiv:2606.29829, ''] Let $n\geq1$ be a positive integer, and $\mathfrak{f}_n:\{0,1\}^n\rightarrow\{0,1\}$ be a Boolean function indexed by $n$. Also, let $X_1,\dots,X_n$ be independent Bernoulli$(\frac{1}{2})$ random variables. Given $0<\varepsilon<1$, the sequence of Boolean functions $\{\mathfrak{f}_n\}_n$ is asymptotically 
	\begin{itemize}
		\item \emph{noise sensitive} if \quad
		$\displaystyle\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\cov(\mathfrak{f}_n(X_1,\dots,X_n),\mathfrak{f}_n(X_1(\varepsilon),\dots,X_n(\varepsilon)))=0,\quad\text{ and }$
		\item \emph{noise stable} if \quad
		$\displaystyle\lim_{\varepsilon\rightarrow0}\sup_n\mathbb{P}(\mathfrak{f}_n(X_1,\dots,X_n)\neq \mathfrak{f}_n(X_1(\varepsilon),\dots,X_n(\varepsilon)))=0,$
	\end{itemize}
	where, 
	\[X_i(\varepsilon)=\begin{cases}
		X_i&\text{ with probability }1-\varepsilon,\\
		1-X_i&\text{ with probability }\varepsilon,
	\end{cases}\text{ for all }1\leq i\leq n.\]
title: Defn def:BKS_NS+NStable of arXiv:2606.29829

[Def Exceptional Divisor of arXiv:2609.04023, 'Characterizing Contractions and Weighted Blowdowns'] Suppose $Y_\bullet \hookrightarrow X$ is a weighted embedding defined by $I_\bullet.$ 
   The inclusion $I_{\bullet +1} \subset I_\bullet$ induces an inclusion $\mathcal{O}_{\operatorname{Bl}_Y X}(1) \hookrightarrow \mathcal{O}_{\operatorname{Bl}_Y X}$ of invertible sheaves.
   The {\em exceptional divisor} $\mathcal{E}$ is the Cartier divisor associated with this inclusion. 
   In particular, $\mathcal{O}_{\operatorname{Bl}_Y X}(-\mathcal{E}) \simeq \mathcal{O}_{\operatorname{Bl}_Y X}(1).$
title: Exceptional Divisor

[Lemma 43 (Finite-dimensional relative entropy chain rule) of arXiv:2608.28827, 'Quantitative Target Convergence and Uniform-in-Time\\ Propagation of Chaos for Langevin-Re'] Fix \(N\geq1\).  Let \(P_t^N\) and \(Q_t^N\) be the laws of two
diffusions on \((\R^d)^N\) with common diffusion coefficient
\(\sqrt{2\varepsilon}I\) and respective drifts \(b_t^N\) and
\(\bar b_t^N\), that is, with Fokker-Planck equations given by
\begin{equation}
    \partial_tP_t^N
    =
    -\nabla\cdot(b_t^NP_t^N)+\varepsilon\Delta P_t^N,
    \qquad
    \partial_tQ_t^N
    =
    -\nabla\cdot(\bar b_t^NQ_t^N)+\varepsilon\Delta Q_t^N,
\end{equation}
where \(\varepsilon>0\).
Suppose that \(P_0^N,Q_0^N\in\mathcal P_2((\R^d)^N)\)
and that, for every \(T<\infty\), \(b_t^N\) and
\(\bar b_t^N\) are in $C_{\mathrm{loc}}^{\alpha/2,\,1+\alpha}
    \bigl((0,T]\times\mathbb R^{dN};\mathbb R^{dN}\bigr)$ for some $\alpha \in (0,1)$, and
satisfy
\[
    \|b_t^N(X)\|+\|\bar b_t^N(X)\|
    \leq C_{N,T}(1+\|X\|),
    \qquad 0\leq t\leq T.
\]
If \(\KL(P_0^N\|Q_0^N)<\infty\), then 
\(u\mapsto\KL(P_u^N\|Q_u^N)\) is locally absolutely continuous and,
for \(0\leq s\leq t\),
\begin{align}
    \KL(P_t^N\|Q_t^N)-\KL(P_s^N\|Q_s^N)
    &=
    \int_s^t\int
       \left\langle
          b_u^N-\bar b_u^N,
          \nabla\log\frac{dP_u^N}{dQ_u^N}
       \right\rangle
       dP_u^N\,du
    \notag\\
    &\quad
    -\varepsilon\int_s^t
       I(P_u^N\|Q_u^N)\,du.

\end{align}

    converges absolutely and defines the unique extension of the
    distribution $\flap u$ of Definition~\ref{def_fracLap} to a tempered
    distribution. Consequently, if $F\in\mathscr S'(\R^n)$ and $\flap u=F$
    in $\mathscr D'(\R^n)$, then
    $\langle F,\eta\rangle=\int_{\R^n}u\,\flap\eta\,dx$ for all
    $\eta\in\mathscr S(\R^n)$.

body:
[Lemma of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Let $G$ be any compact Lie group. Then there exists a natural equivalence ${{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_\textup{$G$-gl}^{\circ}[-]\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}\Phi_G(-)(\textup{id}_G)$ of functors $\cat{$\bm G$-$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top}\to\Spc$, where $\Phi_G\colon{{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_\textup{$G$-gl}\to\PSh(\textup{Glo}_{/\mathbb B{G}})$ is obtained from the unique equivalence $\ul{{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_\textup{gl}\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}\ul\Spc_\textup{Glo}$ by evaluating at $\mathbb B{G}$.
    \begin{proof}
        If we continue to view $\cat{$\bm G$-$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top}$ as an \emph{unenriched} category, the cocartesian unstraightening of the 1-functor $\cat{$\bm G$-$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top}\to\textbf{\textup{Cat}}\hookrightarrow\Cat_\infty,X\mapsto \cat{$\bm G$-$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top}_{/X}$ is given by $\Ar(\cat{$\bm G$-$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top})$. Postcomposition with $\Phi_G$ and localizing therefore yields a natural transformation ${{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_\text{$G$-gl}[-]\to\PSh(\textup{Glo}_{/\mathbb B{G}})_{/\Phi_G(-)}$ given pointwise by the composite equivalence
        \[
            {{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_\text{$G$-gl}[X]\xrightarrow[\raise3.5pt\hbox{$\smash{\scriptstyle\sim}$}]{\,\textup{Lemma~(lemma:slice-over-fibrant of the paper)}\,}({{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_\text{$G$-gl})_{/X}\xrightarrow[\raise3.5pt\hbox{$\smash{\scriptstyle\sim}$}]{\;\,\Phi_G\,\;}\PSh(\textup{Glo}_{/\mathbb B{G}})_{/\Phi_G(X)},
        \]
        which clearly restricts to ${{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_\text{$G$-gl}^\circ[X]\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}\PSh(\textup{Glo}_{/\mathbb B{G}})_{/\Phi_G(X)}^\circ$. We will now construct for every small $\infty$-category $T$ with a terminal object $1$ a natural equivalence $\PSh(T)_{/-}^\circ\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}\ev_1$ of functors $\PSh(T)\to\Spc$; applying this to $T=\textup{Glo}_{/\mathbb B{G}}$ (with terminal object $\textup{id}_{\mathbb B{G}}$) will then complete the proof of the theorem.
        
        To prove the claim, note that the cocartesian unstraightening of $\PSh(T)_{/-}$ is given by the target map $\Ar(\PSh(T))\to\PSh(T)$, so that the cocartesian unstraightening of $\PSh(T)_{/-}^\circ$ is given by the forgetful map $\PSh(T)_{1/}\to\PSh(T)$. The latter is also the cocartesian unstraightening of ${\textup{Hom}}(1,-)$, which agrees with $\ev_1\colon\PSh(T)\to\Spc$ by the Yoneda lemma.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Certificate (campaign status: proved): (S14 (10)-(20).) Put d = ceil(n/3), s = 3d-n in {0,1,2}; choose cyclically ordered U = {u_1,...,u_d} with exactly s gaps of length two and d-s of length three (lengths sum 2s+3(d-s) = n). Write a length-two gap as u_j,m_j,u_{j+1} and a length-three gap as u_j,m_j,w_j,u_{j+1}. Then B_n = {A} u {C_{u_j,m_j} : all j} u (length-three gaps) {C_{m_j,w_j}, B_{w_j}} u (length-two gaps) {B_{m_j}} has 1+d+2(d-s)+s = n+1 forms and is a coordinate basis: relative to A a length-two gap contributes B_{u_j}+B_{m_j}, B_{m_j}, a length-three gap B_{u_j}+B_{m_j}, B_{m_j}+B_{w_j}, B_{w_j}, on disjoint coordinate sets. Selectors: B_{u_j} -> -A (residual L_{u_j}); B_{m_j} -> C_{u_j,m_j} in a length-three gap (residual -L_{u_j}); with v_j = m_j or w_j, C_{v_j,u_{j+1}} -> B_{v_j} (residual L_{u_{j+1}}). Notes: All selector residuals lie in the d-dimensional R = span{L_u}, so d_cb(A_n) <= d, and with S10's lower bound this proves d_cb = d_geo = ceil(n/3).

[Proposition prop.finite.marg of arXiv:2609.01007, 'Global universality of the expected number \\of zeros of non-analytic random signals'] If $a_1$ admits a finite moment of order three and if $f$ satisfies the condition $\mathbf{(H1)}$, then $\mathbb{P}-$almost surely, the finite marginals of $(g_n(t))_{t\in[0,2\pi]}$ converge to the ones of a stationary Gaussian process $(g_{\infty}(t))_{t\in [0,2\pi]}$ with covariance function
$$\mathbb{E}_X[g_{\infty}(t)g_{\infty}(s)] = \rho(t-s),~~\text{with}~\left\{\begin{array}{l}\displaystyle \rho(u):=\frac{1}{u}\int_0^{u}(f\ast \widetilde{f})(x)dx,~u\neq 0 \\\rho(0)=\langle f,f \rangle \end{array}\right.,$$
where $\widetilde{f}(x):=f(-x)$ for $x\in {\rm I\kern-0.16em R}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 26 of arXiv:2603.24616, 'Pinning in non-critical half-space geometric last passage percolation'] Fix $T_1$, $\vec{y}$, $q$, and $c$ as in Definition \ref{Def.InterlacingInteractingPairs}, and suppose that $g: \llbracket 0, T_1 \rrbracket \rightarrow \mathbb{Z}$ is an increasing path with $g(T_1) \leq y_{2k}$. Let $\mathfrak{Q} = \{Q_i\}_{i = 1}^{2k}$ be a line ensemble with law $\mathbb{P}^{T_1, \vec{y}, g}_{\ice; q,c}$, and define the $\llbracket 1, 2k+1 \rrbracket$-indexed line ensemble $\mathfrak{L} = \{L_i\}_{i = 1}^{2k+1}$ on $\llbracket 0, T_1 \rrbracket$ through
$$L_i(s) = Q_i(s) \mbox{ and } L_{2k+1}(s) = g(s) \mbox{ for } i \in \llbracket 1, 2k \rrbracket \mbox{ and } s \in \llbracket 0, T_1 \rrbracket.$$
Then, $\mathfrak{L}$ satisfies the interacting pair Gibbs property of Definition \ref{Def.IPGP} with $N = 2k+1$.

body:
[Lemma lem:covering of arXiv:2412.04539, 'Counting minimal cutsets and $p_c<1$'] Let $n \geq 1$. Let $P=(p_{i,j})_{i,j \in [n]}$ be a symmetric matrix of non-negative entries such that\footnote{We can think of $P$ as the transition matrix of a Markov chain which is killed at $i$ with probability $1-\sum_{j} p(i,j)$.} $\sum_{j \in [n]} p(i,j) \leq 1$ for all $i \in [n]$. Let $\Gamma$ be the set of all sequences $\gamma=(\gamma_0,\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_k)$ in $[n]$ (for any $k \geq 1$) with $\gamma_0=1$ such that the unique element $i\in [k]$ satisfying both $\gamma_i=1$ and $\{\gamma_0,\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_i\} = [n]$ is $i=k$. For every such sequence $\gamma$, define
\[
          p(\gamma) := \prod_{i=1}^k p\left(\gamma_{i-1},\gamma_i\right).
\]
For each $\varepsilon > 0$, if every non-empty proper subset $I$ of $[n]$ satisfies
\begin{equation} 
          \sum_{i \in I} \sum_{j \in [n] \backslash I} p(i,j) \geq \varepsilon,
\end{equation}
then $\delta :=\frac{\varepsilon^2}{16e^2}$ satisfies
\[
          \sum_{\gamma \in \Gamma} p(\gamma) \geq \delta^n.
\]

For f in L^1_loc(R^d) define the centred maximal function Mf(x) = sup_{r > 0} (1/|B(x,r)|) integral_{B(x,r)} |f(y)| dy. Then M is of WEAK type (1,1): for every f in L^1(R^d) and every lambda > 0, |{x : Mf(x) > lambda}| <= 3^d ||f||_1 / lambda. For 1 < p <= infinity, M is bounded on L^p: ||Mf||_p <= C(d,p) ||f||_p, with C(d,p) blowing up like p/(p-1) as p decreases to 1. M is NOT bounded on L^1: if f is not almost everywhere zero then Mf(x) >= c_d ||f||_1 / |x|^d for |x| large, which is not integrable, so Mf is in L^1 only when f = 0 a.e. The uncentred maximal function (supremum over all balls containing x) is comparable to the centred one, with constants depending only on d. [standard; e.g. Stein and Shakarchi, Real Analysis, Theorem 1.1 and Chapter 3]
f in L^1(R^d) for the weak (1,1) bound; f in L^p for the strong bound

body:
Let X be a discrete random variable taking values in a finite set of size m, let Y be any random variable jointly distributed with X, and let X_hat = g(Y) be any estimator of X computed from Y alone, so that X -> Y -> X_hat forms a Markov chain. Let P_e = Pr(X_hat != X) be the error probability. Then H(X|Y) <= H_b(P_e) + P_e * log(m-1), where H_b(p) = -p*log p - (1-p)*log(1-p) is the binary entropy function. Consequently, if the conditional entropy H(X|Y) is bounded away from 0, the error probability P_e cannot be made arbitrarily small.

X_hat is a function of Y alone, so X -> Y -> X_hat is a Markov chain
P_e = Pr(X_hat != X)

Expand the joint conditional entropy H(E,X|Y) two different ways using the chain rule: H(E,X|Y) = H(X|Y) + H(E|X,Y) = H(E|Y) + H(X|E,Y). Since E is a deterministic function of X and X_hat (itself determined by Y), H(E|X,Y) = 0. Conditioning cannot increase entropy, so H(E|Y) <= H(E) = H_b(P_e). For H(X|E,Y): when E=0, X = X_hat is already known, contributing 0; when E=1, X takes one of the remaining m-1 possible values, so H(X|E=1,Y) <= log(m-1); weighting by Pr(E=1)=P_e gives H(X|E,Y) <= P_e*log(m-1). [Lemma 5 of arXiv:2608.19744, 'Conditioned Brownian motion and local equivalence of path ensembles'] For every  $\tau>0 $, define
\[
 g_\tau(x)=\mathbb E^{\prob_x}[\mathrm e^{-\beta A_\tau}]
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \ell_{\tau,x}(f)=(\mathrm e^{-\tau H_\beta}f)(x)
\]
for any $f\in L^2(\mathbb R^d)$.
Then  $g_\tau\in L^2(\mathbb R^d) $, and for $x\in\mathbb R^d$ we have
\begin{equation}
 |\ell_{\tau,x}(f)|\le (4\pi\tau)^{-d/4}\|f\|_2.
 
\end{equation}
Moreover, for  $T\ge 2\tau $,
\begin{equation}
 Z_T(\beta,x)=\mathbb E^{\prob_x}[\mathrm e^{-\beta A_T}]
 =\ell_{\tau,x}\!\left(\mathrm e^{-(T-2\tau)H}g_\tau\right).
 
\end{equation}

body:
[Theorem Boundary-Corrected Li--Yau Estimate of arXiv:2608.12376, 'A Heat Kernel Expectation Approach to Boundary-Corrected Li--Yau Estimates for the Dirichl'] Let

\[
w_t=\Delta w
\]

be a positive solution of the Dirichlet heat equation on

\[
\mathbb R^n_+
=
\{x_n>0\},
\]

with nonnegative initial data.

Then for every

\[
x\in\mathbb R^n_+,
\qquad
t>0,
\]

we have

\[
\boxed{
\Delta\log w(x,t)
\geq
-\frac n{2t}
-\frac1{x_n^2}
}.
\]

Equivalently,

\[
\boxed{
\frac{\Delta w}{w}
-
\frac{|\nabla w|^2}{w^2}
\geq
-\frac n{2t}
-\frac1{x_n^2}
}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Boundary-Corrected Li--Yau Estimate

body:
[Thm 9 of arXiv:2609.02686, 'The Bonnet-Myers theorem on Finsler manifolds with integral weighted Ricci curvature bound'] Let $(M, F, m)$ be an $n$-dimensional $(n \geq 2)$  forward complete connected Finsler metric measure manifold with $\Lambda_{F}<\infty$. Assume that $\mathbf{S}\geq -\vartheta$ for some $\vartheta \geq 0$. Let $R_{0}>\Lambda_{F}\pi$ be a constant. Given $p \in (\frac{n}{2}, n]$, $\alpha\in [\frac{1}{2},1)$. Then there exist nonnegative constant $\varepsilon =\varepsilon(n,p,\Lambda_{F},\vartheta,\alpha,R_{0})$ and positive constants $C_{3}=C_{3}(n,p,\Lambda_{F},\vartheta,\alpha,R_{0})$ and $\beta =\beta(n,p,\vartheta,\alpha,R_{0})$ such that when
$$
\overline{\left\|{\rm{Ric}}_{\infty}^{\Lambda_{F}^{2}}\right\|}_{p, R_{0}, \vartheta}\leq \varepsilon ,
$$
we have
\be
{\rm{diam}}(M) \leq \Lambda_{F}^{-1}\left(\pi+C_{3}\overline{\left\|{\rm{Ric}}_{\infty}^{\Lambda_{F}^{2}}\right\|}_{p, R_{0}, \vartheta}^{\beta}\right) \leq \frac{\Lambda_{F}^{-1}(\Lambda_{F}+1)\pi}{2}, 
\ee
where
\beqn
\varepsilon &:=&\min\Big\{\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)^{2-\frac{1}{p}}, C_{3}^{-\frac{1}{\beta}}\left(\frac{(\Lambda_{F}-1)\pi}{2}\right)^{\frac{1}{\beta}}, \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{\frac{2p-1}{p}} D_{1}(n,p,\vartheta,R_{0})^{-\frac{2p-1}{p}}\Big\},\\
C_{3} &:=&\max\Big\{\left(32 e^{\frac{\vartheta R_{0}}{2 p-1}} \Lambda_{F}^{\left(3\vartheta R_{0} b(p,\alpha)+\frac{9n-2p}{2p-1}\right)} D_{2}\right)^{\frac{2p-1}{(2p-1)\vartheta R_{0} b(p,\alpha)+4n-2p}} R_{0},\\
&&\ \ \ \ \ \ \left(2^{8p-3}C_{1}e^{2\vartheta R_{0}}\Lambda_{F}^{3(2p-1)\vartheta R_{0} b(p,\alpha)+8n-1} \right)^{\frac{1}{(2p-1)\vartheta R_{0}b(p,\alpha)+3n-1}} R_{0}^{2},\\
&&\ \ \ \ \ \ \left(2\Lambda_{F}^{-\frac{2p-n}{2p-1}}D_{2}(n,p,\Lambda_{F},\vartheta,\alpha,R_{0})\right)^{-\frac{2p-1}{2p-n}} R_{0}\Big\},\\
\beta &:=& \min\left\{\frac{p}{(2p-1)\vartheta R_{0} b(p,\alpha)+4n-2p}, \ \frac{(n-1)p}{(2p-1)\left[(2p-1)\vartheta R_{0}b(p,\alpha)+3n-1\right]}\right\}.
\eeqn
Furthermore, $M$ is in fact compact.

Then ${\mathcal{C}}_*$ is $S$-cocomplete and the forgetful functor $\textup{fgt}\colon{\mathcal{C}}_*\to{\mathcal{C}}$ admits a $T$-left adjoint $(-)_+$ enjoying the following universal property: for any pointed $S$-cocomplete ${\mathcal{D}}$, restriction along $(-)_+$ defines an equivalence
    \[
        \ul{\textup{Fun}}^\textup{$S$-cc}_T({\mathcal{C}}_*,{\mathcal{D}})\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}
        \ul{\textup{Fun}}^\textup{$S$-cc}_T({\mathcal{C}},{\mathcal{D}}).
    \]
    \begin{proof}
        It is clear that the forgetful functor admits a pointwise left adjoint (given by coproduct with the terminal object), and the Beck--Chevalley condition follows from fiberwise cocompleteness.

        To show that ${\mathcal{C}}_*$ is $S$-cocomplete, we apply Lemma~(lemma:S-cocompleteness-repr of the paper). First note that the composite
        \[
            \PSh(T)^{\textup{op}}\xrightarrow{\;{\mathcal{C}}\;}\CAT_\infty^1\xrightarrow{\;(-)_*\;}\CAT_\infty^*\subset\CAT_\infty,
        \]
        where $\CAT_\infty^1\subset\CAT_\infty$ denotes the subcategory of $\infty$-categories with a terminal object and functors preserving terminal objects, is limit-preserving (as $(-)_*$ is a right adjoint). Thus, this composite describes the limit extension of ${\mathcal{C}}_*$. Given any $Y\in\PSh(T)$ and $(f\colon X\to Y)\in\ul\Spc_{S\triangleright T}(Y)$, we may therefore identify $f^*\colon{\mathcal{C}}_*(Y)\to{\mathcal{C}}_*(X)$ with $f^*\colon{\mathcal{C}}(Y)_{1/}\to{\mathcal{C}}(X)_{1/}$ which has a left adjoint given by the composite
        \[
            {\mathcal{C}}(X)_{1/}\xrightarrow{\;f_!\;}{\mathcal{C}}(Y)_{f_!1/}\xrightarrow{\;\varepsilon_!\;}{\mathcal{C}}(Y)_{1/}.
        \]
        To verify the Beck--Chevalley condition, consider a pullback
        \[
            \begin{tikzcd}
                A'\arrow[r, "t'"]\arrow[d,"s'"'] & B'\arrow[d,"s"]\\
                A\arrow[r,"t"'] & B
            \end{tikzcd}
        \]
        in $\PSh(T)$ with $s\in\ul\Spc_{S\triangleright T}(B)$. Then the Beck--Chevalley map $s'_!t'^*\to t^*s_!$ is a natural transformation of cocontinuous functors ${\mathcal{C}}(B')\to{\mathcal{C}}(A)$; we may therefore check invertibility after applying the equivalence from the previous proposition, i.e.\ after precomposing with $(-)_+\colon{\mathcal{C}}(B)\to{\mathcal{C}}(A)$. However, as Beck--Chevalley maps compose, this fits into a commutative diagram
        \[
            \begin{tikzcd}
                s'_!t^*(-)_+\arrow[r,"\sim"]\arrow[d,"\textup{BC}_!(-)_+"'] &[.5em] s'_!(-)_+t^*\arrow[r,"\textup{BC}_!t^*"] &[.5em] (-)_+s'_!t^*\arrow[d, "(-)_+\textup{BC}_!"]\\
                t^*s_!(-)_+\arrow[r,"t^*\textup{BC}_!"'] & t^*(-)_+s_!\arrow[r,"\sim"'] & (-)_+t^*s_!\rlap,
            \end{tikzcd}
        \]
        where the unlabelled equivalences come from $(-)_+$ being a $T$-functor. The two horizontal Beck--Chevalley maps are equivalences since $(-)_+$ is a left adjoint, as is the right-hand vertical map since ${\mathcal{C}}$ is $S$-cocomplete. Thus, also the left-hand vertical map is an equivalence by 2-out-of-3, finishing the proof that ${\mathcal{C}}_*$ is $S$-cocomplete.

        Finally, we will show that the restriction along $(-)_+$ defines an equivalence ${\textup{Hom}}_{\CAT_T^\text{$S$-cc}}({\mathcal{C}}_*,{\mathcal{D}})\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}{\textup{Hom}}_{\CAT_T^\text{$S$-cc}}({\mathcal{C}},{\mathcal{D}})$; the corresponding claim for param\-etrized functor categories will then follow by replacing ${\mathcal{D}}$ by $\ul{\textup{Fun}}({\mathpalette\ulhelper{A}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}\times[n],{\mathcal{D}})$ for varying $A\in T$, $n\ge0$.

[Dfn 17 of arXiv:2507.08909, 'Annealed almost periodic entropy'] If $S$ is any set (not necessarily finite), $Q$ is a positive semidefinite $S$-by-$S$ matrix, and $E,F,G$ are pairwise disjoint finite subsets of $S$, then the \textbf{conditional log-determinant mutual information between $E$ and $F$ given $G$ in $Q$} is defined by
\[\rmI_Q(E\,;\,F\mid G) := \rmI_{Q'}(E\,;\,F)\]
with $Q' := Q[E\cup F\mid G)]$.
title: Definition 17 of arXiv:2507.08909

Own work, proof (unaudited); standard-form construction, novelty unestablished.
Let p be a Lebesgue density supported on a finite interval [a,b],
p(x)>=m>0 for almost every x in that interval. Assume E u=0,
E u^2=1. No continuity, differentiability, or upper bound on p is
assumed. Define, almost everywhere on its support,

 tau(x)=[integral_x^b y*p(y)dy]/p(x),
 eta(x)=[integral_x^b (y^2-1)*p(y)dy]/p(x),
 zeta(x)=[integral_x^b (tau(y)-1)*p(y)dy]/p(x).       (1)

Then, for every bounded C1 h with bounded derivative,

 E[u*h(u)]=E[tau(u)*h'(u)],
 E[(u^2-1)*h(u)]=E[eta(u)*h'(u)],
 E[(tau(u)-1)*h(u)]=E[zeta(u)*h'(u)],               (2)

and the explicit bounds are

 0<=tau<=1/m, E tau=1,
 |eta|<=2/m, |zeta|<=2/m.                           (3)


Matrix corollary: let U in R^(N by M), V in R^(P by M) be independent iid factor arrays with fixed real laws having the preceding compact-density, centering and variance hypotheses, each with its own positive density floor. Let Z be independent standard Gaussian noise, X=UV^T/sqrt(N), Y=sqrt(s)X+Z, and I be measured in nats. If P/N->alpha>0 and M/N->beta>0 are finite, every limiting upper or lower per-entry information envelope satisfies I(X;Y)/(NP)=beta*s/2-beta^2*s^2/4+beta^3*s^3/6-(beta^4+alpha*beta^2)*s^4/8+O(s^5) as s decreases to zero. The remainder constant depends on the fixed priors and aspect bounds, not the matrix dimensions. No assertion of information-limit uniqueness or discrete-prior coverage is made.
Real Lebesgue density p supported on a finite interval; p>=m>0 almost everywhere
Mean zero and variance one; no continuity, derivative or upper density bound assumed
For the matrix corollary: fixed independent iid real factor laws, Gaussian observation noise, N,P>=2,M>=1, positive finite aspect limits

Let p be a Lebesgue density supported on a finite interval [a,b],

E u^2=1. No continuity, differentiability, or upper bound on p is

 tau(x)=[integral_x^b y*p(y)dy]/p(x),

 E[u*h(u)]=E[tau(u)*h'(u)],
 E[(u^2-1)*h(u)]=E[eta(u)*h'(u)],
 E[(tau(u)-1)*h(u)]=E[zeta(u)*h'(u)],               (2)

and the explicit bounds are

 0<=tau<=1/m, E tau=1,
 |eta|<=2/m, |zeta|<=2/m.                           (3)

Consequently any two fixed independent priors of this form satisfy
every scalar hypothesis of042v2, with T_U=1/m_U,T_V=1/m_V,
e_U<=4/m_U^2,e_V<=4/m_V^2,z_V<=4/m_V^2 and finite fourth moments.
Thus042(4)-(7) and its completely explicit constants apply, proving
the dimension-uniform residual bound and limiting sharp quartic
information expansion on a nonparametric class of two non-Gaussian
factor priors. This is a whole new descriptive range beyond the beta
examples; no finite list of densities is being extrapolated.

## Proof of every kernel hypothesis

Write F_g(x)=integral_x^b g(y)*p(y)dy for centered integrable g.
It is absolutely continuous, F_g'=-g*p almost everywhere, and
F_g(a)=F_g(b)=0. Ordinary integration by parts for an absolutely
continuous function and C1 h gives

 integral_a^b g(x)*p(x)*h(x)dx
 =integral_a^b F_g(x)*h'(x)dx.

All integrals here are absolutely convergent: the interval is compact,
g is integrable, and h,h' are bounded. Dividing by p defines a
measurable kernel almost everywhere; since p>=m>0 it satisfies
|F_g/p|<=E|g|/m. The zero endpoint conditions are essential.

Apply this first with g(x)=x, centered by assumption. The first
identity in (2) follows. For x>=0 the tail integral defining tau is
nonnegative. For x<=0 use mean zero to write it as
-integral_a^x y*p(y)dy, also nonnegative. Cauchy-Schwarz gives
E|u|<=1, proving 0<=tau<=1/m. Choose a bounded C1 function equal
to x on the compact support. The first identity gives E tau=E u^2=1.
In particular the valid numerical bound1/m is automatically at least1.

Apply the same construction to g=x^2-1. It is centered, and
E|u^2-1|<=E u^2+1=2. This proves the eta identity and its bound.
Finally tau-1 is centered because E tau=1, and
E|tau-1|<=E tau+1=2 by nonnegativity. Applying the construction
to this g proves the zeta identity and its bound. Square integrability
of eta,zeta follows from their pointwise bounds. Compact support
pays every factor moment used by042. This proves the claimed
nonparametric matrix-factor corollary without new posterior arguments.

## A discontinuous-density check, not a smoothness assumption

For an exact non-Pearson example take p=1/3 on[-1,1] and p=1/6
on[-2,-1] union[1,2]. Its total mass is1, mean0, variance1,
fourth moment11/5, and density floor m=1/6.
For x>=0 its kernels in (1) are

 0<=x<=1:
 tau=5/4-x^2/2, eta=x-x^3/3, zeta=-x/4+x^3/6;
 1<=x<=2:
 tau=2-x^2/2, eta=2/3+x-x^3/3, zeta=2/3-x+x^3/6.

Extend tau evenly and eta,zeta oddly. The kernels themselves jump
at |x|=1, but the fluxes p*tau,p*eta,p*zeta are continuous there.
Their derivatives are exactly -x*p, -(x^2-1)*p, -(tau-1)*p
on every interval, and all boundary fluxes vanish at -2 and2.
These facts certify (2) for every smooth test, not merely for the
finite monomial checks. scripts/check_density_floor_flux.py verifies
the local rational polynomial identities, joins and endpoint values.

Scope remaining: the density-floor hypothesis excludes atoms and
does not provide constants uniform when m goes to zero. In particular
approximating a discrete law by a sequence of tiny density bridges
does not prove the discrete-prior theorem: the kernel constants in

body: [Lemma 9 (Convergence to sin-tree) of arXiv:2605.21459, 'Network evolution with self-reinforcement'] {\it Suppose that a sequence of trees $(\cT_n)_{n\geq 1}$ converges in probability, in the fringe sense, to $\varpi$. Moreover, suppose that $\varpi$ is a fringe distribution in the sense of Definition~\ref{fringedef}. Then $(\cT_n)_{n\geq 1}$ converges in probability, in the {\em extended} fringe sense, to a limiting infinite random sin-tree $\TT_{\infty}$ whose law $\varpi^{{\rm \sss EF}}$ is uniquely obtained from $\varpi$ via~\eqref{ftoef}.} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 106 of arXiv:2609.03875, 'Measure theory without infinities'] Let $\mf A$ be an HTM, $\sm{\mf A}{k\in K}{f(k)}$, and $x = \sum_{k\in K}f(k)$.
  \begin{enumerate}
  \item[(i)] Let $\sm{\mf A}{k\in K}{g(k)}$. Then $\sum_{k\in K}(f(k) + g(k)) = x + \sum_{k\in K}g(k)$.
  \item[(ii)] Let $\mf B$ be an HTM and $\varphi\colon\mf A\to\mf B$ be a continuous homomorphism. Then $\sum_{k\in K} \varphi(f(k)) = \varphi(x)$.   
  \item [(iii)] Suppose $\mf A$ is an HTG. Then $\sum_{k\in K}(-f(k)) = -x$.
  \item [(iv)] Suppose $\mf A$ is an HTG and $\sm{\mf A}{k\in K}{g(k)}$. Then $\sum_{k\in K}(f(k) - g(k)) = x - \sum_{k\in K}g(k)$.
  \end{enumerate}

[Lemma 8 of arXiv:2605.12269, 'It\^o integral for a two-sided L\'evy process'] Let $h \in \cH^{\otimes k}$ be arbitrary. Then, for any $y \in \bR$,
\[
\bE[I_k(h)|\cF_y]=I_k(h^y), 
\]
where $h^y(x_1,z_1,\ldots,x_k,z_k)=h(x_1,z_1,\ldots,x_k,z_k) 1_{(-\infty,y]^k}(x_1,\ldots,x_k)$.
title: Lemma 8 of arXiv:2605.12269

[Theorem of arXiv:2609.01926, 'On Sum Ranges for $3n$-convergence'] Consider a sequence $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}$ that satisfies:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item[(1)] Each element $a_k \in A$ appears at most once.
    \item[(2)] Each $a_k$ is in exactly two zero triples.
    \item[(3)] Elements have sufficiently fast growth determined by $|a_{3k+1}|,|a_{3k+2}| \geq \sum_{i=1}^{3k} |a_i|$.
\end{enumerate}
Then, $\textnormal{SR}_3(A)$ is not a countable additive subgroup of reals. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Unnumbered theorem of arXiv:2609.01926, 'On Sum Ranges for $3n$-convergence'

[Proposition 11 (\textsf{Proposition~3.2 in \cite{DVZ18}}) of arXiv:2608.12451, '2608.12451'] Let $F=I_q^{\eta}(f)\in L^4(\PP)$ and define $F_t$ by
\eqref{Ft_P}.  Then $(F,F_t)$ is exchangeable and

\noi
\begin{align}
 \frac1t\E[F_t-F | \eta]  &\xrightarrow{t\downarrow 0} -qF  \quad\text{in $L^4(\PP)$},  
 \notag \\
 \frac1t\E[(F_t-F)^2 | \eta]  &\xrightarrow{t\downarrow 0}    2\Gamma(F,F)  \quad \text{in $L^2(\PP)$},  
 \notag \\
 \frac1t\E[(F_t-F)^4] &\xrightarrow{t\downarrow 0}   -4q\,m_4(F)+12\E[F^2\Gamma(F,F)]  \geq0.  
 \notag
\end{align}

\noi
Moreover, the first regression is exact:
$
 \E[F_t-F | \eta]
 =-(1-e^{-qt})F.
$
Moreover, if $F, G$ live in the sum of finitely many chaoses, 
with $F_t, G_t$ defined as above, we have 
\noi
\begin{align}
 \frac1t\E[(F_t-F)(G_t-G) | \eta]
\xrightarrow{t\downarrow 0}    2\Gamma(F,G)  \quad\text{in $L^2(\PP)$}.
 
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \textsf{Proposition~3.2 in \cite{DVZ18}}

[Theorem thm:consistency of arXiv:2510.22778, 'Free denoising diffusion models'] Suppose the family $\{g_{\theta}\}$ is rich enough to contain, for each $t$, the map
$X_{t}\mapsto\Econd{W^{*}(X_{t})}[\sqrt{\alpha_{t}}X_{0}]$. Then any minimiser of
(equation eq:loss of the paper) satisfies, for a.e.\ $t$,
$g_{\theta^{\star}}(X_{t},t)=\Econd{W^{*}(X_{t})}[\sqrt{\alpha_{t}}X_{0}]$ in
$L^{2}(\tau)$, and consequently $\widehat\xi_{t}(X_{t})=\xi_{\mu_{t}}(X_{t})$.
Moreover, for any $g$,
\begin{equation}
  \tau\Big[\big(g(X_{t},t)-\sqrt{\alpha_{t}}X_{0}\big)^{2}\Big]
  =\tau\Big[\big(g(X_{t},t)-\Econd{W^{*}(X_{t})}[\sqrt{\alpha_{t}}X_{0}]\big)^{2}\Big]
  +c_{t},
\end{equation}
with $c_{t}$ independent of $g$, so that (equation eq:loss of the paper) and the (unavailable)
score-matching loss differ by a constant.

body:
[Theorem 61 (Sharp singular Wick multipliers on the torus) of arXiv:2607.16724, 'Algebraic Transfer for Operator-Valued Gaussian Chaoses: Oriented Schatten Profiles and Si'] Let $m\ge2$ and $(m-1)D/(2m)<\sigma\le D/2$, and set
$\beta_m:=m(D/2-\sigma)$.  On
$\mathbb T^D=(\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z)^D$ with normalized Haar measure,
define
\[
 X_N(\theta):=\sum_{|x|\le N}g_x\langle x\rangle^{-\sigma}
 e^{\mathrm i x\cdot\theta},
\]
and define its order-$m$ Wick power by
\[
 V_{m,N}(\theta):=\wick{X_N(\theta)^m}
 =\sum_{x_1,\ldots,x_m}
 \wick{g_{x_1}\cdots g_{x_m}}
  \prod_{j=1}^m\bigl(\langle x_j\rangle^{-\sigma}
  \mathbf1_{\{|x_j|\le N\}}\bigr)
 e^{\mathrm i(x_1+\cdots+x_m)\cdot\theta}.
\]
Here the real isonormal process is extended complex-linearly; thus $X_N$
is generally complex-valued, and no relation between $g_x$ and $g_{-x}$
is imposed.  In particular, this is the complexified real-isonormal model,
not the conjugate-symmetric real Fourier model.
Let $J$ be the Fourier multiplier
$Je^{\mathrm iq\cdot\theta}=\langle q\rangle e^{\mathrm iq\cdot\theta}$.
Write $\norm{f}_{H^t}:=\norm{J^tf}_{L^2}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] Fix $1\le r<\infty$ and $a,b\ge0$.  Then
$J^{-a}M_{V_{m,N}}J^{-b}$ is Cauchy in
$L^2(\Omega;\Sch_r(L^2(\mathbb T^D)))$ if and only if
\[
 a>\beta_m,\qquad b>\beta_m,\qquad
 a+b>\beta_m+\frac Dr,
\]
which is precisely \eqref{eq:all-order-singular-lattice-range}.  Under these
conditions
it converges in every finite $L^p$, converges almost surely in $\Sch_r$,
and satisfies all rates in
Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-singular-lattice-transfer}.
In particular, trace-norm convergence holds exactly when
\[
 a>\beta_m,\qquad b>\beta_m,\qquad a+b>\beta_m+D.
\]

\item[(ii)] For every $\varepsilon>0$,
\begin{equation}

 V_{m,N}\longrightarrow V_m
 \quad\text{in}\quad
 \begin{cases}
  L^2(\Omega;H^{-\beta_m-\varepsilon}(\mathbb T^D)),&\sigma<D/2,\\
  L^2(\Omega;H^{-\varepsilon}(\mathbb T^D)),&\sigma=D/2.
 \end{cases}
\end{equation}
These Sobolev indices are mean-square sharp: the cutoffs are not Cauchy in
$L^2(\Omega;H^{-\beta_m})$ below the endpoint or in
$L^2(\Omega;L^2(\mathbb T^D))$ at the endpoint.

\item[(iii)] Fix $a,b\ge0$.  The cutoffs
$J^{-a}M_{V_{m,N}}J^{-b}$ converge in
$L^2(\Omega;\cL(L^2(\mathbb T^D)))$ to a random compact operator if and
only if
\begin{equation}

 a>\beta_m,\qquad b>\beta_m.
\end{equation}

\item[(iv)] Fix $1\le r<\infty$.  For the balanced sandwich
$a=b=s/2$, $s\ge0$, the exact
finite-$r$ Schatten phase diagram is
\begin{equation}

 s>\max\left\{2\beta_m,\ \beta_m+\frac Dr\right\}
 \quad(\sigma<D/2),
 \qquad
 s>\frac Dr
 \quad(\sigma=D/2).
\end{equation}
In this balanced case, the compactness condition in part~(iii) reduces to
$s>2\beta_m$, equivalently to $s>0$ when $\sigma=D/2$.
The exact trace-class threshold is $s>\beta_m+D$.
Indeed, the local hypothesis gives $\beta_m<D/2$, so this condition already
implies $s>2\beta_m$.
\end{enumerate}

body:
Consider bond first-passage percolation on Z^2 with iid edge weights supported in [a,b], where 0<a<=b<infinity, and fixed distinct vertices u,v. Let X=T(u,v) and choose a measurable canonical topmost minimizing geodesic (atoms and ties are allowed). Partition the edges into deterministic blocks Lambda. For each block independently redraw its weights from the original law, independently of the environment, and write X^Lambda for the passage time with only that block replaced. Let U_Lambda be the event that the original chosen geodesic uses an edge in Lambda. Give the blocks iid Uniform[0,1] labels tau_Lambda independent of all original and redrawn weights. F_t reveals each labeled block and its original/redrawn weight pair when tau_Lambda<=t; equivalently, for the probabilities of U_Lambda one may reveal only original weights. Define A2=sum_Lambda E[1_U_Lambda (X^Lambda-X)^2], A2plus=sum_Lambda E[((X^Lambda-X)^+)^2], A4=sum_Lambda E[1_U_Lambda ((X^Lambda-X)^+)^4], and Pbar(kappa)=sum_Lambda E[P(U_Lambda|F_(1-kappa))^2]. For every 0<kappa<1, Var(X)<=kappa A2plus+sqrt(A4 Pbar(kappa))<=kappa A2+sqrt(A4 Pbar(kappa)). Positivity and boundedness localize all relevant paths to a deterministic finite edge set, so only finitely many blocks contribute. The proof needs independent blocks, off-geodesic monotonicity and conditional expectations; isotropy and FKG are not assumptions.
iid edge weights in [a,b] with 0<a<=b<infinity
