body:
[Theorem 2 (Growing-block colored shuffle profiles) of arXiv:2606.29530, 'Cutoff profiles for colored top-\texorpdfstring{$m$}{m}-to-random shuffles with growing bl'] Fix $p\ge1$.  Let $m_n,k_n$ satisfy the assumptions of Theorem \ref{thm:coupon-poisson-intro}, and set
\[
        M_n=(Q_{n,p}^{(m_n)})^{*k_n},\qquad U_n=U_{n,p}.
\]
Then, for every continuous $\Phi:[0,\infty)\to\R$ of polynomial growth,
\[
        \mathcal I_{\Phi}(M_n,U_n)\to \mathcal I_{\Phi,p}(\lambda).
\]
In particular, with $c=-\log\lambda$,
\[
        \normTV{M_n-U_n}\to f_p(c),
        \qquad
        f_p(c):=\sum_{\ell=0}^{\infty}a_{\ell,p}\bigl(s_{\ell,p}(e^{-c})-1\bigr)_+.
\]
Moreover,
\[
        \sepd(M_n,U_n)\to
        \begin{cases}
        1-e^{-\lambda}(1+\lambda),&p=1,\\
        1-e^{-\lambda},&p\ge2.
        \end{cases}
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Growing-block colored shuffle profiles

body:
[Lem Lemma: Inverse limit approximation of arXiv:2605.16921, '${\ASL_n}(\mathbb Z)$ invariant random subsets of $\mathbb Z^n$'] Let $Y$ be an ergodic $\mathbb{Z}^d$-system with $f_1,f_2 \in L^\infty(Y)$ taking values in $[0, 1]$, and let $\underline{Y_1}, \underline{Y_2}$ be the point processes obtained by drawing $y \in Y$ at random and keeping each $t \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ independently with probability $f_1((-t) \cdot y)$ and $f_2((-t) \cdot y)$ respectively. 
    Then there is a coupling of $\underline{Y_1}$ and $\underline{Y_2}$ such that
    $$d(\underline{Y_1} \Delta \underline{Y_2}) \leq \|f_1-f_2 \|_2$$
    almost surely - where for a subset $A \subset \mathbb{Z}^d$, $d(A)$ denotes the \emph{density}
    $$ d(A) = \limsup_{N \rightarrow \infty} \frac{\vert A \cap [-N,N]^d\vert }{(2N+1)^d}.$$
title: Lem Lemma: Inverse limit approximation of arXiv:2605.16921

[Theorem thm1 of arXiv:2607.12459, 'Renormalisation of Inhomogeneous Random Graphs'] {\bf [Averaged homogeneous attractor]}

Suppose that
\[
(\Box) \qquad
\begin{aligned}
&0 < \mathbb{E}_X\big[g^{\neq}(X_1,X'_1)\big] < \infty,\\
&0 \leq \mathbb{E}_X\big[g^{=}(X_1)\big] < \infty,\\
&k^{-2} \sum_{i=1}^k g^{\neq}(X_i,X_i)  \xrightarrow[k\to\infty]{\mathbb P} 0,
\end{aligned}
\]
where \(X'_1\) is an independent copy of \(X_1\) and $(X_i)_{i\in\mathbb{N}}$ are i.i.d.\ copies of $X_1$. Put
\[
q^{\neq} = \mathbb{E}_X\big[g^{\neq}(X_1,X'_1)\big],
\qquad
q^{=}=\mathbb{E}_X\big[g^{=}(X_1)\big],
\]
and
\[
p^{\neq} = 1-\mathrm{e}^{-q^{\neq}},
\qquad
p^{=} = 1-\mathrm{e}^{-\frac12(q^{\neq}+q^{=})}.
\]
Then
\[

[Satz thm:HigherOrder2 of arXiv:2507.08692, 'Some notes on higher order concentration of measure'] Given Assumptions (ass:Set2 of the paper) (1)--(3), let $f\colon \Omega \to {\mathbb R}$ be a suitable function with ${\mathbb E} f = 0$.
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item Assuming that $\lVert \Gamma^{(j)} f \rVert_1 \le \sigma^{d-j}$ for all $j=1,\ldots,d-1$ and $\lVert \Gamma^{(d)} f \rVert_\infty \le 1$, it holds that
		\[
		\int \exp\Big\{\frac{c_{p,d,r_0,L}}{\sigma^p} |f|^{p/d} \Big\} d\mu \le 2,
		\]
		where a possible choice of the constant $c_{p,d,r_0,L}$ is given by
		\[
		c_{p,d,r_0,L} = \frac{(r_0^{1/p}-1)^p}{2e\max(L^{1/d}, L)^pr_0\max(r_0,p/d)}.
		\]
		\item For any $t\ge 0$, it holds that
		\[
		\mu(|f| \ge t)\le
		2 \exp\Big\{- \frac{C_{p,r_0,L}}{(d\sigma)^p} \min\Big(\min_{k=1, \ldots,d-1} \Big(\frac{t}{\lVert \Gamma^{(k)} f \rVert_1}\Big)^{p/k}, \Big(\frac{t}{\lVert \Gamma^{(d)} f \rVert_\infty}\Big)^{p/d}\Big)\Big\},
		\]
		where a possible choice of the constant $C_{p,r_0,L}$ is given by
		\[
	    C_{p,r_0,L} = \frac{\log(2)}{r_0(Le)^p}.
		\]
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Let X be a smooth projective algebraic variety over the complex numbers. Its cohomology group H^{2p}(X,C) decomposes by the Hodge decomposition into subspaces H^{q,q'}; a rational Hodge class is a class of type (p,p) that also lies in the rational cohomology H^{2p}(X,Q). The Hodge conjecture asserts that every rational Hodge class is a rational linear combination of cohomology classes of complex algebraic subvarieties of X of codimension p, that is, every rational Hodge class is algebraic. It is OPEN in general, proved only in special cases such as p=1, the Lefschetz (1,1) theorem, and is one of the Clay Mathematics Institute Millennium Prize Problems.

[Theorem thm:spectral-rank of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] For every $h\geq2$,
\begin{align}
 \mathcal R^{[0]}(h,4)&=\{M_h\},\\
 \mathcal R^{[1]}(h,4)&=
 \{M_h-M_{h-j}:2\leq j\leq h\},\\
 \mathcal R^{[2]}(h,4)&=
 \mathcal R(h,4)\setminus
 \bigl(\mathcal R^{[0]}(h,4)\cup\mathcal R^{[1]}(h,4)\bigr).
 
\end{align}
The first two layers have cardinalities $1$ and $h-1$ exactly.  As
$h\to\infty$, the third has cardinality
$|\mathcal R(h,4)|-h=\Theta(h^3)$; in particular, all but a
$\Theta(h^{-2})$ proportion of the distinct values have minimum rank two.
Moreover, as $h\to\infty$,
\[
 \left|\mathcal R^{[2]}(h,4)\cap
 \left[M_h-\frac{h^3}{250},M_h-\frac{h^3}{400}\right]\right|
 \gg h^3.
\]
For every rank-two cardinality, the realization count is an exact
quasipolynomial in $q-1$ of degree two and the normalized shape locus is
zero-dimensional.  Such a cardinality has no realization of normalized
diameter exceeding $h^2$; conversely, the rank-zero and rank-one labels are
exactly those admitting arbitrarily large diameter.  The largest rank-two
label is $M_h-2$, whose least possible normalized diameter is
$1+\binom{h+1}{2}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma equiv-spectra-homotopy-po of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Pushouts along unbased level h-cofibrations are homotopy pushouts in the $G$-equivariant model structure.
    \begin{proof}
        Consider a pushout as depicted on the left, where $i$ is an unbased level h-cofibration, and pick a factorization of $f$ as a cofibration $j$ followed by a \emph{level} weak equivalence $g$, leading to the iterated pushout depicted on the right:
        \[
            \begin{tikzcd}
                A\arrow[r, "f"]\arrow[dr,phantom,"\ulcorner"{very near end}]\arrow[d,"i"'] & B\arrow[d] &[3em] A\arrow[dr,phantom,"\ulcorner"{very near end}]\arrow[r, "j"]\arrow[d,"i"'] & X\arrow[dr,phantom,"\ulcorner"{very near end}]\arrow[d,"i'"]\arrow[r,"g","\sim"'] & B\arrow[d]\\
                C\arrow[r] & D & C\arrow[r]& Y\arrow[r,"h"'] & D\rlap.
            \end{tikzcd}
        \]
        If $H\subset G$ and $V$ is any $H$-representation, then $i(V)$ is in particular an h-cofibration in $\textbf{\textup{$\bm H$-Top}}$, whence so is $i'(V)$. As $g(V)$ is an $H$-equivariant weak equivalence, so is $h(V)$ by Lemma~(lemma:h-cof-compute-po of the paper), i.e.\ $h$ is again a $G$-equivariant level weak equivalence. This in particular shows that the original square is a homotopy pushout.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Lemma lem:markovian_cpi_exploration of arXiv:2609.04138, 'The conformally invariant metric on $\CLE_4$ I:\\ subsequential limits of the non-simple C'] Fix $z \in \overline{\BD}$ and let $\eta_z$ denote the branch of the CPI exploration targeted at $z$ of an iterated $\cwBCLE_{\kappa^\prime}(0)$/$\ccwBCLE_\kappa(-\kappa/2)$ construction. Let also $\tau$ be a stopping time for $\eta_z$ such that $\eta_z(\tau)$ is not on a simple loop a.s. Let $D_{\tau}$ denote the connected component of $\BD \setminus \eta_z([0,\tau])$ containing $z$. Then, we have that the iterated process of loops in $D_{\tau}$ obtained from the restriction to $D_{\tau}$ of the CPI exploration tree rooted at $\eta_z(\tau)$ has the law of an iterated $\cwBCLE_{\kappa^\prime}(0)$/$\ccwBCLE_\kappa(-\kappa/2)$ construction on $D_{\tau}$ conditionally on $\eta_z|_{[0,\tau]}$. Moreover, the simple true loops obtained from the new construction are the same as the simple loops of the original $\cwBCLE_{\kappa^\prime}(0)$/$\ccwBCLE_\kappa(-\kappa/2)$ construction which are contained in $D_{\tau}$.

body:
[Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2411.19163, '\bfseries Random polytopes in convex bodies:\\ Bridging the gap between extremal container'] Fix integers $d\geq 2$ and $m\in\{1,\ldots,d\}$, and an $m$-tuple $\operatorname{bd}=(d_1,\dotsc,d_m)\in \mathbb{N}^m$, such that $d_1+\ldots+d_m = d$. Further, let $\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_m\geq 0$ and set ${\boldsymbol{\beta}}:=(\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_m)$. We consider the random block-beta polytope $\mathcal{P}_{n,\operatorname{bd}}^{\boldsymbol{\beta}}$ and define $k_{\max} := \max\limits_{i=1,\dotsc,m} k_i$ and $\#k_{\max} := \#\left\{i: k_i = k_{\max}\right\}$. 
Then,
\begin{equation*}
    \mathbb{E} f_{d-1}(\mathcal{P}_{n,\operatorname{bd}}^{{\boldsymbol{\beta}}}) \asymp n^{\frac{k_{\max}-1}{k_{\max}+1}} (\ln n)^{\#k_{\max}-1}.
\end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2411.19163

body:
[Lemma 27 (BDG inequality) of arXiv:2511.04938, 'Uniform dimension theorems for parabolic SPDEs'] Whenever $Z=\{Z(s\,,y)\}_{s>0,y\in\T}$ is a predictable random field
	with values in the space of $p\times p$ matrices, 
	\[
		\left\| \int_{(0,t)\times\T} G_{t-s}(x\,,y) Z(s\,,y)\,\xi(\d s\,\d y)\right\|_k^2
		\le 4kp\int_0^t\d s\int_{\T}\d y\ [G_{t-s}(x\,,y)]^2
		\left\| Z(s\,,y)\right\|_k^2,
	\]
	for every $t>0$, $x\in\T$, and $k\in[2\,,\infty)$.

Let (X, Y, Z) be jointly Gaussian in R^a x R^b x R^c with covariance blocks A = Cov(X), C = Cov(Y), G = Cov(Z), B = Cov(X, Y), E = Cov(X, Z), F = Cov(Y, Z), possibly singular, and put A_c = A - E G^+ E^T, C_c = C - F G^+ F^T, B_c = B - E G^+ F^T and K = [[A_c, B_c], [B_c^T, C_c]]. Then I(X; Y | Z) is finite if and only if rank K = rank A_c + rank C_c, and in that case I(X; Y | Z) = (1/2) log(pdet(A_c) pdet(C_c) / pdet(K)), where pdet is the product of the nonzero eigenvalues; otherwise it is +infinity.

body:
[Corollary 13 (Exact radial flux transport) of arXiv:2609.00571, '\textbf{Shape Optimization and Bernoulli Free Boundary Problems\\ for the Riemannian $p$-L'] Let $L'=f(L)$ and let
\[
Q_\varepsilon
:=
-\partial_{\nu_g}U(L')
=
-|U'(L')|
\]
be the geometric boundary flux of the transported radial state.
Then
\begin{equation}
\boxed{
Q_\varepsilon
=
\frac{-u'(L)}{f'(L)}
=
\frac{-u'(L)}
{A\left(J_{\mathcal R}(L')/J_{\mathcal R}(L)\right)^{1/(p-1)}}.
}

\end{equation}
Thus the transported boundary flux is determined exactly by the
radial derivative of the contraction at the outer boundary. In
particular, if $f'(L)\to1$, then
\[
Q_\varepsilon\longrightarrow -u'(L).
\]
More generally, the flux error is explicitly
\[
\left|Q_\varepsilon+u'(L)\right|
=
|u'(L)|
\left|
\frac1{f'(L)}-1
\right|.
\]

[Proposition 6 of arXiv:2608.19976, 'Random valuations'] Assume that $\Phi$ is a random valuation such that almost all of its
  realisations are continuous translation-invariant valuations. Then
  \begin{equation}
    
    \Phi(K)=\sum_{i=0}^d \Phi_i(K),
  \end{equation}
  where each $\Phi_i$ is a random valuation such that almost all its
  realisations are continuous, translation-invariant valuations
  which are homogeneous of degree~$i$, that is,
  $\Phi_i(cK)=c^i\Phi_i(K)$ a.s.\ for all $K\in\Kd$ and $c>0$.

[Corollary 27 of arXiv:2604.03213, 'Asymptotic expansion for transport maps \\ between laws of multimatrix models'] Let $f\in\cC^k(X_1,\dots,X_d)$ then if $f^j$ is the function defined in Corollary \ref{cor:taylorineq}, $g_{a,b}\in\cC^k(X_1,\dots,X_d)$ for $a\in [0,j],\ b\in [1,d] $ , then
    $$ \cg \coloneqq f\circ\big( ( g_{a,b} )_{0\leq a\leq j, 1\leq b\leq d} \big)$$
    belongs to $\cC^k(X_1,\dots,X_d)$. Besides, for some constant $C_k$,
    \begin{equation}
        
        \norm{\cg}_{\cC^{k-j},R} \leq C_k \norm{f}_{\cC^k,S} \left( \sup_{1\leq a\leq j}\ \sum_{b=1}^d\ \norm{g_{a,b}}_{\cC^k,R} \right)^j,
    \end{equation}
    where
    $$S\coloneqq \sup_{1\leq b\leq d} \sum_{a=1}^d \norm{g_{0,b}}_{0,R}.$$

[Lemma 22 of arXiv:2609.01362, '{Double cluster swapping for spin models: \\Pfaffian relations and sharpness}'] Let $A,B \subset V$ be disjoint and also let $U \subset V$ be disjoint from $A$. Let $k$ be the minimum size of a set $K \subset U$ separating $A$ from $B$.
	Then, there exists a collection of pairwise $U$-disjoint paths $\path_1,\ldots,\path_k$ from $A$ to $B$. 	
	If there is no such set, then there is a path $\tau$ from $A$ to $B$ avoiding $U$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm 10 of arXiv:2608.12804, 'Scaling Limits for Ising Models on Inhomogeneous Random Graphs and Applications'] The conditional law of $S_N$ given $A_N$, viewed as a
$\mathcal P(D[0,1])$-valued random probability measure, where
$D[0,1]$ is equipped with the Skorokhod topology and
$\mathcal P(D[0,1])$ with the corresponding topology of weak convergence,
converges weakly in probability to the law of $X$. In particular, the
unconditional laws of $S_N$ converge weakly to the law of $X$ as probability
measures on $D[0,1]$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Method: Exact integral manipulation, Palm calculus, mass transport, limiting obstruction or conditional construction Result: Let V be typical-cell volume and V0 the zero-cell volume. Volume bias gives E V0=E V^2/E V, while mass conservation gives E V=1/lambda. Therefore E V0-E V=lambda*Var(V) exactly whenever these moments are finite. If a finite-intensity coupling produces a nonnegative excess D_lambda converging in law to the proposed ideal-cell excess D, then Fatou gives only E D<=liminf E D_lambda. A uniform bound on E D_lambda^(1+epsilon) would supply the missing uniform integrability and hence the desired equality of limits. Check: Substituting E V=1/lambda into the variance decomposition cancels the squared mean term exactly. Nonnegative variables equal to n with probability 1/n and zero otherwise show why weak convergence alone cannot pass the expected excess to the limit. Obstruction: Neither a suitable finite-intensity excess coupling nor uniform integrability is proved. The algebraic variance identity is known Palm calculus and is not claimed as a solution.

body:
[Lem 28 of arXiv:2608.05185, '\large\bf ON THE HEAT FLOW CONJECTURE FOR RANDOM MATRICES'] There is a unique probability measure \(\mu\) whose Cauchy transform, in
the convention
\[
 \C_+=\{w\in\C:\Im w>0\},
 \qquad
 \C_-=\{w\in\C:\Im w<0\},
\]
satisfies
\[
 m(z)=\int_{\R}\frac{\dd\mu(x)}{z-x},
 \qquad z\in\C_+.
\]
This transform solves the Pastur equation
\begin{equation}
 m(z)=\int_{\R}\frac{\dd\mu_0(a)}{z-a-sm(z)}.
\end{equation}
Almost surely,
\[
 L_{\mathbf{B}_N}\overset{\mathrm{w}}{\longrightarrow}\mu.
\]
The deterministic mean measures satisfy
\[
 \mathbb{W}_1(\overline{\mu}_N,\mu)\longrightarrow0.
\]
The measure \(\mu\) is compactly supported, is absolutely continuous, and
has density at most \(1/(\pi\sqrt{s})\).  This measure is the additive free
convolution \(\mu_0\boxplus\mathfrak{sc}_s\).

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Controlled generators, exact finite-state diagnostic, coupling, renewal reward or capacity comparison Result: For an absolutely continuous size law with hazard h, a job at attained service a allocated b servers completes at instantaneous rate h(a)*s(b), while its age advances at rate s(b). A formal controlled generator therefore has both an age-drift term s(b)*partial_a V and a completion term h(a)*s(b)*(V_after_departure-V). Maximizing the departure rate alone drops the learning and continuation terms. The common exponential case removes age learning but does not justify that omission for a general size law. Check: Conditional survival over work da is 1-h(a)*da+o(da); substituting da=s(b)*dt derives both generator terms from the same clock. A nonexponential two-point law instead requires jump boundary conditions, so the density formula is explicitly limited. Obstruction: No solution of the infinite-state average-cost control equation or verification theorem is supplied.

Let $\nu_1$ denote the number of offspring of individual 1 (arbitrarily
labelled) in an exchangeable Cannings population  model of genetic
reproduction for a haploid population  of constant population size
$N$. Suppose 
\be
\lim_{N\to \infty}~ c_N~ =~ 0,

\be
   \lim_{N\to \infty} \frac{(N)_2\ensuremath{\mathds{E}\left[ (\nu_1)_2(\nu_2)_2  \right]} }{ (N)_4c_N } = 0,
\ee
and there exists a finite measure $\Lambda$ on the unit interval $[0,1]$ such
that for $x \in (0,1]$ fixed
\be
   \lim_{N\to \infty} \frac{N}{c_N}\ensuremath{\mathds{P}\left( \nu_1 > Nx \right)} = \int_x^1 y^{-2} \Lambda(dy),
\ee
then we have convergence to a $\Lambda$-coalescent. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Cor 6 of arXiv:2608.30554, 'Strong law of large numbers for generalized operator means II'] Let $f \colon (0,\infty) \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ be an operator monotone function such that $f(1) = 0$ and  $$\int_\mathbb{P} \|f(y)\| \: d\mu(y) < \infty. $$

body: [Lemma lem-disconnect-infty of arXiv:2604.17170, 'CaTherine wheels from trees and Liouville quantum gravity'] The following is true a.s. Let $\sigma : [0,\infty)\to\mathbb C$ be a $D$-geodesic from some point to $\infty$ and let $t > 0$. Then there is no path from any point of $\sigma(0,t)$ to any point of $\sigma(t,\infty)$ in $Z_\infty- \{\sigma(t)\}$. In particular, every point of $Z_\infty$ is a cut point and there is a unique path in $Z_\infty$ between any two points of $Z_\infty$, modulo time change.

In that case s and t induce norms on V/ker s and W/ker t, A induces a linear map between these quotients, and the least such C is that map's operator norm.

Fix K>=1 and independent iid factor arrays U in R^(N by M),V in R^(P by M) from fixed centered variance-one real laws with finite absolute moments of order2K+2. Aspect ratios P/N,M/N stay in compact subsets of(0,infinity). For X=UV^T/sqrt(N), the first K right Taylor coefficients a_j(N) at s=0 of I(X;sqrt(s)X+Z)/(NP) differ from their Gaussian-factor values by O_K(1/N); odd moments need not vanish. If aspect ratios converge, each coefficient has a prior-independent limit. The core double-cover st-order lemma031 pays every higher-block term, including local bridges. The explicit finite-size remainder is at most [2^K(2K)!/(2(K+1)!)] E||vec X||^(2K+2)s^(K+1)/(NP), for s>=0. This remainder is not uniform in dimension. No thermodynamic expansion, exchanged limits, nonzero means, triangular-array priors or first prior-dependent limiting order is asserted. Novelty unestablished.
K fixed positive integer
Independent factor arrays with fixed iid centered real variance-one entry laws
Both factor laws have finite absolute moments of order2K+2
P/N and M/N bounded above and away from zero
Independent standard Gaussian channel noise; natural logarithms
Coefficient limits additionally require convergence of the aspect ratios

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:2236018031d6fd49ad182ce32eb57039da01f4d03f5d86784b25360fef27f9c3","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/22/2236018031d6fd49ad182ce32eb57039da01f4d03f5d86784b25360fef27f9c3.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:13469eb43ce2832dcdec7940e941823fddca997fdd31a9e3d4f7045f3065ea4d","bundle_entry_key":"asymmetric-iid-matrix-factors-universal-fixed-information-coefficients-w718","bundle_id":"population.t287-general-core-cover-asymmetric-coefficients-v1","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Graph cycle ranks and extensive-rank Gaussian-channel information","draft":"w718/bundle_011.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.gaussian_channels:asymmetric-iid-matrix-factors-universal-fixed-information-coefficients-w718","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Fixed-order coefficients for centered asymmetric iid matrix factors

Target1 partial result. Proof draft, UNAUDITED; novelty is unestablished.
The new ingredient is the general core double-cover lemma in
core_double_cover_st_order.md. It replaces the symmetry/Euler-circuit
restriction of claim011, not the finite-dimensional Taylor machinery.

## 1. Statement and scope

Fix K>=1. Let U in R^(N by M) and V in R^(P by M) be independent
arrays with iid entries within each array from fixed centered real
laws of variance one. Assume both laws have finite absolute moments
of order 2K+2. No symmetry or vanishing odd moment is assumed. Suppose
P/N and M/N remain in compact subsets of (0,infinity). Put

    X=UV^T/sqrt(N),     i_N(s)=I(X;sqrt(s)X+Z)/(NP),

with independent standard real Gaussian Z. Write a_j(N) for the right
Taylor coefficient of s^j at zero, and a_j^G(N) for the corresponding
Gaussian-factor product with exactly the same N,P,M. For 1<=j<=K,

    |a_j(N)-a_j^G(N)| <= C_K/N.                         (1)

The constant depends on K, the compact aspect-ratio ranges and the
two factor laws' moments through order 2K+2, but not N,P,M. If the
ratios converge to positive finite limits, each a_j(N) converges and
its limit is the same as for Gaussian factors.

For each finite size and s>=0, the explicit remainder is

 |i_N(s)-sum_(j=1)^K a_j(N)s^j|
 <= A_K E||vec X||^(2K+2) s^(K+1)/(NP),
 A_K=2^K (2K)!/[2(K+1)!].                              (2)

This is NOT a size-uniform bound, and (1) does NOT prove a high-noise
expansion of lim_N i_N. In particular it does not find, or exclude,
a prior-dependent coefficient after exchanging these limits.
Nonzero factor means and dimension-dependent factor laws are not
asserted here. A fixed-positive-SNR projection argument is insufficient
to control their Taylor coefficients at zero.

## 2. Finite-dimensional coefficient representation

Use the finite-vector Taylor and cumulant representation underlying
claims004/011. Centered isotropic X has covariance b I, b=M/N. Under
the standardization a=s/(1+bs), the formal relative Gaussian density
is generated by

    exp(sum_(k>=3) C_k:t^k a^(k/2)/k!).

The symmetry restriction is absent: odd k are included. At any fixed
order<=K, only finitely many terms and Wick pairings occur. A full
pairing has an even total number of endpoints, so its power of a is
an integer even when individual tensor degrees are odd.

Normal ordering excludes self-pairings within a Hermite factor.
Claim010's chromatic-polynomial identity applies to arbitrary degrees
k>=3, not just even degrees. After its exact entropy cancellations,
only loopless connected no-articulation contraction graphs G remain,
with v>=2 tensor vertices and e Wick edges. The Gaussian covariance
part is exactly (NP/2)log(1+bs) and is common to both factor laws.

For bounded nonsymmetric vector inputs the same finite Hermite
calculation is justified by Gaussian L^p domination. Centered bounded
vector truncations, with covariance whitening, converge in L^(2K+2)
to X. Their finitely many moment polynomials converge. The posterior
replica streaming bound used in claim011 does not use symmetry:

    |F^(K)(s)|<=2^K(2K)! E||X||^(2K+2),
    F(s)=E||E[X|sqrt(s)X+Z]||^2,
    I^(K+1)(s)=-F^(K)(s)/2.

Taylor's integral remainder gives (2). Passing through these finite
identities requires neither an analytic unbounded-input series nor
an exponential-moment assumption. These are inherited analytic
ingredients; their proofs remain independently unaudited.

## 3. Raw-factor blocks and exact index exponent

At a tensor vertex of degree k, write W_(ij)=u_i v_j for one hidden
column. Its joint cumulant is the sum over partitions rho,sigma of
the k positions with connected join of

    product_(A in rho) kappa_(|A|)(U) delta_row(A)
    times product_(B in sigma) kappa_(|B|)(V) delta_col(B).

Centering kills singleton blocks. It does not kill odd blocks. All
these finite moment identities remain valid under the stated moment
assumptions. Summing the independent hidden columns contributes M per
tensor, while the normalization contributes N^(-k/2). If c_i,c_j
are the global row and column equality-class counts, the exact index
factor for a completely contracted term is

    M^v N^(c_i-e) P^c_j.                                (3)

The proof in core_double_cover_st_order.md applies directly: its B
has the c_i+c_j equality classes as vertices and the e Wick pairs as
edges, and its label graph is G. Each local raw graph is connected
with minimum degree two, including when it has bridges. The local
positions map to DISTINCT edges of B because G has no self-loops.

Therefore c_i+c_j-e+v<=2 always. If any raw block has size>=3, its
local graph has cycle rank>=2, and the strict bound is

    c_i+c_j-e+v<=1.                                     (4)

This is the new step that pays all odd cumulants without assuming
local Euler circuits or bridgelessness.

## 4. Comparison and coefficient limits

Every all-pair raw term has the same value for the two factor laws,
since their second cumulants are one. Every other term contains a
higher block, so by (3)/(4), after division by NP it is O(1/N).
There are finitely many graphs and raw partitions at each fixed K;
their moment and aspect-ratio factors are bounded under the stated
hypotheses. This proves (1), including after the finite change from
a to s. For Gaussian factors, the same weak exponent bound shows that
each coefficient is a finite sum of integer powers of N with power
at most zero after normalization, with coefficients polynomial in
M/N and P/N and fixed finite rational combinatorial constants. Hence
it has a limit when the ratios converge. Equation(1) transfers it.

## 5. Exact obstruction remaining for Target1

The explicit moment in (2) grows with dimension; it has not been
replaced by a connected-posterior estimate of order NP. The result
therefore pays the formal fixed-order asymmetric power counting,
but not an expansion with a uniform thermodynamic remainder. It
cannot identify a first unsuppressed fourth-cumulant term in the
limiting information by exchanging limits silently.

Least trusted inherited step: the finite entropy chromatic reduction
claim010 together with the finite-moment Taylor extension. Least
trusted new translation step: looplessness is essential for the
edge-bijection in the double-cover graph lemma. No independent PASS
has been received for these dependencies.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:5dc5e55fd52de17190c46ce82824b733f184b71e297dcfbd13ccb4dc60f2d10c","revision_digest":"sha256:8ecf2e0a76d024a81709752977204c2dcd7494bda210c852621f6d0675f242f3","source_id":"owner:w718:T287:asymmetric-iid-matrix-factors-universal-fixed-information-coefficients-w718","source_revision":"2026-10-21-v1","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

AUTHOR-CHECKED; independent w346 audit PENDING. Let Z be a finite-type Galton-Watson process with finite mean matrix M
(row i lists expected type-j children) and finite deterministic initial population z.
Let R be the forward-reachable types from the support of z. If rho(M_R)<1,
then w=(I-M_R)^(-1)*1 is finite, positive, and M_R*w=w-1.
The expected total population is z_R*w<infinity, hence extinction occurs almost surely.
Unreachable supercritical types do not affect this conclusion; positive regularity
is unnecessary. This is a branching-process certificate, not a full interpretation criterion.
Finite type set and finite offspring means
Correct initial support and mean matrix
Pivot interpretation requires separate identification of the process

body:
[Corollary cor:density of arXiv:2512.17808, 'Zeros of polynomial powers under the heat flow'] Let $D\subset \mathbb{C}\setminus B$ be a simply connected domain such that $\Gamma_{i,j}^D:=\{z\in D:G(z,u_t^i(z))=G(z,u_t^j(z))\}\neq \emptyset$ for exactly one pair $1\leq i <j \leq d+1$  and $\Gamma_{i,j}^D$  is a real analytic curve. For simplicity, let us assume that $\Gamma_{i,j}^D$ separates $D=D_i\cup D_j\cup \Gamma_{i,j}^D$ into two simply connected open domains $D_i,D_j$. Then, $\mu_t(\Gamma_{i,j}^D)>0$ if and only if the branch of the maximally relevant saddle point switches at $\Gamma_{i,j}^D$, which means that  $u_t^*(z) = u_t^i(z)$ for $z\in D_i$ and $u_t^*(z) = u_t^j(z)$ for $z\in D_j$. In this case, the density $\varrho:\Gamma_{i,j}^D\to\mathbb{R}$ of $\mu_t$ (restricted to $\Gamma_{i,j}^D$) with respect to the length measure on $\Gamma_{i,j}^D$ is given by
	$$\varrho(z)=\frac {|u_t^i(z)-u_t^j(z)|} {2\pi t}.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary cor:density of arXiv:2512.17808

[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2609.01362, '{Double cluster swapping for spin models: \\Pfaffian relations and sharpness}'] Let $\langle \cdot \rangle_G$ be a classical spin system on a finite graph $G=(V,E)$ 
    satisfying Pfaffian relations on $W\subseteq V$. 
    Then, 
	\begin{itemize}
		\item 
    there exists a set $U \subseteq V$ of vertices of Ising type, 
    such that the path-induced graph $G'$ from $G$ by $U\cup W$ is a planar graph with $W$ lying on one of its faces.
    		\item 
			Moreover, there exists an Ising model $\sigma \sim \left< \cdot  \right>_{G'}$ on $G'$ with ferromagnetic (nonnegative) coupling constants $J'$ such that 
    for all $I \subset W$,
    \[
        {\Big \langle \prod_{v \in I} {\vp_{v} } \Big\rangle_G}
	= \Big \langle \prod_{v\in I} \sigma_{v}\Big \rangle_{G'} .
    \]
	\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 3 of arXiv:2609.01362

\[2d(n-d)+2m_1+k+1\leq \TC(C(Gr_d(\CC^n), S(\overline{m}(k))))\leq 2(d(n-d)+ m_1+k).\]

	\[
			U_\mu( A\times [t-q,t]) = \pi(A) \frac{q}{\E_\pi[Z_1]} + \Or( \e^{- \eps t})
	\]

	\[
		U_\mu\bigl(A\times [t-q,t]\bigr) = \Or(\e^{-\eps|t|}).
	\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition prop:order_dependence of arXiv:2607.22908, 'Epidemic Phase Transitions in the Zero-Range Process'] Let $(\xi_t)_{t\ge 0}$ be the
  slot-priority dynamics. Fix a priority level $r^\star\in \mathbb{R}$, and let $\pi^\star:
  \Xi_{\text{packed}} \to \mathbb{N}_0^{\mathbb{Z}^d}$ be the projection that counts particles with priority at most
  $r^\star$, defined as $\pi^\star(\xi)(x) = n_{\le r^\star}(\xi, x)$. The projected process
  $\zeta_t = \pi^\star(\xi_t)$ satisfies:
  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item $(\zeta_t)_{t\ge 0}$ is a zero-range process.
    \item For each realization, the trajectory of $(\zeta_t)_{t\ge
      0}$ is a deterministic function of the initial configuration $\zeta_0$ and the full set of
      Poisson clocks $(\mathcal{P}_{x,y}^i)_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d, y\sim x, i\in\mathbb{N}}$.
  \end{enumerate}
title: Order dependence

[Proposition P:arc-endpoint-safe-partition of arXiv:2607.15966, 'Canonical Mandelbrot Cascades on Curves Are Rajchman'] For every \(\xi\neq0\),
\[
        \chi_{\xi,0}(t)
        +
        \chi_{\xi,1}(t)
        +
        \chi_{\xi,\mathrm{sd}}(t)
        +
        \sum_{d\in \mathfrak D_{\xi}}\chi_{\xi,d}(t)
        =
        1
        \qquad(0\leq t\leq1).
\]
If \(|\xi|\geq16\), then
\[
\operatorname{spt}\chi_{\xi,0}\subset[0,2|\xi|^{-1/2}], \qquad       
\operatorname{spt}\chi_{\xi,1}\subset[1-2|\xi|^{-1/2},1],
\]
and
\[
        \operatorname{spt}\chi_{\xi,\mathrm{sd}}
        \subset
        \{t\in[0,1]:h_\xi(t)^{1/2}\leq2|\xi|^{-1/2}\}.
\]
For \(d\in \mathfrak D_{\xi}\),
\[
        \frac{d}{2}
        \leq
        h_\xi(t)^{1/2}
        \leq
        2d
        \qquad
        (t\in\operatorname{spt}\chi_{\xi,d}),
\]
and
\[
        c_\gamma|\xi|d
        \leq
        |\phi_\xi'(t)|
        \leq
        C_\gamma|\xi|d
        \qquad(t\in\operatorname{spt}\chi_{\xi,d}).
\]
Moreover,
\[
        \frac12|\xi|^{-1/2}
        \leq
        d
        \leq
        2
        \qquad(d\in \mathfrak D_{\xi}).
\]
In particular, \(\mathfrak D_{\xi}\) is finite.

[Definition eq:labeled-bounded-lipschitz-cut-distance-prob-graphons of arXiv:2606.21556, 'Mean field limit of non-exchangeable interacting diffusions on co-evolutionary networks'] The space of probability-graphons over a Polish space \(\mathcal{Y}\) is defined as 
	\[
		\mathcal{PG}(\mathcal{Y}):=\{q:[0,1]^2\to \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{Y}) \text{ measurable}\},
	\]  
	where \(\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{Y})\) is equipped with the narrow topology, and as usual we identify 
	two probability-graphons if they are equal almost everywhere. For any two probability-graphons 
	\(q,\bar{q} \in \mathcal{PG}(\mathcal{Y})\), we define the labeled bounded-Lipschitz cut distance as 
	\begin{equation} 
		d_{\text{BL},\square}(q,\bar{q}):= \sup_{S,T\subset [0,1]} d_{\text{BL}}\left( \iint_{S\times T} q^{\xi,\xi'}d\xi d\xi', \iint_{S\times T} \bar{q}^{\xi,\xi'}d\xi d\xi' \right). 
	\end{equation}
title: Probability-graphons and bounded-Lipschitz cut distance

body:
[Prop eq:Ac of arXiv:2606.06187, 'How to Study Reflected Brownian Motion in a Quadrant via Kernel Functional Equations?\\ \m'] Let $(Z_t)_{t\ge 0}$ be a reflected Brownian motion in $\mathbb{R}_+^2$ satisfying
\[
Z_t = Z_0 + \mu t + B_t + R L_t,
\]
where the covariance matrix, the reflecting matrix and the drift are
\[
\Sigma =
\begin{pmatrix}
\sigma_{11} & \sigma_{12}\\
\sigma_{12} & \sigma_{22}
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
R =
\begin{pmatrix}
r_{11} & r_{12}\\
r_{21} & r_{22}
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\mu= \begin{pmatrix}
\mu_1 \\
\mu_2 
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Define
\begin{equation}
A =
\begin{pmatrix}
\sigma_{11}^{-1/2} & 0\\
0 & \sigma_{22}^{-1/2}
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
c = |A\mu|= \sqrt{
\frac{\mu_1^2}{\sigma_{11}} + \frac{\mu_2^2}{\sigma_{22}}
},

\end{equation}
and introduce the process
\[
\bar Z_t = c\, A\, Z_{t/c^2}.
\]
Then $(\bar Z_t)_{t\ge 0}$ is a reflected Brownian motion in $\mathbb{R}_+^2$ satisfying
\[
\bar Z_t = \bar Z_0 + \bar\mu t + \bar B_t + \bar R\, \bar L_t,
\]
where the covariance matrix, the reflecting matrix and the drift are
\[
\bar\Sigma =
\begin{pmatrix}
1 & \rho\\
\rho & 1
\end{pmatrix}
\text{ with }
\rho = \frac{\sigma_{12}}{\sqrt{\sigma_{11}\sigma_{22}}},
\quad
\bar R =
\begin{pmatrix}
1 &
\sqrt{\frac{\sigma_{22}}{\sigma_{11}}} \frac{ r_{12}}{r_{22}}\\[1em]
\sqrt{\frac{\sigma_{11}}{\sigma_{22}}} \frac{ r_{21}}{r_{11}} &
1
\end{pmatrix},
\quad
\bar\mu = \frac{A\mu}{|A\mu|}
\text{ with }
|\bar\mu|=1,
\]
and
\[
\bar L_t^i = \frac{cr_{ii} }{\sqrt{\sigma_{ii}}}\; L_{t/c^2}^i,
\qquad i=1,2,
\]
is the local time of the process on the axes.

body: [Definition $\Mzp$-convergence of arXiv:2605.10491, 'Zero-couplings of infinite measures with cyclically monotone support and multivariate regu'] Let $\mu_n, \mu \in \mathrm{M}_{0}(\mathbb{R}^d),n\geqslant1$. We say that $\mu_n$ converges to $\mu$ in $\mathrm{M}_{0}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ if $\mu_n(f)\xrightarrow[]{}\mu(f)$ for each $f \in \mathrm{C}_{b,0}^{+}(\mathbb{R}^d) $. When no confusion is possible we sometimes write that $\mu_n$ $\mathrm{M}_{0}$-converges to $\mu$ and use the symbol $\mu_n\raisebox{-0.5pt}{\,\scriptsize$\stackrel{\raisebox{-0.5pt}{\mbox{\tiny $0$}}}{\longrightarrow}$}\,\mu$ to denote this convergence.
title: $\Mzp$-convergence

[Theorem thm:stahri of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Fix $\rho \in \mathbb{R} \cup \{-\infty\}$, and let $\mathcal{L}^\rho$ be the half-space directed landscape of parameter $\rho$. Then there exists a random function $\mathcal{H}^\rho \in \mathcal D(2\rho \vee 0)$ with explicit marginals given in Proposition (P:half-space-horizon-marginals of the paper) below, such that if we consider 
		\[
		\mathcal{H}_t^\rho(\lambda, x) := \sup_{y\ge 0} \mathcal{H}^\rho(\lambda, y) + \mathcal{L}^\rho(y,0;x,t),
		\]
		then the function$(\lambda, x) \mapsto \mathcal{H}_t^\rho(\lambda, x) - \mathcal{H}_t^\rho(\lambda, 0)$ is equal in law to $\mathcal{H}^\rho$. We call $\mathcal{H}^\rho$ the \emph{half-space stationary horizon} with (boundary) parameter $\rho$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:stahri of arXiv:2604.10020

[campaign result 2026-09-14, author checked; depends on the companion memo on Problem 20.2] This is the negative part of the answer recorded for Svante Janson's Problem 20.4 in Simply generated trees, conditioned Galton-Watson trees, random allocations and condensation, Probability Surveys 9 (2012), arXiv:1112.0510. Problem 20.4 asks for a Gaussian extension of Theorem 7.12, the law of large numbers for fringe-subtree counts. Let T_n be the simply generated tree, equivalently the conditioned Galton-Watson tree, with n vertices. Let N_T be the number of vertices whose fringe subtree equals a fixed finite ordered rooted tree T, and let N_d be the number of vertices with d children. For the one-vertex tree bullet, N_bullet = N_0 exactly, since its occurrences are precisely the leaves. In both constructions of the companion memo on Problem 20.2, the subcritical law of its Theorem A (nu < 1) and the critical infinite-variance law of its Theorem B (nu = 1, sigma^2 = infinity), most vertices have degree 0 or 1, but N_0 = n - N_1 - sum_{d>=2} N_d and sum_{d>=2} N_d is of order n whenever pi_d > 0 for some d >= 2, so N_0 = n - N_1 + O(1) does not follow. Since N_0 - n pi_0 = -(N_1 - n pi_1) - sum_{d>=2} (N_d - n pi_d), N_bullet inherits, with the sign reversed, the non-Gaussian limit of (N_1 - n pi_1)/sqrt(n) (a two-point law in the first construction, a mixture of two Gaussians in the second) if sum_{d>=2} (N_d - n pi_d) = o(sqrt n) in probability, which is not shown; otherwise its limit depends on the joint fluctuations of all the degree counts. So the negative answer, that fringe-subtree counts are not asymptotically normal in general when nu < 1, nor when nu = 1 with sigma^2 = infinity, is not established by this reduction. The finite-variance critical case is resolved in the literature by Janson (Random Structures Algorithms 48, 2016, Theorem 1.5) and is not included here as own work. This is an unrefereed campaign result.
T_n is an ordered rooted tree, and its one-vertex fringe subtrees are leaves.

[Lemma of arXiv:2602.08591, 'The Yang--Mills measure on compact surfaces as a \\ universal scaling limit of lattice gau'] Let $u<0$, and $\alpha \in (0,1)$. Then, for any integers $A<B$, we have
\begin{itemize}
    \item if $u>-1$, there exists a constant $C(u)>0$ such that
    $
        \sum_{A \leqslant p < q \leqslant B} (q-p)^u \leqslant C(u)\,(B-A)^{u+2},
    $
    \item if $u \leqslant -1$, there exists a constant $c(u)>0$ such that
    $
        \sum_{A \leqslant p < q \leqslant B} (q-p)^u \geqslant c(u)\,(B-A).
    $
    \item there exists $C(u,\alpha)>0$ such that \[
\sum_{A\leqslant p<q\leqslant B}\frac{p^u}{(q-p)^{1+\alpha u}}
\leqslant C(u,\alpha)\,(B-A)^{1+u-\alpha u}.
\]
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 4 (Right edge) of arXiv:2511.12623, 'The eigenvector bead process'] Fix integers $K,\ell\ge 1$ and let $q=N/T\in(0,1]$ be kept constant in the asymptotic regime $N,T\to\infty$.
Consider a Wishart matrix $W_{N+K}$ and let $\{\lambda_j^{(s)}\}_j$ denote the (increasingly ordered) eigenvalues at level $s$.
Then the array of edge increments
\[
\left(
\frac{\sqrt{q}}{1+\sqrt{q}}\bigl(\lambda_{N+s+1}^{(s+1)}-\lambda_{N+s}^{(s)}\bigr),\,
\frac{\sqrt{q}}{1+\sqrt{q}}\bigl(\lambda_{N+s}^{(s+1)}-\lambda_{N+s-1}^{(s)}\bigr),\,
\dots,\,
\frac{\sqrt{q}}{1+\sqrt{q}}\bigl(\lambda_{N+s+1-\ell}^{(s+1)}-\lambda_{N+s-\ell}^{(s)}\bigr)
\right)_{0\le s\le K-1}
\]
converges in distribution, as $N,T\to\infty$, to a random array with independent
Gamma-distributed entries on $(0,\infty)$ with density
$\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\, x^{-1/2} e^{-x/2}$. Moreover, this array is independent of the array of eigenvalues as stated in Theorem~\ref{thm:left-edge}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Right edge

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Given a variable $f:X\to\mathbb R$ which follows the uniform law of $[a,b]$, its moments are given by the following formula,
$$M_k=\frac{1}{k+1}\cdot\frac{b^{k+1}-a^{k+1}}{b-a}$$
with the small order moments being as follows:
$$M_1=\frac{a+b}{2}$$
$$M_2=\frac{a^2+ab+b^2}{3}$$
$$M_3=\frac{a^3+a^2b+ab^2+b^3}{4}$$
$$M_4=\frac{a^4+a^3b+a^2b^2+ab^3+b^4}{5}$$
In particular, the mean is $E=(a+b)/2$, and the variance is $V=(b-a)^2/12$.

[Theorem thm:fibers of arXiv:2607.24705, 'Derangetropy Operators'] Let $f, g \in \mathcal{D}_{+}^{2}$. Then $U_{f} = U_{g}$ if and only
		if $Q_{g} = M\circ Q_{f}$ for a M\"obius map $M$, increasing and
		finite on the range of $Q_{f}$; that is, if and only if $g$ is a
		projective change of variable of $f$. The fiber within a fixed
		support interval $I$ is the group of increasing M\"obius self-maps
		of $I$, of dimension one when $I$ is bounded or a half-line, and of
		dimension two, the increasing affine group, when
		$I = \mathbb{R}$.

[Definition 13 of arXiv:2605.02430, '\textbf{Scaling limit of the range of tree-valued branching random walks in random environ'] (\textbf{Infinite GW trees})  Let $\mathbf r \eqo (r(j,k))_{k\geq j\geq 1}$ be a probability measure 
on $\{ (j,k)\ino (\bbN^*)^2\! : \! j\! \leq \! k\}$. 
Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\bbN$ whose mean $\ttm_\mu \! :=\! \sum_{k\in \bbN} k\mu (k)$ is finite and positive. 
 Let $(\bT \! , \boo)\! :\!  \Omega \! \rightarrow \!   \overline{\bbT}^\bullet\! $ be a 
Borel-measurable random pointed tree such that 
$$ \textrm{$\bP$-a.s.} \quad  \bbn \boo \bbn \! = \! 0 \quad \textrm{and} \quad \bbn \bT \bbn_-\!\! = \! -\infty \; .$$ 
Recall from (\ref{ancestral}) that the notation $L_\boo\eqo \{ \boo (p) ; p\ino \bbN\}$ for the 
the ancestral line of $\boo$ and recall from (\ref{spinedfbis}) the definition of the spine $\partial L_\boo$ of $(\bT, \boo)$.  
Recall from (\ref{extremdef}) the notation $\mathtt{end} (\cdot)$.  

\smallskip

\noi
$(\textbf{a})$ We say that $(\bT, \boo)$ is an \emph{infinite GW tree with offspring distribution $\mu$ and dispatching measure $\mathbf r$} if: 
\begin{compactenum}

\smallskip

\item[$-$]  the 
r.v.s $S\! :=\! \big( \mathtt{end} (\boo (p)), k_{\boo (p +1)} (\bT)\big)_{\! p\in \bbN}$ are i.i.d.~with law $\mathbf r$, 

\smallskip

\item[$-$] conditionally given $S$, 
the subtrees $(\theta_{u} \bT \, ; \, u\ino \partial L_\boo )$ are independent GW($\mu$)-trees (as in Definition \ref{GWfordef} $(\mathbf a)$) 

\smallskip

\end{compactenum}

\noi
More specifically: 

\smallskip

\noi
$(\textbf{b})$ $(\bT, \boo)$ is an \emph{infinite GW tree with offspring distribution $\mu$} if
$r(j,k)\! = \! \frac{\mu (k)}{\ttm_\mu}$, for all $k\! \geq \! j\! \geq \! 1$.  \cq
title: Definition 13 of arXiv:2605.02430

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2609.01520, 'A stable limit theorem for SDEs driven by multiplicative $\alpha$-stable processes'] Let Assumptions $\ref{dis}$--$\ref{gro-bou}$ hold.
For any initial data $Y_0=y\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$, the time-rescaled process
$(Y_{t/\varepsilon})_{t\geq0}$ has the same law as the unique strong
solution $(Y_t^\varepsilon)_{t\geq0}$ of \eqref{3.2} with
$Y_0^\varepsilon=y$.
Moreover, for any $m\in[1,\alpha)$, there exists
	$C_m>0$ 
	such that
	\begin{equation}
		\sup_{\varepsilon\in(0,1)}
		\sup_{t\geq0}\mathbb{E}|Y_t^\varepsilon|^m
		\leq C_m(1+|y|^m).
	\end{equation}

Let mu_1, ..., mu_n be finite Borel measures on R^n, each of which assigns measure zero to every hyperplane (for instance the Lebesgue measures of n bounded measurable sets). Then there exists a hyperplane H such that for every i the two open half-spaces bounded by H carry equal mu_i-measure, mu_i(H^+) = mu_i(H^-) = mu_i(R^n)/2. The number n of objects cannot in general be increased to n + 1 in dimension n.

\[T \geq C\left( s_{0} + \kappa_{d}(\varepsilon)^{- 1}\left( \log N_{\varepsilon}(M) + \log\frac{1}{\delta} \right) \right),\]

one has, for every reconstruction radius \(r\) with
\(C_{low}\,\varepsilon \leq r \leq C_{up}\, \operatorname{reach}(M)\),

\[\mathbb{P}_{z}\left( H_{q}\left( \Gamma_{T}^{r} \right) \cong H_{q}(M)\ \text{for every }q = 0,\ldots,d \right) \geq 1 - \delta.\]

body:
[Theorem thm:exp-decay-centered-moments of arXiv:2605.20697, 'Uniform-in-time propagation of chaos for \\ Second-Order Consensus-Based Optimization'] Let \(p\geqslant2\), and assume (assump:centered-decay of the paper) for this value of \(p\).
Assume also that
\[
    \mathbf{E}\left[
        \momentp{p}{\mu_{\mathcal X^J_{0}}}
        +
        \momentp{p}{\mu_{\mathcal V^J_{0}}}
    \right]
    <\infty.
\]
Define
\begin{equation}
    \lambda_{p}
    :=
    \begin{cases}
        \displaystyle
        \frac{\min\{v_1,v_3\}}{c_2^{(2)}},
        & p=2,\\[1.2em]
        \displaystyle
        \frac{p\mu_{\mathrm{gap},p}}{4\gamma},
        & p>2.
    \end{cases}
\end{equation}
Then the expected centered Lyapunov functional decays exponentially:
\begin{equation}
    \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm d t}\mathcal L_p(t)
    \leqslant
    -\lambda_{p}\mathcal L_p(t).
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
    \mathcal L_p(t)
    \leqslant
    e^{-\lambda_{p}t}\mathcal L_p(0).
\end{equation}
Moreover, there exists a finite constant \(C_p>0\), depending only on the parameters
and on the norm-equivalence constants, such that
\begin{equation}
    \mathbf{E}\left[
        \mathfrak M_p(\mu_{X_t^J})
        +
        \mathfrak M_p(\mu_{V_t^J})
    \right]
    \leqslant
    C_p e^{-\lambda_{p}t}
    \mathbf{E}\left[
        \mathfrak M_p(\mu_{X_0^J})
        +
        \mathfrak M_p(\mu_{V_0^J})
    \right].
\end{equation}

body: Consider the initial value problem y'(x) = f(x, y(x)), y(x_0) = y_0, where f is a real-valued function only assumed continuous (not necessarily Lipschitz) on an open rectangle around (x_0, y_0). Then there exists at least one continuously differentiable solution y(x) on some open interval containing x_0. Continuity alone need not give uniqueness: for y' = 2 sqrt(|y|), y(0) = 0, both the constant solution y(x) = 0 and y(x) equal to x^2 for x >= 0 and -x^2 for x < 0 solve the problem, and in fact infinitely many solutions pass through the same point.
title: Peano existence theorem

body:
[Theorem 8 of arXiv:2608.12839, 'Spiking Neural Networks with Elephant Reinforcement'] Consider the nonlinear replica mean-field process with firing rate
$
\lambda(v,s,k)
=
\mathbf 1_{\{v>\alpha s^{+}\}},
$
leakage rate
$
\gamma\mathbf 1_{\{v>0\}}$,
 $\gamma>0,
$
and mean-field input rates
\[
a_i(\boldsymbol{\pi})
=
\beta_{i-1}(\pi_{i-1})
+
\beta_{i+1}(\pi_{i+1}),
\]
where
\[
\beta_i(\pi_i)
=
\int_E \lambda(v,s,k)\,\pi_i(dv,ds,dk).
\]

Let
$
\boldsymbol{\pi}
=
(\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_N)
$
be an invariant family of probability measures for the nonlinear RMF
dynamics. Then, for every \(i\),
\[
\beta_i(\pi_i)=0
\]
and
\[
\pi_i\bigl(\{(v,s,k)\in E:v=0\}\bigr)=1.
\]

Conversely, every family of probability measures
$
\boldsymbol{\pi}
=
(\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_N)
$
satisfying
\[
\pi_i(V=0)=1,
\qquad i=1,\ldots,N,
\]
is invariant. 
Thus the invariant probability measures are exactly the probability measures
supported on silent states:
\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{supp}(\pi_i)
\subseteq
\{0\}\times\mathbb Z\times\mathbb N^{*}.
}
\]

For \(n\geq1\), define the bounded test function
\[
f_n(v,s,k)=k\wedge n.
\]
Leakage and incoming spikes do not change \(k\). At a firing event,
$
k\longmapsto k+1.
$
Therefore,
\begin{align*}
\mathcal A_{i,\boldsymbol{\pi}}f_n(v,s,k)
=
\lambda(v,s,k)
\left[
(k+1)\wedge n-k\wedge n
\right]
=
\lambda(v,s,k)\mathbf 1_{\{k<n\}}.
\end{align*}

Since \(\pi_i\) is invariant and \(f_n\) is bounded,
\[
\int_E
\mathcal A_{i,\boldsymbol{\pi}}f_n(v,s,k)
\,\pi_i(dv,ds,dk)
=
0.
\]
Hence
\[
\int_E
\lambda(v,s,k)\mathbf 1_{\{k<n\}}
\,\pi_i(dv,ds,dk)
=
0.
\]

[Definition 11 of arXiv:2604.11682, 'Semilocalization for inhomogeneous random graphs'] Two paths $\gamma$ and $\gamma'$ are \emph{edge-intersecting} if there exists $i$ and
  $j$ such that $\gamma_{i} = \gamma'_{j}$ and either $\gamma_{i-1} = \gamma'_{j-1}$ or
  $\gamma_{i-1} = \gamma'_{j+1}$. Two paths $\gamma$ and $\gamma'$ are
  \emph{edge-disjoint} if they are not edge-intersecting.

[Prop 16 ({\cite{CaPe20,BCP21}}) of arXiv:2608.28148, 'Flows and homotopies of Banach Lie algebroids'] Consider a Banach almost Lie algebroid  $\left(A,\pi,M,\rho ,\LB_{A} \right) $ and denote for $U\subseteq M$ open  by $\LB$ the Lie bracket of vector fields on $U$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For any open $U\subseteq M$ and any $ \left(  \mathfrak{u}_{1}, \mathfrak{u}_{2} \right) \in \Gamma\left( A_{ U} \right) ^2$, the map
\[
\left(  \mathfrak{u}_{1}, \mathfrak{u}_{2} \right)\mapsto \rho \left( \LB[ \mathfrak{u}_1, \mathfrak{u}_2]_A \right) -\LB[\rho( \mathfrak{u}_1), \rho( \mathfrak{u}_2)]
\]
only depends on the $1$-jet of $\rho$ and the values of $\mathfrak{u}_1$ and $\mathfrak{u}_2$ at $x\in U$.
\item
If the  Jacobiator $J_{A_{U}}$ vanishes identically,  then  we have:
\begin{equation}

\forall \left(  \mathfrak{u}_{1}, \mathfrak{u}_{2} \right) \in \Gamma\left( A_{ U} \right) ^2,\; \rho \left( [ \mathfrak{u}_1, \mathfrak{u}_2]_A \right) =[\rho( \mathfrak{u}_1), \rho( \mathfrak{u}_2)].
\end{equation}
\item
If property \eqref{eq_rhoCompatible} is true, then $J_{A_{U}}\colon \Gamma\left( A_{ U} \right)^3 \rightarrow \Gamma \left( A_{ U} \right)$ is a smooth morphism which takes values in $\ker \rho$ over $U$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 17 of arXiv:2608.21255, 'Laws of the iterated logarithm for random Dirichlet series with general weights'] Let $N$ be a positive integer-valued function. 
Fix any $\gamma\in (0, (\sqrt{5}-1)/2)$, pick any $\rho=\rho(\gamma)$ satisfying
\begin{equation}
(1-\gamma)(1+\gamma)^2(2-\exp(8(1+\gamma)\rho c_\beta))>1,
\end{equation}
where $c_\beta:=(c\,2^{1-\beta}\Gamma(1+\beta))^{-1/2}$, and put $g(s):=(2v(s)\log\log 1/s)^{-1/2}$ for $s\in (0,1/\eee)$ and $s_n:=\exp(-n^{1-\gamma})$ for $n\in\mn$. 
Then
$$\limsup_{n\to\infty}g(s_n)\sum_{k>N(s_n)}\frac{a_k\tilde \eta_{k,\rho}(s_n)}{k^{1/2+s_n}}\leq 1+\gamma\quad \text{{\rm a.s.}}$$

[Proposition 1 (Unequal-shape decision boundaries) of arXiv:2609.00774, 'Semi-Supervised Classification with Informative Missing Labels in Weibull Mixture Models'] Suppose $k_1\neq k_2$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item The equation $\delta(y;\theta_U)=0$ has at most two positive roots.
\item If $k_1>k_2$, then $\delta(y)\to-\infty$ as $y\downarrow0$ and as $y\to\infty$. The log-posterior odds function has a unique global maximum. Hence it has either no positive root, one double root, or two simple roots $0<y_1<y_2$. In the two-root case, class 1 is selected on $(y_1,y_2)$ and class 2 in the two tails.
\item If $k_1<k_2$, then $\delta(y)\to+\infty$ as $y\downarrow0$ and as $y\to\infty$. The log-posterior odds function has a unique global minimum. Hence it has either no positive root, one double root, or two simple roots $0<y_1<y_2$. In the two-root case, class 2 is selected on $(y_1,y_2)$ and class 1 in the two tails.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Unequal-shape decision boundaries

[Theorem Main.Thm01 of arXiv:2411.15485, '\bf\Large Stochastic Volterra Equations for Local Times of Spectrally Positive L\'evy Proc'] For each $\zeta\geq 0$, the process $L^\xi_\zeta$ equals in distribution to the unique non-negative continuous solution of the stochastic Volterra equation
 	\begin{eqnarray}
 	X_\zeta(t) \!\!\!&=\!\!\!& \zeta\cdot c \cdot W'(t)  
 	+  \int_0^\zeta\int_0^\infty \big( W(t)-W(t-y) \big) \, N_0(dz, dy)   + \int_0^t \int_0^{X_\zeta(s)}   W'(t-s) \, B_c(ds,dz) \cr
 	\!\!\!&\!\!\!& + \int_0^t \int_0^{X_\zeta(s)} \int_0^\infty  \big( W(t-s)-W(t-s-y) \big) \, \widetilde{N}_\nu(ds,dz,dy), \quad t\geq 0,
 	\end{eqnarray}
 	where $N_0(dz, dy)$ is a  Poisson random measure on $(0,\infty)^2$ with intensity $\bar\nu(y)\,dz\,dy$, $B_c(ds,dz)$ is a Gaussian white noise on $(0,\infty)^2$ with intensity $2c\cdot ds\, dz$ and $\widetilde{N}_\nu(ds,dz,dy)$ is a compensated Poisson random measure on $(0,\infty)^3$ with intensity $ds\, dz\,\nu(dy)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 7 of arXiv:2609.01574, 'A linear bound for Fujita's freeness conjecture'] Assume that $(X,\Delta)$ is log canonical near a point $x\in X$. For a nonzero coherent ideal $\mathfrak a\subset\mathcal O_X$, its \emph{local log canonical threshold at $x$} is
\[
 \lct_x\bigl((X,\Delta);\mathfrak a\bigr)
 :=\inf_{\substack{F\text{ prime over }X\\
 x\in c_X(F),\ \ord_F(\mathfrak a)>0}}
 \frac{A_{X,\Delta}(F)}{\ord_F(\mathfrak a)}.
\]
For an effective $\mathbb Q$-Cartier $\mathbb Q$-divisor $D$, we similarly write
\[
 \lct_x\bigl((X,\Delta);D\bigr)
 :=\sup\{t\in\mathbb Q_{\geq0}\mid (X,\Delta+tD)
 \text{ is log canonical near }x\}.
\]
title: Definition 7 of arXiv:2609.01574

body:
[Cor 12 of arXiv:2607.03924, 'Tree Coordinates and Range Martingales for Positive Operator-Valued Measures'] Let $X=\left\{ X_{w}\right\} $ be a bounded range
martingale for $E$, and let $h\in H$ be a unit vector. Define the
scalar probability measure 
\[
\nu_{h}\left(B\right)=\left\langle h,E\left(B\right)h\right\rangle ,\qquad B\in\mathcal{B}\left(\Omega_{m}\right).
\]
For each word $w$ with $\nu_{h}\left(\left[w\right]\right)>0$, set
\[
x^{h}_{w}=\frac{\left\langle E^{1/2}_{w}h,X_{w}E^{1/2}_{w}h\right\rangle }{\left\Vert E^{1/2}_{w}h\right\Vert ^{2}}.
\]
On words with $\nu_{h}\left(\left[w\right]\right)=0$, define $x^{h}_{w}=0$.
Let $\mathcal{F}_{n}$ be the finite $\sigma$-algebra generated by
the cylinders of length $n$, and define 
\[
M^{h}_{n}\left(\omega\right)=x^{h}_{w},\qquad\omega\in\left[w\right],\quad\left|w\right|=n.
\]
Then $\left\{ M^{h}_{n}\right\} _{n\geq0}$ is a bounded scalar martingale
with respect to $\left\{ \mathcal{F}_{n}\right\} _{n\geq0}$ and $\nu_{h}$.

[Proposition prop:wedge-wellposedness of arXiv:2609.00698, 'Kinetic Wedge Layers and Diffusive Limit of Neutron Transport in Polygonal Domains'] Let $0<\omega<\pi$, $1<\beta<\pi/\omega$ and $s>\beta+2$, and suppose the measurable source and incoming ray data in (equation eq:defect-wedge-problem of the paper) satisfy $\mathcal A_{s}<\infty$ in the sense of (equation eq:abstract-wedge-data-assumption-v6 of the paper). Then the wedge-corrector problem (equation eq:defect-wedge-problem of the paper) has a unique bounded mild solution $D$, and
\begin{align}
 \esssup_{Y,v}\left\langleR\right\rangle^\beta
 \Big(\abs{D(Y,v)}+\abs{\mathbf P D(Y)}\Big)
 \le C(\omega,\beta,s)\mathcal A_{s}.
 
\end{align}
As a consequence $\abs{D(Y,v)}+\abs{\mathbf P D(Y)}\le C\mathcal A_{s}\left\langleR\right\rangle^{-\beta}$, and the solution depends linearly and continuously on $F,h_1,h_2$ in the weighted norms (equation eq:wedge-data-weighted-norms of the paper).
title: Well-posedness of wedge layer

Own-work draft; status: independently checked proof; exact claim F0124_C8 version 1. For the two-sided iid nearest-neighbor walk with P(X_t=+1)=p, independent iid fair sign scenery, condition on ANY exterior color word at 0<|t|<=m. An upward cut separates times t,t+1 when all positions at earlier times in [-m,m] are strictly below every later position. Split the finite vertex-time interval at all upward cuts. Every non-singleton block with L internal steps has at least L/3 backward steps. For 32/33<p<1, let alpha=2(4(1-p)/p)^(1/3)<1. The posterior probability that a specified length-L interval is one maximal block is at most 2alpha^L. If L0 is the number of internal steps of the block containing time zero, P(L0>=n|exterior)<=2alpha^n[(n+1)/(1-alpha)+alpha/(1-alpha)^2], uniformly over m and the exterior. Replacing a block by +1 steps preserves record compatibility; its integrated path/color weight changes by at most 2(4q/p)^B and the repair has at most 2^L preimages. At p=1 all blocks are singletons. This tail estimate alone does not control the relative weights of different short blocks and does not by itself prove goodness.

body: The lower bound S^2/(S^2 + S - Q), S = sum_i P(A_i), Q = sum_i P(A_i)^2, holds for pairwise independent events but not in general: if A_1 = A_2 = A_3 = A with P(A) = 1/2, then S = 3/2, Q = 3/4 and S^2/(S^2 + S - Q) = 3/4, while the union is A, of probability 1/2. The general Chung-Erdős denominator sum_{i,j} P(A_i and A_j) must be used instead; here it equals 9/2 and gives exactly 1/2.

\begin{enumerate}[wide,label=(\roman*),labelindent=0pt]
\item  A marked point process $\tilde \mathcal{P} = \{(x, U(x))\}_{x \in \mathcal{P}}$ has  {\em $\textnormal{BL}$-mixing
  correlations} if there exists a family $( \omega_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ of  functions $\omega_k : [0, \infty) \to [0, \infty)$ with $\lim_{r \to \infty}\omega_k(r) = 0$ for all $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and 
   such that for all $p,q \in \mathbb{N}$, $x_1,\ldots,x_{p+q} \in \mathbb{R}^d$, and all $f \in \textnormal{BL}(\mathbb{K}^p), g \in \textnormal{BL}(\mathbb{K}^q)$, 
    we have
\begin{align} \nonumber
& \left|\mathbb {E} _{\bk x1{p+q}}[f(\bk U1{p})g(\bk U{p+1}{p+q})]\rho^{(p+q)}(\bk x1{p+q}) - \mathbb {E} _{\bk x1p}[f(\bk U1p)] \rho^{(p)}(\bk x1{p})\mathbb {E} _{\bk x{p+1}{p+q}}[g(\bk U{p+1}{p+q})]\rho^{(q)}(\bk
x{p+1}{p+q})\right|\\
&\hspace{0.1\linewidth}\le \omega_{p+q}(s),
\end{align}

where
\begin{equation}

s := d(\bk x1p,\bk x{p+1}{p+q}):= \inf_{i \in \{1,...,p\}, j \in \{p + 1,...,p + q\} } |x_i - x_j|.
\end{equation}
We refer to $(\omega_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$  as the correlation decay functions for $\tilde \mathcal{P}$ and without loss of generality, we assume that the  collection $(\omega_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ is  an {\em increasing-decreasing family} of functions, by which we mean that for all $k \in \mathbb{N}$ we have $ \omega_k \leq \omega_{k + 1}$  and $\omega_k(s) \downarrow 0$ as $s \to \infty$.

\item   $\tilde\mathcal{P}$ has {\em 
 fast $\textnormal{BL}$-mixing correlations}  if in addition to  (equation e.mppmixing of the paper), 
   for all $k\in \mathbb{N}$,  the correlation decay function $\omega_k$ is  fast decreasing, in accordance with property~(equation varphibd of the paper). 
 \item  A {\em family of marked point processes}   $(\tilde\mathcal{P}_l)_{l \in \mathbb{N}},$ 
 has  $\textnormal{BL}$-mixing correlations,
 if there exists a family $( \omega_k)_{k\in\mathbb{N}}$ of increasing-decreasing functions $\omega_k :  [0, \infty) \to [0, \infty)$ 
  and such that  (equation e.mppmixing of the paper) holds uniformly in
 $l \in \mathbb{N}$ with respect to the Palm distributions  of marks $\mathbb {E} _{\bk  x1{p+q}}
[f(\bk{U_l}1{p})g(\bk {U_l}{p+1}{p+q})]$ of $\tilde{\mathcal{P}}_l$.
  The family  $(\tilde\mathcal{P}_l)_{l \in \mathbb{N}}$ has 
  {\em  fast} $\textnormal{BL}$-mixing correlations, if
  the increasing-decreasing family of correlation decay functions $(\omega_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$
 is fast decreasing.
 \end{enumerate}

body:
[Theorem thm:full-trace-unique of arXiv:2607.18070, 'The Brownian loop-catcher'] Let \(D\) be a bounded Jordan domain and \(a\ne b\in\partial D\).
For \(0<\lambda\leq1\), a probability law $\mathbb{P}$ on compact connected
\(K\subset\overline D\) with \(K\cap\partial D=\{a,b\}\) is determined by
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb{E}\!\left[
 \mathbf 1_{\{K\cap A=\varnothing\}}e^{-\lambda m_D(K,A)}\right],
 \qquad \forall A\subset \overline{D}\ \hbox{compact}.
\end{equation}
Here $\mathbb{E}$ denotes the expectation with respect to $\mathbb{P}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Full-trace uniqueness

body:
[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2606.09121, 'Truncated Signature Information for Mixed Fractional Brownian Paths'] Let $\mathcal H=\{h_0,\ldots,h_{L-1}\}$ consist of distinct positive scales.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item If $L\ge2K$, then $\Psi_{\mathcal H}$ and $\Phi_{2,\mathcal H}$ are injective and
\[
    \operatorname{rank}D\Psi_{\mathcal H}(\theta)=2K
    \qquad (\theta\in\mathcal P_K).
\]
If $L<2K$, then $\Phi_{2,\mathcal H}$ cannot have full local rank $2K$.
\item If $L\ge K$, then $\Gamma_{\mathcal H}$ and $\Phi_{3,\mathcal H}$ are injective and
\[
    \operatorname{rank}D\Gamma_{\mathcal H}(\theta)=2K
    \qquad (\theta\in\mathcal P_K).
\]
If $L<K$, then $\Phi_{3,\mathcal H}$ cannot have full local rank $2K$.
\end{enumerate}
Thus the selected third-level coordinate reduces the number of scales sufficient for global identification from $2K$ to $K$.  These same counts are necessary for full $2K$-dimensional local rank; no stronger minimality claim is made for exceptional forms of local injectivity.

[Corollary 34 (Polynomial reset regime) of arXiv:2605.14511, 'Clumsy and Careless:\\ Stationary-Entry Flux in Non-monotone Coupon Collectors'] Assume
\[
        \rho_n\sim\frac{\lambda}{n},
        \qquad \lambda>0,
\]
and put
\[
        a_n:=\frac{n\rho_n}{1-\rho_n}.
\]
Then
\[
        s_n=\Gamma(1+a_n)n^{-a_n}(1+o(1)),
\]
and therefore
\[
        \rho_n\Gamma(1+a_n)n^{-a_n}T_n
        \Rightarrow\Exp(1).
\]
Moreover, all fixed positive integer moments converge to the corresponding exponential moments under this normalization.

If, in addition,
\[
        (a_n-\lambda)\log n\to0,
\]
then the simpler normalization is valid:
\[
        \frac{\lambda\Gamma(\lambda+1)}{n^{\lambda+1}}T_n
        \Rightarrow\Exp(1),
\]
again with convergence of every fixed positive integer moment.

[Proposition 28 of arXiv:2608.19976, 'Random valuations'] Let $\Phi:\Kd\to\R$ be a square-integrable stochastic process such
  that $K\mapsto \E\Phi(K)$ is a deterministic valuation.
  Then $\Phi$ is a random valuation with 
  uncorrelated increments if and only if 
  \begin{equation}
    
    C(K,L)=\sigma^2(K\cap L),\quad K,L\in\Kd,\; K\cup L\in\Kd, 
  \end{equation}
  and $\sigma^2(\cdot)$ is a monotone valuation.

[Definition def:ising-DLR of arXiv:2603.01322, 'Gibbs conditioning, atypical consensus and splitting Gibbs measures on random regular grap'] An Ising measure on $T^\k$ with interaction parameter $\beta\in \R$ and external field $B\in \R$, abbreviated to Ising $(T^\k,\beta, B)$ measure, is a probability measure $\ising\in \P\cpr{\pr{1,-1}^{T^\k}}$ such that for any finite set $\Lambda \subset T^\k$ and 
    $\omega_{\Lambda^c}\in \pr{1,-1}^{\Lambda^c}$, 
    the  conditional marginal distribution $\ising_\Lambda (\cdot|\omega_{\Lambda^c})$, of $\ising$ on $\Lambda$ given $\omega_{\Lambda^c}$,  is equal to 
    $\gamma_\Lambda (\cdot |\omega_{\partial \Lambda})$, where the family of kernels $\gamma_\Lambda$ are defined as follows: for any $\sigma_\Lambda\in \pr{1,-1}^\Lambda$, 
    \begin{equation} 
    
\gamma_\Lambda \cpr{\sigma_\Lambda|\omega_{\partial \Lambda}} :=\frac{1}{Z_\Lambda(\beta,B,\omega)}\exp \pr{\beta\sum_{\stackrel{\pr{u,v}\in E(T^\k)}{u,v\in \Lambda}}\sigma_u\sigma_v+B\sum_{u\in \Lambda}\sigma_v+\beta\sum_{\stackrel{\pr{u,v}\in E(T^\k)}{u\in \Lambda,v\in \Lambda^c}}\sigma_u\omega_v},
    \end{equation}
    where $Z_\Lambda(\beta,B,\omega)$ is the normalization constant that makes $\gamma_\Lambda(\cdot|\omega_{\partial \Lambda})$ a probability measure.  
 For fixed  $\omega_{\partial \Lambda} \in \pr{1,-1}^{\partial \Lambda}$, we refer to  the measure $\gamma_\Lambda\cpr{\cdot|\omega_{\partial \Lambda}}$  in $\P\cpr{\pr{1,-1}^\Lambda}$ as the finite volume Ising measure on $\Lambda$ with interaction parameter $\beta$, external field $B$ and boundary condition $\omega_{\partial \Lambda}$.
title: Ising measures on the infinite regular tree

[Lem subgaussiannorm of arXiv:2412.00593, 'A new approach to strong convergence II.\\The classical ensembles'] There exist universal constants $C,c,\kappa>0$ such that for any   
GUE matrix $G^N$ of dimension $N$, we have
$$
	\mathbf{P}[\|G^N\| \geq  \kappa + t] 
	\leq C e^{-cNt^2}\quad\text{for all }t\ge 0,
$$
and
$$
	\mathbf{E}[\|G^N\|^p] \le 
	\left(\kappa+ C \sqrt{\frac{p}{N}}\right)^p
	\quad\text{for all }p\in\mathbb{N}.
$$

[Definition 25 (Local paracontrolled solution) of arXiv:2607.10813, '2607.10813'] Let $K\Subset\R^3$ and $0<T\le T_0$.  Let $\Xi$ satisfy
Definition~\ref{def:Xi-assumptions}, and let
$\Theta\in C_T\mathcal C_{\mathrm{loc}}^{-1-\betasum-\kappa}$.  For every
$\chi\in C_c^\infty(\R^3)$ one then has
$\chi\Theta\in C_T\mathcal C^{-1-\betasum-\kappa}$; only this localized
quantity enters the fixed-point problem.  A triple $(u,v,\mathcal N)$ is a local paracontrolled solution associated with
$(\Theta,\Xi)$ on $[0,T]\times K$ if there exist an adapted localization pair
$(\chi,\rho)$ and a fixed point
$Z=(X_{\W},X_{\K},Y_{\W},Y_{\K})\in\mathcal Z_T$ of the map defined by
\eqref{eq:mild-X}--\eqref{eq:mild-Y} such that, on $\mathcal Q_{K,T}$,
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
  u&=\rho(\Psi_{\W}+V_{\W})+X_{\W}+Y_{\W},\\
  v&=\rho(\Psi_{\K}+V_{\K})+X_{\K}+Y_{\K},
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal N
  =\Theta+\mathscr F_X^{\chi,\rho}(Z)
          +\mathscr F_Y^{\chi,\rho}(Z),
\end{equation}
where the source maps are defined in
\eqref{eq:localized-X-source} and \eqref{eq:localized-Y-source}.  Every localized component of $\Xi$, together with $\chi\Theta$, must be
formed using this same pair $(\chi,\rho)$; components constructed with
different localization pairs are not combined in one fixed-point problem.  The
remainder terms satisfy
\[
 (X_a(0),\partial_tX_a(0))=(0,0),
 \qquad a\in\mathfrak C,
\]
while
\[
 (Y_{\W}(0),\partial_tY_{\W}(0))=(u_0,u_1),
 \qquad
 (Y_{\K}(0),\partial_tY_{\K}(0))=(v_0,v_1).
\]
Moreover,
\[
  L_{\W}u=\mathcal N+\xi_{\W},
  \qquad
  L_{\K}v=\mathcal N+\xi_{\K}
\]
in $\mathcal D'((0,T)\times K)$.  Two such solutions are identified if
their fields and nonlinear sources agree on $[0,T]\times K$.

[Definition of arXiv:2510.13659, 'On the energy image density conjecture of Bouleau and Hirsch'] Let $(X,d,\mu)$ be a metric measure space and $p \in (1,\infty)$. 
		For $f \in L^p(X,\mu)$, we define
		\[

		\]
		where the infimum is taken over all sequences, $(g_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ such that there exists a
		sequence, $(f_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ with $f_i \xrightarrow{L^p(\mu)} f$
		and such that $g_i$ is an upper gradient for $f_i$ for all $i \in \mathbb{N}$. The Sobolev space $H_{1,p}:= H_{1,p}(X,d,\mu)$ is defined as $\{f \in L^{p}(X,\mu) \vert \norm{f}_{1,p} <\infty\}$.

[Prop 13 of arXiv:2605.31568, 'Lipschitz continuity of the time constant for continuum percolation'] Given $d \ge 2$, there exists $C_d < \infty$ such that the following holds.
    If $G$ is an induced subgraph of $G_\lam$, for any $W \subset \R^d$ 
    and any path $\gamma$ in $G$, 
    there exists a self-avoiding path $\gamma'$ in $G$
    with the same endpoints as $\gamma$
    such that all vertices of $\gamma'$ lie in $\gamma$, and
    \[
        |\gamma' \cap W| \le C_d \mathrm{vol}(W + B(1/2)).
    \]
    Moreover,
    we can either take $\gamma = \gamma'$
    or $|\gamma'| < |\gamma|$.

[Proposition P:airy1-alpha-mixing of arXiv:2607.17113, 'Two-time spatial decorrelation for the flat KPZ fixed point'] For each fixed $s>0$, there are constants $C_s,c_s>0$ such that the process
  $\{\mathfrak{h}(s,y): y\in \mathbb{R}\}$ has the $\alpha$-mixing coefficient
  \begin{align}
    \alpha_s(d)& \coloneqq 
    \sup_a
    \sup_{\substack{
    E_-\in\sigma(\mathfrak{h}(s,y):y\le a)\\
    E_+\in\sigma(\mathfrak{h}(s,y):y\ge a+d)}}
    |\mathbb{P}(E_-\cap E_+)-\mathbb{P}(E_-)\mathbb{P}(E_+)| \nonumber \\
    &
    \le
    C_s \,\mathrm{e}^{-c_s d^3/s^2},
    \qquad d\ge0.
    
  \end{align}
title: Proposition P:airy1-alpha-mixing of arXiv:2607.17113

body: FIRES WHEN a proof about a constrained operator bounds the constrained part and then treats the UNCONSTRAINED part as if it were also bounded. WHAT HAPPENED: the definition of a xi-QSO constrains only same-block pairs; cross-block pairs may have arbitrary coefficients P_{ij,k}. The first pass bounded the new empty-body mass by x_0' >= x_0^2 + (1/q)(1 - x_0)^2 and concluded convergence, but that last inequality quietly assumes the cross-block coefficients sum to at most one - which the definition permits but does not force - so the mass produced at states other than 0 is uncontrolled and can be recycled into cross-block pairs at the next step. Whether that recycling can sustain a nontrivial fixed point is exactly what the Cauchy-Schwarz bound does NOT decide. CONDITION OF FAILURE: any unconstrained coefficient block that the bound silently constrains. THE FIX that closed it: lower-bound x_0' by the contributions that MUST land on 0 under the definition - the pair (0,0), the pairs containing 0, and the same-block pairs - which gives 1 - x_0' <= (1 - 1/q)(1 - x_0)^2 with no assumption on the cross-block coefficients at all.

body: Let M be a block matrix [[A, B], [C, D]] with A a p by p invertible matrix, D a q by q matrix, B a p by q matrix, and C a q by p matrix. Then M is invertible if and only if the Schur complement S = D - C A^{-1} B is invertible, and in that case det(M) = det(A) det(S). If in addition M is Hermitian (C = B*, A and D Hermitian) and A is positive definite, then M is positive semidefinite (respectively positive definite) if and only if S is positive semidefinite (respectively positive definite). [standard, e.g. Boyd and Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization, Appendix A]

[Definition 1 of arXiv:2607.28215, 'Almost stochastic dominance via optimal transport'] A \emph{quasi-pseudo-metric} is a mapping $d: E \times E \to [0,\infty)$ satisfying the following two properties:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item $d(x,x) = 0$ for all $x \in E$,
\item  $d(x,z) \le d(x,y)  + d(y,z)$ for all  $x,y,z \in E$.
\end{enumerate}
The mapping $d$ is called a \emph{pseudo-metric}, if it satisfies in addition the property
\begin{enumerate}[resume*]
\item $d(x,y) = d(y,x)$ for all  $x,y \in E$,
\end{enumerate}
and the pseudo-metric is a \emph{metric}, if in addition
\begin{enumerate}[resume*]
\item $d(x,y) = 0$ if and only if $x=y$. 
\end{enumerate}
title: Definition 1 of arXiv:2607.28215

C e^{Ct_L}\,\eta (t_L+1)\,\max(1,\alpha),

[Theorem rosenthal of arXiv:2604.24914, 'SPDEs with time-independent\\ L\'evy colored noise'] Let $\{M_t\}_{t \geq 0}$ be a c\`adl\`ag square-integrable martingale with $M_0=0$ and $\langle M \rangle$ be its predictable quadratic variation. We denote by $(\Delta M)_t$ the jump size of $M$ at time $t$. Then for any $p \geq 2$, there exists a constant $\mathcal{B}_p>0$ depending on $p$ such that for any $t>0$,
$$\|\sup_{s \leq t}|M_s|\|_p \leq \mathcal{B}_p \Big(\| \langle M \rangle_t^{1/2}\|_p +\|\sup_{s \leq t}|(\Delta M)_s| \|_p\Big).$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Rosenthal's inequality

[Definition1 weak_Markovian_halfplane of arXiv:2603.05491, '\textbf{Local limits of uniform triangulations with boundaries in high genus}'] A random triangulation of the half-plane $H$ is said to satisfy a weak spatial Markov property if there exists a function $a$ such that, for any $t$, we have
\[
\mathbb{P}(t \subset H) = a(|\partial^{*}t| - |\partial t|, |t_{\mathrm{in}}|).
\]
We say that $H$ is strongly Markovian if there exist constants $\beta,\lambda > 0$ such that, for any $t$, we have 
\[
\mathbb{P}(t \subset H) = \beta^{|\partial^{*}t| - |\partial t|}\lambda^{|t_{\mathrm{in}}|}.
\]
title: Definition1 weak_Markovian_halfplane of arXiv:2603.05491

body: [Corollary 8 (FIID sparse unique infinite clusters) of arXiv:2504.02435, 'Poisson-Voronoi percolation in higher rank'] Let $G$ be a connected higher rank semisimple real Lie group with property (T). Let~$\Pi$ be the Poisson point process on $G$ of intensity $1$ equipped with iid ${\rm Unif}[0,1]$ marks. ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Check both implications through the ergodic theorem for the environment process. Result: One direction is standard: if an invariant absolutely continuous probability measure Q exists and is ergodic, the ergodic theorem for the environment chain gives X_n/n -> E_Q[local drift] a.s., and transience in direction l plus Kozlov's theorem (Q equivalent to P, unique) makes the limit velocity well defined; it is nonzero in direction l provided E_Q[d(0,omega) . l] > 0, which follows from transience in direction l ONLY IF one also knows the velocity cannot vanish under transience, which is itself the ballisticity question, so this direction reduces to: invariant a.c. measure + transient in l implies v . l > 0. Under (E) the Kalikow-type argument gives v . l >= 0 but not strict positivity. The converse (ballistic implies invariant a.c. measure) is known under (UE) and (IID) from the renewal structure with finite expected regeneration time; under (ERG) only, regenerations are unavailable and the construction of Q fails. Both directions therefore reduce to statements known under (IID)+(UE) and unproved under (ERG)+(E). Obstruction: Without i.i.d. renewal structure neither the construction of the invariant measure nor strict positivity of the velocity is available.

[Lemma 78 (Pure-area operator cells) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] Let $A$ be a skew Hilbert--Schmidt operator on a real Hilbert space $H$.  For
every $p\in(2,3)$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathbf P^A_{s,t}:=\exp_\otimes((t-s)A)
 
\end{equation}
defines a weakly geometric step-two $p$-rough path with zero first level and
logarithm $(t-s)A$.  It is the $p$-variation limit of signatures of
finite-dimensional bounded-variation loops whenever $A$ is approximated in
Hilbert--Schmidt norm by finite-rank skew operators.  Its unique extension to
any fixed tensor degree is natural under bounded linear maps.

OPEN PROBLEM (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status attempted_unsolved). For d = 2 and fixed band width W, all bulk eigenvectors of the random band matrix on a box of side N are localised with localisation length of order exp(W^2), and the local eigenvalue statistics are Poisson as N -> infinity. Source: Bourgade: Random band matrices, ICM 2018 survey, Conjecture (0.2), p. 2 and Section 2.2, p. 7. Status notes: The delocalised side W >> (log N)^{1/2} in d = 2 was addressed in arXiv 2503.07606 (2025) per the bounded search; the localisation side at fixed W is not known to be proved.
Posed in Bourgade: Random band matrices, ICM 2018 survey

[Theorem 9 of arXiv:2603.29446, 'Law of large numbers for stochastic multiscale spatial gene networks'] Let $0<\alpha<\beta<1/2$, $\tilde \beta>\beta$, $T\ge 0$, $(v^N)_{N\in\mathbb N}$ a sequence in $C([0,T];H^N)$ and 
	$v\in C([0,T];H^{-\alpha})$ such that 
\[v^N\to v, \text{when} \, N\to \infty \text{ in }  C([0,T];H^{-\alpha}).\]
Let $(u_0^N)_{N\in\mathbb N}$ a sequence in $H_N$ and $u_0\in H^{\tilde\beta}\cap C([0,1])$ such that:
\[ u_0^N\to u_0, \text{when} \, N\to \infty \text{ in }  H^{\tilde\beta}\cap L^\infty.\]
Then, there exists a unique solution $w\in C(\mathbb R^+,H^\beta\cap L^\infty)$ to \eqref{eq_w}.
For $N\in\mathbb N$, let $w^N$ be the solution of \eqref{eq:wN} . Then 
\[ w^N\to w, \text{when} \, N\to \infty \text{ in }  C([0,T]\times[0,1])\] 
and 
\[ \|w^N-P_Nw\|_{H^\beta} \to 0, \text{when} \, N\to \infty .\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 9 of arXiv:2603.29446

body: [Corollary 9 of arXiv:2512.19517, 'Spiking and Resetting'] For any $A=[a,b] \subset (0,1]$ and any $t>0$, the sequence of simple point processes $(N^\varepsilon)_{\varepsilon>0}$ conditioned to the no-jump event $\{e_1^\varepsilon \ge t\}$ converges weakly in the Skorokhod space{\footnote{$D([0,t], \mathbb N_0)$ is the space of c\`adl\`ag functions from $[0,t]$ into $\mathbb N_0$, the latter being considered as a metric space equipped with the trivial distance.}} $D([0,t], \mathbb N_0)$ to a one dimensional Poisson process ${N} (A)$, with intensity $\lambda_* (A)$, restricted to the time interval $[0,t]$.

Let T be the rooted tree in which each vertex at depth n-1 has 8 children when n is a positive power of two and 2 children otherwise. T has maximum degree 9, is not quasi-transitive, has Bernoulli bond threshold p_c(T)=1/2, and the root belongs to an infinite open cluster at p=1/2 with probability at least 4/5. Thus bounded degree and p_c<1 alone do not imply critical extinction.

body:
Let X and Y be finite sets and let F = Y^X be the set of all objective functions f : X -> Y. A search algorithm a is a deterministic rule that, given the sequence of points sampled so far and their values, picks a new point of X not yet sampled; d_m(f, a) denotes the sequence of m sampled values it produces on f. For any two algorithms a and b, any m, and any sequence d of m values, the number of functions f in F with d_m(f, a) = d equals the number with d_m(f, b) = d. Hence every performance measure that depends only on the sampled value sequence has the same average over all of F for every algorithm.
finite search and value spaces
0 <= m <= |X|, since an algorithm that never revisits a point can sample at most |X| points
the average is uniform over ALL functions in Y^X; for a non-uniform prior, or a structured class of functions, algorithms can and do differ
algorithms never resample a point

body: A non-degenerate probability distribution \mu is said to be stable (or strictly stable if d_n = 0) if for every n \ge 2 and independent random variables X_1, \dots, X_n \sim \mu, there exist constants c_n > 0 and d_n \in \mathbb{R}$ such that \sum_{k=1}^n X_k \stackrel{d}{=} c_n X_1 + d_n. The scaling constant necessarily takes the form c_n = n^{1/\alpha} for a unique parameter \alpha \in (0, 2], called the characteristic exponent (or index of stability).
title: Stable Probability Distribution

body: Let H(q,p,t) be a Hamiltonian on phase space with canonical coordinates (q,p), whose flow is generated by Hamilton's equations dq/dt = dH/dp, dp/dt = -dH/dq. Liouville's theorem states that the time-t flow map preserves phase-space (Lebesgue) volume: for every measurable region D, the volume of the image of D under the flow equals the volume of D, for all t; equivalently the flow's Jacobian determinant is identically 1. If rho(q,p,t) is the phase-space density of an ensemble evolving under H, this is equivalent to partial rho/partial t + {rho, H} = 0, where {.,.} is the Poisson bracket, so density is constant along trajectories.
title: Liouville's theorem (Hamiltonian mechanics)

[Proposition 5 of arXiv:2607.16479, 'The Site Frequency Spectrum in an Exponentially-Growing Population with Selection'] The scaled SFS has the following exact form:
  
  \[e^{-\lambda_0t}\mathbb{E}[S_j(t)]=(av+\mu)\int_0^t e^{-\lambda_0 s}P_j(s)\,ds=(av+\mu)\frac{\Gamma(j)\Gamma(\lambda_0/\lambda_1+1)}{\Gamma(j+\lambda_0/\lambda_1+1)}\sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{(\lambda_0/\lambda_1)_n(j)_n}{(j+1+\lambda_0/\lambda_1)_nn!}p_1^n\]

  And, the following frequency asymptotic:

  \[\lim_{t\to\infty}e^{-\lambda_0t}\mathbb{E}[S_j(t)]=(av+\mu)\frac{q_1\Gamma(\lambda_0/\lambda_1+1)}{\lambda_1j^{\lambda_0/\lambda_1+1}}(1-p_1)^{-\lambda_0/\lambda_1}+\mathcal{O}\left(\frac{1}{j^{\lambda_0/\lambda_1+2}}\right)\]
