body:
Assuming the axiom of choice, the closed unit ball B in R^3 can be partitioned into finitely many pieces which can be reassembled by rigid motions (rotations and translations) into two disjoint copies of B; five pieces suffice (Robinson), and four do not. More generally (the strong form) any two bounded subsets of R^n, n >= 3, with nonempty interior are equidecomposable: one can be cut into finitely many pieces and moved by isometries onto the other. The pieces are necessarily non-measurable, so no contradiction with Lebesgue measure arises - the theorem shows that no finitely additive, isometry-invariant measure defined on ALL subsets of R^3 and normalising the ball can exist. In dimensions 1 and 2 the paradox fails: Banach showed that Lebesgue measure on R and R^2 extends to a finitely additive isometry-invariant measure on all subsets, because the isometry groups of R and R^2 are amenable (solvable), while SO(3) contains a free group on two generators, which is the source of the paradox (Hausdorff, 1914). Tarski's theorem (1929) makes this exact: a group action admits a paradoxical decomposition if and only if it carries no finitely additive invariant probability measure, i.e. it is non-amenable. With choice the result is a theorem; in ZF plus the axiom of determinacy, or in Solovay's model, every set of reals is measurable and the decomposition does not exist.
the axiom of choice (used in step 3 to select orbit representatives; the result is not a theorem of ZF alone)
n >= 3 for the paradox; rigid motions of R^n (isometries); 'pieces' are arbitrary sets, necessarily non-measurable

[Definition def:SC-infinity of arXiv:2608.11931, '\texorpdfstring{Nonlinear parabolic characterizations of stochastic completeness at infini'] A graph $G=(X,w,\kappa,\mu)$ satisfies \emph{stochastic completeness at infinity} \hyperref[def:SC-infinity]{\textup{{(SC\textsubscript{$\infty$})}}}{} if for some (and hence all) $t>0,$
$$e^{-tL}1+\int_0^t e^{-sL}\left(\frac{\kappa}{\mu}\right)\,\mathrm d s=1.$$
When $\kappa=0$ and the above holds, then $G$ is said to  satisfy \emph{stochastic completeness} \hyperref[def:SC]{\textup{(SC)}}{}.
Otherwise, a graph is said to be \emph{stochastically incomplete (at infinity)}.
title: Stochastic completeness at infinity

[Corollary cor:atomic of arXiv:2607.08551, 'Weighted-threshold Coupon Collection'] Fix $s>1$ and $t>0$. Then
\[
M_N^{(s)}(t)\xrightarrow[N\to\infty]{L^1} M_\infty^{(s)}(t),
\]
and the limiting random variable is non-degenerate,
\[
\mathrm{Var}\bigl(M_\infty^{(s)}(t)\bigr)\ge
\bigl(q_1^{(s)}\bigr)^2 e^{-\lambda q_1^{(s)} t}\bigl(1-e^{-\lambda q_1^{(s)} t}\bigr)>0.
\]
In particular, the atomic regime does not collapse to a deterministic discovered-mass curve.

body:
[Lemma 17 of arXiv:2608.15914, 'Absorption cutoff and stationary singularities for rounded Gaussian random dynamical syste'] Assume $0<A<A_c(N)$, and let $x_0\in\R^N$ be deterministic. Run the
  chain $X^{(N)}$ from $X_0^{(N)}=x_0$ and $Y^{(N)}$ from
  $Y_0^{(N)}=Q_\varrho(x_0)$ with the same Gaussian matrices.
  There is $C_N<\infty$, depending only on $N$, such that the following holds.
  For $0<C_0<\infty$, define
  \begin{equation*}
    T_\varrho:=\left\lfloor C_0\log(1/\varrho)\right\rfloor .
  \end{equation*}
  There exists $p=p(A,N,C_0)$ satisfying
  \begin{equation}
    0
    \leq
    p
    \leq
    C_N(1+C_0)
    \left(
      1+\frac1{\gamma_{A,N}}
    \right),
  \end{equation}
  and
  \begin{equation}
    \Pp\left(
      \max_{0\leq t\leq T_\varrho}
      \norm{Y_t^{(N)}-X_t^{(N)}}_2
      >
      \varrho\,\left(\log(1/\varrho)\right)^p
    \right)
    \to0
  \end{equation}
  as $\varrho\downarrow0$.
title: Lemma 17 of arXiv:2608.15914

[Theorem 2 (Cubic global thin obstacle solutions) of arXiv:2609.00703, 'Ellipsoidal Positivity Sets for Fractional Obstacle Problems with Quadratic Forcing'] Let \(n\ge2\), and let \(W\) be a global solution of the thin obstacle problem in \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\)
with cubic growth and nonempty bounded positivity set on the thin space.
Then, after a translation in the thin variables, there exist \(K>0\) and a positive definite symmetric
matrix \(B\) such that
\[
\{W(\cdot,0)>0\}
=
\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\langle Bx,x\rangle<1\}
\]
and
\[
W(x,0)
=
K\bigl(1-\langle Bx,x\rangle\bigr)_+^{3/2}.
\]
In particular, the positivity set on the thin space is an ellipsoid.
Hence the conjecture of Fern\'andez-Real and Yu \cite[Conjecture~4.2]{FRY}
holds in the nonempty bounded-positivity case. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Cubic global thin obstacle solutions

AUTHOR-DERIVED FINITE IDENTITY, explicit referee acceptance pending. On a finite connected graph with iid Uniform[1,2] edge weights and fixed terminals, define clipped off-edge thresholds a_e in [0,1] so that centered coordinate costs are min(U,a_e)-a_e+a_e^2/2 for U uniform on [0,1]. For a<=b, K(a,b)=a^2[b(2-b)/4-a/6], and K is symmetric. Under independent rate-one coordinate refresh, Var(T)=integral_0^infinity exp(-t)H(t)dt, where H(t)=sum_e E K(a_e(eta),a_e(eta^t)) and only off-edge coordinates are coupled inside H. Its limit is the first-order Hoeffding energy L, not generally zero. H(t)-L is the sum over |S|>=2 of |S|exp(-(|S|-1)t)||T_S||_2^2. A full-kernel integrable decay envelope for all t is impossible when L>0. No lattice exponent estimate is asserted.

[Definition landing of arXiv:2604.17170, 'CaTherine wheels from trees and Liouville quantum gravity'] A {\em ray} is a half-open interval in $Z$ (i.e.\/ a subspace homeomorphic to $[0,1)$).
It is a {\em proper ray} if the inclusion $[0,1) \subset Z$ is a proper embedding. 
A ray {\em lands} if it extends continuously to an embedding of $[0,1]$; the
image of $1$ is called the {\em landing point}.

A half-zipper has the {\em strong landing property} if every ray in $Z$ lands, and
if every point in $S^2$ is the landing point of some ray in $Z$.
title: Landing ray

[Definition 16 of arXiv:2606.24056, 'Decorated stable $p$-adic self-similar processes with stationary increments'] Assume \(0<\alpha<2\) and $d\geq 1$.  If a real symmetric \(S\alpha S\) vector
\(V=(V_1,\ldots,V_d)\) has the representation
\[
  V=\int_E f(x)\,M_\alpha(dx),
  \qquad f:E\to\R^d,
\]
then its projective spectral measure is defined as the pushforward of
\(\|f(x)\|^\alpha\mu(dx)\) restricted to \(\{x:f(x)\ne0\}\) under
\[
  x\mapsto [f(x)]\in\mathbf P^{d-1}(\R),
\]
where \(\mathbf P^{d-1}(\R)\) is the \((d-1)\)-dimensional real projective space.
Its projective spectral support is defined as the support of the projective spectral measure.

body: [Definition def:cle_metric of arXiv:2507.15589, 'Tightness of approximations to metrics on non-simple conformal loop ensemble gaskets'] Suppose that $\mathcal {L}$ is a random non-self-crossing loop in $\mathbf{C}$, and let $D$ be the regions surrounded by $\mathcal {L}$. Given $\mathcal {L}$, let $\Gamma_D$ be a conditionally independent ${\rm CLE}_{\kappa'}${} in each connected component of $D$, and let $\Gamma = \{\mathcal {L}\} \cup \Gamma_D$. We call a family of random metrics $(\metapproxres{\epsilon}{V}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma})_{V \in \metregions}$ coupled with $\Gamma$ that satisfies the assumptions above an \emph{approximate ${\rm CLE}_{\kappa'}${} metric}. In the case $\epsilon = 0$ we call $(\metres{V}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma})_{V \in \metregions}$ a \emph{${\rm CLE}_{\kappa'}${} metric}. We call $\metapproxres{\epsilon}{V}{\cdot}{\cdot}{\Gamma}$ the \emph{internal metric in $V$}.

[Lemma 5 of arXiv:2609.02850, 'Canonical-row Chern flow on Bott--Samelson towers:\\ realizable-volume models for Schubert'] Let $f_k\in\RR[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ be homogeneous of degree $d+k$ for
$0\le k\le r$, and put
\[
 \widehat f(x,z)=\sum_{k=0}^r f_k(x)z^{r-k},
 \qquad
 S=\bigcup_{k=0}^r\Supp(f_k).
\]
Assume that $\Supp(\widehat f)$ is $M$-convex.  Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item $S$ is $M^\natural$-convex and
\[
 S=\operatorname{conv}(S)\cap\ZZ^n.
\]
\item If $a_k\ne0$ for every nonzero layer, then
\[
 \Supp\!\left(\sum_{k=0}^r a_k f_k\right)=S.
\]
\item The parameter polynomial $\sum_{k=0}^r f_k(x)\beta^k$ has saturated
Newton polytope in $\ZZ^{n+1}$.
\end{enumerate}

[Definition defn:Whitney_McShane_operator of arXiv:2609.03129, 'A Closed-Form Formula for Consistent Lipschitz Regression on Metric Spaces with Sparse Neu'] Let $(X,\rho)$ be a bounded metric space and fix $N\in \mathbb{N}_+$.  The \textit{$N$-point Whitney-McShane operator} is the map
\[
\begin{aligned}
    \mathcal{E}:
    (\operatorname{Lip}((X,\rho);1),\|\cdot\|_\infty)
    \times
    ([X\times \mathbb{R}]^N,\rho_1)
&\longrightarrow
    (\operatorname{Lip}((X,\rho);1),\|\cdot\|_\infty),
\\
    (f,\mathcal{D}_N)
&\longmapsto
    \mathcal{E}(f,\mathcal{D}_N),
\end{aligned}
\]
where, for every $\mathcal{D}_N\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}} (x_n,y_n)_{n=1}^N\in [X\times \mathbb{R}]^N$, for each $z\in X$ by
\[
        \mathcal{E}(f,\mathcal{D}_N)(z)
    \ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}}
        \max_{n\in[N]_+}
        \,
            \big\{
                [f(x_n)+y_n]-\rho(z,x_n)
            \big\}
.
\]
title: $N$-Point Whitney-McShane Operator

body: [Definition def:matbracket of arXiv:2601.10359, 'An Operator It\^o Formula for Volterra Gaussian Processes:\\ The Intrinsic Bracket via Cau'] Define $\langle X^i, X^j\rangle^{(D,\Pi)}_t := \inner{\Pi DX^i_t}{\Pi DX^j_t}_\mathcal{H}$, where $D$ is the Malliavin derivative with respect to the common Brownian motion $W$ and $\mathcal{H} = L^2([0,T])$. Since $DX^i_t = K_i(t,\cdot)$ is deterministic, the cross-bracket equals $\langle X^i, X^j\rangle^{(D,\Pi)}_t = \int_0^t K_i(t,r)K_j(t,r)\,dr = \mathbb{E}[X^i_t X^j_t]$, and is deterministic.
title: Matrix-valued intrinsic bracket

[Prop 11 of arXiv:2604.12334, 'On additive averaging kernels for finite Markov chains'] Consider some ergodic $P \in \mathcal{L}(\pi)$ and let $|\mathcal{X}| \geq 2$. Recall the function h introduced in \eqref{eq:h(S)}. Any solution
    $$U^* = \{x^*\} \in \argmax_{S\in \mathcal{A}} h(S)$$
    is an additive $2\alpha(1-\alpha)$-approximate minimiser of the squared Frobenius distance $\|A_\alpha(S) - \Pi\|_{F,\pi}^2$. That is, 
    $$S^* \in \argmin_{S\in \mathcal{A}} \|A_\alpha(S) - \Pi\|_{F,\pi}^2$$ 
    satisfies 
    $$ 0\leq \|A_\alpha(U^*) - \Pi\|_{F,\pi}^2 - \|A_\alpha(S^*) - \Pi\|_{F,\pi}^2 \leq 2\alpha(1-\alpha).$$

Let 1<=r<min(p,q), n>p+1, x_i iid N(0,I_p), and y_i=(W0+Delta)x_i+e_i, where e_i iid N(0,sigma^2 I_q) are independent of all inputs, W0 is fixed, and rank(Delta)<=r. Set X=[x_i], Y=[y_i], C=XX^T/n, and M=(Y-W0X)X^T(XX^T)^(-1)C^(1/2). Let W_hat=W0+trunc_r(M)C^(-1/2), where trunc_r is a best rank-r singular-value truncation. This is a global rank-constrained empirical least-squares estimator. There is a universal constant K such that E||W_hat-(W0+Delta)||_F^2 <= K*sigma^2*r*max(p,q)/n * E||C^(-1)||_op. The stronger n>p+1 assumption ensures that the inverse-covariance expectation is finite. This is the exact-rank isotropic specialization of Zindari-Mulayoff-Stich, arXiv:2605.19018, Theorem 2 (p.5) using Proposition 2 (p.3), with proof in Appendix V.1. It is a guarantee for the global estimator; it is not an initialization-specific convergence theorem for the factor GD iterates.

[Lemma 13 of arXiv:2609.02105, 'Contact fundamental forms and \\ adjoint varieties'] For  $v_1,\ldots,v_N\in\fh_1$, put
$$
{\rm Sym}(v_1\cdots v_N):=\frac1{N!}\sum_{\sigma\in\mathfrak S_N}
v_{\sigma(1)}\cdots v_{\sigma(N)}.
$$
Let us use the convention ${\rm Sym}(v_1 \cdots v_N)=1$ if $N=0$ and ${\rm Sym}(v_1 \cdots v_N)=0$ if $N<0$.  Then for any $x \in \fh_1$, 
\begin{equation}
x\,{\rm Sym}(v_1\cdots v_N)
={\rm Sym}(xv_1\cdots v_N)
+\frac12\sum_{r=1}^N [x,v_r]\,
{\rm Sym}(v_1\cdots\widehat v_r\cdots v_N),
\end{equation}
where $v_1\cdots\widehat v_r\cdots v_N$ means the collection of vectors with $v_r $ removed.

DRAFT Own-work; proof (unaudited), claim w725-T329-001; independent audit pending. Let n>=4, fixed d,C>=2, and admissible separated bounded samples as in Vardi?Yehudai?Shamir Theorem 6.2. Normalize r>=1,delta<=1 and assume r/delta<=n^a for fixed a, so h=log_2(d*n*C*r/delta)=Theta(log n). Write the displayed precision certificate as A*s*h/sqrt(log_2 s), with fixed A>0, and require this certificate to be <=beta=c*log_2 n. Then f(s)=s/sqrt(log_2 s)<=c/A, so s<=(c/A)^2 because log_2 s<=s for integer s>=2. For c sufficiently large, s=2 meets the budget. The displayed depth expression n*h/f(s) is then Theta(n log n); it provides W=O(d+n log n), not a lower bound on actual W. Its comparison with the finite-description counting lower scale Omega(n/log n) leaves a factor (log n)^2. The exact product of the two unscaled certificate expressions is (h*f(s))*(n*h/f(s))=n*h^2. No optimal memorization theorem follows from this limitation on a certificate. Fixed d and fixed r/delta bound n by (1+2r/delta)^d, so an unbounded-n comparison needs a growing geometric scale. body: In combinatorics, two Latin squares of the same size (order) are said to be orthogonal if when superimposed the ordered paired entries in the positions are all distinct. A set of Latin squares, all of the same order, all pairs of which are orthogonal is called a set of mutually orthogonal Latin squares. This concept of orthogonality in combinatorics is strongly related to the concept of blocking in statistics, which ensures that independent variables are truly independent with no hidden confounding correlations. "Orthogonal" is thus synonymous with "independent" in that knowing one variable's value gives no further information about another variable's likely value.
title: Mutually orthogonal Latin squares

body:
[Lem 252 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] If $\bX:\R^{N'}\to\R^N$ is $L$-Lipschitz, $\bg$ is a standard gaussian in $\R^{N'}$, and $\E[\|\bX(\bg)\|^2] = N$, then for any $\delta > 0$, there exists $c(\delta) > 0$ such that 
    \[
    \P\bigg(
    \bigg|\frac{\|\bX(\bg)\|^2}{N} - 1\bigg|
    \ge \delta\bigg)
    \le e^{-c(\delta)N}\,.\]

\begin{proof}
    Since $\bg \mapsto \|\bX(\bg)\|$ is $L$-Lipschitz, it follows from Lemma~\ref{l:lip.subgaus} that $\|\bX(\bg)\|-\E\|\bX(\bg)\|$ is subgaussian with variance proxy $2L^2$, and satisfies the concentration bound \eqref{e:lip.subgaus}:
    \[
    \P\bigg( \Big|
    \|\bX(\bg)\| - \E\|\bX(\bg)\|\Big| \ge t
    \bigg) \le 2\exp\bigg\{-\frac{t^2}{2L^2}\bigg\}\,.
    \]
It follows that $\|\bX(\bg)\|$ has variance $O(L^2)$, which implies
    \[
     \frac{O(L^2)}{N}
     \ge
    \frac{\E[\|\bX(\bg)\|^2] - ( \E\|\bX(\bg)\|)^2}{N}
    =1- \frac{ ( \E\|\bX(\bg)\|)^2}{N}\,.
    \]
Combining the last two displays gives the claim.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 252 of arXiv:2608.29416

[Theorem thm:critArithmetic of arXiv:2606.30517, '\textsc{Convergence towards Ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations with a focus on Diestel--'] Let $r >0$ and the sequence $(\lambda_n)_{n \geq 1}$ be given. 
		If the limit $\nu\coloneqq  \lim_{n \to \infty} \lambda_n \iota_{nr}^*\mu$ exists and is nonzero, then:
		\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
			\item  There exist $p>1$, $\xi\in\mathbb R$, a probability measure $\varphi$ on $(0,r]$ and a family of probability measures $\nu_t$ on $\partial E$ for $0<t\leq r$ such that the map $t\mapsto \nu_t$ is measurable (i.e., $\nu_{(\cdot)}$ is a Markov kernel from $(0,r]$ to $\partial E$) and 
			\begin{eqnarray}
				
				
				
				\nu&=& \sum_{j\in\mathbb Z} (p-1)p^{j+\xi} \int_0^r \left(\nu_t\otimes\delta_{jr+t}\right) \varphi(dt),\\
				
				\iota_{ir}^* \nu &=& p^i \nu,\quad \forall i\in\mathbb Z,\\
				
				\limsup_{n \to \infty} \lambda_n F(nr) &\leq& \nu\left(\mathrm{Lip}_1^{\leq 0}\right) = p^\xi,\\
				
				\liminf_{n \to \infty} \lambda_n F^-(nr) &\geq & \nu\left(\mathrm{Lip}_1^{<0}\right) = p^\xi\left(1-\frac{p-1}{p} \varphi(\{r\})\right).
			\end{eqnarray}
			Also, $p, \xi$ and $\varphi$ are uniquely determined and $\nu_{(\cdot)}$ is unique up to modification on $\varphi$-null sets.
			\item  The shifted Poisson point process $\iota_{nr} X^{(\lambda_n)}$ converges weakly as $n\to \infty$ to a Poisson point process $(\Theta_i,\Delta_i)_{i\geq 1}$ on $\widehat{\partial E}$ with intensity measure $\nu$. In other words, the delay process $(\Delta_i)_{i\geq 1}$ is a Poisson point process on $\mathbb R$ with intensity measure $\beta^{(\xi)}(A)\coloneqq \sum_{j\in \mathbb Z} (p-1)p^{\xi+j} \varphi(A-jr)$ for $A\subseteq \mathbb R$. In addition, conditionally on $(\Delta_i)_{i\geq 1}$, the points $(\Theta_i)_{i\geq 1}$ are independent points on $\partial E$ such that $\Theta_i$ has distribution $\nu_{\Delta'_i}$, where $\Delta'_i$ is the unique number in $(0,r]$ such that $\Delta_i-\Delta'_i\in r\mathbb Z$.
			\item  For all except countably many $a\in\mathbb R$, the function $n\mapsto F(a+nr)$‌ is log-regularly-varying with index $b\coloneqq \ln p$ and, if $\mu_n$ is the normalized restriction of $\mu$ to  $B_{a+(n+1)r}(\mathbf{o} )\setminus B_{a+ n r}(\mathbf{o})$, then $\iota_{n r}^*\mu_n$ converges weakly to the normalized restriction of $\nu$ to ${\mathrm{Lip}_1^{(a,a+r]}}$.
		\end{enumerate}

Applying the Chinese remainder theorem to the safe modulus $\widehat n=f_nn$ gives
\begin{equation}
\sum_{\substack{a\bmod f_nd^2n\\
a\bmod d^2\in\mathcal R_{r,d}(Q)}}

[Lemma AveragedEstimate of arXiv:2411.06089, '{\Large \bf Averaging principle for semilinear slow-fast rough partial differential equati'] Suppose that conditions $(\mathbf{H1})$ and $(\mathbf{H2})$ hold.
For any $T>0$, $x\in \mathcal H$ and $\mathbf B=(B,B^2)\in \mathscr{C}^\gamma([0,T]; \mathbb R^d)$ with $\gamma \in (1/3, \gamma_0)$,
Eq.~(equation Averagedeq of the paper) has a unique global solution $(\bar{X},\bar{X}^\prime) \in \mathcal D_{\mathbf B}^{2\gamma, \eta}([0,T]; \mathcal H)$ with $\eta \in [0,\gamma)$ such that
$\bar{X}^\prime=G_1(\bar{X})$ and
$$\bar{X}_t=S_t x +\int_0^t S_{t-s} \bar{F}_1(\bar{X}_s)ds +\int_0^t S_{t-s} G_1 (\bar{X}_s) d \mathbf B_s, ~~~~ t\in [0,T].$$
Moreover, there exists a constant $C>0$ such that
\begin{equation}
	 \|\bar{X}\|_{\eta, 0} \leq C(1+\|x\|_{\mathcal H}).
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma AveragedEstimate of arXiv:2411.06089

[Proposition prop:entangled-recovery of arXiv:2607.18070, 'The Brownian loop-catcher'] Let $(P_1,\ldots,P_r)$ be the output records of independent normalized random walks
$\omega_i:a_i\to b_i$ ($1\le i\le r$) in Definition~(def:entangled of the paper), and let $\gamma_i$ be the corresponding
 entangled multipath LERW.  Independently sample an unrooted random-walk loop soup in $R$ with intensity $1$, and assign each loop that intersects $C_r$ to the smallest $i$ for which
it intersects $\gamma_i$, and then to the earliest path time $s$ on $\gamma_i$
at which such an intersection occurs.  If the loop visits $\gamma_i(s)$ more than once, choose uniformly one of those visits as its starting time. For each time on the entangled multipath LERW, order its assigned random-walk loops by an independent
uniform permutation and insert them in that order. Then conditioned on
$(P_1,\ldots,P_r)$, the resulting tuple of paths has the same law as the conditional law of $(\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_r)$ given $(P_1,\ldots,P_r)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 6 (Critical rigidity) of arXiv:2609.03339, 'Exterior Serrin Rigidity for the Homogeneous \texorpdfstring{$k$}{k}-Hessian Equation\\'] Let $k=\frac{n}{2}$, and let $\Omega\Subset\R^n$ be smooth,
		bounded, strictly star-shaped, and strictly $(k-1)$-convex.  For some
		$\mathcal{A}>0$, suppose that $u\in C^{1,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\overline E)$  is a k-admissible solution of
			\begin{equation}
			\begin{cases}
				\sigma_k(D^2u)=0&\text{in }~\R^n\setminus\overline\Omega,\\
				u=0& \text{on}~\partial\Omega,\\
				u(x)-\mathcal{A}\log|x|=O(1)&\text{as }|x|\to\infty.
			\end{cases}
		\end{equation}	
	
	
	
	
	
		If $u_\nu=|Du|=c>0$ on $\partial\Omega$, then for some
		$x_0\in\R^n$,
		\[
		\Omega=B_R(x_0),\qquad
		R=\frac{\mathcal{A}}{c},\qquad
		u(x)=\mathcal{A}\log\frac{|x-x_0|}{R}.
		\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 5 (Inverse-stable size-biased factor) of arXiv:2606.18458, 'Stable size-biasing and the positive scale-mixture order of generalized Gaussian laws'] Let $a>b>0$, set $\alpha=b/a\in(0,1)$, and let $S_\alpha$ be as in Lemma~2. Put

W_0=S_\alpha^{-b},
\]
and let $W$ be the $W_0$-size-biased version of $W_0$. Then, for $\Repart s>-1$,

\E W^s=\frac{\Gamma(a(s+1))\Gamma(b)}{\Gamma(b(s+1))\Gamma(a)}.

V=2^{a-b}W,
\]
then
\begin{equation}
\E V^s=2^{(a-b)s}\frac{\Gamma(a(s+1))\Gamma(b)}{\Gamma(b(s+1))\Gamma(a)},\qquad \Repart s>-1.

\end{equation}

body:
The model used by Wang-Huang-Li-Wu in arXiv:2609.02728 is Gaussian-feature, online least-squares regression. In the covariance eigenbasis, a feature vector phi has centered Gaussian law N(0,H) with H=diag(lambda_1,lambda_2,...) positive trace class, lambda_1>=lambda_2>=...>0. A label is y=<phi,theta_star>+epsilon with epsilon~N(0,sigma^2) independent of phi. The target has finite prediction energy sum_j lambda_j*|theta_star_j|^2<infinity; the pairing can equivalently be read as its mean-square-convergent Gaussian series. The population risk is R(theta)=E(<phi,theta>-y)^2/2, and the excess risk is Ecal(theta)=sum_j lambda_j*|theta_j-theta_star_j|^2/2=R(theta)-sigma^2/2. Their source/capacity assumptions are beta>1,s>0, lambda_j asymp j^(-beta) and lambda_j*|theta_star_j|^2 asymp j^(-(1+s*beta)), where asymp means upper and lower bounds by fixed positive constants, uniform in j. The label-noise standard deviation sigma is bounded above and away from zero by fixed constants (the constant-order noisy setting). At iteration k a fresh IID batch of B examples, independent of all past batches, gives the AVERAGED gradient g(theta;batch)=B^(-1)*sum_i phi_(k,i)*(<phi_(k,i),theta>-y_(k,i)). For a constant eta>0 and constant rho in[0,1), SGD uses theta_(k+1)=theta_k-eta*g(theta_k;batch); Polyak uses theta_(k+1)=theta_k-eta*g(theta_k;batch)+rho*(theta_k-theta_(k-1)); Nesterov first sets theta_k_la=theta_k+rho*(theta_k-theta_(k-1)) and uses theta_(k+1)=theta_k_la-eta*g(theta_k_la;batch). The source scaling-law analysis takes theta_0=theta_-1=0. For a one-pass data budget D, take T=D/B updates (or integer rounding at the exponent level), and B=D^(b+o(1)) with fixed b in[0,1). Hyperparameters can depend on D but are constant within each run. This protocol concerns final expected excess risk; it is not a finite-data repeated-epoch protocol, nor a theorem giving explicit constants in the critical-batch trade-off.
Definition of the specific source model; beta>1,s>0,uniform power-law comparison constants.
Fresh independent Gaussian features and independent Gaussian constant-order label noise; averaged minibatch gradients.
Zero initial iterate and zero initial momentum for the scaling-law protocol.

[Theorem 28 of arXiv:2609.01098, 'Gaussian upper bounds for averaged heat semigroups on graphs'] Let $o\in X$, $n>0$, $r\geq 0$, $C\geq 1$, $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, $q\colon [r,\infty)\to (0,\infty)$ monotone increasing with $q(t)\to\infty$ as $t\to\infty$, and
\[
A\geq  
\left((2C)^{3(2C)^{21n}}\cdot 1\vee  m(B(r)^{\frac{(2C)^{21n}}{q(r)}}\right)^\frac{q(r^2)}{q(r^2)-1}.
\] 
Assume \[
\mathcal{P}_{r}(t,o,o)
 \leq 
\frac{C}{\sqrt[\frac{q(t)}{q(t)-1}]{m(B(\sqrt t))}}
\]
for all $r^2\leq t\leq 2A^4r^2$ and
\[
\frac{m(B_x(s_2))}{m(B_x(s_1))}\leq C\left(\frac{s_2}{s_1}\right)^n
\]
for all $x\in B(2Ar)$ and $r\leq s_1\leq s_2\leq 2A^2r$.
Then, for all $U\subset B(r)$ satisfying $m(U)\geq \varepsilon m(B(r))$, we have 
\[
\lambda(U)
\geq 
\frac{C_n}{A^4r^2}
\left(
\frac{m(B(r))}{m(U)}\right)^{\frac{2}{N}},
\]
where $C_n=\frac{1}{C^{\frac{4}{n}}2^{5+\frac{4}{n}}}$ and 
\[
N\geq n\frac{q(r^2)}{q(r^2)-1}+ \frac{\ln\frac{1}{\epsilon}}{\ln A}+\frac{1}{q(r^2)-1}\ln(1\vee m(B(r))).
\]

[Lemma 12 of arXiv:2506.11918, 'Central limit theorems for the Euler characteristic in the Random Connection Model for hig'] Let $F=\chi_a\big(\Delta_W\big)$.
There are constants $C_i>0$, $i\in\{1,\dots,7\}$, not depending on $W\in\Bf$, such that
\begin{align}
\int_{W^3} \E{ \left( \Lambda_{(x_1,U_1),(x_2,U_2)}^1F \right)^2 \left( \Lambda_{(x_2,U_2),(x_1,U_1)}^1F \right)^2}^\frac{1}{2} \hspace{4cm} & \nonumber \\
\times \, \E{ \left(\Lambda_{(x_1,U_1),(x_3,U_3),(x_2,U_2)}^2 F\right)^2 \left(\Lambda_{(x_2,U_2),(x_3,U_3),(x_1,U_1)}^2 F\right)^2}^\frac{1}{2}  \; \lambda^3 \, (\d {x}) &\;\leq\; C_1|W|,  \\[8pt]
\int_{W^3} \E{ \left(\Lambda_{(x_1,U_1),(x_3,U_3),(x_2,U_2)}^2 F\right)^2 \left(\Lambda_{(x_2,U_2),(x_3,U_3),(x_1,U_1)}^2 F\right)^2} \; \lambda^3 \, (\d {x}) &\;\leq\; C_2|W|,  \\[8pt]
\int_W \E{ |\Lambda_{(x,U)}F|^3 } \; \lambda \, (\d x) &\;\leq\; C_3|W|,  \\[8pt]
\int_W \E{ \left(\Lambda_{(x,U)}F\right)^4 }^\frac{3}{4} \; \lambda \, (\d x) &\;\leq\; C_4|W|,  \\[8pt]
\int_W \E{ \left(\Lambda_{(x,U)}F\right)^4 } \; \lambda \, (\d x) &\;\leq\; C_5|W|,  \\[8pt]
\int_{W^2} 6\; \E{ \left(\Lambda_{(x_1,U_1)}F\right)^4 }^\frac{1}{2} \E{ \left(\Lambda_{(x_1,U_1),(x_2,U_2)}^2 F\right)^4 }^\frac{1}{2} \hspace{3.66cm} & \nonumber \\
+ 3\; \E{ \left(\Lambda_{(x_1,U_1),(x_2,U_2)}^2 F\right)^4 } \; \lambda^2 \, (\d {x}) &\;\leq\; C_6|W|,  \\[8pt]
\int_W \E{ \left(\Lambda_{(x,U)}F\right)^4 }^\frac{1}{2} \; \lambda \, (\d x) &\;\leq\; C_7|W|, 
\end{align}
where the integration is to be understood with respect to the points $x_i$.

[Theorem thm:matrixBernstein of arXiv:2510.01021, '\Large Random Matrices, Intrinsic Freeness, and Sharp Non-Asymptotic Inequalities\relatedv'] Let $\{H_k\}_{k=1}^n$ be a sequence of independent random symmetric $d\times d$ matrices. Assume that each $H_k$ satisfies:
 \[
  \mathbb{E} H_k = 0 \text{ and } \lambda_{\max}\left( H_k \right) \leq R \text{ almost surely.}
 \]
Then, for all $t\geq 0$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb{P}\left[ \lambda_{\max}\left( \sum_{k=1}^n H_k \right) \geq t \right] \leq d \cdot \exp\left( \frac{-t^2}{2\sigma^2 + \frac23Rt} \right) \text{ where } \sigma^2 = \left\| \sum_{k=1}^n\mathbb{E}\left(H_k^2\right) \right\|.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Matrix Bernstein~\cite{Oliveira1-2010,Oliveira2-2010,Tro12:User-Friendly-Tail,Tro15:Introduction-Matrix}

[Definition 25 (Iterative maximal feasible independent set (IMFIS) process) of arXiv:2608.07239, 'Unified framework for asymptotically uniform iterative construction of generalised random '] Consider a tuple $(G,F,R,\b)$, where $G=(V,E)$ is a graph with $F\subset V$ a set of forbidden vertices, $R\subset V^2$ an equivalence relation of forbidden pairs of vertices, and $\b:V\to\mathbb{R}$ a weight function.
		
		Start with the empty set $\boldsymbol{S}_0=\emptyset$. For $r=0$ onward, if $(V\setminus\overline{N}(\boldsymbol{S}_r))\setminus(F\cup R^*(\boldsymbol{S}_r))$ is empty, let $\boldsymbol{S}_{r+1}=\boldsymbol{S}_r$. Otherwise, choose $v\in(V\setminus\overline{N}(\boldsymbol{S}_r))\setminus(F\cup R^*(\boldsymbol{S}_r))$ at random with probability proportional to $e^{-\b(v)}$, and let $\boldsymbol{S}_{r+1}=\boldsymbol{S}_r\cup\{v\}$. Finally, define $\boldsymbol{S}_{\infty}=\cup_{r=0}^{\infty}\boldsymbol{S}_r$.
title: Iterative maximal feasible independent set (IMFIS) process

body:
[Defn rational SLE0 of arXiv:2505.14762, 'Multiple radial SLE($\kappa$) and quantum Calogero-Sutherland system'] In the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$, let $e^{i\theta} \in \partial \mathbb{D}$ be the growth point, and let $u_1, u_2, \dots, u_m \in \overline{\mathbb{D}}$ be marked points. A symmetric double divisor $(\boldsymbol{\sigma}^+, \boldsymbol{\sigma}^-)$ assigns a charge distribution on $e^{i\theta}$ and $\{u_1, \dots, u_k\}$, where
\[
\boldsymbol{\sigma}^+ = a \cdot e^{i\theta} + \sum_{j=1}^{k} \sigma_j \cdot u_j,
\quad \text{and} \quad
\boldsymbol{\sigma}^- = \overline{\boldsymbol{\sigma}^+}|_{\mathbb{D}},
\]
and the total charge satisfies the neutrality condition $\int\boldsymbol{\sigma}=-2$.

We define the rational $\mathrm{SLE}_0[\boldsymbol{\sigma}]$ Loewner chain as a normalized conformal map $g_t(z)$ with initial conditions $g_0(z) = z$ and $g_t'(0) = e^{-t}$. The evolution of $g_t$ is governed by the Loewner differential equation:
\[
\partial_t g_t(z) = g_t(z) \frac{e^{i\theta(t)} + g_t(z)}{e^{i\theta(t)} - g_t(z)}, \quad g_0(z) = z.
\]

In the angular coordinate, let $h_t(z)$ be the covering map of $g_t(z)$ defined by $e^{i h_t(z)} = g_t(e^{i z})$. Then $h_t(z)$ evolves according to
\[
\partial_t h_t(z) = \cot\left( \frac{h_t(z) - \theta(t)}{2} \right), \quad h_0(z) = z.
\]

The driving function $\theta(t)$ evolves according to
\[
d\theta(t) = \frac{\partial \log \mathcal{Z}(\boldsymbol{\theta})}{\partial \theta} \, dt.
\]

where the Coulomb gas partition function is
\begin{equation} 
\mathcal{Z}(\boldsymbol{\theta}) = \prod_{j < k} \sin\left( \frac{\theta_j - \theta_k}{2} \right)^{\sigma_j \sigma_k} 
\cdot \prod_j e^{\frac{i}{2} \sigma_j (\sigma_0 - \sigma_\infty)\theta_j}.
\end{equation}

The flow $g_t$ is well-defined up to the first time $\tau$ at which $w(t) = g_t(w)$ for some $w$ in the support of $\boldsymbol{\sigma}$. For each $z \in \overline{\mathbb{D}}$, the process $t \mapsto g_t(z)$ is well-defined up to $\tau_z \wedge \tau$, where $\tau_z$ is the first time such that $g_t(z) = e^{i\theta(t)}$. Denote
\[
K_t = \left\{ z \in \overline{\mathbb{D}} : \tau_z \leq t \right\}
\]
as the hull associated with the Loewner chain.

Furthermore, the rational $\mathrm{SLE}_0$ Loewner chain is invariant under Möbius transformations in $\mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{D})$ (up to a time reparameterization), due to the conformal invariance of the Coulomb gas correlation. Consequently, rational $\mathrm{SLE}_0[\boldsymbol{\sigma}]$ in any simply connected domain $\Omega$ is defined by pulling back via a conformal map $\phi: \Omega \rightarrow \mathbb{D}$.
title: Rational $\mathrm{SLE}_0$

body:
[Proposition 40 of arXiv:2506.10494, 'Geometric Jensen-Shannon Divergence Between Gaussian Measures On Hilbert Space'] [\cite{Minh:2022KullbackGaussian}, Theorem 11]
	
	Let $0 \leq \alpha \leq 1$.
	Let $A\in \Sym(\Hcal) \cap \HS(\Hcal)$, $I+A > 0$. Then
	\begin{align}
		0 &\leq \log\det[(1-\alpha)(I+A)^{-\alpha} + \alpha (I+A)^{1-\alpha}] 
		\nonumber
		\\
		&\leq \alpha(1-\alpha)||(I+A)^{-1}||\;||A||^2_{\HS}.
	\end{align}
	Let $B\in \Sym(\Hcal) \cap \HS(\Hcal)$, $I+B > 0$. Then
	\begin{align}
		&\left|\log\det[(1-\alpha)(I+A)^{-\alpha} + \alpha (I+A)^{1-\alpha}] \right.
		\nonumber
		\\
		&\left. -\log\det[(1-\alpha)(I+B)^{-\alpha} + \alpha (I+B)^{1-\alpha}]]\right| 
		\\
		&\leq \alpha (1-\alpha)||(I+A)^{-1}||\;||(I+B)^{-1}||
		\nonumber
		\\
		& \quad \times [||A||_{\HS} + ||B||_{\HS} + ||A||_{\HS}||B||_{\HS}]||A-B||_{\HS}.
	\end{align}
	Consequently, let $\{A_k\}_{k\in \Nbb} \in \Sym(\Hcal) \cap \HS(\Hcal)$, $I+A_k > 0$ $\forall k \in \Nbb$, be such that
	$\lim_{k \approach \infty}||A_k - A||_{\HS} = 0$. Then
	\begin{align}
		&\lim_{k \approach \infty}\log\det[(1-\alpha)(I+A_k)^{-\alpha} + \alpha (I+A_k)^{1-\alpha}]
		\nonumber
		\\
		&=
		\log\det[(1-\alpha)(I+A)^{-\alpha} + \alpha (I+A)^{1-\alpha}].
	\end{align}
	Let $\beta \in \R$ be fixed but arbitrary. Then
	\begin{align}
		&\lim_{k \approach \infty}\det[(1-\alpha)(I+A_k)^{-\alpha} + \alpha (I+A_k)^{1-\alpha}]^{\beta}
		\nonumber
		\\
		&=
		\det[(1-\alpha)(I+A)^{-\alpha} + \alpha (I+A)^{1-\alpha}]^{\beta}.
	\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 40 of arXiv:2506.10494

body:
[Theorem thm:romiksniady-main of arXiv:2607.24018, 'Jeu de taquin forests \\ and the inverse infinite RSK correspondence'] \begin{enumerate}

\item The Plancherel measure $P$ is the push-forward of the
infinite-dimensional Lebesgue measure $\Lambda$ on
$[0,1]^\mathbb{N}$ under the map $\RSK(\cdot)$.

\item The jeu de taquin map $J$ is a measure-preserving
transformation on the Plancherel measure space $(\Omega,
\mathcal{F}, P)$.

\item The jeu de taquin map is intertwined with the shift map $S$
on $[0,1]^\mathbb{N}$ (defined by $S(z_1,z_2,\ldots)=(z_2,z_3,\ldots)$)
by the map $\RSK(\cdot)$, in the sense that the
relation
\[
J \circ \RSK = \RSK\circ S
\]
holds $\Lambda$-almost surely on $[0,1]^\mathbb{N}$. 

\item The RSK map $\RSK(\cdot)$ is an isomorphism between
the two measure-preserving dynamical systems $([0,1]^\mathbb{N},
\mathcal{B}, \Lambda, S)$ and $(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, P, J)$.

\item The inverse map $\RSK^{-1}(\cdot)$ is given explicitly by
\begin{equation} 
\RSK^{-1}(T) = ( \zeta(T), \zeta\circ J(T), \zeta \circ J^2(T), \ldots)
\quad \textrm{for $P$-almost every }T\in \Omega,
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}

\zeta(T) =
1 - F\left(\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{x_n-y_n}{\sqrt{T_{x_n,y_n}}} \right),
\end{equation}
where $((x_n,y_n))_{n=0}^\infty$ denotes the jeu de taquin
path associated with $T$ as in (equation eq:jdt-path of the paper) and
$F(u)$ is given by
\begin{equation}

F(u) = \frac{1}{2\pi} \int_{-2}^u \sqrt{4-s^2} \, ds
\qquad (-2 \le u \le 2).
\end{equation}
(This statement includes the assertion that the limit in
(equation eq:inverse-rsk-firstcoord of the paper) exists and takes a value in $[-2,2]$
$P$-almost surely.)

\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:romiksniady-main of arXiv:2607.24018

body:
Every loopless planar graph is properly 4-colourable: its vertices can be coloured with four colours so that adjacent vertices receive different colours. Equivalently, the regions of any map drawn in the plane (each region connected) can be coloured with four colours so that regions sharing a boundary segment differ. Four is best possible (the complete graph K_4 is planar and needs four colours). The five-colour theorem (Heawood 1890) has a short proof; the four-colour theorem was proved by Appel and Haken in 1976 with a computer check of 1,936 reducible configurations, reproved by Robertson, Sanders, Seymour and Thomas in 1997 with 633 configurations and 32 discharging rules, and formally verified in the Coq proof assistant by Gonthier in 2005. No proof is known that a human can check unaided; every published proof rests on a machine-checked case analysis.
the graph is planar (embeddable in the plane without crossings) and loopless; multiple edges do not matter for colouring
proper colouring: adjacent vertices differ
the proof is computer-assisted; the sketch names the method and the published verifications

[Definition def:restricted of arXiv:2608.24830, 'Motion helps the contact process: survival below\\ the percolation threshold on Poisson Br'] An event $A$ is \emph{restricted} to a region $X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d$ and a time interval $[t_0,t_1]$ if
it is measurable with respect to the $\sigma$-field generated by the particles lying in $X$ at
time $t_0$, their trajectories on $[t_0,t_1]$ and the marks those particles carry on $[t_0,t_1]$.
When the isolation rule is in force, the $\sigma$-field also includes the trajectories on
$[t_0,t_1]$ of the particles lying within distance $2r$ of $X$ at time $t_0$, since these decide
whether those marks are effective.
A particle has \emph{displacement inside} $X'$ during $[t_0,t_1]$ if $X_u(t)-X_u(t_0)\in X'$ for
every $t\in[t_0,t_1]$. An event is \emph{increasing} if it is preserved by adding particles, in
the sense of (prop:mono of the paper)(ii). For an increasing event $E$ restricted to $X$ and $[0,t]$, we
write $\nu_E(\zeta,X,X',t)$ for the probability that $E$ holds when the particles in $X$ at time
$0$ form a Poisson process of intensity $\zeta$ and are conditioned to have displacement inside
$X'$ during $[0,t]$.
title: Restricted, increasing, and the associated probability

[Theorem 38 of arXiv:2609.02267, 'Locally Conformally Flat Manifolds with Positive Scalar Curvature: Kleinian Groups, Moduli'] Let \((M^n,g)\), \(n\geq4\), be a complete, open, simply connected, locally
conformally flat \(n\)-manifold with nonnegative scalar curvature. Let
\(\Phi\colon M\to S^n\) be the developing map, set
\(\Omega:=\Phi(M)\), and let \(\Lambda:=S^n\setminus\Omega\).
Assume that \(M\) is \(\left\lfloor \frac{n-2}{2}\right\rfloor\)-connected at infinity and that \(\Lambda\) satisfies the small loops condition in \(S^n\). Then
\(M\) is homeomorphic to \(\mathbb{R}^n\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 38 of arXiv:2609.02267

[Theorem thm: Ito map continuity even p of arXiv:2604.05941, 'Banach spaces of continuous paths with finite $p$-th variation'] Assume the setting of Theorem~(thm: transported Banach of the paper), where $p\in 2\mathbb N$.
    Suppose in addition that the embeddings $B\hookrightarrow C([0,1])$ and $B\hookrightarrow L^p([0,1])$ are continuous. For $f\in C^p(\mathbb R)$, define the F\"ollmer-It\^o map via (equation def: Rama Nicolas of the paper)
    \[
        \mathcal I_f:\mathcal L_{\bar x}(B)\to C([0,1]),\qquad
        \mathcal I_f(y)(t):=\int_0^t f'(y_u)\,dy_u.
    \]
    Then $\mathcal I_f$ is continuous with respect to the norm $\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal L}$ on $\mathcal L_{\bar x}(B)$
    and the uniform norm on $C([0,1])$.

body: [Lemma 28 of arXiv:2608.29972, '\bf Cram\'er transform, half-space depth and threshold phenomena for convex bodies'] If $\mu$ is a log-concave probability measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$ then \[c_1n \leq \mathbb{E}_\mu[\Lambda_\mu^\ast] \leq c_2n\log n.\] In addition, if $K$ is a convex body in $\mathbb{R}^n$, we have that\[\Var_{\mu_K}(\Lambda_K^\ast) \geq \frac{c_3}{n^2} \bigl(\mathbb{E}_{\mu_K}[\Lambda_K^\ast]\bigr)^2.\] Therefore, \[\beta(\mu_K) \geq \frac{c_3}{n^2},\] where $c_1,c_2,c_3>0$ are absolute constants.

body:
PRIVATE NUMERICAL EVIDENCE, not a proof. Lyons (ICM 2014, Question 2.8) asks whether for H = H_1 (+) H_2 orthogonal in l^2(E) there is a coupling of the determinantal projection measures P_{H_1}, P_{H_2} whose union has law P_H. Since the cardinalities are dim H_1, dim H_2 and dim H almost surely, the union must be disjoint, and the question is the nonemptiness of the transportation polytope with the three marginals. Exact LP (HiGHS, minimum total violation) on 1360 random pairs of orthogonal subspaces with |E| in {3,...,6} over all dimension splits, on generic instances with |E| = 7 and 8, on Fourier-mode subspaces of cycles of length 5..8, and on star-space splits in the edge space of K_4 found a feasible coupling with zero violation every time (intake raw/C_lyons_q28_lp_check.json and _structured.json). A structural observation: the naive rule 'sample X_1 from P_{H_1} conditioned on X_1 subset C, set X_2 = C minus X_1' does NOT reproduce the P_{H_2} marginal in general (checked on |E| = 4), so the coupling, when it exists, is not the conditional splitting. Open: a general construction.
Finite E, orthogonal subspaces H_1, H_2
Evidence is computational on |E| <= 8 only
title: Lyons's union-marginal coupling question: transportation polytope feasible in every tested instance, naive conditional splitting fails

body:
[Dfn 11 of arXiv:2507.08909, 'Annealed almost periodic entropy'] For any finite positive semidefinite matrix $Q$, its \textbf{log-determinant entropy} is
\[\rmH(Q) := \log \det Q,\]
with the usual convention that $\log 0 = -\infty$.

If $S$ is any set (not necessarily finite), $Q$ is a positive semidefinite $S$-by-$S$ matrix, and $F$ is a finite subset of $S$, then we define
\[\rmH_Q(F) := \rmH(Q[F]),\]
where $Q[F]$ is the $F$-by-$F$ submatrix of $Q$. (Recall our notation for submatrices from Section~\ref{sec:lin-alg}.)

Let $\mu$ be a finite positive measure on $\mathbb{R}$ with Stieltjes transform $m(z) = \int \frac{d\mu(t)}{t - z}$, defined and analytic for $\operatorname{Im} z > 0$, with $\operatorname{Im} m(z) > 0$ there. Then for every $a < b$ that are continuity points of $\mu$, $\mu((a, b]) = \lim_{\eta \downarrow 0} \frac{1}{\pi}\int_a^b \operatorname{Im} m(x + i\eta)\,dx$, and if $\mu$ has a continuous density $f$ at $x$ then $f(x) = \frac{1}{\pi}\lim_{\eta \downarrow 0} \operatorname{Im} m(x + i\eta)$. The real part has the companion limit $\operatorname{Re} m(x + i\eta) \to \pi H_f(x) := \mathrm{PV}\int \frac{f(t)}{t - x}\,dt$ wherever $f$ is Hölder continuous, so the boundary value $\breve m(x) = \lim_{\eta\downarrow0} m(x + i\eta) = \pi H_f(x) + i\pi f(x)$ (Sokhotski-Plemelj). In particular two measures with the same Stieltjes transform on $\mathbb{C}^+$ coincide, and a sequence of probability measures converges weakly if and only if the Stieltjes transforms converge pointwise on $\mathbb{C}^+$ (to the transform of a probability measure).
mu a finite positive Borel measure on the real line
for the density statement: mu absolutely continuous with a density continuous at x; for the real-part statement: the density Hölder continuous near x

body:
[Proposition prop:anisotropic-JM of arXiv:2608.30904, 'Entire monotone solutions of the anisotropic Allen--Cahn equation in dimension 5'] Let $v$ be the global minimizer obtained in
(prop:four-dimensional-global-minimizer of the paper), set $s_0:=v(0)$, and define
\begin{equation}
\kappa_*
:=
q_5'\bigl(q_5^{-1}(s_0)\bigr)
=
\frac{\sqrt{2W(s_0)}}{F_5(e_5)}.
\end{equation}
For every $\kappa\in(0,\kappa_*)$, there exists a global minimizer
\[
U\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^5),
\qquad
-1<U<1,
\]
such that
\begin{equation}
-\operatorname{div} a_5(DU)+W'(U)=0,
\qquad
\partial_5U>0
\qquad\text{in }\mathbb R^5,
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
U(0)=s_0,
\qquad
\partial_5U(0)=\kappa.
\end{equation}
The solution is even in the first four variables and is not
one-dimensional.

body:
Fix 0<gamma<2. For the zero-boundary GFF on the unit disk, with covariance singularity log(1/|x-y|), let mu_gamma be the GMC of Lebesgue measure defined by the weak limit of 2^(-n*gamma^2/2) exp(gamma*h_{2^(-n)}(y))dy. Almost surely, for mu_gamma-almost every interior x, the centered logarithmic disk potential T_x(r) has log exponent 2-gamma^2/2. A strictly positive continuous local weight multiplying mu_gamma preserves this conclusion. This is a derived Euclidean-potential corollary, not an exact metric dimension formula.

$H$ that is bounded above.  For $g,h\in H$, define
\[
  z(t)=e^{tL}g-\int_0^t e^{rL}h\,\dd r.
\]
Then
$
  z\in C^\infty((0,\infty);\Dom(L))
$,
where $\Dom(L)$ is equipped with its graph norm, and
\begin{align}
  z'(t)=Lz(t)-h,
  \qquad t>0.
\end{align}

[Cor 3 of arXiv:2609.01101, '2609.01101'] Let $K$ be a fixed number field, let $L$ be its Galois closure, and set
$$
G=\Gal(L/\Q),\qquad H=\Gal(L/K),\qquad
\rho_K=|H\backslash G/H|.
$$
Assume GRH for $\zeta_L$.  Then, for every fixed real $k>0$ and all
sufficiently large $T$,
\begin{equation}
\int_T^{2T}
\left|\zeta_K\left(\tfrac12+it\right)\right|^{2k}\,dt
\gg_{K,k}
T(\log T)^{\rho_Kk^2}.
\end{equation}
If $K$ is a non-Galois cubic field whose Galois closure has group $S_3$,
then $\rho_K=2$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 89 (Strings of commutation vectorfields and vectorfield seminorms) of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] Recall that 
	$\Fullset = \{\Lunit, \muX, \Yvf{2},\Yvf{3}\}$, 
	$\Tanset = \{\Lunit,\Yvf{2},\Yvf{3}\}$,
	and 
	$\Angularset = \{\Yvf{2},\Yvf{3}\}$ are the sets of commutation vectorfields 
	defined in \eqref{E:COMMUTATIONVECTORFIELDS}.
	We adopt the following definitions for differential operators constructed out of strings of commutation vectorfields.
	In this section, $f$ denotes a scalar function.
	
	\begin{itemize}
		\item $\comder^{N;M} f$ denotes an arbitrary string of $N$ commutation vectorfields in $\comder$ applied to $f$, where the string contains \emph{precisely} $M$ factors of $\muX$. We set $\comder^{0,0}f = f$. We often write
		$\comder f$ instead of $\comder^{1;1} f$ and $\comder^{N;M} f$ when the string contains \emph{precisely} factors of $\muX$.
		\item $\tander^N f$ denotes an arbitrary string of $N$ commutation vectorfields in $\tander$ applied to $f$. We set $\tander^0 f = f$. We often write $\tander f$ instead of $\tander^1 f$.
		\item $\tanderY^N f$ denotes an arbitrary string of $N$ commutation vectorfields in $\mathscr{Y}$ applied to $f$. We set $\tanderY^0 f = f$.
		\item $\comdersmall^{N;M} f$ denotes an arbitrary string of $N$ commutation vectorfields in $\comder$ applied to $f$, where the string contains \emph{at least} one factor of $\tander$ and \emph{precisely} $M$ factors of $\muX$.
		\item $\tandersmall^N$ denotes an arbitrary string of $N$ commutation vectorfields in $\tander$ applied to $f$, where the string contains \emph{at least two factors} of $\Lunit$ or \emph{at least one factor of $\Yvf{2}, \Yvf{3}$}.
		\item $\comderdoublesmall^{N;M} f$ denotes an arbitrary string of $N$ commutation vectorfields in $\comder$ applied to $f$, 
		where the string contains at least two factors of $\Lunit$ or at least one factor of $\Yvf{A}$ and \emph{precisely} $M$ factors of $\muX$.
		\item $\mathfrak{P}^{(N)}$ denotes the set of all differential operators of the form $\tander^N$.
		\item $\mathfrak{Y}^{(N)}$ denotes the set of all differential operators of the form $\tanderY^N$.
		\item $\mathfrak{Z}_*^{(N;1)}$ and $\mathfrak{Z}_*^{(N;\le 1)}$ denote the set of all differential operators of the form $\comdersmall^{N;1}$ and $\comdersmall^{N;\le 1}$.
		\item  We define order $N$ strings of $\ell_{t,u}$-projected Lie derivatives
	such as $\angLie_{\tander}^N$ and $\angLie_{\comder}^{N;M}$ in an analogous fashion.  
	Such operators act on $\ell_{t,u}$-tangent tensorfields $\upxi$, e.g., $\angLie_{\tander}^N \upxi$.
		\item $\angLie_{\mathfrak{P}}^{(N)}$ denotes the set of all differential operators of the form $\angLie_{\tander}^N$.
		\item $\angLie_{\mathfrak{Y}}^{(N)}$ denotes the set of all differential operators of the form $\angLie_{\tanderY}^N$.
		\item  $\comder^{\leq N;M} f$ denotes the array of all terms of the form
		$\comder^{N';M} f$, where $0 \leq N' \leq N$. 
		\item If $N_1 < N_2$, then
		$\comder^{[N_1,N_2];M} f$ denotes the array of all terms of the form
		$\comder^{N';M} f$, where $N_1 \leq N' \leq N_2$.
		\item We define arrays such as $\tanderY^{\leq 2} f$ in an analogous fashion.
	\end{itemize}
	We also define pointwise seminorms:
	\begin{itemize}

		\item $|\comder^{\leq N;M} f|$ denotes the sum over all terms of the form $|\comder^{N';M} f|$ with $N' \leq N$.

	Finally, if $v$ is any other continuous random-field solution to (equation SHE:1 of the paper) on

	$\sup_{s\in(0,t_0]}(s^\alpha\|v(s)\|_{C[0,1]})<\infty$ a.s.~for

body: In statistics, sufficiency is a property of a statistic computed on a sample dataset in relation to a parametric model of the dataset. A sufficient statistic for a model parameter contains all of the information that the dataset provides about that parameter. It is closely related to the concepts of an ancillary statistic which contains no information about the model parameters, and of a complete statistic which only contains information about the parameters and no ancillary information.

[Definition 20 of arXiv:2609.00567, 'Hodge--Tate splitting and Akizuki--Nakano vanishing in positive characteristic'] Let \(\iota \colon X \to S\) be a morphism of $\F_p$-stacks.
We say that $X$ is \emph{Hodge--Tate split} (\emph{HT-split}, for short) over $S$ if the homomorphism
\[
\nu_{X/S}^{\sharp} \colon \cO_{X^{(1)}} \to R\nu_{X/S,*}\cO_{(X/S)^{\dR}} \eqdef \OdR{X/S}
\]
is ind-split in $\mcalD_{\qcoh}(X^{(1)})$, where \(X^{(1)}\) is the Frobenius twist of \(X\) over \(S\).

We say that an \(\setF_p\)-stack \(X\) is \emph{HT-split} if $X$ is HT-split over $\Spec(\F_p)$.

[Lemma lem: technical lemma bound on S prime of arXiv:2605.28770, 'Cutoff profiles for conjugacy invariant random walks on symmetric groups'] Let $r\geq 1$.
    Let $n\geq 3r$. Let $\lambda \vdash n$ such that $r(\lambda) = r$. Let $\sigma \in {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{S}}} _n$ such that $f:= f_1(\sigma) \geq 2r$, and denote its cycle structure written in weakly increasing order by $\alpha$. Let $K\in \left\{  0, 2,3,4, \ldots\right\} $. Let $S'(\lambda, \alpha, K)$ be the set of all ribbon tableaux of $\lambda$ with weight $\alpha$ such that all but $K$ boxes in $\lambda^*$ are filled with 1-ribbons. Then
\begin{equation}
    |S'(\lambda, \alpha, K)| \lesssim_r
    f^{r-K} G(\sigma)^K \leq M(\sigma)^r.
\end{equation}
Moreover, $S'(\lambda, \alpha, 0)$ consists of $d_{(\lambda_1-k, \lambda_2, \lambda_3, \ldots)}$ ribbon tableaux of height 0.

[Definition 1 of arXiv:2506.16260, 'Fractional Compound Poisson Random Fields on Plane'] (\textbf{Two parameter L\'evy process})
A real valued two parameter random process $\{X(t_1,t_2),\ (t_1,t_2)\in\mathbb{R}^2_+\}$ is called L\'evy process if \\
\noindent (i) $X(0,t_2)=X(t_1,0)=0$ almost surely,\\
\noindent (ii) for fix $(h,k)\in\mathbb{R}^2_+$,  the distribution of $\Delta_{t_1,t_2}X(t_1+h,t_2+k)$ is independent of the choice of $(t_1,t_2)$. This is known as the stationary increment property,\\
\noindent (iii) for disjoint rectangles $R_1,R_2,\dots,R_m$ in $\mathbb{R}^2_+$ of type $(s_1,t_1]\times (s_2,t_2]$, the random variables $X(R_1),X(R_2)$, $\dots,X(R_m)$ are independent of each other. This property is known as the independent increments property.
title: Definition 1 of arXiv:2506.16260

Let u and v be bounded and uniformly continuous on R^n × [0,T], with u a viscosity subsolution and v a viscosity supersolution of w_t + H(x,Dw) = 0 in R^n × (0,T). If u(x,0) ≤ v(x,0) for all x ∈ R^n, then u ≤ v on R^n × [0,T]. Consequently the Cauchy problem u_t + H(x,Du) = 0 in R^n × (0,T), u(·,0) = g, has at most one viscosity solution that is bounded and uniformly continuous on R^n × [0,T].

Let Phi be a stationary simple locally finite planar point process with finite positive intensity, bounded Voronoi cells, finite nonempty edge-neighbor sets, no four cocircular points, no three collinear points, and almost surely unique nearest nuclei p_x at deterministic observation points. Define F6(x) as the mean of ((q-p_x)/|q-p_x|)^6 over its Delaunay edge-neighbors. Put C6(x,y)=E[F6(x)conjugate(F6(y))]-E[F6(x)]E[conjugate(F6(y))], V(t)=P(Phi intersect B(0,t) is empty), and alpha(A,B)=sup |P(E intersect H)-P(E)P(H)| over events of the restrictions to A and B. Suppose for D=|x-y|>6r and r>=r0, uniformly in x,y,r, alpha(B(x,3r),B(y,3r))<=Am(1+r)^kappa(1+D-6r)^(-p), and V(t)<=Av exp(-a t^nu) for t>=t0, with p,a,nu>0, kappa>=0, and finite Am,Av. Then |C6(x,y)|=O(D^(-p)(log D)^(kappa/nu)). Thus an eventual lower bound cD^(-eta), c,eta>0, is impossible when p>eta. This is a conditional correlation-transfer result and does not construct a Riesz Gibbs phase.

Let $W \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a bounded measurable set, and let $f$ be a real-valued measurable functional defined on finite simplicial complexes with vertices in $\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{A}$. For $(x, a, t, u) \in \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{A} \times [0, 1] \times \mathbb{M}$, let $\Delta_W^{(x, a, t, u)}$ denote the simplicial complex restricted to $W$ obtained from the augmented Poisson process $\Psi + \delta_{(x, a, t, u)}$. The difference operator $\Lambda_{(x, a, t, u)} f(\Delta_W)$ is defined by $\Lambda_{(x, a, t, u)} f(\Delta_W) := f(\Delta_W^{(x, a, t, u)}) - f(\Delta_{W \setminus \{x\}}^{(x, a, t, u)})$, which measures the exact change in $f$ caused by the addition of the vertex $(x, a)$ with auxiliary randomization marks $(t, u)$.

[Proposition prop:poly-growth of arXiv:2604.13968, 'Divisible sandpiles via random walks in random scenery'] Let $G=(V,E)$ be an infinite, locally finite, connected graph with degree bounded by~$d$.  Assume:
		\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(H\arabic*)}]
			\item \textup{(Volume growth)}\; $|B(o,r)|\leq C_{\mathrm{vol}} r^{d_f}$ for some $o\in V$, $d_f>0$, and all $r\geq 1$.
			\item \textup{(Spectral dimension)}\; $\sup_{x\in V}\mathbb{P}_x(X_n=x)\leq A n^{-d_s/2}$ for all $n\geq 1$, for some $d_s\in(0,2)$ and $A<\infty$.
			\item \textup{(Walk dimension)}\; For all $x\in V$, all $n\geq 1$, and all $r\geq 1$,
			\[
			\mathbb{P}_x\bigl(\tau_{B(x,r)}\leq n\bigr)\leq C_{\mathrm{disp}}\exp\biggl(-c_{\mathrm{disp}}\Bigl(\frac{r^{d_w}}{n}\Bigr)^{\!1/(d_w-1)}\biggr)\,,
			\]
			for some $d_w\geq 2$ and constants $C_{\mathrm{disp}},c_{\mathrm{disp}}>0$.
		\end{enumerate}
		Let $(\xi(v))_{v\in V}$ be i.i.d.\ and independent of the walk with $\mathbb{E}[\xi]\in[-\infty,0)$ and $\mathbb{E}[(\xi^+)^p]<\infty$ for some $p>\max(2d_f/(d_w\,d_s),\,1)$.  Then $\sup_\tau\mathbb{E}_o[S_\tau\mid\xi]<\infty$ almost surely. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:colorTASEPconv of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] For $\epsilon>0$, define the rescaling $(x, s)_\epsilon = (\lfloor 2\epsilon^{-1}x \rfloor, 2\epsilon^{-3/2}s)$ and define $H_\epsilon:\mathbb H^2_\uparrow \to \mathbb{R}$ by
		\[
		H_\epsilon(x, s; y, t) = -\epsilon^{1/2}H((x, s)_\epsilon; (y, t)_\epsilon) + \epsilon^{-1}(t-s).
		\]
		Take either (i) fixed $\alpha > \frac{1}{2}$ and $\rho=-\infty$, or (ii) $\alpha = \frac{1}{2}-\rho\epsilon^{1/2}/2$ for some $\rho\in\mathbb{R}$.
		Then as $\epsilon\to 0$, $H_\epsilon$ converges in distribution to $\mathcal{L}^\rho$ in the uniform-on-compact topology. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:colorTASEPconv of arXiv:2604.10020

[Lemma timedecor of arXiv:2601.05361, 'Noise sensitivity in last-passage percolation'] For $i \in {\mathbb{N}}$, we denote by $\mathrm{pr}_i:\{0, 1\}^{{\mathbb{N}}}\to{\mathbb{R}}$ the map $x \mapsto x_i$. For all $t \geq 0$ and $f \in L^2$,
\begin{equation}
P_t \nabla_i f = e^{-t} (p-\mathrm{pr}_i) P_t \Big( \frac{\nabla_i f}{p - \mathrm{pr}_i} \Big)  .
\end{equation}
It follows that $\I_i(P_t f) = {\mathbb{E}} \big[|\nabla_i P_t f| \big]$ decays exponentially in $t$, in that
\[
\I_i(P_t f) \leq 2 e^{-t} \max(p, 1-p) \I_i(f)  .
\]

[Definition def:heavy-neighbor-light-root of arXiv:2607.05384, 'Well-invertible column subsets of sparse matrices are rare'] For a $G=(I,J,M)$ with maximum right degree $d$. 
For $i\in I$, write
\[
D_i:=|N_G(i)|.
\]
Let
\(
N^\dagger_G(i)\subseteq N_G(i)
\)
be any set of cardinality $\lceil \tfrac{1}{32d} D_i\rceil$, 
such that
\[
|M_{ij}|\ge |M_{ij'}|
\qquad
\forall j\in N^\dagger_G(i),\ 
\forall j'\in N_G(i)\setminus N^\dagger_G(i).
\]
A right vertex $j_\star\in J$ is \hyperref[def:heavy-neighbor-light-root]{\textcolor{PineGreen}{\emph{light}}}{} if
\[
j_\star\notin N^\dagger_G(i)
\qquad
\forall i\in N_G(j_\star).
\]
title: Heavy-neighbor sets and light roots

[Definition def:rgen of arXiv:2608.24963, 'Why and When Neural Networks Improve Local Approximation in Optimization'] Fix a floor $\epsilon_{g,0}\ge0$ and a rate $\kappa_g>0$, and set
$\bar e_g(\delta):=\epsilon_{g,0}+\kappa_g\delta$, with $\bar e_f$ defined analogously from
$\epsilon_{f,0}$ and $\kappa_f\delta^2$. The \emph{effective generalization radius} around
$x$ is
\begin{equation}
r_{\mathrm{gen}}(x) := \sup\bigl\{\Delta>0:\ e_f(x,\delta)\le \bar e_f(\delta)\ \text{and}\ e_g(x,\delta)\le \bar e_g(\delta)\ \text{ for every } 0<\delta\le\Delta \bigr\}.
\end{equation}
title: Effective local generalization radius

for $\xi:=f(x_{t_{0}})$
$$
f(x_{t_{0}})-\Pi_{n}(t_{0})\xi
=\int_{\Gamma_{n+1}(t_{0})}
Q^{k_{n+1}}_{t_{n+1},t_{n}}\cdot...\cdot
Q^{k_{1}}_{t_{1},t_{0} }f(x_{t_{n+1}})\,dw^{k_{n+1}}_{t_{n+1}}\cdot...\cdot dw^{k_{1}}_{t_{1}},
$$
$$
E\big|f(x_{t_{0}})-\Pi_{n}(t_{0})\xi
\big|^{2}
$$
$$
= \int_{\Gamma_{n+1}(t_{0})}T_{0,t_{n+1}}Q_{t_{n+1},...,t_{0}}f(x_{0})\,
dt_{n+1}\cdot...\cdot dt_{1},
$$
$$
E \big(f(x_{t_{0}})\mid\cF^{w}_{t_{0}}\big)=T_{0,t_{0}}f(x_{0})
$$
$$
+\sum_{m=1}^{\infty}\int_{\Gamma_{m}(t_{0})}T_{0,t_{m}}

[Definition def:OPRE-alternative-embedding of arXiv:2507.00329, 'Oriented bond-site percolation in random environment and contact processes with periodic r'] Let $B\in\{0,1\}$ be a Bernoulli random variable with parameter $1/2$ independent of everything else. Given (a realisation of) $B$ and $X$, consider the graph $G=(V,E)$ with vertex set
    \[
    	V=\big\{(t,X_i)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}^2 \colon t\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}, t+i+B \text{ even}\big\}
    \]
and edge set
    \[
    	E=\big\{(t,X_i)\to(t+1,X_{i\pm 1}) \colon  (t,X_i)\in V\big\}.
    \]
Consider $\kappa_\lambda\colon[0,\infty)\to[0,1]$ as in Definition~(def:OPRE-model of the paper).
We consider the independent bond-site percolation model on $G$, where for either $(t,X_{i})\in V$ or $(t,X_{i+1})\in V$, the edges \((t,X_{i})\to(t+1,X_{i+1})\) and \((t,X_{i+1})\to(t+1,X_{i})\), respectively, are open with probability \(\kappa_\lambda(\nu_{i,i+1})\).
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    
    Similarly, vertices $(t,X_i)\in V$ are open independently with probability \(\kappa_\lambda(\xi_i)\).
    
    
    
    We denote by $\mathbb{P}_\lambda^X(A):=\mathbb{P}_\lambda(A|X)$ the probability measure, conditionally given $X$ (as defined in~(equation eq:OPRE-stationarised-renewal-X of the paper)).
title: Alternative stationary spatial embedding

body:
[Ppn 140 (\hyperlink{proof:p.Ising-IAMP-analysis}{proved in \S\ref{ss:proof.iamp.diffus.limit}}) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] In the setting of Theorem~\ref{thm:IAMP-main}\ref{i:IAMP-main-main}, and recalling the notation \eqref{e:state.evol.piecewise}, there exist standard Brownian motions $B$ and $W$ such that the behavior of the state evolution limit \eqref{e:state.evol.x.y.increments} can be described as follows:
\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
\item 
  
The random variables $V^k,Y^k,\prxY^k$ can be written as
  \begin{align*}
  V^k
  &=
        V^0
        +
  \int_{q_0}^{q_0+k\delta}
  s_\delta(t_\delta)
  \,\de B(t),
  \\
  Y^k
  = \breve{Y}(q_0+k\delta)
  &=
        \breve{Y}(q_0)
        +
  \int_{q_0}^{q_0+k\delta}
  \frac{w_{t_\delta}(\prxY(t))}
  {
  \bbE[w_{t_\delta}(\prxY(t))^2]^{1/2}
  }
  \,\de W(t),
  \\
  \prxY^k
  = \prxY(q_0+k\delta)
  &=\prxY^0+
  \int_{q_0}^{q_0+k\delta}
  w_{t_\delta}(\prxY(t))
  \,\de W(t)
  .
  \end{align*}

\item

The random variables $M^k$, $X^k$, $\prxX^k$ can be written as
  \begin{align*}
  M^k
  &=
  \int_{q_0}^{q_0+k\delta} \frac{s_\delta(t_\delta)}{p(t_{\delta})}
  \Big(\sigma_{t_{\delta}}(\prxX(t))-1\Big)
  \,\de B(t);
  \\
  X^k = \breve{X}(q_0+k\delta)
  &=
  \int_{q_0}^{q_0+k\delta}
  s_\delta(t_\delta)
  \sigma_{t_{\delta}}(
  \prxX(t))
  \,\de B(t)
  +
  \int_{q_0}^{q_0+k\delta}
  p'(t_{\delta})^{1/2}
  b_{t_{\delta}}(\prxX(t))
  \,\de t
  \\
  \prxX^k
  =\prxX(q_0+k\delta)
  &=
  \prxX^0
  +
  \int_{q_0}^{q_0+k\delta}
  s_\delta(t_\delta)
  \sigma_{t_{\delta}}
  (\prxX(t))
  \,\de B(t)
  +
  \int_{q_0}^{q_0+k\delta}
  p'(t_{\delta})^{1/2}
  b_{t_{\delta}}
  (\prxX(t))\,\de t
  .\end{align*}
(Recall from Definition~\ref{d:iamp.v1} that $\breve{X}(q_0)=0$.)
\end{enumerate}
Recall $\prxX^0$ and $\prxY^0$
are equidistributed respectively as $X(q_0)$ and $Y(q_0)$ from the SDEs
\eqref{e:IAMP.X.SDE} and \eqref{e:IAMP.Y.SDE}. Moreover $\prxY^0$ is independent of $W$, and $\prxX^0$ is independent of $B$.\footnote{We recall from the discussion after Corollary~\ref{cor:psi-state-evolution} that $N$-dimensional and $M$-dimensional state evolution variables such as $W$ and $B$ are defined on different probability spaces, and can thus be  thought of as independent.} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
For N unit-speed servers with Poisson input N*lambda, independent uniformly chosen destinations, and independent nonnegative job sizes S with rho=lambda*E S<1 and E S^2 finite, the product stationary workload law consists of N independent M/G/1 workloads. The stationary mean workload per server is exactly lambda*E S^2/(2*(1-rho)) for every N. Its first-order 1/N bias and remainder are zero, and off-diagonal covariances are zero. This is the d=1 random-routing case; no zero-bias claim is made for workload-dependent least-of-d routing.
All hypotheses and scope restrictions in the statement apply.

Status: proof written; w346 KEEP pending. This is the d=1 random-routing special case, not a result for interacting least-of-d routing with d>=2.

Consider N rate-one workload servers, a Poisson input of rate N*lambda, independent uniformly chosen routing destinations, and i.i.d. nonnegative job sizes S independent of routing. Assume rho=lambda*E[S]<1 and E[S^2]<infinity. The N workload processes are independent M/G/1 workload processes when started in their product stationary law. For every N, the stationary mean of one server (and of the empirical mean workload) is

    lambda*E[S^2]/(2*(1-rho)).

Consequently its expansion in 1/N has exactly zero bias coefficient and zero remainder for this observable; stationary off-diagonal covariances are zero.

Proof: marked Poisson thinning produces N independent rate-lambda input processes with independent job marks. Each queue drains at rate one while positive and has upward jumps S. Its stability and stationary construction follow from the negative-drift reflected compound-Poisson input. The stationary idle mass is 1-rho by workload balance. For beta(s)=E[e^(-sS)] and L(s)=E[e^(-sW)], the bounded stationary generator test e^(-sW) gives

    0=s*(L(s)-(1-rho))+lambda*(beta(s)-1)*L(s),
    L(s)=(1-rho)*s/(s-lambda+lambda*beta(s)), s>0.

The second-moment assumption gives beta(s)=1-E[S]*s+E[S^2]*s^2/2+o(s^2). Expansion at zero gives L(s)=1-[lambda*E[S^2]/(2*(1-rho))]*s+o(s); the right derivative of a nonnegative variable's Laplace transform identifies its finite mean. Product stationarity proves all finite-N claims. This handles the actual empty-workload boundary, unlike a Gaussian OU control model.

For exponential service sizes of rate mu>lambda, P(W=0)=1-lambda/mu and P(W>x)=(lambda/mu)*exp(-(mu-lambda)*x) for x>=0, so the mean is lambda/(mu*(mu-lambda)). These formulas are a control for implementations of any proposed first-order correction. They do not justify setting the correction to zero under workload-dependent routing.

Checks: Laplace-transform generator identities, mean calculations for several service parameters, and exact Poisson-thinning algebra. body:
[Theorem thm: weighted mvt of arXiv:2609.02073, 'Existence of closed non-planar $p$-elasticae'] Let $f: [a, b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be a continuous function and let $g: [a, b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be an integrable function that does not change sign on the interval $[a, b]$. 
Then there exists at least one point $c \in (a, b)$ such that
\begin{equation*}
    \int_{a}^{b} f(x)g(x) \, dx = f(c) \int_{a}^{b} g(x) \,dx.
\end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Weighted Mean Value Theorem for Integrals

body: [Definition 4 (Covering number and $\epsilon$-net) of arXiv:2608.22636, 'Q-Learning with Stable Infinite-Dimensional \\Linear Function Approximation'] An $\epsilon$-net of $(\mbb L,\rho)$ is a subset $\mfk N\subseteq\mbb L$ such that, for every $\ell\in\mbb L$, there exists $\ell'\in\mfk N$ with $\rho(\ell,\ell')\leq\epsilon$. For $\epsilon>0$, let $\cN_\rho(\epsilon)$ denote the covering number of $\mbb L$ by $\rho$-balls of radius $\epsilon$; that is, $\cN_\rho(\epsilon)$ is the smallest cardinality of any $\epsilon$-net. Moreover, let $\mfk N_\rho(\epsilon)$ denote an $\epsilon$-net satisfying $|\mfk N_\rho(\epsilon)|=\cN_\rho(\epsilon)$.
title: Covering number and $\epsilon$-net

[Lemma 217 ($L^2$ estimates for the error terms in the elliptic-hyperbolic identities) of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] Let $\varsigma \in [0,1)$,
	let $(\ubar,u) \in [\leftubar,\ubarboot) \times [\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]$,
	let
	$
	\EllipticHyperbolicCurrentIntegralIdentityTotalSpacetimeErrorTerm[\cdot,\cdot]
	$
	be the error term defined by \eqref{E:ELLIPTICHYPERBOLICINTEGRALIDENTITYBULKERRORTERM},
	and let $\ellipticCoerciveQuadratic[\cdot,\cdot]$ be the coercive quadratic form defined in 
	\eqref{E:NULLHYPERSURFACEADAPTEDCOERCIVEQUADRATICFORM}.
	Then the following spacetime integral estimates hold,
	where the implicit constants are \textbf{independent} of $\varsigma$:
	\begin{subequations}
	\begin{align} 
	\begin{split} 
		\left|
		\int_{\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubar)}{[\moreinterestingu_1,u]}}
			\EllipticHyperbolicCurrentIntegralIdentityTotalSpacetimeErrorTerm[ \tander^{\Ntop} \vortrenormalized, \pmb{\partial} 			
			\tander^{\Ntop} \vortrenormalized] \weight^{\blowupratetoporderacoustic}\ReciprocalLunitAppliedtoTimeFunction 
		\, \voldiamond
		\right|
		& \lesssim 
			\varsigma 
			\int_{\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubar)}{[\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]}}
				\ellipticCoerciveQuadratic[\pmb{\partial}\tander^{\Ntop} \vortrenormalized,\pmb{\partial} \tander^{\Ntop} \vortrenormalized] 
				 \weight^{\blowupratetoporderacoustic}\ReciprocalLunitAppliedtoTimeFunction 
			\, \voldiamond
				\\
	& \ \ + (1 + \varsigma^{-1}) \initialsmall^2 + (1 + \varsigma^{-1}) \int_{u' = \moreinterestingu_1}^u \fluxcontrolVortVort_{\le \Ntop }(\ubar,u') \rmd u' \\
	& \ \  +(1 + \varsigma^{-1}) \int_{u' = \moreinterestingu_1}^u \left\{ \fluxcontrolVort_{\le \Ntop}(\ubar,u') + \fluxcontrolGradEnt_{\le N} (\ubar,u') \right\}\rmd u' \\
	& \ \ +
		\left(
			1 
			+ \varsigma^{-1} + \varsigma_0^{-1}
		\right)\fundbootsmall^2 
		\int_{\ubar' = \leftubar}^{\ubar} 
			\frac{1}{|\ubar'|^{0.5}}
			\totalfluxcontrolvelocity_{[1,\Ntop]}(\ubar',u) 
		\, \rmd \ubar' \\
		& \ \  +
		\left(
			1 
			+ \varsigma^{-1} + \varsigma_0^{-1} +  \varsigma^{-1}\varsigma_0^{-1}
		\right)\fundbootsmall^2 
		\int_{u' = \moreinterestingu_1}^{u} 
			\totalfluxcontrolvelocity_{[1,\Ntop]}(\ubar,u') 
		\, \rmd u' \\
		& \ \ + (1 + \varsigma^{-1} + \varsigma_0^{-1} + \varsigma^{-1} \varsigma_0^{-1}) \fundbootsmall^2\strongangularcontrolvelocity_{[1,\Ntop]}(\ubar,u),
	\end{split}
			\\
	\begin{split}  
		\left|
		\int_{\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubar)}{[\moreinterestingu_1,u]}}
			\EllipticHyperbolicCurrentIntegralIdentityTotalSpacetimeErrorTerm[ \tander^{\Ntop} \GradEnt, \pmb{\partial} \tander^{\Ntop} \GradEnt] \weight^{ \blowupratetoporderacoustic}\ReciprocalLunitAppliedtoTimeFunction 
		\, \voldiamond
		\right|
		& \lesssim  
			\varsigma
			\int_{\characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubar)}{[\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]}}
				\ellipticCoerciveQuadratic[\pmb{\partial}\tander^{\Ntop} \GradEnt,\pmb{\partial} \tander^{\Ntop} \GradEnt]
				 \weight^{\blowupratetoporderacoustic}\ReciprocalLunitAppliedtoTimeFunction 
			\, \voldiamond
				\\
	& \ \ +  (1 + \varsigma^{-1}) \initialsmall^2 + (1 + \varsigma^{-1}) \int_{u' = \moreinterestingu_1}^u \fluxcontrolDivGradEnt_{\le \Ntop }(\ubar,u') \rmd u' \\
	& \ \  +(1 + \varsigma^{-1}) \int_{u' = \moreinterestingu_1}^u \left\{ \fluxcontrolVort_{\le \Ntop}(\ubar,u') + \fluxcontrolGradEnt_{\le N} (\ubar,u') \right\}\rmd u' \\
	& \ \ +
		\left(
			1 
			+ \varsigma^{-1} + \varsigma_0^{-1}
		\right)\fundbootsmall^2 
		\int_{\ubar' = \leftubar}^{\ubar} 
			\frac{1}{|\ubar'|^{0.5}}
			\totalfluxcontrolvelocity_{[1,\Ntop]}(\ubar',u) 
		\, \rmd \ubar' \\
		& \ \  +
		\left(
			1 
			+ \varsigma^{-1} + \varsigma_0^{-1} +  \varsigma^{-1}\varsigma_0^{-1}
		\right)\fundbootsmall^2 
		\int_{u' = \moreinterestingu_1}^{u} 
			\totalfluxcontrolvelocity_{[1,\Ntop]}(\ubar,u') 
		\, \rmd u' \\
		& \ \ + (1 + \varsigma^{-1} + \varsigma_0^{-1}  +  \varsigma^{-1} \varsigma_0^{-1}) \fundbootsmall^2\strongangularcontrolvelocity_{[1,\Ntop]}(\ubar,u),	\end{split}
	\end{align}
	\end{subequations}

[Lemm 11 (Almost sure asymptotics for $R_{n,k}$ and $\tR_{n,k}$) of arXiv:2608.19104, 'Record times for coverage thresholds and maximal spacings'] Let  $k \in \N$.
	Then
	\begin{align}
\lim_{n \to \infty} (n \theta  f_0 \tR_{n,k}^d /\log n) =  1,
~~~ a.s.

	\end{align}
If $B \subset A^o $ is compact
	with $\lambda_d(B) >0$ and $\lambda_d(\partial B)=0$,

 

	then almost surely,
	\begin{align}
\lim_{n \to \infty} (n \theta  f_0 R_{n,k}^d /\log n) =  1.

	\end{align}

	If $B=A$ and $\partial A \in C^{1,1} $ 
	then
	a.s.,
	\begin{align}
	\lim_{n \to \infty} (n \theta R_{n,k}^d/\log n) =
	\max( 1/f_0, (2-2/d)/f_1).

	\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Almost sure asymptotics for $R_{n,k}$ and $\tR_{n,k}$

    E[X_W^\alpha]\le &  C_\alpha
                       \quad\text{ for }\alpha\in[0,\tfrac12), \qquad
                       \lim_{W\downarrow 0}E[X_W^\alpha]=C_\alpha. 
                       
  \end{align}

[Lemma 51 of arXiv:2607.08536, 'Soft edge limit of the Laguerre beta-ensemble at the lower edge'] Define 
\begin{align*}
    \mathcal{A}_{n,1}^G &= \{|g_k|\le \log n,\quad 1\le k\le n\},\\
    \mathcal{A}_{n,2}^G &= \{ |Y_k-\sqrt{n-k}|\le  2 \beta^{-1/2}\sqrt{\log(\beta(n-k))},\quad 1\le k\le n-\lfloor\sqrt{n}\rfloor\},\\
    \mathcal{A}_{n,3}^G &= \{\sqrt{\tfrac{{n-k}}{\log n}}\le Y_k\le \sqrt{(n-k)\log n},\quad n-\lfloor\sqrt{n}\rfloor\le k<n\}.
\end{align*}
    Let $\mathcal{A}_n^G=\mathcal{A}_{n,1}^G\cap \mathcal{A}_{n,2}^G\cap \mathcal{A}_{n,3}^G$, then  $\pr(\mathcal{A}_n^G)\ge 1- c_\beta(\log n)^{-\beta/2}$, where $c_\beta>0$ is independent of $n$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 51 of arXiv:2607.08536

body:
[Definition 15 (Boolean-polynomial description) of arXiv:2608.31157, 'Sharp Approximation Rates for Neural Networks with Affine Latent Parameterizations'] Let $d,r,s,d_{\mathrm{pol}}\in\N^+$, let $X\subseteq\R^{d}$, and let
\[
 \calF:=\{g_{\bmmu}:X\to\R:\bmmu\in\R^r\}.
\]
Its joint truth set is
\begin{equation}
 \calS
 :=\left\{(\bmx,t,\bmmu)\in X\times\R\times\R^r:
 g_{\bmmu}(\bmx)>t\right\}.
\end{equation}

Choose a number of leaf occurrences $s_0$ with $1\le s_0\le s$.
For each occurrence $j=1,\ldots,s_0$, choose a polynomial
\[
 p_j\in\R[x_1,\ldots,x_{d},t,\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_r]
\].
We use the standard convention that the zero polynomial has degree
$-\infty$; thus identically zero atoms are covered by every nonnegative
degree bound below.
The $j$th atom produces the bit
\begin{equation}
 A_j(\bmx,t,\bmmu)
 :=\one_{\{p_j(\bmx,t,\bmmu)>0\}}.
\end{equation}
Finally, choose one Boolean formula tree
$\mathfrak{B}(Z_1,\ldots,Z_{s_0})$ as described above, and let
$\mathsf{B}:\{0,1\}^{s_0}\to\{0,1\}$ be the map obtained from its recursive
evaluation.  We say that $\calS$
has an $(s,d_{\mathrm{pol}})$ Boolean-polynomial description in the parameter
$\bmmu$ when, for every $(\bmx,t,\bmmu)$,
\begin{equation}
 \one_{\calS}(\bmx,t,\bmmu)
 =\mathsf{B}\bigl(
 A_1(\bmx,t,\bmmu),\ldots,
 A_{s_0}(\bmx,t,\bmmu)\bigr),
\end{equation}
and, for each fixed $(\bmx,t)$,
\begin{equation*}
 \deg_{\bmmu}p_j(\bmx,t,\cdot)\le d_{\mathrm{pol}},
 \qquad j=1,\ldots,s_0.
\end{equation*}
The integer $s$ is only an upper bound; $s_0$ is the number of leaf
occurrences actually used after all comparisons have been written in the
strict-positivity form of \eqref{eq:atom-truth-value}.
title: Boolean-polynomial description

[Lemma lem:lower of arXiv:2609.03448, 'Prime-power Diophantine tuples'] Let $A=\{a_1<a_2<\cdots\}$ be a positive reduced $D(\varepsilon N)$-tuple.
If $\varepsilon=1$, then $a_3>N^{1/4}$, so at most two elements fail the lower
bound $a>N^{1/4}$. If $\varepsilon=-1$, then $a_2>N^{1/2}$, so at most one
element fails the stronger lower bound $a>N^{1/2}$.

[Lem Nondegeneracy_metric_entropy of arXiv:2609.03129, 'A Closed-Form Formula for Consistent Lipschitz Regression on Metric Spaces with Sparse Neu'] Let $(X,\rho,\mathfrak{m})$ be a compact metric measure space.
Assume that $(X,\rho,\mathfrak{m})$ is $0<d$-Ahlfors regular, and write
$
    \mathcal{F}_1
\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}}

Then, there are constants
$

$
and
$
    0<\varepsilon_0<1
$

$
    0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0
$,
\begin{equation}

    c\,\varepsilon^{-d}
    \le
    \log_2
    \mathcal N
    \bigl(
        \mathcal{F}_1,
        \|\cdot\|_{\infty},
        \varepsilon
    \bigr)
    \le
    C\,\varepsilon^{-d}.
\end{equation}

[Lemma 25 of arXiv:2604.24684, 'Waning Immunity Fails to Restore a Positive Epidemic Threshold on Power--Law Networks'] Fix any $\delta\in (0,1)$, and set
$
\tilde{\varepsilon}=\frac{\delta}{20\tau},
\bar\varepsilon=\frac{\tilde{\varepsilon}}{4.4\tau}
$.
Let $G=G(n,\tau)$ be a power-law random graph on $n$ vertices with exponent $\tau>2$, and let
$
\bm d=(d_1,\dots,d_n)
$
denote its degree sequence. Suppose that $v_1,v_2,\dots,v_{\lceil n^{1-\delta}\rceil}$ are vertices with degrees greater than $n^{2\tilde{\varepsilon}}$. Let $A$ denote the event that, for each $j=1,\dots,\lceil n^{1-\delta}\rceil$, the vertex $v_j$ has at least $\lceil n^{\tilde{\varepsilon}}\rceil$ distinct neighbors
$
u_1^{(j)},\dots,u_{\lceil n^{\tilde{\varepsilon}}\rceil}^{(j)}
$
such that all vertices in the collection
$
\{
u_i^{(j)}:
1\le j\le \lceil n^{1-\delta}\rceil,\,
1\le i\le \lceil n^{\tilde{\varepsilon}}\rceil
\}$
are distinct and have degrees between $n^{\bar\varepsilon}$ and $n^{3\bar\varepsilon}$. Then, for all sufficiently large $n$,
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{P}(A\mid \bm d)\ge 1-\exp(-n^{\bar\varepsilon (\tau-2)/2}), \qquad \text{on the event $D_{\bar\varepsilon}$ defined in \eqref{eq_D}. }
\end{equation}

body:
[Theorem Thm:PW_Robin of arXiv:2609.02325, 'A Payne-Weinberger inequality\\for quantum dot Dirac operators'] Let $\Omega\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a bounded simply connected domain with $C^2$~boundary and let~$\delta_\Omega$ denote its isoperimetric deficit, as in (equation Eq:IsopDeficit of the paper).
    Then, for all $a>0$ there holds
    \begin{equation} 
        |\Omega| \, \mu_\Omega^\mathrm{Rob} \bigg(\frac{a}{\sqrt{|\Omega|}}  \bigg)
         - \pi \, \mu_\mathbb{D}^\mathrm{Rob}\bigg(\frac{a}{\sqrt{\pi}}  \bigg) 
        \leqslant 
        F \left(\sqrt{\mu_\mathbb{D}^\mathrm{Rob}\big(\tfrac{a}{\sqrt{\pi}}\big)} \right) \delta_\Omega( \delta_\Omega+2) +  G \left(\sqrt{\mu_\mathbb{D}^\mathrm{Rob}\big(\tfrac{a}{\sqrt{\pi}}\big)} \right) \delta_\Omega,
    \end{equation}
    where $F$ and $G$ are as in (equation Eq:def_FG of the paper). In particular, 
    \begin{equation} 
        |\Omega| \, \mu_\Omega^\mathrm{Rob} \bigg(\dfrac{a}{\sqrt{|\Omega|}}  \bigg)
        - \pi \, \mu_\mathbb{D}^\mathrm{Rob}\bigg(\dfrac{a}{\sqrt{\pi}}  \bigg) 
        \leqslant  
        C_{\mathrm{PW}} \, \delta_\Omega( \delta_\Omega+2) + \pi j_{0,1} \, \delta_\Omega
    \end{equation}
    and the equality holds in (equation Eq:PW_Robin_uniform of the paper) if and only if $\Omega$ is a disk. Here, $C_{\mathrm{PW}}>0$ is the constant in~(equation Eq:PW_Dirichlet of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem 112087 of arXiv:2606.29143, 'Comonotonic and moment matching approximations for sums of lognormal random variables'] Let $X$ be a random variable, not necessarily continuous, $\omega(x)$ a nonnegative weight function such that $0 < E[\omega(X)] < \infty$ and ${X_\omega}$ the weighted version of $X$ associated with $\omega$. \item $F_{X_\omega}(x)  = G_{X, \omega}(F_X(x)) \,\, \text{for any} \,\, x \in \mathbb{R}$, 
\item $F_{X_\omega}^{-1}(p) = F_X^{-1}(G^{-1}_{X, \omega}(p))$ for any $p \in (0, 1)$, 
 \item $F_{X_\omega}^{-1+}(p) = F_X^{-1+}(G^{-1+}_{X, \omega}(p))$ for any $p \in (0, 1)$,

Let A_1, ..., A_m be events, X_i = 1_{A_i}, U their union, V = span{X_1, ..., X_m} in L2(P), alpha_i = P(A_i) and Sigma_ij = P(A_i and A_j). Then G = alpha^T Sigma^+ alpha (Sigma^+ the Moore-Penrose inverse) equals ||P_V 1_U||^2, the squared norm of the orthogonal projection of 1_U onto V, so P(U) - G = ||1_U - P_V 1_U||^2 >= 0 (Gallot 1966, Kounias 1968). The bound is exact, G = P(U), if and only if 1_U is a linear combination of the X_i almost surely. G = max over c with c^T alpha > 0 of (c^T alpha)^2/(c^T Sigma c), so it is at least the Chung-Erdős value (sum_i alpha_i)^2 / sum_{i,j} Sigma_ij obtained at c = (1, ..., 1).

[Definition 37 of arXiv:2609.03976, '2609.03976'] Suppose $f_{1},...,f_{r} \in \mathbb{C}[x_{1},...,x_{n}]$ are polynomials of degree $d$. We say these polynomials have the polynomial PDE property if they satisfy the condition in Theorem \ref{PDE_theorem}, that is, there exist polynomials $P_{\alpha_{1},...,\alpha_{r}}$ indexed by $\alpha_{1},...,\alpha_{r} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$ satisfying the following conditions.
	
	$(1)$ $P_{\alpha_{1},...,\alpha_{r}}$ is homogeneous of degree $d \cdot (\alpha_{1}+...+\alpha_{r})$,
	
	$(2)$ $P_{0,...,0} \neq 0$,
	
	$(3)$ $x_{i}P_{\alpha_{1},...,\alpha_{r}}(x)=\sum_{k=1}^{r}\partial_{i}f_{k}(\partial) \cdot P_{\alpha_{1},...,\alpha_{k}+1,...,\alpha_{r}}(x)$.

[Proposition 2 (Basic properties of normal random variables) of arXiv:2605.14630, '2605.14630'] \begin{enumerate}
\item   One has $X\sim\cN(m,\sigma^2)$ if, and only if, $X = m + \sigma Y$ 
with $Y \sim \cN(0,1)$. 

\item   Assume $X\sim\cN(m_1,\sigma_1^2)$ and $Y\sim\cN(m_2,\sigma_2^2)$ 
are defined on a common probability space, and let $Z = X + Y$. Then 
$Z$ is Gaussian, with parameters 
\begin{equation}
 Z \sim \cN \bigpar{m_1+m_2, \sigma_1^2 + \sigma_2^2 + 2\cov(X,Y)}\;.
\end{equation} 

\item   Two Gaussian variables $X$ and $Y$ are independent if, and only if, 
they are uncorrelated, that is, $\cov(X,Y) = \expec{XY} - \expec{X}\expec{Y} = 0$. 
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Basic properties of normal random variables

 \mathfrak R_{j+1}\subseteq\mathfrak R_j\quad\text{a.s.},\qquad
 \{\Xi_j\ne0\}=\{\mathfrak R_j\ne\varnothing\},

then
\begin{equation}
 \Pp(\exists N:\mathfrak R_N=\varnothing)=1.

body: [Definition1 of arXiv:2603.05491, '\textbf{Local limits of uniform triangulations with boundaries in high genus}'] For any order $(i_j)$ and any $1 \le j \le 1000 \varepsilon |\mathbf{p}|$, step $j$ is said to be \textbf{SEP} if $e_{i_{j}}\in \alpha^j_{s}$ and $v_{i_{j}} \in \alpha^j_{s}$ for some $s \in \{1,\cdots,\ell_j\}$. Otherwise, it is said to be \textbf{NSEP}. Thus, a \textbf{SEP} step splits the boundary $\alpha_s^j$ containing $e_{i_j}$ into two boundaries. The \textbf{NSEP} occurs when $f_{i_{j}}$ connects two distinct boundaries.\\

[Thm 8 of arXiv:2608.25829, 'Topology of low-dimensional generalized Ricci solitons and string backgrounds'] If $(M, g, H, f)$ is a compact generalized Ricci soliton, then $M$ is finitely covered by $N \times T^k$, where:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $\pi_1(N) = 0$,
    \item $g = g_N + g_F$ where $g_F$ is a flat metric on $T^k$,
    \item $H = \pi_N^* H_N$ for a closed three-form on $H_N$,
    \item $f = \pi_N^* f_N$ for $f \in C^{\infty}(N)$.
\end{enumerate}
Hence, $(g_N, H_N, f_N)$ is a generalized Ricci soliton.
\begin{proof} Since a generalized Ricci soliton has nonnegative Bakry-\'Emery Ricci curvature, all of the claims except item (3) follow immediately from \cite[Theorem 6.6]{wei2009comparison}.  Given this structure, inspecting the generalized Ricci soliton equation it follows that for any Killing field $X$ tangent to the torus we have $i_X H = 0$.  Using \cite[Proposition 2.8]{kopfer2023bochner} it follows that $H$ is Levi-Civita parallel with respect to $X$, and hence item (3) follows.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
