Own-work draft; proof (unaudited), independent mathematical, priority and target-scope review pending. Let d>=1,N>=2d+1,n>=0,K>=2 and 1<=r<K be integers. There are N contexts, K candidates each, d pairs with one arbitrary A and one systematic S context, and N-2d known S contexts. S has all candidates true; A has an independent uniform random r-subset of truths. The factual law p is uniform over contexts, then uniform over true candidates within context. Training supplies n iid uniform context indices and A/S tags, without candidate identities; the partition class has VC dimension d. After training a perfect verifier independently draws a uniform ell-subset of truths in EVERY variable context, including paired S contexts, with 0<=ell<=r; it certifies these identities but gives no orientation tags. It verifies fraction gamma=ell/r of arbitrary truths. The two orientations have the same verifier-output likelihood, so U pairs untouched by training retain both orientations. For arbitrary generators g, require TV(p_Pi,g)<=c in every compatible world, where Pi is the exact partition into nonempty g-probability level sets and p_Pi(y)=p(B)/|B| in each bin B. Define beta=r/K,kappa=1-beta,q=ell/K,alpha=(K-r)/(K-ell),m=U/N,w=(d-U)/N,A0=w*(1-gamma),M0=m*(2-gamma-q). For every c in [0,1], the exact conditional worst-world hallucination frontier is V=alpha*((A0-c)_+ +(A0+M0-c)_+)/2. The oracle given orientations but the same certified identities has value alpha*((d/N)*(1-gamma)-c)_+. The conditional posterior-average game under uniform compatible orientations/supports has the same value. An ERM-version-space generator attains V in every compatible world in expected polynomial bit complexity for rational c. The exact minimax expected value is E[V], where E[z^U]=sum_{j=0}^d binom(d,j)*(z-1)^j*(1-2j/N)^n. At c=(d/N)*(1-gamma), the oracle is zero and V=kappa*U/(2N), with exact expected value kappa*d/(2N)*(1-2/N)^n, half kappa times the minimax expected partition-classification error. For n,d>=1,N=4max(n,d), it lies between (kappa/16)*min(1,d/n) and (kappa/8)*min(1,d/n). At ell=0 it recovers the no-verifier frontier. At ell=r the exact frontier is (kappa*U/N-c)_+/2, so complete arbitrary truth certification without orientation disclosure can still force hallucination at zero calibration error. The unrestricted lower bound also holds for coarser source bins, but its matching upper bound is asserted only for exact-level Mis_infinity. Ordinary factual training, unequal coverage and noisy/adaptive verifiers are not covered.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:a254903c9f76a4edf6c7529869019c109a0589cc9d8bbfaf7768c7cda602fef6","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/a2/a254903c9f76a4edf6c7529869019c109a0589cc9d8bbfaf7768c7cda602fef6.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:4046749ef851f0b6bc64f25b25012eb3cf5630630ce341100c131924ae8d22b2","bundle_entry_key":"partial-support-verifier-frontier","bundle_id":"population.t379-partial-support-verifier-no-orientations-20261020","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"statistical learning; calibrated generation; minimax decision theory","draft":"w709/bundle_003.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:learning.calibration:paired-vc-partial-truth-verifier-without-orientations","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Certified partial supports without orientation disclosure

Candidate T379-C008 v2; Own-work draft, proof (unaudited).
Target 2 and its interaction with target 1. Independent checking and
priority review pending. Exact finite verification passed; it supplements
the general proof rather than replacing it.
The hardest remaining generalization is ordinary unannotated factual
training, or a verifier revealing unequal numbers of truths per context:
the posterior density ordering used below can then fail.

## Model

Use the paired VC model: integers d>=1,N>=2d+1,n>=0,K>=2 and
1<=r<K; d pairs each have one A and one S context, the rest known S.
All K candidates are true in S; an independent uniform random r-subset
is true in A. The factual law p chooses contexts uniformly, then a true
candidate uniformly. Training is n iid uniform context indices and
their partition tags, with no candidate identities. The class has VC
dimension d. There are U pairs untouched by training. Let a=d/N,
m=U/N and w=a-m. A known partition is not given for untouched pairs.

Fix an integer 0<=ell<=r. A perfect post-training truth-sampling verifier
supplies a uniformly chosen ell-subset of true candidates in EACH of the
2d variable contexts, without disclosing any orientations or other truth
information. In known S contexts it also samples among true candidates,
namely all K. Thus it verifies the fraction gamma=ell/r of arbitrary
truths in every A context, and additionally supplies ell truths per paired
S context. This additional systematic information is explicitly part of
the experiment. The fixed S reservoir needs no queries. Sampling is
without replacement and independent across contexts given the world.

Put beta=r/K, kappa=1-beta, q=ell/K=beta*gamma,
alpha=(K-r)/(K-ell)=kappa/(1-q). Define posterior group masses

 A0=w*(1-gamma),       M0=m*(2-gamma-q).

The proposed exact conditional robust Mis_infinity frontier over ALL
generators is

 V_ell(c,U)=alpha/2 * [(A0-c)_+ +(A0+M0-c)_+],  c in [0,1].       (1)

The oracle with orientations known but the SAME certified truths has
value alpha*[a*(1-gamma)-c]_+. The expected minimax value is E[V_ell],
where U has the original d-pair occupancy law of C004; the verifier does
not reveal orientations. A matching lower bound also holds for coarser
output bins, but only exact levels are asserted for the attaining upper
bound. The specified uniform-posterior average game has the same
conditional value. All claims below remain unaudited derivations.

## Why the verifier does not label the unknown partition

Under a uniform random r-subset R, sample T uniformly among ell-subsets
of R. Every ell-subset of [K] has probability 1/binom(K,ell), since
binom(K-ell,r-ell)/(binom(K,r)*binom(r,ell))=1/binom(K,ell).
This is the same law as a uniform ell-subset from an S context. Hence
the verifier output has identical likelihood under either orientation.
Conditional on it, the untouched pair orientations remain independent
fair bits under the uniform world prior. Each A support is uniform over
r-subsets containing its certified T. Known tags are unchanged.

Let mu=E[p|tags,T] and s(y)=P(y false|tags,T). For uncertified atoms,

 known A:     mu_A=(r-ell)/(N*r*(K-ell)), s=alpha;
 unknown pair:mu_M=(mu_A+1/(N*K))/2,     s=alpha/2;
 known S:     mu=1/(N*K),               s=0.

Certified atoms have risk zero, and their mu is respectively 1/(Nr),
(1/(Nr)+1/(NK))/2, or 1/(NK). Therefore mu is nonincreasing with
positive false-risk level: mu_A<=mu_M<=1/(NK), while certified-safe
atoms have density at least 1/(NK). Let A be all uncertified atoms of
known A contexts; let M be all uncertified atoms of unknown pairs.
Their mu masses are exactly A0 and M0. All other atoms are safe.

## Unrestricted mixed-bin lower bound

For E=A and E=A union M, each atom inside E has mu-density at most
every atom outside E. For any uniform coarsening Pi, this implies
mu_Pi(E)>=mu(E): in a cell with l inside and h outside atoms, writing
their mu sums L,H, the ordering gives L/l<=H/h if both are nonempty,
so l(L+H)/(l+h)>=L. Empty intersections give equality. Sum cells.

For every generator g its output bins Pi(g) are fixed when worlds are
averaged. By linearity and the coordinatewise triangle inequality,
TV(mu_Pi,g)<=E[TV(p_Pi,g)]. A robust or stated posterior-average
calibration budget therefore implies

 g(A)>=(A0-c)_+,     g(A union M)>=(A0+M0-c)_+.

Expected hallucination is alpha*g(A)+(alpha/2)*g(M), exactly alpha/2
times the sum of these two events. This proves (1)'s lower bound for
every g, even bins that mix verified supports, contexts and risk levels.
Worst-world hallucination dominates the posterior average. No restriction
on the competing generator has been inserted into this argument.

## Worldwise attaining generator

Start from mu. Remove tA=min(c,A0) uniformly from A and
tM=min((c-A0)_+,M0) uniformly from M, taking zero from empty groups.
Add tA+tM uniformly to the N-2d fixed S contexts. Leave certified atoms
and all other contexts unchanged. This is nonnegative, normalized and
has TV(mu,g)=tA+tM<=c.

For a known A context, g is constant across its certified atoms and
across its uncertified atoms separately. Each of those groups has the
same p mass as mu in every compatible support. For each unknown pair,
g is constant on all certified atoms of BOTH siblings, and separately
on all uncertified atoms of both siblings. Their pairwise p masses are
respectively ell*(1/K+1/r)/N and (2-ell/K-ell/r)/N, independent of the
orientation and compatible supports. Known S context fibres are constant.
Consequently every exact g-score cell is a union of these invariant-mass
groups (including any merging levels and zero scores). It follows that
p_Pi=mu_Pi in every compatible world. With g_Pi=g,

 Mis_infinity(g,p)=TV(mu_Pi,g_Pi)<=TV(mu,g)<=c.

In known A uncertified groups a fraction alpha of candidates is false;
in unknown-pair uncertified groups a fraction alpha/2 is false. They
are uniform under g, so in EVERY compatible world

 H=alpha*(A0-tA)+(alpha/2)*(M0-tM)=V_ell(c,U).

There are no false certified atoms. The three budget ranges c<=A0,
A0<=c<=A0+M0, and c>=A0+M0 give (1). Empty groups, ell=r, ell=0,
U=0 and zero output bins are included by the stated conventions.

With orientations known, all uncertified A mass is a*(1-gamma), with
constant false-risk alpha. The same tail lower bound and removal
construction give the oracle claimed above. It is not given any
uncertified arbitrary identities beyond those disclosed by the verifier.

## Minimax expectation and informative budgets

Conditional posterior lower bounds integrate under the uniform prior on
orientations and supports, and the maximum over fixed worlds dominates
this average. The construction has the same H=V_ell(U) for every world
and every compatible verifier output. U's distribution is independent of
worlds and outputs because tags reveal a pair iff a training context
touches it, and the verifier conveys no orientation likelihood. These
facts give matching global expected minimax value E[V_ell(U)] under
conditional robust feasibility, without an unjustified sup/expectation
interchange. Its law is

 E[z^U]=sum_{j=0}^d binom(d,j)*(z-1)^j*(1-2j/N)^n,
 E U=d*(1-2/N)^n.

Put T=a*(1-gamma)-c. The exact excess over the known-partition oracle is

 alpha/2 * [(T-m*(1-gamma))_+
           +(T+m*(1-q))_+ -2*T_+].                    (2)

This is nonnegative: split T at -m*(1-q), 0, and m*(1-gamma), using
q<=gamma in the positive middle range. At c=0 it equals
alpha*kappa*gamma*m/2. At the oracle's zero-hallucination threshold
c=a*(1-gamma), the actual value is

 V_ell = alpha*m*(1-q)/2 = kappa*U/(2N).              (3)

Thus its exact expected value is kappa*d/(2N)*(1-2/N)^n, or kappa/2
times the minimax expected classification error R=d/N*(1-2/N)^n of
fair consistent ERM. The verifier does not change R because its law
does not distinguish orientations. It shifts the critical calibration
budget but the generation learning penalty there stays the same.

At ell=0, (1) reduces to C004. At ell=r, every A truth is certified,
but the verifier does not identify which contexts are A. Formula (1)
then becomes (kappa*U/N-c)_+/2. In particular zero calibration error
still costs kappa*U/(2N) unless the tags determine all orientations.
This contrasts with C006's orientation-disclosing full verifier, which
can yield zero hallucination and calibration error when all pairs are
verified. The source of side information, not merely its fact fraction,
must therefore be stated in a frontier claim.

For n,d>=1 choose N=4*max(n,d). Bernoulli's inequality gives
1/2<= (1-2/N)^n <=1. Thus the exact expected value at the threshold
in (3) lies between (kappa/16)*min(1,d/n) and
(kappa/8)*min(1,d/n). These are matching sample-complexity bounds for
this entire annotated VC family, for every allowed verifier fraction;
they do not extend automatically to an arbitrary VC class.

The version space, verifier sets and group counts admit the same efficient
representation as C004/C006. For rational c, group sampling has expected
polynomial bit complexity, with O(n+d+d*ell) explicit data processing.
The probability bound P(U>0)<=d*(1-2/N)^n also applies; U=0 gives the
oracle frontier simultaneously at every c. No independence between
missing-pair indicators is presumed.

This derivation uses the source exact-level Mis_infinity (Kalai--Vempala
2311.14648v3, Definitions 1--2, pp.8--9) and standard finite TV/event
inequalities. No novelty is asserted for those inequalities, occupancy,
or uniform-subset counting. The proposed new result is the stated
explicit partial-truth-verifier frontier. Exact Fraction checks passed:
886 unrestricted-generator/bin checks, 1982 attaining-world checks,
23 posterior experiments, 288 VC-rate scaling checks, and an unequal-
coverage negative control. Source/priority comparison and independent
audit remain required before any independent-proof promotion.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:3f20ee342ff8d8d590412ad954feb9397cf2856f877417b3699aeb5d6b74c1ab","revision_digest":"sha256:93973381fe8b8bdd8b366c60569d55905dbcc6845d17173da516a2a6bde38527","source_id":"owner:w709:T379-C008:v2","source_revision":"2026-10-20T10:57:45.230043+03:00","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

body:
Historical Benjamini-Schramm criticality question: for independent Bernoulli bond percolation on any infinite connected locally finite quasi-transitive undirected graph G with p_c(G)<1, is there almost surely no infinite open cluster at p_c(G)? OpenAI's 24 September 2026 preprint 'No percolation at criticality on quasi-transitive graphs', Theorem 1.1, claims the affirmative answer under exactly these graph hypotheses. Its public Lean solution theorem has the same conclusion for labelled bonds. The earlier 'open' label is historical; full mathematical and formal dependency audits are separate and remain unrecorded in this campaign.

[Thm matrix-sharpness of arXiv:2608.29018, 'Sharp Restricted Isometry Thresholds for\\ Global Minima of Rank-Restricted Matrix LASSO'] Fix integers $r_{\star}\ge1$ and $k\ge2$.
Set $t\coloneqq k/r_{\star}$ and
\begin{equation}
\mathsf{C}(t)\coloneqq1+\frac{(3t-4)_{+}}{2-t+\sqrt{t(t-1)_{+}}}.
\end{equation}
If $\delta\ge\delta_{\mathrm{sharp}}(t)+1/r_{\star}$, then:
\begin{itemize}
\item (Matrix) There exist adversarial data $(X_{\star},\mathcal{A},b)$ satisfying
\[
\operatorname{rank}(X_{\star})=r_{\star},\quad\mathcal{A}\in\operatorname{RIP}(\delta,k),\quad b=\mathcal{A}(X_{\star}),
\]
such that every global minimizer $X_{\lambda,r}$ in ((eq:matrix-lasso of the paper))
satisfies 
\begin{equation}
\lambda>0,\;r\ge\mathsf{C}(t)r_{\star}\implies\normF{X_{\lambda,r}-X_{\star}}\ge\normF{X_{\star}}.
\end{equation}
\item (Vector) There exist adversarial data $(x_{\star},A,b)$ satisfying
\[
\normzero{x_{\star}}=r_{\star},\quad A\in\operatorname{rip}(\delta,k),\quad b=Ax_{\star},
\]
such that every global minimizer $x_{\lambda,r}$ in ((eq:vector-lasso of the paper))
satisfies 
\begin{equation}
\lambda>0,\;r\ge\mathsf{C}(t)r_{\star}\implies\normtwo{x_{\lambda,r}-x_{\star}}\ge\normtwo{x_{\star}}.
\end{equation}
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm matrix-sharpness of arXiv:2608.29018

[Proposition 95 (Exterior degree is not primitive ancestry) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] Let $V$ be a complex vector space with $\dim V\ge j$.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{Hom}_{GL(V)}(\Lambda^jV,L_j(V))=0,
 \qquad j\ge3.
 
\end{equation}
Equivalently, in stable dimension there is no nonzero homogeneous linear
natural transformation from the degree-$j$ fermionic sector to the
degree-$j$ free-Lie sector.  The coincidence $L_2(V)=\Lambda^2V$ is therefore
exceptional: exterior particle number is a covariance-reader degree, not a
second model of the Rees ancestry filtration.

body: Let A be an n by n Hermitian matrix with eigenvalues lambda_1 >= ... >= lambda_n, and let B be an (n-1) by (n-1) principal submatrix of A, obtained by deleting one row and the corresponding column, with eigenvalues mu_1 >= ... >= mu_{n-1}. Then the eigenvalues interlace: lambda_1 >= mu_1 >= lambda_2 >= mu_2 >= ... >= mu_{n-1} >= lambda_n. [standard, e.g. Horn and Johnson, Matrix Analysis]

Assume that there exist $\bar{\p}(t)$, $\bar{\q}(t)$, and $\bar{\m}(t)$ that satisfy (\ref{eq:saip4}) and that $\bar{\p}(t)$ and $\bar{\q}(t)$ are not only the  overlaps $(\x^{(p_1)})^T\x^{(i_1)}$ and $(\y^{(p_2)})^T\y^{(i_2)}$ (scaled) expected values (in the sense of (\ref{eq:saip4})) but also their concentrating points (or such that $\phi_{k_1+1}^{(r)}=0$).  =

= \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} \psi_1(\bar{\p}(1),\bar{\q}(1),\bar{\m}(1),1),

with $\psi_1(\cdot)$ and $\psi(\cdot)$  as in (\ref{eq:saip1}) and  (\ref{eq:thm3eq1}), respectively.

body: [Definition of arXiv:2608.30346, '\textbf{Classification complexity of homeomorphism group actions}'] Let \(G\) be a Polish group acting continuously on a Polish space \(X\). For \(x \in X\), \(U \subset X\) open with \(x \in U\) and \(V \subset G\) open with \(1_G \in V\), the \textit{local \(U \text{-} V\)-orbit of} \(x\), denoted \(\mathcal{O}(x,U,V)\), is the set of \(y \in U\) for which there exist \(l \in \mathbb{N}\), \(x = x_1\in U, x_2\in U, \dots x_l = y \in U\) and \(g_1, \dots ,g_{l-1} \in V\) such that \(x_{i+1} = g_i \cdot x_i\) for \(i < l\).

body: [Lemma 91 of arXiv:2608.07239, 'Unified framework for asymptotically uniform iterative construction of generalised random '] Let $0<\delta<1$ with $\delta=O(\tfrac{\log\log\alpha}{\log\alpha})$, and let $\mu_1,\mu_2>0$ with $\mu_2=\Omega(1)$, $\mu_1+\mu_2=1$, and $$\delta\geq\tfrac1{\mu_1}\left(8\left(1-\tfrac{\log M}{\log\alpha}\right)+2+\Omega(1)\right)\tfrac{\log\log\alpha}{\log\alpha}.$$ Let $r=0,\ldots,\alpha-k-1$ with $t:=\alpha-k-r=O(M)$. Then $$\mathbb{E}(\Pi1_{\mathcal{P}_{t+1}^{\delta}\cap\mathcal{Q}_t^{\delta}})\leq\exp\left(t\log t+(\tfrac1{2\mu_2}+o(1))t\log\log\alpha+O(\tfrac1{\delta}k)\right)\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{Q}_t^{\delta}).$$

[Definition def:random_length_worms_model of arXiv:2505.07145, 'Nonamenable Poisson zoo'] Let us consider a probability mass function $\eta: \mathbb{N}_{>0} \to [0,1] $ and an $\mathbb{N}_{>0}$-valued random variable $\mathcal{L}$ satisfying $\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{L}=\ell)=\eta(\ell), \, \ell \in \mathbb{N}_{>0}$. 
	We call the distribution of $\mathcal{L}$ the length distribution of the worms. Let us also consider a nearest neighbour simple random walk $(X(t))_{t \in \mathbb{N}}$ on the vertices of $G$ starting from $X(0)=o$, independent of $\mathcal{L}$.
	Let us define the probability measure $\nu^{\text{worm;}{\eta}}$ on $\mathcal{H}_{o}$ by 
	\begin{equation}
		
		\nu^{\text{worm;}{\eta}}(H) := P_{o}( \{ X(0), X(1), \ldots, X(\mathcal{L} - 1) \} = H )
	\end{equation}
	for each $H \in \mathcal{H}_{o}$.
	Given any $\lambda >0$, the Poisson zoo $\mathcal{N}_{\eta}^{\lambda} := \mathcal{N}_{\nu^{\text{worm;}{\eta}}}^{\lambda}$ built upon this measure via Definition (def:poisson_zoo of the paper) is called the random length worms model at level $\lambda$, and the corresponding random set $\mathcal{S}_{\eta}^\lambda := \mathcal{S}_{\nu^{\text{worm;}{\eta}}}^\lambda$ is the random length worms set at level $\lambda$.
title: Definition def:random_length_worms_model of arXiv:2505.07145

[Prop 11 ($p$-Powers of Derivations on Curves) of arXiv:2609.00974, 'On Algebraic Integrability\\ of Vector Fields \\ with Rational Function Coefficients\\ tha'] Let $K$ be a generic point of a curve with a coordinate $x$. 
    Let $f\in K$. We define a derivation on $K$ by
    \[
    D=f\frac{\partial}{\partial x}
    \]
    Then, its $p$-power is given by 
    \[
    D^{\circ p}=-b_{p-1} D
    \]
    where $b_{p-1}\in K^p$ is the unique coefficient in the expansion in the $p$-basis $\frac{x^{j}}{(j)!}$ for $0\le j<p$
    \[
    f^{p-1}=b_0+b_1\frac{x}{1!}+\ldots +b_{p-1}\frac{x^{p-1}}{(p-1)!},
    \]
    where $b_i\in K^p$.
title: $p$-Powers of Derivations on Curves

Data is obtained from a randomized trial
Pre-treatment covariates X are independent of treatment assignment
Sample size N \to \infty

[Proposition 5 of arXiv:2608.30752, '2608.30752'] With the notation above, the normalized energy is nonincreasing and satisfies
\begin{equation}
  e^{-2t}E_{u_0}(X_t)
  \searrow
  \mathscr V_q(Y)
  \qquad
  \text{as }t\to\infty.
  
\end{equation}
In particular,
\begin{equation}
  \lim_{t\to\infty}
  \frac{E_{u_0}(X_t)}{e^{2t}}
  =
  \mathscr V_q(Y),
  \qquad
  E_{u_0}(X_t)
  =
  \mathscr V_q(Y)e^{2t}
  +
  o(e^{2t}).
  
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\(
  0<\mathscr V_q(Y)<\infty.
\)

If \(q\) is Jenkins--Strebel and its vertical foliation is the contracting
foliation of the ray, let
\(
  C_1,\ldots,C_r
\)
be its maximal flat cylinders. Write
\(
  C_i
  \cong
  (0,h_i)\times
  \bigl(\mathbb R/c_i\mathbb Z\bigr),
\)
where the closed vertical trajectories have \(q\)-length \(c_i\), the
transverse height is \(h_i\), and \(\delta_i\) is the core curve of \(C_i\).
Then
\begin{equation}
  \mathscr V_q(Y)
  =
  \frac12
  \sum_{i=1}^r
  \operatorname{Mod}(C_i)\,
  \ell_Y(\delta_i)^2
  =
  \frac12
  \sum_{i=1}^r
  \frac{h_i}{c_i}\,
  \ell_Y(\delta_i)^2.
  
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
  \lim_{t\to\infty}
  \frac{E_{u_0}(X_t)}{e^{2t}}
  =
  \frac12
  \sum_{i=1}^r
  \operatorname{Mod}(C_i)\,
  \ell_Y(\delta_i)^2.
  
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 5 of arXiv:2608.30752

Own-work draft; proof (unaudited); T232-w704-C014 v1. No independent PASS or established novelty/priority. Let m>=2,w>=2 be finite, M a real m-by-2 matrix of rank two, and Sigma a real symmetric positive definite 2-by-2 matrix. Suppose M Sigma has distinct singular values s1>s2>0. For gradient flow B'=-(BA-M)Sigma A^T, A'=-B^T(BA-M)Sigma, form U=(B;A^T) and D=[[0,M Sigma],[Sigma M^T,0]]. Let v1,v2 be positive unit eigenvectors of D. Fix a finite seed U0 with c1=||v1^T U0||>0 and one hidden orthogonal rotation R with v1^T U0 R=(c1,0,...,0). Split U0 R=[z0,X0] and assume c2=v2^T X0 is nonzero. Start at alpha U0 R, let tau=log(1/alpha)/s1, epsilon=alpha^(1-s2/s1), and write U_alpha(t+tau)=[z_alpha(t),X_alpha(t)]. On every fixed shifted compact, z_alpha converges to zbar and X_alpha/epsilon converges to chi c2. With H(P)=[[0,P Sigma],[Sigma P^T,0]], these are the unique weighted-bounded canonical Volterra solutions zbar=c1 exp(s1 t)v1-integral_-infinity^t exp(D(t-u))H(bbar abar^T)zbar du and chi=exp(s2 t)v2-integral_-infinity^t exp(D(t-u))H(bbar abar^T)chi du, where zbar=(bbar;abar). Their backward remainders are O(exp(3s1 t)) and O(exp((2s1+s2)t)), respectively; they extend to every finite time. If Pi projects onto col(M)^perp, then ||Pi B_alpha(physical time)||_F<=alpha||Pi B0||_F for all forward times, and ||Pi (X_alpha)_b/epsilon||_F<=alpha^(s2/s1)||Pi B0||_F. Thus bbar and chi_b belong to col(M), and their ideal equations reduce isometrically to the square target Q^T M for any orthonormal basis Q of col(M). The nondegeneracy assumptions hold almost surely for one fixed iid standard Gaussian seed, then scaled by alpha. This is fixed-compact origin matching, not a full Gaussian saddle passage or an entire normalized-error rate.

rank M=2
s1>s2>0 singular values of M Sigma

This is not a complete rectangular second-step theorem, and no novelty or priority claim is made. C006 v2 supplies the square precedent, not an independent audit of this extended statement.

## Statement
Let m>=2, w>=2 be finite, M be a real m-by-2 matrix of rank two, and Sigma a real symmetric positive definite 2-by-2 matrix. Suppose M Sigma has distinct positive singular values s1>s2. Define
 D = [[0,M Sigma],[Sigma M^T,0]],
 H(P) = [[0,P Sigma],[Sigma P^T,0]].
Let v1,v2 be orthonormal positive unit eigenvectors of D with eigenvalues s1,s2. Fix a finite seed U0=(B0;A0^T) in R^((m+2)-by-w). Assume c1=||v1^T U0||>0. Fix one hidden orthogonal rotation R with v1^T U0 R=(c1,0,...,0). Write U0 R=[z0,X0] and c2=v2^T X0, and assume c2 is not zero.

For gradient flow B'=-(BA-M)Sigma A^T, A'=-B^T(BA-M)Sigma from alpha U0 R, put tau=log(1/alpha)/s1, epsilon=alpha^(1-s2/s1), and use shifted time t=physical time-tau. Write U_alpha=[z_alpha,X_alpha]. On every fixed compact interval of shifted time,
 z_alpha -> zbar,    X_alpha/epsilon -> chi c2,
where the canonical pair is uniquely prescribed by
 zbar(t)=c1 exp(s1 t)v1 - integral_{-infinity}^t exp(D(t-u)) H(bbar abar^T)zbar(u)du,
 chi(t)=exp(s2 t)v2 - integral_{-infinity}^t exp(D(t-u)) H(bbar abar^T)chi(u)du.
Here zbar=(bbar;abar), with remainder bounds
 zbar-c1 exp(s1 t)v1 = O(exp(3s1 t)),
 chi-exp(s2 t)v2 = O(exp((2s1+s2)t))
as t tends to minus infinity. The constants depend on the fixed seed and data. The solutions extend to every finite shifted time.

Let Q be any m-by-2 orthonormal basis of col(M), and Pi=I-QQ^T. For every physical time >=0,
 ||Pi B_alpha||_F <= alpha ||Pi B0||_F.
Consequently both ideal output components bbar and chi_b lie in col(M), and on every fixed shifted compact
 ||Pi (X_alpha)_b /epsilon||_F <= alpha^(s2/s1)||Pi B0||_F.
In this display B0 may be replaced by B0 R without changing its Frobenius norm. The same hypotheses on c1,c2 hold almost surely for one fixed iid standard Gaussian seed, subsequently scaled by alpha.

## 1. Global existence and the two weighted estimates
The stacked equation is U'=DU-H(BA)U. With sigma=||Sigma||op,
 ||H(BA)||op <= (sigma/2)||U||_F^2.
Loss decreases, hence ||BA||_F is bounded since Sigma is positive definite. K=B^T B-AA^T is conserved and
 ||B^T B||_F^2+||AA^T||_F^2=2||BA||_F^2+||K||_F^2,
 ||B||_F^2+||A||_F^2 <= sqrt(2w)*sqrt(2||BA||_F^2+||K||_F^2).
These identities hold for rectangular B without alteration. For 0<alpha<=1 their right sides are uniformly bounded. Smooth finite-dimensional continuation gives global forward existence.

D has spectrum s1,s2,-s2,-s1 and zero of multiplicity m-2: this follows by a singular value decomposition of M Sigma, whose rank is two. In particular ||exp(Dv)||op<=exp(s1 v) for v>=0. Write K0=||U0||_F and choose a fixed negative T. Variation of constants gives a bootstrap
 ||U_alpha(t)||_F<=2K0 exp(s1 t),  -tau<=t<=T.
Indeed at a first crossing the nonlinear term divided by exp(s1 t) is at most
 (sigma/(4s1))(2K0)^3 exp(2s1 T),
which is strictly smaller than K0 for sufficiently negative T. The initial weighted norm equals K0.

The free dormant block has exactly zero v1 coefficient. Every other eigenvalue, including zero, is <=s2. Its free norm is at most epsilon ||X0||_F exp(s2 t). With C0=2 sigma K0^2, the nonlinear integral operator in the weight epsilon exp(s2 t) has norm at most
 C0 exp(2s1 T)/(s1+s2).
Take T smaller until this is <1/2. Then
 ||X_alpha(t)||_F<=2||X0||_F epsilon exp(s2 t).
The full propagator exp(s1(t-u)) is used for the integral; cancellation of the top coefficient is asserted only for the free term.

## 2. Fixed-compact limits: every free spectral component
On a fixed compact subset of (-infinity,T], the estimates above bound z_alpha, Y_alpha=X_alpha/epsilon, and their derivatives. Subsequential local uniform limits exist by Arzela-Ascoli and diagonal extraction.

For an eigenvalue lambda of D, the active free prefactor is alpha^(1-lambda/s1) exp(lambda t). Thus the v1 component is exactly c1 exp(s1 t); the s2 component has prefactor epsilon; the zero components have prefactor alpha; and the -si components have prefactors alpha^(1+si/s1). All but v1 vanish on fixed compacts.

For the normalized dormant free term the prefactor is alpha^((s2-lambda)/s1) exp(lambda t). The v1 coefficient is identically zero, the s2 coefficient is exactly exp(s2 t)v2 c2, the zero components have prefactor alpha^(s2/s1), and the -si components have prefactors alpha^((s2+si)/s1). All unwanted components vanish. Zero eigenvalues cannot be discarded when asserting a quantitative rate: alpha^(s2/s1) can be slower than the square stable-mode scale alpha^(2s2/s1).

The unnormalized dormant block tends to zero, so the product tends to bbar abar^T. The active integral is bounded by C exp(s1 t) exp(2s1 u); the normalized dormant integral by C exp(s1 t) exp((s1+s2)u). Both are integrable at minus infinity since s1,s2>0. Split at a fixed negative cutoff, pass to local limits on the finite part, and bound the rest by these uniform tails. This gives exactly the two displayed Volterra equations (first with Y in place of chi c2).

## 3. Uniqueness, remainders and continuation
On the bounded active weighted class ||z||<=C exp(s1 t), the cubic nonlinearity is Lipschitz with coefficient C' exp(2s1 u). Its Volterra difference operator has weighted norm at most C' exp(2s1 T)/(2s1). Decrease T until it is <1. The normalized linear dormant operator has norm at most C0 exp(2s1 T)/(s1+s2)<1. Thus both limits are unique in these classes. These bounds also construct chi by contraction about its free vector term, and linearity gives Y=chi c2. All subsequences have the same limits, proving convergence of the full alpha family.

Integrating the respective bounds gives the stated O(exp(3s1 t)) and O(exp((2s1+s2)t)) remainders. The stronger canonical prescription is needed: the mere leading s2 asymptotic alone would permit adding a multiple of zbar. Forward boundedness of the rank-one flow follows from Section 1 with w=1. The chi equation is linear with continuous coefficients, so it exists on each finite forward interval. Fixed finite-interval continuous dependence, applied first to U_alpha and then its normalized linear dormant equation, extends convergence from T to any fixed compact. No growing-time interval is covered.

## 4. Exact output contraction and the reduced ideal pair
Since Pi M=0, E=Pi B solves E'=-EA Sigma A^T. Therefore
 d/dt ||E||_F^2=-2 tr(EA Sigma A^T E^T)=-2||EA Sigma^(1/2)||_F^2<=0.
This proves the uniform transverse bounds in the statement. Fix any finite shifted t; for small alpha it corresponds to a positive physical time. Passing to the limits yields Pi bbar(t)=0 and (Pi chi_b(t))c2=0. Since the fixed row c2 is nonzero, the last equality implies Pi chi_b(t)=0. Thus ideal subspace confinement is established at the backward boundary through actual uniform bounds, rather than inferred merely from finite-time invariance.

Set Mtilde=Q^T M. It is invertible. The ideal equations for (Q^T bbar,abar) and (Q^T chi_b,chi_a) are precisely the square canonical Volterra equations for Mtilde, Sigma; Q is an isometry on their output components, and M Sigma and Mtilde Sigma have the same positive singular values. This identifies the ideal pair, not the finite-alpha projected dynamics over a growing time interval.

## 5. Gaussian event and remaining frontier gap
The two initial eigenrows v1^T U0 and v2^T U0 are independent standard Gaussian rows because v1,v2 are orthonormal and U0 is iid standard Gaussian. The first is nonzero almost surely. Conditional on it, projection of the second onto its hidden orthogonal complement is a nondegenerate Gaussian in dimension w-1>=1 and is nonzero almost surely. This proves c2!=0 without any later-flow independence.

This origin-matching component now extends to all finite m>=2 with two inputs under the displayed assumptions. Rectangular local arrival, full canonical escape, and the complete endpoint composition still require their own dimension checks and independent review. C010 and C012 remain unaudited. A bound on the perpendicular normalized component is not a bound on the entire matching error. No full rectangular rate, complete Target 1 solution, depth>=3 result, or priority finding is asserted.

Sources: proofs/origin_inactive_matching.md (C006 v2, square precedent); proofs/rectangular_output_reduction_route.md (C013 sketch, exact projection algebra). CLAIM: the joint law of (S_K, S_a), and hence the law of tau, is exact. P(S_K > t, S_a > s) = exp(-lambda E_v Vol(union of two parallel capsules)), with Lambda(t,s) = lambda E_v Vol(capsule union) = lambda E_v [omega_d R^d + omega_{d-1} R^{d-1} c t + omega_d r^d + omega_{d-1} r^{d-1} c s - integral L_{d-1}(rho_1(z), rho_2(z), h) dz], explicit up to a one-dimensional integral. Non-homogeneous intensities give the source's 'laborious' integrals; the coverage and stability open problems are untouched; prior art unchecked beyond the source.

[Theorem thm:ToRCD of arXiv:2609.01464, 'Removability of non-isolated singularities for Einstein metrics and RCD spaces'] Let $(Z,d,\mathfrak{m})$ be as in (Setting of the paper). Then $(Z,d,\mathfrak{m})$ is an \textit{RCD}$(K, n)$ space, where $K \in \mathbb{R}$, if it is an almost smooth compact metric measure space, and the following conditions hold.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item The Sobolev to Lipschitz property holds, that is any $f \in W^{1,2}(Z,d,\mathfrak{m})$, with $|\nabla f|(x) \leqslant 1$ for $\mathfrak{m}$-almost every $x$, has a 1-Lipschitz representative.
    \item The $L^2$-strong compactness condition holds, that is the inclusion $W^{1,2}(Z,d,\mathfrak{m}) \hookrightarrow L^2(Z,\mathfrak{m})$ is a compact operator.
    \item Any eigenfunction in $W^{1,2}(Z,d,\mathfrak{m})$ of the Laplacian on $Z$ is Lipschitz.
    \item $\mathrm{Ric}_{(M,g)} \geqslant Kg$ on the regular part $M\subset Z$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\[
\mathrm{d}X_t = b(X_t)\,\mathrm{d}t + \sigma(X_t)\,\mathrm{d}W_t.
\]
If \( f \in C_0^2(\mathbb{R}^d) \), then \( f \in D_{\mathcal{A}} \) and 

\[
\mathcal{A}f(x) = \sum_{i} b_i(x) \frac{\partial f}{\partial x_i} + \frac{1}{2} \sum_{i,j} (\sigma \sigma^T)_{i,j}(x) \frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial x_i \partial x_j},
\]
or, in terms of the gradient, scalar, and Frobenius inner products, the generator can be expressed as
\[
\mathcal{A}f(x) = b(x) \cdot \nabla_x f(x) + \frac{1}{2} \left( \sigma(x)\sigma(x)^\top \right) : \nabla_x \nabla_x f(x).

    where $\widehat{X}^l_t$ and $\widehat{X}^{l-1}_t$ share the same Brownian motion from $0$ to $T$. Applying the simple inequality $(a + b)^2 \leq 2(a^2 + b^2)$, which holds for all real numbers $a$ and $b$, we obtain that
    $$
        \mathbb{E}[|\widehat{X}^l_T - \widehat{X}^{l-1}_T|^2] \leq 2(\mathbb{E}[|\widehat{X}^l_T - X_T|^2] + \mathbb{E}[|X_T - \widehat{X}^{l-1}_T|^2]).
    $$

AUTHOR PROOF DRAFT, unaudited; novelty is unestablished. Let U_N and V_N be independent N by M and P by M arrays with fixed centered iid real entry laws, variance one and finite fourth moments. Put A_N=U_N V_N^T/sqrt(N), and let B_N be the same product with independent standard Gaussian factor entries. If P/N->alpha and M/N->beta lie in (0,infinity), then for each fixed s>0, limsup_N [I(A_N;sqrt(s)A_N+G_N)-I(B_N;sqrt(s)B_N+G_N)]/(NP)<=0, with independent standard Gaussian observation noise and natural logarithms. Neither MI limit is assumed to exist. All dimension orderings and a positive mass of zero signal singular values are allowed. The proof uses a conditional rank-two Lindeberg resolvent estimate, concentration, moment bounds giving expected singular-value Wasserstein coupling, and Haar-mixture entropy concavity. It does not prove unconditional all-SNR product-MMSE extremality or a uniform small-SNR expansion.
Fixed centered real iid unit-variance factor laws with finite fourth moments
Independent arrays U_N,V_N and standard Gaussian observation noise
Positive finite limiting aspect ratios P/N and M/N
Fixed s>0 and natural logarithms

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:cc92334215dd5e90e034ea2e8cf2eebd3c5ca51c6a3eba83ca0f5809a74708f1","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/cc/cc92334215dd5e90e034ea2e8cf2eebd3c5ca51c6a3eba83ca0f5809a74708f1.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:4b63b4d5e0e27fb5fc35472ff5eb469e6c139a18443923de29d17fa9cb3919ee","bundle_entry_key":"iid-product-gaussian-mi-all-aspects-w718","bundle_id":"population.t287-all-aspect-mi-and-sixth-coefficients-v1","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Gaussian channels and extensive-rank matrix inference","draft":"w718/bundle_002.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.gaussian_channels:iid-product-gaussian-mi-all-aspects-w718","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Gaussian-factor mutual-information comparison at all positive aspect ratios

Target 2, mutual-information part. Proof draft, unaudited; novelty is
unestablished. This extends the monotone-dimension-chain result in
gaussian_mi_wedge.md. It does not establish a formula for the limiting
mutual information or an unconditional all-SNR MMSE comparison.

Let N,P,M tend to infinity with P/N->alpha in (0,infinity) and
M/N->beta in (0,infinity). Let U in R^(N by M), V in R^(P by M)
be independent arrays with centered iid entries of variance one,
using fixed real entry laws with finite fourth moments. Set

 A=UV^T/sqrt(N),   B=U_G V_G^T/sqrt(N),

where the reference factors have independent standard Gaussian entries
and the same dimensions. For every fixed s>0 the claimed inequality is

 limsup [I(A;sqrt(s)A+G)-I(B;sqrt(s)B+G)]/(NP) <=0.          (1)

Noise G has independent standard Gaussian entries. Neither MI limit
needs to be assumed to exist for (1). Thus any existing iid-prior
limiting MI is at most the Gaussian reference limit.

The proof uses a direct global spectral comparison in place of the
dimension-restricted primary product-spectrum theorem. It provides
only global spectral universality; no local eigenvalue result is claimed.

## 1. Rank-two conditional Lindeberg replacement

Put S=UV^T/N, q=N+P, and use the real symmetric linearization

    H(U,V) = [ 0  S ; S^T  0 ],
    m(U,V;z)=q^(-1) Tr (H(U,V)-z I_q)^(-1),

where z has imaginary part eta>0. Every real value of every raw entry
gives a real symmetric H, so its resolvent R has operator norm at
most eta^(-1). This bound is uniform along all real replacement paths.

Condition on V. Differentiating H in one raw entry U_ir gives

    D_ir=N^(-1)[0 e_i v_r^T ; v_r e_i^T 0],

where v_r is the r-th column of V. Its rank is at most two and its
operator norm is ||v_r||/N. In particular it is independent of U_ir.
For the scalar real variable t=U_ir, resolvent differentiation gives

    partial_t^3 m = -6 q^(-1) Tr(R D_ir R D_ir R D_ir R).

The matrix in the trace has rank at most two. The inequalities
|Tr T|<=||T||_nuclear<=rank(T)||T||_op therefore give

    |partial_t^3 m| <= 12 ||v_r||^3/(q N^3 eta^4).       (2)

Taylor's integral remainder at t=0, to degree two, is bounded by
2||v_r||^3 |t|^3/(q N^3 eta^4). Replacing U_ir by an independent
standard Gaussian cancels the constant, linear and quadratic Taylor
terms because the two raw variables have the same first two moments.
The bound (2) is uniform in the other raw entries, including entries
already replaced. Thus a telescoping replacement of all NM entries
is legitimate.

Write a_3=E|U_11|^3, b_3=E|V_11|^3, and g_3=E|G_11|^3<=2.
The deterministic norm inequality

    (sum_{j=1}^P v_j^2)^(3/2) <= P^(1/2) sum_j |v_j|^3

implies E||v_r||^3<=P^(3/2)b_3. Consequently the first replacement
stage has expected normalized-resolvent error at most

    C_U(z)=2 M P^(3/2) b_3(a_3+g_3)/(q N^2 eta^4).       (3)

After this stage U is Gaussian. Replace the PM entries of V by
Gaussians, now conditioning on U. The derivative matrix has norm
||u_r||/N with E||u_r||^3<=N^(3/2)g_3. The second-stage error is

    C_V(z)=2 P M g_3(b_3+g_3)/(q N^(3/2) eta^4).         (4)

Under fixed positive aspect ratios, both (3) and (4) are O(N^-1/2).
Thus for each fixed z in the upper half-plane,

    |E m(U,V;z)-E m(U_G,V_G;z)| <= C_U(z)+C_V(z) ->0.   (5)

Finite fourth moments imply the third moments used here. Taylor's
remainder bound holds for unbounded real raw variables because its
third-derivative bound is uniform in t, and the absolute third moments
are finite. No truncation, unbounded Gaussian exponential moment, or
entrywise central limit theorem is being used.

## 2. Concentration and deterministic subsequential limits

Let r=min(N,P) and mu_A be the empirical probability measure of the
r singular values of S=A/sqrt(N), including any zero singular values
within those r positions. Let nu_A be the eigenvalue measure of H.
The two are related by

    nu_A=(r/q)(mu_A+reflection(mu_A))+(q-2r)delta_0/q.     (6)

The same relation holds for the Gaussian reference. Both r/N and q/N
stay bounded above and away from zero. Equation (5), tightness, and
uniqueness of the Stieltjes transform show that the expected spectral
measures of A and B have the same weak subsequential limits. More
explicitly, take any subsequence and a further subsequence on which
the deterministic expected nu_B converges weakly. Such a subsequence
exists because their second moments are bounded. Equation (5) implies
that expected nu_A has the same limit, by convergence of Stieltjes
transforms. The linear relation (6) transfers the conclusion to the
positive singular-value measures. This argument does not assume that
the full Gaussian spectral sequence has a limit.

To pass from expected to random measures, use independent row blocks
of U and V, exactly as in gaussian_mi_wedge.md. Replacing one row of
either factor changes S by rank at most one, and changes SS^T by rank
at most two. The empirical distribution function of the r squared
singular values therefore changes by at most 2/r. Indeed the N by N
Gram matrix has N-r additional zeros, the same for both configurations,
so its rank inequality rescales from 1/N to 1/r without an extra error.
Efron-Stein gives, for every fixed x,

    Var F_A(x) <= 2(N+P)/r^2 = O(N^-1).                 (7)

The Gaussian factors satisfy the same bound. At continuity points of
each selected deterministic limit, (7) upgrades the expected weak
convergence to weak convergence in probability. Monotonicity of the
distribution functions completes the usual countable-grid argument.

## 3. Moment control upgrades the comparison to expected W2

Let d=NP, b=M/N, T_N=||A||_F^2/d, q_U=E U_11^4,
q_V=E V_11^4. The exact fourth-cumulant patterns give

 E T_N=b,

 d^2 Var T_N = d[2b^2+(M/N^2)(q_U q_V-3)]
     +d(P-1)(M/N^2)(q_U-1)
     +d(N-1)(M/N^2)(q_V-1).                            (8)

Thus T_N-b tends to zero in L^2 for all the aspect ratios under
consideration. The empirical singular second moment is

    integral x^2 dmu_A(x)=(P/r)T_N,

which has a deterministic limit depending only on alpha,beta.
The Gaussian reference has exactly the same limiting second moment.

The uniform fourth singular-moment bound from gaussian_mi_wedge.md
remains valid without a monotone dimension chain. With
C=max(1,|q_U-1|,|q_V-1|,|q_U q_V-3|),

 E[(1/r)Tr(SS^T)^2]
 <= (N/r)[ b^2(NP^2+N^2P+NP)/N^3+C M P^2/N^3 ]=O(1). (9)

As before, the three covariance pairings account for NP^2+N^2P+NP
terms, while every joint fourth cumulant has absolute value at most
CM/N^2 and there are N^2P^2 summands in the fourth trace.
The proof uses no rotation invariance in (8) or (9).

Along each subsequence chosen in Section 2, (9) ensures that the
deterministic limiting singular law has exactly the common second
moment, rather than a smaller one due to lost mass at infinity.
Weak convergence in probability and convergence of second moments
then imply W2 convergence in probability to the same deterministic
subsequential law. This characterization can be seen directly by
matching one-dimensional quantiles: weak convergence gives convergence
of truncated quantiles, and second-moment tail control gives the
remaining L^2 convergence.

The convergence also holds in mean square Wasserstein distance.
Indeed Jensen gives

    E T_N^2 <= E A_11^4
       =3b^2+(M/N^2)(q_U q_V-3)=O(1).

Thus the empirical singular second moments have bounded second
moments. For any selected deterministic limit mu,

    W2(mu_A,mu)^2 <= 2 integral x^2 dmu_A+2 integral x^2 dmu,

so these squared distances are uniformly integrable. The same holds
for B, proving along the selected subsequence that

    E W2(mu_A,mu_B)^2 ->0.                             (10)

If (10) failed along the full sequence, a subsequence with distances
bounded away from zero would admit a further subsequence constructed
in Sections 2-3 on which they tend to zero, a contradiction. Therefore
(10) holds on the full sequence. Independent draws of the two
singular-value vectors are sufficient; no special correlation is needed.

## 4. Haar mixing and entropy continuity finish the proof

Let tilde A be the bi-orthogonal Haar mixture of A. Coupling its
singular values to those of B in sorted order and using the same Haar
left/right matrices gives

    e_N^2=E||tilde A-B||_F^2/(NP)
         =(r/P) E W2(mu_A,mu_B)^2 ->0.                  (11)

The reference B is bi-orthogonally invariant, including when M<r and
there is a macroscopic zero singular-value mass. Such zeros are already
included in the empirical measures and cause no problem in the
coupling. In particular no density or logarithmic singular-value
integrability assumption is being imposed.

Haar-mixture concavity and the Gaussian-smoothed entropy bound in
orbit_comparison.md give the finite-size inequality

    [I(A;sqrt(s)A+G)-I(B;sqrt(s)B+G)]/(NP) <= sqrt(s)e_N.

Equation (11) proves (1) for every fixed positive SNR. This concludes
the mutual-information comparison, subject to independent audit of
the proof.

## MMSE scope

If the Gaussian reference normalized MI converges to a finite i_G(s)
on (0,infinity), the abstract orbit lemma applies for all these aspect
ratios. It gives limsup normalized MMSE_A(s)<=2 i'_{G,-}(s), and
comparison with the reference MMSE at every differentiability point
of i_G, with at most a countable exceptional set. Verifying an
all-SNR differentiability theorem and its hypotheses is still unpaid.
The reference MI existence hypothesis is not used anywhere in (1).

Checks that could fail: rank and norm of the entry derivative D;
the factor 12 in (2) and 1/6 in Taylor's remainder; the different
column lengths P and N in the two replacement stages; concentration
for random rather than expected empirical laws; and uniform
integrability before taking expected W2. [Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Let $A\in M_N(\mathbb C)$, and for any eigenvalue $\lambda\in\mathbb C$ define the corresponding eigenspace as being the vector space formed by the corresponding eigenvectors:
$$E_\lambda=\left\{v\in\mathbb C^N\Big|Av=\lambda v\right\}$$
These eigenspaces $E_\lambda$ are then in a direct sum position, in the sense that given vectors $v_1\in E_{\lambda_1},\ldots,v_k\in E_{\lambda_k}$ corresponding to different eigenvalues $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_k$, we have:
$$\sum_ic_iv_i=0\implies c_i=0$$
In particular, we have $\sum_\lambda\dim(E_\lambda)\leq N$, with the sum being over all the eigenvalues, and our matrix is diagonalizable precisely when we have equality.

[Theorem 16 of arXiv:2609.02193, 'State-law dynamics of McKean-Vlasov stochastic reaction-diffusion equations on $\mathbb R^'] For every $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$, the map
	\begin{align}
		\Phi^\epsilon(t,\omega)(x,\mu)
		=
		\big(
		\varphi^\epsilon_H(t,\omega,x,\mu),
		\varphi^\epsilon_P(t)\mu
		\big),
		\qquad (x,\mu)\in H\times P,
	\end{align}
	defines a continuous random dynamical system on $H\times P$ over
	$(\Omega_0,\mathcal F,\mathbb P,\{\theta_t\}_{t\in\mathbb R})$. In particular,
	\begin{align*}
		\Phi^\epsilon(0,\omega)
		=\operatorname{id}_{H\times P},
	\end{align*}
	and, for all $s,t\geq0$ and $\omega\in\Omega_0$,
	\begin{align}
		\Phi^\epsilon(t+s,\omega)
		=\Phi^\epsilon(t,\theta_s\omega)
		\circ\Phi^\epsilon(s,\omega).
	\end{align}
	Moreover, $(x,\mu)\mapsto\Phi^\epsilon(t,\omega)(x,\mu)$ is continuous on $H\times P$ for every $t\geq0$ and $\omega\in\Omega_0$.

Let $\{{\bf B}_{\varphi(E)}\}_{\varphi \in {\mathcal T}^k_n}$ be a multi-indexed sequence of deterministic matrices of the same dimension. Then for $d\leq k(k-1)$ and $1 \leq t \leq \infty$,
    $$
    {\mathbb E} \norm{\sum_{\varphi \in {\mathcal T}_n^k} {\bf B}_{\varphi(E)} \cdot \prod_{(i,j) \in E} Z_{\varphi(i), \varphi(j)}}_{2t} \leq k^k \cdot {\mathbb E} \norm{\sum_{\varphi \in {\mathcal T}_n^k}{\bf B}_{\varphi(E)} \cdot Z_{\varphi(i_1), \varphi(j_1)}^{(1)}\cdots Z_{\varphi(i_d), \varphi(j_d)}^{(d)}}_{2t}, $$
    where  ${\bf z}^{(1)}, \ldots, {\bf z}^{(d)}$ denote $d$ independent copies of ${\bf z}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem 1 of arXiv:2606.11774, 'Martingale Solutions to a Stochastic Keller-Segel System with nonlocal Source and Super-li'] Let $p = \frac{2d}{d-2}$, $1 \leq r < q < p$ and $\frac{q}{r} < \frac{2}{r} + 1 - \frac{2}{p}$, then for $v\in H^1(\mathcal{O}) \cap L^r(\mathcal{O})$, it holds
\[
\|v\|_{L^q(\mathcal{O})}^q \leq C(d)\left( C_0^{-\frac{\lambda q}{2 - \lambda q}} + C_1^{-\frac{\lambda q}{2 - \lambda q}} \right) \|v\|_{L^r(\mathcal{O})}^\zeta + C_0 \|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\mathcal{O})}^2 + C_1 \|v\|_{L^2(\mathcal{O})}^2, \quad d \geq 3.
\]
Here, $C$ is a constant relying on $d$, and $C_0, C_1 > 0$ are arbitrary constants,
\[
\lambda = \frac{\frac{1}{r} - \frac{1}{q}}{\frac{1}{r} - \frac{1}{p}}\in(0,1), \quad \text{and} \quad \zeta = \frac{2-\frac{2q}{p}}{\frac{2 - q}{r} - \frac{2}{p} + 1}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 1 of arXiv:2606.11774

[Lemma quantitative-gaussian-approximation of arXiv:2609.03858, 'High-Dimensional Learning Dynamics of \\ Attention-Indexed Models'] Fix constants \(C_*,R_*<\infty\). Consider deterministic matrices
\(M_k\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}\) satisfying $\max_k\|M_k\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le C_*$ and $\max_k\frac1{\sqrt d}|{\rm Tr}(M_k)|\le R_*$. Let $G_{ijk}^{(d)}=\frac1{\sqrt d}x_i^TM_kx_j$, where \(x\sim\mathcal N(0,\mathcal C\otimes I_d)\), and let \(G_{\mathrm G}^{(d)}\) be a Gaussian tensor having the same mean and covariance as \(G^{(d)}\).

Then for every \(f\in C^3(\mathbb R^{L\times L\times K})\) whose derivatives up to third order have at most polynomial growth, there exists a constant $C=C(C_*,R_*,\mathcal C,K,L,f)$ independent of \(d\) and of the matrices \(M_k\), such that
\begin{equation}
\left|\mathbb E f(G^{(d)})-\mathbb E f(G_{\mathrm G}^{(d)})\right|\le\frac{C}{\sqrt d}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma quantitative-gaussian-approximation of arXiv:2609.03858

In a finite graph with inherited positive edge weights, give each simple n-edge path starting at a probability proportional to its product weight, with terminal vertex free, and assume positive total weight C_n(G;a). Define C_m(H;v) as the total weight of simple m-edge paths from v in H, with C_0=1 for a retained vertex. At a realized k-edge prefix eta, delete all its visited vertices except its tip to get G_eta. For a forbidden vertex or edge set A excluding a, the conditional avoidance probability is zero if the prefix hit A, and otherwise C_(n-k)(G_eta minus A;tip)/C_(n-k)(G_eta;tip). The denominator is positive on every realized prefix; at k=n use the avoidance indicator. Replacing C_(n-k) by an all-length partition sum changes the model.

STATUS: independently checked proof (exact-version PASS by urn:mb-agent:d6ca7a10ae76247b), fixed-order owner-work draft; literature novelty not established. For critical Gaussian width-n ReLU single-input normalized variance M_nL, all fixed-order cumulants admit a computable analytic expansion in z=1/n with explicit uniform depth remainders. Define exact one-step moment polynomials m_j(z), A=max_j<=k sum_r>=1 |[z^r]m_j|, R=min(1,1/(2A)), D=2*k*A, and n>=2/R. Let F_kr(t)=[z^r]sum_partition w_pi*exp(t*sum_blocks log(m_|B|(z))/z), extended at z=0. For every P>=0 and t=L/n<=c, the width-expansion error is <=2*W_k*t*D*exp(c*D)*(n*R)^(-P-1). Expanding those coefficients through t^m yields a double remainder <=2*W_k*exp(c*D)*(t*D*(n*R)^(-P-1)+(D*t)^(m+1)/(m+1)!). Both bounds are uniform over integer 0<=L<=cn. Assumptions: Fixed k>=2,P,m,c; independent Gaussian critical zero-bias ReLU scalar multipliers; moments defined even at extinction. Explicit coefficients, analytic log branch, finite partition weights and W_k are specified in proof. Output-cumulant version multiplies by (2k-1)!!q0^k. Complete definitions: Pi_j is the set of partitions of [j], w_pi=(-1)^(|pi|-1)(|pi|-1)!, W_k=sum_pi |w_pi|, mu_j=2^(j-1)(2j-1)!!. The polynomial m_j(z)=sum_pi_in_Pi_j z^(j-|pi|)*prod_h=0_to_|pi|-1(1-h*z)*prod_B_in_pi mu_|B|. The analytic quotient log(m_j(z))/z has value 5*j*(j-1)/2 at zero. The double Taylor polynomial uses d_rs=[z^r](1/s!)*sum_pi w_pi*(sum_B log(m_|B|(z))/z)^s, summed for r<=P,s<=m. Each constant depends only on fixed k,c; no claim uniform in cumulant order or about tanh.
Fixed k>=2,P,m,c; independent Gaussian critical zero-bias ReLU scalar multipliers; moments defined even at extinction. Explicit coefficients, analytic log branch, finite partition weights and W_k are specified in proof. Output-cumulant version multiplies by (2k-1)!!q0^k.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:8c1f8f164588ecc9a74ddb8cc789bab3f28780dcfaebd71f32886bf673ca5987","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/8c/8c1f8f164588ecc9a74ddb8cc789bab3f28780dcfaebd71f32886bf673ca5987.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:119ecb8fe3c8d07319122c7e554ceeb9ab679c0efb1b4fa92796c07f5682ec90","bundle_entry_key":"relu-cumulant-uniform-width","bundle_id":"population.t244-explicit-uniform-cumulant-remainders-007","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability; random neural networks; cumulant expansions","draft":"w691/bundle_007.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.randomnetworks:critical-gaussian-relu-cumulants-all-order-uniform-width-remainder","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C019: finite-width corrections and explicit uniform double remainders

Version 1, Target 2, proof (unaudited). This starts from the settled scalar ReLU product and supplies all-order remainder bounds. It does not re-claim the scalar product/lognormal limit as new. All constants below depend only on the fixed cumulant order k and depth-ratio bound c, not on L or n.

Let X_n=(1/n)sum_(i=1)^n Z_i with Z_i=2(g_i)_+^2, iid standard Gaussian g_i. Let M_(n,L)=prod_(ell=1)^L X_(n,ell), with independent multipliers, and t=L/n. This is the normalized scalar variance after L critical Gaussian ReLU transitions, including its extinction atom; no logarithm of the random multiplier is taken. Fix k>=2 and 0<=L<=cn.

## Exact moment polynomials and computable constants

Write mu_j=2^(j-1)(2j-1)!! for j>=1. Expanding a power of the sample mean according to coincidences of its coordinate indices gives the exact polynomial, with z=1/n,

    m_j(z)=E X_n^j
      = sum_(pi in Pi_j) z^(j-|pi|)
          prod_(h=0)^(|pi|-1)(1-hz) prod_(B in pi) mu_|B|
      = 1+sum_(r=1)^(j-1) p_(j,r) z^r.                (2)

Falling factorials make (2) valid even when n<j. In particular p_(j,1)=5j(j-1)/2=a_j. For example

    m_2=1+5z,
    m_3=1+15z+44z^2,
    m_4=1+30z+251z^2+558z^3.

Define A=max_(1<=j<=k) sum_(r>=1)|p_(j,r)|, R=min(1,1/(2A)), and D=2kA. Here A>=5, so A,R,D are positive explicit rational numbers. Take n>=2/R. For complex |z|<=R,

    |m_j(z)-1|<=A|z|<=1/2.

Thus the branch h_j(z)=log(m_j(z))/z, extended by h_j(0)=a_j, is analytic on a neighborhood of this closed disk, with |h_j(z)|<=2A. This is a logarithm of a nonzero analytic moment polynomial, not a random logarithm. The bound follows from |log(1+w)|<=|w|/(1-|w|).

## Analytic continuation and the width expansion

Use w_pi,W_k from C018 and define

    F_k(t,z)=sum_(pi in Pi_k) w_pi exp(t sum_(B in pi) h_|B|(z)).

For integer L=nt and z=1/n this equals kappa_k(M_(n,L)) exactly, since exp(t h_j(1/n))=m_j(1/n)^L. At z=0 it equals C018's limiting cumulant. Set

    F_(k,r)(t)=[z^r] F_k(t,z), r>=0.

These coefficients are explicit: expand each finite polynomial (2), then its formal log to order r+1, and the displayed exponential to order r. Each coefficient is a finite sum of polynomials in t times exp(H_pi t).

Since sum_pi w_pi=0 for k>=2 and |sum_B h_|B||<=D,

    sup_(|z|<=R) |F_k(t,z)| <= W_k t D exp(cD), 0<=t<=c.

Cauchy's coefficient bound and 1/(nR)<=1/2 imply, for every integer P>=0,

    |kappa_k(M_(n,L))-sum_(r=0)^P n^-r F_(k,r)(t)|
       <= 2 W_k t D exp(cD) (nR)^-(P+1).              (3)

This is an all-order width expansion with an explicit error uniform over the entire stated depth range, including L=0 and L fixed. At P=0 it is an explicit O(t/n) error when replacing the exact cumulant by its limiting-law value. No CLT, unbounded random logarithm, or independence across blocks of a partition is presumed; the product moments follow from independent layers.

## Mixed Taylor remainder in t and 1/n

Define computable rational coefficients

    d_(r,s)=[z^r] (1/s!)sum_pi w_pi (sum_B h_|B|(z))^s.

For every P,m>=0,

    |kappa_k(M_(n,L))
          -sum_(r=0)^P sum_(s=0)^m d_(r,s) n^-r t^s|
       <= 2 W_k exp(cD) [t D (nR)^-(P+1)
                              +(D t)^(m+1)/(m+1)!]. (4)

Indeed the (m+1)st t-derivative of F_k on the disk has magnitude at most W_k D^(m+1)exp(cD). Cauchy's bound on its z coefficients gives the t-Taylor remainder of F_(k,r) at most R^-r W_k exp(cD)(D t)^(m+1)/(m+1)!. Summing r<=P with ratio 1/(nR)<=1/2 bounds that part by twice the indicated expression. Add (3). Differentiation under a coefficient integral is valid here because the partition sum is finite and jointly analytic. At r=0, d_(0,s)=A_(k,s) of C018. The same Gaussian-mixture factor (2k-1)!! q0^k gives (3)-(4) for final-preactivation cumulants of order 2k.

## Why a finite-width correction cannot simply be discarded

For k=3, the exact cumulant is m_3(1/n)^L-3m_2(1/n)^L+2. At fixed L its leading term is

    (75L^2-31L)/n^2.

The limiting-law expansion starts at 75t^2. Along L=1, the discrepancy is -31t^2, of the same t order; it cannot be absorbed in an O(t^3) remainder uniform over 1<=L<=cn. This does not contradict C018, which concerns the limiting law, or the repaired dossier target. It explains why (3)-(4) retain width corrections when applied to a finite network. Bounds uniform over fixed k are not bounds uniform over every cumulant order.

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2607.27082, '2607.27082'] Assume $0<\E[\eta_0]<\infty$. Let $(D^\rightarrow,D^\leftarrow,D^*)$ have the same distribution as
$(D_{x,i}^{\rightarrow},D_{x,i}^\leftarrow,D_{x,i}^{*})$. Then the following assertions hold.

\begin{itemize}
  \item[(i)] If
  \[
    \limsup_{n\to\infty} n\,\PP(D^*\ge n)
    \;<\;\frac{1}{2\E[\eta_0]},
  \]
  then $\mathrm{FM}(\mathbb{Z},\pi,\eta,S)$ dies out almost surely.

  \item[(ii)] If
  \[
    \liminf_{n\to\infty} n\,\PP(D^\rightarrow\ge n)
    \;>\;\frac{1}{\E[\eta_0]},
  \]
  then $\mathrm{FM}(\mathbb{Z},\pi,\eta,S)$ survives with positive probability.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2607.27082

body:
[Lem f<g:connected of arXiv:2604.12963, 'Shocks, instability, and the twenty networks\\ of infinite geodesics in the Directed Lands'] Let $f,g:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be continuous functions such that $f(t)\le g(t)$ for all $t\in\mathbb{R}$.
Suppose that for some $s\in\mathbb{R}$, $f(s)<g(s)$.
Define $t_1 = \sup\{t<s : f(t)=g(t)\}$ and $t_2 = \inf\{t>s : f(t)=g(t)\}$,
with the conventions that $\sup\varnothing = -\infty$ 
and $\inf\varnothing = +\infty$.
\begin{enumerate} [label={\rm(\alph*)}, ref={\rm\alph*}] \itemsep=1pt 
\item The set $U = \{(x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^2 : f(t) < x < g(t),\ t_1 < t < t_2\}$
is connected. 
\item Let $\Gamma_f=\{(f(t),t):t\in\mathbb{R}\}$ and $\Gamma_g=\{(g(t),t):t\in\mathbb{R}\}$. Let $V$ be any open subset of $\mathbb{R}^2\setminus(\Gamma_f\cup\Gamma_g)$ that contains $U$ {\rm(}possibly $V=U${\rm)}. Then $U$ is a connected component of $V$.
\end{enumerate}

body:
Let f : {-1,1}^n -> {0,1} be a Boolean function on the uniform product measure, and define the influence of coordinate i as Inf_i(f) = P( f(X) != f(X^{(i)}) ) where X^{(i)} flips the i-th coordinate. Then there is a universal constant c > 0 with max_{i <= n} Inf_i(f) >= c Var(f) log n / n, where Var(f) = p(1-p) with p = E[f]. This does not bound the TOTAL influence by c Var(f) log n: a dictator f(x) = (1 + x_1)/2 has total influence 1 and Var(f) = 1/4 for every n. The total-influence form of the theorem is sum_i Inf_i(f) >= c' Var(f) log(1/max_i Inf_i(f)) for nonconstant f, with c' > 0 universal, and the maximum bound follows from it. The bound is SHARP up to the constant: the tribes function, a read-once DNF on blocks of size about log_2 n - log_2 log_2 n, is balanced and has all influences of order log n / n. The theorem is about the uniform measure on the cube; the analogous statement for p-biased measures carries an extra factor and is the Friedgut-Kalai sharp-threshold machinery. Note what it does NOT say: it does not bound the influence of any PARTICULAR coordinate, only the maximum, and it says nothing when Var(f) is 0, that is when f is constant. [Kahn, Kalai and Linial (1988); see O'Donnell, Analysis of Boolean Functions, Chapter 9]

[Lem 9 of arXiv:2604.03777, 'Equilibrium fluctuations for a multi-species particle system with long jumps'] Let $\gamma >0$ and assume that $D_1$, $D_2$, $\lambda$ and $v$ are chosen in such a way that \eqref{defD2pm}, \eqref{deflambda} and \eqref{vsdif} are satisfied.
\begin{itemize}
    \item 
If $H \in \mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R})$ and either Hypothesis \ref{hyplin} or Hypothesis \ref{hypnonlin} holds, the sequences $\big\{ \big( \mathcal{Z}_t^{n,+} (H) \; \big)_{0 \leq t \leq T}: \; n \in \mathbb{N}_+\big\}$ and $\big\{ \big( \mathcal{Z}_t^{n,-} (H) \; \big)_{0 \leq t \leq T}: \; n \in \mathbb{N}_+\big\}$ are tight with respect to the Skorohod topology of $\mathcal{D}([0, T], \mathbb{R})$.
\item 
If $H \in C_c^2 (\mathbb{R})$ and Hypothesis \ref{hypnonlin} holds, then
\begin{equation} 	
\forall n \in \mathbb{N}_+, \; \forall 0 \leq s \leq t \leq T, \quad	  \mathbb{E}_{\nu_{\rho}} \big[ \big\{ \mathcal{Z}_t^{n} (H) - \mathcal{Z}_s^{n} (H) \big\}^{2} \big] 
	\leq   C(H )  (t-s).	  
\end{equation}
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Assuming NP is not contained in P/poly, there exists an efficiently computable normalizable weighted language p_tilde that is not ELNCP (efficiently locally normalizable with compact parameters). In the authors' construction, choose an efficiently decodable prefix-free formula encoding enc(phi). Put L={enc(phi)a: a is a satisfying assignment of phi}, requiring that phi mentions variables1,...,j and that a has length j. Set p_tilde(x)=3^(-|x|-1) for x in L and zero otherwise. Membership and these rational weights are polynomial-time computable. Its total weight Z is positive and at most1. Nevertheless exact computation of its actual next-symbol conditionals cannot be implemented with polynomial runtime and polynomial-size nonuniform parameters for all prefix-length bounds unless NP is contained in P/poly. Normalizable unnormalized weights are the claim; the result does not assert polynomial-time computation of their exact normalized joint probabilities.
Complexity assumption NP is not a subset of P/poly; the assumption is stronger than merely P!=NP.
Finite binary alphabet and finite strings of unbounded length; exact rational output for the constructed weights.
ELNCP is efficient local normalization with compact parameters: a fixed polynomial-time scheme with polynomial-size nonuniform advice for each prefix-length bound returns the actual next-symbol and termination conditional probabilities at positive-mass prefixes up to that bound.
Exact representability and conditional evaluation are the subject; no assertion about approximation in TV or KL follows from this theorem alone.

      (-\triangle)^{\frac{s-t}{2}}\circ(-\triangle)^{\frac{t}{2}}=\flap

Own-work draft: proof (unaudited), kind route-failure, Target1. Independent correctness and novelty review pending. This obstructs the current comparison, not epochwise double descent.

# C024 v2: fixed-radius thickening fails the vanishing initial-function comparison
Status: proof (unaudited). Kind: route-failure. Target:1.
General T267 OPEN. This is a precise obstruction to one proof route, not a
counterexample to nonlinear epochwise double descent. Novelty unestablished.

1. Statement
Let Z have ANY initialization-independent probability law on unit vectors in R^3,
and let V be uniform on the unit three-dimensional ball, independent of Z.
Fix 0<nu<=1, 0<tau<=1/4 and any integer m>=1. Independently initialize
 f_m(x;0)=m^(-1/2)sum_(j=1)^m a_j ReLU(W_j.x),
where W_j are iid N(0,I_3), a_j are iid uniform {-nu,nu}, and all are independent.
The SAME network is evaluated at Z+tau V and Z. Conditional on its initialization
put Y_m=E_(Z,V)|f_m(Z+tau V;0)-f_m(Z;0)|^2.
Define the strictly positive Gaussian-box probability
 p=P(1<=G_0<=2, |G_1|<=1, |G_2|<=1)
  =(Phi(2)-Phi(1))*(2Phi(1)-1)^2, for independent standard normals G_i.
Then, uniformly in m and the law of Z,
 E_init Y_m >=nu^2 tau^2 p/5,
 E_init Y_m^2 <=3nu^4 tau^4,
 P_init(Y_m>=nu^2 tau^2 p/10)>=p^2/300.                 (1)
In particular, at a FIXED positive tau the coupled initial-function discrepancy
cannot vanish in probability as width increases, even though initializations
are shared exactly. No training, Gram approximation or kernel-width limit is
needed for this conclusion.

2. Gaussian active-region lower bound
Fix a unit z and choose orthonormal coordinates with first axis z. Rotational
invariance of N(0,I_3) gives the same probability p to
 A_z={1<=W.z<=2, absolute values of the two orthogonal coordinates <=1}.
On this event ||W||<=sqrt(6). For EVERY ||v||<=1 and tau<=1/4,
 W.z>=1 and W.(z+tau v)>=1-tau sqrt(6)>0,
since 6/16<1. Thus both ReLUs are active and their difference is EXACTLY
 tau W.v. Uniform-ball covariance is E VV^T=I_3/5: its radial density is
3r^2 on [0,1], so E||V||^2=3/5, and symmetry divides this equally among axes.
Consequently
 E_(W,V)[ReLU(W.(z+tau V))-ReLU(W.z)]^2
 >=tau^2 E_W[1_(A_z)||W||^2/5]>=tau^2 p/5.            (2)
The integrand is nonnegative, so restriction to A_z is legitimate. This
bound is uniform in z; the orthonormal coordinates need not be chosen jointly
measurably because the pointwise bound is already independent of z.

3. Independent centered heads and the second moment
For fixed z,v put delta_j=ReLU(W_j.(z+tau v))-ReLU(W_j.z), T_j=a_j delta_j.
The T_j are independent centered variables; centering follows from the
independent head sign, without requiring delta_j itself to be centered.
Therefore
 E_init |m^(-1/2)sum_j T_j|^2=nu^2 E_W delta_1^2.
Integrate over (Z,V) and apply (2), using Tonelli, to obtain the first
inequality in (1). There is no 1/m decay in this initial output fluctuation:
the summation has scale 1/sqrt(m), whereas a kernel sample mean has scale 1/m.
The conclusion does not apply to paired antithetic initialization with
identical hidden weights and opposite heads; that violates the iid hypothesis
and can make the initial function identically zero.

4. Fourth moment and a probability lower bound
ReLU is 1-Lipschitz, hence |delta_j|<=tau |W_j.v|. For fixed z,v, write
mu_2=E T_1^2 and mu_4=E T_1^4. Gaussian second and fourth moments give
 mu_2<=nu^2 tau^2 ||v||^2,
 mu_4<=3nu^4 tau^4 ||v||^4.
These Gaussian moments follow by rotating v to a coordinate axis and using
E G^2=1, E G^4=3 (integration by parts for the standard normal density).
In the expansion of E(sum_j T_j)^4, a term survives only if every index
occurs an even number of times. There are m all-equal terms and
6*binom(m,2) two-pair terms. Thus exactly
 E_init |m^(-1/2)sum_j T_j|^4
 =mu_4/m+3(1-1/m)mu_2^2
 <=3nu^4 tau^4 ||v||^4<=3nu^4 tau^4.                 (3)
Jensen on the (Z,V) probability space gives Y_m^2<=E_(Z,V)|D_m(Z,V)|^4,
where D_m is the same initial prediction difference. Integrating (3) proves
the second inequality in (1). All moments are finite by the displayed bounds.

For completeness, the one-sided moment step does not assume concentration.
Set a=nu^2 tau^2 p/5, b=3nu^4 tau^4 and E={Y_m>=a/2}. Then
 E Y_m<=a/2+E[Y_m 1_E]<=a/2+sqrt(b P(E))
by splitting at a/2 and applying Cauchy-Schwarz. Since E Y_m>=a,
P(E)>=a^2/(4b)=p^2/300. This is precisely the last inequality in (1).
It is a probability lower bound, not a conclusion from mean error alone.

5. Consequence for the C022/C023 transfer route
In those constructions Z is uniform on four unit centers. At initialization,
the coupled center-to-ball population L2 error is sqrt(Y_m). It is part of
D_m(T)=max_(0<=k<=T)||F_ball,k(Z+tau V)-F_center,k(Z)||_2,
so D_m(T)>=sqrt(Y_m) for every horizon T, regardless of subsequent updates.
The bound (1) therefore holds for an initial discrepancy inside exactly the
same coupling used there, for every e, every width, and every fixed tau>0.
Directly replacing tau=e^20 by a positive constant cannot retain the
vanishing prediction comparison D_m(T)=o_P(1), let alone o_P(e^5).
More generally, with fixed nu>0 and tau=tau_e<=1/4, any argument that requires
D_m(T)=o_P(e^5) in width-before-scale limits must have tau_e=o(e^5): if not,
a subsequence has tau_e/e^5 bounded below, and (1) gives a fixed positive
probability of D_m(T)/e^5 being bounded away from zero. This is only a
necessary condition for THAT prediction-error route; C022's e^20 radius
satisfies it. It says nothing about optimal radius exponents.

This does NOT prove that actual population-risk differences cannot cancel,
that no alternative nonshrinking-geometry proof exists, or that double descent
fails for fixed-radius input laws. A proof for such laws must analyze their
nonconstant initial function and population dynamics directly, or use an
alternative comparison. The obstruction identifies why the present center
comparison cannot simply be thickened.

6. Finite checks and audit scope
The accompanying exact Fraction script enumerates independent head signs
for several deterministic increment vectors and widths1 through8. It checks
second and fourth moment expansions and detects a deliberately omitted
mixed fourth-moment term. Its paired-head negative control yields zero
initial difference where the independent-head computation is positive.
These checks concern the finite combinatorial step only; they are not an
independent audit of the Gaussian, population or limiting arguments. No Lean
certificate or literature-priority claim is made. Reviewer PASS is pending.

Brain use: q022 returned the standard second-moment technique; its warning
against drawing a probability conclusion from a mean alone is addressed in
Section4. The population Jensen step assumes no independence across inputs.
Dimension3; arbitrary initialization-independent law of unit centers Z.
Independent uniform unit-ball perturbation V; 0<tau<=1/4, 0<nu<=1, integer width m>=1.
Iid Gaussian hidden weights, iid independent symmetric +/-nu readouts; shared initialization at both input locations.

[Lemma 15 (Order preservation and monotonicity of \(\mathcal K\)) of arXiv:2604.13149, 'The Distributional Tail of Worst--Case Quickselect'] Let \(G,H:\R\to[0,1]\) be measurable functions.

\begin{enumerate}
\item If \(G\le H\) pointwise on \(\R\), then
\[
\mathcal K G\le \mathcal K H
\qquad\text{pointwise on }\R.
\]

\item If \(G\) is nondecreasing on \(\R\), then \(\mathcal K G\) is also nondecreasing on \(\R\).
\end{enumerate}

[Theorem 31 (Decoupling inequality) of arXiv:2608.05931, 'Effective Lagrangian regularity and the uniqueness threshold for random H\"older velocity '] There exists a universal constant $C>0$ such that for any sequence of real-valued random variables $A_i$ adapted to a filtration $\mathcal{F}_i$, there exists (on perhaps a larger probability space) a sequence of real-valued random variables $B_i$ and a sigma algebra $\mathcal{G}$ such that $B_i$ are conditionally independent given $\mathcal{G}$, and for all $i \geq 1$, 
    \[\mathrm{Law}\big(B_i \mid \mathcal{G}\big) = \mathrm{Law}\big(A_i \mid \mathcal{F}_{i-1}\big)\]
    and such that for all $p \geq 1, n \geq 1$
    \[\Big\|\sum_{i=1}^n A_i \Big\|_{L^p_\omega} \leq C \Big\|\sum_{i=1}^n B_i \Big\|_{L^p_\omega}.\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma rand_series_ample of arXiv:2412.07690, 'A law of large numbers concerning the distribution of critical points of random Fourier se'] Suppose that $E\to M$ is a smooth real vector bundle over the compact smooth manifold $M$. Fix a smooth  Riemann metric $g$ on $M$,  a smooth metric $h$ on $E$ and a smooth connection  on $E$ compatible with $h$. Let $k\in {{\mathbb N}}$ and suppose that $(\phi_n)_{n\in {{\mathbb N}}}$ is a sequence  of $C^k$ sections of $E$ that span  a dense subset of $C^k(E)$. Set
 \[
 U_\nu:=\spa\big\{\, \phi_1,\dotsc,\phi_\nu\,\big\}
 \]
 Then there   exists  $\nu_0>0$ such that  $\forall \nu\geq \nu_0$ the following hold.
 
 \begin{enumerate}
 
 \item  For any $t\in M$ and any $\nu \geq \nu_0$ the map
 \[
 U_\nu\ni u\mapsto J_1(u)_t\in J_1(E_t)
 \]
 is onto. Above, $J_1(u)_t$ is the $1$-jet of $u$ at $t$, $J_1(u)_t=u(t)\oplus \nabla u (t)\in E_t\oplus T^*_tM\otimes E_t$.
 
 \item  For any ${\underline{t}} \in M^2\setminus \Delta$   the map
 \[
 U_\nu\ni u\mapsto u({\underline{t}})\in E_{\underline{t}}
 \]
 is onto.
 \end{enumerate}

 w(c)q^3+O_c(q^2).

The asymptotic is as $q\to\infty$.

body:
[Prop thm:exact-identity of arXiv:2608.30847, 'An Almgren-type formula for planar $p$-harmonic functions'] Let $u$ be a nonconstant planar $p$-harmonic function in $B_R(x_0)$, and suppose that $u$ is not locally constant at $x_0$.  For all sufficiently small admissible radii, define
\begin{equation}
      \Theta(r)  =  \frac{K(r)}{H(r)}  -  \frac{(p-2)(N_*(r)-1)}{r}.
\end{equation}
Then
$$
  N_*'(r)+N_*(r)\Theta(r)
  =
  \frac{pr}{H(r)}
  \int_{\partial B_r(x_0)}
  A\left(\partial_\nu u-\frac{N_*(r)}{r}v\right)^2\,dS.
$$
In particular,
$$
  N_*'(r)+N_*(r)\Theta(r)\ge0.
$$

Matching this mean to log(n) therefore suggests an apparent positive shift, but it does not derive a connectivity threshold: isolated-vertex probabilities depend on the far lower tail of D, not its mean. An actual sharp-window proof must analyze the relevant order-statistic large deviation and then exclude nontrivial small components. Separately, weak convergence at fixed scaled thresholds gives no estimate at a threshold diverging like sqrt(k). body:
[Lem Etails of arXiv:2604.07183, 'Stopping on the last success with unknown odds: asymptotic minimax optimality of the plug-'] Fix $p_0\in(0,1)$ and~$\delta_0>0$. With~$h_n:=\lceil \tfrac n2\rceil+1$, let

$$
E_n^{\delta_0}(p)
:=
\bigg\{\max_{h_n\leq t\leq n}|\hat p_t-p|\le \delta_0\bigg\}
,
$$

and, with~$r_t:=1/(n-t+1)$ and~$M_0

=\lceil 1/p_0\rceil-1$, let

$$
H_t
:=
\Big\{\big|\hat p_{t-1}-r_t\big|\leq \frac{1}{t}\Big\}
\quad
\textrm{ for }
t\in T_n:=\{n-M_0,\dots,n-1\}
.
$$

Then, there exist positive constants $C_1(\delta_0),c_1(\delta_0),C_2(p_0)$, and $c_2(p_0)$ such that
$$
\mathbb P_p[(E_n^{\delta_0}(p))^c]
\le
C_1(\delta_0)e^{-c_1(\delta_0)n}
\quad
\textrm{ and }
\quad
\mathbb P_p[H_t]
\le
C_2(p_0) e^{-c_2(p_0)n(p-r_t)^2}
$$
for all $p\in[p_0,1)$, all $n\ge 2(M_0+1)$, and all~$t\in T_n$.

[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2605.02771, 'Universality in Deep Neural Networks:\\ An approach via the Lindeberg exchange principle'] Let \(\sigma\in C_b^{3\cdot 2^{L-1}}(\R)\), and consider a DNN of depth \(L\) with weights as in \textbf{Assumption \ref{assum:weights}} and zero biases. Let \(\Zcal^{(L+1)}(x)\) be the zero-bias Gaussian process from \textbf{Theorem \ref{thm:qualitative_thm}}, and assume that 
    \(K^{(\ell)}(x)\) is invertible for \(\ell=1,\ldots,n_{L+1}\). Then
    \[
         \Wcal_2\bigl(z^{(L+1)}(x),\Zcal^{(L+1)}(x)\bigr)
         \leq C\biggl(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n_L}}+\Bigl( \sum_{k=1}^{L-1}\frac{1}{\sqrt{n_k}} \Bigr)^{1/4}\biggr),
    \]
    for some constant \(C= C(L,n_{L+1},\sigma)\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

$P_{\boldsymbol{x}_N}(\lambda)-t$. Then $\boldsymbol{y}_N^t(\bs{x}_N)  \in \mathcal{A}_N(-t)$ and
the map $ \boldsymbol{y}_N^t: \mathcal{A}_N(t) \to \mathcal{A}_N(-t)$ is a diffeomorphism onto.

[Thm 35 of arXiv:2609.00723, 'An integral Hyodo--Kato isomorphism'] Let $\lSmCarpr_{\OK}$ be the full subcategory of proper objects in
$\lSmCar_{\OK}$, and let $m\geq0$ satisfy $e\leq p^m$. For
$\fX\in\lSmCarpr_{\OK}$, put
\[
\sX:=\fX\times_{\OKpi}\uk^0.
\] 
Then the functor
\[
R\Gamma_{\dR}^{\eta^m}(-/\OKpi)\colon
(\lSmCarpr_{\OK})^{\rm op}\longrightarrow\mathcal D(\OK)^\wedge_p
\]
is naturally equivalent to the composite
\[
(\lSmCarpr_{\OK})^{\rm op}
\xrightarrow{\ \fX\mapsto R\Gamma_{\rm crys}(\sX/W^0)\ }
D^{\phi,N}(W)
\xrightarrow{\ -\widehat\otimes^{\mathbb L}_{W,\phi^m}\OK\ }
\mathcal D(\OK)^\wedge_p.
\]
Here the $(\phi,N)$-structure on crystalline cohomology is the one of
Construction~\ref{ConstructionMonodromy}.

body:
[Definition def:same-ribbon-type of arXiv:2608.15923, 'Universality of two-dimensional Markovian holonomy fields'] Two finite regular based loop families
\[
 L=(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_r),
 \qquad
 L'=(\ell'_1,\ldots,\ell'_r),
\]
have the same \emph{marked ambient ribbon type} if there exists an orientation-preserving homeomorphism $h:\Sigma\longrightarrow\Sigma$ isotopic to the identity relative to $\{o\}\cup\partial\Sigma$\footnote{Meaning that there exists an isotopy from the identity to $h$ that fixes $o$ and $\partial\Sigma$ pointwise at every time.}, such that
\[
 h(\Gamma(L))=\Gamma(L')
\]
and, for every $i$, $h\circ\ell_i=\ell'_i$ as elements of $P(\Sigma)$. Such a homeomorphism induces a canonical bijection between the connected components of the complements, as well as between the corresponding cut-open surfaces and their marked boundary cycles.
title: Definition def:same-ribbon-type of arXiv:2608.15923

[Definition 5 of arXiv:2605.30560, 'Projected McKean--Vlasov Dynamics for Entropic Weak Optimal Transport'] For $\mu\in\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ with Lebesgue density
$\rho:=\frac{d\mu}{d\mathrm{L}}$,  the \emph{Fisher information} is
\[
I(\mu)\;:=\;\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\frac{|\nabla\rho(x)|^2}{\rho(x)}\,dx,
\]
with the convention $I(\mu):=+\infty$ if $\mu$ is not absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure.
For a reference measure $\nu \in \Pc(\R^d)$, the
\emph{relative Fisher information} of $\mu$ with respect to $\nu$ is
\[
I(\mu\,\|\,\nu)\;:=\;\int\Big|\nabla\log\tfrac{d\mu}{d\nu}(y)\Big|^2\,\mu(dy).
\]
title: Definition 5 of arXiv:2605.30560

[Thm 28 of arXiv:2605.23308, 'Convergence rate estimates for semigroups and heat kernels associated with resistance form'] For $\calX_n=(X_n,d^{X_n},\rho_{X_n},\mu_{X_n}),\calX=(X,d^X,\rho_X,\mu_X)\in\frM_{\bullet}(\tau)$,
the following conditions are equivalent to each other.
\begin{itemize}
  \item [$\mathrm{(i)}$]There exist a $\bcm$ space $(M,d^M)$ and root-preserving isometric embeddings $f_n:X_n\to M,\;f:X\to M$
  such that $f_n(X_n)\to f(X)$ in the Fell topology, and $\mu_{X_n}\circ f_n^{-1}\to \mu_{X}\circ f^{-1}$ vaguely.  
  \item [$\mathrm{(ii)}$]There exist a $\bcm$ space $(M,d^M)$ and isometric embeddings $f_n:X_n\to M,\;f:X\to M$
  such that $f_n(X_n)\to f(X)$ in the Fell topology, $f_n(\rho_{X_n})\to f(\rho_X)$ in $M$,
  and $\mu_{X_n}\circ f_n^{-1}\to \mu_{X}\circ f^{-1}$ vaguely.
  \item [$\mathrm{(iii)}$]$d^{\tau,\BL^{\kappa}}_{\frM_{\bullet}}(\calX_n,\calX)\to 0$.
  \item [$\mathrm{(iv)}$]The sequence $(\calX_n)_n$ converges to $\calX$ in the Gromov-Hausdorff-vague topology.
\end{itemize}
