body:
[Theorem thm:certified-music-landscape of arXiv:2609.03264, 'Certified Spherical MUSIC for 3D Localization under Adversarial Subspace Perturbations'] Let
		$$
		X=\{\bm{x}_1,\dots,\bm{x}_s\},\quad s\ge 2
		$$
		be an  $s$-point cloud and 
			\[
	\delta_X:=\min_{j\ne k}\abs{\bm{x}_j-\bm{x}_k}
	\]
	be its minimum separation.  
	

Suppose		$$
		\bigcup_{j=1}^s\overline{B_\rho(\bm{x}_j)}
		\subset B_1(\bm{0})\subset\mathbb R^3, \quad\rho\le \frac{\delta_X}{2}.	$$
 Define two  fundamental dimensionless constants:
		\begin{eqnarray}
		
	\gamma:=\rho{\kappa}, \qquad \mu_X
		:=
		\frac{9}{2}
		\frac{s^{2/3}}{\kappa\delta_X}<1
\end{eqnarray}
with  $\kappa>0$ 
	and four other derived constants
	\begin{eqnarray}
\nu_X
		&:=&
	 \frac{64c_\nu^2}{27}
\frac{\mu_X^2}{s} = 	48c_\nu^2
		\frac{s^{1/3}}{\kappa^2\delta_X^2} ,\qquad c_\nu:=\sup_{t>0}\left|t\cos t -\sin t\right|/t \,\,\approx 1.0631,\\
				\nonumber	C_1&:=&
			\frac{\gamma^2}{9}
			+
			\nu_X+\sqrt{1+\nu_X}
			\sqrt{				\left(
				\frac{1}{3}+\frac{\gamma^2}{10}
				\right)^2
				+
				4\nu_X
			}\\
			\nonumber 	C_2&:=& \frac{8}{15} \gamma^2 +6\nu_X+ \frac{2\mu_X}{1-\mu_X} C_1.
\end{eqnarray}
Let \(\widetilde{\mathcal U}\) be any $s$-dimensional subspace of $\mathcal{H}$ 
satisfying
\[
    \|P_{\widetilde{\mathcal U}}-P_{\mathcal U_X}\|_2 =\varepsilon_{\rm sub}.
\]
Assume 
\begin{eqnarray}
 
 A_\gamma& :=& \frac{b_\gamma-\mu_X-\nu_X}{1-\mu_X}>0,\quad b_\gamma
		:=
		1-\sup_{t\ge \gamma} \operatorname{sinc}^2(t)
 \end{eqnarray}
			and 	\begin{eqnarray} C_2<\frac23,\qquad
\varepsilon_{\rm sub}
	< \min\left\{ \frac{\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\gamma
            \left(\frac23-C_2\right)
       }{1+\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\gamma \left(\frac{2}{\sqrt5}+\frac23\right)},\,\,   \sin\left(
        \frac12\arcsin\sqrt{A_\gamma}.
    \right)\right\},
		\end{eqnarray}
		Define
\begin{eqnarray}

\tau_0:=\varepsilon_{\rm sub}^2,\qquad    \tau_1
    :=
    \sin^2\left(
        \arcsin\sqrt{A_\gamma}-\arcsin\varepsilon_{\rm sub}
    \right).
\end{eqnarray}
Then  \(\tau_0<\tau_1\) and:

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item
For every \(j\),
\begin{eqnarray}

    C_0^-\kappa^2I_3
    \preceq
    \nabla^2\widetilde q({\bm z})
    \preceq
    C_0^+\kappa^2I_3,
    \qquad
    {\bm z}\in\overline{B_\rho({\bm x}_j)}
\end{eqnarray}
where
\begin{eqnarray}
C^-_0&:=&	\frac23
			-
			C_2
			-
			\left(
			\frac{2}{\sqrt5}+\frac23\right) 	\varepsilon_{\rm sub} > \frac{
            \frac23-C_2
       }{1+\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\gamma \left(\frac{2}{\sqrt5}+\frac23\right)},\\
    C_0^+
    &:=&\frac23+C_2
      +\left(\frac2{\sqrt5}+\frac23\right)\varepsilon_{\rm sub}.
\end{eqnarray}

\item
Every point outside the certified wells satisfies
\begin{eqnarray}
    \widetilde q({\bm z})\geq\tau_1,
    \qquad
    {\bm z}\in
    B_1(0)\setminus
    \bigcup_{j=1}^sB_\rho({\bm x}_j).
\end{eqnarray}
\item
Each \(B_\rho({\bm x}_j)\) contains exactly one critical point
\(\widetilde{\bm x}_j\), which is its unique minimizer, and
\begin{eqnarray}

    |\widetilde{\bm x}_j-{\bm x}_j|   \le  \frac{2\varepsilon_{\rm sub}}{\sqrt3\,C_0^-\kappa}<\rho,
    \qquad
    \widetilde q(\widetilde{\bm x}_j)\leq\tau_0.
\end{eqnarray}

\item 	If the  fill distance of  a finite set \(G\subset B_1(0)\)
	\begin{equation}
	
		{\rm mesh}_{B_1}(G)
		:=
		\sup_{{\bm z}\in B_1(0)}
		\min_{\bm g\in G}|{\bm z}-\bm g|
	\end{equation}
 satisfies
\[
    \operatorname{mesh}_{B_1}(G)
    <
    \min\left\{
        \rho- \frac{2\varepsilon_{\rm sub}}{\sqrt3\,C_0^-\kappa},
        \,
        \frac{\sqrt3}{2\kappa}(\tau_1-\tau_0)
    \right\},
\]
then
\[
    G_{\tau_1}:=
    \{{\bm g}\in G:\widetilde q({\bm g})<\tau_1\}
\]
contains at least one point in every certified well and no point
outside their union.

\item
For
\[
    0<h\leq
    \frac{2}{(C_0^-+C_0^+)\kappa^2}
    =
    \frac{3}{2\kappa^2},
\]
the gradient map
\[
    T_h({\bm z}):={\bm z}-h\nabla\widetilde q({\bm z})
\]
maps every \(\overline{B_\rho({\bm x}_j)}\) into \(B_\rho({\bm x}_j)\) and is
a contraction there with factor
\[
    r_h:=1-hC_0^-\kappa^2<1.
\]
Consequently, every accepted initialization converges geometrically
to the unique minimizer in its well. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:Q-norm of arXiv:2608.12415, 'Sharp Phase Transition for Ellipsoid Fitting'] For a symmetric linear combination of backbone-dangling shapes $K$ with ground-set $\mathcal{B}(K)$ s.t. \[ 
	K = \sum_{\tau \in\mathcal{B}(M)} c_\tau \cdot \mathsf{M} _{\tau}\,,
	\] we have \[ 
	\|K \|_{sp} \leq (2+o_d(1))  ,
	\]
	provided $\mathrm{Var}(K)=1$ 
	
	Quantitatively, let $\|c(K)\| = \sum_{\tau\in B(K)} |c_\tau|$ and $D_V$ be the size bound for shapes in $K$,  with high probability, \[ 
	\|K \|_{sp} \leq 2 + B_q(\mathsf{NonIdeal}) 
	\]	for \[ 
	B_q(\mathsf{NonIdeal}) \coloneqq  O(1) \cdot 3^{|V(\tau)|} \cdot   c(\tau) \cdot    \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \cdot \|c(K)\|_1^{  2|V(\tau_i)|}  \cdot (q\cdot D_V)^{2}\,.
	\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Spectral Radius for Linear Combination of Backbone-Dangling Shapes

body: [Lm Ohlin \cite{Ohlin} of arXiv:2607.08869, 'Inequalities for convex functions of random points inside and on the boundary of convex bo'] Let $X$ and $Y$ be integrable random variables with $\mathbb E X = \mathbb E Y$. If their distribution functions $F_X$ and $F_Y$ cross exactly once, with $F_X \leqslant F_Y$ to the left of the crossing point and $F_X \geqslant F_Y$ to the right, then $\mathbb E f(X) \leqslant \mathbb E f(Y)$ for every convex $f \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Ohlin \cite{Ohlin}

[Theorem 14 of arXiv:2506.10494, 'Geometric Jensen-Shannon Divergence Between Gaussian Measures On Hilbert Space'] [\textbf{Limiting behavior of the regularized geometric Jensen-Shannon divergence}]
		
		Let
		$\mu_i = \Ncal(0, C_i) \in \Gauss(\Hcal)$, $i=0,1$. Let $0 \leq \alpha \leq 1$ be fixed. Assume that $\mu_0 \sim \mu_1$. Then
		\begin{align}
			\lim_{\gamma \approach 0^{+}}\JS_{G_{\alpha}}^{\gamma}(\mu_0||\mu_1) = \JS_{G_{\alpha}}(\mu_0||\mu_1).
		\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\min_{\psi_w(V_0)}f\le h(x)\le \max_{\psi_w(V_0)}f.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem AdDecomp of arXiv:2506.18207, 'Cartan's Path Development, the Logarithmic Signature and a Conjecture of Lyons-Sidorova'] Let $S(\gamma)$ be the signature of $\gamma$.
Then one has
\begin{equation}
S(\gamma)=\big(\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\int_{0<t_{1}<\cdots<t_{n}<1}e^{x_{t_{1}}{\rm ad}_{{\rm e}_{1}}}({\rm e}_{2})\otimes\cdots\otimes e^{x_{t_{n}}{\rm ad}_{{\rm e}_{1}}}({\rm e}_{2})dy_{t_{1}}\cdots dy_{t_{n}}\big)\otimes e^{{\rm e}_{1}},
\end{equation}
where 
\[
e^{{\rm ad}_{\xi}}(\eta)\triangleq\sum_{m=0}^{\infty}\frac{({\rm ad}_{\xi})^{m}}{m!}(\eta).
\]
In particular, 
\[
\tilde{L}(\gamma)\triangleq\log\big(\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\int_{0<t_{1}<\cdots<t_{n}<1}e^{x_{t_{1}}{\rm ad}_{{\rm e}_{1}}}({\rm e}_{2})\otimes\cdots\otimes e^{x_{t_{n}}{\rm ad}_{{\rm e}_{1}}}({\rm e}_{2})dy_{t_{1}}\cdots dy_{t_{n}}\big)
\]
is a Lie series.

[Lemma lem:cut-gamma-in-half of arXiv:2509.04333, 'The limiting law of the Discrete Gaussian level lines'] Fix any $V, U, F$, and any points $A, B \in V$. Let $b(\gamma)$ be the first horizontal bond where the upper envelope $\mathsf{UE}(\gamma)$ hits the vertical line $x = m$ for a fixed $m \in [A_1, B_1]$. Then there exists a constant $C > 0$ such that for any $k \geq 0$, we have 
		\[Z^n_{V, U; F, \mu}(A, B \mid |\partial D_{b(\gamma)}| \geq k) \leq e^{-(\beta - C)k/2}Z^n_{V, U; F, \mu}(A, B)\,.\]
		In particular, we have
		\[Z^n_{V, U; F, \mu}(A, B \mid D_{b(\gamma)} = \emptyset) \geq (1 - \varepsilon_\beta)Z^n_{V, U; F, \mu}(A, B)\,.\]
        The same holds replacing $Z^n_{V, U;F, \mu}$ with ${\widetilde {\mathsf Z}}_{V, U}$ or ${\widehat Z}^n_{V, U}$.

[Lemma 43 (Thin marked successor) of arXiv:2609.02267, 'Locally Conformally Flat Manifolds with Positive Scalar Curvature: Kleinian Groups, Moduli'] Assume \(n\geq4\).  Let $H\subset\operatorname{int}B$ be a closed regular
neighborhood of an embedded rank-two rose with wedge vertex \(x\), assume
$x\in\operatorname{int}H$, and let
$\mathfrak{m}:F_2\xrightarrow{\cong}\pi_1(H,x)$ be a marking.  For every
$\varepsilon>0$, $\tau>1$, $\delta>0$, $\eta>0$, there are an embedded
rank-two PL rose $\Gamma'\subset\operatorname{int}H$ with wedge vertex
$x$, a connected closed regular neighborhood
$H'\Subset\operatorname{int}H$ of $\Gamma'$ satisfying
$\Gamma'\subset\operatorname{int}H'$
(in particular $x\in\operatorname{int}H'$), a marking
$\mathfrak{m}':F_2\xrightarrow{\cong}\pi_1(H',x)$, and a
finite family $\{U'_\ell\}$ of open balls with
\[
 H'\subset\bigcup_\ell U'_\ell\Subset\operatorname{int}H,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{diam}U'_\ell<\delta,
 \qquad
 \sum_\ell(\operatorname{diam}U'_\ell)^\tau<\eta,
\]
and, for the inclusion $i:H'\hookrightarrow H$,
\[
 i_*\circ\mathfrak{m}'=\mathfrak{m}\circ\omega,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{cap}(H')<\varepsilon.
\]
The petals of $\Gamma'$ may be oriented and labeled $a$ and $b$ so
that $\mathfrak{m}'(a)$ and $\mathfrak{m}'(b)$ are represented by the
corresponding oriented petal loops based at $x$.  Moreover, the data may
be chosen together with a triangulation $\mathcal{T}'$ of $S^n$ in which
$\Gamma'$ is the polyhedron of a nonempty, proper, full subcomplex, the simplicial map
$f':|\mathcal{T}'|\to[0,1]$ that takes value $0$ on the vertices of this
subcomplex and value $1$ on all other vertices, and a number
$t'\in(0,1)$ such that
\[
(f')^{-1}(0)=\Gamma',\qquad H'=(f')^{-1}([0,t']),
\]
and, for every $c\in(0,1)$, $(f')^{-1}([0,c])$ is a closed regular
neighborhood of $\Gamma'$ with
\[
\partial\bigl((f')^{-1}([0,c])\bigr)=(f')^{-1}(c).
\]
In particular, $i_*$ is injective. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thin marked successor

[Lemma LEM:EpsLip of arXiv:2411.07840, 'Central limit theorem for the focusing $Φ^4$-measure in the infinite volume limit'] On the set $D_L \cap B_K$, $\bar{\mathcal{E} }(h^\perp, t)$ is 
Lipschitz in $t$, with the Lipschitz norm   given in (equation eqn: F-lip of the paper)
\begin{equation*}
\sup_{h^\perp}\|\bar{\mathcal{E} }(h^\perp,\cdot)\|_{\mathcal{L}}=\sup_{h^\perp}\sup_{t,t'\in \mathbb{R}}\frac{|\bar{\mathcal{E} }(h^\perp,t)-\bar{\mathcal{E} }(h^\perp, t')|}{|t-t'|}.
\end{equation*} 

\noindent 
In particular, the Lipschitz norm satisfies $\sup\limits_{h^\perp}\| \bar{\mathcal{E}}\|_{\mathcal{L}}=O(L^{\frac 32+}) $.

body: In probability theory, in particular in the study of stochastic processes, a stopping time is a specific type of "random time": a random variable whose value is interpreted as the time at which a given stochastic process exhibits a certain behavior of interest. A stopping time is often defined by a stopping rule, a mechanism for deciding whether to continue or stop a process on the basis of the present position and past events, and which will almost always lead to a decision to stop at some finite time.
title: Stopping time

(Thm 1.1) Let 1 <= k < n and E a k-dimensional subspace of R^n. There are gamma_1,...,gamma_n in [0,1] with sum gamma_i = k (depending only on E) such that for all bounded probability densities f_1,...,f_n on R, the product f(x) = prod f_i(x_i) satisfies ||pi_E(f)||_{L^inf(E)} <= min{ (n/(n-k))^{(n-k)/2}, 2^{k/2} } prod ||f_i||_inf^{gamma_i}, where pi_E(f)(x) = int_{E^perp + x} f is the marginal density on E. In particular, if X has independent coordinates with densities <= 1, then P_E X has density <= min{ (n/(n-k))^{(n-k)/2}, 2^{k/2} } <= 2^{k/2}. For the uniform cube the first bound is attained when n-k divides n and 2^{k/2} when k <= n/2; for those k the cube is the worst case over all such X and all E.

Assumes: independent coordinates (product density); coordinate densities bounded by 1 (in general the bound carries the weight prod ||f_i||_inf^{gamma_i}); 1 <= k < n

[Prop 11 of arXiv:2509.01797, 'Relation between Wick powers and excursion clusters of the 2D GFF'] The composition law $\odot$ is associative,
but it is not commutative.
The monomial sequence $(x^{n})_{n\geq 0}$
is the unique left-neutral and the unique right-neutral element for $\odot$.
Endowed with this composition law, $(\mathtt{S}_{\R},\odot)$ forms a group,
and in particular every element of $\mathtt{S}_{\R}$ has an inverse for $\odot$.

[Corollary 2 of arXiv:2604.10051, 'Ergodicity of the voter model with dynamic anti-voter bonds'] Let~$(\xi_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a Feller process on a metric space~$\mathcal C$. Let~$I$ be an index set and, for each~$i \in I$, let~$(Z^i_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a Markov chain with countable state space~$\mathcal S_i$ and~$Q$-matrix satisfying~$\eqref{eq_q_finite}$. Suppose that, for every~$i \in I$, the processes~$(\xi_t)$ and~$(Z^i_t)$ are dual with respect to~$D_i:\mathcal C \times \mathcal S_i \to [0,\infty)$, which satisfies conditions~$(i)$ and~$(ii)$ of Lemma~\ref{lemma_uniqueness_1} for all~$z \in \mathcal S_i$.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item[(1)] If, in addition, the family of functions~$\xi \mapsto D_i(\xi,z)$, indexed by~$i \in I$ and~$z \in \mathcal S_i$, is measure-determining (that is, two probability measures coincide whenever their integrals against all these functions coincide), then every measure in~$\mathscr{I}_\infty$ is stationary for~$(\xi_t)_t$.
    \item[(2)] If, furthermore, the metric space~$\mathcal C$ is compact and~$(\xi_t)_t$ admits a unique stationary measure, then $(\xi_t)_t$ is ergodic.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:intro-scaling-limit of arXiv:2512.20338, 'Up-down chains and scaling limits: \\ application to permuton- and graphon-valued diffusio'] Let $ \iota  $ denote the map from $   \mathbb S   $ to $  E  $.
Suppose that \orange{$ \{  X _n \}_{ n \ge 0 } $ are up-down chains satisfying}
Assumptions (assumption finite state spaces of the paper) and (assumption:commutation of the paper)
(or more generally, \orange{Markov chains satisfying (assumption finite state spaces of the paper)--(assumption intertwining of the paper)}), and that (assumption state space approximation of the paper)--(assumption continuous density functions are limits of the paper) are satisfied.
Suppose also that $  c _n \to \infty $ and
that the distributions of $  \iota (  X _n( 0 ) ) $ converge to $\mu$, a distribution on $  E  $.

Then the following statements hold.
 \begin{enumerate}
   \item
    There exists a Feller process $  F  $ in $  E  $ with initial distribution $ \mu $
    such that the convergence
	$$
		\big(
			 \iota (  X _n (  \lfloor   c _n t  \rfloor  ) )
		\big)_{ t \ge 0 }
			\Longrightarrow
        		\big(
        				 F ( t )
        		\big)_{ t \ge 0 }
	$$
	holds in distribution in the Skorokhod space $ D([0,\infty), E )$.
	\item 
	The transition semigroup $ \{   \mathcal T  (t) \}_{ t \ge 0 } $ of $  F  $ admits the diagonal description
	$$
		  \mathcal T  (t) h_s^o 
			= 
				e^{ -t  c _{ k-1 } } 
				h_s^o
			,
				\qquad
				s \in   \mathbb S  _k, 
				\,
				k \ge 0,
				\,
				t \ge 0
			.
	$$ 

  \item The process $  F $ is ergodic with a unique stationary measure $M$,
	which is the weak limit of the stationary measures $M_n$ of $X_n$
	(or, more precisely, of their push-forwards on $  E $).
 \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 3 of arXiv:2606.07839, 'Bounds on Spectral Gaps for Non-Reversible Markov Chains with Applications to Temporal Dif'] Let $P$ be a Markov kernel and $\lambda \in [0,1)$. The following properties hold.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item  $P^{(\lambda)}$ is a Markov kernel. 
  \item If $\mu$ is an invariant probability distribution for $P$, then $\mu$ is an invariant probability distribution for $P^{(\lambda)}$.
  \item  If $P$ is irreducible, then so is $P^{(\lambda)}$.
  \item 
    \label {it:sampledDirichlet} If $\cE_{P}$ and $\cE_{P^{(\lambda)}}$ are the Dirichlet forms of $P$ and $P^{(\lambda)}$ with respect to an invariant probability distribution, $\mu$, then $\cE_{P^{(\lambda)}}(f,f)\ge(1-\lambda)\cE_P(f,f)$. 
  \item   $\gap(P^{(\lambda)})\ge (1-\lambda) \gap(P)$.
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Lemma 7 (Early-time tracking from a zero output layer) of arXiv:2608.24007, '2608.24007'] Initialize
\[
    a_j(0)=0,
    \qquad
    w_j(0)=\varepsilon {\omega_j^0},
    \qquad
    {\omega_j^0}\in\mathbb S^{d-1}.
\]
Let $(\bar u_j,{\bar\omega_j})$ solve the self-selected teacher-only system
\[
    \dot{\bar u}_j
    =
    \Phi({\bar\omega_j}),
    \qquad
    {\dot{\bar\omega}_j}
    =
    \tanh(\bar u_j)
    \nabla_{\mathbb S^{d-1}}\Phi({\bar\omega_j}),
\]
with
\[
    (\bar u_j(0),{\bar\omega_j(0)})
    =
    (0,{\omega_j^0}).
\]
For every fixed $T<\infty$, there are constants $L_T<\infty$ and
$\varepsilon_T>0$ such that, for $0<\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_T$,
\[
    \sup_{0\leq t\leq T}
    \left(
        |u_j(t)-\bar u_j(t)|
        +
        \|{\omega_j(t)-\bar\omega_j(t)}\|_2
    \right)
    \leq
    L_Tm\varepsilon^2,
\]
where
\[
    a_j(t)=\varepsilon\sinh(u_j(t)),
    \qquad
    {\omega_j(t)}=\frac{w_j(t)}{\|w_j(t)\|_2}.
\]

body:
[Theorem 21 of arXiv:2506.13913, '2506.13913'] {}{}
Let \(\{X_t\}_{t \geq 0}\) be an Itô diffusion in \(\mathbb{R}^d\) satisfying the SDE
\[
\mathrm{d}X_t = b(X_t)\,\mathrm{d}t + \sigma(X_t) \,\mathrm{d}W_t.
\]
Assume that \(b(x) \in C^1( \mathbb{R}^d; \mathbb{R}^d)\) and \(\sigma(x) \in C^2(\mathbb{R}^n; \mathbb{R}^{d \times m})\). If \(p(t, x)\) is the probability density of \(X_t\), that is, 
\[ \mathbb{P}(X_t \in A) = \int_A p(t, x)\,\mathrm{d}x, \quad \forall A \in \mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R}^d), 
\]
and satisfies \( p(t, x) \in C^{1,2}((0, \infty) \times \mathbb{R}^d) \), with \( p_0(x) \in C^2(\mathbb{R}^d) \) and sufficient decay as \( \|x\| \to \infty \), that is, 
\[
p_0(x) \leq \frac{C}{(1 + \|x\|)^\alpha}, \quad \text{for some } C > 0, \alpha > 0.
\]
Then \( p(t, x) \) satisfies the \textbf{Fokker–Planck equation}
\[
\begin{cases}
\frac{\partial p}{\partial t}(t, x) = \mathcal{L}^* p(t, x), & t > 0, \, x \in \mathbb{R}^d, \\
p(0, x) = p_0(x), & x \in \mathbb{R}^d,
\end{cases}
\]
where the adjoint operator is
\[
\mathcal{L}^* p = - \sum_{i=1}^{n} \frac{\partial}{\partial x_i} \left( b_i(x) p \right) + \frac{1}{2} \sum_{i,j=1}^{n} \frac{\partial^2}{\partial x_i \partial x_j} \left( a_{ij}(x) p \right),
\]
where \(a(x) = \sigma(x) \sigma^\top(x)\) is the diffusion tensor. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 21 of arXiv:2506.13913

body:
Let $T: X \to X$ be a continuous map of a COMPACT metric space and let $M(X, T)$ be the (nonempty, by Krylov-Bogolyubov) set of $T$-invariant Borel probability measures. Then
$$h_{top}(T) = \sup\{ h_\mu(T) : \mu \in M(X, T) \},$$
and the supremum may be restricted to ERGODIC invariant measures. The inequality $h_\mu(T) \le h_{top}(T)$ for every invariant $\mu$ is Goodwyn's half; the existence, for every $c < h_{top}(T)$, of an invariant $\mu$ with $h_\mu(T) > c$ is the Dinaburg-Goodman half (Misiurewicz's proof below). Both sides may be $+\infty$. A measure attaining the supremum is a measure of maximal entropy; it need NOT exist for a general continuous $T$ (there are continuous maps, and even homeomorphisms, with $h_{top} < \infty$ and no measure of maximal entropy), but it exists whenever $\mu \mapsto h_\mu(T)$ is upper semicontinuous, e.g. for expansive maps and for $C^\infty$ maps of compact manifolds. The variational principle is the case $\varphi = 0$ of the variational principle for topological pressure, $P(T, \varphi) = \sup_\mu \{ h_\mu(T) + \int \varphi\,d\mu \}$.

WHERE IT FAILS OR NEEDS CARE. (1) Non-compact $X$: the statement depends on which notion of topological entropy is used; for the Bowen metric entropy on a non-compact space the supremum over invariant measures can be strictly smaller, and $M(X,T)$ may be empty (translation on $\mathbb{R}$). (2) The supremum need not be a maximum (see above). (3) Restricting to a non-invariant measure is meaningless: $h_\mu(T)$ is defined only for invariant $\mu$. (4) The principle relates ENTROPY to entropy; it does not say that a generic point has orbit-growth rate $h_{top}$, nor that the measure of maximal entropy is unique (uniqueness = intrinsic ergodicity, a much stronger property that holds e.g. for topologically mixing shifts of finite type but fails for many systems).
X is a compact metric space
T is continuous
the supremum is over T-invariant Borel probability measures; it need not be attained

Let $\\xi = \\{A_1, \\dots, A_k\\}$ be a finite Borel partition and $\\delta > 0$. By regularity choose compact $K_i \\subset A_i$ with $\\mu(A_i \\setminus K_i) < \\delta$, and set $K_0 = X \\setminus \\bigcup_i K_i$, $\\eta = \\{K_0, K_1, \\dots, K_k\\}$. Then $H_\\mu(\\xi \\mid \\eta) \\le \\mu(K_0) \\log k \\le k\\delta \\log k < 1$ for $\\delta$ small, so $h_\\mu(T, \\xi) \\le h_\\mu(T, \\eta) + 1$. The sets $U_i = K_0 \\cup K_i$, $i = 1..k$, form an open cover $\\mathcal{U}$ (each $K_0 \\cup K_i$ is the complement of the compact set $\\bigcup_{j \\ne i} K_j$), and every element of the join $\\mathcal{U}^n_0$ meets at most $2^n$ elements of $\\eta^n_0$ (at each time $j$ the set $T^{-j}U_{i_j}$ meets only $T^{-j}K_0$ and $T^{-j}K_{i_j}$). Hence $H_\\mu(\\eta^n_0) \\le \\log(2^n N(\\mathcal{U}^n_0))$ (a partition each of whose atoms lies in one of $N$ sets, each of which contains at most $2^n$ atoms, has at most $2^n N$ atoms, and entropy is at most log of the number of atoms), so $h_\\mu(T, \\eta) \\le \\log 2 + h_{top}(T, \\mathcal{U}) \\le \\log 2 + h_{top}(T)$. Thus $h_\\mu(T, \\xi) \\le h_{top}(T) + \\log 2 + 1$ for every $\\xi$, i.e. $h_\\mu(T) \\le h_{top}(T) + \\log 2 + 1$. Apply this to $T^m$: $m\\,h_\\mu(T) \\le m\\,h_{top}(T) + \\log 2 + 1$; divide by $m$ and let $m \\to \\infty$. MISIUREWICZ'S PROOF OF THE REVERSE INEQUALITY. Fix $\\varepsilon > 0$ and for each $n$ a maximal $(n, \\varepsilon)$-separated set $E_n$, with $\\frac1n \\log \\#E_n \\to s(\\varepsilon) := \\limsup_n \\frac1n \\log s(n, \\varepsilon)$ along a subsequence $n_j$. Let $\\nu_n$ be the uniform probability on $E_n$ and $\\sigma_n = \\frac1n \\sum_{k<n} T^k_* \\nu_n$; pass to a further subsequence along which $\\sigma_{n_j} \\to \\mu$ weak*. The limit $\\mu$ is $T$-invariant (standard: $\\|T_*\\sigma_n - \\sigma_n\\| \\le 2/n$). Choose a finite Borel partition $\\xi$ with $\\operatorname{diam}(A) < \\varepsilon$ for all $A \\in \\xi$ and $\\mu(\\partial A) = 0$ for all $A$ (possible: balls $B(x, r)$ have $\\mu$-null boundaries for all but countably many $r$). Each atom of $\\xi^n_0$ has $d_n$-diameter $< \\varepsilon$ and so contains at most one point of $E_n$; hence $H_{\\nu_n}(\\xi^n_0) = \\log \\#E_n$. Fix $q \\ge 1$; for each $0 \\le r < q$ split $\\{0, \\dots, n-1\\}$ into the blocks $[r + iq, r + (i+1)q)$, $0 \\le i < \\lfloor (n - r)/q \\rfloor$, plus at most $2q$ leftover indices. Subadditivity of $H$ over joins and $H(\\text{partition into } \\le k^{2q} \\text{ sets}) \\le 2q\\log k$ give $\\log \\#E_n = H_{\\nu_n}(\\xi^n_0) \\le \\sum_i H_{\\nu_n}(T^{-(r+iq)}\\xi^q_0) + 2q \\log k = \\sum_i H_{T^{r+iq}_*\\nu_n}(\\xi^q_0) + 2q\\log k$. Summing over $r = 0, \\dots, q-1$ and using concavity of $H$ in the measure ($\\sum_{m<n} H_{T^m_*\\nu_n}(\\xi^q_0) \\le n\\, H_{\\sigma_n}(\\xi^q_0)$): $q \\log \\#E_n \\le n\\, H_{\\sigma_n}(\\xi^q_0) + 2q^2 \\log k$, i.e. $\\frac1n \\log \\#E_n \\le \\frac1q H_{\\sigma_n}(\\xi^q_0) + \\frac{2q \\log k}{n}$. Since every atom of $\\xi^q_0$ has $\\mu$-null boundary, $\\sigma_{n_j}(A) \\to \\mu(A)$ for each atom, so letting $n = n_j \\to \\infty$: $s(\\varepsilon) \\le \\frac1q H_\\mu(\\xi^q_0)$. Let $q \\to \\infty$: $s(\\varepsilon) \\le h_\\mu(T, \\xi) \\le h_\\mu(T)$. Since $h_{top}(T) = \\lim_{\\varepsilon\\to0} s(\\varepsilon)$, for every $c < h_{top}(T)$ some invariant $\\mu$ has $h_\\mu(T) > c$. Ergodic measures suffice because $h_\\mu$ is affine and the ergodic decomposition $\\mu = \\int \\mu_x\\,d\\mu$ gives $h_\\mu(T) = \\int h_{\\mu_x}(T)\\,d\\mu(x)$, so some ergodic component has entropy at least $h_\\mu(T)$.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:7fec18fa0aba2240046bd2fd5e80722dbe7eaa9f8d4e958d304d7c9fdacf2273","revision_digest":"sha256:95cd3f5a581ee5b3b33c5ba6ef9422e6da7205ab57a2fb35db6f9be50cdf92b0","source_id":"wikipedia:Topological_entropy","source_revision":"as-read-2026-09-12","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Definition 19 (Skorohod integral) of arXiv:2606.08776, 'Approximation of certain stochastic integrals with anticipating integrands'] \
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
            \item We let $\dom(\delta)$ be the set of $u \in L_2([0,1]\times\Omega)$ such that
            \[
                  \left|\mathbb{E}\int_{0}^{1} D_tF u_tdt\right|^2 \leq C_u \E |F|^2
            \]
            for all $F \in \mathbb{D}_{1,2}$, where $C_u\ge 0$ is a constant depending on $u$.

            \item If $u\in \dom(\delta)$, then $\delta(u)$ is the element of $L_2(\Omega)$ characterized by
            \[
            \mathbb{E}(F\delta(u)) = \mathbb{E}\int_0^1 (D_t F) u_t dt \sptext{1}{for}{1} F \in \mathbb{D}_{1,2}.
            \]
           
      \end{enumerate}
The operator $\delta$ is called the {\normalfont divergence operator} and the divergence $\delta(u)$ is called the {\it Skorohod integral} of the process $u$, denoted by
      \[
            \delta(u) = \int_0^1 u_t \delta W_t.
      \]
title: Skorohod integral

body: [Proposition 117 of arXiv:2609.03875, 'Measure theory without infinities'] Let $\mf A$ be an HTM, $\mf B$ be a topological submonoid of $\mf A$. Suppose $f(k)\in\mf B$ for all $k\in K$. If $\sm{\mf B}{k\in K}{f(k)}$, then $\sm{\mf A}{k\in K}{f(k)}$ and $\sum^{\mf A}_{k\in K} f(k) = \sum^{\mf B}_{k\in K}f(k)$. If $\sm{\mf A}{k\in K}{f(k)}$ and $\sum^{\mf A}_{k\in K} f(k)$ belongs to $\mf B$, then $\sm{\mf B}{k\in K}{f(k)}$.

[Lemma 19 of arXiv:2608.18688, 'Regularity Preservation for Jump-Type Stochastic Transport Equations with Singular Drift'] Take $\lambda, T>0$ and $p,q\in (1,\infty)$. For any $f\in \mL_p^q(T)$, there exists a unique solution $U\in \mH_p^{2,q}(T)$ to the backward parabolic system (\ref{Dackward-PDE1}). For this solution there exists a constant $C$ depending only on $d,p,q,T$ such that  for all $\lambda\geq 0$
\ce 
\|\nabla^2 U\|_{\mL_p^{q}([0,T])}\leq C\|f\|_{\mL_p^q([0,T])}
\de 
Moreover, for any $\vartheta\in[0,2)$ and $p'\in [p,\infty]$, $q'\in [q,\infty]$ satisfying 
\ce 
\frac{d}{p}+\frac{2}{q}<2-\vartheta+\frac{d}{p'}+\frac{2}{q'}
\de 
there exists a constant $C$ depending only on $d,p,q,T, p',q'$ such that  for all $\lambda>0$
\be 
\lambda^{\frac{1}{2}(2-\vartheta+\frac{d}{p'}+\frac{2}{q'}-\frac{d}{p}-\frac{2}{q})}
\|U\|_{\mW^{q'}_{\vartheta,p'}([0,T])}\leq  C\|f\|_{\mL_p^q([0,T])}.
\ee (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 19 of arXiv:2608.18688

[Definition def:weighted-bipartite-graph of arXiv:2607.05384, 'Well-invertible column subsets of sparse matrices are rare'] Let $G=(I,J,M)$ be a weighted bipartite graph, where
\[
M\in\mathbb R^{I\times J}.
\]
We call $I$ the left vertex set and $J$ the right vertex set. We declare that
\begin{align}
  
(i,j) \in I\times J \mbox{ is an edge}
\quad
\Leftrightarrow
\quad
M_{ij}\ne0
\end{align}
and, when $(i,j)$ is an edge, its weight is $M_{ij}$.
With this convention, we define the support of $G$ to be the set of edges
\[
E_M:=\{(i,j)\in I\times J:M_{ij}\ne0\}.
\]
By the support graph of $G$ we mean the unweighted bipartite graph $(I,J,E_M)$.
title: Weighted bipartite graph and support graph

[Theorem 1 (Uniform Laplace principle of bridges) of arXiv:2511.14757, 'A weak convergence approach to the large deviations of the dynamic Schr\"odinger problem'] Under Assumptions \ref{ass:b-sigma-local-properties}--\ref{ass:log-gradient-convergence}, for any compact set $K \Subset D$,
    \begin{equation}
        \lim_{\eta \downarrow 0} \sup_{x,y \in K} \left|-\eta \log \bE\left[\exp - \frac{1}{\eta} F(X^{\eta, xy}) \right] - \inf_{\varphi \in \calC_1} \left[F(\varphi) + I_B^{xy}(\varphi)\right]\right| = 0,
    \end{equation}
    where $X^{\eta, xy}$ is given by the dynamics \ref{eq:R-SDE-main-results}, conditioned on starting in $x$ at $t=0$ and ending in $y$ at $t=1$.
    The good rate function $I_B$ is given by
    \[ I_B(\varphi) = \inf_{\nu \in U^{xy}_\varphi} \frac{1}{2} \int_0^1 |\nu(t)|^2 dt,\]
    where $U^{xy}_\varphi \coloneq \{\nu \in L^2([0,1]:\bR^d): \varphi(\cdot) = \int_0^{\cdot} (b(s, \varphi(s) + \sigma(s, \varphi(s))\nu_s)ds\}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm mr3 of arXiv:2411.06571, 'Moment-based approach for two erratic KPZ scaling limits'] Let $\eta$ be a space-time white noise on $\Bbb R_+\times\Bbb R$, and let $\eta^\epsilon:= \varphi_\epsilon *\eta$ where the convolution is in space only, and where $  \varphi_\epsilon (y):= \epsilon^{-1} \varphi(\epsilon^{-1}y)$ for some fixed smooth even mollifier $\varphi \in C_c^\infty(\Bbb R)$ such that $\|\varphi\|_{L^2(\Bbb R)}<1$ (equivalently $\sup_{x\in \Bbb R} \varphi*\varphi(x)<1$). 
    
    Denote by $\mathcal Z^\epsilon_{s,t}(x,y)$ the propagators given by the It\^o-Walsh solution of the SPDE \begin{equation}\tag{aSHE}\partial_t u(t,y) = \frac12 \partial_y^2 u(t,y) + u(t,y)\eta^\epsilon(t,y) + \epsilon^{1/2}\partial_y\big(u(t,y)\eta^\epsilon(t,y)\big),\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\; t\ge 0,y\in\Bbb R.
    \end{equation}
Then $\mathcal Z^\epsilon$ converges in law as $\epsilon\to 0$ to the family of propagators given by the It\^o-Walsh solution of $$\partial_t \mathcal U(t,y) = \tfrac12 \partial_y^2 \mathcal U(t,y) +  \gamma_{\mathrm{ext}} \mathcal U(t,y) \xi(t,y), \;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\gamma_{\mathrm{ext}}^2 := \int_\mathbb R\frac{\varphi*\varphi(a)}{1- \varphi*\varphi(a)}da.$$ Here $\xi$ is another space-time white noise. The convergence is in the sense of finite-dimensional laws $(\mathcal Z^\epsilon_{s_1,t_1},...,\mathcal Z^\epsilon_{s_m,t_m}),$ where each coordinate has the topology of $\mathcal M(\Bbb R^2)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Scaling limit of the SHE with advective noise

[Def WB of arXiv:2609.04023, 'Characterizing Contractions and Weighted Blowdowns'] Let $Y_\bullet \hookrightarrow X$ be a weighted embedding defined by ideal sheaves $I_n$ and let $I_\bullet = \bigoplus_{n \ge 0} I_nt^n \subset \mathcal{O}_X[t]$ be the associated Rees algebra.
   Let $I_+$ be the ideal generated by $t$.
   The {\em weighted blowup of $X$ along $Y = V(I_1)$} is defined by the morphism
   \[
   \operatorname{Bl}_{Y}X := \mathscr{P}{\mathrm{roj}}_X(I_\bullet)\rightarrow X.
   \]
   We call $Y$ the {\em reduced center} of the weighted blowup.

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Conservation, explicit coupling reduction, exact law comparison or spectral calculation Result: The exactly solvable one-particle sector provides a dilute check. On the cycle of length L, waking a particle runs rate-one simple random walk until an independent Exp(lambda) sleep time. For $\theta=2\pi/L$, its first Fourier multiplier is $r_L=\lambda/(\lambda+1-\cos\theta)$. After k wakes, a point start has cosine expectation $r_L^k$, whereas stationarity is uniform with expectation zero. Hence TV is at least $r_L^k/2$, and reaching TV<=1/4 requires $k\ge\log2/(-\log r_L)\sim\lambda\log2\,L^2/(2\pi^2)$. Check: The multiplier is the integral of lambda*exp(-lambda*t)*exp(-(1-cos(theta))*t) over positive t. Equivalently it is the resolvent eigenvalue of the walk generator. For zero particles the state space is a singleton and mixing takes zero steps. Obstruction: One particle has density tending to zero, so this does not prove the positive-fixed-density lower bound or the supercritical upper bound. Neither is claimed solved.

Let A be a nonempty finite vertex set in a connected infinite graph of maximum degree at most three, and kill discrete-time simple random walk at its first exit from A. With J=|A|+1 and epsilon=3^(-J), P_x(tau_(A^c)>t)<=(1-epsilon)^(floor(t/J)) for every x in A and integer t>=0. The degree-normalized killed diagonal kernel is bounded by the same expression. Thus, for any fixed A, c,beta>0, p_(2 floor(n/2))^A(x,x)>=c n^(-beta) cannot hold for all sufficiently large n. This does not exclude a polynomial lower bound on a bounded macroscopic window, or in a region growing with time. I0012-U1 v1 passed w667 and w668;

## Statement

Let A be a nonempty finite vertex subset of a connected infinite graph of maximum degree at most three. A discrete-time simple random walk killed on exit from A has, at every vertex x in A, exponentially bounded survival and diagonal kernel. In particular, for any fixed finite comb rectangle A, constants c>0 and beta>0, an inequality p_{2 floor(n/2)}^A(x,x)>=c n^(-beta) cannot hold for every sufficiently large integer n.

This shows that the unrestricted-time statement of source Lemma 4.8, (4.68), arXiv:2609.05343v1, p.28, needs an upper-time restriction. It does not refute a lower bound on a bounded macroscopic window, and does not refute source Lemma 4.9 or the accepted conditional I0012 theorem.

## Proof

For each y in A, connectedness to the infinite exterior gives a simple path from y to a vertex outside A, stopping on its first exit. No vertex before the exit is repeated, so its length is at most |A|. Fix J=|A|+1. The walk follows this path with probability at least 3^(-J), because every step has probability at least 1/3 and at most J steps are used. Thus, with epsilon=3^(-J)>0,

    inf_{y in A} P_y(tau_{A^c}<=J) >= epsilon.

At each deterministic multiple of J, conditional on survival to that time, the current vertex is in A and the same escape estimate applies. The ordinary Markov property therefore gives

    P_x(tau_{A^c}>kJ) <= (1-epsilon)^k

for every nonnegative integer k. At any time t,

    p_t^A(x,x) = P_x(X_t=x, tau_{A^c}>t)/deg(x)
               <= (1-epsilon)^(floor(t/J)),

since deg(x)>=1. With t=2 floor(n/2), this upper bound is exponentially small in n. For any c,beta>0 it is eventually smaller than c n^(-beta), because an exponential dominates every positive power. This contradicts the claimed all-time polynomial lower bound in a fixed box.

For a fixed environment of the finite-tooth comb and fixed N,b, the rectangle in (4.68) is finite and satisfies all these hypotheses. At gamma=1/3 its purported exponent is beta=2/3. Therefore the contradiction applies exactly to the displayed critical specialization, as well as to every gamma in (0,1).

## Scope

No gamma>1/3 requirement is inferred. The defect is time/box quantification, rather than a critical exponent. A corrected range such as n<=constant*N^(4/(1+gamma)) is compatible with exponential late-time decay; its constant and containment must be proved separately.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:7eb1c3de89ebff6970233fcf997d1d41bd3bff3ab5fc125d337afc30020b63f3","revision_digest":"sha256:95e3936149632e097b28dee910cbf0a9dfaff7c6071f4e630385724cda5abed3","source_id":"own-work:w664:I0012-U1:v1","source_revision":"version 1; w667 and w668 PASS; novelty UNCHECKED","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

CANDIDATE COUNTEREXAMPLE, AUTHOR CHECKED; NOVELTY UNVERIFIED. Rational Weyl clock-shift pairs converge strongly to an irrational rotation pair, whereas every selected sum is nilpotent and the limiting sum has Haar-circle Brown measure. Strong convergence includes all fixed matrix-coefficient amplifications. The matrices may share a Haar conjugation and are dependent. This addresses the literal unrestricted family question, not independent-entry or free-limit subclasses. The parent supplied matrix amplification and trace/norm proof arguments, so its review does not independently certify the amended proof.

metadata_json:
{"artifact_digest":"sha256:801cd94b91360bdb765994754a3f10b2d444419f51d59d171f1a48582d878714","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/80/801cd94b91360bdb765994754a3f10b2d444419f51d59d171f1a48582d878714.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:782e3ef5bbb0faf01a685eb529732c0d77bfa3843ab0c5c3cb1c854a588ec117","bundle_entry_key":"brown-measure-counter","bundle_id":"population.probability-candidate-obstructions-and-spatial-lemmas-005","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability theory","draft":"codex-probability-1000-20h-20260906/bundle_005.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.free:candidate-strong-convergence-does-not-force-brown-measure","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# P0189: candidate counterexample to Brown-measure continuity under strong convergence

Status: complete candidate construction, checked by the author; no independent review and no novelty claim. This addresses the literal general conjecture in van Handel, *The strong convergence phenomenon*, arXiv2507.00346v2 (11 February2026), Section6.9, pp.69-70. It does not address the narrower conjectures for independent Ginibre matrices or free limiting families.

Primary source for the question: https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.00346 . Primary source for the established limiting Brown measure: Fang, Jiang, Lin and Xu, *On generalized universal irrational rotation algebras and the operator u+v*, https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.4771 , Theorem12.2. Its introduction also states simplicity and uniqueness of trace of the irrational rotation algebra. These literature theorems are dependencies, not results proved here.

## Finite matrices

Fix an irrational theta in(0,1). Choose reduced rational approximants p_j/q_j tending to theta, with q_j tending to infinity. Let omega_j=exp(2*pi*i*p_j/q_j). On the standard basis indexed by k modulo q_j define

\[
 U_j e_k=\omega_j^k e_k,\qquad
 S_j e_k=e_{k-1},\qquad
 V_j=e^{\pi i/q_j}S_j.
\]

Then U_j and V_j are unitary and satisfy

\[
 V_jU_j=\omega_jU_jV_j,\qquad U_j^{q_j}=I,\qquad V_j^{q_j}=-I.
\]

Put A_j=U_j+V_j. Its characteristic polynomial is exactly z^{q_j}. Indeed, in the determinant of zI-U_j-V_j only the all-diagonal permutation and the full cyclic permutation contribute (for q_j>=2). The former contributes

\[
 \prod_{k=0}^{q_j-1}(z-\omega_j^k)=z^{q_j}-1,
\]

because omega_j is primitive. The latter contributes minus the product of the cyclic weights, namely -exp(pi*i)=+1. Thus det(zI-A_j)=z^{q_j}. Cayley-Hamilton gives A_j^{q_j}=0, and every empirical eigenvalue distribution is delta_0.

An equivalent algebraic check is the root-of-unity binomial identity (U_j+V_j)^{q_j}=U_j^{q_j}+V_j^{q_j}=0. The determinant calculation supplies the conclusion without relying on that identity.

## Strong convergence of the pair

Let A_theta be the universal unital irrational rotation C*-algebra generated by unitaries u,v satisfying vu=exp(2*pi*i*theta)uv. This algebra is simple and has a unique faithful tracial state tau, as recalled in the cited primary paper.

Consider the norm quotient

\[
 \mathcal Q=\prod_j M_{q_j}(\mathbb C)\big/\bigoplus_j M_{q_j}(\mathbb C),
\]

where the direct sum consists of sequences whose operator norms tend to zero. The classes of (U_j) and (V_j) are unitaries and satisfy the irrational relation exactly, since omega_j tends to exp(2*pi*i*theta). Universality therefore gives a unital *-homomorphism A_theta to Q. Simplicity makes it injective, hence isometric. Since the quotient norm of a bounded sequence is its limsup norm, for every noncommutative *-polynomial P,

\[
 \limsup_j\|P(U_j,V_j,U_j^*,V_j^*)\|
 =\|P(u,v,u^*,v^*)\|.
\]

The same argument applies to every subsequence. If the norms failed to converge to the displayed value, a subsequence uniformly separated from that value would contradict the same limsup identity. Consequently the pair converges strongly.

The normalized traces also converge to tau. Using the commutation relation, every fixed word is a phase times U_j^a V_j^b. When b is a fixed nonzero integer and j is large, the shift has no diagonal entries, so its trace is zero. If b=0 and a is fixed nonzero, the geometric sum of omega_j^{ak} is zero for all q_j>|a|. The identity word has trace one, and phases converge. These are exactly the canonical irrational-rotation trace values. Thus both norm and tracial versions of strong convergence are satisfied, with a faithful limiting trace.

In particular A_j converges strongly, including all *-polynomials in A_j alone, to a=u+v.

The survey Definition 1.1 also allows fixed finite-dimensional matrix coefficients. For each fixed D, amplify the quotient homomorphism to M_D(A_theta). An injective *-homomorphism is completely isometric, and M_D(Q) identifies with the quotient of the product of M_D(M_qj) by norm-null sequences. Therefore the same limsup identity and subsequence argument apply to every D-by-D matrix-valued *-polynomial. The identification follows entrywise in finite D: a matrix sequence tends to zero in norm exactly when all its entries do, and the quotient norm is the limsup of the block-matrix norms. Thus the precise matrix-coefficient definition is covered.

A separate norm-convergence proof uses the trace computation above for the lower bound and needs no appeal to simplicity. Write P_j for a fixed matrix-valued polynomial and P for its limit. For every positive integer m, with normalized traces on the matrix factors,
\[
 \|P_j\|\ge\big[(\mathrm{tr}_D\otimes\mathrm{tr}_{q_j})((P_j^*P_j)^m)\big]^{1/(2m)}.
\]
Taking the lower limit in j and then m to infinity gives liminf ||P_j|| >= ||P||, because the limiting trace tr_D tensor tau is faithful. Complete contractivity of the universal quotient homomorphism gives limsup ||P_j|| <= ||P||. This independently proves the required full norm convergence. The parent suggested these two explicit extensions during its first bounded review on 6 September 2026; the author checked and incorporated them. The remaining review and novelty status is pending.

## The Brown-measure mismatch

The cited Theorem12.2 states that the Brown measure of u+v, in the tracial von Neumann algebra generated by the irrational rotation pair, is Haar probability measure on the unit circle. It is therefore different from delta_0. The finite empirical measures are all delta_0 and do not converge to the Brown measure of a, despite strong convergence.

The same example also prevents a universal lower spectral-radius conclusion: every A_j has spectral radius zero, whereas the source Theorem11.1 gives spectrum of u+v equal to the closed unit disk and hence spectral radius one.

To make the matrices random rather than deterministic, take Haar unitary Q_j and replace the pair by (Q_j U_j Q_j*,Q_j V_j Q_j*). For every outcome, norms, normalized traces, nilpotency, and eigenvalue distributions are unchanged. This supplies genuinely random families satisfying the same convergence. The two members are dependent; the construction does not claim otherwise. Equivalently, the single random matrix Q_j A_j Q_j* is already a counterexample for a one-variable polynomial.

## Optional realization in every integer dimension

The dimensions q_j suffice for a counterexample along a sequence tending to infinity. If an all-integer-dimension formulation is required, take consecutive continued-fraction denominators, which are coprime. For each sufficiently large N, choose the largest j with q_j*q_{j+1}<=N. The elementary coin theorem gives N=a*q_j+b*q_{j+1} for nonnegative integers a,b. Define the N-dimensional pair as the block direct sum of a copies of the j-th pair and b copies of the(j+1)-st pair. Both block dimensions tend to infinity as N does. Polynomial norms are the maximum of their block norms, traces are convex combinations of block traces, and the sum remains nilpotent. Thus the same counterexample exists with dimension exactly N for every sufficiently large integer N.

## Scope and remaining checks

This is a candidate refutation of the survey's literal implication from arbitrary strong convergence to empirical Brown-measure convergence. It is not a refutation for independent-entry ensembles, free limits, or holomorphic polynomials in independent Ginibre matrices. Yi Han's June2026 paper, arXiv2606.01664, claims the latter case and is compatible with this construction.

Load-bearing obligations are the precise survey scope, the primitive-root determinant sign, isometry of the quotient homomorphism, faithful-trace interpretation, and the cited Brown-measure theorem. All are explicit here. It remains possible that the construction or the general failure of continuity is already known; current-literature novelty is unverified. No validator, numerical eigenvalue computation, or brain ingestion is treated as proof review. In fact numerical eigenvalues of these nilpotent matrices would be an especially unreliable check because of their extreme nonnormality.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:556c6b1fcc6b4db785822e5b4cae963c5ea31477c78e3e04ba1fa72416f504a4","revision_digest":"sha256:95f7fa682f99681a02d3d0204e801cfa0ad80c8f37c5983f3a1fa86b9d71ff07","source_id":"owner-original-probability-research-20260906:brown-measure-counter","source_revision":"author-checked-20260906-v1","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

body:
[Prop P:only-easy-consequences of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Take any half-space pre-landscape $\mathcal{M}^\rho$ continuously extended to $\mathbb{H}^2_\uparrow$. Let $\mathcal{K}^\rho(x, s; y, t) = \mathcal{M}^\rho(x, s; y, t) + \frac{(x-y)^2}{(t-s)}$ for any $(x,s;y,t)\in \mathbb{H}^2_\uparrow$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textup{(Modulus of continuity, analogue of [DOV]).} For any $b \ge 2, \epsilon \le 1$, define
$$
K^\epsilon_b = \{(x, t; y, t + s) \in \mathbb H^2_\uparrow : s \in [\epsilon, b], \text{and } |t|, x, y \le b \}.
$$
For two points $u_i = (x_i, t_i; y_i, s_i)\in K^\epsilon_b$, $i = 1, 2$, let 
\begin{align*}
    \tau &= \tau(u_1, u_2) = \|(t_1, s_1) - (t_2, s_2)\|_2, \\
    \xi &= \xi(u_1, u_2) = \|(x_1, y_1) - (x_2, y_2)\|_2.
\end{align*}
Then if $\tau^{1/3} + \xi^{1/2} \le \min(\epsilon/b, 1/(\rho \vee 0))$, we have
$$
|\mathcal{K}^\rho(u_1) - \mathcal{K}^\rho(u_2)| \le M \left(\tau^{1/3}\log^{2/3}(\tau^{-1}) + \xi^{1/2}\log^{1/2}(4b\xi^{-1}) \right),
$$
with a random variable $M$  satisfying
$\mathbb{P}(M > a) \le b^{4}[(b/\epsilon)^{10} + (\rho \vee 0)^{10}] \exp(-ca^{3/2})$
for all $a > 0$. Here $c>0$ is a universal constant.
\item \textup{(Shape bound, analogue of [DOV]).} Fix $\rho_0 > 1$ and assume $\rho < \rho_0$. Then there exists $c > 0$ depending on $\rho_0$ such that the following holds. For all $u = (x, t; y, t + s) \in \mathbb H^2_\uparrow$ with $s \le \rho_0$, we have
$$
\left|\mathcal{K}^\rho(u) \right|\le M s^{1/3} \log^2\left(\frac{2\|u\|_2}{s}\right),
$$
where $M > 0$ is a random variable satisfying
$\mathbb{P}(M > a) \le 2\exp(-ca^{3/2})$
for all $a > 0$.
\item \textup{(Metric composition holds everywhere, analogue of [DOV])}
For each $u = (x, r;y, t) \in \mathbb H^2_\uparrow$ and $s \in (r, t)$, define
	$f_{u, s}(z) = \mathcal{M}^\rho(x,r;z,s)+\mathcal{M}^\rho(z,s;y,t)$. Then on an event of probability $1$, $\mathcal{M}^\rho$ satisfies the metric composition law
	\begin{equation}
	
	\mathcal{M}^\rho(u)=\max_{z \in \mathbb R} f_{u, s}(z)
	\end{equation}
	for every $u = (x, r;y, t) \in \mathbb H^2_\uparrow$ and $s \in (r, t)$. Moreover, for any compact set $K \subset \mathbb H^2_\uparrow$, there exists a random variable $B_K$ such that for all $u = (x, r;y, t) \in K$ and $s \in (r, t)$, the set where $f_{u, s}$ attains its maximum is contained in the interval $[-B_K, B_K]$.
\end{enumerate}
title: Prop P:only-easy-consequences of arXiv:2604.10020

[Lem 63 of arXiv:2605.23308, 'Convergence rate estimates for semigroups and heat kernels associated with resistance form'] Fix $x,y\in F,\;y_n\in F_n,\;t>0,\;\kappa\in [1/2,1],\;p_0,p,q\in [1,\infty],$ and $\alpha\in (0,\alpha_0)$.
\begin{itemize}
  \item [$\rm{(i)}$]Under the conditions $1_{\kappa,p_0}$ and $2_{\kappa,p,q}$, we have that
\begin{align*}
  \MoveEqLeft\left| \left(\int P_{\varepsilon}f_{r}d\mu\right)p(t,x,y)-\left( \int \overline{P_{\varepsilon}f_r}d\mu_n \right)\overline{p_n}(t,x,y_n) \right|\\
  \lesssim&L(t)\mu\left( B\left(x,4r\right)\right)r+M(t)\left\{ \frac{\delta}{r}+\frac{\varepsilon}{m(\delta)(r-\delta)} \right\}\\
  &+\g{c}{sg2,n}\Bigl\{c_2(\alpha,\varepsilon,\kappa,p)\mu(B(x,r))^{1/p} +c_3(\alpha,\varepsilon,\kappa,q) \mu(B(x,r))^{1/q}\Bigr\}\\
  &\quad\times \Bigl\{ d_{\rm{H}}(F,F_n)+d_{\rm{H}}(F,F_n)^{\kappa}+d(y,y_n)+d_{\BL^{\kappa}}(\mu,\mu_n)\Bigr\}\\
  &+L(t)\Bigl\{\mu(B(x,4r+\rho))+(1+\rho^{-\kappa})d_{\BL^{\kappa}}(\mu,\mu_n)\Bigr\}r\\
  &+M(t)c_1(\varepsilon,\kappa,p_0)\mu(B(x,r))^{1/p_0}d_{\rm{H}}(F,F_n)^{\kappa},
\end{align*}
where $f_r:=1_{B(x,r)}:F\to [0,1]$ and $\overline{P_{\varepsilon}f_r}$ is a McShane extension with exponent $\kappa$, and 
  $\varepsilon\in (0,1],\;\rho\in (0,\infty),\;r\in [d_{\rm{H}}(F,F_n),\infty),$ and $\delta\in (0,r)$.
  \item [$\rm{(ii)}$]Moreover, if the assumption $\rm{(A3)}$ is additionally satisfied, then it holds 
  for $\varepsilon,\rho\in (0,1),\;\xi\ge d_{\rm{H}}(F,F_n),$ and $0<r<\eta<1$ that
\begin{align*}
  \MoveEqLeft\left| \left(\int P_{\varepsilon}f_{r}d\mu\right)p(t,x,y)-\left( \int \overline{P_{\varepsilon}f_r}d\mu_n \right)\overline{p_n}(t,x,y_n) \right|\\
  \lesssim&L(t)\mu\left( B\left(x,\eta\right)\right)\eta+M(t)\exp[-c(\eta-r)^{1+\beta}/\varepsilon^{\beta}]\\
  &+\g{c}{sg2,n}\Bigl\{c_2(\alpha,\varepsilon,\kappa,p)\mu(B(x,r))^{1/p} +c_3(\alpha,\varepsilon,\kappa,q) \mu(B(x,r))^{1/q}\Bigr\}\\
  &\quad\times \Bigl\{ d_{\rm{H}}(F,F_n)+d_{\rm{H}}(F,F_n)^{\kappa}+d(y,y_n)+d_{\BL^{\kappa}}(\mu,\mu_n)\Bigr\}\\
  &+L(t)\Bigl\{\mu(B(x,\eta+\xi+\rho))+(1+\rho^{-\kappa})d_{\BL^{\kappa}}(\mu,\mu_n)\Bigr\}(\eta+\xi)\\
  &+M(t)c_1(\varepsilon,\kappa,p_0)\mu(B(x,r))^{1/p_0}d_{\rm{H}}(F,F_n)^{\kappa}.
\end{align*}
\end{itemize}
title: Lem 63 of arXiv:2605.23308

body:
[Theorem theorem2 of arXiv:2412.01070, 'A note on Lévy-driven McKean-Vlasov SDEs under monotonicity'] Assume that Assumptions $({\bf A}_1)$-$({\bf A}_{3})$   hold, and suppose further  $X_0\in L^\beta(\Omega\to\mathbb R^d,\mathscr F_0,\mathbb{P})$.
Then, the McKean-Vlasov  SDE (equation MV of the paper) admits a unique strong solution $(X_t)_{t\ge0}$ satisfying that,
for any fixed $T>0$, there exists a constant $C_T>0$ such that
\begin{align}
\mathbb{E}|X_t|^\beta \le C_T(1+\mathbb{E}|X_0|^{\beta}),\quad 0\le t\le T.
\end{align}
In addition, if Assumption
 $({\bf A}_2)$ is replaced by the following stronger  one: for some    $L_3>0,$
 \begin{equation}
 \<x,b(x,\mu)\> \vee
 \nu( |f(x,\mu,\cdot)|^2\mathds 1_U(\cdot))
 \le L_3 \big(1+|x|^2+\mu(|\cdot|^{\beta})^{\frac{2}{\beta}}\big ),
\end{equation}
then, for any $T>0$, there exists a constant $C_T'>0$ such that
\begin{align}
\mathbb{E}\Big(\sup_{0\le t\le T}  |X_t|^{\beta}\Big)   \le C_T'(1+\mathbb{E}|X_0|^{\beta}).
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem theorem2 of arXiv:2412.01070

body:
[Thm thm-fixed-gf of arXiv:2411.06301, 'Inverting the operation of conditioning a branching process on extinction'] Consider a $d$-type branching process $X = \{X(n)\}_{n\in\mathbbm N_0}$ with generating function $f$ satisfying the following hypotheses. 
\begin{enumerate}[I.]
\item $X$ is subcritical, i.e., $\rho <1$. 
 
\item $X$ is positive regular and non-singular (Definition~(def-bp-basic of the paper)).   
\item For each $k\in\mathbbm N$, the $k$th component $f_k$ of the generating function is a continuous function from $(0,\infty]^d$ to $(0,\infty]$ (with $(0,\infty]$ equipped with the topology of a half-open interval). 
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists a conjugate branching process for $X$, equivalently, there exists $q \in (1,\infty)^d  $ such that $f(q) = q$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let f be convex and L-smooth on R^n with a minimizer x*. Gradient descent x_{k+1} = x_k - (1/L) grad f(x_k) satisfies f(x_k) - f(x*) <= L ||x_0 - x*||^2 / (2 k) for every k >= 1: sublinear O(1/k) convergence of function values. If f is additionally mu-strongly convex, the iterates converge linearly: ||x_k - x*||^2 <= (1 - mu/L)^k ||x_0 - x*||^2.

body:
Consider a finite-state, finite-action Markov decision process with transition probabilities p(s_next|s,a), target policy pi, and behavior policy mu having stationary probabilities d_mu(s)>0 for every state. Assume coverage: pi(a|s)>0 implies mu(a|s)>0. Let gamma(s), lambda(s) belong to [0,1], let i(s)>0, and suppose discount products tend to zero almost surely from each starting state along the target chain. Let Phi have row phi(s)^T and full column rank. Write P_pi(s,s_next)=sum_a pi(a|s)p(s_next|s,a), Gamma=diag(gamma), Lambda=diag(lambda), and d(s)=d_mu(s)i(s). For emphatic TD(lambda), rho_t=pi(A_t|S_t)/mu(A_t|S_t), F_t=i(S_t)+rho_(t-1)gamma(S_t)F_(t-1), M_t=lambda(S_t)i(S_t)+(1-lambda(S_t))F_t, and e_t=rho_t[gamma(S_t)lambda(S_t)e_(t-1)+M_t phi(S_t)]. Assume the finite conditional limits lim_t E_mu[F_t|S_t=s] and lim_t E_mu[e_t|S_t=s] exist for every s, as in the source theorem. Then A=lim_t E_mu[e_t(phi(S_t)-gamma(S_(t+1))phi(S_(t+1)))^T] is positive definite in the real quadratic-form sense: v^T A v>0 for every nonzero v, although A need not be symmetric. Explicitly, f=(I-Gamma P_pi^T)^(-1)d, m=Lambda d+(I-Lambda)f, M=diag(m), P_pi_lambda=(I-P_pi Gamma Lambda)^(-1)P_pi Gamma(I-Lambda), and A=Phi^T M(I-P_pi_lambda)Phi. This gives stability of the expected linear update for sufficiently small constant step sizes; this theorem alone does not establish almost-sure convergence of the stochastic iterates.
Finite state and action sets
Behavior stationary distribution strictly positive on all states
Target-policy coverage by behavior policy
State-dependent gamma and lambda in [0,1]; target discount products vanish almost surely
Strictly positive interest i(s)
Full column rank feature matrix
Existence and finiteness of both conditional trace limits in Theorem 1

Consequently S=(K+K^T)/2 has positive row sums and nonpositive off-diagonal entries, so S has positive diagonal and is strictly diagonally dominant. Gershgorin Circle Theorem therefore gives that S is positive definite. Hence y^T K y=y^T S y>0 for nonzero real y. Full column rank of Phi yields v^T A v=(Phi v)^T K(Phi v)>0. body: [Theorem 1 of arXiv:2512.19517, 'Spiking and Resetting'] Let us fix $\delta\in(0,1]$ and $T>0$. We equip the space of Borel measures on the compact set $[0,T]\times[\delta,1]$ with the weak topology. We have that the restriction of the simple point process $(\mathbb{Q}^{\varepsilon})_{\varepsilon>0}$ to $[0,T]\times[\delta,1]$ converges in law to the restriction of the simple point process $\mathbb{Q}$ to $[0,T]\times[\delta,1]$.

[Theorem 28 (Completed Wick-chaos product theorem) of arXiv:2607.16724, 'Algebraic Transfer for Operator-Valued Gaussian Chaoses: Oriented Schatten Profiles and Si'] Fix $2\le r<\infty$ and $1\le p<\infty$.  Let
\[
 K\in\mathfrak W_{m,r}(\cH_{\mathbb R};\cC,\cD),
 \qquad
 L\in\mathfrak W_{n,r}(\cH_{\mathbb R};\cD,\cE).
\]
Then \eqref{eq:ordered-wick-product} extends from finite-support kernels to
an identity in $L^p(\Omega;\Sch_r(\cC,\cE))$.  Moreover,
\begin{align}

 \norm{I_n(L)I_m(K)}_{L^p(\Omega;\Sch_r)}
 &\le
 \Prof_{n,r}(L)\Prof_{m,r}(K)\\
 &\quad\times
 \sum_{k=0}^{m\wedge n}
 \binom{m}{k}\binom{n}{k}k!\,
 A_{m+n-2k}(p+r)^{(m+n-2k)/2}.
 \notag
\end{align}
Here $\Prof_{m,r}$ denotes the norm of the same-field profile completion,
and $A_0=1$.

  \sim
  \Gamma(\beta)(1-2r)^{\gamma\beta}
  n^{-\gamma\beta}L(n^\gamma).
\]

[Theorem thm:MPZ of arXiv:2605.17725, 'Limit theorems for random walks with spatio-temporal drift'] Assume that the following two conditions hold.
    \begin{itemize}
        \item Condition $(H^{\alpha}_\sigma)$:
        There exist constants $\kappa_0\ge1$ and $\alpha\in(0,1)$ such that
        \begin{align*}
       & \kappa_0^{-1}|\xi|^2
        \le \langle\sigma(x)\sigma(x)^\top\xi,\xi\rangle
        \le \kappa_0|\xi|^2\quad\text{and}\quad |\sigma(x)-\sigma(y)|\le\kappa_0|x-y|^{\alpha}
        \quad\forall\,x,y,\xi \in\mathbb{R}^d.
        \end{align*}

        \item Condition $(H^{0}_b)$:
        There exists a constant $\kappa_1>0$ such that
        $
        |b(0)|\le\kappa_1,
        $
        and
        $$
        |b(x)-b(y)|
        \le
        \kappa_1\bigl(1\vee |x-y|\bigr)
        \quad\forall\,x,y\in\mathbb{R}^d.
        $$
    \end{itemize}
    Then the SDE (equation eq:sde_MPZ of the paper) admits a unique weak solution. Moreover, for any
    $T>0$, there exist constants $C_0\ge1$ and
    $\lambda_0\in(0,1]$, depending only on
    $T,\alpha,\beta,\kappa_0,\kappa_1$ and $d$, such that for all
    $0<t\le T$ and $x,y\in\mathbb{R}^d$, the transition density
    $p_t(x,y)$ exists and satisfies the two-sided Gaussian bound
    \begin{equation}
        C_0^{-1}\,
        g_{\lambda_0^{-1}}\!\bigl(t,\theta^{(1)}_{t}(x)-y\bigr)
        \le
        p_t(x,y)
        \le
        C_0\,
        g_{\lambda_0}\!\bigl(t,\theta^{(1)}_{t}(x)-y\bigr),
    \end{equation}
    where
    $
    g_\lambda(t,z):=t^{-d/2}\exp(-\lambda|z|^2/t),
    $
    and $\theta^{(1)}_t(x)$ is the mollified flow defined in
    (equation eq:flow of the paper) with $\varepsilon=1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Tm characterization of arXiv:2411.05441, 'Sticky diffusions on star graphs : characterization and It\^o formula'] Let $X(t) = (i(t), x(t))$ be the process generated by (equation generator2 of the paper) and (equation eq:domain of the paper) with $\eta > 0$. Then there exists a nonsticky diffusion $\tilde Y$ on $\Gamma$ and a strictly increasing continuous function $V^{-1}$ such that $X$ and $\tilde Y(V^{-1}(\cdot))$ are indistinguishable. Moreover, there exists an increasing process $\ell_X$, adapted to the completion of the natural filtration of $X$ with respect to the collection of probability measures $\left ( \mathbf P_\mathsf{x} \right)_{\mathsf{x} \in \Gamma}$, such that $\ell_X$ almost surely increases only when $X = \mathsf{v}$, that $\eta \ell_X(t) = \int_0^t \mathbf{1}_{\{X(s) = \mathsf{v}\}} \, ds$ and $\ell_X(t) = \ell_{\tilde Y}(V^{-1}(t))$ almost surely, where $\ell_{\tilde Y}$ is the process appearing in (tm:FW_FS of the paper)-(item:FS of the paper).

[Dfn 80 of arXiv:2507.08909, 'Annealed almost periodic entropy'] For any separable representation $\pi$, its \textbf{zeroth-order AP entropy along $\bspi$} is
\[\rmh^0_{\bspi}(\pi) = \inf\big\{\rmh^0_{\bspi}(\Phi^\pi_{x_1,\dots,x_k}):\ k\ge 1,\ x_1,\dots,x_k \in H_\pi\big\}.\]
Its \textbf{lower zeroth-order AP entropy along $\bspi$} is defined analogously using $\ul{\rmh}^0$.

[Lemma lem:logdet-subgaussian of arXiv:2411.09075, 'Weak Poincar{\'e} Inequalities, Simulated Annealing, and Sampling from Spherical Spin Glas'] There exists a $H_{N,2}$-measurable random variable $X$ that the following holds.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item With probability $1-e^{-cN}$, $X = \log \det ((1 + \xi''(0)) I - \nabla^2 H_N(0)) - N \xi''(0) / 2$.
        \item $X$ has mean $O_\eps(1)$ and is $O_\eps(1)$-subgaussian.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The moments of the negative binomial law $c_{mp}$ are
$$M_1=\frac{m(1-p)}{p}$$
$$M_2=m\,\frac{1-p}{p^2}(1+m-mp)$$
$$M_3=m\,\frac{1-p}{p^3}[(m+1)(m+2)(1-p)^2+3(m+1)(1-p)p+p^2]$$
$$M_4=m\,\frac{1-p}{p^4}[(m+1)(m+2)(m+3)(1-p)^3
+6(m+1)(m+2)(1-p)^2p+7(m+1)(1-p)p^2+p^3]$$
$$\vdots$$
with the computation in general being possible by recurrence.

[Proposition 13 of arXiv:2608.19976, 'Random valuations'] An infinitely divisible random valuation has independent increments
  if and only if $\Phi(K_2)-\Phi(K_1)$ and $\Phi(K_4)-\Phi(K_3)$ are

body:
[Thm t:abelianization-form0 of arXiv:2607.24640, 'The Yang-Mills measure on surfaces via Morse theory'] Let $\gamma_1,\tilde{\gamma}$ be two elementary curves which are both of type $\operatorname{I}$ or $\operatorname{II}_\pm$ such that $\tilde{\gamma}\preccurlyeq\gamma_1$. Set 
$$
\gamma(t)=\gamma_1\circ\tau(t),
$$
where $\tau$ is the function appearing in Definition~(d:included-curve of the paper). Then, for any bounded and measurable function $\Psi$ on $G$, one has
$$
\forall t\in[0,1],\quad\mathbb{E}\left(\Psi\left(\mathrm{g}_\gamma(t)\right)|\widetilde{\mathcal{F}}_{\tilde{\gamma}}(1)\right)=e^{\left(\mathscr{A}_\gamma(t)-\mathscr{A}_{\tilde{\gamma}}(t)\right)\frac{\Delta_G}{2}}\Psi\left(\mathrm{g}_{\tilde{\gamma}}(t)\right).
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm t:abelianization-form0 of arXiv:2607.24640

body:
[Lemma 32 (Exact top-\texorpdfstring{$m$}{m} occupancy mixture) of arXiv:2604.09933, 'Explicit cutoff profiles for colored top-\texorpdfstring{$m$}{m}-to-random shuffles'] Fix \(1\le m\le n\) and \(k\ge0\). Then
\begin{align}
(Q^{(m)})^{*k}
&=\sum_{a=0}^{n}\mu_k^{(m)}(a)\,\widetilde Q_{a,p},
\\
&=\sum_{u=0}^{n}P_k^{(m)}(u)\,\widetilde Q_{n-u,p}.

\end{align}
In particular,
\[
P_k^{(m)}(u)=\mu_k^{(m)}(n-u),
\qquad
(Q^{(m)})^{*k}=\widetilde Q_{\mu_k^{(m)},p}.
\]
If \(k\ge1\), then
\begin{equation}
\mu_k^{(m)}(a)
=
\frac{1}{(n)_m^k}\binom{n}{a}
\sum_{j=0}^{a}(-1)^j\binom{a}{j}(a-j)_m^k,
\qquad
0\le a\le n,
\end{equation}
with the convention \((x)_m=0\) for \(x<m\).

body:
DRAFT hypothesis audit of w393 L1-L3, directly read by w394; further referee check pending. Use decreasing finite-box geodesic events E_n in the filtration F_n of inside edges. If predictable q_n in [0,1] satisfy P(E_(n+1)|F_n)<=1_(E_n)(1-q_n), and sum q_n diverges almost surely on infinite survival, the compensated indicator 1_(E_n) exp(sum_(j<n)q_j) is a nonnegative supermartingale and rules out survival. Positive q_n alone is insufficient: independent q_n=1/(n+1)^2 leave limiting survival probability 1/2. For an iid atomless law with mass arbitrarily near zero, the cheap-ring construction gives q_n=G([0,m/(8(n+1))))^(8(n+1)), m the minimum of the origin incident weights. These specific lower bounds are summable and therefore do not provide the needed divergence. No bound on the true killing hazards is inferred.
Decreasing F_n-measurable events
Specified conditional inequality
Divergence along survival is an additional premise
Support near zero is needed only for the displayed ring construction
title: DRAFT P0117 conditional annular killing divergence gap

[Proposition prop:sdp.certificate of arXiv:2604.22453, 'Adapted Wasserstein Barycenters of Gaussian Processes'] Let $t\in[T]$ and $\mathbf P_t\in\mathscr{P}_+(K,d)$. Suppose there exist symmetric matrices $Z_t^1,\ldots,Z_t^K\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$ such that
\begin{equation}

\mathbf S_t:=\diag(Z_t^1,\ldots,Z_t^K)-\mathbf C_t\succeq0
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\mathbf S_t\mathbf P_t=0.
\end{equation}
Then $\mathbf P_t$ minimizes $\Phi_t$ over $\mathscr{P}_+(K,d)$. Conversely, every minimizer of $\Phi_t$ over $\mathscr{P}_+(K,d)$ admits a certificate (equation eq:sdp.certificate of the paper).

  \begin{equation}
    
    Z(\mu+\delta_x)=Z(\mu), \quad x\in\mu_{Z(\mu)}.
  \end{equation}

  \eqref{eq:hull-partial}.

body:
Let n >= 2 and U_0, ..., U_n be mutually independent Rademacher variables. For every subset A of {1, ..., n} put X_A = U_0 prod_{i in A} U_i. The 2^n variables X_A are pairwise independent Rademacher variables, but they are not mutually independent: their product is identically 1.

U_0, ..., U_n are mutually independent Rademacher variables

[Theorem 7 (Simple bounded-degree configuration model: averaged version) of arXiv:2604.20514, 'Macroscopic loops in the random loop model on sparse random graphs'] Let \(G_n\) be the simple graph obtained from the configuration model with degree sequence \((d_i^{(n)})_{i=1}^n\), that is, the pairing model conditioned on simplicity. Assume that
\[
1\le d_i^{(n)}\le \Delta
\qquad\text{for all }i,n,
\]
and
\[
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n d_i^{(n)}\to \rho.
\]
Fix \(u\in[0,1]\) and \(\theta>0\). If
\begin{equation}
\rho>2c_{\theta,u}
=
2\bigl(1+\theta\max\{u,1-u\}\bigr),

\end{equation}
then there exist \(\eta>0\), \(s>0\), and \(c>0\) such that for every \(a\ge 0\),
\[
\Pbb\!\left(
\frac1s\int_a^{a+s}\Pbb^{G_n}_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\,\dd t \ge c
\right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 26 of arXiv:2608.27374, '\Large \bf Distribution-constrained optimal multiple stopping: the Root-type solution'] For all $t \geq 0$, let $Y_t=x+W_t$ with $(W_t)_{t \geq 0}$ a standard Brownian motion and $M_t:=\sup_{0\le s\le t}|W_s|$. For $K>0$, define $\delta_x(K):=\sup_{0\le r\le t} \mathbb P(X_r\le x+K)+\mathbb P(M_t>K)$.
For $\tau\in\mathcal T_t$, there exists some $K$ such that
$$g^\xi(t-\tau)-v^\xi(t-\tau,Y_\tau)\leq\delta_x(K),$$
Moreover, $\delta_x(K)\longrightarrow 0$, when $x\to -\infty$.

body:
[Theorem 19 of arXiv:2608.30991, 'A block-Toeplitz approach to the spectrum of the Neumann-Poincaré operator on self-similar'] For every $\lambda\notin\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(\widetilde K^*_\Gamma)$, the function
	$a_\lambda$ admits a right Wiener--Hopf factorisation with respect to
	$\mathbb T$ in the sense of Definition~\ref{def:app-factorisation}, with fibre
	space $H^{-1/2}_0(\Gamma_0)$,
	\[
	a_\lambda(z)=a_{\lambda,-}(z)\,\Lambda_\lambda(z)\,a_{\lambda,+}(z),
	\qquad
	\Lambda_\lambda(z)=
	\begin{pmatrix}
		z^{\nu_1} & & &\\
		& \ddots & &\\
		& & z^{\nu_J} &\\
		& & & I
	\end{pmatrix},
	\]
	where the middle factor acts on the direct sum
	$H^{-1/2}_0(\Gamma_0)=\operatorname{Im}(\Pi_1)\oplus\cdots\oplus
	\operatorname{Im}(\Pi_J)\oplus\operatorname{Im}(I-\Pi)$, where $\Pi_1,\dots,\Pi_J$ are rank-one idempotents with $\Pi_i\Pi_j=0$ for $i\neq j$, and
	$\nu_1,\dots,\nu_J\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$ are the non-zero partial indices.
	Since the Fredholm index vanishes outside the essential spectrum, these satisfy $\sum_{j=1}^{J}\nu_j=0$. Moreover
	\[
	\lambda \text{ is an eigenvalue of } \widetilde K^*_\Gamma
	\iff
	\text{the factorisation of $a_\lambda$ is non-canonical, i.e. }J\ge1,
	\]
	and in that case
	\[
	\dim\ker(\lambda I-\widetilde K^*_\Gamma)=\sum_{\nu_j<0}(-\nu_j).
	\]
	The corresponding eigenfunctions are square summable across the components of the chain.

body:
[Theorem thm:improvedBernstein of arXiv:2510.01021, '\Large Random Matrices, Intrinsic Freeness, and Sharp Non-Asymptotic Inequalities\relatedv'] Let $Y_1,\dots,Y_n\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$ be random independent symmetric matrices satisfying $\mathbb{E} Y_i=0$, and such that $\|Y_i\|\leq R$, for all $i\in[n]$, almost surely. Then
\[
\mathbb{E} \left\| \sum_{i=1}^n Y_i  \right\| \leq 2\sigma + C \Big( v^{\frac12}\sigma^{\frac12}(\log d)^\frac34 + R^{\frac13}\sigma^{\frac23}(\log d)^\frac23 + R \log d \Big),
\]
and
\[
\mathbb{P}\left[  \left\| \sum_{i=1}^n Y_i  \right\| \geq 2\sigma + C \Big( v^{\frac12}\sigma^{\frac12}(\log d)^\frac34 + \sigma_\ast t^{\frac12}+ R^{\frac13}\sigma^{\frac23}t^\frac23 + R t \Big)    \right] \leq de^{-t}
\]
where, $C$ is a universal constant, 
\begin{equation}
\sigma^2 = \left\|  \sum_{i=1}^n \mathbb{E} Y_i^2   \right\| \text{, } v^2 = \left\| \cov(Y) \right\|, R=\big\| \max_i \|Y_i\| \big\|_{\infty} \text{ and }, \sigma_\ast^2 = \sup_{\|u\|=\|w\|=1}\mathbb{E} \left| v^TYw \right|^2.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Suppose that we have the setup described above and let $(\xi_n)_{n \in \NN}$ be a sequence in $(0,\infty)$ such that $\xi_n \to \xi$ as $n \to \infty$ for some $\xi \in (0,\infty)$. Then, the sequence of metrics $(\widetilde{D}_h^{\xi_n})_{n \in \NN}$ is tight with respect to the topology induced by the convergence in Definition~\ref{def:lower_semi_cont}, and let $(\xi_{k_n})_{n \in \NN}$ be a subsequence such that $(\widetilde{D}_h^{\xi_{k_n}})_{n \in \NN}$ converges in law to some random function $\widetilde{D} : \CC \times \CC \rightarrow \RR \cup \{\pm \infty\}$. body:
[Lemma LM61 of arXiv:2412.08886, 'On domination for (non-symmetric) Dirichlet forms'] Let $({\mathscr A},\mathcal{D}({\mathscr A}))$ be a Dirichlet form on $L^2(E,m)$ satisfying ${\mathscr E}'\preceq {\mathscr A}\preceq {\mathscr E}$,  where $({\mathscr E}',{\mathscr F}')$ is assumed to be quasi-regular.  Then, there exists a locally compact separable metric space $\widehat{E}$ and a measurable map $j:E\rightarrow \widehat{E}$ such that,  by defining $\widehat{m}:=m\circ j^{-1}$,  the operator $j^*$ is a unitary map from $L^2(\widehat{E},\widehat{m})$ onto $L^2(E,m)$,  and the following hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(1)] $j$ is a quasi-homoemorphism that maps $({\mathscr E}',{\mathscr F}')$ to the quasi-regular image Dirichlet form $j({\mathscr E}',{\mathscr F}')$ on $L^2(\widehat{E},\widehat{m})$.
\item[(2)] The image Dirichlet form $j({\mathscr A},\mathcal{D}({\mathscr A}))$ is quasi-regular on $L^2(\widehat{E},\widehat{m})$.
\item[(3)] The image Dirichlet form $j({\mathscr E},{\mathscr F})$ is regular on $L^2(\widehat{E},\widehat{m})$.   
\end{itemize}
Particularly,  the domination relationship
\[
	j({\mathscr E}',{\mathscr F}')\preceq j({\mathscr A},\mathcal{D}({\mathscr A}))\preceq j({\mathscr E},{\mathscr F})
\]	
is preserved under the transformation $j$.

body:
[Thm Upsilon-ff of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] The functor $\Upsilon$ restricts to an equivalence $\textup{Glo}\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}\mathfrak O_\textup{gl}\subset{{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_\textup{gl}$.
    \begin{proof}
        We already observed above that $\Upsilon(H)\simeq\textbf{\textup{L}}(V,-)/H$ for any faithful $H$-representation $V$. It remains to show that the induced map $\Upsilon\colon{\textup{Hom}}(\mathbb B{G},\mathbb B{H})\to{\textup{Hom}}(\Upsilon(\mathbb B{G}),\Upsilon(\mathbb B{H}))$ is an equivalence for all compact Lie groups $G,H$. Fixing $H$ but varying $G$, we may equivalently show that the composite
        \begin{equation}
            {\textup{Hom}}_{\textup{Glo}}(-,\mathbb B{H})\xrightarrow{\;\Upsilon\;}{\textup{Hom}}_{{{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_\textup{gl}}(\Upsilon(-),\Upsilon(\mathbb B{H}))\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}(\ul{{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_\textup{gl})_{/(\textbf{\textup{L}}(V,-)/H)}^\circ
        \end{equation}
        with the equivalence from Proposition~(prop:the-horrible-proof-we-dont-talk-about of the paper) is invertible. By the explicit description of the latter, $((eq:Upsilon-hom-composite of the paper))$ sends $\textup{id}_{\mathbb B{H}}$ to the unit $(\textbf{\textup{L}}(V,-)\to\textbf{\textup{L}}(V,-)/H)\in{{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_\text{$H$-gl}$, and by the Yoneda lemma this uniquely characterizes the transformation. As the composite
        \[
            {\textup{Hom}}_{\textup{Glo}}(-,\mathbb B{H})\xrightarrow{\;\upsilon\;}{N_\textup{top}}\big({\textup{Fun}}_\textup{cont}(-,\cat{$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top})_{/(\textbf{\textup{L}}(V,-)/H)}^\circ\big)\xrightarrow{\;\text{loc}\;}(\ul{{\mathfrak S\kern-.4pt}}_\textup{gl})_{/(\textbf{\textup{L}}(V,-)/H)}^\circ
        \]
        has the same property, it therefore necessarily agrees with $((eq:Upsilon-hom-composite of the paper))$. The claim now follows from Proposition~(prop:lc-upsilon-equiv of the paper).
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm Upsilon-ff of arXiv:2608.28504

Let p and q be probability mass functions on a finite set S and A a subset of S with a = p(A) > 0 and b = q(A) > 0. Let c be the total variation distance between the conditional laws p(.|A) and q(.|A), d = d_TV(p, q), M = max(a, b) and m = min(a, b). Then max(|a - b|, M c) <= d <= 1 - m(1 - c), and for every a, b in (0, 1] and c in [0, 1] both ends are attained on a finite set. When the conditional laws are disjoint (c = 1) this gives M <= d <= 1 and no more: d = 1 - sum over x outside A of min(p_x, q_x), so d = 1 exactly when the restrictions of p and q to the complement of A are also disjoint. For example p = (1/2, 0, 1/2), q = (0, 1/2, 1/2) and A = {1, 2} give c = 1 and d = 1/2.

		\[

			\qquad\text{and}\qquad
			\Var\mathcal U_R(T,x)
			\longrightarrow
			T^{(4-d)/2}\Var\mathcal U(1,0)\, ,

		\[
			\mathbb{E} u_t(0)\sim \mathbb{E}\mathcal U(1,0)t^{(4-d)/4}\, ,
			\qquad
			\Var(u_t(0))\sim \Var\bigl(\mathcal U(1,0)\bigr) t^{(4-d)/2}\, .
		\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Theorem thm:law_of_sle_excursion of arXiv:2412.04005, '$\SLE_{\kappa}(\rho)$ processes in the light cone regime on\\ Liouville quantum gravity'] Fix $\kappa \in (0,4)$, $\rho \in (\kappa/2 - 4, -2)$, $\rho > -\kappa/2 - 2$.  Let $\eta$ be an ${\rm SLE}_{\kappa}(\rho)$ process in $\mathbf{H}$ from $0$ to $\infty$ with the force point located at $0_+$.  Fix $x > 0$ and let $T_x$ be the first time that~$\eta$ separates~$x$ from $\infty$.  Let $S_x = \sup\{ t < T_x : W_t = V_t\}$ be the most recent time before $T_x$ that~$\eta$ hits its force point. Then the conditional law of $\eta|_{[S_x,T_{x}]}$ given $\eta|_{[0,S_x]}$ and $\eta(T_x)$ is that of an ${\rm SLE}_{\kappa}(\rho+2; \kappa-4-\rho)$ process from $\eta(S_x)$ to $\eta(T_x)$ in $\mathbf{H}_{S_x}$ with the weight $\rho+2$ force point located at $\infty$ and the weight $\kappa-4-\rho$ force point located at $(\eta(S_x))^+$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:law_of_sle_excursion of arXiv:2412.04005

Assume that \(\boldsymbol{X}\) is scale-invariant, in the sense that
\[
\boldsymbol{X}^{(n)}_{s,t}
\sim
(t-s)^{nH}\boldsymbol{X}^{(n)}_{0,1}
\]
for every \(n=2,\ldots,\lfloor\frac1H \rfloor\) and \(0\leq s<t\leq1\). Then
\(
\boldsymbol{X}^{(n)}_{s,t}\in L^q
\)
for every \(n=2,\ldots,\lfloor\frac1H \rfloor\) and every
\(
0<q<\frac{1}{n(H-\eta)}.
\)
Consequently, \(\boldsymbol{X}\) is square-integrable, and the conclusions of
(thm:localfbm of the paper) remain valid when square-integrability is
replaced by scale-invariance.

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Given a population of size $N\in\mathbb N$, with $m\in\{0,\ldots,N\}$ of these objects having a certain feature, the probability of having $s$ successes, when performing $p\in\{0,\ldots,N\}$ draws without replacement, and looking for that feature, is
$$P(s)=\frac{\binom{m}{s}\binom{N-m}{p-s}}{\binom{N}{p}}$$
with this being called hypergeometric law of parameters $(N,m,p)$. When doing the same thing, but with replacement, we obtain a binomial law of parameter $m/N$.

[Dfn 203 (buckets for Ising perceptron) of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] For the Ising perceptron, first apply Definition~\ref{d:buckets}  to obtain $\vX^{\trunc,\RomI:\RomIII}$ and $\vX^{\frstar,\RomI:\RomIII}$. We separately apply an analogous procedure in the Ising coordinate: let 
$X^{\trunc,\Ising}(q_0) \equiv X^{\trstar,\Ising}(q_0)$
and
$X^{\frozen,\Ising}(q_0) \equiv X^{\frstar,\Ising}(q_0)$,
and suppose inductively that 
$X^{\trunc,\Ising}(q_\ell)$
and $X^{\frozen,\Ising}(q_0)$
have been defined for all $0\le\ell\le d$. Then let
    \begin{align*}
    B^\Ising(q_d, K(q_{0:d})) 
    &\equiv \Big\{ i\in[N]:
    X^{\trunc,\Ising}(q_\ell,i)
    \in K(q_{\ell})
    \textup{ for each }0\le\ell\le d
    \Big\}\,,\\
    B^{\frozen,\Ising}(q_d, K(q_{0:d})) 
    &\equiv \Big\{ i\in[N^\frozen]:
    X^{\frozen,\Ising}(q_\ell,i)
    \in K(q_\ell)
    \textup{ for each }0\le\ell\le d
    \Big\}\,,\end{align*}
analogously to \eqref{e:bucket} and \eqref{e:bucket.fr}. Then define the \textbf{buckets}
    \begin{align*}
    B^\Ising(q_d,i)
    &= \begin{cases}
    B^\Ising(q_d, K(q_{0:d}))
    &\textup{if $i\in B^\Ising(q_d, K(q_{0:d}))$,}\\
    \{i\}
    &\textup{otherwise, meaning $X^{\trunc,\Ising}(i)\notin[-\trK,\trK)$;}
    \end{cases} \\
    B^{\frozen,\Ising}(q_d,i)
    &= \begin{cases}
    B^\frozen(q_d, K(q_{0:d}))
    &\textup{if }i\in B(q_d, K(q_{0:d}))\,,\\
    \{i\}
    &\textup{otherwise, meaning }X^{\frozen,\Ising}(i)\notin[-\trK,\trK)\,.
    \end{cases}
    \end{align*}
Write $\mathcal{B}^\Ising(q_d)\equiv\{B^\Ising(q_d,i):i\in[N]\}$
and $\mathcal{B}^{\frozen,\Ising}(q_d)
\equiv\{B^{\frozen,\Ising}(q_d,i):i\in[N^\frozen]\}$. Lastly, let
    \begin{align*}
    X^{\trunc,\Ising}(q_{d+1},i)
    &=\begin{cases}
    X^{\trstar,\Ising}(q_{d+1},i)
    &\textup{if $|B^\Ising(q_d,i)| 
        \ge N/\BUCKETS^2$,}\\
    X^{\trunc,\Ising}(q_d,i)
    &\textup{otherwise.}
    \end{cases}\\
    X^{\frozen,\Ising}(q_{d+1},i)
    &=\begin{cases}
    \vX^\frstar(q_{d+1},i)
    &\textup{if $|B^{\frozen,\Ising}(q_d,i)  \cap[N]  | 
        \ge N/\BUCKETS^2$,}\\
    X^{\frozen,\Ising}(q_d,i)
    &\textup{otherwise.}
    \end{cases}
    \end{align*}
Note that when determining whether buckets are too small we only look at particle indices in $[N]$, that is, we ignore the added particles from Definition~\ref{d:froze} when determining bucket size. Altogether we denote
$\vX^\trunc\equiv(\vX^{\trunc,\RomI:\RomIII},X^{\trunc,\Ising})$ and $\vX^\frozen\equiv(\vX^{\frozen,\RomI:\RomIII},X^{\frozen,\Ising})$. One can verify by induction that the set of buckets $B^\Ising\in \mathcal{B}^\Ising(q_d)$ can be obtained by taking $B^\Ising = B^{\frozen,\Ising}\cap[N]$ for each $B^{\frozen,\Ising}\in\mathcal{B}^{\frozen,\Ising}(q_d)$.
title: buckets for Ising perceptron

[Defn 12 (Kinetic solution of the penalized equation) of arXiv:2607.28238, 'Well-posedness and large deviations for the obstacle problem of first-order stochastic con'] A predictable process $u_n$ is called a kinetic solution of \eqref{eq:penalized-hyperbolic}, if it satisfies \eqref{eq:usual moment bound} and there exists a kinetic measure $m_n$ such that $f_n=\one_{\{u_n>\xi\}}$ satisfies, for every $\varphi\in C_c^1\big(\mathbb T^N\times[0,T)\times\mathbb R\big)$,
\begin{align}
&\int_0^T\langle f_n(t),\partial_t\varphi(t)\rangle\dd t+\langle f^0,\varphi(0)\rangle+\int_0^T\langle f_n(t),a(\xi)\cdot\nabla_x\varphi(t)\rangle\,\dd t\nonumber\\
&=-\sum_{k\geq1}\int_0^T\int_{\mathbb T^N}g_k(x,u_n)\varphi(x,t,u_n)\dd x\dd\beta_k(t)\nonumber\\
&\quad-\frac12\int_0^T\int_{\mathbb{T}^N}G^2(x,u_n)\partial_\xi\varphi(x,t,u_n)\dd x\dd t\nonumber\\
&\quad+m_n(\partial_\xi\varphi)-\int_0^T\int_{\mathbb T^N}b_n(u_n-\psi)\varphi(x,t,u_n)\dd x\dd t,
\qquad\text{a.s.},
\end{align}
where
$f^0=\one_{\{u^0>\xi\}}$.
title: Kinetic solution of the penalized equation
