body:
Let F and G be two cumulative distribution functions on \mathbb{R}. The Lévy distance L(F, G) between F and G is defined as L(F, G) = \inf\{ \epsilon > 0 : F(x - \epsilon) - \epsilon \le G(x) \le F(x + \epsilon) + \epsilon \text{ for all } x \in \mathbb{R} \}.
F, G are cumulative distribution functions on \mathbb{R}
title: Lévy Metric on Distribution Functions

[Defn def:pems of arXiv:2608.30031, 'Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures'] A \textbf{model $\mathbb{T}^3$-type planar lamination} is any lamination which can be constructed starting from an irrational linear foliation on $\mathbb{T}^3$, possibly splitting open some leaves, and then possibly removing a tubular neighborhood of a transverse link to obtain a lamination on a manifold with boundary. Similarly define a \textbf{model $\mathbb{T}^2$-type planar lamination}.

    If $\Lambda$ is a lamination with a neighborhood which is lamination-preserving, boundary preserving homeomorphic to a neighborhood of some model planar lamination, then we say that $\Lambda$ is a \textbf{$\mathbb{T}^3$-type} or \textbf{$\mathbb{T}^2$-type} planar lamination respectively.
title: Defn def:pems of arXiv:2608.30031

body:
TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). In two-dimensional critical or near-critical percolation, RSW theory states that if crossing probabilities of n x n squares are uniformly bounded away from 0 as n grows, then crossing probabilities of rho n x n rectangles, for any fixed aspect ratio rho, are also uniformly bounded away from 0 by a constant depending on rho but not on n. The matching bound away from 1 needs the same input for the dual model (at criticality on a self-dual lattice it follows by duality); a lower bound for the primal model alone does not give it, since in the supercritical phase both crossing probabilities tend to 1. The classical proof glues together several square-crossing events using the FKG inequality and translation and reflection symmetry of the lattice. RSW estimates are the essential multi-scale input for proving arm-exponent bounds, conformal-invariance-adjacent results, and, via the Duminil-Copin-Tassion approach, for establishing sharpness of the phase transition without relying on exact self-duality. RSW does not by itself prove existence of a scaling limit as n -> infinity, does not give the exact value of any crossing probability, only two-sided bounds; and the classical form required exact self-duality (p=1/2 on the square lattice), so extending the theory to general planar lattices or to p != 1/2 required a genuinely new, duality-free argument (Tassion, 2016). Typical failure: Assuming that RSW-type bounded-away-from-0/1 crossing estimates transfer automatically to a new planar model merely because it is monotone and planar; RSW requires either exact self-duality or the more robust but still nontrivial Tassion-style construction, and models without FKG, or with strong enough long-range dependence, can fail to admit the needed gluing arguments even though they look superficially similar to Bernoulli percolation. Canonical reference: Russo, 1978, Zeitschrift fur Wahrscheinlichkeitstheorie und verwandte Gebiete; Seymour and Welsh, 1978, Annals of Discrete Mathematics; Tassion, 2016, Probability Theory and Related Fields.

body:
[Theorem 7 of arXiv:2608.06523, 'On the Gardner Transition in the Ising Pure $p$-Spin Glass II'] Let $\mu$ be a probability measure such that
\[
 0<q<q'<1,\qquad q,q'\in\operatorname{supp}\mu,
 \qquad \operatorname{supp}\mu\cap(q,q')=\varnothing,
\]
then the following four conditions
\begin{equation}
 \Gamma_\mu(q)=q,\qquad \Gamma_\mu(q')=q',\qquad
 \Gamma_\mu'(q)\leq1,\qquad \Gamma_\mu'(q')\leq1.
 
\end{equation}
cannot hold simultaneously.  More precisely, the endpoint
conditions would imply
\begin{equation}
 \Gamma_\mu(s)-s\Gamma_\mu'(s)>0,\qquad q<s<q'.
 
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\[
 \Gamma_\mu(s)<s,\qquad
 \Gamma_\mu(s)=s\Gamma_\mu'(s)
\]
cannot hold simultaneously for $q<s<q'$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 7 of arXiv:2608.06523

[Theorem 5 (Stability in relative entropy under partial terminal observation) of arXiv:2607.19176, 'Exponential Convergence of the Sinkhorn Algorithm for the Schrödinger Bridge with Regime S'] Let Assumptions~ \ref{assum:reference_marginals_partial}, \ref{assum:po_measures} and~\ref{assum:po_map_c2} hold for the pair $(\rho,\mu_{\mathrm p})$. Let $\bar M_0$, $\bar M_1$, and $\bar M_2$ be defined in \eqref{eq:partial_M_constants}, and set
\[
\bar B
:=
\max\left\{
\bar M_2+\frac{\bar M_1^2}{2},
\,4\bar M_0
\right\}.
\]
Then, for every $\nu_{\mathrm p}\in\mathcal P(\mathbb R^d)$ such that
\begin{equation}

H(\mu_{\mathrm p}\mid\nu_{\mathrm p})
+
H(\nu_{\mathrm p}\mid\mu_{\mathrm p})
<+\infty,
\end{equation}
one has
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal H\left(Q^{\rho,\mu_{\mathrm p}}\mid Q^{\rho,\nu_{\mathrm p}}\right)
&=
H\left(\gamma^{\rho,\mu_{\mathrm p}}\mid\gamma^{\rho,\nu_{\mathrm p}}\right)
\\
&\le
H(\mu_{\mathrm p}\mid\nu_{\mathrm p})
+
\bar B C_{\mu_{\mathrm p}}H(\nu_{\mathrm p}\mid\mu_{\mathrm p}).
\end{aligned}
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Stability in relative entropy under partial terminal observation

  \[
    p_{\varphi_{x,x'}}(T) \lesssim p_{\varphi_x}(T') + p_{\varphi_{x'}}(T') \lesssim \max_{a\in\{x,x'\}} p_{\varphi_a}(T').
  \]

[Corollary 9 of arXiv:2605.31471, 'Convergence Rates of Continuous-Time Random Walks to Time-Fractional Diffusions with Unbou'] Fix $\alpha\in\R$ and $r\in\N_0$.  Let Assumptions
    \ref{asm:classical}, \ref{asm:weighted-regular}, \ref{asm:rw},
    \ref{asm:rw-bounded}, \ref{asm:rw-weighted-stability}, and
    \ref{asm:heavy-tail} hold.  Let
    $\bar\mu_{\alpha,r}$ and $\mu_{\alpha,r+4}$ denote admissible growth
    bounds for $F_t$ and $U_h^{\lfloor s/h\rfloor}$ on
    $\cC^r_{\alpha,\infty}(\cX)$ and for $F_t$ on
    $\cC^{r+4}_{\alpha,\infty}(\cX)$, respectively.  If
    $c\ge\mu_{\alpha,r+4}\ge\bar\mu_{\alpha,r}$, then for every
    $f\in\cC^{r+4}_{\alpha,\infty}(\cX)$,
    \begin{equation} 
        \|u_h(T,\cdot)-u(T,\cdot)\|_{\alpha,r}
        \le
        C_{\alpha,r,\mathrm{frac}}\bigl(h+h^{\chi(\beta)}\bigr)
        \|f\|_{\alpha,r+4}.
    \end{equation}
    If $\bar\mu_{\alpha,r}\le c<\mu_{\alpha,r+4}$, then
    \begin{equation} 
        \|u_h(T,\cdot)-u(T,\cdot)\|_{\alpha,r}
        \le
        C_{\alpha,r,\mathrm{frac}}^{\log}
        \Bigl((\log(1/h))^{-1/\beta}+h^{\chi(\beta)}\Bigr)
        \|f\|_{\alpha,r+4}.
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Own-work draft; proof (unaudited). Fix compact intervals lambda_h in[H0,H1] and lambda_l in[L0,L1] with13673160/358811<H0<=H1<infinity and0<L0<=L1<38. {"artifact_digest":"sha256:ddf3d679f6a0e95ae15723ad39b49116bb4557f84fa9e24f1cc3b8ea1e38ea01","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/dd/ddf3d679f6a0e95ae15723ad39b49116bb4557f84fa9e24f1cc3b8ea1e38ea01.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:bf9d60fd295110c837acc17ffc46fa35cc67c9fc39712881ce89a999e711bd00","bundle_entry_key":"threshold-invariant","bundle_id":"population.adam-corrected-backward-witness-fullrank-mixed-spectrum-006","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"discrete dynamical systems and adaptive optimization","draft":"w706/bundle_006.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:optimization.adam:adam-bounded-complete-orbit-threshold-away-from-zero-gradient-rigidity","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"T421-W706-016 v3; target1; kind narrowed; proof (unaudited).

STATEMENT
Put lambda_star=13673160/358811. Fix compact intervals

 lambda_h in[H0,H1], lambda_l in[L0,L1],
 lambda_star<H0<=H1<infinity, 0<L0<=L1<38.

There exists delta>0, depending only on these intervals, such that
for EACH fixed eigenvalue pair in these intervals and EACH eta>0,
ordinary separately bias-corrected Adam with beta1=.9,beta2=.999,
epsilon=eta outside sqrt and standard zero moments satisfies

 limsup_t |eta*C_active,t-38|>=delta                     (1)

for Lebesgue-almost every initial position in R^2. The exceptional
null set may depend on the eigenvalues and eta. For fixed eigenvalues,
the conclusion holds simultaneously along any specified countable
eta sequence under any absolutely continuous joint initialization law;
coordinate independence is not assumed.

Hence generic p=1 nontracking holds for EVERY fixed pair
lambda_h>lambda_star and0<lambda_l<38. This extends016v2's fixed
[2000,3000]x[10,20] windows to the entire strict mixed unstable/subcritical
range. It does NOT include lambda_l=38, the neutral high boundary,
or the regime38<lambda_l<lambda_star. No attracting dynamics or time
average is identified. The delta is existential, not computed.

AUDIT / HARDEST PIECE
This is UNAUDITED. It uses012v2's low-cap convergence,015v3's corrected
scalar countable cycle basin and uniform local capture,023v1's direct
zero-work full-path classification, and025v1's Green origin decay.
The difficult standard-initialization cycle countability in015v3
remains an independent audit burden. Unlike021's singular-floor proof,
this proof needs no source potential or closed-relation singular lift:
the scalar high floor rho=1/lambda_h stays strictly positive.

1. NORMALIZATION, BOUNDEDNESS AND THE LOW COORDINATE
For either coordinate let X=x/eta,M=m/(eta*lambda),
V=v/(eta*lambda)^2,rho=1/lambda. The raw scalar map is

 M'=bM+(1-b)X, V'=dV+(1-d)X^2,
 X'=X-M'/(sqrt(V')+rho).                                (2)

Corrected maps have their ordinary separate clock factors. The
elementary absorbing argument in033 Section1 gives uniform tail
bounds |X|,|M|<=802,V<=802^2, after a start-dependent burn-in.
For high rho in[1/H1,1/H0], the corrected maps converge uniformly
on this compact physical box to the continuous map F_rho in(2).
Claim012v2 gives X_l,M_l,V_l->0 since lambda_l<38, regardless of its
standard initial position.

2. A NARROW ACTIVE BAND IMPOSES A CLOSED SCALAR BAND ON THE OMEGA SET
Suppose limsup |A_t-38|<delta, A_t=eta*C_active,t. Eventually its
defined values lie within delta. Multiply this inequality by the
nonnegative active denominator sum_i g_i^2/P_i. At exact zero gradient
times both extended sides are zero. All coefficients are bounded;
the low coordinate vanishes. For any point (X,M,V) of the high
omega-limit K, taking an adjacent-state limit therefore gives

 X^2*|kappa_rho(X,V)-38|<=delta*X^2,
 kappa_rho(X,V)=1/(sqrt(dV+(1-d)X^2)+rho).                (3)

The harmless positive factor1/(sqrt(V')+rho) was canceled when X!=0;
when X=0 both sides of(3) are zero. Thus(3) remains a closed constraint
at zero positions. K is nonempty compact, F_rho(K)=K, and internally
chain transitive for F_rho. To see the latter, follow a late actual
segment between visits near prescribed x,y in K. Actual tail distance
to K and corrected-map distance to F_rho tend to zero. Project each
segment node into K. Uniform continuity of F_rho bounds each chain
error separately, independently of the segment length.

3. UNIFORM SMALL-BAND REDUCTION TO CRITICAL NEIGHBORHOODS
For delta=0, EVERY full F_rho-path in a compact invariant K satisfying
(3) is a bounded full scalar zero-work path. By023 it is an origin or
cycle path, with a=1/38-rho>0. Hence K is contained in the three
critical states; internal chain transitivity forces one critical orbit.

This exact statement gives a uniform near-critical statement on the
compact rho interval. Fix sufficiently small neighborhoods of the
origin and of the two cycle phases, centered continuously in rho.
For all sufficiently small delta, EVERY compact fully invariant
internally chain-transitive K satisfying(3) lies in their union.
Otherwise take delta_n->0, rho_n converging, and offending K_n. A
Hausdorff subsequence gives K in the common physical compact box.
Uniform convergence F_rho_n->F_rho passes full invariance and(3)
to the limit. It also passes internal chain transitivity: project
the nodes of an arbitrarily fine F_rho_n-chain into K and use uniform
continuity to control each new jump, without accumulating errors.
Thus K is one critical orbit. A selected point outside the chosen
neighborhoods persists outside at the limit, a contradiction.

Choose OUTER neighborhoods first, with these properties uniformly
over rho: they are disjoint; a corrected late step with both ends in
their union cannot change orbit groups or select a wrong cycle phase;
cycle neighborhoods are within015v3's uniform physical capture region;
the origin neighborhood is small enough for the uniform Green estimate
in Section4. Uniform continuity at the separated critical states and
compactness give the nonjump conditions. Use INNER half-radius
neighborhoods for the preceding compactness reduction. For delta small
enough, K lies in the inner union; hence the actual tail lies in the
outer union. Nonjump separation makes it eventually stay in the
origin group or the alternating cycle group.

4. THE ORIGIN ALTERNATIVE CONTRADICTS THE ACTIVE BAND
For high lambda in[H0,H1], the limiting position-pair matrix

 A_h=[[1+b-(1-b)*lambda_h,-b],[1,0]]

has real roots -b<r_s<0,r_u<-1. Their gaps from b and the unit circle
are uniform on the compact high interval. Choose
sup |r_s|<q<nu<b. Eigenbases and inverses are uniformly bounded.
The origin neighborhood and late clocks can be chosen so the actual
position-pair coefficients, throughout that neighborhood, are close
enough to A_h for BOTH Green contractions in036 Section2 (weighted
q and bounded weight1). This argument requires only boundedness and
small coefficient perturbations, NOT prior origin convergence.
Consequently a high-coordinate tail staying in this neighborhood has
|X_h,t|<=C*q^t. Stable raw moment and variance recursions then imply
M_h,V_h->0 as well. Thus both coordinates actually approach their origins.

If the standard low initial position is nonzero,025 gives a subsequence
of active sharpness tending to lambda_l<=L1<38. This is incompatible
with an eventual band delta<(38-L1)/2. We may remove the line x_l,0=0
as a null exceptional set; no assertion on that line is needed here.
Thus the origin alternative is excluded for almost every start.

For clarity, the low-coordinate lower-rate estimate can be chosen
uniformly too: the explicit matrix Q in036 Eq10 is positive definite
for fixed nu<b and every low trace T with |T|<=1+b. It obeys
A_l^T Q A_l=nu^2 Q+A_l^T A_l. On compact low parameters its strict
gain margin is uniform, and actual coefficients approach A_l once
the low coordinate decays. This confirms the rate comparison across
the whole stated low interval, including repeated-root parameters.

5. THE CYCLE ALTERNATIVE HAS A NULL STANDARD-INITIALIZATION SET
If the actual high tail stays in the alternating cycle neighborhoods,
015v3's corrected local capture gives convergence to that scalar cycle.
Here rho<=1/H0<rho_star, and015v3 applies uniformly on this compact
range. For fixed eta and lambda_h, its standard initial positions
converging to this corrected cycle form a countable set. Thus full
initial positions reaching this alternative lie on countably many
vertical lines. Together with the removed low-zero line they have
Lebesgue measure zero. No product law or coordinate independence is
needed. Outside this exceptional set, the assumed strict limsup band
is impossible, proving(1).

Active quotients at finite zero-gradient times can be treated either
by the zero extension used in Section2 or by removing their null
initial lines. For fixed finite time, a nonzero scalar standard initial
position maps analytically to its position on either sign half-line:
positive raw variance after the first update makes all subsequent
square roots analytic. The bounded-increment properness estimate
prevents that analytic function from being identically zero. Its
zeros are countable. Hence the countable union of finite-time zero
events is null, and generic trajectories have all their quotients
defined. Along any specified countable eta sequence, union the null
exceptional sets; an absolutely continuous joint law still assigns
zero mass. This gives the stated simultaneous conclusion.

CHECKS AND LIMITS
Zero-work identities: logs/zero_work_algebra_exact.json.
General low-gain certificate: logs/origin_rate_algebra_exact.json.
Hyperbolic high cycle range: audited003v1 plus015v3's proof031;
logs/unstable_window_exact.json. Exact finite algebra is not an
independent audit of the compactness, capture or countability arguments.
Unlike016v2, no fixed numerical high/low eigenvalue windows are used.
Unlike021, no singular rho->0 limit is used. The theorem remains an

[Lemma 16 (Properties of Poisson-Voronoi percolation) of arXiv:2504.02435, 'Poisson-Voronoi percolation in higher rank'] Let $G$ be a non-compact connected semisimple real Lie group, $(X,d_X)$ be its symmetric space, $\lambda>0$ and $p\in (0,1)$.
    Then $\omega_p^{(\lambda)}$ defines a random closed subset of $X$ which
    \begin{itemize}
        \item[{\rm (i)}] is $G$-invariant and ergodic, and, moreover, is invariant under all isometries of $(X,d_X)$.
        \item[{\rm (ii)}] satisfies the Harris-FKG-inequality.
        \item[{\rm (iii)}] satisfies $\mathbb P\big(o\in \partial \omega_p^{(\lambda)}\big)=0$.
    \end{itemize}
    Moreover, the Voronoi diagram $\mathrm{Vor}(\mathbf{Y}^{(\lambda)})$ consists of compact subsets of $X$.
title: Properties of Poisson-Voronoi percolation

[Definition def:tfcob of arXiv:2608.27771, 'A normal form for the Thin Flat Surfaces category'] A \textbf{thin-flat cobordism} from $n$ to $m$ is an oriented compact surface $S$
with corners whose boundary decomposes into $\partial S = \partial_v S \cup \partial_h S$,
where $\partial_v S$ consists of $n$ incoming boundary intervals and $m$ outgoing
boundary intervals, and every boundary component is subdivided into alternating
horizontal and vertical boundary arcs.  Two such tf-cobordisms are considered
equivalent if they are diffeomorphic relative to the vertical boundary.
title: Definition def:tfcob of arXiv:2608.27771

[Lemma 11 of arXiv:2506.10522, 'On the Law of the Iterated Logarithm for $m$-dependent stationary random variables under s'] Let $\{X_n; n\ge 1\}$ be a martingale difference sequence in a probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},P)$ with respect to the
filtration $\{\mathcal F_n\}$ such that $|X_n|\le  m_n$ a.s. for some $\mathcal F_{n-1}$-measurable random variable
$m_n$, with $U_n\to \infty$  and $m_n/\{U_n(\log\log U_n)^{-1/2}\}\to 0$  a.s., where $U_n^2=\sum_{i=1}^n X_i^2$.  Then
$$ \limsup_{n\to \infty}\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n X_i}{U_n(2\log\log U_n)^{1/2}}=1\;\; a.s. $$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem SLLN-CLT-geometric-bessel of arXiv:2512.10625, 'Bessel and Dunkl processes with drift'] Let $R$ be a root system and $k\ge0$ a multiplicity such that the associated Dunkl-Bessel theory fits to some geometric case.
  Let $(X_t^\lambda)_{t\ge0}$ be a Bessel process on some associated closed Weyl chamber $C\subset \mathbb R^N$
  with some drift $\lambda$ with start in 0.
Then
    $$\lim_{t\to\infty} \frac{X_t^\lambda}{t} = \lambda \quad{a.s.}.$$
Moreover, if  $\lambda$ is in
  the interior of $C$, then
   $(X_t^\lambda-t\lambda)/\sqrt t$ tends in distribution
to  $N(0,I_N)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem SLLN-CLT-geometric-bessel of arXiv:2512.10625

body:
[Theorem 2 (Hydrodynamic limit) of arXiv:2607.23640, '{\sl Non-equilibrium fluctuations of a two-species exclusion process with slow boundary }'] Let \(\{\mu^n\}_{n\in\mathbb N}\) be a sequence of probability measures on \(\Omega_n\) associated with \(\bm\rho_0\). 
	Then, for every \(t\in[0,T]\), every \(\delta>0\), every \(k\in\{1,2\}\), and every \(f_k\in C^\infty([0,1];\mathbb R) \),
	\[
	\lim_{n\to\infty}
	\mathbb P_{\mu^n}^n
	\left(
	\left|
	X_k^{n,t}(f_k)
	-
	\int_0^1 f_k(u)\rho_k(t,u)\,du
	\right|>\delta
	\right)
	=0,
	\]
	where $ \bm\rho(t,u)
	=
	\begin{pmatrix}
		\rho_1(t,u)\\
		\rho_2(t,u)
	\end{pmatrix} $
    is the unique weak solution of the reaction-diffusion system with Robin boundary conditions
	\begin{equation}
		\begin{cases}
			\partial_t\bm\rho(t,u)
			=
			\Delta\bm\rho(t,u)+M\bm\rho(t,u),
			& t>0,\ u\in(0,1),\\[0.2cm]
			\partial_u\bm\rho(t,0)
			=
			K_L\bm\rho(t,0)-\bm\alpha,
			& t>0,\\[0.2cm]
			\partial_u\bm\rho(t,1)
			=
			\bm\beta-K_R\bm\rho(t,1),
			& t>0,\\[0.2cm]
			\bm\rho(0,u)=\bm\rho_0(u),
			& u\in[0,1].
		\end{cases}
	\end{equation}
	Here $ \bm \alpha = \left( \alpha_1,\alpha_2 \right)^{\top} $, $ \bm \beta = \left( \beta_1,\beta_2 \right)^{\top} $, and
	\[
	M=
	\begin{pmatrix}
		-\gamma_1 & \gamma_2\\
		\gamma_1 & -\gamma_2
	\end{pmatrix},
	\qquad
	K_L=
	\begin{pmatrix}
		1-\alpha_2 & \alpha_1\\
		\alpha_2 & 1-\alpha_1
	\end{pmatrix},
	\qquad
	K_R=
	\begin{pmatrix}
		1-\beta_2 & \beta_1\\
		\beta_2 & 1-\beta_1
	\end{pmatrix}.
	\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Hydrodynamic limit

[Theorem 39 (Ramified relative de Rham lattice at the irregular boundary) of arXiv:2608.14475, '\vspace{-1.2cm}\textbf{Finite Gaussian Reconstruction of Polynomial Orbits:\\ From Correla'] Let \(P=P_m+\cdots+P_0\) satisfy
\eqref{eq:principal-isolated} and set
\[
 t=s^{m-2},
 \qquad
 x=s^{-1}u,
 \qquad
 G(u)=-\frac{q(u)}{2}+iP_m(u).
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 F_{P,s^{m-2}}(s^{-1}u)
 =
 \frac{G(u)}{s^2}
 +\frac{iP_{m-1}(u)}s
 +\sum_{k=0}^{m-2}i\,s^{m-2-k}P_k(u).
 
\end{equation}
The rescaled differential
\[
 \mathfrak D_s
 =
 s^2\left(
  \mathrm d_u+
  \mathrm d_uF_{P,s^{m-2}}(s^{-1}u)\wedge
 \right)
\]
extends over \(s=0\) and has the form
\begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
 \mathfrak D_s
 &=
 \mathrm dG\wedge
 +is\,\mathrm dP_{m-1}\wedge\\
 &\quad
 +s^2\bigl(\mathrm d_u+i\,\mathrm dP_{m-2}\wedge\bigr)
 +\sum_{k=0}^{m-3}i\,s^{m-k}\mathrm dP_k\wedge.
 \end{split}
 
\end{equation}
On the \(s\)-adic completion of polynomial forms, it deformation retracts
onto
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal J(G)[[s]][-d],
 \qquad
 \mathcal J(G)
 =
 \C[u_1,\ldots,u_d]/
 (\partial_1G,\ldots,\partial_dG),
 
\end{equation}
which is free of rank \(\mu=(m-1)^d\).  Thus
the relative \(u\)-de Rham cohomology is a free \(\C[[s]]\)-lattice of
rank \(\mu\) for the ramified rescaled model at \(s=0\).  We call it the
ramified Rees--Jacobi lattice.  No connection in the \(s\)-direction, or
stability under such a connection, is asserted here.

If \(G\) is Morse with pairwise distinct critical values and
\(c_1,\ldots,c_\mu\) are its critical points, then steepest descent on
the continued thimbles gives the leading asymptotic exponential factors
\begin{equation}
 \exp\!\left(
  \frac{G(c_\alpha)}{s^2}
  +\frac{iP_{m-1}(c_\alpha)}s
  +O(1)
 \right),
 \qquad 1\leq\alpha\leq\mu.
 
\end{equation}
In particular, the principal asymptotic directions of the
thimble-switching walls between two distinct levels satisfy
\[
 \Im\!\left(
  \frac{G(c_\alpha)-G(c_\beta)}{s^2}
 \right)=0.
\]
The equal-magnitude rays instead satisfy
\[
 \Re\!\left(
  \frac{G(c_\alpha)-G(c_\beta)}{s^2}
 \right)=0.
\]

body:
[Proposition prop:NL-MC-construction of arXiv:2607.00800, 'Brownian motion in Minkowski normed spaces'] For each $z \in \mathbb{R}^d$, let $u^z$ be a probability solution to the nonlinear Fokker--Planck equation (equation gen-nl-fpe of the paper) with initial datum $z$, such that
    \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
        \item $(t,z) \mapsto u^z(t,x) \,\mathrm d x$ is injective from $[0,\infty)\times \mathbb{R}^d$ to  $\mathcal P$ (here we write $u^z(0,x) \,\mathrm d x := \delta_z$);

        \item for each $z \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and $s \in [0,\infty)\setminus \{0\}$, $u^z_{s+}$ is an extreme point in the convex set of probability solutions to (equation gen:lin-fpe of the paper) with $u^z(s+t)$ replacing $v(t)$ and with initial datum $u^z(s,x) \,\mathrm d x$.
    \end{enumerate}
    Then, for each $z \in \mathbb{R}^d$, there exists a unique weak solution $X^z$ to the McKean--Vlasov SDE (equation gen-DDSDE of the paper) with the prescribed one-dimensional time marginals $\mathcal{L}(X^z_t) = u^z(t,x) \,\mathrm d x$, $t > 0$, and $X^z_0 = z$. 
    The family of solution path laws $\{P^z\}_{z\in \mathbb{R}^d}$, $P^z = \mathcal{L}(X^z)$, is a nonlinear Markov core for $\{u^z(t)\}_{t>0, z\in \mathbb{R}^d}$ and is uniquely determined by $\{u^z\}_{z \in \mathbb{R}^d}$ and (equation gen-DDSDE of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Let X be a Banach space and A: D(A) ⊂ X → X linear and densely defined. (1) If A is dissipative and Ran(λ_0 − A) = X for some λ_0 > 0, then A is closed, Ran(λ − A) = X for every λ > 0, and A generates a contraction C_0-semigroup. (2) If A is dissipative and Ran(λ_0 − A) is merely dense for some λ_0 > 0, then A is closable, its closure Ā is dissipative with Ran(λ − Ā) = X for all λ > 0, and Ā generates a contraction C_0-semigroup. (3) Conversely, if A generates a contraction C_0-semigroup, then A is densely defined, closed, Ran(λ − A) = X for all λ > 0, and A is dissipative in the strong sense that Re⟨Ax, x*⟩ ≤ 0 for every x ∈ D(A) and every x* ∈ J(x). (4) If X is reflexive, a dissipative A with Ran(λ_0 − A) = X for some λ_0 > 0 is automatically densely defined. (5) Hilbert space corollary: if A is densely defined and closed and both A and A* are dissipative, then A generates a contraction C_0-semigroup; and a densely defined symmetric operator S with S ≤ 0 that is self-adjoint generates the contraction semigroup e^{tS}. Quasi-contractive version: if A − ω is dissipative and Ran(λ_0 − A) = X for some λ_0 > ω, then A generates a C_0-semigroup with ‖T(t)‖ ≤ e^{ωt}.
X is a Banach space
A is densely defined (automatic in reflexive X under the range condition)
A is dissipative
a range condition: Ran(λ_0 − A) = X (or dense) for some λ_0 > 0

[Prop ideal equality of arXiv:2609.04023, 'Characterizing Contractions and Weighted Blowdowns'] Suppose $\mathcal{X}$ and $\mathcal{Z}$ are smooth separated Deligne--Mumford stacks of dimension $n$, and there is a representable contraction $f : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Z}$ where the exceptional $\mathcal{E}$ is a smooth irreducible Cartier divisor. 
    Moreover, suppose there is a smooth closed irreducible Deligne--Mumford substack $\mathcal{Y} \subseteq \mathcal{Z}$ such that $(f^{-1}\mathcal{Y}) \simeq \mathcal{E}$ set-theoretically, and $f : \mathcal{X} \setminus \mathcal{E} \xrightarrow{\sim} \mathcal{Z} \setminus \mathcal{Y}.$ Then $f^{-1}\mathcal{I}_{\mathcal{Y}/\mathcal{Z}}.\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{X}\simeq\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{X}(-\mathcal{E})$, as ideal sheaves on $\mathcal{X}$. Here $f^{-1}\mathcal{I}_{\mathcal{Y}/\mathcal{Z}}\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{X}:=\operatorname{im}(f^\ast\mathcal{I}_{\mathcal{Y}/\mathcal{Z}}\rightarrow \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{X})$. Furthermore, $\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{X}(-\mathcal{E})$ is relatively ample with respect to $f:\mathcal{X}\rightarrow \mathcal{Z}$.

\[
  I^{\lambda,\mu,\mathrm{u}}_t\ \subseteq\ I^{\infty,\mu,\mathrm{i}}_t\qquad\text{for every }t\ge0 ,

body:
[Theorem 9 (Linear-subspace characterization) of arXiv:2609.00673, '2609.00673'] Let the Frenet data satisfy the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:phase-parametrization}, and set
\[
x_i=\tan\frac{\theta_i}{2},\qquad x=(x_1,\ldots,x_{n-1})^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Define torsion-dependent offsets by
\[
\beta_1=0,\qquad \beta_{i+1}=\pi-\phi_i-\beta_i,
\quad 1\le i\le n-2,
\]
and vectors $a,b\in\mathbb R^{n-1}$ by
\[
a_i=\cos\beta_i,
\qquad
b_i=-(-1)^{i-1}\sin\beta_i.
\]
Then the data arise from a discrete general helix with a non-orthogonal axis if and only if
\[
\boxed{\ x\in\operatorname{span}\{a,b\}.\ }
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\operatorname{rank}[a\ b\ x]=\operatorname{rank}[a\ b].
\]
If $\operatorname{rank}[a\ b]=2$, the coefficients $u,v$ in $x=ua+vb$ are unique, $u=x_1>0$, and
\[
\tan\alpha=\sqrt{u^2+v^2},
\qquad
\psi_1=\operatorname{atan2}(v,u).
\]
If $\operatorname{rank}[a\ b]=1$ and the membership condition holds, then necessarily $\phi_i=\pi$ for every $i$ and $x_i$ is constant; this is the fully alternating nonuniqueness case.

body:
Let X be a Banach space, K : X -> X a compact linear operator, and T = I - K. Then: (i) ker T is finite-dimensional and the range of T is closed; (ii) T is injective if and only if it is surjective, and in that case T has a bounded inverse; (iii) dim ker T = dim ker T* where T* = I - K* is the adjoint on the dual X*, and the equation T x = y is solvable exactly when y annihilates ker T* (the closed-range theorem). So either T x = y has a unique solution for every y, or the homogeneous equation T x = 0 has a nontrivial finite-dimensional solution space and T x = y is solvable exactly for y orthogonal (in the duality sense) to the finitely many solutions of the adjoint homogeneous equation. For a Hilbert space and a self-adjoint compact K this is the classical alternative for integral equations of the second kind; the same conclusions hold for lambda I - K with any nonzero lambda.

K compact and linear

[Theorem 2 (The splitting field and $X(14)$) of arXiv:2609.03455, '2609.03455'] The modular function field $\A_0(\G(14))$ is the splitting field of
\eqref{eq:main-cubic-intro} over $\A_0(\G(7))$.  More precisely,
\[
 \A_0(\G(14))
 =
 \C(\u,\psi,g_1,\delta)
 =
 \C(\u,\psi,g_1,g_2),
\]
where $\delta$ is a suitably normalized square root of the discriminant
of $P_\u(T)$.  Consequently an affine model of $X(14)$ is given by
\begin{equation}
 \left\{ \ 
 \begin{aligned}
  &Y^7=X^4(X-1),\\
  &XZ^3+XZ^2-(X^2-1)Z+(X-1)^2=0,\\
  &W^2=X(X-1)(X^3-8X^2+5X+1).
 \end{aligned}
 \right.
\end{equation}
Here $X=\u$, $Y=\psi$, $Z=g_1$ and $W=\delta$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Ppn 132 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let $u,v$ be real numbers such that $v\geq u^2 - \bar{\lambda}$, and let $P_1,P_2>0$.
Set
\beq
    \sigma 
    \equiv
    \bigg(
    \frac{P_1v + 2
    (P_1P_2)^{1/2}
    u+P_2}{P_1+P_2}
    \bigg)^{1/2}
\eeq
Then we have the bound
\beq
  u^2 + \Big((v-u^2 + 2\bar{\lambda})^{1/2}-1\Big)^2 
  \ge \bigg(1+\frac{P_2}{P_1}\bigg)(\sigma-1)^2\,.
\eeq
Given any $\sigma\ge0$, if we let $(u,v)$ be defined by the equations
	\[
	u^2 = \frac{P_2}{P_1}(\sigma-1)^2 
	= v-\sigma^2 + 2\bar{\lambda}\,,
	\]
then $(u,v)$ achieves equality in both \eqref{e:sigma.of.u.v} and \eqref{eq:u-v-to-sigma-bound}. 

\begin{proof}
Denote $\tilde{v}\equiv v-u^2 + 2\bar{\lambda} \ge0$. The above definition of $\sigma$ can then be rewritten as
	\beq    
	(P_1+P_2)\sigma^2
	= P_1 \tilde{v}  +
	\Big( (P_1)^{1/2} u + (P_2)^{1/2}
	\Big)^2\,.
	\eeq
Consider optimizing the left-hand side of \eqref{eq:u-v-to-sigma-bound} subject to the constraint 
\eqref{eq:LM-constraint}: the Lagrangian is
	\[
	\mathscr{L}
	= u^2 + \Big(\tilde{v}^{1/2}-1\Big)^2 
	+ \lambda
	\bigg\{
	(P_1+P_2)\sigma^2
	- P_1 \tilde{v}  -
	\Big( (P_1)^{1/2} u + (P_2)^{1/2}
	\Big)^2
	\bigg\}\,.
	\]
The Lagrangian stationarity conditions are
	\begin{align*}
	0&=\frac{\partial\mathscr{L}}
		{\partial u}
	= 2u - 2\lambda (P_1)^{1/2}
	\Big( (P_1)^{1/2} u + (P_2)^{1/2}
	\Big)\,\\
	0&=\frac{\partial\mathscr{L}}
		{\partial\tilde{v}}
	= 1-\frac{1}{\tilde{v}^{1/2}}
	- \lambda P_1\,.
	\end{align*}
Simplifying the above equations gives
	\[
	u
	= \bigg(\frac{P_2}{P_1}\bigg)^{1/2}
	 \frac{\lambda P_1}{1-\lambda P_1}
	=
	\bigg(\frac{P_2}{P_1}\bigg)^{1/2}
	(\tilde{v}^{1/2}-1)
	\,.
	\]
Combining this with \eqref{eq:LM-constraint} gives $\sigma^2=\tilde{v}$. Substituting this back into the left-hand side of \eqref{eq:u-v-to-sigma-bound} gives
	\[
	u^2 + (\tilde{v}^{1/2}-1)^2
	= \bigg(1+ \frac{P_2}{P_1}\bigg)
	(\tilde{v}^{1/2}-1)^2
	= \bigg(1+ \frac{P_2}{P_1}\bigg)
	(\sigma-1)^2\,,
	\]
so \eqref{eq:u-v-to-sigma-bound} holds with equality in the case of an interior stationary point. It remains to check the boundary case $\tilde{v}=0$. In this case we have
	\[
	\sigma
	=\bigg|\bigg( \frac{P_1}{P_1+P_2}\bigg)^{1/2} u
	+\bigg( \frac{P_2}{P_1+P_2}\bigg)^{1/2}\bigg|
	\equiv
	\Big| (A_1)^{1/2} u + (A_2)^{1/2}
	\Big|\,,
	\]
with $A_1+A_2=1$. The desired bound \eqref{eq:u-v-to-sigma-bound} then simplifies to
	\begin{align*}
	u^2 + 1
	&= \bigg(\frac{-(A_2)^{1/2}\pm\sigma}{(A_1)^{1/2}}\bigg)^2+1
	= \frac{A_2 + \sigma^2
		\pm 2 (A_2)^{1/2}\sigma}{A_1}
		+1
	= \frac{1+\sigma^2
		\pm 2 (A_2)^{1/2}\sigma}{A_1}
	\\
	&\ge
	\frac{1 + \sigma^2-2\sigma}{A_1}
	= \bigg(1+\frac{P_2}{P_1}\bigg)(\sigma-1)^2\,,
	\end{align*}
which gives the bound for the boundary case $\tilde{v}=0$. This concludes the proof.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

The Hadamard conjecture states that a Hadamard matrix of order 4k exists for every positive integer k. A necessary condition for the existence of an n x n Hadamard matrix with n > 2 is that n is divisible by 4, but whether this condition is sufficient remains an unsolved problem.
k is a positive integer

[Definition 4 of arXiv:2605.02430, '\textbf{Scaling limit of the range of tree-valued branching random walks in random environ'] (\textbf{Contour process}) $(\textbf{a})\, $ Let $\fftree\ino \bbT$, possibly infinite.  
Let $(v_k)_{0\leq k \leq 2(\# t-1)}$ (with an obvious convention if $\# t \eqo \infty$) 
the sequence of vertices of $\fftree$ be defined recursively as follows.

\smallskip

\begin{compactenum}
\item[] \emph{We set $v_{0}\eqo \varnothing$ and $R_k \eqo\{ w\ino  \fftree\backslash \{v_0,  \ldots, v_k\} : \overleftarrow{w}\eqo v_k \}$; if $R_k$ is empty, then we set 
$v_{k+1} \eqo \overleftarrow{v}_{\! \! k}$; otherwise we take $v_{k+1}$ as the $<_{\mathtt{lex}}$-least vertex of $R_k$.}
\end{compactenum}

\smallskip
\noi
We call $(v_k)$ the exploration of $t$ in the \emph{contour order}.  

\smallskip 

\noi
$(\textbf{b})\, $ Let $t\ino \bbT$ be finite. For all $k\ino \lgeo 0, 2(\# t \! -\! 1)\rgeo$ we set $C_k (t)\eqo |v_k|$ and we conveniently set $C_{2\# t \! -\! 1} (t)\eqo  C_{2\# t} (t)\eqo 0$. We next extends $C(t)$ continuously on $[0, 2\#t]$ by setting for all $k\ino \lgeo 0, 2\# t \! -\! 1\rgeo$ and all $s\ino [0, 1]$: $ C_{k+s}(\fftree) \eqo C_k (\fftree)+ s (C_{k+1} (\fftree) \! -\! C_k (\fftree))$. 
The resulting continuous function $s\ino [0, 2\#t ] \! \mapsto  \! C_s(\fftree)$ is called the \emph{contour process} of $\fftree$. 

\smallskip 

\noi
$(\textbf{c})\, $ Let $t\ino \bbT$ be the tree associated with the forest of finite trees 
$(t^{_{(k)}}_{^{\,}})_{k\in \bbN^*}$ (Definition \ref{Ulamtree} $(\textbf{c})$). The contour process of the forest is denoted by $C(t)$. It is obtained by concatenating the $C(t^{_{(k)}}_{^{\,}}) $ in the following way. Recall notation $\sigma_k$ from Definition \ref{Lukadef} $(\textbf{b})$. Then for all $k\ino \bbN^*$, all $ s\ino [ 2\sigma_{k-1}, 2\sigma_k] $, we set $C_{s} (t)\eqo 
C_{s-2\sigma_{k-1}} (t^{_{(k)}}_{^{\,}})$.  \cq

body: In mathematics, the probabilistic method is a nonconstructive method, primarily used in combinatorics and pioneered by Paul Erdős, for proving the existence of a prescribed kind of mathematical object. It works by showing that if one randomly chooses objects from a specified class, the probability that the result is of the prescribed kind is strictly greater than zero. Although the proof uses probability, the final conclusion is determined for certain, without any possible error.
title: Probabilistic method

Consequently risk>=c[1+min(BT,T^2)]^-s uniformly in eta,beta,B,T; for B=D^(b+o(1)), the data exponent is at most s min(1,2(1-b)). For fixed B and 1<s<2-1/alpha, even horizon-retuned stable HB cannot improve the exponent s attained by a fixed-step SGD setting. This is a necessary barrier, not an attainable threshold.
alpha>1,s>1,C>0
fresh independent Gaussian mini-batches, noiseless labels
w_0=w_-1=0
B,T positive integers
eta>0,0<=beta<1 constant during each run
global stability: d_1>0, S<1; horizon-dependent choice allowed

body:
[Lemma lem:stationary-derivative-band-partition-paper of arXiv:2606.08683, 'Exact Fourier dimensions of dyadic Mandelbrot cascades under minimal integrability'] There exists an absolute constant \(C\ge1\) such that, for every \(\xi\neq0\), there exist nonnegative \(C^1\) functions
\[
\chi_{\xi,\mathrm{stat}},
\qquad
\chi_{\xi,d}\quad(d\in\mathfrak D_\xi),
\]
on \(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}\), where \(\mathfrak D_\xi\) is a finite set of dyadic numbers, satisfying the following properties.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item Partition of unity:
\[
\chi_{\xi,\mathrm{stat}}(t)+\sum_{d\in\mathfrak D_\xi}\chi_{\xi,d}(t)=1
\qquad(t\in\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}).
\]

\item Number of bands:
\[
\#\mathfrak D_\xi\le C(1+\log_2(2+\Lambda)).
\]

\item Stationary tube:
\[
\operatorname{spt}\chi_{\xi,\mathrm{stat}}
\subset
\{t:\operatorname{dist}(t,Z_\xi)\le C\Lambda^{-1/2}\}.
\]

\item Localization of derivative bands:
for every \(d\in\mathfrak D_\xi\),
\[
C^{-1}\Lambda^{-1/2}\le d\le C,
\]
and
\[
\operatorname{spt}\chi_{\xi,d}
\subset
\{t:C^{-1}d\le\operatorname{dist}(t,Z_\xi)\le Cd\}.
\]

\item Derivative size:
on \(\operatorname{spt}\chi_{\xi,d}\),
\[
C^{-1}\Lambda d\le \lvert\phi_\xi'(t)\rvert\le C\Lambda d.
\]

\item Cutoff derivative:
\[
\lvert\chi_{\xi,d}'(t)\rvert\le Cd^{-1}.
\]

\item Bounded overlap:
\[
\sum_{d\in\mathfrak D_\xi}\mathbf 1_{\operatorname{spt}\chi_{\xi,d}}(t)\le C
\qquad(t\in\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}).
\]
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Lemma 17 (Error Decomposition and Control) of arXiv:2506.20789, 'Central limit theory for Peaks-over-Threshold partial sums of long memory linear time seri'] Let Assumptions~\ref{asu:coef},~\ref{asu:G_n} and~\ref{asu:f} hold, let $k_0$ be as defined by Lemma~\ref{lem:f}, and let $k>k_0$.
  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item
    We can write
    $
    P_{-k}\,\mathcal{U}_n(X_0)
     =
    R_1
     +
    R_2
     +
    R_3
    $,
    where
  \begin{align*}
    R_1
    &\ := \
    G_{k-1,n}(X_0-X_{0,k-1})
    \ - \
    \int
    G_{k-1,n}(X_0-X_{0,k}+a_kz)
    \,\mathrm{d}\PP_\varepsilon(z)
    \\&
    \qquad\ - \
    a_k\cdot\varepsilon_{-k}
    \cdot
    G'_{k-1,n}(X_0-X_{0,k})
    \,,
    \\
    R_2
    &\ := \
    a_k\cdot\varepsilon_{-k}
    \left(
    G_{\infty,n}'(X_0-X_{0,k})
    \ - \
    G_{\infty,n}'(0)
    \right)
    \,,
    \\
    R_3&\ := \
    a_k\cdot\varepsilon_{-k}
    \left(
    G_{k-1,n}'(X_0-X_{0,k})
    \ - \
    G_{\infty,n}'
(X_0-X_{0,k})
    \right)
    \,.
  \end{align*}
  \item
    Let $\gamma\in(0,1)$ and $r\in[1,2]$ such that
  \begin{align*}
    \gamma_G
    \ < \
    \gamma
    \ < \
\min
\left\{
    \frac{d}{1-d}
    \,,
    1
    -
    \frac{1}{r(1-d)}
    \,,
    \frac{\alpha}{r}
    -
    1
\right\}
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    \frac{1}{1-d}
    \ < \
    r
    \ < \
    \alpha
    \,.
  \end{align*}
    For each $j\in\{1,2,3\}$, we have
    $
    \norm{R_j}_{L^r(\PP)}
    \
 \lesssim
    \
      k^{-(1-d)(1+\gamma)}
      \cdot
      u_n^{-\gamma+\gamma_G}
    $.
    Therefore
    \begin{align}
      
      \norm{
      P_{-k}\, \mathcal{U}_n(X_0)
      }_{L^r(\PP)}
      \
      \lesssim
      \
      k^{-(1-d)(1+\gamma)}
      \cdot
      u_n^{-\gamma+\gamma_G}
      \,.
    \end{align}
   \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary 5 of arXiv:2609.02193, 'State-law dynamics of McKean-Vlasov stochastic reaction-diffusion equations on $\mathbb R^'] Under the assumptions of Proposition~\ref{PrLawProjection}, suppose that $\mathcal A_P=\{\mu^*\}$. Then $\varphi_P(t)\mu^*=\mu^*$ for every $t\geq0$, and
	\begin{align}
		\psi(t,\omega)x
		=
		\varphi_X(t,\omega,x,\mu^*)
	\end{align}
	defines a continuous random dynamical system on $X$. Moreover,
	\begin{align}
		\mathcal A(\omega)
		=
		A_X(\omega)\times\{\mu^*\},
		\qquad
		A_X(\omega)=\Pi_X\mathcal A(\omega),
	\end{align}
	and $A_X$ is the unique $\mathfrak D_X$-pullback random attractor for $\psi$.

[Theorem thm:FFR of arXiv:2609.01557, '$L^\infty$ Variational Approximation of the Aubry Set'] Let \(M\) be a smooth manifold and let \(H:T^*M\to\mathbb R\) be a Tonelli Hamiltonian.  
The Mather quotient has vanishing one-dimensional Hausdorff measure in either of the following cases:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
    \item \(\dim M=1\) or \(2\) and \(H\in C^2\);
    \item \(\dim M=3\) and \(H\in C^{k,1}\) for some \(k\geq3\).
\end{enumerate}
That is,
\[
    \mathcal H^1(\mathcal A_M,\delta_M)=0.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Definition 4 (Granularity) of arXiv:2608.25188, 'Transforms for LLM Quantization:\\ The Great Inversion and Format Co-Design'] A scale may be shared \emph{per-tensor} (one $s$), \emph{per-row} (one $s$ per output row of $W$, the \emph{per-output-channel} weight scale, which the weight-only literature usually just calls \emph{per-channel}, or one $s$ per token row of $X$, the \emph{per-token} activation scale that is the deployed default), \emph{per-column} (one $s$ per input channel, the axis a \emph{per-channel activation} scale shares), or \emph{per-group/block} (contiguous groups of $G$ entries, e.g.\ $G\in\{32,128\}$). Finer granularity lowers distortion at the cost of storing more scales; in the limit a full-precision scale per element would be no compression at all, so a scale must be amortized over a group, which is what makes a single outlier in that group unavoidable. The group size $G$ is the single most important deployment knob and reappears in the block-scaled hardware formats of \Cref{sec:live}.
title: Granularity

[Corollary 32 (Diameter and circle convergence on a persistent large-diameter tail) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] Let \(M\) be \(\TT^3\), a compact \(\Nil\) torus bundle with nontrivial
unipotent monodromy, or a compact \(\Sol\) torus bundle with hyperbolic
monodromy, and let \(g(t)\), \(t\geq0\), be an immortal Ricci flow on \(M\).
Fix a particular application of
Proposition~\ref{input:bamler-fixed-threshold}, with cutoff \(c_0\) and tail
data \(T_B(c_0),\eps_B^{c_0}\), and suppose that
\[
        \diam(M,g(t))\geq c_0\sqrt t
\]
for every sufficiently large \(t\).  Then there are constants
\(C<\infty\) and \(\ell_\infty>0\) such that
\[
        \diam(M,g(t))\leq C\sqrt t
\]
for all sufficiently large \(t\), and
\begin{equation}
        (M,t^{-1}g(t))\longrightarrow C_{\ell_\infty}
\end{equation}
in the Gromov--Hausdorff sense, where \(C_{\ell_\infty}\) is the metric
circle of length \(\ell_\infty\).

body:
[Definition 19 (Regular polygonal \(N\)-gaskets) of arXiv:2608.03497, 'Connective Constants on Nested Fractal Graphs'] Let \(N\ge3\) with \(4\nmid N\).  Identify \(\R^2\) with \(\mathbb C\), and put
\[
  q_j=\exp(2\pi\mathrm i j/N),
  \qquad
  V_0^{(N)}=\{q_j:j\in\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z\}.
\]
Let \(F_0^{(N)}\) be the cycle on \(V_0^{(N)}\).  Write
\[
  k_N=\lfloor N/4\rfloor,
  \qquad
  \ell_N=N-4k_N,
  \qquad
  s_N=k_N+1,
\]
and define
\[
  \rho_N
  =
  \frac{\sin(\pi/N)}
       {\sin(\pi/N)+\sin((2s_N-1)\pi/N)},
  \qquad
  \Psi_j^{(N)}(x)=q_j+\rho_N(x-q_j).
\]
The attractor of the \(N\) homotheties
\(\{\Psi_j^{(N)}:j\in\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z\}\) is the
\emph{regular polygonal \(N\)-gasket}.  Its finite graphs and its one-sided graph
are denoted by \(F_m^{(N)}\) and \(F_\infty^{(N)}\).  In the construction
\eqref{eq:finite-graphs}, the
indices are relabeled by \(\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z\), the root is
\(O=q_0\), and \(\Psi_0^{(N)}\) is the map fixing \(O\).  The number
\(\rho_N\) is the \emph{first-contact
ratio}~\cite[Section~7]{TysonWu2006}.
When \(4\mid N\), two consecutive first-level fractal cells in the
first-contact construction share a non-degenerate line segment.  Since
\(V_0^{(N)}\) is finite, this intersection cannot equal the intersection
of their boundary vertex sets.  Thus \textup{(NF4)} fails, so this
construction is not a nested fractal and is excluded from the definition.
title: Regular polygonal \(N\)-gaskets

[Defn 14 of arXiv:2608.28355, 'About the contractibility of the walking coinductive equivalence'] Given an $\omega$-category $\cD$, we say that it is:
    \begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*]
        \item \emph{contractible} if $\cD\to[0]$ is a weak equivalence in the model structure $\omega\cat_{\mathrm{can}}$.
        Equivalently, $\cD$ is contractible if it has the right lifting property with respect to the cell boundary inclusions $\partial\cC[k]\hookrightarrow\cC[k]$ in $\omega\cat$ for all $k\geq0$.
      \item \emph{gaunt} if for all $k\geq0$ the $k$-core $\mathrm{core}_k\cD$ is a gaunt $k$-category; that is, $\mathrm{core}_k\cD$ has no non-identity isomorphisms.
Equivalently, $\cD$ is gaunt if it has the right lifting property with respect to the canonical map $\Sigma^k\cI\to\Sigma^k[0]\cong\cC[k]$ in $\omega\cat$ for all $k\geq0$.
    \end{itemize}
title: Definition 14 of arXiv:2608.28355

body:
the observable is T_n, the minimal passage time between two opposite sides of an n by n square - a minimum over crossings, not a point-to-point passage time
a curvature assumption on the limit shape (unproven in first-passage percolation)
the edge weights t_e are exponentially distributed
d = 2

WHY A SEPARATE ARGUMENT WAS NEEDED, in the authors' words: 'previous arguments to bound the fluctuations of T(x,y) only give a constant lower bound for those of T_n (even assuming curvature)', so they represent T_n as a minimum of cylinder passage times and use the Markov property to get finer distributional information. The minimum-over-crossings structure is the whole difficulty and the whole difference.
COROLLARY they state: the first polynomial lower bounds on higher central moments of the discrete torus passage time, under the same curvature assumption.
THE MISQUOTE THIS NODE EXISTS TO BLOCK: 'polynomial variance lower bounds are known in FPP'. They are known for this observable, under an unproven curvature assumption, for one weight law (extended by Dembin-Elboim to absolutely continuous laws). Nothing polynomial is known unconditionally for Var T(0,x).
SOURCE: arXiv:2204.06592v1, 'Fluctuation bounds for first-passage percolation on the square, tube, and torus'. Official arXiv API record retrieved by lane P4 on 2026-08-22.

title: Damron-Houdre-Ozdemir (2022): a POLYNOMIAL fluctuation lower bound does exist in planar first-passage percolation, but for a different observable - T_n, the minimal passage time between two opposite sides of an n by n square - under a curvature assumption and for exponentially distributed weights, where the fluctuations of T_n are at least of order n^{1/8-epsilon} for every epsilon > 0. This is NOT a bound on the point-to-point passage time T(0,x), where the best lower bound is still logarithmic.

body:
[Conjecture 6 ({Global orientation principle, Paper~III}) of arXiv:2608.15805, 'Spectral duality structures and the Fisher--Rao geometry of reset distributions'] Under \textup{(S1)--(S4)},
\[
\operatorname{sgn}\bigl(\partial_\gamma C(\pi,\gamma)\bigr)
=\operatorname{sgn}\,L_\gamma(\pi)
\qquad\text{for all }\pi\in\Delta_{m-1}^\circ,\
\gamma\in(0,1).
\]
By \eqref{eq:C-minus-Cstar}, $\operatorname{sgn}L_\gamma(\pi)
=\operatorname{sgn}\bigl(C(\pi,\gamma)-C^\ast\bigr)$ identically,
so the conjectured identity reads
$\operatorname{sgn}\partial_\gamma C
=\operatorname{sgn}(C-C^\ast)$ whence, wherever $C(\pi,\gamma)\neq C^\ast$,
\[
\frac{\partial}{\partial\gamma}\bigl|C(\pi,\gamma)-C^\ast\bigr|
=\operatorname{sgn}\bigl(C(\pi,\gamma)-C^\ast\bigr)\,
\partial_\gamma C(\pi,\gamma)>0 .
\]
Thus $|C(\pi,\cdot)-C^\ast|$ is non-decreasing on $(0,1)$ and
strictly increasing on any interval on which it does not vanish.
\textup{(}The qualification matters: $\pi\notin\Sigma$ only says
that $C(\pi,\cdot)$ is non-constant, and $L_\gamma(\pi)$ may still
vanish at isolated rates.\textup{)} The response would then be
monotone in $\gamma$ for every interior $\pi$. The geometric reading as a two-sided
boundary, however, requires care, because three distinct objects
are in play. The instantaneous zero set at a given $\gamma$ is the
hyperplane
$\ker\bigl(\psi(\gamma)|_{T_{\pi^\ast}\Delta_{m-1}}\bigr)$, of
codimension one, which moves with $\gamma$. Its intersection over
all $\gamma$ is the local separatrix $\Sigma_{\mathrm{loc}}=V^\perp$,
of codimension $r$ in the tangent space. And $\Sigma$ itself is the
global object, with
$\dim(\Sigma^\circ)=n_{\mathrm{pair}}+n_0-1$, so
that it too has codimension $r$. The three coincide only when
$r=1$; and only then does a single hyperplane, fixed as $\gamma$
varies, separate the simplex into two sides. For $r\ge2$ each
instantaneous hyperplane strictly contains $\Sigma$, no one of them
is $\Sigma$, and a set of codimension $r\ge2$ does not separate at
all. (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)

body: CORRECTION to the bounded-density quadratic-form conjecture (2026-09-22 evening): the general (non-separable) universal constant is NOT pi; it is > pi, at least 3*sqrt(2) ~ 4.243. pi is sharp only for the SEPARABLE case. RANK-3 COAREA LEMMA (the real 'why 3'): if (Y1,Y2,Y3) has joint density rho and |lambda_i|>=1 (any signs), then S=sum lambda_i Y_i^2 has density <= C0 ||rho||_inf (C0=pi isotropic). Proof: a rank-3 indefinite form's zero-set is a 2-D cone; resolving Y3, signature (2,1) gives integral u^{-1/2}du (convergent) where a rank-2 indefinite form gives integral u^{-1}=log (unbounded) - the 2-D cone's area element cancels the vertex gradient blowup. General C>pi because a 3-D projection of a high-dim product concentrates (||rho_3D||>1); for (1,1,-1) with uniform min-variance inputs sigma^2=1/12 the Gaussian limit gives p_Q(0)=1/(2 sqrt2 sigma^2)=3 sqrt2, confirmed numerically (rotated (1,1,-1) peak 2.97 at n=3 -> 4.16 at n=40). ROUTE to the general theorem: condition on the other n-3 directions, apply the rank-3 coarea lemma, Fubini => ||p_Q||<=C0*M with M a bound on the conditional 3-D projection density; proving M uniform (Rudelson-Vershynin type) closes it. Supersedes the earlier claim 'general constant is pi'.
title: CORRECTION to the bounded-density quadratic-form conjecture (2026-09-22 evening): the general (non-separable) universal constant is NOT pi;

[Thm 6 of arXiv:2604.26316, 'Smallest distances between zeros of Gaussian analytic functions'] Given $(z_1,..., z_k) \in M^k\backslash \Delta^{(k)}$ and a partition $\mathcal P=\{I_1,.., I_\ell\}$ of $\{1,..., k\}$ such that the minimal distance $\eta$ between different clusters is at least $\log^2n/\sqrt{n}$, then   the correlation function exhibits the following splitting property,
		\beq
		\rho_k(z_1,.., z_k)=\prod_{I_i \in \mathcal{P}} \rho_{|I_i|}\left(\underline{z}_{I_i}\right)+O\big(n^{-\infty}\big),
		\eeq  
		
		
		
		
		where $n^{-\infty}$ is an error term that decays faster than $n^{-c}$ for any $c>0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem 11 of arXiv:2608.20613, 'Random walks on wreath products \\and spectral gaps for coloured interchange processes'] Let $\Lambda=(\lambda^\gamma)_{\gamma\in\Gamma}$ be a $G$-multipartition of $n$.  Then the multiplicity of $V_\Lambda$ in $\mathcal P_n(G)$ is $\prod_{\gamma\in\Gamma}\dim\Schur_{\lambda^\gamma}(\C^{d_\gamma})$.  Consequently,
\[
\mathcal P_n(G)
\cong
\bigoplus_{\substack{\Lambda=(\lambda^\gamma)_{\gamma\in\Gamma}\
\sum_\gamma\abs{\lambda^\gamma}=n\,,\ 
\len(\lambda^\gamma)\leqslant d_\gamma\text{ for every }\gamma}}
\left(
\prod_{\gamma\in\Gamma}\dim\Schur_{\lambda^\gamma}(\C^{d_\gamma})
\right)V_\Lambda .
\]
title: Theorem 11 of arXiv:2608.20613

[Lemma lem:f^SI-monotone of arXiv:2411.12076, 'Explicit solutions of the SI and Bass models on sparse Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi and regular netwo'] The expected infection level~$f^{\rm ER}_{\rm SI}(t)$  
in the {\rm SI} model on sparse infinite {\rm ER}~networks
is monotonically increasing in~$t$ from $f^{\rm ER}_{\rm SI}(0) = I^0$ to  $f_{\rm SI}^{\infty}:= 
\lim_{t\rightarrow\infty}f^{\rm ER}_{\rm SI}(t)$,
where  $0<f_{\rm SI}^{\infty}<1$. Furthermore, 
$f_{\rm SI}^{\infty}$~is the unique solution in~$(0, 1)$ of 
\begin{equation}
	 
	f_{\rm SI}^{\infty} = 
	1- (1-I^0)e^{-\lambda f_{\rm SI}^{\infty}}.
\end{equation}

body: [Proposition 18 of arXiv:2606.14038, 'Trivariate Hypergeometric Series Formulas\\ for Pure Partition Functions of Multiple $3$-S'] Let $A_{\u n}$ and $B_{\u n}$, $\u n\in\N_0^3$, be given by Theorem \ref{Theorem-AB@N}. [Proposition 44 of arXiv:2608.05931, 'Effective Lagrangian regularity and the uniqueness threshold for random H\"older velocity '] Let $\alpha \in (\frac{1}{2},1)$, $\delta>0, y \in \T^d$, and $V^{\delta,y}(t,z)$ defined by~\eqref{eq:V delta def}. If for some $K >0$ and all $j \in \N, n \in \{0,1,2\}$, we have the almost sure bound
\[\|\nabla^n u^j\|_{\mathcal{C}^0_{x}} \leq K 2^{(n-\alpha)j},\]
    then almost surely there exists a unique solution to~\eqref{eq:V delta ODE} for all $a$, thus~\eqref{eq:V delta flow} almost surely has a unique solution. Further, the unique solution $\Psi^{\delta,y}$ to~\eqref{eq:V delta flow} is almost surely spatially Lipschitz uniformly in $s$ and $t$. That is,
    \[\P\Big(\sup_{s,t\in[0,1]} \|\nabla \Psi^{\delta,y}_{s,t}\|_{\mathcal{C}^0_a} < \infty\Big) = 1.\]

[Proposition 22 (Reducedness and the prefix-signature lift) of arXiv:2607.26377, '\textbf{Entire Logarithmic Signatures\\ of Bounded-Variation Paths in Finite Dimensions}'] Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real normed vector space and let $\eta:[0,T]\to E$ be a continuous bounded-variation path. Put
\[
q(t)=\Var(\eta;[0,t]),
\qquad L=q(T),
\]
and let $\bar\eta:[0,L]\to E$ be the variation parametrisation, so that
\[
\eta_t=\bar\eta_{q(t)},
\qquad
\Var(\bar\eta;[u_1,u_2])=u_2-u_1.
\]
When $L=0$, $\bar\eta$ is understood to be constant. Set
\[
r_t=S(\eta|_{[0,t]}),
\qquad 0\leq t\leq T.
\]
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item $\bar\eta$ is the Hambly--Lyons reduced representative of the tree-like equivalence class of $\eta$;
\item every restriction $\eta|_{[s,t]}$ with trivial signature is constant;
\item if $r_s=r_t$ for $0\leq s<t\leq T$, then $\eta|_{[s,t]}$ is constant; equivalently, the prefix-signature lift is injective after constant waiting intervals are collapsed.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, every restriction of a path satisfying these conditions again satisfies them.

[Lemma 7 ($\widetilde{X}$ lemma) of arXiv:2604.04267, 'On Sharpest Tail Bounds for Functions \\ of Tail Bounded Random Variables'] Let $f \searrow 0$ on $\mathbb{R}, \ f(t) \rightarrow 1$ as $t \rightarrow -\infty$, and $f$ be left continuous. 
      Define
      \begin{equation}
      \widetilde{X}(s) := \sup f^{-1}[1-s,1], \ \forall s \in (0,1).
      \end{equation}
      Then $\widetilde{X}$ has the following properties.
      \begin{enumerate}[label = (\roman*)]
      \item $\widetilde{X}$ is a neat r.v.
      \item $\widetilde{X}$ is right continuous and $P(\widetilde{X} \geq t) = f(t), \ \forall t \in \mathbb{R}$
      \item If $X \in \mathcal{N}$ and $P(X \geq t) \leq f(t), \ \forall t \in \mathbb{R}$, then $$X(s) \leq \widetilde{X}(s), \ \forall s \in (0,1)$$
      \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: $\widetilde{X}$ lemma

[Thm Thm_strongly_convex of arXiv:2606.22183, 'Expected loss of quasi-arithmetic means of exchangeable random variables'] Let $I\subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be a nondegenerate interval, $\mu\in\mathbb{R}_+$, and $L: I\to\mathbb{R}$ be a strongly convex function with modulus $\mu$.
Then, for each $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in I$, we have that
 \begin{align*}
  L\left( \frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=1}^n x_k \right)
     \leqslant \frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=1}^n L(x_k)
          - \frac{\mu}{n} \sum_{k=1}^n \left(x_k - \frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^n x_j \right)^2.
 \end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm Thm_strongly_convex of arXiv:2606.22183

CURRENT AUDIT STATUS: independently checked proof, T336-w727-C004 v1; urn:mb-agent:7a4f9e38007c2a28 PASS in AUDITS_FROM_REVIEWER.tsv. Exact proof SHA256 ac56184efa730025dd3c81b11d4fced2712fb1d3290a9bc2a089ca9a9af705a5. No novelty or Lean certification is claimed. The following original submission text retains historical pre-audit status notices.

For raw inputs in [0,1]^d, every bounded rank-at-most-p GP with coordinatewise K-Lipschitz feature map has an explicit residual ReLU-attention transformer attaining uniform noisy predictive forward KL <= eps over contexts of length <=n and labels bounded by B. Unlike C002, feature computation is counted. The constants, grid size, width, heads, hidden width, and depth are explicit in C004 Sections 1-5. Status: proof (unaudited), T336-w727-C004 v1. Complete theorem, constants and scope:
# Target 1 with raw inputs and an explicit Lipschitz feature encoder

Claim T336-w727-C004 v1. Rung: proof (unaudited), subject to recorded checks and dependent on unaudited C002 v1. No Lean certification or independent audit is claimed. This gives a quantitative raw-input subclass of Target 1, rather than assuming exact feature computation outside the size count.

The hardest steps are the explicit residual-MLP encoder and the perturbation budget linking its feature errors to the original GP predictive distribution. The proof does not use a triangle inequality for KL.

## 1. Assumptions and explicit size

Fix integers d,p>=1,n>=0, real s>0, B>=0,R>=0,K>=0,eps>0. The raw domain is X=[0,1]^d. The fixed zero-mean GP prior has kernel k(x,x')=z(x)^T z(x'), where z:X->R^p satisfies ||z(x)||_2<=R and, for each coordinate j,

    |z_j(x)-z_j(x')|<=K ||x-x'||_1.

The observation noise is independent N(0,s). Context labels satisfy |y_i|<=B, and contexts have length t<=n. The target is the predictive law of a new noisy observation. The input encoding supplies only raw coordinates, labels, two binary role flags (context and query), and fixed constants. Zero padding fixes N=n+1 tokens. A padding token has raw coordinates zero and both flags zero; the query has only its query flag set; actual context tokens have only their context flag set. No label is supplied for the query.

Define the following fixed constants:

    S=R+1,
    C_A=n(2R+1),
    C_m=nB[(R+S)/s + S C_A R/s^2],
    C_v=R+S+S^2 C_A/s > 0,
    eta=min(1, sqrt(s eps)/(2(1+C_m)), s sqrt(eps)/(2 C_v), s/(4 C_v)),
    eps0=min(eps/4,1/16),
    m=max(1,ceil(K d sqrt(p)/eta)), J=(m+1)^d, E=3+ceil(log_2 J).

For the solver set

    kappa=1+max(1,n)S^2/s, M=nS^2B/s,
    delta0=min(1/2,s/(2S^2),sqrt(s eps0)/(1+M),s sqrt(eps0)/S^2),
    T=ceil(sqrt(kappa) log(2/delta0)/2).

There is a residual normalized ReLU-attention transformer (Bai et al. Definition 1 and Definition 2) with

    token width D=7p+6+d+Jd+pJ,
    depth L_total=E+T+2=T+5+ceil(log_2 J),
    at most five attention heads per layer,
    tokenwise MLP hidden width at most H=2Jd+pJ+4p+1,

whose Gaussian output satisfies forward KL<=eps uniformly over all these raw-input contexts and queries. A dense parameter upper bound is

    L_total(15D^2+2DH)+2D.

Fixed affine input placement is not counted; all nonlinear feature computation is counted. Every weight is specified below or in C002 v1 and depends only on the fixed prior feature map (through finitely many grid samples) and the displayed bounds, never on observed contexts, query labels, or future data. This is a real-weight size theorem, not a finite-bit complexity theorem or training guarantee.

## 2. Posterior perturbation caused by an approximate feature map

First suppose a map ztilde satisfies sup_x ||ztilde(x)-z(x)||<=eta<=1. Then ||ztilde||<=R+eta<=S. For any fixed admissible context and query, put

    A=sI+sum_i z_i z_i^T, b=sum_i z_i y_i, q=z(x_*),
    Atilde=sI+sum_i ztilde_i ztilde_i^T, btilde=sum_i ztilde_i y_i, qtilde=ztilde(x_*).

Both matrices are symmetric positive definite with inverse operator norm <=1/s. For vectors u,v,

    ||uu^T-vv^T||_op
      =||(u-v)u^T+v(u-v)^T||_op
      <=||u-v|| (||u||+||v||).

Thus

    ||A-Atilde||<=n(2R+eta)eta<=C_A eta,
    ||b-btilde||<=nB eta, ||b||<=nRB,
    ||A^{-1}-Atilde^{-1}||
      =||A^{-1}(Atilde-A)Atilde^{-1}||<=C_A eta/s^2.

The true and perturbed noisy predictive parameters are

    mu=q^T A^{-1}b, v=s+s q^T A^{-1}q,
    mutilde=qtilde^T Atilde^{-1}btilde,
    vtilde=s+s qtilde^T Atilde^{-1}qtilde.

Both variances are >=s. Add and subtract qtilde^T A^{-1}b and qtilde^T Atilde^{-1}b. Cauchy-Schwarz and the preceding bounds give

    |mu-mutilde|
      <=eta nRB/s + S C_A eta nRB/s^2 + S nB eta/s
      =C_m eta.

For the variance, first replace both q factors while retaining A^{-1}, and then replace the inverse. This gives

    |v-vtilde|
      <=s[eta(R+S)/s+S^2 C_A eta/s^2]=C_v eta.

The definition of eta ensures

    |mu-mutilde|<=sqrt(s eps)/2,
    |v-vtilde|<=min(s/4,s sqrt(eps)/2).

No probabilistic context distribution or independence between observed features is needed here.

## 3. A finite-grid cone encoder

Let G={0,1/m,...,1}^d, so |G|=J. For each feature coordinate define

    ztilde_j(x)=min_{a in G}[z_j(a)+K sum_{r=1}^d |x_r-a_r|].

The Lipschitz assumption shows every term in this minimum is >=z_j(x). Choose a nearest grid point coordinate by coordinate; its L1 distance is <=d/(2m). The same Lipschitz bound then gives

    0<=ztilde_j(x)-z_j(x)<=Kd/m.

Consequently ||ztilde(x)-z(x)||<=sqrt(p)Kd/m<=eta. This also holds for K=0, when the error is zero and m=1. In particular |ztilde_j(x)|<=||ztilde(x)||<=S on the whole input cube.

The encoder is exact as an implementation of this finite minimum, including all absolute values. It is not a numerical approximation to the finite minimum.

## 4. Exact tokenwise residual-MLP construction

Use the 7p+4 core registers of C002. Add d registers for raw x, Jd zero-initialized absolute-value registers, pJ zero-initialized cone registers, and two role flags. This is D=7p+6+d+Jd+pJ. Initially the feature registers z_c,z_q are zero. The core constant is one=1; the variance-output register starts at s, and the query/padding label register is zero. Encoder MLP layers preserve raw x, the flags, and all core constants.

Each MLP has the residual form h^+=h+W2 ReLU(W1 h), with a constant register implementing affine biases. All unspecified matrix entries are zero. The attention block in each encoder layer is the identity (all value matrices zero).

Layer 1 uses 2Jd hidden units for ReLU(x_r-a_r) and ReLU(a_r-x_r), for all a in G,r. Their sums are written into the initially zero absolute-value registers, yielding |x_r-a_r| exactly.

Layer 2 uses Jd identity-ReLU units on the nonnegative absolute registers and one unit on the constant one. Its output matrix writes

    F_{j,a}=z_j(a)+K sum_r |x_r-a_r|

into each initially zero cone register. Negative fixed grid values cause no difficulty: they occur in the output matrix applied to the constant unit.

Next compute the minimum independently for each coordinate j by a balanced binary tournament on the J cone registers. A pair of current registers u,v is replaced in the first slot by

    u-ReLU(u-v)=min(u,v),

leaving the other slot unused thereafter. This is one residual MLP unit: W1 reads u-v and W2 subtracts its ReLU from the u register. Distinct pairs at the same level use disjoint output slots. An unpaired register passes unchanged. After ceil(log_2 J) levels one designated cone slot contains ztilde_j(x). Each level uses at most p floor(J/2) units, bounded by pJ. This works for signed cone values and for every J, not only powers of two.

One final gating layer writes the feature registers. For any |f|<=S and binary flag r define

    g(f,r)=ReLU(f+S(r-1))-ReLU(-f+S(r-1)).

If r=1, this equals f; if r=0, both arguments are <=0 and it equals zero. Apply g to every computed feature with the context flag to populate z_c, and with the query flag to populate z_q. The registers start at zero, so the residual connection adds precisely the desired values. This uses 4p units. Query, padding, and context feature routing now matches C002 exactly. Both flags and the raw x registers are preserved throughout.

There are E=3+ceil(log_2 J) MLP encoder layers. The stated H bounds every hidden width. Biases are realized through the constant register, rather than being omitted from the construction. All grid feature values are fixed weights of the known prior; no context-dependent parameter is selected.

## 5. Solver composition and KL budget

Apply C002 v1 to ztilde with feature bound S and accuracy eps0. Its core 7p+4 registers embed in the larger width D; all additional registers are preserved by zero extension of its matrices. The solver uses its one-head broadcast layer, T five-head Chebyshev layers, and four-head readout layer. All solver MLPs are identities. The resulting parameters muhat,vhat obey

    vhat>=s,
    |mutilde-muhat|<=sqrt(s eps0)<=sqrt(s eps)/2,
    |vtilde-vhat|<=s sqrt(eps0)<=min(s/4,s sqrt(eps)/2).

Combine these with Section 2 using ordinary triangle inequalities for scalar errors, not for KL:

    |mu-muhat|<=sqrt(s eps),
    |v-vhat|<=min(s/2,s sqrt(eps)).

Since v,vhat>=s, put h=(v-vhat)/vhat in [-1/2,1/2]. As proved directly in C002 Section 5,

    KL(N(mu,v)||N(muhat,vhat))
      <=(mu-muhat)^2/(2s)+(v-vhat)^2/(2s^2)<=eps.

The depth is E+T+2. There are at most five heads, each with three D-by-D matrices. Counting two D-by-H/H-by-D MLP matrices at every layer, even when they are zero, and a two-coordinate linear readout, gives the stated dense parameter bound.

## 6. What this does and does not settle

This is a quantitative raw-input theorem for every bounded finite-rank GP feature map satisfying the displayed Lipschitz assumption, in every fixed input dimension. It counts the encoder rather than treating it as a free feature oracle. The bound is deliberately explicit and can be very large because J=(m+1)^d.

C003 shows that dropping all raw-feature regularity makes the literal bounded-kernel statement false for continuous Gaussian-output transformers. C004 therefore supplies a precise constructive assumption, while C002 remains the smaller theorem when features are supplied directly.

The finite-grid envelope and ReLU min/max identities are classical elementary constructions, not claims of new approximation theory. The claimed target contribution is their fully costed composition with the accelerated posterior solver and a uniform original-posterior forward-KL budget. C004 remains a proof candidate dependent on C002 until independent review passes both exact versions.

    ||uu^T-vv^T||_op
      =||(u-v)u^T+v(u-v)^T||_op
      <=||u-v|| (||u||+||v||).

Thus

    ||A-Atilde||<=n(2R+eta)eta<=C_A eta,
    ||b-btilde||<=nB eta, ||b||<=nRB,
    ||A^{-1}-Atilde^{-1}||
      =||A^{-1}(Atilde-A)Atilde^{-1}||<=C_A eta/s^2.

The true and perturbed noisy predictive parameters are

    mu=q^T A^{-1}b, v=s+s q^T A^{-1}q,
    mutilde=qtilde^T Atilde^{-1}btilde,
    vtilde=s+s qtilde^T Atilde^{-1}qtilde.

Both variances are >=s. Add and subtract qtilde^T A^{-1}b and qtilde^T Atilde^{-1}b. Cauchy-Schwarz and the preceding bounds give

    |mu-mutilde|
      <=eta nRB/s + S C_A eta nRB/s^2 + S nB eta/s
      =C_m eta.

For the variance, first replace both q factors while retaining A^{-1}, and then replace the inverse. This gives

    |v-vtilde|
      <=s[eta(R+S)/s+S^2 C_A eta/s^2]=C_v eta.

The definition of eta ensures

    |mu-mutilde|<=sqrt(s eps)/2,
    |v-vtilde|<=min(s/4,s sqrt(eps)/2).

No probabilistic context distribution or independence between observed features is needed here.

## 3. A finite-grid cone encoder

Let G={0,1/m,...,1}^d, so |G|=J. For each feature coordinate define

    ztilde_j(x)=min_{a in G}[z_j(a)+K sum_{r=1}^d |x_r-a_r|].

The Lipschitz assumption shows every term in this minimum is >=z_j(x). Choose a nearest grid point coordinate by coordinate; its L1 distance is <=d/(2m). The same Lipschitz bound then gives

    0<=ztilde_j(x)-z_j(x)<=Kd/m.

Consequently ||ztilde(x)-z(x)||<=sqrt(p)Kd/m<=eta. This also holds for K=0, when the error is zero and m=1. In particular |ztilde_j(x)|<=||ztilde(x)||<=S on the whole input cube.

The encoder is exact as an implementation of this finite minimum, including all absolute values. It is not a numerical approximation to the finite minimum.

## 4. Exact tokenwise residual-MLP construction

Use the 7p+4 core registers of C002. Add d registers for raw x, Jd zero-initialized absolute-value registers, pJ zero-initialized cone registers, and two role flags. This is D=7p+6+d+Jd+pJ. Initially the feature registers z_c,z_q are zero. The core constant is one=1; the variance-output register starts at s, and the query/padding label register is zero. Encoder MLP layers preserve raw x, the flags, and all core constants.

Each MLP has the residual form h^+=h+W2 ReLU(W1 h), with a constant register implementing affine biases. All unspecified matrix entries are zero. The attention block in each encoder layer is the identity (all value matrices zero).

Layer 1 uses 2Jd hidden units for ReLU(x_r-a_r) and ReLU(a_r-x_r), for all a in G,r. Their sums are written into the initially zero absolute-value registers, yielding |x_r-a_r| exactly.

Layer 2 uses Jd identity-ReLU units on the nonnegative absolute registers and one unit on the constant one. Its output matrix writes

    F_{j,a}=z_j(a)+K sum_r |x_r-a_r|

into each initially zero cone register. Negative fixed grid values cause no difficulty: they occur in the output matrix applied to the constant unit.

Next compute the minimum independently for each coordinate j by a balanced binary tournament on the J cone registers. A pair of current registers u,v is replaced in the first slot by

    u-ReLU(u-v)=min(u,v),

leaving the other slot unused thereafter. This is one residual MLP unit: W1 reads u-v and W2 subtracts its ReLU from the u register. Distinct pairs at the same level use disjoint output slots. An unpaired register passes unchanged. After ceil(log_2 J) levels one designated cone slot contains ztilde_j(x). Each level uses at most p floor(J/2) units, bounded by pJ. This works for signed cone values and for every J, not only powers of two.

One final gating layer writes the feature registers. For any |f|<=S and binary flag r define

    g(f,r)=ReLU(f+S(r-1))-ReLU(-f+S(r-1)).

If r=1, this equals f; if r=0, both arguments are <=0 and it equals zero. Apply g to every computed feature with the context flag to populate z_c, and with the query flag to populate z_q. The registers start at zero, so the residual connection adds precisely the desired values. This uses 4p units. Query, padding, and context feature routing now matches C002 exactly. Both flags and the raw x registers are preserved throughout.

There are E=3+ceil(log_2 J) MLP encoder layers. The stated H bounds every hidden width. Biases are realized through the constant register, rather than being omitted from the construction. All grid feature values are fixed weights of the known prior; no context-dependent parameter is selected.

## 5. Solver composition and KL budget

Apply C002 v1 to ztilde with feature bound S and accuracy eps0. Its core 7p+4 registers embed in the larger width D; all additional registers are preserved by zero extension of its matrices. The solver uses its one-head broadcast layer, T five-head Chebyshev layers, and four-head readout layer. All solver MLPs are identities. The resulting parameters muhat,vhat obey

    vhat>=s,
    |mutilde-muhat|<=sqrt(s eps0)<=sqrt(s eps)/2,
    |vtilde-vhat|<=s sqrt(eps0)<=min(s/4,s sqrt(eps)/2).

Combine these with Section 2 using ordinary triangle inequalities for scalar errors, not for KL:

    |mu-muhat|<=sqrt(s eps),
    |v-vhat|<=min(s/2,s sqrt(eps)).

Since v,vhat>=s, put h=(v-vhat)/vhat in [-1/2,1/2]. As proved directly in C002 Section 5,

    KL(N(mu,v)||N(muhat,vhat))
      <=(mu-muhat)^2/(2s)+(v-vhat)^2/(2s^2)<=eps.

The depth is E+T+2. There are at most five heads, each with three D-by-D matrices. Counting two D-by-H/H-by-D MLP matrices at every layer, even when they are zero, and a two-coordinate linear readout, gives the stated dense parameter bound.

## 6. What this does and does not settle

This is a quantitative raw-input theorem for every bounded finite-rank GP feature map satisfying the displayed Lipschitz assumption, in every fixed input dimension. It counts the encoder rather than treating it as a free feature oracle. The bound is deliberately explicit and can be very large because J=(m+1)^d.

C003 shows that dropping all raw-feature regularity makes the literal bounded-kernel statement false for continuous Gaussian-output transformers. C004 therefore supplies a precise constructive assumption, while C002 remains the smaller theorem when features are supplied directly.

The finite-grid envelope and ReLU min/max identities are classical elementary constructions, not claims of new approximation theory. The claimed target contribution is their fully costed composition with the accelerated posterior solver and a uniform original-posterior forward-KL budget. The analogous statement holds for $\sup_{s\leq \cdot } x^n_s$. In particular, we have $\inf_{s\leq \cdot}x^n_s \rightarrow \underline{\phi} \circ \tau$ and $\sup_{s\leq \cdot}x^n_s \rightarrow \overline{\phi} \circ \tau$ in $(D[0,T],M_1)$. body: [Defi 11 of arXiv:2511.10535, 'Eigenvalues of Brownian Motions on $\mathrm{GL}(N,\mathbb{C})$'] A {\bf Haar Unitary Ensemble} $U^N$ is a random $N\times N$ matrix whose distribution is the Haar measure on $\mathrm{U}(N)$.  In a $W^\ast$-probability space $(\A,\tau)$, a {\bf Haar unitary operator} $u\in\A$ is a unitary operator whose $\ast$-distribution is determined by $\tau[u^n] = \tau[u^{\ast\,n}]=\delta_{n0}$ for all $n\in\N$.

[Thm lwc-saart of arXiv:2510.18856, 'Evolution of recursive trees with limited memory'] Consider the sequence of random trees $\left\{\mathcal{T}_n:n\geqslant 2\right\}$ distributed as an SAART with attachment distribution $V$.  Then $\left\{\mathcal{T}_n:n\geqslant 2\right\}$ converges in probability in the extended fringe sense (Def.~(def:local-weak of the paper)~(equation it:fringe-b of the paper)) to the unique infinite {\tt sin}-tree with fringe distribution $\boldsymbol{\varpi}_{V}$. This implies in particular, the degree distribution satisfies the asymptotics for $k\geqslant 1$,
     \[
\frac{N_k(n)}{n} \stackrel{P}{\longrightarrow} \pr(\mathcal{P}_V(T_1) = k-1) \text{ as } n\to\infty,
\]
where $T_1\sim \exp(1)$ independent of $\mathcal{P}_V(\cdot)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Definition of arXiv:2411.10829, 'Airy$_\beta$ line ensemble and its Laplace transform'] For $\vec s\in \mathscr B$, we construct a walk $\vec r$ of another operator $(\hat{\mathfrak D}_{i_m'}^{N_m})^{k_m} \cdots (\hat{\mathfrak D}_{i_1'}^{N_1})^{k_1}$ without types III or B indices, as follows.
For each $j\in J$ that is minimal under $\prec$, we let $r_j=\sum_{j':j\preceq j'}s_{j'}$, and $i_\ell'=j$ for each $\ell$ with $j\preceq i_\ell$; and let $r_j= 0$ for each non-minimal $j$.
We use $\mathcal M$ to denote the map $\vec s\mapsto \vec r$, and let $\mathbf m(\vec s)$ be the number of non-minimal $j\in J$.
Note that $\mathbf m(\vec s)$ equals the number of type III (or type B) indices of $\vec s$.

[Lemma 17 (Relative-entropy nets give partial colorings) of arXiv:2606.16005, '\bfseries An Algebraic Matrix Spencer Theorem'] Let \(A_1,\ldots,A_n\) be self-adjoint satisfying $\|A_i\|\le1$ and which are block diagonal with respect to a fixed common block decomposition, and let \(\Delta\) denote the corresponding block-diagonal spectraplex. Let \(S\subseteq[n]\), \(s:=|S|\), and define
\[
A_S(X):=\bigl(\operatorname{tr}(A_iX)\bigr)_{i\in S}.
\]

Assume that there exists a finite relative-entropy net \(T_0\subseteq\Delta\) of the  block-diagonal spectraplex with $|T_0|\le \exp(C_0s)$ such that 
 for every \(X\in\Delta\) there exists \(Y\in T_0\) satisfying
\[
S(X\|Y)\le D
\]
Then for every point \(y\in(-1,1)^S\), there exists an increment \(z\in\mathbb R^S\) such that
\[
y+z\in[-1,1]^S, \quad |\{i\in S: |y_i+z_i|=1\} |\ge cs,
\]
and
\[
\left\|
\sum_{i\in S}z_iA_i
\right\|
\le
C\sqrt{sD}.
\]
Here \(c>0\) is an absolute constant, and \(C>0\) depends only on \(C_0\).

[Lemma lem:principal-angle-stability of arXiv:2609.03264, 'Certified Spherical MUSIC for 3D Localization under Adversarial Subspace Perturbations'] For a unit vector \(u\in\mathcal H\), define
$$
    \alpha_{\mathcal U}(u)
    :=
     \arccos\|P_\mathcal{U} u\|_2,\qquad  \alpha_{\widetilde \mathcal{U}}(u)
    :=
     \arccos\|P_{\widetilde\mathcal{U}} u\|_2. 
$$
 Then
\begin{equation}

    \left|
        \alpha_{\mathcal U}(u)
        -
        \alpha_{\widetilde{\mathcal U}}(u)
    \right|
    \leq
    \arcsin\varepsilon_{\rm sub}.
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}

    \|(I-P_{\widetilde \mathcal{U}})u \|_2
    \geq
    \sin\left(
        \left(
            \arcsin\|(I-P_\mathcal{U})u\|_2
            -
            \arcsin\varepsilon_{\rm sub}
        \right)_+
    \right).
\end{equation}

[Corollary 31 of arXiv:2609.00567, 'Hodge--Tate splitting and Akizuki--Nakano vanishing in positive characteristic'] We use \Cref{notation:log-dR}.
We assume $X$ is projective over $k$ and $F^{\dR}_{(X,D)}$ splits in $\mcalD_{\qcoh}(X')$.
Then  for every ample line bundle \(L\) on \(X\), we have
\[
H^i(X,\Omega^j_{X/k}(\log D)\otimes L^{-1})=H^i(X,\Omega^j_{X/k}(\log D)(-D)\otimes L^{-1})=0 \qquad
(i+j<d) 
\]
and
\[
H^i(X,\Omega^j_{X/k}(\log D)\otimes L)=H^i(X,\Omega^j_{X/k}(\log D)(-D)\otimes L)=0
\qquad
(i+j>d).
\]
Furthermore, the logarithmic Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence is $E_1$-degenerate.

Let g:R^d->R^d be C2, g(0)=0, and let phi(x,t) solve theta_prime=g(theta), with phi(x,t) defined for every x in R^d and every real t. Let the eigenvalues of J=Dg(0) be lambda_1,...,lambda_d, counted with algebraic multiplicity and ordered by real part. Assume lambda_1 is real and lambda_1>max{Re(lambda_2),0}; in particular it is algebraically simple. Choose real vectors v,u with Jv=lambda_1 v, u^T J=lambda_1 u^T and u^T v=1. For a>0 define z_a(t)=phi(a v,t+log(1/a)/lambda_1). Then z(t)=lim_{a down to 0}z_a(t) exists for each fixed t in R and z(t)=phi(z(0),t). Suppose delta_a->0 and liminf_{a down to 0}<delta_a,u>/||delta_a||_2>0. Put gamma=lambda_1-Re(lambda_2)>0. For every fixed t in R and every epsilon>0 there is C>0 such that, for all sufficiently small a, ||phi(delta_a,t+log(1/<delta_a,u>)/lambda_1)-z(t)||_2<=C||delta_a||_2^(gamma/(lambda_1+gamma)-epsilon). Choosing epsilon in (0,gamma/(lambda_1+gamma)) gives convergence to the same canonical orbit. No diagonalizability of J and no uniformity in t are asserted. The left/right eigenvectors are specified by their equations to remove the transposed naming slip in the printed Appendix E.3 sentence.
C2 real vector field with equilibrium at zero
Complete flow for every starting point and every real time
Algebraically simple positive real top eigenvalue strictly larger than every other eigenvalue real part
Biorthogonally normalized top right/left eigenvectors
The initialization family tends to zero with strictly positive relative alignment with the left eigenvector
Constants may depend on fixed t, epsilon, the vector field and the initialization family
