body:
[Theorem 8 of arXiv:2609.02416, '2609.02416'] For $n\in\mathbb N$, let
\[
\cA_nu=d(J_n*u-u)+q_n(x)u'+a_n(x)u,
\qquad
\cA u=d(J*u-u)+q(x)u'+a(x)u.
\]
Assume that the kernels satisfy common support, normalization and nondegeneracy hypotheses and that $q_n,q\ge q_0>0$.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{(i) Semicontinuity under local convergence.}
Suppose that $J_n\to J$ in $C_c^1(\R)$ with a common compact support, and that $q_n\to q$, $a_n\to a$ locally uniformly in $\R$, with common local bounds. Then $\Lp(\cA)\ge \limsup_{n\to\infty}\Lp(\cA_n)$.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{(ii) Quantitative global stability.}
Let $\cA_1,\cA_2$ satisfy common global structural bounds, including a common bound for the supports and $C^1$ norms of their kernels, the bounds for $q_i,a_i$, and the positive lower bound for $q_i$. There exists $C>0$, depending only on these structural data, such that
\[
\big|\Lp(\cA_1)-\Lp(\cA_2)\big|
\le C\Big(
\|J_1-J_2\|_{L^1(\R)}
+\|q_1-q_2\|_{L^\infty(\R)}
+\|a_1-a_2\|_{L^\infty(\R)}
\Big).
\]
Consequently, under uniform convergence of the coefficients and $C_c^1$ convergence of the kernels with common structural bounds, $\Lp(\cA_n)\to\Lp(\cA)$. If $\phi_n>0$ is a principal eigenfunction normalized by $\phi_n(0)=1$, then every subsequence contains a further subsequence converging in $C^1_{\rm loc}(\R)$ to a positive eigenfunction associated with $\Lp(\cA)$. If $\Lp(\cA)$ is simple in the positive cone, the whole sequence converges to the normalized principal eigenfunction. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 8 of arXiv:2609.02416

[Theorem thm:mixinglower of arXiv:2608.24830, 'Motion helps the contact process: survival below\\ the percolation threshold on Poisson Br'] There are $c_0,c_1,C>0$ depending only on $d$ such that the following holds. Fix $K>\ell>0$
large enough and $\epsilon\in(0,1)$, and tessellate $Q_K$ into subcubes of side $\ell$. Let
$(x_j)_{j\in J}\subset Q_K$ be a configuration with at least $\varrho\ell^d$ points in each
subcube, where $\lfloor\varrho\ell^d\rfloor>0$. Let $\Delta\ge c_0\ell^2\epsilon^{-4/\kappa}$,
let $Y_j$ be the position at time $\Delta$ of a Brownian motion started at $x_j$, these being
independent, and let $K-K'\ge c_1\Delta^{1/2}\epsilon^{-1/d}$. Then $(Y_j)_{j\in J}$ can be
coupled with a Poisson process $\psi$ of intensity $\varrho(1-\epsilon)$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$, independent

\[
  \psi\cap Q_{K'}\subseteq\{Y_j\}_{j\in J}\quad\text{with probability at least}\quad
  1-\Gamma\exp\{-C\varrho\epsilon^2\Delta^{d/2}\} ,
\]
with $\Gamma$ as in (equation eq:Gamma of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 7 of arXiv:2607.06428, 'Impact of spinning on the early-warning signs in non-Markovian stochastic systems'] Let $(W^H_t)_{t\geq 0}$ be a scalar fractional Brownian motion with Hurst index in $H(0,1)$. Then:
\begin{description}
    \item[{\bf(Long-range dependence)}] If $H>1/2$ then 
    \[ \sum\limits_{n=1}^\infty \E [W^H_1(W^{H}_{n+1}-W^H_n)]=\infty. \]
    \item[{\bf(Short-range dependence)}] If $H<1/2$ then
    \[ \sum\limits_{n=1}^\infty \E [W^H_1(W^{H}_{n+1}-W^H_n)]<\infty. \]
 \item [(Self-similarity)] Let $a>0$. Then 
 \[ (a^H W^H_t)_{t\geq 0} \stackrel{\text{law}}{=}(W^{H}_{at})_{t\geq 0}. \]
 \item [(Time-inversion)] It holds
 \[ (t^{2H}W^H_{1/t})_{t>0}\stackrel{\text{law}}{=}(W^H_t)_{t> 0}.  \]
\item [(Stationarity of the increments)] For all $h>0$ we have 
\[ (W^{H}_{t+h} -W^H_t )_{t\geq 0} \stackrel{\text{law}}{=} W^H_h. \]
\item [(Regularity of the increments)] The scalar fractional Brownian motion has a version which is $\alpha$-H\"older continuous with $\alpha<H$. 
\end{description} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Unit-rate iid exponential slowdowns give mean effort E X for every d, while identical deterministic slowdowns give d*E X. The corresponding completion times are E X/d and E X. Thus the same replica count can buy latency without extra mean work in one model, or multiply mean work without reducing latency in another. A degree optimizer must account for both the joint slowdown law and load. Check: The minimum of d unit-rate exponentials has rate d, so multiplying its mean by d cancels exactly. Own-work draft: C21 v1, proof (unaudited), kind route-failure, Target3; no novelty or full-target claim. Fix d>=2 and unit u, with X uniform on the sphere of radius sqrt(d), target y=X.u, and exponential predictor f=integral a exp(b+p.X) dmu, p=w/sqrt(d). Use original Euclidean gradient flow in a,b,w. For every L>=1 initialize a=b=0 and let p have law (1-L^-2)delta_0+L^-2 Unif(L S^(d-1)). This law is rotation invariant, has initial normalized weight second moment 1 and loss 1/2, and satisfies the invariant b=a^2/2. For F=integral a^2 exp(2b+||p||^2) dmu, the actual local flow has F(0)=F prime(0)=0 and F double-prime(0)=2 exp(L^2) M_d prime(L)^2/(d L^2)>=2 exp(L^2)/d, where M_d(s)=E exp(s X_1). Hence no uniform finite C depending only on d, the stated loss and second moment bounds can ensure F(t)<=C t^2 even on law-dependent neighborhoods of zero. Each initial law has compact support and its own local smooth existence interval; no common interval is asserted. This is not an obstruction for fixed support radius or uniformly exponentially integrable initial weights, and it does not disprove a first-order Gronwall bound or give fixed-time learning rates.    e^{ - \frac {1} {h} |X- T|^2 - \frac {2i} {h} Y \cdot (X-T) } dT $$
   
is continuous and satisfies,
   
   $$ |   ( {\cal V }_W F)  (X , Y) | \leq \psi (Y),$$
   
 with the function $\psi\in L^1(\R^{2n}) \cap L^{\infty}(\R^{2n})$. 
   Then, for all $F\in S_W$, $ F \star \nu_h ^{\rm Weyl} $ 
   is belonging to  $D_{h} ( \R^{2 n })$ 
 and for some $C>0$,
   
    $$ \Vert F \star \nu_h ^{\rm Weyl} \Vert _{D_{h} ( \R^{2 n })} \leq C 
   ( \Vert \psi  \Vert _{L^1(\R^{2n})}  
   + \Vert \psi  \Vert _{ L^{\infty}(\R^{2n})} ).   $$

Consequently,  the operator 
${\rm Op}   _h ^{\rm Weyl} (F)  $ can be defined by 
(\ref{def-gene}) for every  $F\in S_W$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lemma6.61 of arXiv:2504.15992, 'Repeated singular values of a random symmetric matrix and decoupled singular value estimat'] Fix $B>0,\zeta\in\Gamma_B$ and $A_{n}\sim\operatorname{Sym}_n(\zeta)$. We further assume that $\zeta$ has a finite, $n$-independent Log-Sobolev constant. Let $X$ be a random vector with $X\sim\operatorname{Col}_n(\zeta)$, and define the random vector $\widetilde{X}:=(X-X')_J$, where $X'$ is an independent copy of $X$ and $J$ is a $\mu$-subset of $[n]$. 

Fix some $\kappa>0$ and $\Delta>0$. 
    Fix two locations
   $\lambda_1,\lambda_2\in[-(2-\kappa)\sqrt{n},(2-\kappa)\sqrt{n}]$ with $|\lambda_1-\lambda_2|\geq \Delta\sqrt{n}$. 
   
   
   Then there exists an event $\Omega(A_n)$ depending on $\kappa,\Delta$ with probability $\mathbb{P}(A_n\in\Omega(A_n))\geq1-\exp(-\Omega(n))$ such that whenever $A_n\in\Omega(A_n)$, the following hold:
   \begin{enumerate}
       \item Fix any given $(\theta_1,\theta_2)\in\mathbb{R}^2$ satisfying $|\theta_1\theta_2|=1$,
  
   
   Then there exists some $J\in\{1,2\}$ (which is chosen in (equation choiceofbigJ of the paper) in a way depending on $A_n$ and the relative ratio $|\theta_1/\theta_2|$) such that, for any $1\leq k\leq {c_0}_{(lemma6.61 of the paper)}n$ and for any \begin{equation}s\in\left(e^{-cn}, \frac{C_{(lemma6.61 of the paper)}\cdot \mu_k(\lambda_J)}{{\left(\prod_{i=1}^2\mu_1(\lambda_i)\right)^{1/2}}}\right),\end{equation} we have the estimate
    \begin{equation}
\mathbb{P}_{\widetilde{X}}\left(\left\|\sum_{i=1}^2 \frac{\theta_i}{\mu_1(\lambda_i)}(A_n-\lambda_i I_n)^{-1}\widetilde{X}\right\|_2\leq s
\right) \lesssim s e^{-ck},
    \end{equation} where ${c_0}_{(lemma6.61 of the paper)}>0$ and $C_{(lemma6.61 of the paper)}>0$ are two constants that depend only on $\kappa,\Delta,B$ and the Log-Sobolev constant of $\zeta$. The constant $c>0$ depends only on $B$.
    \item  Fix any given $(\theta_1,\theta_2)\in\mathbb{R}^2$ satisfying $\max(|\theta_1|,|\theta_2|)=1$. Then there exist some $I,J\in\{1,2\}$ depending on $A_n$ and the relative ratio $|\theta_1/\theta_2|$ such that, for any $1\leq k\leq {c_0}_{(lemma6.61 of the paper)}n$ and any

s\in(e^{-cn},\frac{\mu_k(\lambda_J)}{\mu_1(\lambda_I)})
    \end{equation} we have the same estimate (equation 212212212 of the paper).
     \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 29 (Neck detection for surgically modified flows) of arXiv:2608.25971, 'Positive \texorpdfstring{$\tau$}{tau}-bi-Ricci curvature and Mean curvature flow with surg'] Fix $\eps>0$, $k\in\mathbb N$, $L\geq10$, and $\Theta>0$, and choose
the standard replacement with $m_0\geq k+2$.  There exist
  \begin{equation*}
  \eta_{\mathrm{surg}}
  =
  \eta_{\mathrm{surg}}(n,\tau,\alpha,\eps,k,L,\Theta)>0
  \end{equation*}
  and
  \begin{equation*}
  H_{\mathrm{surg}}
  =
  H_{\mathrm{surg}}(n,\tau,\alpha,\eps,k,L,\Theta)<\infty
  \end{equation*}
  with the following property.

  Let $(p,t)$ lie in a surgically modified flow satisfying
  Theorem~\ref{thm:estimates-through-surgery}, assume
  $t\geq\tau_nR^2$, and put $r=(n-1)/H(p,t)$.  
  Suppose that
  \begin{equation*}
  H(p,t)\geq H_{\mathrm{surg}}R^{-1},
  \qquad
  \lambda_1(p,t)\leq\eta_{\mathrm{surg}}H(p,t),
  \end{equation*}
  and that $\mathcal P\bigl(p,t,2(L+2)r,\Theta r^2\bigr)$  
  is surgery-free.  Then $p$ is the center of an $(\eps,k,L)$-neck of
  radius $r$.  If $\Theta\geq L^2$, the rescaled flow is $\eps$-close in
  parabolic $C^k$ norm on the corresponding backward cylinder to a round
  shrinking cylinder whose radius at time zero is one.

body:
[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2609.03962, '$L^p$ isomorphisms for the fractional Laplacian on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and their application'] Let $n\ge2$, $s\in(0,2)$, and $p\in(1,\infty)$.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item[\textup{(i)}] Suppose $f\in L^p(\R^n)^n$ and $g\in V_{s,p}$.
        Then \eqref{intro_stokes} has a solution
        $(u,P)\in\Lambda^{s,p}(\R^n)^n\times W_0^{1,p}(\R^n)$, and the
        solutions in this class are exactly the pairs $(u+\lambda,P+c)$
        with $(\lambda,c)$ in
        \[
          \mathcal N_{s,p}
          :=\big\{(\lambda,c)\in(\mathcal P_{[s-n/p]})^n\times
          \mathcal P_{[1-n/p]}:\ \mathrm{div}\,\lambda=0\big\}.
        \]
        Moreover every solution satisfies
        \[
          \inf_{(\lambda,c)\in\mathcal N_{s,p}}
          \big(\|u-\lambda\|_{\Lambda^{s,p}}+\|P-c\|_{W_0^{1,p}}\big)
          \le C\big(\|f\|_{L^p}+\|g\|_{L^p}+\|\flap g\|_{W_0^{-1,p}}\big).
        \]
  \item[\textup{(ii)}] Suppose $f\in\Lambda^{-1,p}(\R^n)^n$ and
        $g\in\Lambda^{s-2,p}(\R^n)$. Then
        \eqref{intro_stokes}---its two equations holding in
        $\Lambda^{-1,p}(\R^n)^n$ and $\Lambda^{s-2,p}(\R^n)$ respectively,
        with the operators extended along the scale as in
        Section~\ref{sec:appstokes}---has a solution
        $(u,P)\in V_{s,p}^n\times L^p(\R^n)$ if and only if
        \[
          f\perp\mathcal P_{[1-n/p']}\quad\text{and}\quad
          g\perp\mathcal P_{[2-s-n/p']}.
        \]
        In that case the pressure $P$ is unique and the solutions are
        exactly the pairs $(u+\lambda,P)$ with
        $\lambda\in(\mathcal P_{[s-1-n/p]})^n$; thus the solution is
        unique whenever $s-1<n/p$, in particular for all $0<s\le1$, and
        unique up to an additive constant vector when $s-1\ge n/p$.
        Moreover every solution satisfies
        \[
          \|P\|_{L^p}
          +\inf_{\lambda\in(\mathcal P_{[s-1-n/p]})^n}
           \|u-\lambda\|_{\Lambda^{s-1,p}}
          \le C\big(\|f\|_{\Lambda^{-1,p}}+\|g\|_{\Lambda^{s-2,p}}\big).
        \]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 4 of arXiv:2609.03962

[Definition def:irreducibility of arXiv:2510.00748, '\bf On irreducible central limit theorems'] Fix $d \ge 2$ and consider the sequence of homogeneous sum $\{ Z_n({\bf X}): n \geq 1\} = \{Z_n \} $ defined in (equation eq:defpolchaos of the paper).  We say that $\{Z_n\}$ is \emph{reducible} if for any $n \in \mathbb{N}$ there exist subsets (``boxes'') $B_1,\ldots,B_{m_n} \subset V_n$ (where $B_i = B_i{(n)}$ may depend on $n$), such that $B_i \cap B_j = \emptyset$ for $i\ne j$ (that is, the boxes $B_i$ are disjoint) and
\begin{enumerate}[label={\rm (\roman*)}]
    \item  $m_n \to \infty \,;$
    \item  $\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{d!\|q_n\|^2} \sum_{i=1}^{m_n} \sigma_n^2(B_i) = 1\,;$
    \item  $\lim_{n\to\infty}  \frac{1}{d!\|q_n\|^2} \max_{i=1,\ldots,m_n} \sigma_n^2(B_i) =0 \,.$ 
\end{enumerate}
We say that $\{Z_n\}$ is \emph{irreducible} if it is not possible to find disjoint sets $B_1,\ldots,B_{m_n} \subset V_n$ such that (redCLTcond1 of the paper), (redCLTcond2 of the paper) and (redCLTcond3 of the paper) hold. If $\{Z_n\}$ is irreducible and verifies (equation eq:CLT of the paper), we say $\{Z_n\}$ {\em verifies an irreducible CLT}.
title: Reducibility/Irreducibility

(2) Given a matrix $U\in M_N(\mathbb C)$, we have indeed the following equivalences, with the first one coming from the polarization identity, and the other ones being clear:

For any \( b \in L_{\text{loc}}^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}_{+} ; L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{d}))+ L_{\text{loc}}^{q}(\mathbb{R}_{+} ; L^{p}(\mathbb{R}^{d})) \) and \( x_{0} \in \mathbb{R}^{d} \), there exists a weak solution to SDE \eqref{EQ:SDE:101}. [Lem 92 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] We have $\sM^{\Lip,\sym}(\alpha,0) \subseteq \sM^{\BOGP,\sym}(\alpha,0)$.

\begin{proof}
We repeat the most relevant part of Definition~\ref{d:SDE.classification.sym}:
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}[h]{r|cccccccc}
\MSRheader\\
\hline
\BOGPdefn{sy}\\
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
    By Lemma~\ref{l:control.problems.Lip.to.Lip.sym}, it suffices to show $\sym(\sM^{\Lip,\chaos}(\alpha,0)) \subseteq \sM^{\BOGP,\sym}(\alpha,0)$, where $\sM^{\Lip,\chaos}(\alpha,0)$ is defined in \eqref{e:sM.Lip.0.chaos}.
    Consider any $\mu \in \cM^{\Lip,\chaos}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)$ (recall \eqref{e:cM.Lip.0.chaos}), where $L$ is sufficiently large depending on $\alpha,\epsilon$.
    There exists a sequence of $L$-Lipschitz $((\cA_{N_j})^\circ)_{j\ge 1}$ such that
    \[
    \WERR((\cA_{N_j})^\circ,\mu)
    =
        \max\bigg\{
            \bbW_2\Big(\mu((\cA_{N_j})^\circ), \mu\Big),
            \bbW_2\Big(\mu^{\Ising}((\cA_{N_j})^\circ), \cP(\{\pm 1\})\Big)
        \bigg\} \le \epsilon\,,
    \]
    and the correlation functions $\chi_{(\cA_{N_j})^\circ}$ satisfy $\lim_{j\to\infty} \chi_{(\cA_{N_j})^\circ}(0) = 0$ and
    \beq
        
        \chi_{\cA_{N_j}^\circ}(1-\epsilon) \le \epsilon\,.
    \eeq
    That is, we have the same information about the algorithms $((\cA_{N_j})^\circ)_{j\ge 1}$ as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{l:Lip.in.BOGP} (instantiated with $q_0 = 0$), and in addition the estimate \eqref{e:Lip.in.BOGP.sym.chaos}.
    For $\cA_{N_j}$ the perturbation of $(\cA_{N_j})^\circ$ given by Proposition~\ref{p:wlogable},  the estimate \eqref{e:Lip.in.BOGP.sym.chaos} implies
    \[
        \chi_{\cA_{N_j}}(1-\epsilon)
        = \bigg(1-\frac{1}{L^2}\bigg) \chi_{\cA_{N_j}^\circ}(1-\epsilon)
        + \frac{1-\epsilon}{L^2} 
        \le \bigg(1-\frac{1}{L^2}\bigg) \epsilon + \frac{1-\epsilon}{L^2} 
        \le 2\epsilon\,,
    \]
where the last inequality holds for $L$ sufficiently large depending on $\alpha,\epsilon$. By passing to a subsequence of the $j$'s, we may assume that $\chi_{\cA_{N_j}}$ converges both pointwise and in $L^1$ to a limiting function $\chi$, which must then satisfy 
    \[
        \chi(1-2\epsilon) \le \chi(1-\epsilon) \le 2\epsilon\,.
    \]
Therefore $p \equiv \chi^{-1}$ satisfies $p(2\epsilon) \ge 1-2\epsilon$, as required by condition~\ref{it:3.6} (with $2\epsilon$ in place of $\epsilon$).
Arguing identically to the proof of Lemma~\ref{l:Lip.in.BOGP} shows that for some $\hat\epsilon(\epsilon) \ge 2\epsilon$ tending to $0$ as $\epsilon \rightarrow 0$, we have 
    \[
        \cM^{\Lip,\chaos}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)
        \subseteq \cB_{\hat\epsilon}\Big(
            \cM^{\BOGP,\chaos}(\alpha,0;\tilde C(L),\hat\epsilon)
        \Big)\,.
    \]
    Taking a union in $L$ and intersection in $\epsilon$, and applying $\sym$ to both sides, shows
    \begin{align*}
       & \sym(\sM^{\Lip,\chaos}(\alpha,0))
        \subseteq \sym\bigg(
        \adjustlimits
            \bigcap_{\epsilon > 0} \bigcup_{L>0} \cB_{\epsilon}\Big(
                \cM^{\BOGP,\chaos}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)
            \Big)
        \bigg)\\
       &\qquad \subseteq 
        \adjustlimits
        \bigcap_{\epsilon > 0} \bigcup_{L>0}
        \cB_{\epsilon}\Big(
            \sym(\cM^{\BOGP,\chaos}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon))
        \Big)\\
        &\qquad\stackrel{\eqref{e:BOGP.sym.relation}}{=} \adjustlimits
        \bigcap_{\epsilon > 0} \bigcup_{L>0}
        \cB_{\epsilon}\Big(
        \cM^{\BOGP,\sym}(\alpha,0;L,\epsilon)
        \Big)
        \stackrel{\eqref{e:measure.classes.sym.cM}}{=} \sM^{\BOGP,\sym}(\alpha,0)\,.
    \end{align*}
This concludes the proof.

Let f be holomorphic on a punctured disk {z : 0 < |z - a| < r} (an isolated singularity at a) and let f(z) = Σ_{n in Z} c_n (z - a)^n be its Laurent expansion there. The residue of f at a is Res(f,a) = c_{-1}, equivalently Res(f,a) = (1/2πi) ∫_{|z-a|=ρ} f(z) dz for any 0 < ρ < r, the circle positively oriented (the value is independent of ρ). Computation rules: if a is a pole of order at most m, Res(f,a) = lim_{z→a} (1/(m-1)!) d^{m-1}/dz^{m-1} [(z - a)^m f(z)]; in particular for a simple pole Res(f,a) = lim_{z→a} (z-a) f(z), and if f = g/h with g, h holomorphic near a, h(a) = 0 and h'(a) ≠ 0, then Res(f,a) = g(a)/h'(a). The residue at infinity of a function holomorphic on |z| > R is Res(f,∞) = -(1/2πi)∫_{|z|=ρ} f(z) dz for ρ > R; for a rational function the sum of all residues in C together with the residue at infinity is 0. A removable singularity has residue 0, but residue 0 does not imply removable (example: 1/(z-a)^2).

[Lemma 7 (Variational lower bound from stationarity) of arXiv:2607.13183, '2607.13183'] Let $(Z_t)_{t\ge0}$ be a finite irreducible reversible continuous-time chain with
stationary law $\pi$ and generator $\mathcal L$. Write
$\cE(f,f):=-\langle f,\mathcal L f\rangle_\pi$ for its Dirichlet form. If
$B$ is a subset of the state space and $0\le F\le1$ satisfies $F=1$ on $B$, then
\begin{equation}
        \E_\pi\tau_B\ge \frac{(1-\E_\pi F)^2}{\cE(F,F)} .
\end{equation}

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:723539c0125e0923b393cbcaeb16eea58030f466c9ec59ec30240b4c8d2b95cc","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/72/723539c0125e0923b393cbcaeb16eea58030f466c9ec59ec30240b4c8d2b95cc.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:77195be7bddee76d800b272b0d976777508944a28c6935e1df2658ebfccc0f00","bundle_entry_key":"w733_t363_positive_two_sectors_two_clocks_v1","bundle_id":"population.w733-t363-positive-two-sector-two-clocks-v1","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"neural-network implicit bias","draft":"w733/bundle_009.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:learning.implicit_bias:w733_t363_positive_two_sectors_two_clocks_v1","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Positive activation families with two occupied live sectors

Claim w733-T363-025 v1. Target 2; kind narrowed; proof (unaudited).
No novelty claimed. This is a sufficient family, not a complete basin classification.

## Statement and dependencies

Let x1=(1,1/4), x2=(-1,1/4), both labels +1. Train both layers of the bias-free network f(x)=sum_j v_j ReLU(w_j.x) by gradient flow of summed exponential or logistic loss, with ReLU'(0)=0. Initially every neuron is strictly dead on both examples (D, output arbitrary), or has v_j>0 and lies strictly in A (x1 only), B (x2 only), or C (both active). Assume at least two of A, B, C are occupied.

A global absolutely continuous flow exists. Every such flow reaches normalized parameter margin sqrt(17)/16 and has a convergent normalized parameter direction. No uniqueness at grazing contacts is asserted. There is no initial balance, tilt, prediction-gap, or scale condition.

We use claims 015 and 017 as prior unaudited results: A/B positive neurons never leave their sectors; D remains fixed; each C has at most one strict sector exit; boundary contact sets are null; global existence holds; once both A and B exist, claim017 gives the stated direction and global margin. The elementary existence and contact arguments in claim017 section1 do not require both seeds. The extension proved here is finite creation of B from nonempty A and C, with any number of C neurons. Reflection proves the B/C case. The A/B case is already claim017.

## 1. A surviving shared neuron must exist if B never forms

Suppose initially A and C are occupied, B is absent, and no neuron ever enters strict B. Write w_j=(u_j,y_j), z_ij=w_j.x_i, a_i=-ell'(f_i)>0, and a=norm(x_i)=sqrt(17)/4. Positive live outputs are nondecreasing. For C, ydot_j=v_j(a1+a2)/4>0 almost everywhere before a strict exit. Thus a C cannot hit both boundaries together. Every strict exit under the supposition is C to A, and is irreversible. There are finitely many such exits.

They cannot remove all C. Otherwise take the last finite exit time, including all neurons exiting simultaneously. At this time all x2 predictions vanish, so f2=0, whereas the permanent A seed ensures f1>0. For either loss this gives a1<a2. For every neuron in the last exit group the incoming C equation at z2=0 is

    zdot_2 = v[(17/16)a2-(15/16)a1] > 0.

By continuity of the parameters and losses, this derivative stays strictly positive on incoming C portions of a sufficiently small left neighborhood. Boundary portions are null, and a neuron in this group has not yet strictly exited. Its nonnegative z2 therefore cannot approach zero from above at that time. This contradicts the purported last exit. Consequently at least one C survives forever. Choose a finite base time b after all strict exits, outside the null contact sets; surviving C obey their C equations almost everywhere forever after b. The A sector remains nonempty.

## 2. Eventual output dominance without an initial balance assumption

Set I_i(t)=integral_b^t a_i(s)ds and T=I1+I2. Let N=sum_j(v_j^2+norm(w_j)^2). The bound Ndot<=2a(a1+a2)N implies that bounded T would bound N and both predictions. Their loss derivatives would then have a positive lower bound on the infinite physical-time trajectory, contradicting bounded T. Thus T tends to infinity.

For each surviving C neuron, v_j(t)>=v_j(b)>0 and

    y_j(t)>=y_j(b)+v_j(b)T(t)/4 -> infinity.

The homogeneous balance invariant delta_j=v_j^2-u_j^2-y_j^2 is constant, as follows by differentiating it in every mask almost everywhere. Hence v_j^2>=y_j^2+delta_j, and eventually v_j>=3y_j/4. Finitely many surviving neurons allow a common finite time L after which all these inequalities hold forever. Reset both clocks to zero at L.

## 3. Two weighted inequalities, valid at every C tilt

For a surviving C neuron the cone gives |u|<=y/4 and 0<=z_i<=y/2. Therefore, for t>=L,

    z_i <= 2v/3,
    q_i=z_i/a <= 8v/(3sqrt(17)) < v,
    s_i=v+q_i satisfies v<=s_i<2v.

The strict algebraic certificate for the middle inequality is 64<153. Put c=x1.x2=-15/16. The exact C equations imply

    sdot_1 = a*a1*s1 + a2*(z2+(c/a)*v),
    sdot_2 = a*a2*s2 + a1*(z1+(c/a)*v).

Define b0=15/(8sqrt(17))-1/3>0, certified by 45^2>64*17. Since z_i<=2v/3 and v>=s_i/2, these yield

    sdot_1 <= (a*a1-b0*a2)*s1,
    sdot_2 <= (a*a2-b0*a1)*s2.

Also n=v^2+u^2+y^2<=26v^2/9<=26s_i^2/9. Integrating each inequality and summing over survivors gives finite constants C1,C2>0 such that

    N_C <= C1 exp(2a I1-2b0 I2),
    N_C <= C2 exp(2a I2-2b0 I1).

These are two bounds on the same surviving-C norm, not an independence assertion.

## 4. Both clocks diverge, then shared mass becomes impossible

If I2 were bounded, T tending to infinity would force I1 to infinity; the second bound would imply N_C tending to zero. This contradicts the fixed positive lower bound on every surviving output. If I1 were bounded, the first bound gives the symmetric contradiction. Thus both clocks diverge.

Let H_A be the prediction on x1 from permanent A neurons. The exact one-point hyperbolic solution gives

    H_A >= H_A(L) exp(2a I1), with H_A(L)>0.

Indeed H_A=alpha exp(2a I1)-beta exp(-2a I1), alpha>beta>=0, which bounds it below by (alpha-beta)exp(2a I1). The first C norm bound now gives

    N_C/H_A <= C exp(-2b0 I2) -> 0.

All contributions are nonnegative; f1>=H_A and f2 consists only of surviving C contributions. The C cone estimate from claim016 gives f2<=N_C/sqrt(17); even the weaker elementary f2<=a N_C/2 suffices. Hence E=f1-f2 tends to positive infinity.

For exponential loss a1/a2=exp(-E). For logistic loss f2>=0 gives a1/a2<=2exp(-E). Thus a1/a2 tends to zero. For any epsilon>0, integrating the eventual inequality a1<=epsilon*a2 and using I2 tending to infinity proves I1/I2 tending to zero. Return to the first weighted bound:

    s1(t) <= s1(L) exp(a I1-b0 I2) -> 0.

This contradicts s1>=v>=v(L)>0. The supposition that B never forms is false. A finite strict B sector therefore forms, while the original A persists. Claim017 applies from that finite time with all remaining positive C neurons and dead neurons. It supplies the direction limit and global margin sqrt(17)/16. This completes the extension, conditional on the cited unaudited dependency017.

## 5. Exact Gaussian masses and disjoint inventory change

For independent centered Gaussian hidden coordinates and outputs, each with variance sigma^2>0, put p=atan(1/4)/pi and q=1/4-p/2. The category probabilities A+, B+, C+, D (either output sign) are q,q,p/2,p. The newly completed whole A/C or B/C family has mass

    L_m=2[(1/4+p)^m-(1/4+p/2)^m-(3p/2)^m+p^m].

This is inclusion-exclusion for one required one-point category and C, with D optional, then reflection. It includes claim023's exactly-one-C family J_m=m*p*[(1/4+p/2)^(m-1)-p^(m-1)]. Thus the new disjoint probability increment is L_m-J_m, not L_m itself.

Combining with claim017's disjoint A/B family H_m gives the sufficient global-family mass

    K_m=((1+p)/2)^m-2(1/4+p/2)^m-(3p/2)^m+2p^m.

These expressions hold at sigma=1e-6 and every other positive scale; they are not total basin probabilities. They already contain all claim020 subcone events, so no claim020 probability may be added to K_m.

Separating the two D output signs, the entire L family has 2*binom(m+1,3) permutation orbits. At widths2..6 these are [2,8,20,40,70], totaling140. The disjoint increment over claim023 (at least two C) is [0,2,8,20,40], totaling70. Conditional on acceptance of the analytic claims, the proposed global inventory grows from196 to266 and unknown decreases from2643 to2573;20 source-bad and135 nonfitting orbits are unchanged. No negative-output live orbit or pure-C orbit is classified here. Exact coefficient and orbit checks are recorded separately; no floating-point experiment or independent review is asserted by this proof.

## Review focus

The least trusted step is the simultaneous-last-exit exclusion in section1 under arbitrary absolutely continuous continuations. Section3 is the new weighted two-clock argument; it uses both inequalities to establish divergence before suppressing C mass. Independent reviewer PASS is required for this exact version and dependency017. body: [Defn 3 of arXiv:2608.13727, 'Hitting-time mixing for the star transposition shuffle'] Let \(\nu_t\) be the probability measure on \(\mathfrak{S}_n\) generated as follows. First, sample \(M_t \in \{0, 1, \ldots, n\}\) from the truncated Poisson law \[\bbP(M_t = x) = \frac{\bbP(\mathrm{Pois}(\gamma_{n, t}) = x)}{\bbP(\mathrm{Pois}(\gamma_{n, t}) \leq n)}.\] Then, choose a uniformly random subset \(S_t \subset [n]\) of size \(M_t\). Finally, sample a uniformly random permutation on \([n]\setminus S_t\) and extend it to an element of \(\mathfrak{S}_n\) by fixing every element of \(S_t\).

body:
[Theorem thm:main1 of arXiv:2605.10361, 'Limit shape of single-source stochastic sandpiles with $p$-topplings on $\Z$'] Denote the final limit shape after stabilizing $n\in\mathbb{N}$ particles placed at the origin by
    $\mathcal{S}_n:=[\mathtt{l}_{n},\mathtt{r}_{n}]\cap\mathbb{Z}.$
    Then for every $\varepsilon>0$
    $$\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{P}\Big([-\tfrac{n}{2}(1-\varepsilon),\tfrac{n}{2}(1-\varepsilon)]\cap\mathbb{Z}\subseteq \mathcal{S}_n\subseteq [-\tfrac{n}{2}(1+\varepsilon),\tfrac{n}{2}(1+\varepsilon)]\cap\mathbb{Z}\Big)=1.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Limit shape of the single-source model

body:
[Coro 3 of arXiv:2606.03122, 'Propagation of support for super-Brownian motion with general branching mechanism'] Let $X$ be a super-Brownian motion with  spatially dependent (sub)critical branching mechanism $\Psi$ satisfying \begin{equation}
\Psi(x,u)\geq \beta(x)\Phi(u),
\qquad x\in\mathbb{R}^d,\quad u\geq0,
\end{equation}
where $\beta$ is a positive bounded continuous function and $\Phi$ is
regularly varying at infinity with index $1+p$ for $p\in(0,1]$, that is,
$$
\Phi(u)=u^{1+p}L(u),
\qquad u\to\infty,
$$
for a slowly varying function $L$ at infinity.
 Set $\beta_R:=\inf_{x\in\overline{B(0,R)}}\beta(x).$
  Then $X$ has the finite-time compact support property provided that
\begin{equation}
\limsup_{R\to\infty}\frac{\ln \beta_R}{R^2}>-\infty.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 11 (Subadditivity and orientation reversal) of arXiv:2609.03916, 'Halfspace Theorems for Anisotropic Minimal Surfaces and Perimeter Minimizers'] Let $\mu$ and $\eta$ be vector-valued Radon measures.  Then, as Radon
measures,
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal F_\Phi(\mu+\eta;\cdot)
 \le\mathcal F_\Phi(\mu;\cdot)+\mathcal F_\Phi(\eta;\cdot).
\end{equation}
Consequently, for any locally integral $n$-currents $T$ and $S$,
\begin{equation}
 \mu_{T+S}^\Phi\le\mu_T^\Phi+\mu_S^\Phi.
\end{equation}
Moreover, for $\Phi^-$ defined in
\eqref{old-eq:reversed-integrand-definition},
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal F_\Phi(-\mu;\cdot)=\mathcal F_{\Phi^-}(\mu;\cdot),
 \qquad
 \mu_{-T}^\Phi=\mu_T^{\Phi^-},
 \qquad
 \Mphi(-T_E;A)=P_{\Phi^-}(E;A)
\end{equation}
for every Borel set $A$.
No evenness of $\Phi$ is required.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:5a97bfda925aeb33d42f14155d25e178a1c4ee7f9b0f3fecd45ecd1769eb4a1c","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/5a/5a97bfda925aeb33d42f14155d25e178a1c4ee7f9b0f3fecd45ecd1769eb4a1c.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:7d0eea2e16ac1b1ce942e880243710f4e999e07d103b25b6ca1a0401be321f24","bundle_entry_key":"claim-010","bundle_id":"population.adam-unstable-cycle-basin-cone-and-gap-classification-004","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"deterministic adaptive optimization","draft":"w706/bundle_004.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:optimization.adam:adam-standard-moment-momentum-cone-supercritical-finite-escape","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"T421-W706-010 v1; target2; kind special; proof (unaudited).

Statement (finite escape of a perturbed dormant coordinate).
Take scalar full-batch Adam, corrected from time0 or uncorrected, with
0<b<1, 0<d<1, eta,lambda,epsilon>0 and m0=v0=0. Put
 c=(1-b)/(1+b), rho=epsilon/(eta lambda).
Suppose rho<c/2. Choose ANY R with 0<R<c/2-rho and set
 q=c/(rho+R)-1>1.
Every standard initialization 0<|x0|<eta R has a finite first time N
with |x_N|>eta R. While |x_0|,...,|x_t|<=eta R, signs alternate and
 |x_(t+1)|>=q |x_t|.
Consequently N is at most the smallest positive integer with
q^N |x0|>eta R. Equality |x0|=eta R is also harmless; a step leaves it.
This holds for BOTH usual separate bias corrections and uncorrected Adam.

For b=.9 and p=1, every dormant eigenvalue lambda2>38 obeys the premise.
In claim008's diagonal family the active coordinate evolves independently.
Any nonzero perturbation of its dormant x2, with moments still initialized
to zero, eventually exceeds eta R, however small that perturbation is.
Thus the zero-coordinate trajectory is unstable in the x2 direction, with
an explicit finite escape scale R<1/38-1/lambda2. This does NOT say that
the perturbed trajectory has a particular asymptotic curvature or cannot
later return to a small neighborhood.

Proof. Normalize X=x/eta,M=m/(eta lambda),V=v/(eta lambda)^2. At time t,
 M'=bM+(1-b)X, V'=dV+(1-d)X^2,
 X'=X-M'/[(1-alpha_t)(sqrt(Vhat')+rho)],
where alpha_t=b^(t+1),Vhat'=V'/(1-d^(t+1)) in the corrected case, and
alpha_t=0,Vhat'=V' in the uncorrected case.

Assume past |X_s|<=R, s<=t. The corrected Vhat' is a convex combination
of X_0^2,...,X_t^2 (standard v0=0). Hence sqrt(Vhat')<=R. For the raw
variance its weights sum to 1-d^(t+1)<1, giving the same bound.
Let D=sqrt(Vhat')+rho<=R+rho<c/2.

Induct on the invariant momentum cone
 M X<=0,   |M|<=c |X|,   X!=0.                              (1)
It holds initially since M0=0. Write M=-r X, 0<=r<=c. Then
 M'=h X, h=1-b-br in [c,1-b],
because 1-b-bc=c. Set E=(1-alpha_t)D<=D<=R+rho<c/2.
Now
 X'=-X G, G=h/E-1 >= c/(R+rho)-1=q>1,
so the sign flips and amplitude grows. Moreover
 |M'|/|X'|=hE/(h-E)<=c.
Indeed the latter is equivalent to E<=ch/(h+c), and h>=c implies
ch/(h+c)>=c/2>E. The new momentum is opposite the new position.
Thus the cone (1) propagates until the first exit, and so does the stated
geometric lower bound. If no exit occurred, |X_t|>=q^t|X0| would contradict
|X_t|<=R. The bound on N follows by the same contradiction.

The proof uses exact inequalities only; no linearization at the singular
raw-v origin and no uniform-in-time Taylor expansion is needed. The
second-moment parameter d affects the convex weights but not the escape
criterion. In diagonal dimension2, coordinate independence transfers this
scalar escape directly to the perturbation of the dormant coordinate.

Prior-work scope. The momentum threshold and gradient-reversal mechanism
are already in Fong-Yang 2608.20638v2; no novelty claim is made for the
threshold. This records the direct standard-moment cone and explicit
finite escape as a limitation on robustness of target2's exact alignment.
It does not enlarge the audited p=1 attraction interval of claim006 or
settle target1 for p>1. In that latter regime rho->0, the same escape
statement applies for fixed R<c/2 and sufficiently small eta.

[Definition 40 of arXiv:2605.02002, 'Glauber dynamics for random field Ising models on bounded degree graphs and MLSI'] (Uniform spatial mixing) We say the RFIM measure $\mu_{\widetilde{G}}$ on $G$ satisfies $\operatorname{USM}(C)$ for some constants $C>0$ if for any edge $(u,v)\in E$ and all $r\geq 1$, we have 
$$\begin{aligned}
\mathbb{E}_h[
\sup_{\theta\in[0,\theta_*]}\sup_{\Lambda\subset V,\tau_0\in\Omega(\mu_\Lambda)}&\sup_{\tau_1,\tau_2\in\Omega(\partial B((u,v),r))}\\&d_{TV}({(1-\theta)\otimes\mu^{\tau_0,\tau_1}}(\sigma_{uv}\in\cdot),{(1-\theta)\otimes\mu^{\tau_0,\tau_2}}(\sigma_{uv}\in\cdot)
]\leq e^{-Cr},
\end{aligned}$$where we use $\sigma_{uv}$ to denote the configuration $(\sigma_u,\sigma_v)$. Here $d_{TV}$ is the total variation distance and the outer expectation is taken with respect to the random field $h$. The subset $
\partial B((u,v),r)$ is the boundary of the $r$-neighborhood of the edge $(u,v)$ defined in \eqref{neighborhood}, and thus $\tau_1,\tau_2$ ranges over any two possible boundary configurations of the $r$-neighborhood $B((u,v),r)$. We use the notation ${(1-\theta)\otimes \mu^{\tau_0,\tau_i}}$ to stand for the measure $(1-\theta)\otimes \mu^{\tau_0}$ further pinned by $\tau_i$ on $\partial B((u,v),r)$, and we assume that $\tau_1,\tau_2$ are consistent with $\tau_0$ whenever they have overlapping supports.

Own-work draft; T419-C015 v1, proof (unaudited); no novelty claimed. Let Delta=u v^T, where u in R^m and v in R^p are unit vectors and m,p>=1. Consider simultaneous GD on f(b,a)=||b a^T-Delta||F^2/2, with b0=0 and a0~N(0,s^2 I_p), any s>0. Fix 0<rho<1 and 0<eps<1. Define the following deterministic real constants:

 D=2p s^2/rho, nu_bar=1+D/2,
 U_bar=2+32 nu_bar/(s^2 rho^2),
 V_bar=1+4 sqrt(p)/rho^(3/2),
 T=(1+D) log[16 nu_bar(V_bar+U_bar)/eps],
 R=sqrt(D+4)+2, L=6R^2+1,
 M=(R^2/2+1)R.

Choose any constant step

 0<eta<=min{1,1/M,[eps/(4RM)] exp[-L(T+1)]},

and take N=ceil(T/eta). With probability at least 1-rho over a0,

 ||b_N a_N^T-Delta||F<=eps.

The guarantee includes p>1, a proper input-side rank-one bottleneck, at every initialization scale. The signal condition number is 1. For a rank-one target of singular value lambda>0, use normalized scale s/sqrt(lambda), normalized step eta lambda, and normalized requested error eps/lambda in this statement. It is only a hitting-time guarantee for the prescribed eps, with no efficiency or independently checked proof claim.
Exact rank one, arbitrary input/output dimensions; zero output factor and iid Gaussian input factor with s>0
High-probability finite-accuracy statement; constant step is permitted to depend on eps and can be extremely small
No one-step-for-all-accuracies, efficiency, expectation or independent-audit conclusion

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:af20ba1d93c91c59f91fc73963b765154efe901c9edb835424dd8a4c25f00702","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/af/af20ba1d93c91c59f91fc73963b765154efe901c9edb835424dd8a4c25f00702.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:d5427a86385ff05607dd6ee1e6f91c71d4b1ce8a40776ab41bf8c4918f3bcda4","bundle_entry_key":"rank-one-gd","bundle_id":"population.t419-lora-rank-one-all-scale-finite-accuracy-and-boundedness-20261020","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"LoRA and unbalanced linear-network gradient dynamics","draft":"w705/bundle_005.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:optimization.lowrank:lora-rank-one-all-scale-gaussian-gd-finite-accuracy-euler","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# T419-C015 v1: rank-one population GD at all Gaussian scales, finite requested accuracy

Kind: narrowed. Target: 1. Status: proof (unaudited). No novelty claimed.
This covers arbitrary input/output dimensions and every s>0 at rank one. The chosen constant GD step depends on eps and can be extremely small. It is not a linear-convergence theorem for one step size simultaneously for all accuracies.

Prior work: Kunin, Raventos, Domine, Chen, Klindt, Saxe and Ganguli, Get rich quick: exact solutions reveal how unbalanced initializations promote rapid feature learning, arXiv:2406.06158, Appendix A.2, especially A.2.4 equations (30)-(33), printed p.19, and A.2.5 equation (34), p.20, already give the single-neuron unbalanced gradient-flow solutions and basin boundary under whitened data. With zero output weight, their saddle boundary reduces to w0^T beta_star=0. Gradient-flow convergence from the present initialization is therefore settled, not a new result. The quantitative estimate below uses an equivalent spectral expression for that known flow and an elementary, deliberately conservative finite-horizon Euler-error argument to obtain a specified ordinary GD hitting time. Du-Hu-Lee arXiv:1806.00900, Theorem 3.2 instead initializes both rank-one factors with a small Gaussian; it is not the zero/random all-scale theorem here. Literature novelty of the finite-step corollary is unresolved.

## Statement

Let Delta=u v^T, where u in R^m and v in R^p are unit vectors and m,p>=1. Consider simultaneous GD on f(b,a)=||b a^T-Delta||F^2/2, with b0=0 and a0~N(0,s^2 I_p), any s>0. Fix 0<rho<1 and 0<eps<1. Define the following deterministic real constants:

 D=2p s^2/rho, nu_bar=1+D/2,
 U_bar=2+32 nu_bar/(s^2 rho^2),
 V_bar=1+4 sqrt(p)/rho^(3/2),
 T=(1+D) log[16 nu_bar(V_bar+U_bar)/eps],
 R=sqrt(D+4)+2, L=6R^2+1,
 M=(R^2/2+1)R.

Choose any constant step

 0<eta<=min{1,1/M,[eps/(4RM)] exp[-L(T+1)]},

and take N=ceil(T/eta). With probability at least 1-rho over a0,

 ||b_N a_N^T-Delta||F<=eps.

The guarantee includes p>1, a proper input-side rank-one bottleneck, at every initialization scale. The signal condition number is 1. For a rank-one target of singular value lambda>0, use normalized scale s/sqrt(lambda), normalized step eta lambda, and normalized requested error eps/lambda in this statement. It is only a hitting-time guarantee for the prescribed eps, with no efficiency or independently checked proof claim.

## One initial event; no independence multiplication

Write x0=v^T a0 and z0=a0-x0 v. With probability at least 1-rho,

 d=||a0||^2<=D, |x0|>=s rho/2.

Indeed E||a0||^2=ps^2 and Markov bounds the first failure probability by rho/2. The standard normal density is at most 1/sqrt(2pi), so P(|x0|<s rho/2)<=sqrt(2/pi)rho/2<rho/2. Use a union bound; the two events need not be independent. Fix this event. In particular d>0 and x0 is nonzero.

## Known flow in a spectral representation

Both GD and gradient flow keep b in span(u), so write b=beta u and a=x v+z with z orthogonal to v. The normalized gradient flow is

 beta'=x-beta||a||^2,
 x'=beta-beta^2 x,
 z'=-beta^2 z,
 beta(0)=0, x(0)=x0, z(0)=z0.

As in the cited primary source, ||a||^2-beta^2=d is conserved. In Z=(beta,x,z) coordinates define the symmetric block operator

 H_d=[[ -d/2, 1 ],[ 1, d/2 ]] on (beta,x),
 H_d=(d/2)I on the z coordinates.

Then the exact flow is equivalently

 Z'=H_d Z-(||Z||^2/2)Z,
 Z(t)=w(t)/sqrt(1+integral_0^t ||w(tau)||^2 d tau),
 w(t)=exp(t H_d)Z0.

The displayed expression follows by differentiating its positive scalar denominator. It starts at Z0 and solves the same ODE, so uniqueness identifies it with the source's known single-neuron flow; it is not an additional claimed discovery. Its denominator never vanishes. Alternatively, boundedness below gives global existence directly.

Let nu=sqrt(1+d^2/4), g=nu-d/2=1/(nu+d/2). The two eigenvalues of the 2-by-2 block are nu and -nu, with orthonormal eigenvectors e_plus,e_minus. Choose e_plus with positive beta and x entries. Decompose

 w(t)=a_plus e^(nu t)e_plus+a_minus e^(-nu t)e_minus+e^(d t/2)z0.

Because Z0=(0,x0,z0), the spectral projections give

 a_plus^2=x0^2(1+d/(2nu))/2>=x0^2/2,
 a_minus^2=x0^2(1-d/(2nu))/2<=a_plus^2.

In particular a_plus is nonzero. The limiting factors are

 Z_star=sign(a_plus)sqrt(2nu)e_plus,

and their product is the target: the positive eigenvector obeys x/beta=nu+d/2=1/g, while its scaled squared norm is 2nu=g+1/g, hence beta_star^2=g and beta_star x_star=1. Its z component is zero.

## Explicit exponential flow error bound

Let h(t)^2=1+integral_0^t ||w(tau)||^2 d tau and

 Q(t)=h(t)^2/[a_plus^2 e^(2nu t)/(2nu)].

Orthogonality of the three spectral components gives the exact formula

 h(t)^2=1+a_plus^2(e^(2nu t)-1)/(2nu)
          +a_minus^2(1-e^(-2nu t))/(2nu)
          +||z0||^2(e^(d t)-1)/d.

Subtract the leading exponential term. Since 2nu>=2g, ||z0||^2<=d, and a_plus^2>=x0^2/2, it follows that

 |Q(t)-1|<=U e^(-2gt), U=2+8nu/x0^2.

To see every term, the initial constant and the two constant/decaying eigenmode corrections contribute at most (2nu/a_plus^2+1+a_minus^2/a_plus^2)e^(-2nu t), bounded by (4nu/x0^2+2)e^(-2gt). The z integral contributes at most [2nu||z0||^2/(d a_plus^2)]e^(-(2nu-d)t), bounded by (4nu/x0^2)e^(-2gt).

Also, after division of w(t) by a_plus e^(nu t), the nonleading vector has norm at most

 V e^(-gt), V=1+sqrt(2)||z0||/|x0|.

When U e^(-2gt)<=1/2, Q>=1/2, Q^(-1/2)<=sqrt(2) and |Q^(-1/2)-1|<=sqrt(2)|Q-1|. Consequently

 ||Z(t)-Z_star||<=2sqrt(nu)(V+U)e^(-gt).

For completeness, flow loss decreases from f0=1/2, so ||beta a||<=2. The invariant gives beta^2(beta^2+d)<=4, whence beta^2<=2 and ||Z(t)||^2=2beta^2+d<=4+d<=6nu. Also ||Z_star||^2=2nu. The product map is Lipschitz with bound at most ||Z(t)||+||Z_star||<=4sqrt(nu) along the segment between these points, so

 ||beta(t)a(t)-v||<=8nu(V+U)e^(-gt).

On the chosen event, nu<=nu_bar, U<=U_bar, V<=V_bar, and g>=1/(1+D). The definition of T therefore ensures for every t>=T both the required Q condition and

 ||beta(t)a(t)-v||<=eps/2.

For the Q condition explicitly, e^(-gT)<=eps/[16nu_bar(V_bar+U_bar)], so U e^(-2gT)<=U_bar/[256nu_bar^2(V_bar+U_bar)^2]<1/2. This avoids any implicit large-time qualification.

## Rigorous finite-horizon GD transfer

This is an analytical Euler-error bound; no floating-point computation is used or asserted as a certificate. Let F=-grad f for the reduced pair Z=(beta,a), with f=||beta a-v||^2/2. Set H=T+1. The exact flow has ||Z(t)||<=sqrt(D+4)=R-2 for every t>=0. On the whole pair-norm ball of radius R,

 ||F(Z)||<=(R^2/2+1)R=M,
 ||DF(Z)||op<=6R^2+1=L.

The first bound follows from ||beta a-v||<=R^2/2+1. For the second, expand the Hessian quadratic form

 ||d_beta a+beta d_a||^2+2<beta a-v,d_beta d_a>;

its absolute value is at most (3R^2/2+1)(d_beta^2+||d_a||^2), which is smaller than L times that squared norm. The larger L is deliberately conservative.

For one exact-flow step, integration of F and its Lipschitz bound gives the local defect

 ||Z(t+eta)-Z(t)-eta F(Z(t))||<=eta^2 L M/2.

Let E_k=||Z_k^GD-Z(k eta)||. Provided the current GD point is in the radius-R ball, the segment to the flow point is also in it and

 E_(k+1)<=(1+eta L)E_k+eta^2 L M/2.

With E_0=0 this yields

 E_k<=(eta M/2)[(1+eta L)^k-1]
     <=(eta M/2)e^(L H)<=eps/(8R)

whenever k eta<=H. This also closes the ball condition inductively: the exact flow is within R-2 and eps/(8R)<1, so every proposed GD point stays within R-1. No boundedness of the computed GD sequence is assumed without proof.

Since eta<=1, N eta lies in [T,T+1]=[T,H]. The product map (beta,a)->beta a has derivative norm at most R on the radius-R ball, so

 ||beta_N a_N-beta(N eta)a(N eta)||<=R E_N<=eps/8.

Combining the flow error eps/2 and this transfer error gives a GD residual at most 5eps/8<eps. Reintroducing the unit output vector u preserves Frobenius residual norms and proves the statement.

## Limits

The step is constant during this finite run, chosen from deterministic parameters s,p,rho,eps rather than the sampled initializer. It may scale exponentially poorly with T and is not offered as a practical algorithmic rate. Choosing a different eta for a smaller eps is permitted in this theorem; claiming convergence at one fixed eta for all eps would require another argument. The high-probability event is essential and C013 still permits a rare escape event outside it. No expectation statement follows.

The entire rank-one flow component is known from the cited primary paper. The Euler argument is a standard method applied explicitly here, not an assertion of specialist-level novelty. The proper input-side bottleneck at ranks greater than one and arbitrary scales, efficient step/rate dependence, and Target 2 excess risk remain open in this work. [Theorem 2 of arXiv:2604.01701, '\bf Chung-type laws of the iterated logarithm for $m$-fold weighted integrated fractional '] We have that 
\begin{align}
 \lim_{T\to \infty}  \Bigg\{ & \sup_{1\le t\le T}\bigg|  \frac{J_{m,\bm\alpha}(I_{\gamma}B_H)(t)}{t^{H+\gamma+m-\alpha_1-\cdots-\alpha_m}}\bigg|-\sigma_{B,m,\bm \alpha,\gamma}\sqrt{2\log\log T}\Bigg\}=0\;\; a.s. 
  \end{align} 
for all $m\ge 0$,   $\gamma\ge 0$ and  $\alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_i<H+\gamma+i$, $i=1,\ldots,m$; and
\begin{align}
  
 \lim_{T\to \infty}  \Bigg\{ & \sup_{1\le t\le T}\bigg|  \frac{J_{m,\bm\alpha}(W_{\lambda})(t)}{t^{\lambda+m-\alpha_1-\cdots-\alpha_m}}\bigg|-\sigma_{W,m,\bm \alpha,\lambda}\sqrt{2\log\log T}\Bigg\}=0\;\; a.s.
\end{align}
for all $m\ge 0$,   $\lambda> 0$ and  $\alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_i<\lambda+i$, $i=1,\ldots,m$, where
$$\sigma_{B,m,\bm \alpha,\gamma}^2= \Var\left\{J_{m,\bm\alpha}(I_{\gamma}B_H)(1)\right\}, $$
$$\sigma_{W,m,\bm \alpha,\lambda}^2= \Var\left\{J_{m,\bm\alpha}(W_{\lambda})(1)\right\} $$
and
$$\sigma_{B,0, 0,\gamma}^2=\frac{1}{\Gamma^2(\gamma)}\int_0^1\int_0^1x^{2H+1}[(1-x)(1-xy)]^{\gamma-1}\left[1+y^{2H}-(1-y)^{2H}\right]dxdy,$$
$$\sigma_{W,0, 0,\lambda}^2= \Var\left\{ W_{\lambda}(1) \right\}=\frac{1}{2\lambda \Gamma^2\big(\lambda+1/2\big)}.$$

body: For 0 < eps < 1 and any integer n, let k be a positive integer with k > 8 log(n)/eps^2 (any k = O(eps^{-2} log n) with a suitable absolute constant suffices). Then for any n points x_1,...,x_n in a Euclidean space of arbitrary dimension there is a linear map f into R^k, obtainable with high probability from a random projection, such that for every pair i, j: (1-eps) ||x_i - x_j||^2 <= ||f(x_i) - f(x_j)||^2 <= (1+eps) ||x_i - x_j||^2. So any n points embed into O(log n / eps^2) dimensions while nearly preserving all pairwise distances. Due to William Johnson and Joram Lindenstrauss.
title: Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma

body: In mathematics, the Cantor function is an example of a function that is continuous, but not absolutely continuous. It is a notorious counterexample in analysis, because it challenges naive intuitions about continuity, derivative, and measure. Although it is continuous everywhere, and has zero derivative almost everywhere, its value still goes from 0 to 1 as its argument goes from 0 to 1. Thus, while the function seems like a constant one that cannot grow, it does indeed monotonically grow.
title: Cantor function

Let F : R^n x R^m -> R^m be continuously differentiable near (a, b) with F(a, b) = 0 and the partial Jacobian D_y F(a, b) (in the last m variables) invertible. Then near a there is a unique continuously differentiable g with g(a) = b and F(x, g(x)) = 0, and Dg(a) = -(D_y F)^{-1} D_x F evaluated at (a, b).
F continuously differentiable
D_y F(a,b) invertible
F(a,b) = 0

body:
[Lemma G_function_minimization_outside_waterfall of arXiv:2507.22011, 'Random Lozenge Waterfall:\\Dimensional Collapse of Gibbs Measures'] Fix $A\in \mathbb{Z}$, and
	let
	$d_{\mathbf{k}}^{A}(x;y)>0$.
	Assume that the configuration $\vec z$ is restricted to an interval
	$a\le z_1<\ldots<z_N \le b$, and
	\begin{equation}
		
		a\ge
		\lfloor \tfrac12(A-\mathbf{k}-1) \rfloor -
		\lfloor \tfrac{N-1}2 \rfloor +1
		\qquad
		\textnormal{or}
		\qquad
		b\le
		\lfloor \tfrac12(A-\mathbf{k}-1) \rfloor
		+ \lfloor \tfrac{N-1}2 \rfloor.
	\end{equation}
	Then for any such restricted $(N-1)$-point configuration $\vec z$, we have
	in the two cases in (equation eq:G_function_minimization_outside_waterfall of the paper), respectively:
	\begin{equation*}
		\sum\nolimits_{i=1}^{N-1}\mathscr{G}_{\mathbf{k}}(x,y,z_i\mid A)
		\ge
		\sum\nolimits_{i=a}^{a+N-2}\mathscr{G}_{\mathbf{k}}(x,y,i\mid A)
		\qquad
		\textnormal{or}
		\qquad
		\ge
		\sum\nolimits_{i=b-N+2}^{b}\mathscr{G}_{\mathbf{k}}(x,y,i\mid A).
	\end{equation*}

Own-work draft: C22 v1, proof (unaudited), route-failure, Target3; no novelty or full-target claim. Fix d>=2, unit u, X uniform on the radius-sqrt(d) sphere, Z=X.u, and continuous target q(Z) with q(sqrt(d))>0. Use the aligned exponential model f=integral a exp(b+gamma Z) dmu, w=sqrt(d) gamma u, with all a,b,w trained at original Euclidean learning rate. Initialize a=b=0 and an essentially unbounded positive scale tail: mu(gamma_0>R)>0 for every finite R. There is no common positive interval of finite absolutely continuous aligned characteristics satisfying the actual field almost everywhere, with a defined L-infinity predictor satisfying norm(f_t)_infinity to 0 at initialization. For scales above a fixed threshold, positivity of q near the pole and a hypothetical small predictor imply positive exponential lower bounds for both characteristic forces. The invariant b=a^2/2 then gives d/dt integral_0^a exp(-s^2/2) ds >= A exp(z2 gamma_0), although this transform is bounded by 3 for a>=0. The unbounded tail contradicts every common interval. A scale density proportional to exp(-gamma^4) has every finite quadratic exponential moment and a positive lower density on every compact interval, yet satisfies this obstruction. Pure degree-1 and normalized zonal harmonic targets are included because only positivity near the pole is needed. This does not exclude L2-continuous flows with narrow pole layers, other weak or non-aligned evolutions, or the bounded-scale prepared flows C5/C11, and it is not a ReLU counterexample. Locator: proofs/unbounded_aligned_scales_no_regular_flow.md, Exact statement, cap bounds (3)-(4), bounded transform (5), and Scope.

[Coro cor:cdfbounding of arXiv:2605.07920, 'Primitive Sequences for Probability Measures on Compact Intervals'] Suppose that $c_1, \ldots, c_m$ are the first $m \geq 1$ terms of an admissible sequence for $[a,b]$. Then for every $x_0 \in [a,b]$,
    \begin{equation*}
    \bar{F}_m(x_0; c_{1:m}) := \sup_{\mu \in \pazocal{F}_m(c_{1:m})} \mu([a,x_0]) 
    \quad \text{and} \quad 
    \underline{F}_m(x_0; c_{1:m}) := \inf_{\mu \in \pazocal{F}_m(c_{1:m})} \mu([a,x_0))
\end{equation*}
are attained by $(m+1)$-atomic measures. Equivalently, if $X$ is any random variable on $[a,b]$ with given moments $\mathbb{E}[X^k]$ for $k=1,\ldots,m$, then sharp bounds on $F_X(x_0) = \mathbb{P}(X \leq x_0)$ and on $F_X(x_0-) = \mathbb{P}(X < x_0)$ are attained by discrete random variables supported on at most $m+1$ points.

[Prop 10 (Composition of pseudo-differential operators) of arXiv:2609.01105, 'Obstruction to quasi-invariance of Gaussian measures under transport flows on Riemannian M'] \cite[Théorème 10.13]{Alazard2023}
Let $m,n \in \mathbb{R}$ and $a \in S^m$ and $b\in S^n$. Then there exists $a\#b \in S^{m+n}$ satisfying
\[
    \Op(a) \circ \Op(b)=\Op(a\#b). 
\]
Moreover, $a\#b$ admits the following asymptotic expansion: 
\[
    a\#b (x,\xi) \sim \sum_{\alpha \in \mathbb{N}^d} \frac{1}{i^{|\alpha|}\alpha !}\partial_{\xi}^\alpha a(x,\xi) \partial_x^{\alpha}b(x,\xi),
\]
that is for all $N\geq 1$, the symbol $a\# b - \displaystyle \sum_{|\alpha|<N}\frac{1}{i^{|\alpha|}\alpha !}\partial_{\xi}^\alpha a(x,\xi) \partial_x^{\alpha}b(x,\xi)$ belongs to $S^{m+n-N}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Composition of pseudo-differential operators

The normalizing constants can be chosen as b_n = 0 and a_n = F^{-1}(1 - 1/n).

body:
[Proposition 44 of arXiv:2609.02416, '2609.02416'] Let $\varepsilon>0$, $\delta\ge0$, $q\in C([-L,L])$ with $q\ge q_0>0$, and $a\in C([-L,L])$. Consider
\[
\cT_{\varepsilon,\delta}u
=q(x)u'(x)+\varepsilon\int_{-L}^{L}u(y)\,dy-\delta u(x)+a(x)u(x).
\]
Its principal eigenvalue $\lambda_{\varepsilon,\delta}$ is the unique real number satisfying
\[
1=\varepsilon\int_{-L}^{L}\int_x^L\frac1{q(t)}
\exp\left(\int_x^t\frac{a(r)+\lambda_{\varepsilon,\delta}-\delta}{q(r)}\,dr\right)dt\,dx.
\]
Up to multiplication by a positive constant, the corresponding eigenfunction is
\[
\phi_{\varepsilon,\delta}(x)
=\int_x^L\frac1{q(t)}
\exp\left(\int_x^t\frac{a(r)+\lambda_{\varepsilon,\delta}-\delta}{q(r)}\,dr\right)dt.
\]
Put
\[
T_q=\int_{-L}^{L}\frac{dx}{q(x)},\qquad
A_q=\int_{-L}^{L}\frac{a(x)}{q(x)}\,dx.
\]
Then, as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$,
\[
\lambda_{\varepsilon,\delta}
=\delta+\frac1{T_q}\left[
\log\frac1\varepsilon+2\log\log\frac1\varepsilon
-2\log T_q-\log q(-L)-A_q
\right]+o(1).
\]
The remainder is independent of $\delta$; in particular it is uniform when $\delta$ ranges in arbitrary subsets of $[0,\infty)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Lemma (campaign status: proved): Let $A=\{\pm1\}\times A'$ span $\mathbb R\oplus V'$ and suppose $g(s,x)=as+g'(x)$ is sign-valued on $A$. For every $x\in A'$ both $a+g'(x)$ and $-a+g'(x)$ lie in $\{\pm1\}$; therefore either $a=0$ and $g'$ is sign-valued on $A'$, or $|a|=1$ and $g'$ vanishes on the spanning set $A'$, so $g=\pm s$. Hence the projective full dual of a free product is exactly the disjoint union of the free coordinate and the full dual of the reduced factor. Notes: Consequence: deleting or reinserting free coordinates creates NO hidden full-dual form. This is what justifies every occurrence of 'after zero Gale columns are deleted' in the finite reduction -- a hypothesis-preservation lemma, not just a counting one.

[Definition dfn:B-gate of arXiv:2608.05262, 'The law of $(1+1)$D SOS with an area tilt in a wedge'] We denote by 
$\mu_{\lambda,\mathfrak a,\ell}^{\mathfrak{o}}$ the probability measures on $C(\mathbb R,\mathbb R^\ell)$ 
obtained as the weak limit $T \to \infty$  of the probability measures 
$\mathbb P^{\underline{0},\underline{0}}_{\ell;-T,T}\left(\cdot\mid \mathfrak a,\lambda\right)$
from [CIW19b].  The existence of such a limit follows from the tightness in 
[CIW19b] together with the monotonicity property of [CIW19b].
The associated stochastic process is called a Brownian {\sc{\lowercase{gate}}}
(of $\ell$ curves and area tilt $\mathfrak a \lambda^{i-1}$ for curve~$i$).

[Proposition prop:dc-clean-normalized-trace-defect-direct of arXiv:2608.02772, 'Non-Abelian Hirota-Miwa Equations for the KPZ Universality Class'] Under the hypotheses of
Proposition~(prop:dc-clean-dressed-waves of the paper), assume additionally
that $\dim E<\infty$, that $H$ is a real separable Hilbert space
with $K(u)\in\mathfrak S_1(H)$, that $K$ is $C^1$ in $\partial_1$
and $C^2$ in $\partial_2$ in trace norm, and that
$C_2(u)\in\operatorname{GL}(E)$ for every $u\in\mathcal V$.  Define
$F(u)\vcentcolon= \det_H(I-zK(u))$ and
$\mathcal B(u)\vcentcolon= \Delta_2(u)C_2(u)^{-1}$.
Then
\begin{align}
\frac{
\left(D_1-\frac{1}{2}D_2^2\right)
F(S_3u)\cdot F(u)
}{
F(S_3u)F(u)
}
&=
\frac{1}{2}
\left[
\operatorname{tr}_E\bigl(\mathcal B(u)^2\bigr)
-
\bigl(\operatorname{tr}_E\mathcal B(u)\bigr)^2
\right]
\notag \\
&\quad
+\operatorname{tr}_E
\left[
\mathcal B(u)
\left(
C_1(u)+\Lambda_2(u)C_2(u)^{-1}
\right)
\right].

\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:dc-clean-normalized-trace-defect-direct of arXiv:2608.02772

[Lemma 26 (One-step \(p\)-moment drift for RLMC) of arXiv:2605.24937, '2605.24937'] Fix \(p\ge 2\). Under Assumption~\hyperref[ass:D]{\textup{(A4)}}, there exist constants
\(q>0\) and \(C_p>0\), depending only on \(p\), \(d\), \(a\), \(b\), and \(\beta\), such that for all
\(\lambda\in(0,1]\),
\[
  \E\|Y'_{n+1}\|^p
  \le
  e^{-q\lambda}\,\E\|\widetilde Y_n\|^p
  +
  C_p\lambda,
\]
where
\[
  Y'_{n+1}\sim P_\lambda(\widetilde Y_n,\cdot),
  \qquad
  \widetilde Y_n=(1-\eta_n)Y_n' + \eta_n\bar Y_n,
  \qquad
  \eta_n\in[0,1].
\]

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The following integral converges, for any real number $s>0$,
$$\Gamma(s)=\int_0^\infty x^{s-1}e^{-x}\,dx$$
satisfies $\Gamma(s+1)=s\Gamma(s)$, and extends the usual factorial, $\Gamma(n)=(n-1)!$ for $n\in\mathbb N$.

Conjecture and exact unresolved input, not a proved theorem. In iid finite nonnegative nonatomic nearest-neighbor FPP on Z^2, put a=essential infimum of the weight law and use the deleted-edge capacity H_infinity of this bundle. The support-collapse assertion is H_infinity<=a almost surely for either orientation of a fixed edge. Since F(h)=0 exactly for h<=a, the conditional threshold identity makes this equivalent to zero probability of a bigeodesic through the fixed edge. Countably many edges then give simultaneous absence everywhere. For the standard literature regime additionally assume E[min(t_1,t_2,t_3,t_4)^2]<infinity for independent samples. Local detours give only H_infinity<=d(u,v); this is insufficient. No proof of support collapse is supplied. body: [Lemma unique-algebra-structure-initial of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Let $(A,a)$ be an idempotent algebra, viewed as an object of $\CAlg({\mathcal{C}})$. If $B\in\CAlg({\mathcal{C}})$ is arbitrary, then ${\textup{Hom}}_{\CAlg({\mathcal{C}})}(A,B)$ is empty or contractible, and there exists a map $A\to B$ of commutative algebras if and only if (the underlying object of) $B$ is an $A$-module. In particular, $A$ is the initial commutative algebra that is also an $A$-module.\qed (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

  \]
  of matrices $A_\ell \in \R^{N_\ell \times N_{\ell-1}}$ and bias vectors $b_\ell \in \R^{N_\ell}$,
  where $N_\ell \in \N$ specifies the width of the $\ell$-th layer of the network.
  We define the \emph{input- and output dimensions} of $\CalW$ as
  $d_{\mathrm{in}}(\CalW) := N_0$ and $d_{\mathrm{out}}(\CalW) := N_L$.

  The associated \emph{neural network function} using the ReLU activation function
  $\varrho : \R \to \R$, $\varrho(x) = \max \{ 0, x \}$ is given by
  \[
    R_\varrho (\CalW) : \quad \R^{d_{\mathrm{in}}(\CalW)} \to \R^{d_{\mathrm{out}} (\CalW)},
    \quad
    R_\varrho (\CalW)
    := T_L \circ (\varrho \circ T_{L-1}) \circ \cdots \circ (\varrho \circ T_1)
    ,
  \]
  where $T_\ell \, x = A_\ell \, x + b_\ell$, and where $\varrho$ acts componentwise on vectors,
  i.e.,
  \[
    \varrho \bigl( (x_1,\dots,x_m)\bigr)
    = \bigl(\varrho(x_1), \dots, \varrho(x_m)\bigr)
    .
  \]
  In this paper, we measure the ``complexity'' of
  $\CalW$ in terms of the \emph{number of non-zero weights}
  \[
      \norm{\CalW}_{\ell^0}
    := \sum_{j=1}^{L} \bigl(\| A_j \|_{\ell^0} + \| b_j \|_{\ell^0}\bigr)
    ,
  \]
  in terms of the \emph{network depth} $L(\CalW) := L$,
  and in terms of the \emph{weight magnitude}
  \[
      \| \CalW \|_{\ell^{\infty}}
    := \max_{1 \leq j \leq L} \bigl(\| A_j \|_{\ell^\infty} + \| b_j \|_{\ell^\infty}\bigr)
    .
  \]
  Here, for a matrix (or vector) $A$, the quantity $\| A \|_{\ell^0}$
  counts the total number of non-zero entries of $A$,
  and $\| A \|_{\ell^\infty} := \max_{i,j} |A_{i,j}|$.

  Now, given $d,g \in \N$, we define for $n \in \N$ the set of ReLU networks $\R^d \to \R$
  with at most $n$ non-zero weights, weight magnitude "of moderate growth",
  and number of layers growing at most poly-logarithmically with $n$ as
  \[
    \CalNN_n (g, \R^d)
    := \Bigl\{
         R_\varrho (\CalW)
         \,\,:\,\,
         \begin{array}{l}
           \CalW \text{ neural network weights with }
           d_{\mathrm{in}}(\CalW) = d,
           d_{\mathrm{out}}(\CalW) = 1, \\
           \norm{\CalW}_{\ell^0} \leq n, \,\,
           \norm{\CalW}_{\ell^{\infty}} \leq g \cdot n^{g},
           \text{ and }
           L(\CalW) \leq (\ln(e n))^g
         \end{array}
       \Bigr\}
    .
  \]

body:
[Theorem thm:shocks_coal of arXiv:2605.26048, 'Classification of the eternal solutions and multiple coalescing shocks in the KPZ fixed po'] For almost-every $\omega$, the following holds for all $b \in \mathcal{B}_\omega$. 
\begin{enumerate} [label=(\roman*), font=\normalfont] 
    \item  For each $\xi \in \pmb{\xi}^b$, the set $\mathfrak{C}^b(\xi)$ is connected and unbounded. Specifically, we may write
    \begin{equation} 
    \mathfrak{C}^b(\xi)=\bigcup_{s<t_{\text{ext}}(\xi)} (\mathfrak{a}^s_\xi,\mathfrak{b}^s_{\xi}]\times \{s\},
    \end{equation}
    for numbers $\mathfrak{a}^s_\xi \in [-\infty,\infty)$ and $\mathfrak{b}_s^\xi \in (-\infty,\infty]$ with $\mathfrak{a}^s_\xi<\mathfrak{b}^s_{\xi}$ for all $s < t_{\text{ext}}(\xi)$, and $t_{\text{ext}}(\xi) \in (-\infty,\infty]$ is called the \textbf{extinction time} for the color $\xi \in \pmb{\xi}^b$. If $\mathfrak{a}_\xi^{s'} > -\infty$ for some $\xi \in \pmb{\xi}^b$ and $s' <t_{\text{ext}}(\xi)$, then $\mathfrak{a}_\xi^s > -\infty$ for all $s <t_{\text{ext}}(\xi)$, and the function $s \mapsto \mathfrak{a}_\xi^s$ is continuous. Similarly, if $\mathfrak{b}_\xi^{s'} < \infty$, for some $s' <t_{\text{ext}}(\xi)$, then $\mathfrak{b}_\xi^s < \infty$ for all $s <t_{\text{ext}}(\xi)$, and $s \mapsto \mathfrak{b}_\xi^s$ is continuous. 
    

    
     \item  For $\xi \in \pmb{\xi}^b$, $t_{\text{ext}}(\xi)<\infty$  if and only if $\mathfrak{a}_\xi^s > -\infty$ and $\mathfrak{b}_\xi^s < \infty$ for some $s \in \mathbb{R}$. That is, a color survives forward in time if and only if it is not bounded between two other colors. If this is the case, the following limits exist and are equal:
    \begin{equation} 
    x_{\text{ext}}(\xi) :=\lim_{s\uparrow t_{\text{ext}}}\mathfrak{a}_\xi^s=\lim_{s\uparrow t_{\text{ext}}}\mathfrak{b}_\xi^s
    \end{equation}
    We call $p(\xi) :=  (x_{\text{ext}}(\xi),t_{\text{ext}}(\xi))$ the \textbf{extinction point} of the color $\xi$. 
  
    \item  No two colors share the same extinction point. From every extinction point, there exists three disjoint semi-infinite geodesics \rm{(}i.e., they are distinct except at the initial point\rm{)}. Furthermore, the set of extinction points is locally finite. 
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:shocks_coal of arXiv:2605.26048

body:
[Corollary 8 (One-sheet graphical convergence) of arXiv:2609.03916, 'Halfspace Theorems for Anisotropic Minimal Surfaces and Perimeter Minimizers'] Let $E_j$ be $\Phi$-perimeter minimizers in $B_2$, suppose that $T_{E_j}$ is
absolutely $\Phi$-mass minimizing in $B_2$, and assume
$0\in\supp|D\chi_{E_j}|$.  Let $H$ be a halfspace with measure-theoretic outer
unit normal $\nu_H$, let $0\in P:=\partial H$, and suppose that
\begin{equation}
 \chi_{E_j}\to\chi_H
 \quad\text{in }L^1(B_2),
 \qquad
 D\chi_{E_j}\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}D\chi_H,
 \qquad
 |D\chi_{E_j}|\stackrel{*}{\rightharpoonup}|D\chi_H|.
\end{equation}
Then there exists $\theta_*=\theta_*(n,\lambda)>0$ such that, for all
sufficiently large $j$, there is a function
$u_j:P\cap B_{\theta_*}\to\R$ of class $C^2$ for which
\begin{equation}
 \supp|D\chi_{E_j}|\cap\mathcal C_{\theta_*}(\nu_H)
 =\{y+u_j(y)\nu_H:y\in P\cap B_{\theta_*}\}.
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 \|u_j\|_{C^1(P\cap B_{\theta_*})}\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \sup_{\supp|D\chi_{E_j}|\cap
       \mathcal C_{\theta_*}(\nu_H)}
 |\nu_{E_j}-\nu_H|\longrightarrow0.
\end{equation}
Thus the whole support in the smaller cylinder is one sheet, not merely one
regular component.

[Definition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] We say that a random variable $f:X\to\mathbb R$ is exponential, with parameter $\lambda>0$, if its law is as follows:
$$\mu(x)=\lambda e^{-\lambda x}\chi_{[0,\infty]}(x)dx$$
That is, the density of $f$ must be $\varphi(x)=\lambda e^{-\lambda x}$, over the positive numbers.

[Lemma leminv of arXiv:2607.12459, 'Renormalisation of Inhomogeneous Random Graphs'] {\bf [Invariance property for the connection probability]}

For every $\delta \in (0,\infty)$ and $\eta \in [0,\infty)$, the choice 
\[
g^{\neq}_\delta(x,y) = \delta xy, \qquad g^{=}_\eta(x) = \eta x,
 \]
is invariant under addition of the weights in the aggregation. In other words, the renormalised graph has the same connection functions as the original graph, provided the weight of an aggregated vertex equals the sum of the weights of the constituent vertices, i.e., the aggregated vertex $I^{(1)}$ has weight $\bar{X}_{I^{(1)}} = \sum_{i \in I^{(1)}} X_i$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\]

Let mesh-delta_j square-lattice Dobrushin domains (Omega_j,a_j,b_j) converge in the Caratheodory sense to a simply connected marked domain (Omega,a,b), with delta_j tending to zero. In the critical FK-Ising random-cluster model q=2 and p=sqrt(2)/(1+sqrt(2)), let F_j be Smirnov's parafermionic observable of spin sigma=1/2. Then delta_j^(-1/2) F_j converges uniformly on compact subsets away from the boundary to (Phi')^(1/2), where Phi maps Omega conformally to a horizontal strip of width 2 and sends a,b to its ends. This theorem has q=2 and an observable conclusion; it does not directly establish the independent square-bond q=1 target.

The Schwartz space $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)$ is the set of $f\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C)$ such that $p_{\alpha,\beta}(f)=\sup_{x\in\mathbb R^d}|x^\alpha\partial^\beta f(x)|<\infty$ for all multi-indices $\alpha,\beta$. With the countable family of seminorms $p_{\alpha,\beta}$ it is a Frechet space. It contains $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$ and the Gaussians $e^{-\pi a|x|^2}$ ($a>0$); it is contained in $L^p(\mathbb R^d)$ for every $1\le p\le\infty$, is dense in $L^p$ for $1\le p<\infty$, and is closed under multiplication by polynomials, differentiation, products and convolution. Its continuous dual $\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^d)$ is the space of tempered distributions; the Fourier transform extends to $\mathcal S'$ by $\langle\hat T,\varphi\rangle=\langle T,\hat\varphi\rangle$, which is consistent with the integral definition on $L^1$ and with Plancherel on $L^2$. Note $C_c^\infty$ is not closed under the Fourier transform (a nonzero compactly supported function has a transform that is not compactly supported), while $\mathcal S$ is.
functions are smooth and complex-valued on R^d

		\begin{enumerate}
			\item For any $\sigma\in \mcT$ and $\tau=X^k\prod_{j=1}^n\mcI_{b_j}(\tau_j)$ we have
			$$

			\begin{equation}
			\Upsilon_F[(\downarrow^k)^*\tau] = \partial^k \Upsilon_F[\tau].

		\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 9 of arXiv:2605.13727, 'Stochastic evolution equations\\ driven by arbitrary cylindrical Lévy processes'] Let $(\Psi_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of $L$-integrable, predictable processes 
	converging to an $L_2(U,H)$-valued predictable process $\Psi$  $P_T$-a.e.  If there exists an $L$-integrable predictable  process $\Upsilon $ satisfying for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$ that
	\[(\zeta_L+\eta_L)(\Psi_n(\omega,t)) \leq (\zeta_L+\eta_L)(\Upsilon(\omega,t)) \quad  \text{for $P_T$-a.a.\ $(\omega,t)\in \Omega\times [0,T]$}, \]
	then $\Psi$ is $L$-integrable  and satisfies
	\[\displaystyle \lim_{n\to\infty} d_T^{em}(I(\Psi_n),I(\Psi))=0.\]

[Corollary 16 of arXiv:2604.13149, 'The Distributional Tail of Worst--Case Quickselect'] Assume that \(L_0:\R\to[0,1]\) is measurable, and let
\[
L_{n+1}\defeq \mathcal K L_n,
\qquad n\ge 0.
\]

\begin{enumerate}
\item If \(L_0\) is nondecreasing, then every \(L_n\) is nondecreasing.

\item If \(L_0\le F\) on \(\R\), then
\[
L_n\le F
\qquad\text{on }\R
\]
for every \(n\ge 0\).

\item If \(L_0\le L_1\) on \(\R\), then
\[
L_n\le L_{n+1}
\qquad\text{on }\R
\]
for every \(n\ge 0\).
\end{enumerate}

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: A zero-one law for Poisson-coloring frontier dimension structural attempt Result: The dimension event is not visibly a tail event of the independent arriving points. Changing an early point can change the color of infinitely many later descendants, so Kolmogorov zero-one cannot be invoked without a finite-modification invariance proof. The potential route is a regeneration principle producing, inside every surviving interface neighborhood, copies with the full essential supremum of the dimension law; countable-union stability of dimension would then force the maximal value. Check: The mere facts that the frontier is closed and has dimension strictly between1 and2 do not imply determinism: a Bernoulli mixture of two fixed compact fractal curves with different dimensions satisfies those facts and has random dimension. This is a logical control, not a Poisson-coloring counterexample. Obstruction: Independent arrivals do not make recursively inherited colors independent across subregions. A regeneration or local-universality statement strong enough to remove early-history effects is missing.

[Thm 2 of arXiv:2609.03821, 'Condensation and Metastability in the Supercritical Two-Species Zero-Range Process via Res'] Suppose that $\alpha>1$. For any $x\in S_{\star}$,
the following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item (Local metastability) Each set $\mathcal{E}^{x}_{N}$ is metastable,
in the sense that from any configuration in $\mathcal{E}^{x}_{N}$,
it reaches $\bm{\xi}^{x}_{N}$ (cf. \eqref{eq:xiNx}) before exiting
$\tilde{\mathcal{E}}^{x}_{N}$ with high probability:
\[
\lim_{N\to\infty}\inf_{\bm{\eta}\in\mathcal{E}^{x}_{N}}\mathbb{P}^{N}_{\bm{\eta}}\left[H_{\bm{\xi}^{x}_{N}}<H_{\Omega_{N}\setminus\tilde{\mathcal{E}}^{x}_{N}}\right]=1.
\]
\item (Dynamical transitions) The law of the accelerated order process $\{X_{N}(\theta_{N}t)\}_{t\ge0}$
starting from any configuration in $\mathcal{E}^{x}_{N}$ converges
weakly, in the Skorokhod topology as $N\to\infty$, to the law of
the limiting Markov chain $\mathbb{X}$ starting from $x$.
\item (Negligibility) The time spent outside $\mathcal{E}_{N}$ is negligible:
\[
\lim_{N\to\infty}\sup_{\bm{\eta}\in\mathcal{E}^{x}_{N}}\mathbb{E}^{N}_{\bm{\eta}}\left[\int^{T}_{0}{\bf 1}\left\{ \bm{\eta}_{N}(\theta_{N}u)\in\Delta_{N}\right\} {\rm d}u\right]=0\qquad\text{for all}\quad T>0.
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 2 of arXiv:2609.03821

[Lemma L_Fs of arXiv:2605.15066, 'The critical activation density in graph bootstrap percolation'] Let $A$ be a graph. 
For each edge $e$ in $A$, put $W_e=F_e=e$. 
Recall that, for all other edges $e$ in 
$\langle A\rangle_H\setminus A$, the WGA 
identifies a copy $H_e$ of $H$ completed by $e$ and  
an inclusion-minimal 
subgraph 
\[
W_e=\bigcup_{f\in E(H_e\setminus e)}W_f\subset A
\]
for which $(e,W_e)\in{\mathcal A}(H)$. 
Then, for each such $e$, 
there is some  $e\subset F_e\subseteq W_e\cup e$, for which 
$\rho(e,F_e)\geqslant\rho(H)$ and 
\begin{equation}
v(F_e)-2\leqslant\sum_{f\in E(H_e\setminus e)} v(F_f). 
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma L_Fs of arXiv:2605.15066

[Lemma lem:sec5-finite-probe of arXiv:2607.18070, 'The Brownian loop-catcher'] For $0\leq\lambda\leq1$, let $S_{\lambda,\times}$ be the output of Algorithm~(alg:time-catcher of the paper) applied in $V$ to the independent normalized random walks with endpoint pairs $(x_i,y_i)$.  Then
\[
 \operatorname{Law}(S_{\lambda,\times})
 =\mathbf p_{\lambda,\times}:=(T_\lambda^V)^{-1}\mathbf h_\times.
\]
Note that for each fixed $\lambda$, the construction in
Algorithm~(alg:time-catcher of the paper) couples these sets so that
$S_{1,\times}\subset S_{\lambda,\times}\subset S_{0,\times}$.
Here $S_{0,\times}$ is the union of $r$ independent normalized random-walk
bridges from $x_i$ to $y_i$, while $S_{1,\times}$ is the entangled multipath
LERW.  Every component of $S_{\lambda,\times}$ contains a path joining one
labelled endpoint pair.  Thus it has at most $r$ components, and it is
connected if all pairs share one endpoint. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Finite interior probe

[Definition 7 (Bernoulli paths and Bernoulli path ensembles) of arXiv:2605.26664, 'Mixing times for Glauber dynamics of lozenge tilings of the hexagon'] Given $p=(x_p,y_p),q=(x_q,y_q)\in \mathbb T_N+(0,1/(2N))$ such that $x_p<x_q$ and $0 \le y_q-y_p \le x_q-x_p$, we call \emph{Bernoulli path} with endpoints $p,q$ any path $S$ that starts at $p$, ends at $q$ and 
 such that 
 each step of $S$  is either $(1/N,0)$  or $(1/N,1/N)$ (that is, steps are either in the SE or in the  NE direction).
 
    Given $n\in \mathbb N$ and distinct points
    $p_1,\dots,p_n,q_1,\dots,q_n$  of $\mathbb T_N+(0,1/(2N))$ such that all the $p_i$ have
    the same $x-$coordinate  $x_p$ (and the $q_i$ also have all the same $x$-coordinate $x_q>x_p$) and ordered so that the $y-$coordinate of $p_i$ is larger than that of  $p_j$ (resp. the $y$-coordinate of $q_i$
    is larger than that of $q_j$) for $i>j$, we let the \emph{Bernoulli path ensemble} with endpoints
    $p_1,\dots,p_n,q_1,\dots,q_n$ denote the uniform measure on
    $n-$ples     $(S_1,\dots,S_n)$ of non-intersecting (i.e., disjoint) Bernoulli paths, where $S_i$ has endpoints $(p_i,q_i)$. (We assume
    that the points $p_i,q_i,i\le n$ are such that the configuration
    space is nonempty).
title: Bernoulli paths and Bernoulli path ensembles

Independent derivation pending w440 review. Replace every edge of the infinite 3-regular tree with L edges, for a positive integer L, and root at an original vertex. The result T_L is quasi-transitive of maximum degree 3 and has p_c=2^(-1/L)<1. Full subdivided edges are independent coarse bonds of retention p^L, so critical clusters are almost surely finite. For 1<=n<=L the critical probability of reaching graph distance n is 1-(1-2^(-n/L))^3, hence 7/8 at n=L. At radii kL, with u_0=1 and u_(k+1)=u_k-u_k^2/4, the probability is 1-(1-u_(k-1)/2)^3. Reciprocal increments tend to 1/4, so (kL) times this probability tends to 6L. Critical susceptibility is infinite because every original-vertex shell has expected connected count 3/2.
L is a positive integer

iid Bernoulli bonds
root is an original degree-3 vertex

body: [Definition 8 of arXiv:2608.18688, 'Regularity Preservation for Jump-Type Stochastic Transport Equations with Singular Drift'] A local random field is a family of real-valued random variable $X_t(x)$, indexed by $x\in\mR^d$ and $t\in  [0,\tau(x))$,  where $\tau(x)=\tau(x,\omega)$ is an accessible, lower semicontinuous stopping time. Specifically, if the random field $\tau(x)$ satisfies $\tau(x)=+\infty$ for all $x\in \mR^d$ almost surely, then $X_t(x)$ is called a global random field or simply a random field. The random field $\tau(x)$ is commonly referred  to as the terminal time of $X_t(x)$.

If $(U_t)_{t\geq 0}$ satisfies that $\overline{X}\in\mathcal{H}$, for any $X\in \mathcal{H}$. Then the following two statements are equivalent:
		\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
			\item $\hat{\mathbb{E}}$ is ergodic;
			\item there exists an ergodic probability $P$ on $\sigma(\mathcal{H})$ such that for any  $X\in \mathcal{H}$,  
			\[\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{T}\int_0^TX\circ \theta_tdt=\int XdP, \text{ }\hat{\mathbb{E}}\text{-q.s.}\]
		\end{enumerate}
		In this case,  $P$ is the unique  ergodic probability with respect to $\theta_t, \ t\geq 0$ in $\mathcal{P}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma LCorollary1 of arXiv:2604.06012, 'Large fringe trees for random trees with given vertex degrees'] Let $\mathbf{n}$ be a degree statistic and let $\mathcal{T}_{\mathbf{n}} \in {\rm Unif}(\mathbb{T}_{\mathbf{n}})$. For $T \in \mathbb{T}$,
\begin{align}
\mathbb{E} N_{\mathbf{n}_{T}}(\mathcal{T}_{\mathbf{n}}) & = |\mathbb{T}_{\mathbf{n}_{T}}|  \cdot  \mathbb{E} N_{T}(\mathcal{T}_{\mathbf{n}}),   \\
{\rm Var}(N_{\mathbf{n}_{T}}(\mathcal{T}_{\mathbf{n}})) & 
=  |\mathbb{T}_{\mathbf{n}_{T}}|^{2}  \cdot  {\rm Var}(N_{T}(\mathcal{T}_{\mathbf{n}})) - |\mathbb{T}_{\mathbf{n}_{T}}| \cdot (|\mathbb{T}_{\mathbf{n}_{T}}|-1) \cdot  \mathbb{E} N_{T}(\mathcal{T}_{\mathbf{n}})
\notag\\&
=|\mathbb T_{{\mathbf{n}}_T}|^2\cdot\bigl(\operatorname{Var} N_T({\mathcal T}_{{\mathbf{n}}})-\operatorname{\mathbb E{}} N_T({\mathcal T}_{{\mathbf{n}}})\bigr)
+ |\mathbb T_{{\mathbf{n}}_T}|\cdot\operatorname{\mathbb E{}} N_T({\mathcal T}_{{\mathbf{n}}})
.
\end{align}
title: Lemma LCorollary1 of arXiv:2604.06012

[Corollary 4 of arXiv:2608.17562, '2608.17562'] Wasserstein bounds.
Let $(X_{i})_{i \ge 1}$ be a sequence of \iid random variables with common distribution function $F$. Assume that $\widebar{F} \in \SRV{\alpha}{\rho}$, with $\alpha > 1$, $\rho < 0$, and auxiliary function~$A$. There exists a positive constant $C$ such that
\begin{equation}
   
\mathrm{d}_{W} (Z_{n}, \mathcal{F}(\alpha)) \leq C\Big(\frac{1}{n} + A(a_n)\Big),
 \quad n \geq 1, 
\end{equation} 
if the $X_{i}$s are continuous random variables.
 If not, then for any $\delta \in (1, \alpha)$, there exists a constant $C_{\delta} > 0$ such that 
\[
\mathrm{d}_{W} (Z_{n}, \mathcal{F}(\alpha)) \leq C_{\delta}\Big(\frac{1}{n} + A(a_n)\Big)^{1 - {1}/{\delta}}, \quad n \geq 1. 
\]
