body: [Lem ftoeflemma of arXiv:2510.18856, 'Evolution of recursive trees with limited memory'] Suppose a sequence of trees $\left\{\mathcal{T}_n\right\}_{n\geqslant 1}$ converges in probability, in the fringe sense, to $\varpi$. Moreover, suppose that $\varpi$ is a fringe distribution in the sense of Definition~(fringedef of the paper). Then $\left\{\mathcal{T}_n\right\}_{n\geqslant 1}$ converges in probability, in the extended fringe sense, to a limiting infinite random sin-tree $\mathcal{T}_{\infty}$ whose law $\varpi^{EF}$ is uniquely obtained from $\varpi$ via~(equation ftoef of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem ftoeflemma of arXiv:2510.18856

[Proposition prop:softlocal of arXiv:2608.24830, 'Motion helps the contact process: survival below\\ the percolation threshold on Poisson Br'] Let $J$ be an at most countable index set and let $(Z_j)_{j\in J}$ be independent random points
of $\mathbb{R}^d$ with densities $g_j$. Let $(\xi_j)_{j\in J}$ be i.i.d.\ exponential random variables
of mean $1$ and define the soft local time
\[
  H_J(y)=\sum_{j\in J}\xi_j\,g_j(y),\qquad y\in\mathbb{R}^d .
\]
Let $\rho\colon\mathbb{R}^d\to[0,\infty)$ be measurable and deterministic. Then there is a coupling
$\mathbb Q$ of $(Z_j)_{j\in J}$ with a Poisson point process $\psi$ of intensity $\rho$
such that for every measurable $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d$
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item $\mathbb Q\big(\{Z_j\}_{j\in J}\cap A\subseteq\psi\big)\ \ge\
  \mathbb Q\big(H_J(y)\le\rho(y)\ \text{ for all }y\in A\big)$;
\item $\mathbb Q\big(\psi\cap A\subseteq\{Z_j\}_{j\in J}\big)\ \ge\
  \mathbb Q\big(H_J(y)\ge\rho(y)\ \text{ for all }y\in A\big)$.
\end{enumerate}

body:
Let Lambda be a compact hyperbolic set for a diffeomorphism f of a manifold. Then for every eps > 0 there is delta > 0 such that every delta-pseudo-orbit in a neighbourhood of Lambda - a sequence (x_n) with d(f(x_n), x_{n+1}) < delta for all n - is eps-SHADOWED by a genuine orbit: there is a point y with d(f^n(y), x_n) < eps for every n. If Lambda is in addition LOCALLY MAXIMAL (isolated) the shadowing point may be taken in Lambda, and if the pseudo-orbit is periodic the shadowing orbit may be taken periodic. Expansiveness of the hyperbolic set makes the shadowing point unique.
Hyperbolicity of the compact invariant set, and delta chosen AFTER eps.
Placing the shadowing orbit inside Lambda requires local maximality - without it the shadowing orbit exists but may leave the set.
Uniqueness uses expansiveness.

Let p and q be probability mass functions on a finite set S with d_TV(p, q) > 0, A = {p > q} and B = {q > p}. For a maximal coupling pi let G_pi be the bipartite graph on A and B with an edge x - y when pi(x, y) > 0. Then pi is an extreme point of the set of maximal couplings if and only if G_pi is a forest. Hence every extreme maximal coupling has at most |A| + |B| - 1 <= |S| - 1 positive off-diagonal entries. The greedy construction, which repeatedly sends the smaller of the remaining row and column masses between the first unfinished points of A and B, produces such a coupling, and if p and q are rational so is every mass it produces.

Fix L>=1,d>=1,k>=1 and nonzero x in R^d, independently of n. Consider the zero-bias fully connected Gaussian MLP with L hidden layers of width n, output width k, weight variance reciprocal to input width in every layer, and squared activation sigma(t)=t^2. Set K_1=||x||^2/d and K_(ell+1)=3K_ell^2. Given all L hidden layers, each final preactivation output has conditional variance Sigma=(1/n) sum_j (z_j^(L)(x))^4. For a finite constant C depending on the fixed model but not n, Var(Sigma)<=C/n and |E Sigma-K|<=C/n. Here K=K_(L+1)>0. Conditional on the hidden layers the k output coordinates are iid N(0,Sigma). This is a restricted specialization of Favaro, Hanin, Marinucci, Nourdin and Peccati, not a new theorem; constants have no asserted uniform dependence on L.
L,d,k,x are fixed as n grows; L>=1; x!=0
Independent Gaussian weights, variance reciprocal input width; zero biases
Squared activation; final preactivation output
No uniform or polynomial-in-L bound is claimed

[Definition def:joint_invariant of arXiv:2605.22787, 'Invariant measures for half-space geometric LPP: classification and the one force--one sol'] For $m \in \mathbb{N}$, we say a measure $\nu$ on the space $(\mathbb{R}^\mathbb{N})^m$ is an $m$-jointly invariant measure if, when $(f_1,\ldots,f_m) \sim \nu$, for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$, we have
   \[
   \Bigl(G_{f_1}(n + k,n) - G_{f_1}(n,n),\ldots, G_{f_m}(n+k,n) - G_{f_m}(n,n)\Bigr)_{ k \in \mathbb{N}} \sim \nu.
   \]

$$

$$
\lim_{n\rightarrow+\infty}\mathbb{E}\left(\int_0^1|H(t)-H_n(t)|^2\mathscr{A}'(t)dt\right)=0.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 12 of arXiv:2609.02779, '2609.02779'] For the Hamiltonian \eqref{eq:twowell-H}, the critical value is $0$, and
\[
 \widetilde{\A}(H_a)
 =\left\{(0,-a),\left(\frac12,-a\right)\right\}.
\]
The two points are distinct static classes and are hyperbolic equilibria.
Moreover, with
\begin{equation}
\Delta:=\frac a2-A=\frac{B-A}{4}>0,
\end{equation}
the selected critical solution satisfies
\begin{equation}
u_0(0)=0,\qquad
u_0\left(\frac12\right)=-\Delta,
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
u_0(x)=\int_0^x\bigl(Q(s)-a\bigr)\,\dd s,
\qquad
u_0'(x)+a=Q(x),
\qquad 0\le x\le\frac12.
\end{equation}

$\langle f,g\rangle_{\mathcal{A}}=\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} f(x)\,g(x)^\top\,dx$.
A family $\{U_k\}_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}\subset\mathbb H$ is called
\emph{$\mathcal A$-orthonormal (of unit vectors)} if
\[\langle U_k,U_u\rangle_{\mathcal A}=\delta_{k,u}\,I_m,
\qquad k,u\in\mathbb Z^d.
\]
If $U\in\mathbb H$ and $\{U(\cdot-k)\}_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}$ is $\mathcal A$-orthonormal,
we call $U$ an \emph{$\mathcal A$-orthonormal vector-valued function}.
title: $\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})$-orthonormal system of translates

body:
For each N let theta_N be a unit vector in R^N, Y_t iid with law P_N, and L_N(x;Y) a loss on the unit sphere S^(N-1). Let its population loss be Phi_N(x)=E L_N(x;Y)=phi(m_N(x)), where m_N(x)=x.theta_N and the same function phi:[-1,1]->R is used for every N. The spherical stochastic gradients exist almost surely; assume explicitly that E grad_S L_N(x;Y)=grad_S Phi_N(x). Let H_N(x;Y)=L_N(x;Y)-Phi_N(x). For constants C_1,iota>0 independent of N, assume sup_x E[(grad_S H_N(x;Y).theta_N)^2]<=C_1 and sup_x E||grad_S H_N(x;Y)||^(4+iota)<=C_1 N^((4+iota)/2). For a fixed integer k>=1, suppose phi is C^(k+1) on [-1,1], phi_prime(m)<0 for 0<m<1, phi^(ell)(0)=0 for 1<=ell<k, phi^(k)(0)<0, and sup_[-1,1]|phi^(k+1)|<infinity. Starting independently of the samples, use online spherical SGD X_tilde_t=X_(t-1)-(delta_N/N) grad_S L_N(X_(t-1);Y_t), X_t=X_tilde_t/||X_tilde_t||. Here alpha_N>0 and delta_N>0, and there are M_N=alpha_N*N fresh-sample updates (M_N integer). The initial law mu_N is uniform on the hemisphere {x in S^(N-1):x.theta_N>=0}. Assume alpha_N grows at most polynomially in N. If alpha_N->infinity for k=1, alpha_N/(log N)^2->infinity for k=2, or alpha_N/[N^(k-2)*(log N)^2]->infinity for k>=3, then there exists a positive step-size sequence delta_N for which m_N(X_(M_N))->1 in probability and in L^p for every finite p>=1. The sequence can be chosen so alpha_N^(-1)<<delta_N<<alpha_N^(-1/2), with alpha_N*delta_N dominating the search scale: 1 for k=1, log N for k=2, and N^((k-2)/2)*log N for k>=3. Here u_N<<v_N means u_N/v_N->0. This card states recovery for a suitably chosen step sequence; its conclusion is not a guarantee for every sequence in the displayed broad window. The number of samples equals the number of online updates, not the number of passes over one reused empirical sample.

Then we have that $\ensuremath{\mathbb{P}}_I( \cdot \;|\; \ensuremath{\mathcal{C}})  \preceq (N_x)_{x\in I}+\sum_{i=1}^\kappa \sum_{j=1}^n \delta_{Y_i^{{(j)}}}$, where 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\kappa$  is a random number in $\{1,\dots, K\}$
\item $n=n(\lambda)$ is as in Lemma (lem:basicPoisson of the paper)
\item The $Y_i^{{(j)}}$'s are random points in $I$.
\item For each $i \in 1,\dots, \kappa$, the $Y_i^{{(j)}}$'s, $j=1\dots,n$, are identical.
\item For $i=1,\dots, \kappa$,  $Y_1^{{(1)}}< \dots < Y_\kappa^{{(1)}}$.
\item Both $\kappa$ and the $(Y_i^{{(j)}})'s$ are  independent of $(N_x)_{x\in I}$.
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Theorem convergence in Ehat of arXiv:2411.04631, 'Existence of Martingale Solutions to Stochastic Constrained Heat Equation'] For $s,t \in [0,T]$ with $s \leq t$ and $\phi \in \mathcal{H}$, the following are true:
\begin{align*}
&1. \;\lim_{n \rightarrow \infty } \left \langle v_{n}(t), Q_{n}(\phi) \right \rangle_{\mathcal{H}}=\left \langle v(t) , \phi \right \rangle_{\mathcal{H}},\; \hat{\mathbb{P}}-a.s. \,. \\
&2.\; \lim_{n \rightarrow \infty } \int_{s}^{t} \left  \langle A v_{n}(h), Q_{n}(\phi)  \right \rangle_{\mathcal{H}} dh=\int_{s}^{t} \left  \langle A v(h),\phi  \right \rangle_{\mathcal{H}},\; \hat{\mathbb{P}}-a.s.\, .\\
&3.\; \lim_{n \rightarrow \infty } \int_{s}^{t} \left \langle  F(v_{n}(h)) , Q_{n}(\phi) \right \rangle_{\mathcal{H}} dh = \int_{s}^{t} \left \langle F(v(h)), Q(\phi) \right \rangle_{\mathcal{H}} dh, \; \; \hat{\mathbb{P}}-a.s.\; \text{ for }\phi \in \mathcal{H}.  \\
&4.\; \lim_{n \rightarrow \infty } \int_{s}^{t} \left \langle  k_{j}(v_{n}(h)) , Q_{n}(\phi) \right \rangle_{\mathcal{H}} dh = \int_{s}^{t} \left \langle k_{j}(v(h)), Q(\phi) \right \rangle_{\mathcal{H}} dh,\; \; \hat{\mathbb{P}}-a.s.\, . \\
&5.\; \lim_{n \rightarrow \infty } \int_{s}^{t} \left \langle  \Lambda_{j}(v_{n}(h)) , Q_{n}(\phi) \right \rangle_{\mathcal{H}} dW_{j}(h) = \int_{s}^{t} \left \langle \Lambda_{j}(v(h)), \phi \right \rangle_{\mathcal{H}} dW_{j}(h) ,\; \; \hat{\mathbb{P}}-a.s.\, .
\end{align*}

body:
[Cor jointedge of arXiv:2412.00610, 'Joint Poisson Convergence of Monochromatic Hyperedges in Multiplex Hypergraphs'] Fix $d\geq 1$ and a finite collection of non-isomorphic graphs $F_1, F_2, \ldots, F_d$. Suppose $G_n = ( V(G_n), E(G_n))$ is a sequence of graphs with edges colored uniformly at random with $c_n$ colors such that the following holds: For all $1 \leq i \leq d$, there exists a constant $\lambda_i \geq  0$ such that 
    $$\lim_{n \to \infty}\bE R(F_i, G_n) = \lim_{n \to \infty}\Var R(F_i, G_n) = \lambda_i. $$ 
      Then, as $n \rightarrow \infty$, 
    $$\left(\begin{array}{c}
        R(F_1, G_n) \\
       	\vdots \\ 
	R(F_d, G_n) 
        \end{array}\right) \dto \left(\begin{array}{c}
            Z_1 \\ 
            \vdots \\ 
            Z_d
            \end{array}\right) , $$
      where $Z_1 \sim \Pois(\lambda_1), \ldots, Z_d \sim \Pois(\lambda_d)$ are independent. \hfill $\Box$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Cor jointedge of arXiv:2412.00610

[Lemma lem:splitting_hokmotopy_groups of arXiv:2609.00233, 'A survey on mapping class groups of 3-manifolds'] We have the following homotopy equivalence
$$\Diff^+({S^n}) \simeq \SO(n+1) \times \Diff^+_{ \partial S^{n-1}}(D^n),$$
which implies that
    \begin{equation}
    \pi_i\Diff^+({S^n}) \cong \pi_i\Diff_{S^{n-1}}^+{(D^{n})} \times \pi_i\SO(n+1)
\end{equation}
for $i \ge 0$.

body:
[Lemma 29 of arXiv:2604.24684, 'Waning Immunity Fails to Restore a Positive Epidemic Threshold on Power--Law Networks'] Let $G=G(n,\tau)$ be the power-law random graph with exponent $\tau>2$, and let
$
\mathrm{diam}(G):=\max_{u,v\in V} d_G(u,v)
$
denote the graph diameter, where $d_G(u,v)$ is the graph distance between $u$ and $v$. Then there exists constants $C>0$ such that
\[
\mathbb P\big(\mathrm{diam}(G)\le C\log n\big)\to 1\qquad\text{as}\quad n\to\infty.
\]

[Lemma lem:ehr-factor of arXiv:2608.01253, 'The pseudo-quantum representation of \\finite reversible Markov chains'] Let $X_t^{(j)}\in\{a,b\}$ be the urn of ball $j$. The processes
$X_t^{(1)},\dots,X_t^{(n)}$ are independent two-state chains, each jumping $a\to b$
and $b\to a$ at rate $1$, and $k_t=\#\{j:X_t^{(j)}=a\}$.
Starting with all $n$ balls in $a$,

\begin{equation}
\pi_t(k)=\binom nk\,p(t)^{k}\bigl(1-p(t)\bigr)^{n-k},\qquad
p(t)=\frac{1+e^{-2t}}2,

\end{equation}

where $p(t)$ is the probability that one ball started in $a$ is in $a$ at time $t$.
This is the function already obtained in (ex:two-state of the paper).

[Lemma lem:Salpha_basic of arXiv:2604.10602, 'Fractional Navier-Stokes Equations with Caputo Derivative Driven by Hermite Noise'] For $0\le\nu<2$ and $0<\alpha<1$, there exists a constant $C>0$ such that for any $t>0$ and any $\chi\in\dot{H}^0$,
\[
\|\mathcal{S}_\alpha(t)\chi\|_\nu \le C t^{\frac{(2-\nu)\alpha-2}{2}} \|\chi\|.
\]
Moreover, for $0<t_1<t_2\le T$,
\[
\|\mathcal{S}_\alpha(t_2) - \mathcal{S}_\alpha(t_1)\|_{\mathcal{L}(\dot{H}^0,\dot{H}^\nu)} \le C (t_2-t_1)^{\frac{2-(2-\nu)\alpha}{2}}.
\]

[Proposition prop:gamma-quantile-estimates of arXiv:2604.25108, 'Terminal Defects, Growing Multiplicity, and Variance Extremality\\in the Double Dixie Cup '] Let $m_n\ge1$, let $b_n$ be the unique solution of
\[
        Q_{m_n}(b_n)=1/n,
\]
and put
\[
        a_n={\frac{Q_{m_n}(b_n)}{f_{m_n}(b_n)}}={\frac1{h_{m_n}(b_n)}}.
\]
Then, uniformly for $x$ in compact subsets of $\mathbb R$,
\[
        {\frac{Q_{m_n}(b_n+a_nx)}{Q_{m_n}(b_n)}}\to e^{-x}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
        {\frac{Q_{m_n}(b_n+a_nx)}{Q_{m_n}(b_n)}}\le e^{-x}
        \qquad (x\ge0),
\]
there are constants $c>0$ and $R_n\to\infty$ such that
\[
        nQ_{m_n}(b_n-a_nx)\ge c e^{cx},
        \qquad 0\le x\le R_n,
\]
the window may be chosen so slowly that
\[
        R_n\le {\frac{b_n}{2a_n}},
        \qquad
        \left(1+{\frac{b_n}{a_n}}\right)^r\exp\{-c e^{cR_n}\}\to0
\]
for every fixed $r>0$, and
\[
        {\frac{n a_n^2}{b_n}}\to\infty.
\]

body:
Let a multi-output predictor f_t(x) in R^D be a family indexed by t (for instance a blend f_t = (1 - t) f_0 + t f_1 of two fitted bases), scored by a case-weighted squared error L(t) = mean_i w_i ||y_i - f_t(x_i)||^2 with weights w_i that depend on the row only. Then L(t) = sum_d L_d(t) with L_d(t) = mean_i w_i (y_id - f_td(x_i))^2, and likewise the case-weighted bootstrap variance of the predictor at a set of rows, V(t) = mean_i w_i sum_d Var_b f_td^(b)(x_i), equals sum_d V_d(t). Hence the transductive covariance penalty R(t) = CV_cal(t) + [V_ev(t) - V_cal(t)] is a sum of per-output criteria R_d(t), and if the family is allowed a separate index t_d per output, the joint minimiser is the vector of per-output minimisers: min over (t_1..t_D) of sum_d R_d(t_d) = sum_d min_t R_d(t) <= min_t R(t). The per-output choice therefore never increases the criterion. It does not follow that it lowers the risk: each R_d is an estimate whose noise is not reduced by the averaging that makes R usable, and D separate argmins select on that noise. Measured on the EMIT and OCO-2 stacking pools (D = 285 and 40 outputs, 70 cells, two calibration/evaluation splits): the per-output blend gives up 0.41 and 0.53 percent of the score against the per-cell blend on EMIT (winning 14 and 12 of 40 cells) and 0.02 and 0.08 on OCO-2, with the identity sum_d R_d = R verified to 4e-16 in the driver's selftest. The information of the criterion is in the sum, not in its summands.
case weights depend on the row only (the per-sample relative L2 has w_i = 1/||y_i||^2; unit weights give the RMSE case); the predictor's outputs are scored by a sum of per-output squared errors
the bootstrap variance is the coordinate-wise variance over resamples, summed over outputs; the empirical sentence refers to the 2026-09-05 measurement (RMT_ENSEMBLE_THEORY.md 6aj, P34)

[Lemma lem:forest_estimates of arXiv:2607.22291, 'Rare subtree patterns in size-conditioned Bienaymé trees: Poisson approximation and declum'] Let $\mathcal G_\ell$ be a forest of $\ell$ independent Bienaym\'e trees.
There exists a constant $C>0$ such that, uniformly in integers
$\ell\ge1$ and $1\le m\le n/2$,
$$
\P(|\mathcal G_\ell|>m)\le C\frac{\ell}{a_m}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\frac{1}{\Psi_n(-1)}
\mathbb{E}\left[
\sup_{x\in\mathbb Z}\Psi_{n-|\mathcal G_\ell|}(x)
\mathbbm{1}_{\{|\mathcal G_\ell|>m\}}
\right]
\le C\frac{\ell}{a_m}.
$$

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Given a variable $f:X\to\mathbb R$ which follows the exponential law of parameter $\lambda>0$, its central moments are given by the following formula,
$$M_k'=\frac{k!}{\lambda^k}\sum_{s=0}^k\frac{(-1)^s}{s!}$$
with the small order central moments being as follows,
$$M_1'=0\quad,\quad 
M_2'=\frac{1}{\lambda^2}\quad,\quad
M_3'=\frac{2}{\lambda^3}\quad,\quad
M_4'=\frac{9}{\lambda^4}\quad,\quad\ldots$$
and with all this being more complicated than for the usual moments.

[Theorem thm:inverse_convergence of arXiv:2605.03896, 'Dimer models on astroidal zig-zag graphs'] {Assume that the angle function is periodic.} Let~$(x,y)\in \mathcal D_c^\circ$ lie in a phase region and let~$\zeta_*$ be as in Definition~(def:zero of the paper). If \((x,y)\in \mathcal F_{(\alpha,\beta)}\), assume also that
\[
(x,y)\notin \bm l_{e(\alpha)}\cup \bm l_{e(\beta)}.
\] 
For a black vertex $\mathsf b$ and a white vertex $\mathsf w$ of $\mathsf C$, let
\[
\mathsf b_n:=\mathsf b+(j_n,k_n),
\qquad
\mathsf w_n:=\mathsf w+(j_n,k_n)
\]
denote their translates in $\mathsf C_n$. Then
\[
\mathsf K^{-1}_{\mathsf b_n,\mathsf w_n}\rightarrow \mathsf A^{\zeta_*}_{\mathsf b,\mathsf w}
\qquad\text{as }n\to\infty,
\]
uniformly over $\mathsf b$ and $\mathsf w$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem 10 of arXiv:2606.04636, 'A Thomson-type variational principle for diffusion coefficients'] The divergence and gradient are adjoint up to
a sign: $\div=-\grad^{*}$. That is, for local $f:\Omega\to\C$ and
a local admissible flow $\phi$,
\begin{equation}
\left\langle \phi,\grad f\right\rangle =-\left\langle \div\phi,f\right\rangle .
\end{equation}
In particular, $\cL=\div\grad$ is negative self-adjoint.

[Definition def-thin-wedge of arXiv:2411.19810, 'Radial conformal welding in Liouville quantum gravity'] For $W\in(0, \frac{\gamma^2}{2})$, the probability measure $\mathcal{M}^{\textup{wed}}(W)$ is defined as follows. Sample a Poisson point process $\{(u, \mathcal{D}_u)\}$ from the intensity measure $\mathds{1}_{t>0}dt\times \mathcal{M}_{0,2}^{\textup{disk}}(\gamma^2-W)$ and concatenate the quantum disks $\{\mathcal{D}_u\}$ according to the ordering induced by $u$. The resulting beaded quantum surface is a \emph{weight $W$ quantum wedge}, and we denote its law by $\mathcal{M}^\mathrm{wed}(W)$. For $x>0$, the \emph{quantum cut point measure} assigns  mass
	$x$ to the collection of cut points between the quantum disks $\{\mathcal{D}_u:u\leq x\}$.
title: Definition def-thin-wedge of arXiv:2411.19810

body: Erdos Problem 548, the Erdos-Sos conjecture (1963): every graph on n vertices with more than (k-1)n/2 edges contains, as a subgraph (not necessarily induced), every tree on k+1 vertices. It was proved in August 2026 by a permutation-word counting argument with induction on the target tree (GPT-6 Astra with Tom Adamczewski; verified by Thomas Bloom and accepted as proved by erdosproblems.com, with a complete formal proof in Lean, repository github.com/tadamcz/erdos548). Whether a given formal statement captures the informal conjecture remains a human judgment.

Let $\Sigma$ be a positive definite $M \times M$ covariance matrix. The minimum-variance weights subject to $\mathbf{1}^T w = 1$ are $w^* = \Sigma^{-1}\mathbf{1} / (\mathbf{1}^T \Sigma^{-1}\mathbf{1})$ with risk $R^* = w^{*T}\Sigma w^* = 1/(\mathbf{1}^T \Sigma^{-1}\mathbf{1})$. Let $S$ be the sample covariance of $n > M + 1$ i.i.d. Gaussian observations with covariance $\Sigma$ and let $\hat w = S^{-1}\mathbf{1}/(\mathbf{1}^T S^{-1}\mathbf{1})$ be the plug-in weights. THEOREM (Pafka and Kondor, 2003; the finite-$n$ moments are those of the inverse Wishart law). In the limit $M, n \to \infty$ with $q = M/n \in (0, 1)$: (i) the true (out-of-sample) risk of the plug-in portfolio satisfies $\hat w^T \Sigma \hat w / R^* \to \frac{1}{1 - q}$; (ii) the in-sample risk $\hat w^T S \hat w / R^* \to 1 - q$; so the realized risk exceeds the optimum by the factor $1/(1-q)$ while the naive in-sample estimate understates the optimum by the factor $1 - q$, the two differing by $1/(1-q)^2$. For $q = 0.025$ the inflation is $2.6$ percent; for $q = 0.5$ it is $100$ percent; as $q \to 1$ the plug-in portfolio's risk diverges.
Sigma positive definite; n > M + 3 for the finite-sample moments
i.i.d. Gaussian observations
M/n -> q in (0, 1)

The inverse-Wishart moments give $E[W^{-1}] = I/(n - M - 1)$, so $E[a^T W^{-1} a] = \\|a\\|^2/(n - M - 1)$ and, with $R^* = 1/\\|a\\|^2$, the ratio of in-sample risk to $R^*$ concentrates at $(n - M - 1)/n \\to 1 - q$ (concentration of the quadratic form $a^T W^{-1} a$ around its mean follows from the variance formula for inverse-Wishart quadratic forms, which is $O(1/n)$ relative). A Hermitian matrix A in C^{n x n} is positive definite if and only if it can be written as A = L L^* with L lower triangular having strictly positive real diagonal entries; when it exists this factorisation is unique. For real symmetric positive definite A the factor L is real, A = L L^T. Equivalently A = R^* R with R = L^* upper triangular. The factor is computed by the Cholesky algorithm in n^3 / 3 flops (half the cost of LU, no pivoting needed): for j = 1..n, l_jj = sqrt(a_jj - sum_{k<j} |l_jk|^2) and l_ij = (a_ij - sum_{k<j} l_ik conj(l_jk)) / l_jj for i > j; the algorithm is backward stable (Wilkinson), and it fails - a nonpositive quantity under the square root - exactly when A is not positive definite, which makes it the standard numerical test of positive definiteness. For positive semidefinite A a factorisation A = L L^* with nonnegative diagonal still exists but is no longer unique. Uses: solving A x = b by two triangular solves, sampling Gaussian vectors with covariance A (x = mu + L z), least squares via the normal equations, and the Kalman filter.
A Hermitian (symmetric in the real case)
positive definite for existence with a strictly positive diagonal and for uniqueness

and

are positive semidefinite.

[Corollary 26 (Coefficient approximation) of arXiv:2608.17540, 'Pathwise stability for one-dimensional SDEs driven by Brownian motion and a symmetric stab'] Let $X$ solve the baseline equation \eqref{eq:X}. For each $n\ge1$, let $X^{(n)}$ be a c\`adl\`ag adapted solution, driven by the same pair $(W,Z)$, such that the pair $(X,X^{(n)})$ satisfies Assumption~\ref{ass:solutions}. Suppose that $X^{(n)}$ solves
\[
X_t^{(n)}=x_0^{(n)}+\int_0^t b_n(X_s^{(n)})\dd s
+\int_0^t a_n(X_s^{(n)})\dd W_s
+\int_0^t \sigma_n(X_{s-}^{(n)})\dd Z_s.
\]
Assume that there exist common constants $L_b,L_a,L_\sigma$ and exponents $\eta_n\in[\wt\eta,1]$, with $\wt\eta\in[1/\alpha,1]$, such that for all $n$ and all $x,y\in\R$,
\[
|b_n(x)-b_n(y)|\le L_b|x-y|,
\qquad
|a_n(x)-a_n(y)|\le L_a|x-y|,
\]
and
\[
|\sigma_n(x)-\sigma_n(y)|\le L_\sigma\bigl(|x-y|^{\eta_n}\vee |x-y|\bigr).
\]
Then the family satisfies Assumption~\ref{ass:perturbed} uniformly with exponent $\wt\eta$. Define
\begin{align*}
B_n&:=\int_0^T\E |b(s,X_s)-b_n(X_s)|\dd s,\\
A_n&:=\left(\int_0^T\E |a(s,X_s)-a_n(X_s)|^2\dd s\right)^{1/2},\\
S_n&:=\left(\int_0^T\E |\sigma(s,X_s)-\sigma_n(X_s)|^\alpha\dd s\right)^{1/\alpha}.
\end{align*}
Suppose that $B_n,A_n,S_n\to0$ and $x_0^{(n)}\to x_0$. Then
\[
\sup_{0\le t\le T}\E|X_t-X_t^{(n)}|^{\alpha-1}\to0.
\]
Moreover, once $B_n,A_n,S_n<1$, the rate is obtained from Theorem~\ref{thm:noncritical} if $\wt\eta>1/\alpha$ and from Theorem~\ref{thm:critical} if $\wt\eta=1/\alpha$.

[Proposition thm|Straightforward of arXiv:2504.08938, 'Fourier Levels and Almost Sure Bounds on Higher-Order Derivatives in First-Passage Percola'] For every $i\neq j$, every $\alpha,\beta\in\{a,b\}$, and every random variable $\varphi$, 
\begin{eqnarray} 
\sigma_i^{\alpha}\circ \sigma_i^{\beta}&=&\sigma_i^{\alpha};   \\
\sigma_i^{\alpha}\circ \sigma_j^{\beta}&=&\sigma_j^{\beta}\circ\sigma_i^{\alpha};   \\
(\partial_i \varphi)\circ \sigma_i^{\alpha} &=& \partial_i \varphi;   \\
\partial_i\partial_i \varphi&=&0;   \\
\partial_i\partial_j \varphi&=&\partial_j\partial_i\varphi;   \\
\varphi\cdot 1_{\omega_i=\alpha}&=&\varphi\circ \sigma_i^{\alpha}\cdot 1_{\omega_i=\alpha}.  
\end{eqnarray} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition thm|Straightforward of arXiv:2504.08938

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2604.25877, 'Asymptotic height of Plancherel random trees'] Let $p(t \to t')$ denote the probability of obtaining $t'$ from $t$ by the above random
leaf-removal procedure, and let
\[
g(t) = \frac{|t|!}{\prod_{v \in V_t} |t_v|}
\]
denote the right-hand side of the hook-length formula.
Then
\[
p(t \to t') = \frac{m_t(t')g(t')}{g(t)}.
\]
title: Lemma 4 of arXiv:2604.25877

$$
{\mathrm{Ent}}_{\Phi_q}(F) \leq {\mathbb E}\Big[\int_\mathcal{X}\big(D_xF^{2\over q}-{2\over q}F^{{2\over q}-1}\,(D_xF)\big)\,\mu(d x)\Big].
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:PhiRSovolev of arXiv:2507.08692

body: For the real eigenvalues of the real Ginibre ensemble, a question left open in the extreme-gaps programme (Lopatto and Meeker 2024, Section 1.3): the smallest gap satisfies P(N^{1/4} g_min > x) -> exp(-kappa x^2) with kappa = 1/(2 sqrt(2 pi)), the slope of the two-point function at 0 (in mean-spacing units a Rayleigh law exp(-pi y^2/2)), and the k-th smallest gaps and the process of squared gaps converge to Poisson limits. The largest gap G_N satisfies theta G_N - (1/2) log N - log(2 theta) - c_b => Gumbel, with theta = zeta(3/2)/(2 sqrt(2 pi)) = 0.5210934894 and c_b = log 2 - 1/4 + (1/(4 pi)) sum_{n>=2} (1/n)(-pi + sum_{m=1}^{n-1} 1/sqrt(m(n-m))) = 0.0625786, the bulk gap constant conjectured by Forrester and proved by FitzGerald, Tribe and Zaboronski; so G_N ~ log N/(2 theta). The proof works from the exact Pfaffian kernel by a cell-mesh Poissonization and a quasi-factorization of Fredholm Pfaffians over separated interval unions, without resolvent bounds or negative association.

[Theorem 172 of arXiv:2605.03236, 'Stochastic It\^o Equations and Parabolic Second-Order Equations with singular Drift'] Let   $\sigma(n)$, $n=1,2,...$, be $d\times d_{1}$-matrix valued functions
on $\bR^{d+1}$ such that for any ball $B\in\bB$ 
and almost every $t$
$$
 \int_{B}|\sigma(n,t,x)-\sigma(t,x)|\,dx\to0
$$ 
 as $n\to \infty$. Suppose that  
 $a(n):=\sigma(n)\sigma^{*}(n),b(n)$ satisfy the assumptions
stated   in the introduction to the
chapter and at the beginning of Section \ref{section 4.16,1}
(with the same constants)
and $b(n)\to b$ in $L_{p}(C)$ for any  
$C\in \bC$.
 Finally, assume that we are given nonrandom $x_{0}(n)\to x_{0}$
  and on a probability space equation
 \eqref{3.15,1} has an $E_{q,p,\beta}$-admissible 
strong solution $x_{t}$ 
and  equation \eqref{3.15,1} with $\sigma(n),b(n), x_{0}(n)$ 
in place
of $\sigma,b,x_{0}$ has also an $E_{q,p,\beta}$-admissible 
strong solution $x_{t}(n)$ for each $n$ 
(on the same probability space with the same Wiener process). Then for any $T
\in(0,\infty)$, $m\geq 1$,
$$
E\sup_{t\leq T}|x_{t}-x_{t}(n)|^{m}
\to 0
$$
as $n\to \infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 13 (Shift identity for symmetric perturbations) of arXiv:2511.12623, 'The eigenvector bead process'] Let \(H,\mathcal{D}\in\mathcal S_N(\mathbb R)\), with normalized eigenpairs
\(\{(\lambda^H_j,\mathbf{u}^H_j)\}\) of \(H\) and \(\{(\lambda^{H+\mathcal{D}}_i,\mathbf{u}^{H+\mathcal{D}}_i)\}\) of \(H+\mathcal{D}\).
Whenever the denominator is nonzero,
\begin{equation}
\lambda^{H+\mathcal{D}}_i-\lambda^H_j
=\frac{(\mathbf{u}^{H+\mathcal{D}}_i)^\top \mathcal{D}\,\mathbf{u}^H_j}{(\mathbf{u}^{H+\mathcal{D}}_i)^\top \mathbf{u}^H_j}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Shift identity for symmetric perturbations

Let n = 3, u0 ∈ C³(R³), u1 ∈ C²(R³). Define, for t > 0 and x ∈ R³, u(t,x) = ⨍_{∂B(x,t)} [ t u1(y) + u0(y) + ∇u0(y)·(y − x) ] dS(y), where ⨍ denotes the average over the sphere ∂B(x,t) (surface measure divided by 4πt²). Equivalently u(t,x) = ∂_t ( t ⨍_{∂B(x,t)} u0 dS ) + t ⨍_{∂B(x,t)} u1 dS. Then u ∈ C²((0,∞)×R³) extends to a C² solution of ∂_t²u − Δu = 0 on [0,∞)×R³ with u(0,·) = u0 and ∂_t u(0,·) = u1, and by finite speed of propagation it is the unique C² solution. In particular u(t,x) depends only on u0, ∇u0 and u1 on the sphere ∂B(x,t).

body: [Definition defn:mdp of arXiv:2608.22765, 'Learning to Control Coupled-Dynamics Environments with Joint Markov Decision Processes'] A finite discounted MDP is a tuple $\mathcal M = (\mathcal S, \mathcal A, P, \gamma)$ where $\mathcal S$ and $\mathcal A$ are finite state and action spaces, $P:\mathcal S\times\mathcal A\to \mathcal P([0,1]\times \mathcal S)$ is the joint reward-transition kernel, and $\gamma \in (0, 1)$ is the discount factor. For $(R,S')\sim P(\cdot \mid s,a)$, we write the mean reward as $r(s,a) = \mathbb E[R \mid s,a]$ and write $P_S(\cdot \mid s,a)$ for the state marginal of $P$.

body: [Prop teo:refMeasure of arXiv:2412.04918, 'On one dimensional weighted Poincar\'e inequalities for Global Sensitivity Analysis'] Consider two probability measures $\mu, \Tilde{\mu} \in \mathcal{P}(a,b)$ with $(a,b)$ finite. Let $\Tilde{g}$ be the function saturating the classical Poincar\'e inequality for $\Tilde{\mu}$. Then the function $g$ defined by $g (x) = \Tilde{g} (x) - \int_{a}^{b} \Tilde{g}(y) \,\mu(dy)$ belongs to $\mathscr{C}^{1,2}_{*}(a,b)$ and satisfies (equation eq: boundary conditions of the paper). Moreover it generates a non-vanishing weight $w_g\in \mathcal{W}(a,b)$ leading to a weighted Poincar\'e inequality for $\mu$. [Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The probability for a random permutation $\sigma\in S_N$ to have exactly $k$ fixed points is given by the following formula:
$$P=\frac{1}{k!}\left(1-\frac{1}{1!}+\frac{1}{2!}-\ldots+(-1)^{N-1}\frac{1}{(N-1)!}+(-1)^N\frac{1}{N!}\right)$$
Thus we have the estimate $P\simeq1/(ek!)$, in the $N\to\infty$ limit.

body:
[Proposition prop_an of arXiv:2411.13972, 'The Stochastic Bessel operator at high temperatures'] ~\\
Set $T>0$, independent of $\beta$. There exist a deterministic function $\eta(\beta)\rightarrow 0$ and an event $\mathcal{E}_0$, $\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{E}_0)\rightarrow 1$, on which, for $\beta$ small enough:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
	\item $\tau_0 < \beta$, 
	\item $\underset{[\tau_0, \tau_c\wedge T]}\sup\big\lvert q^+(t)-r^+(t)\big\rvert <\delta$, 
	\item $\tau_c<T \Rightarrow \lvert\xi^+-\tau_c\rvert<\eta$ and $\lvert\xi_0^+(0)-\tau_c\rvert<\eta$.
\end{enumerate}

\noindent Properties (a), (b) and (c) also hold for the diffusions $q^-$ from (equation SDEq- of the paper) and $r^-$ from (equation eq_r- of the paper), with their corresponding hitting and explosion times. As a consequence, on the event $\mathcal{E}_0$, for $\beta$ small enough,
\begin{equation}
\xi^-<T \Rightarrow \big\lvert \xi^- -\xi_0^-(0)\big\rvert <2\eta.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Limit behavior of the diffusions $q^+$ and $q^-$

[OPEN PROBLEM - not a proved fact. Stated in arXiv:2601.16580, 'Coin flipping and waiting times paradoxes: Why fair coins are exceptional' (openquestion environment labelled oq:stability).] Fix an alphabet size $s$ and a length $k\ge 2$, and consider i.i.d.\ sources with probabilities $(p_1,\dots,p_s)$.
(Here the \emph{uniform} distribution means $p_i=1/s$ for all $i$.)
For patterns of length $k$, orient the complete directed graph by
$A\to B$ iff $\Pr(A\!>\!B)>\tfrac12$ under \emph{independent} sources and \emph{random tie-break}.
Does there exist $\varepsilon=\varepsilon(k,s)>0$ such that whenever $\max_i |p_i-1/s|<\varepsilon$,
this head-to-head tournament on $\mathcal{A}^k$ has \emph{no directed $3$-cycles} (equivalently, is transitive as a tournament)?
More generally, what is the largest neighbourhood of the uniform distribution on which the length-$k$ head-to-head relation is cycle-free? (Verbatim from the paper's TeX; symbols are the source paper's. Stated as open/conjectural; no resolution of it was found in the paper's own text by the rules of problem_index.py - a paper may still prove special cases of a conjecture it states.)
title: Open problem: Stability near fairness at fixed length

body: [Lem 12 of arXiv:2605.18751, '\mytitle'] Let $X$ be the compound sum defined in~\eqref{def.compound-rv}, and assume \(F\) is PF$_2$. Then the posterior kernel \((n,k)\mapsto\prob(N=n\mid X=k)\) is TP$_2$ on $\N_0\times\supp(X)$. In particular, the conditional laws of \(N\) given \(X=k\) are stochastically increasing in \(k\), and \(k\mapsto\E[N\mid X=k]\) is nondecreasing on \(\supp(X)\).

[Lemma 16 of arXiv:2609.01473, 'Keller sequences of exact $\infty$-categories'] Let $i\colon \cal{A} \hookrightarrow \cal{C}$ be an extension-closed exact functor among weakly idempotent complete exact $\infty$-categories.
\begin{enumerate}
\item
If $i$ is right-special then for every $n \geq 0$ and every map $c \to i(A)$ with $c \in \cal{C}$ and $A \in \st(\cal{A})_{[0,n]}$ factors as a composite $c \to i(a) \xrightarrow{i(g)} i(A)$ for some $g\colon a \to A$ with $a \in \cal{A}$ and $\cofib[a \to A] \in \st(\cal{A})_{[1,n]}$.
\item
If $i$ is left-special then for every $m \leq 0$ and every map $i(A) \to c$ with $c \in \cal{C}$ and $A \in \st(\cal{A})_{[m,0]}$ factors as a composite $i(A) \xrightarrow{i(g)} i(a)$ for some $g\colon A \to a$ with $a \in \cal{A}$ and $\fib[A \to a] \in \st(\cal{A})_{[m,-1]}$.
\end{enumerate}

Let $0<\epsilon<\frac{1}{2}$, let $r=n-\l_1$ and suppose that $r+k+1<(\frac12-\epsilon)n$. Then
\begin{multline}
s_\l(k)=\frac{(n-r-1)^{\underline{k}}}{n^{\underline{k}}}\prod_{i=2}^m\left(1-\frac{k}{n-(1+r+\lambda_i-i)}\right)\prod_{i=1}^m\left(1-\frac{k}{n-(r-\lambda_i'+i)}\right)^{-1}\\
+O_\epsilon\left(\exp\left(k\left[\log\frac{(1+\epsilon)(k+1+r)}{n-k}+O_\epsilon\left(r^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right)\right]\right)\right).
\end{multline}
Here, the superscript $\underline{k}$ is the falling factorial. Moreover, when $r<k$, the error term on the second line is actually zero. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 13 of arXiv:2512.01483, 'Scaling Limits of Line Models in Degenerate Environment'] A subordinator $(Z_t)_{t \geq 0}$ is a right-continous, non-decreasing process, with stationary, independent increments. For such a process there exists $\Phi: \mathbb{R}_+ \to \mathbb{R}_+$, called the Laplace exponent of $Z$, such that
\[\forall \lambda \geq 0, \quad \forall t \geq 0, \qquad \mathbb{E}[e^{-\lambda Z_t}] = e^{-t \Phi(\lambda)}. \]

[Defi 38 of arXiv:2608.28148, 'Flows and homotopies of Banach Lie algebroids'] For $i=0,1$  let $c_i\colon [0,1] \to A$ be of class $C^k$, $k\geq 1$. We say that $c_0$ is \emph{homotopic} to $c_1$, if there exists $C^{k}$ maps $a,b\colon [0,1]\times[0,1]\rightarrow A$ with
 \begin{enumerate}
 \item  $a(0,\cdot )=c_0$ and ${a}(1,\cdot )=c_1$ and ${a}$ is a variation of admissible curves 
 \item $\gamma:=\pi\circ {a}=\pi\circ {b}$ and $\rho\circ {b}(\varepsilon,t)=\dis\frac{\partial \g}{\partial \varepsilon}(\varepsilon, t)$.
 \item $\dis\frac{\p {a}_\varepsilon}{\p \varepsilon}=\mathcal{T}_{a_\varepsilon }(b_\varepsilon)$
 \item For every $\varepsilon \in [0,1]$, $b_\varepsilon(0)=0=b_\varepsilon(1)$
 \end{enumerate}
 The pair $({a},{b})$ is called a ($C^k$-)\emph{homotopy} between $c_0$ and $c_1$.

[Lemma lem:fourpoint-relation-ball of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] Let
\[
 A=\{0,a,b,D\},\qquad 0<a<b<D,\qquad \gcd(a,b,D)=1,
\]
and suppose that every nonzero homogeneous relation of $A$ has relation
degree at least $H$, where $H\in\mathbb R$ and $H\geq2$.  Then
\[
 D\geq \binom{H+1}{2}.
\]
If equality holds, then, for the gaps
\[
 g_1=a,\qquad g_2=b-a,\qquad g_3=D-b,
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
 g_1+g_3=H,\qquad
 \gcd(g_1,g_3)=1,\qquad
 g_2=\frac{H(H-1)}2.
\end{equation}

integers $m_N$ such that
\[
m_N\longrightarrow\infty,
\qquad
\frac{m_N}{N}\longrightarrow0,
\]
and
\begin{equation}
 \frac1{Q_N}\sum_{j=1}^{m_N}b_{N,j}

 \qquad
 \frac1{Q_N}\sum_{m_N<j\le \floor{NT}}b_{N,j}
 \xrightarrow[N\to\infty]{}0.
 
\end{equation}

[Lemma 56 of arXiv:2609.02878, '2609.02878'] Let \(U\subset Y^{\rm rv}\) be a Zariski-open product region.  Suppose
\[
 q_i\longrightarrow q_\infty\in U,
 \qquad x_i\in F_{q_i},
 \qquad t_i\nearrow T.
\]
Set \(\tau_i=T-t_i\) and assume that
\begin{equation}
             \tau_i|\Rm(g(t_i))|_{g(t_i)}(x_i)\longrightarrow\infty.
\end{equation}
Choose nested coordinate sets
\[
 q_\infty\in V_0\Subset V_a\Subset V_b\Subset V\Subset U
\]
and holomorphic coordinates \(w=(w^1,\ldots,w^m)\) on \(V\).  After
discarding finitely many terms, assume that \(q_i\in V_0\).

Then there are \(\sigma_j\searrow0\) and a subsequence
\(i(j)\nearrow\infty\) such that the pointed flows
\begin{equation}
 \widehat g_j(t)
 =\frac{1}{\sigma_j\tau_{i(j)}}
   g\bigl(t_{i(j)}+\sigma_j\tau_{i(j)}t\bigr),
 \qquad
 -\frac{t_{i(j)}}{\sigma_j\tau_{i(j)}}\le t\le0,
\end{equation}
have the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.4em]
\item Equipped with the point conjugate heat kernels based at
$(x_{i(j)},0)$, the flows converge in $\mathbb F$, and smoothly on the
full regular spacetime, to a connected noncollapsed K\"ahler shrinking
soliton \(\mathcal Z\).  Write \((Z,g_Z)=\mathcal Z_{-1}\) and
\[
 d\nu_{Z,-1}=(4\pi)^{-(m+1)}e^{-f_Z}\,dV_{g_Z}
\]
for its distinguished shrinker probability measure.  Its normalized
Nash entropy satisfies
\[
 \mathcal N(Z):=
 \int_{\Reg Z}f_Z\,d\nu_{Z,-1}-(m+1)<0.
\]

\item On the localized convergence charts, the maps
\begin{equation}
 \widehat H_j
 =\frac{(w-w(q_{i(j)}))\circ\pi}
        {\sqrt{\sigma_j\tau_{i(j)}}}
\end{equation}
converge smoothly on compact subsets of the regular spacetime to a map
$H_Z$.  Its time-$-1$ restriction extends uniquely to a globally
Lipschitz holomorphic map $H_Z:Z\to\C^m$ satisfying on $\Reg Z$
\begin{equation}
 \nabla^{g_Z}dH_Z=0,
 \qquad
 c|a|^2\le |d(a\cdot H_Z)|_{g_Z}^2\le C|a|^2
 \quad(a\in\C^m).
\end{equation}

\item The time-$-1$ space is smooth.  More precisely, there exists
\(L\in\mathrm{GL}(m,\C)\), with no target translation, such that
\begin{equation}
 Z\cong\C^m\times\PP^1,
 \qquad LH_Z=\operatorname{pr}_{\C^m},
\end{equation}
where $\PP^1$ carries the round metric normalized by
$\Rc(g_{S^2})=\frac12g_{S^2}$.

\item The convergence is realized on a regular exhaustion by embeddings
$\Psi_j$ for which
\begin{equation}
 \Psi_j^*\widehat g_j(-1)\longrightarrow g_Z,
 \qquad
 \widehat H_j\circ\Psi_j\longrightarrow H_Z
\end{equation}
smoothly on compact subsets of \(Z=\Reg Z\).  For every \(U'\Subset Z\)
and all sufficiently large \(j\),
\begin{equation}
 \Psi_j(U')\cap\widehat H_j^{-1}(0)
 =\Psi_j(U')\cap F_{q_{i(j)}}.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}

body: In mathematics, Jensen's inequality, named after the Danish mathematician Johan Jensen, relates the value of a convex function of an integral to the integral of the convex function. It was proved by Jensen in 1906, building on an earlier proof of the same inequality for doubly-differentiable functions by Otto Hölder in 1889. Given its generality, the inequality appears in many forms depending on the context, some of which are presented below. In its simplest form the inequality states that the convex transformation of a mean is less than or equal to the mean applied after convex transformation.
title: Jensen's inequality

[Lemma 4 (Cellular realization of the simplicial replacement) of arXiv:2609.01882, '\textbf{Coxeter Descents and Parabolic Homotopy Colimits}\\[2mm] \large A Hochster-type de'] Let $\mathcal C$ be a finite poset and let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathrm{Top}$ be a diagram of finite CW complexes and cellular maps. In the Bousfield--Kan simplicial-replacement model for $\hocolim_{\mathcal C}F$, the products
\[
  e^p\times\mathring\Delta^q,
  \qquad c_0<\cdots<c_q,
\]
where $e^p$ is an open $p$-cell of $F(c_0)$, form the open cells of a CW structure of dimension $p+q$. With the product orientation, the cellular chain complex is the usual total complex of the normalized simplicial replacement of $C_*^{\mathrm{cell}}(F)$; on a product of cellular degree $p$ and simplicial degree $q$, the simplex-face part of the differential carries the Koszul sign $(-1)^p$.

body:
[Lem 9 of arXiv:2506.20146, 'Parabolic Anderson Model in the Hyperbolic Space. Part I: Annealed Asymptotics'] Let $f\in C_{b}(\Sigma_{R})$ (space of bounded
continuous functions on $\Sigma_{R}$) be given fixed. Let $v(s,(\rho,\sigma))$
be the solution to the following initial-boundary value problem:
\begin{equation}
\begin{cases}
\partial_{s}v={\cal L}^{t}v+fv, & (s,(\rho,\sigma))\in(0,\infty)\times\Sigma_{R};\\
v(s,\cdot)=0 & \text{on }\{\rho=R\};\\
v(0,\cdot)\equiv1.
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
Then one has 
\[
\lim_{t\rightarrow\infty}\frac{1}{\beta(t)}\log v(\beta(t),(\rho,\sigma))=-\lambda_{0}^{{\rm eu}}
\]
uniformly for $(\rho,\sigma)\in[0,R-\varepsilon]\times\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$
for any given fixed $\varepsilon\in(0,R)$. Here $\lambda_{0}^{{\rm eu}}$
denotes the principal Dirichlet eigenvalue of $\Delta_{{\rm eu}}^{+}-f$
on $(\Sigma_{R},g^{\infty})$ with $\Delta_{{\rm eu}}^{+}$ being
the positive Euclidean Laplacian.

body:
[Prop existence_r>2 of arXiv:2506.01746, '\bf Optimal Bregman quantization: existence and uniqueness of optimal quantizers revisited'] Let $r\!\in (0, +\infty)$.

\smallskip
\noindent $(a)$ Case  $r\ge2$.  Assume that the distribution $P$ of $X$ satisfies the  moment assumption~(equation eq:Integrabilite of the paper), that $F$ is $C^2$ on $U$ with $\nabla^2F$ bounded on $U$ and that $\nabla^2F(x)$ is (symmetric) positive definite for  every $x\!\in U$.

Assume that at every $\bar x \!\in\partial\,U$, 

\smallskip
\noindent either
\begin{equation} 
 \nabla^2F \mbox{ can  be continuously extended at } \bar x \mbox{ and } \nabla^2F(\bar x) \mbox{ is (symmetric) positive definite}
\end{equation}
or 

\smallskip
 \quad the l.s.c. extensions $\phi_{_F}(\xi, \cdot)$  (on the closure $ \bar U^{\widehat{\mathbb{R}^d}}$ of $U$) satisfy 

\begin{equation}

 \forall\, \xi \!\in U, \qquad \phi_{_F}(\xi, \bar x) =\displaystyle  \sup_{x\in U}\phi_{_F}(\xi,x)
\end{equation}
and, when $U$ is unbounded, $\bar x = \infty$ satisfies this second condition~(equation eq:Cond-rb of the paper).

\smallskip
Then $G_{r,1}:  \bar U^{\widehat{\mathbb{R}^d}}\to \mathbb{R}_+$  attains a unique strict minimum  at  a point $x^{(r)}\!\in U$  \textcolor{black}{which is the unique solution of the stationarity equation
\[
x^{(r)}= \int_U \xi \,{\rm I\hspace{-1.50ex}Q} _{x^{(r)}}(\mathrm{d}\xi) \!\in U\quad \mbox{ where }\quad {\rm I\hspace{-1.50ex}Q} _{x} (\mathrm{d}\xi)= \frac{\phi_{_F}(\xi,x)^{\frac r2}\cdot P(\mathrm{d}\xi)}{\int_U\phi_{_F}(\xi,x)^{\frac r2}P(\mathrm{d}\xi)}, \quad x\!\in U.
\]
In particular, $x^{(r)}$ is the  unique  critical point of $G_{r,1}$.}

\noindent \textcolor{black}{$(b)$ Case  $r\!\in (0, 2)$. Assume   all the assumption in $(a)$ are in force and, furthermore, that 
\begin{equation}
\exists\, \delta>0,\quad \mathbb{E}\,\phi_{_F}(X,x)^{\frac r2-1-\delta}<+\infty.
\end{equation}

Then,  $G_{r,1} $ attains a minimum on $U$.} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:ergodic theorem for capacity of arXiv:2411.03512, 'Ergodicity and Mixing of Sublinear Expectation System and Applications'] Let $(\Omega,\mathcal{H},U_f,\hat{\mathbb E})$ be a regular sublinear expectation system, where $U_f$ is induced by a measurable transform $f:\Omega\to\Omega$. Let $C$ be the capacity induced by $\hat{\mathbb E}$ on $(\Omega,\sigma(\mathcal{H}))$. Then the following two statements are equivalent:
     \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
         \item $C$ is ergodic;
         \item there exists an ergodic probability $P\in\mathcal{P}$ such that for any $X\in L^1(\Omega,\mathcal{\sigma(\mathcal{H})},P)$, 
 \[C\bigg(\Big\{\omega\in\Omega:\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}X(f^i\omega)=\int XdP\Big\}^c\bigg)=0.\]
     \end{enumerate}
  When the equivalent statements (i) and (ii) hold, one has $\mathcal{P}\cap \mathcal{M}(T)=\mathcal{P}\cap \mathcal{M}^e(T)=\{P\}$.
title: Theorem thm:ergodic theorem for capacity of arXiv:2411.03512

body:
[Theorem 7 (Decision-aligned separation and pointwise validation) of arXiv:2606.07931, 'Pointwise Complexity for Gaussian Fields:\\Upper Envelopes, Algorithmic Lower Bounds, and '] There exist universal constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) with the following property.  Let \(M,N\ge2\) satisfy \(\log N\ge 1024\log M\).  Let
\[
 e_0,e_1,\ldots,e_M,f_1,\ldots,f_N
\]
be orthonormal vectors in \(\mathbb R^{M+N+1}\).  Fix \(R>0\), define
\[
\tau:=\frac{R}{\sqrt{\log M}},
\qquad
S:=\frac18\tau\sqrt{\log N}
      =\frac{R}{8}\sqrt{\frac{\log N}{\log M}},
\]
and set
\[
H_M:=\{Re_0,Re_1,\ldots,Re_M\},
\qquad
C_N:=\{Sf_1,\ldots,Sf_N\},
\qquad
T_{M,N}:=H_M\cup C_N .
\]
Let \(d(s,t)=\|s-t\|_2\), let \(\Delta=R/3\), and let the prior be
\[
\pi(Re_0)=\frac12,
\qquad
\pi(Re_i)=\frac1{2M},\quad i=1,\ldots,M,
\qquad
\pi(Sf_j)=0,
\quad j=1,\ldots,N .
\]
Consider the Gaussian location experiment
\[
Y=\Theta+\tau Z,
\qquad
\Theta\sim\pi,
\qquad
Z\sim N(0,I_{M+N+1}),
\]
and the unrestricted norm-regularized decoder
\begin{equation}
\widehat\Theta_\lambda(Y)
\in
\arg\min_{a\in T_{M,N}}\{\|Y-a\|^2+\lambda\|a\|^2\},
\qquad
\lambda=64 .
\end{equation}
Let \(Q_\tau=N(0,\tau^2I_{M+N+1})\).  Then, for all sufficiently large \(M,N\), the following hold.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.2em]
\item \emph{Fixed-prior Fano relaxation is vacuous.}  Since every \(\Delta\)-ball in \(T_{M,N}\) is a singleton,
\[
q_\pi(\Delta):=\sup_{a\in T_{M,N}}\pi(B_d(a,\Delta))=\frac12 .
\]
Moreover the usual data-processing lower envelope obtained by replacing the exact ghost mass by \(q_\pi(\Delta)\) gives zero at the reference law \(Q_\tau\).

\item \emph{Exact algorithmic ghost mass is small.}  The estimator-dependent ghost mass satisfies
\[
\rho_{\Delta,Q_\tau}(\widehat\Theta_\lambda)
=
\mathbb E_{Y\sim Q_\tau}\pi(B_d(\widehat\Theta_\lambda(Y),\Delta))
\le \frac{C}{M} .
\]
Consequently the exact ghost entropy is of order \(\log M\), whereas the worst-case Fano small-ball entropy for the same prior is only \(\log2\).

\item \emph{Sharp Bayes risk for the actual unrestricted estimator.}
\[
 cR
 \le
 \mathbb E_{\Theta,Y}d(\Theta,\widehat\Theta_\lambda(Y))
 \le
 CR .
\]
The lower bound follows from Proposition~\ref{prop:bayesian-algorithmic-lower} using the exact ghost mass; the upper bound is the actual Bayes risk of the same unrestricted estimator. 

Moreover, the Bayes-optimal risk for the displayed prior is also $\asymp R$. Thus the class-wide Fano relaxation below is vacuous only as a validation; it does not reflect an easy Bayes problem. The same rotationally symmetric class construction can accommodate an arbitrarily large finite family of priors exhibiting the separation, with markedly different local mass profiles. Across this family, the Bayes-optimal oracle may vary substantially, while the unrestricted estimator remains unchanged.

\item \emph{Full-class minimax risk is much larger.}  If
\[
\mathfrak R_{\rm mm}(T_{M,N},\tau)
:=
\inf_{\widehat\theta}
\sup_{t\in T_{M,N}}
\mathbb E_t d(t,\widehat\theta(Y)),
\]
where the infimum is over all measurable estimators with values in the ambient Euclidean space, then
\[
 cS\le \mathfrak R_{\rm mm}(T_{M,N},\tau)\le CS .
\]
Thus, whenever \(\log N/\log M\to\infty\), the full-class minimax risk is asymptotically larger than the Bayes risk under \(\pi\).

\item \emph{Algorithmically induced Gaussian validation matches the selected subatlas.}
For the Gaussian process
\[
  X_t := \langle Z,t\rangle,\qquad t\in T_{M,N},
\]
where \(Z\) is the same standard Gaussian vector as in the location experiment
\(Y=\Theta+\tau Z\), define
\[
  \mathcal G_{\rm alg}
  :=
  \mathbb E_{\Theta,Z}
  \bigl[
    X_{\widehat\Theta_\lambda(\Theta+\tau Z)}-X_\Theta
  \bigr].
\]
Then
\[
  \mathcal G_{\rm alg}
  \asymp
  \mathbb E\sup_{s,u\in H_M}(X_s-X_u)
  \asymp
  R\sqrt{\log M}.
\]
Moreover, under the ghost/reference law \(Y\sim Q_\tau=N(0,\tau^2I_{M+N+1})\),
\[
  Q_\tau\{\widehat\Theta_\lambda(Y)\in C_N\}\le N^{-2}
\]
for all sufficiently large $N$, and hence the ghost-selected subatlas is \(H_M\) up to negligible probability.  Conditional on
\(\widehat\Theta_\lambda(Y)\in H_M\), the ghost selection law is unif (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Own-work C011 v1, proof (unaudited); novelty unestablished. Let phi be C2 with phi(0)=0, 0<lambda<1, lambda<=phi prime<=1, and |phi second|<=beta. For finite data ||x_i||<=1, labels +/-1, network f_i=m^-1 sum_j a_j phi(w_j dot x_i), average logistic loss L and G=average (1+exp(y_i*f_i))^-1, set R^2=sum_j(a_j^2+||w_j||^2), r=R^2/m, A=max_j|a_j|. At every parameter vector, ||grad L||<=R*G/m and m*||Hessian L||op<=G*(1+beta*A+r)<=L*(1+beta*A+r). The per-neuron Hessian has cross block phi prime*x and hidden diagonal a_j*phi second*x*x^T; this explains the trained-output dependence. A fixed acute rank-two family shows no loss-only constant curvature bound can hold everywhere, even on the Gaussian survivor event of C010. Specifically n=d=2, m=4, z1=(3/5,1/5), z2=(3/5,-1/5), labels (1,-1), x_i=y_i*z_i, u=(1,0), all w_j=sigma*u, and a=(1,1,T,-T), T>=1. The opposite large outputs cancel, leaving M_i=(1/2)*y_i*phi(sigma*u dot x_i) and L independent of T. A unit contrast in the last two hidden weights has Hessian Rayleigh quotient (9*T^2/400)*sum_i[g_i*(1-g_i)*phi prime(sigma*u dot x_i)^2], with fixed positive coefficient. Energy is r=sigma^2+1/2+T^2/2. Three neurons lie in the aligned Gaussian ball/sign event, so the gradient-lower-bound event alone cannot eliminate this factor. Strict curvature violations persist on positive-Gaussian-mass neighborhoods, but their mass may shrink with T: this does not rule out a curvature bound excluding an additional Gaussian tail, or refute typical-trajectory burn-in. C011 also extends C010 surviving-gradient control to the centered smooth activation class, by using phi(v)/v for output updates and phi prime(v) for hidden updates; they need not be equal. For literal leaky ReLU, the Hessian formula holds only within an open activation cell with beta=0, and cannot be integrated across kinks. A centered softplus-leaky example meets bounded derivative, Lipschitz derivative and bounded near-homogeneity, so the obstruction is not solely a kink issue. The unpaid step is dynamic control of G_t*(1+beta*A_t+r_t), or an alternative discrete descent potential. 10228 finite exact rational assertions passed, including 2376 Hessian-direction controls, 144 smooth survivor steps, and 108 cancellation-family controls. A separate exact symbolic polynomial coefficient identity verifies the D1 normalization only, not the complete analytic/probability theorem. No Lean certificate or independent audit is claimed.
Centered C2 activation, derivative in [lambda,1], bounded second derivative beta; bounded finite data, no biases, both-layer mean-field model.
Pointwise curvature bound needs no separability or initialization condition.
Survivor-event discussion uses C010 strictly signed-Gram-positive rank>=2 separable data, iid centered Gaussian initialization and actual GD step m*eta.
Proof (unaudited), no novelty, burn-in theorem, trajectory failure or full formal certificate claimed.
title: T368 trained-output logistic Hessian: energy-dependent self-bounding curvature is unavoidable (unaudited)

[Theorem 13 of arXiv:2604.04267, 'On Sharpest Tail Bounds for Functions \\ of Tail Bounded Random Variables'] Let \(\mathfrak{m}(d) = \{m_{j_1,\dots,j_{d+1}}\}_{j_1,\dots,j_{d+1}=1}^n\) have all non-negative entries. Let \(X_1,\dots,X_d\) be real random \(n \times n\) matrices 
with mutually independent components. Denote the \(i,j\) entry of \(X_k\) by \(X^{(k)}_{ij}\) for all \(i,j,k\). Let \(f_{ijk} \in B\) and 
\(X^{(k)}_{ij} \in \mathcal{T}(f_{ijk})\) for all \(i,j,k\). Denote \(\widetilde{X}_k = \{\widetilde{X}^{(k)}_{ij}\}_{i,j=1}^n\) for \(k=1,\dots,d\). Here 
\(\widetilde{X}^{(k)}_{ij}\) is the ``right-shifted'' version of \(X^{(k)}_{ij}\) (see lemma~\ref{Xtilde} \eqref{Xtildedefn}). Then $\forall t \ge 0$,
\begin{equation}
P\bigg(\operatorname{Tr}\big(\mathfrak{M}_{\mathfrak{m}(d)}(X_1,\dots,X_d)\big) \ge t\bigg) \le P\bigg(\operatorname{Tr}\big(\mathfrak{M}_{\mathfrak{m}(d)}(\widetilde{X}_1,\dots,\widetilde{X}_d)\big) \ge t\bigg)
\end{equation}
and the RHS cannot be improved.

[Corollary 2 (Isotropic random walk) of arXiv:2605.13107, 'Discrepancy and Fisher information'] Let $K \subset \R^d$ be a compact, convex, centrally symmetric set with nonempty interior. Let $v_1,\dots,v_n$ be independent symmetric isotropic random vectors in $\R^d$. (That is, for each $j$, the random vectors $v_j$ and $-v_j$ have the same distribution, and $\E v_j v_j^\tran = I_d$.) Then there exists an online
    \footnote{Here \say{online} 
    means that, upon observing \(v_j\), 
    one must immediately decide whether to accept or discard it; the decision may depend on the previous steps, but not on future steps, and it cannot be changed later.} algorithm that discards some steps $v_j$ such that, for each $k$,
	\[
		\sum_{j \le k \text{ accepted}} v_j \in 2K
		\quad \text{deterministically},
	\]
	and
	\[
		\E \#\{\text{discarded}\}
		\le \sqrt{\lambda_1(K)} \, n,
	\]
	where $\lambda_1(K)$ is the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of $K$.
title: Isotropic random walk

[Lemma 36 of arXiv:2609.00567, 'Hodge--Tate splitting and Akizuki--Nakano vanishing in positive characteristic'] Let $\iota\colon X \to  S$ be a smooth representable morphism of \(\setF_p\)-stacks, where \(S\) is an fpqc algebraic stack. 
Let $h\colon S' \to  S$ be a morphism of fpqc algebraic stacks, and set
\[
X' \defeq X\times_S S'.
\]
Let $g\colon (X')^{(1)}_{/S'} \to  X^{(1)}_{/S}$ be the induced morphism between the relative Frobenius twists. 
Then we have
\[
(X'/S')^{\dR}
\simeq
(X/S)^{\dR}
\times_{X^{(1)}_{/S}}
(X')^{(1)}_{/S'}.
\]
In particular, if \(X\) is HT-split over \(S\), then \(X'\) is
HT-split over \(S'\).

[Definition 1 (Iterative Selection Algorithm) of arXiv:2506.17941, 'Greedy Selection under Independent Increments: A Toy Model Analysis'] Let $0 < t_1 < \cdots < t_k = T$ be observation times, and $N > n_1 > \cdots > n_k = 1$ be subset sizes. For fixed realization $\omega \in \Omega$,  an \emph{iterative selection algorithm} consists of $k$ maps $\{f_j\}_{j=1}^k$ such that:
\begin{itemize}
  \item $f_1$ selects $n_1$ indices from all observed histories up to $t_1$:
  \[ f_1: \mathcal{H}_1: =  \{X_i(t)\}_{i\in[N],\, t\le t_1} \mapsto \Sigma_1 \subset [N], \quad |\Sigma_1| = n_1. \]

  \item For $j > 1$, $f_j$ selects $n_j$ indices from updated histories over surviving indices:
  \[ f_j:  \mathcal{H}_i\mapsto \Sigma_j \subset \Sigma_{j-1}, \quad \mathcal{H}_i = \mathcal{H}_{(i-1)} \cup \{X_i(t)\}_{i\in\Sigma_{j-1}, t_{j-1}<t\le t_j},  \quad |\Sigma_j| = n_j. \]

  The final output is the single element $i_* \in \Sigma_k$.
\end{itemize}
title: Iterative Selection Algorithm

Let (X, Sigma, mu) be any measure space and 1 <= p <= infinity. For f, g in L^p(mu), f + g is in L^p(mu) and ||f + g||_p <= ||f||_p + ||g||_p. Hence ||.||_p is a norm on L^p for 1 <= p <= infinity. For 1 < p < infinity, equality holds if and only if f = 0 a.e. or g = lambda f a.e. for some constant lambda >= 0. (For p = 1 equality holds iff f * conj(g) >= 0 a.e.; for 0 < p < 1 the inequality is false in general: see the pitfall on p < 1.)

body:
[Definition 4 of arXiv:2604.03777, 'Equilibrium fluctuations for a multi-species particle system with long jumps'] Let $\gamma \geq 3/2$, $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$ and $\kappa \in\R$. 
We say that a $\mathcal{S}'(\mathbb{R})$-valued stochastic process 
$(\mathcal{Z}_t)_{ 0 \leq t \leq T}$ is a stationary energy solution of the 
fractional SBE with coupling constant $\kappa$ and diffusivity $D>0$ 
(in short, $SBE(\gamma,\lambda, \kappa, D)$) 
\begin{equation} 
\dd \mathcal{Z}_t = ( \mathbb{L}^{ \gamma  } + \widehat{\mathbb{L}}_{\lambda}^{ \gamma}) \; \mathcal{Z}_t \; \dd t + \kappa \nabla \mathcal{Z}_t^2  \; \dd t+  \sqrt{2 D \; \mathcal{P}^{\gamma} } \; \dd \mathcal{W}_t
\end{equation}
 if $(\mathcal{Z}_t)_{ 0 \leq t \leq T}$ satisfies (EE) in the sense of Definition \ref{defEE}, and
\begin{enumerate}
\item for all $t\in[0,T]$, $\mathcal{Z}_t$ is a mean zero Gaussian field with covariance as in~\eqref{covinifie};
\item
 for any $H \in \mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R})$, the processes $\mathcal{M}_t(H)$ and $\mathcal{N}_t(H)$ given by
\begin{align*}
& \mathcal{M}_t(H) := \mathcal{Z}_t(H) - \mathcal{Z}_0(H) - \mathcal{I}_t(H) + \kappa_{\gamma} \mathcal{B}_t(H),  \quad \mathcal{N}_t(H) :=[ \mathcal{M}_t(H)]^2  -2  D_3 t \;    \mathcal{P}^{\gamma} H,
\end{align*} 
 are continuous martingales with respect to the canonical filtration 
generated by $(\mathcal{Z}_t)_{t\in[0,T]}$, where the processes $(\mathcal{I}_t)_{t\in[0,T]}$ and 
$(\mathcal{B}_t)_{t\in[0,T]}$ are respectively defined in~\eqref{intprocess} and~\eqref{e:NonLin}.  
\item the reversed process $\{\widehat{\mathcal{Z}}_{t}:= \mathcal{Z}_{T-t}: t\in[0,T]\}$ 
satisfies items (1) and (2) with $\kappa$, 
and $\mathcal{B}_t$ respectively replaced by $-\kappa$ and 
$\widehat{\mathcal{B}}_t:= \mathcal{B}_{T-t} -\mathcal{B}_T$. 
\end{enumerate}
title: Definition 4 of arXiv:2604.03777

[Lem 15 of arXiv:2606.18877, 'Ergodic Properties of Non-Linear Density-Dependent Perturbations of the Ornstein--Uhlenbec'] Consider the operator~\eqref{K-OU-operator} corresponding to the convariance function of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process. Its eigenvalues are given by 
    \begin{equation}
    \lambda_n
    := \frac{2}{\beta_n^2+4a_0^2},
    \quad n=1,2,\dots
    \end{equation}
    where \(\beta_n\) are the positive roots of the equation \(\tan \beta T=-\beta/(2a_0)\). The eigenfunctions can be chosen as 
    \begin{equation}
        \phi_n(s):=\sin(\beta_n s),
        \quad n\geq 1.
    \end{equation}.

[Lemma main 2 of arXiv:2609.02871, 'Estimating the number of real zeros of linear combinations of radicals of polynomials'] Let $\beta>-1/2$ and $\lambda=-\beta(\beta+1)< \frac{1}{4}$. Let $u$ be a non-zero solution to
\[
\Delta_{\mathbb{D}} u + \lambda u=0 \quad \text{ in punctured Poincare's disc } \quad \mathbb{D}\setminus \{p_k:k=1, \dots, n\},
\]
where $p_k$ are distinct points in $\mathbb{D}$. Assume that $$u(z) = o(1-|z|^2)^{-\beta} \text{ as } z \to \partial \mathbb{D}$$ and that 
$$|u(z)|= o(|z-p_k|^{-A_k}) \text{ as } z\to p_k$$
for some integers $A_k$.
 Then $u$ has at most $N:=\#\{k:A_k=1\} + \sum2(A_k-1)$ nodal domains in $\mathbb{D}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 4 (An explicit positive-definite interpolation grid) of arXiv:2608.14475, '\vspace{-1.2cm}\textbf{Finite Gaussian Reconstruction of Polynomial Orbits:\\ From Correla'] Put
\[
 D_r=\left\lfloor\frac{rm}{2}\right\rfloor,
 \qquad n_r=\frac{r(r+1)}2.
\]
The set \(\cS_r\) defined in \eqref{eq:intro-explicit-spd-grid} lies in
\(\Sym_r^{++}(\Q)\), every one of its matrices satisfies
\[
 \frac12I_r\preceq\Sigma\preceq\frac32I_r,
\]
and
\[
 |\cS_r|=\binom{D_r+n_r}{n_r}.
\]
Evaluation on \(\cS_r\) is an isomorphism from the vector space of
polynomials on \(\Sym_r(\R)\) of total degree at most \(D_r\) onto
\(\R^{\cS_r}\).  Its inverse is an explicit rational finite-difference
transform.

[Defn 17 of arXiv:2605.25715, '2605.25715'] Denote by $M_{d}(\mathbb{R})$ the set of all real $d \times d$ matrices. Let $X \in M_{d}(\mathbb{R})$ with columns $\mathbf{x}_1, \mathbf{x}_2, \dots, \mathbf{x}_d \in \mathbb{R}^d$. The vectorization of $X$, denoted by $\operatorname{Vec}(X)$, is the $d^2 \times 1$ column vector given by
\[
X = \begin{pmatrix}
| & | & & | \\
\mathbf{x}_1 & \mathbf{x}_2 & \dots & \mathbf{x}_d \\
| & | & & |
\end{pmatrix}
\quad \xrightarrow{\quad \text{\rm Vec} \quad} \quad
\text{\rm Vec}(X) = 
\begin{pmatrix}
\mathbf{x}_1 \\ \mathbf{x}_2 \\ \vdots \\ \mathbf{x}_d
\end{pmatrix} \in \mathbb{R}^{d^2}.
\]
Then, the map $\text{Vec}: M_{d}(\mathbb{R}) \to \mathbb{R}^{d^2}$ is indeed a vector space isomorphism.
title: Definition 17 of arXiv:2605.25715

[Thm t:functconvergence2 of arXiv:2411.18236, 'A functional limit theorem for self-normalized partial sum processes in the $M_{1}$ topolo'] Let $(X_{n})$ be a stationary sequence of random variables, which is $\beta$--mixing and jointly regularly varying with index $\alpha \in (0,2)$, and of which the tail process $(Y_{i})_{i \in \mathbb{Z}}$ almost surely has no two values of the opposite sign. Suppose that Condition~(c:mixcond2 of the paper) holds. If $\alpha \in [1,2)$ also suppose that Conditions~(c:step6cond of the paper) and (c:BPScond1 of the paper) hold.
Then
$L_{n} \xrightarrow{d} L$ as $n \to \infty$,
in $D([0,1], \mathbb{R}^{2})$ endowed with the weak $M_{1}$ topology, where $L = (V,W)$, $V$
is an $\alpha$--stable L\'{e}vy process with characteristic triple $(0,
\nu_{1}, \gamma_{1})$ and $W$ is an $\alpha/2$--stable L\'{e}vy process with characteristic triple $(0,
\nu_{2}, \gamma_{2})$,
 where
\begin{align*}
 \nu_{1}(\mathrm{d} x) &= \theta \alpha \big( c_{+} 1_{(0,\infty)}(x) + c_{-} 1_{(-\infty, 0)}(x) \big) |x|^{-\alpha -1}\,\mathrm{d} x,\\
\nu_{2}(\mathrm{d} x) &=  \frac{\theta \alpha}{2} \mathrm{E}\bigg( \sum_{j}\eta_{j}^{2}\bigg)^{\alpha/2} x^{-\alpha/2 -1}1_{(0,\infty)}(x) \,\mathrm{d} x,\\
\gamma_{1} &= \left\{ \begin{array}{ll}
                                   \frac{\alpha}{\alpha-1} \big( p-q - \theta (c_{+}-c_{-}) \big), & \alpha \in (0,1) \cup (1,2),\\[0.2em]
                                   - \theta\mathrm{E}\bigg[ \sum_{j}\eta_{j} \log \Big( \Big| \sum_{i}\eta_{i}\eta_{j}^{-1} \Big|  \Big) \bigg], & \alpha =1,
                                 \end{array}\right.\\
\gamma_{2} &= \frac{\theta \alpha}{2-\alpha} \mathrm{E}\bigg( \sum_{j}\eta_{j}^{2}\bigg)^{\alpha/2},
\end{align*}
with $c_{+} = \mathrm{E} [ ( \sum_{j}\eta_{j} )^{\alpha} 1_{ \{ \sum_{j}\eta_{j} > 0 \}} ]$,
   $c_{-} = \mathrm{E} [( - \sum_{j}\eta_{j} )^{\alpha} 1_{ \{ \sum_{j}\eta_{j} < 0 \}}]$, and $p$ and $q$ as in $((e:mu of the paper))$.
title: Thm t:functconvergence2 of arXiv:2411.18236

[Proposition cor:dilation-coordinate-recurrence of arXiv:2606.21006, 'Law of the Iterated Logarithm for Weighted Sums of Functionals of Long-Memory Gaussian Seq'] Let \(W\), \(U_n\), and \(W_n\) be as in the beginning of this section; thus
\((U_nh)(x)=n^{1/2}h(nx)\) for \(h\in\mathfrak H_{\mathbb R}\), and
\(W_n(h)=W(U_nh)\), \(n\ge3\).
Let \(E\subset D_{\mathbb R}\) be finite-dimensional, and let
\(e_1,\ldots,e_N\) be an orthonormal basis of \(E\) in \(\mathfrak H_{\mathbb R}\). Fix
\(\xi\in E\) with \(\|\xi\|_{\mathfrak H_{\mathbb R}}<1\). 

Then there exists
\(\gamma>1\) and a sparse deterministic sequence \(n_k:=\lfloor\exp(k^\gamma)\rfloor\)
such that, with probability one, there is a subsequence \(k_\ell\to\infty\) satisfying
\[
    \frac{W_{n_{k_\ell}}(h)}
    {(2\log\log n_{k_\ell})^{1/2}}
    \longrightarrow
    \langle h,\xi\rangle_{\mathfrak H_{\mathbb R}}
    \qquad
    \text{for every }h\in E .
\]

[Definition of arXiv:2411.19810, 'Radial conformal welding in Liouville quantum gravity'] Let $m \geq 0$, let $(\alpha_i, z_i) \in \mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{C}$ for $i = 1, \dots, m$ where the $z_i$'s are pairwise distinct, and let $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$. Set 
	\[C_\mathbb{C}^{(\alpha_i, z_i)_i, (\alpha, \infty)} = \prod_{i=1}^m |z_i|_+^{-\alpha_i(2Q-\alpha_i - \alpha)} e^{\sum_{j=i+1}^{m+1} \alpha_i\alpha_j G_\mathbb{C} (z_i, z_j)}.\]
	Sample $(h, \mathbf c)$ from $C_\mathbb{C}^{(\alpha_i, z_i)_i} P_\mathbb{C} \times [e^{(\alpha + \sum_{i=1}^m \alpha_i - 2Q)c}dc]$, and set $\phi(z) = h(z) +(\alpha- 2Q) \log |z|_+ + \sum_{i=1}^m \alpha_i G_\mathbb{C}(z, z_i) + \mathbf c$. We write $\mathrm{LF}_\mathbb{C}^{(\alpha_i,z_i)_i, (\alpha , \infty)}$ for the law of $\phi$.

body: In probability theory, the law of large numbers is a mathematical law which states that the average of the results obtained from a large number of independent random samples converges to the true value, if it exists. More formally, the law of large numbers states that given a sample of independent and identically distributed values, the sample mean converges to the true mean.

[Lemma 8 of arXiv:2604.27519, 'Quantitative homogenization of the maximal action of curves in a Brownian potential'] Suppose that for every deterministic $\bar h\in{\mathcal N}$
we are given a family $\{A_{n}(\bar h)\}_{n=1,\cdots,N}$
of independent random variables with $A_{n}(\bar h)$ $=_{\rm law}A$. 
Suppose that we are also given a random variable $\bar h^*\in{\mathcal N}$ such that
there exists a constant $D\ge e$ such that for every threshold $\nu\ge D$ 
there exists a subset ${\mathcal N}_{\nu}$ $\subset{\mathcal N}$ with

\begin{align}
\ln\mathbb{P}(\bar h^*\not\in{\mathcal N}_{\nu})\le-N\,\nu/D
\quad\mbox{while}\quad
\ln\#{\mathcal N}_{\nu}\le C_0 N\ln\nu,

\end{align} 

where $C_0$ is the universal constant from Lemma \ref{L:count}.
Then we have

\begin{align*}
\big\|N^{-1}\sum_{n=1}^{N} A_n(\bar h^*)\big\|_1\lesssim\|A\|_1\ln D.
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 8 of arXiv:2604.27519

Conditional joint-entrance implication: assume C006 angular functional convergence to the positive-from-zero reciprocal-angle diffusion, scalar log-norm functional convergence, C009 mixed compact generator, and C008 radial locking. Then (V_n,U_n) converges jointly from (0,0) to dV=-(5/2)dt+sqrt(5)dW1, dU=(2U+1/(3pi))dt+(2/sqrt(5))*U dW1+sqrt(6/5)*U dW2, with independent W1,W2. For L/n->t>0, the final two preactivations and n^2*(1-rho_L) converge simultaneously to (exp(V_t/2)*sqrt(q1)*xi,exp(V_t/2)*sqrt(q2)*xi,1/(2*U_t^2)), with xi standard normal independent of (V,U). Scope: Conditional implication only. C005-C006, C008 and C009 require independent checking. No literature priority clearance or quantitative finite-n rate.
Independent Gaussian zero-bias width-n ReLU layers at variance 2/n; initial angle fixed in (0,pi); positive initial Gram diagonal scales converging to q1,q2>0; explicit functional-convergence, mixed-generator and radial-locking premises stated in proof. The final output row is independent of the hidden layers.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:964ed6560a11e5865a94dd564cbf06b094b11115ccea11c969cf597da42380f7","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/96/964ed6560a11e5865a94dd564cbf06b094b11115ccea11c969cf597da42380f7.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:3645276d01e8a91a34b1322dbb1854efd36124045f2a7b37701e9049be9ab27d","bundle_entry_key":"relu-joint-entrance","bundle_id":"population.t244-relu-joint-entrance-conditional-draft-004","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability; random neural networks","draft":"w691/bundle_004.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.randomnetworks:gaussian-relu-joint-entrance-output-angle-conditional-limit","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Conditional joint entrance theorem and simultaneous output/angle law

Status: proof draft (unaudited), Target 1. This is an implication with explicit premises, not an independently checked solution. In particular the angular entrance theorem C006 still depends on the unaudited uniform estimates C005. No novelty or quantitative convergence rate is asserted.

Let the network and initial angle satisfy C006: independent width-n Gaussian zero-bias ReLU layers, critical variance 2/n, fixed theta_0 in (0,pi), positive initial diagonal scales q_(j,n)->q_j>0. Write V_n(s)=log(K_(1,floor(ns))/q_(1,n)), U_n(s)=1/(n theta_floor(ns)). On the exponentially rare extinction/collinearity event assign finite cemetery conventions, chosen consistently in all statements below. They do not affect convergence in law.

Assume the following premises for every finite T:

1. The exact angular processes satisfy the functional convergence asserted in C006, with continuous limit dU=(2U+a)dt+sqrt(2)U dB, U_0=0, a=1/(3pi). In particular U_t>0 almost surely for all t>0, and U_n is C-tight.
2. The single-input log-scale process V_n is C-tight and converges marginally to dV=-(5/2)dt+sqrt(5)dW, V_0=0. This is the settled scalar geometric-Brownian path limit, with the zero-multiplier event removed at exponentially small cost.
3. The joint compact generator statement C009 holds for the exact kernel up to its stated exponentially small bounded-test error.
4. For the output-law conclusion use the conditional radial-locking lemma C008, whose proof is separately unaudited.

Then (V_n,U_n) converges jointly on [0,T] to the unique solution

    dV=-(5/2)dt+sqrt(5)dW1,
    dU=(2U+a)dt+(2/sqrt(5))U dW1+sqrt(6/5)U dW2,
    (V_0,U_0)=(0,0),

where W1,W2 are independent standard Brownian motions. For a pair of final linear Gaussian preactivations Z_(1,n),Z_(2,n) with an independent final weight row, and L/n->t>0,

    (Z_(1,n),Z_(2,n), n^2(1-rho_L))
      => (exp(V_t/2) sqrt(q_1) xi,
          exp(V_t/2) sqrt(q_2) xi,
          1/(2U_t^2)),

where xi is a standard normal independent of the entire limiting (V,U) process. For L^2(1-rho_L), replace the last coordinate by t^2/(2U_t^2). The common final xi is independent of (V,U); the scale V and angle U themselves are generally dependent.

## Joint tightness and interior identification

C-tightness of both coordinates implies joint C-tightness, and every joint subsequential limit has continuous paths, starts at (0,0), and has the two stated marginals. In particular its U coordinate is almost surely positive throughout every closed interval [epsilon,T] with epsilon>0: the explicit scalar solution is positive at every positive time, and its continuous path has a positive minimum on that compact interval.

On any rectangle {|v|<R, d<u<K}, C009 and the vanishing-jump bounds identify the stopped joint martingale problem with generator

    A=-(5/2) partial_v +(2u+a) partial_u
       +(5/2) partial_vv +2u partial_vu +u^2 partial_uu.

One may first use smooth tests compactly supported in an interior rectangle and localization inside slightly larger rectangles, so no assertion about continuity of a boundary hitting-time functional is required. The prelimit bounded-test martingale identities and locally uniform generator convergence pass to the limit by C-tightness and boundedness of the stopped coefficients. The exponentially small bad-event errors contribute at most O(n exp(-cn)) over nT steps. They cannot supply a limiting boundary term.

For each epsilon>0, remove the lower spatial localization d->0 on [epsilon,T]; pathwise positivity and continuity of U justify this removal. Keep |V|<=R and U<=K as upper localizations. We obtain the local martingale problem on every positive-time interval.

## Extension to time zero

On a fixed upper localization, Af is bounded for any smooth compactly supported f on R^2, including near u=0: the coefficients in A are polynomials of degree at most two and have finite limits there. For 0<epsilon<r<t, the local martingale identity is already valid on [r,t]. As epsilon->0,

    f(V_epsilon,U_epsilon)->f(0,0),
    integral_0^epsilon Af(V_s,U_s)ds ->0

in L1 under this localization, by continuity and boundedness. Thus the martingale extends continuously to time zero. Its conditional expectation identity for r>0 and then r=0 follows by bounded convergence; it has no additional term supported at the initial time. Sending R,K to infinity is legitimate since the continuous finite-valued paths are bounded on every compact time interval. This establishes the full local martingale problem for A from (0,0), not merely its two marginal martingale problems.

The displayed diffusion representation has covariance matrix [[5,2u],[2u,2u^2]]. All its drift and diffusion coefficients are globally Lipschitz on R^2. Existence and uniqueness in law therefore identify every subsequential joint limit with that SDE. Since every subsequence has the same limit, the full joint convergence follows. This step uses C009's mixed derivative term; independent marginal Brownian limits alone would not justify the conclusion.

## Simultaneous output/correlation limit

For each fixed s>0, U_n(s)=>U_s>0 implies theta_floor(ns)->0 in probability, and hence rho_floor(ns)->1. Bounded convergence and integration over s imply the angular-defect-average assumption of C008. Its radial-locking conclusion yields

    (K_1,K_2,rho_L,U_n(L/n))
      => (q_1 exp(V_t),q_2 exp(V_t),1,U_t).

Since n^2(1-cos(theta_L)) = [1/(2U_n(L/n)^2)] times a factor tending to one, the fine angular coordinate converges jointly to 1/(2U_t^2). For w in R^2 and any bounded continuous h of the angular coordinate, conditional Gaussianity of the final independent row gives

    E[exp(i w dot Z_n) h(n^2(1-rho_L))]
      = E[exp(-w^T G_L w/2) h(n^2(1-rho_L))].

The integrand is bounded and continuous in the covariance and the positive limiting U coordinate. Its limit is

    E[exp(-exp(V_t)(w dot (sqrt(q_1),sqrt(q_2)))^2/2)
       h(1/(2U_t^2))],

which identifies the stated simultaneous law and the independent auxiliary final Gaussian xi. This is a characteristic-function argument, not a multiplication of conditional probability bounds or a moment-determinacy argument.

## Explicit representation of the coupling

Variation of constants gives

    V_t=-(5/2)t+sqrt(5) W1_t,
    U_t=a integral_0^t exp((t-s)+(2/sqrt(5))(W1_t-W1_s)
                                +sqrt(6/5)(W2_t-W2_s)) ds.

The scalar law of U agrees with the dossier's Brownian exponential functional, but here its coupling to the scale is retained. This formula is a consequence of the conditional theorem, and not evidence that the unaudited premises have already been established independently.

Its displayed q/log-q equations have an Ito discrepancy awaiting Claude review. body: Let X_1, X_2, ... be iid real random variables with mean 0 and variance 1, and let S_n = X_1 + ... + X_n. The law of the iterated logarithm states that, almost surely, limsup_{n -> infinity} S_n / sqrt(2 n log log n) = 1 and liminf_{n -> infinity} S_n / sqrt(2 n log log n) = -1. So for every eps > 0, S_n crosses (1-eps) sqrt(2 n log log n) infinitely often but exceeds (1+eps) sqrt(2 n log log n) only finitely often, pinning the almost-sure growth rate strictly between the CLT scale sqrt(n) and O(sqrt(n log n)). Due to Khinchin (bounded case, 1924) and Hartman-Wintner (general iid finite-variance case, 1941).
title: Law of the iterated logarithm

Unreviewed finite-Gaussian control. For each integer n>=1 set L_n=beta_n=n and K_n=2^(n^2). Take K_n distinct singleton paths of unit weights whose centered Gaussian fields all equal one common standard normal Z. The covariance is PSD with maximum diagonal 1. At fixed xi>=0 the hard log minimum is xi Z, but the soft minimum F_beta=-(1/beta)log sum_p exp(-beta f_p) equals xi Z-n log 2 at beta_n=n. Thus normalized expectations differ by -log 2 although beta_n tends to infinity. This attains the absolute smoothing error bound. The bias does not depend on xi and cancels in endpoint differences; this control alone does not refute an integrated endpoint reduction.
Finite path model; no planar LFPP realization claimed

[Lem elementary of arXiv:2606.21049, '\textsc{Locality of rough path lifts}'] Let $S$ be a non-negative, square-integrable random variable, $\delta \in [0,1)$, $a > 0$, and $b, p \geq 0$. Assume that
\[
\mathbb{E}[S] \geq a p, \qquad \mathrm{Var}[S] \leq bp,\qquad \mathbb{P}[S > 0] \leq \delta.
\]
Then 
\[
p \leq \frac{\delta}{1 - \delta} \frac{b}{a^2}.
\]

$$\Psi(\gamma):=|\gamma(0)|+[\gamma]_\alpha,\quad \gamma\in \mathcal{C}([0,T],\mathbb{R}^d).$$
Then, $\Psi^{-1}([0,R])$ is a compact subset of $C(K,\mathbb{R}^d)$ and we have
$$\mathcal{N}_\varepsilon(\Psi^{-1}([0,R]))\leq \left(4+\frac{144(1+T^\alpha)^2R^2}{\varepsilon^2}\right)^{d\,(1+\frac{2T(6(1+T^\alpha)R)^{1/\alpha}}{\varepsilon^{1/\alpha}})}.$$
for every $\varepsilon>0$.

[Definition def:response-realization of arXiv:2608.02459, 'Response Calculus for Spectral Simplicity\\ and Joint Eigenvalue Densities'] We say that the response is \emph{potential-realizable} if, for every
admissible $\mu$, there exist a real vector space
$\mathcal M_{\rm resp}(\mu)$ of finite signed measures and a linear
map
\begin{equation}
 U_\mu:\mathcal M_{\rm resp}(\mu)\longrightarrowH
 
\end{equation}
such that $\Theta_\mu(u,v)\in\mathcal M_{\rm resp}(\mu)$ whenever $u$ and $v$
belong to a common positive eigenspace of $A_\mu$, and
\begin{equation}
 \inner{U_\mu\sigma}{f}_{H}
 =\int_{S}f\,d\sigma,
 \qquad
 \sigma\in\mathcal M_{\rm resp}(\mu),\qquad f\inH_{\mathrm{reg}}.
 
\end{equation}
It is \emph{faithfully potential-realizable} if every $U_\mu$ is
injective.

[Proposition pro-Bay-2 of arXiv:2411.12623, 'Random signed measures'] Let $\Theta$ be a CRSM satisfying $A00$, $A0$, $A1$ and $A2'$. Assume that $\nu(d\theta)=g(\theta)d\theta$ for some function $g:\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}\to(0,\infty)$. Let $X_1,...,X_m$ be generated i.i.d.~conditional on $\Theta$ according to $X_1=\sum_{k=1}^{K}x_{k}\delta_{\psi_{k}}$ with $x_{k}|\theta_k\stackrel{iid}{\sim} H_{fix}(dx|\theta_{k})$ if $\psi_{k}$ is a fixed atom and $x_{k}|\theta_k\stackrel{iid}{\sim} H_{ord}(dx|\theta_{k})$ otherwise. Then, $\Theta_{post}$ is a CRSM with three parts.
	
	\textnormal{1.} For each $k\in [K_{fix}]$, $\Theta_{post}$ has a fixed atom at $\psi_{fix,k}$ with weight $\theta_{post,fix,k}$ with density $f_{post,fix,k} (\theta)\propto f_{fix,k} (\theta)\prod_{j=1}^m h_{fix}(x_{fix,j,k}|\theta)$.
	
	\textnormal{2.} For each $k\in [K_{new}]$, $\Theta_{post}$ has a fixed atom at $\psi_{new,k}$ with weight $\theta_{post,new,k}$, whose density is proportional to $g(\theta)\prod_{j=1}^m h_{ord}(x_{new,j,k}|\theta)$.
	
	\textnormal{3.} The ordinary component of $\Theta_{post}$ has weight measure $\nu_{post}(d\theta):=\nu(d\theta)H_{ord}(\{0\}|\theta)^m$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition pro-Bay-2 of arXiv:2411.12623

C0048 asks for positive critical spontaneous magnetization for every integer q>=3 and d>=3 in the zero-field nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic Potts model. At beta_MF=(q-1)*log(q-1)/(d*(q-2)), uniform product spins and the ordered product law pi_1=(q-1)/q, pi_i=1/(q*(q-1)) for i>1 have equal limiting scores S(pi)+beta_MF*d*sum(pi_i^2). [Lemma 1 of arXiv:2608.19560, '\textbf{Computing transient probabilities in Markovian queues with balking conditional on '] For each $|z| \leq 1$, the unconditional PGF $\bm{p}^*(z,t)$ is
determined by the following linear differential equation:

\begin{align}
\bm{p}^*(z,0)
&=
\bm{p}(0),

\\
\frac{\partial \bm{p}^*(z,t)}{\partial t}
&=
\bm{p}^*(z,t)\bigl[\bm{Q}(t)-\lambda(t)(1-z)\bm{B}\bigr],

\end{align}

where $\bm{p}(0)$ is given by \eqref{eq:p(0)}, and 
$\bm{B}$ denotes an $|\Omega| \times |\Omega|$
diagonal matrix representing state transitions due to customer balking:

\[
[\bm{B}]_{(k,\ell,s),(k',\ell',s')}
=
\left\{
\begin{aligned}
&1-\beta_\ell,&& (k',\ell',s') = (k,\ell,s),\\
&0,&& \text{otherwise}.
\end{aligned}
\right.
\]
