body:
[Definition def:coalescent of arXiv:2606.09386, 'High-degree vertices in uniform recursive directed acyclic graphs with freezing'] Fix $m,n\in\mathbb{N}$ and fix a choice sequence $\mathbf x$ such that Assumption~$\hyperref[ass:A]{\mathbf{x}}$(item:geq1 of the paper) is satisfied. The \emph{Kingman $(m,n)$-coalescent with freezing} is the sequence of random graphs $(G_n,\ldots,G_1)$, constructed as follows.\\
We initialise $G_n$ as the graph without edges consisting of $A_n$ \emph{active} vertices labelled $a_1,\ldots,a_{A_n}$ and $F_n$ \emph{frozen} vertices labelled $f_1,\ldots,f_{F_n}$. For $2\leq i\leq n$, construct $G_{i-1}$ from $G_i$ in the following way: If $x_i = -1$, select a frozen vertex uniformly at random and \emph{activate} it by relabelling it as $i$. This vertex is now considered active. If $x_i=1$, select $(m+1)\wedge A_i=(m\wedge A_{i-1})+1$ active roots uniformly at random. Then, independently of everything else, choose one of these $(m+1)\wedge A_i$ roots uniformly at random and connect it via directed edges to each of the other selected roots.
title: Definition def:coalescent of arXiv:2606.09386

[Lem 23 of arXiv:2608.13976, 'Boundary Harnack principle for diffusion with jumps on metric measure spaces'] For each $R>0,$ there are constants  $C_k>0, k=1, 2$  such that for any $x\in \sX, r\in (0, R)$ and $t>0,$
$$
\P_x(\tau_{B(x,r)}\leq t)\leq  C_1  \frac{ t}{\phi(r)}\leq C_2 \dfrac{t}{r^{\beta_{2, \phi}}}.
$$
Hence ${\bf (EP)} _{\leq, R, \gamma}$ holds for $X$ for  $\gamma=\beta_{2, \phi}.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

$$
 \mathcal{L}_r^{(-1)}[\mathfrak{M}]= \Phi_{-1}^{\langle-1\rangle} \circ \mathbf{M}_{\eta_{\gamma, a,\nu}(z)} \circ \Phi_{-1},
$$
with a domain 
$$
{\rm Dom}\bigl(\mathcal{L}_r^{(-1)}[\mathfrak{M}]\bigr)=\left\{A\in\mathcal{A}_r^{(-1)}: \eta_{\gamma,a,\nu}(\cdot) \Phi_{-1}(A) \in \mathcal{A}_r\right\}.
$$

body: [Lemma lem:flow_line_representation of arXiv:2411.13133, 'Connectivity of the adjacency graph of\\ complementary components of the $\SLE$ Fan'] Suppose that we have the setup described just above.  Suppose that $V$ is a bounded connected component of $\mathbf{H} \setminus ({\mathbf F}(\theta_1,\theta_2;\gamma) \cup \gamma)$ with $\partial V \cap {\mathbf F}(\theta_1,\theta_2;\gamma) \neq \emptyset$.  We will view $\partial V$ as a collection of prime ends in $V$.  Then there exists $z(V) \in \partial V$ and $\theta(V) \in \mathbf{R}$ so that the boundary conditions for the conditional law of $h$ given $\mathcal {F}_\gamma$ on $\partial V \cap {\mathbf F}(\theta_1,\theta_2;\gamma)$ are given by the right (resp.\ left) side of a flow line of angle $\theta(V)$ starting from $z(V)$ and going in the clockwise (resp.\ counterclockwise) direction until hitting $\gamma$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:constant-escape-gen-multi of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix a send sequence~$\overline{p}$ with $p_0=1$. Fix integers $j\ge 1$ and $\tau \ge 0$ and a real number $\nu\ge 0$. 
Let $R_1,\ldots,R_j$ be independent binomial random variables
where, for all $i\in [j]$, $R_i = {\mathrm Bin}(n_i,\rho_i)$.
Let $\overline{R} = (R_1,\ldots,R_j)$.
Let~$E^+$ be a constant-escape process on $[j]$ with send sequence~$\overline{p}$, start time $\tau$, end-of-step arrival rate $\nu$, and $\overline{\mathrm{arr}}_{[j]}^{E^+}(\tau) = \overline{R}$.   
Then for all $t \ge \tau$, $b_1^{E^+}(t),\dots,b_j^{E^+}(t)$ can be expressed as coordinates of a generalised multinomial random variable.

[Theorem 5 (Identification of coefficients, Proposition \ref{prop-invariant-exp}, Theorem \ref{thm-consistency}) of arXiv:2604.04100, '\LARGE Learning Equilibrium Fluctuation Expansions from Overdamped Langevin Dynamics'] Assume $d=1$. Let $\mu_\varepsilon$ denote the invariant measure of \eqref{SDE-0} and let $(b_m(F))_{0\le m\le n}$ be defined as in Theorem \ref{thm-longtime-intro}. Then for every $F\in C^{n+1}(\mathbb R)$ satisfying \eqref{assump-F}: 
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] There exists $\varepsilon_0\in (0,1]$ and $ (B_m(F))_{0\leq m\leq n} $ such that for every $\varepsilon\in (0,\varepsilon_0)$,
\begin{equation*}
\int_{\mathbb R} F(x)\mu_\varepsilon(\mathrm{d}x)
= \sum_{m=0}^n \varepsilon^{m/2} B_m(F) + R_{n}(F,\varepsilon),
\end{equation*}
where the remainder satisfies
$$
\bigl|R_{n}(F,\varepsilon)\bigr|\le C(n,F)\varepsilon^{(n+1)/2},
$$
for some constant $C(n,F)>0$ independent of $\varepsilon$.
\item[(ii)]  If the initial law of $\xi_0$ satisfies
$$
\mathbb P(\xi_0>0)=\mathbb P(\xi_0<0)=\frac12,
$$
then for every $m\in\{0,\dots,n\}$, we have
$$
B_m(F)=b_m(F).
$$
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Identification of coefficients, Proposition \ref{prop-invariant-exp}, Theorem \ref{thm-consistency}

body: [Proposition lem:independence-across-bands-moduli of arXiv:2606.10973, 'Quasisymmetric rigidity of the Brownian sphere'] For each $\alpha > 0$, $b \in (0, 1)$, and $M > 0$, there exists $\lambda_\ast = \lambda_\ast(\alpha, b, M) \in (0, 1)$ such that for each $\lambda \in (0, \lambda_\ast]$, the following is true: Let $(\BC, \Phi; 0, \infty)$ be a $\sqrt{8/3}$-LQG cone. Let $\{t_j\}_{j \in \BN}$ be a decreasing sequence of positive real numbers such that $t_{j + 1}/t_j \le \lambda$ for every $j \in \BN$. Then for each $n \in \BN$, it holds with probability at least $1 - \lambda^{\alpha n}$ that there are at least $bn$ values of $j \in [1, n]_\BZ$ for which $\Mod(A_{\lambda t_j,t_j}^\bullet(0; D_\Phi)) \ge M$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition lem:independence-across-bands-moduli of arXiv:2606.10973

[Lemma lem:dyadic-maximal of arXiv:2606.21006, 'Law of the Iterated Logarithm for Weighted Sums of Functionals of Long-Memory Gaussian Seq'] Let $N\ge2$, and let $Z_{N+1},\ldots,Z_{2N}$ be centered square-integrable random variables.
For an interval $I\subset\{N+1,\ldots,2N\}$ write
\(
    Z(I):=\sum_{t\in I}Z_t .
\)
Assume that there exist constants $B_N>0$ and $\gamma\ge1$ such that, for every interval
$I\subset\{N+1,\ldots,2N\}$,
\[
    \mathbb E|Z(I)|^2
    \le
    B_N^2\left(\frac{|I|}{N}\right)^\gamma .
\]
Then there exists a universal constant $C<\infty$ such that
\[
    \mathbb E
    \max_{N\le n\le2N}
    \left|
        \sum_{t=N+1}^{n}Z_t
    \right|^2
    \le
    C(\log N)^2B_N^2 .
\]

body:
[Prop finiteNAdjointDuality of arXiv:2609.02743, 'Sharp mean-field estimates for diffusive log/Riesz gases in the Hilbert--Schmidt regime'] For $t\in[0,T]$ and $\phi\in\mathscr D_T$, let $f^r=\mathsf{U}^{r,t}\phi$ denote the classical solution of the backward adjoint problem (equation eq:backwardAdjointEquation of the paper).  Then
\begin{align}
S_N^t(\phi)
=S_N^0(\mathsf{U}^{0,t}\phi)
+\sqrt N\,M_N^t[f]
-\frac{\sqrt N}{2}\int_0^t
\mathsf A_1(\nabla f^r,X_N^r,\mu^r)\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm d r,
\end{align}
where
\begin{align}
M_N^\tau[f]
\coloneqq
\frac1N\sqrt{\frac2\beta}\sum_{i=1}^N
\int_0^\tau\nabla f^r(x_i^r)\cdot \mathop{}\!\mathrm d B_i^r,
\qquad 0\le\tau\le t.
\end{align}
By the boundedness of $\nabla f$, $(M_N^\tau[f])_{0\le\tau\le t}$ is a continuous square-integrable martingale.  The last term in (equation eq:finiteNAdjointDuality of the paper) converges to zero in $L^1$ at rate $O(N^{-1/2})$.
title: Finite-$N$ adjoint-duality identity

[Corollary cor:ranked-effective-length-convergence of arXiv:2607.04264, 'Macroscopic Feynman Cycles and Poisson--Kingman Universality in Bose Condensation'] Assume the assumptions of~(thm:main-canonical-bridge-limit of the paper) hold.
Let
\[
    \ell^L
    =
    (\ell_1^L,\ell_2^L,\ldots)
\]
be the decreasing rearrangement of the length coordinates of  $\Xi^{\mathrm{eff}}$. 
Let
\[
    \ell
    =
    (\ell_1,\ell_2,\ldots)
\]
be the decreasing rearrangement of the length coordinates of the limiting
bridge \(\Pi_{\rho_{\mathrm{eff}}}^{\mathrm{br}}\).
Assume that \(\Pi_{\rho_{\mathrm{eff}}}^{\mathrm{br}}\) has almost surely no ties in the length
coordinate.  Then
\[
    \ell^L
    \Longrightarrow
    \ell
    \qquad
    \text{in } \ell^1_\downarrow .
\]
where
\[
    \ell^1_\downarrow
    :=
    \left\{
        x=(x_i)_{i\ge1}\in[0,\infty)^{\mathbb N}:
        x_1\ge x_2\ge\cdots\ge0,\ 
        \|x\|_1:=\sum_{i=1}^\infty x_i<\infty
    \right\}
\]
is equipped with the usual \(\ell^1\)-metric.
Finite ranked configurations are identified with elements of
\(\ell^1_\downarrow\) by appending zeros.
In particular, if the limiting length marginal of the Poisson intensity is
diffuse, then the no-ties assumption above is satisfied. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 4 (moving one point) of arXiv:2606.08581, '2606.08581'] Let \(A\) be a finite multiset of diameter \(D\), and let \(A'\) be obtained from \(A\) by moving one point by distance one. Then
\[
|I(A')-I(A)|\le 2D+1.
\]
In particular, \(I(A)-I(A')\le 2D+1\).

body:
[Proposition 51 (Counterexample to simultaneous mixed-degree extraction) of arXiv:2608.12492, 'Weak Limits of Wiener Chaos: Primitive--Fock Classification and Hilbert--Stein Extraction'] Let $Q=2,d=1$, and let $e,h$ be orthonormal in $\cK_1$.  Consider
\begin{equation}
 x_1=\alpha e+h,\qquad x_2=e^{\odot2},\qquad 0<\alpha\ll1.
 
\end{equation}
Then $\cN_1(F)=\mathbb Re$, so $h$ belongs to the canonical Gaussian
factor.  Nevertheless the first reduced
promotion is made at weight two and its range contains a nonzero $e\odot h$ component.
Consequently
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb U_2^{-1}M_{2,\mathcal U}^{[J]}
 \not\subset\cW_2(\cN(F))
 
\end{equation}
already after the first promotion.  Moreover the defect is not confined to
the module: for this packet the simultaneous reduced trajectory promotes
$h$ itself after finitely many further steps, so that its terminal residual
at weight one is zero, whereas
$G^{\can}=I_1(h)\ne0$.

[Prop Bertini prop of arXiv:2609.04023, 'Characterizing Contractions and Weighted Blowdowns'] Consider the situation of Theorem (scheme case of the paper) where we assume $r:= \dim Y > 0.$
Then, there exists a Zariski-open subset $\Omega \subseteq \mathfrak{d}^r$ of ordered $r$-tuples $([s_1], \ldots, [s_r])$ for which
\[
Z_i := V_Z(s_1, \ldots, s_i), \ \ \ X_i = V_X(f^*s_1, \ldots, f^*s_i) = X \times_{Z} Z_i,
\]
\[
Y_i := V_Y(s_1|_Y, \ldots, s_i|_Y), \ \ \ E_i := V_E(f^*s_1|_E, \ldots, f^*s_i|_E) = E\times_Z Z_i \subseteq X_i,
\]
satisfies the following, for all $1 \le i \le r$
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] $X_i, Z_i, Y_i$, and $E_i$ are smooth of dimension $n-i, n-i, r-i, n-1-i$, respectively.
\item[(ii)] $Y_r$ is a finite non-empty collection of reduced points
\item[(iii)] If $f_i := f|_{X_i} : X_i \to Z_i$ is the restriction of $f$, then $f_i(E_i) = Y_i$.
\item[(iv)] $E_i$ is a smooth Cartier divisor on $X_i$ where $\mathcal{O}_{X_i}(-E_i) \simeq \mathcal{O}_X(-E)|_{X_i}$.
\item[(v)] The morphism $f_i : X_i \to Z_i$ is projective, birational, and has connected fibers, i.e., $f_i$ is a contraction morphism with exceptional divisor $\mathrm{Exc}(f_i)= E_i$ where $f_i : X_i \setminus E_i \xrightarrow{\sim} Z_i \setminus Y_i$
\end{itemize}

body:
[Definition def:SSS of arXiv:2509.04155, 'An Approach to Sub-Gaussian Heat Kernel Estimates via Analysis on Metric Spaces'] Let $p \geq 1$.
    A \emph{$p$-energy structure} on a metric measure space $(X,d,\mu)$ is a triplet $(\mathcal{F}_p,\Gamma_p,\Psi)$ consisting of the following data.
    \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)}, leftmargin=*]
    \vspace{3pt}
    \item $\mathcal{F}_p$ is subset of $L^p(X,\mu)$ which we call a \emph{Sobolev space}.
    The members of $\mathcal{F}_p$ are called \emph{Sobolev functions}. 
    \vspace{3pt}
    \item $\Gamma_p$ assigns to every $f \in \mathcal{F}_p$ a non-negative finite Borel measure denoted $\Gamma_p\Span{f}$. We call the measure $\Gamma_p\Span{f}$ the \emph{energy measure} of $f$. To emphasize that these are Dirichlet type $p$-energies in many practical cases, we will frequently use the notation
    \[
         \int_{A} \, d\Gamma_p\Span{f} = \Gamma_p\Span{f}(A).
    \]
    \item $\Psi : X \times (0,\infty) \to (0,\infty)$ is a scale function such that the pair $(\mathcal{F}_p,\Gamma_p)$ satisfies both the Poincar\'e inequality (eq:PI of the paper) (Definition (def:PI of the paper)) and the upper capacity estimate (eq:UCap of the paper) (Definition (def:Ucap of the paper)).
    \end{enumerate}

body: [Theorem 3.1 of arXiv:2603.27659, 'Operator Norm Bounds for Multi-leg Matrix Tensors and Applications to Random Matrix Theory'] Let $m,N\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\sigma_{1},\sigma_{2}\in\mathcal{P}([m])$. Let $M(\sigma_{1},\sigma_{2})$ and $C(\sigma_{1},\sigma_{2})$ be the quantities given in Definition 2.1. Then $\displaystyle N^{M(\sigma_{1},\sigma_{2})}\leq\max_{A_{1},\ldots,A_{m}}\left|\left(\mathrm{Tr}_{\sigma_{1}}\otimes\mathrm{Tr}_{\sigma_{2}}\right)\left(A_{1},\ldots,A_{m}\right)\right|\leq N^{C(\sigma_{1},\sigma_{2})},$ where the maximum is taken among all unitary matrices $A_{1},\ldots,A_{m}\in M_{N}(\mathbb{C})\otimes M_{N}(\mathbb{C})$. Here, for the graph $G_{\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k}}$ of the permutations, $M(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})$ is the maximum over blue-edge configurations of the number of directed cycles, and $C(\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{k})=\min_{G^{\prime}}R_{G^{\prime}}$, the minimum over full simple partial graphs $G^{\prime}$ (partial graphs keeping every rectangle and containing no directed cycle for any blue-edge configuration) of the number $R_{G^{\prime}}$ of colored edges removed to obtain $G^{\prime}$ (Definition 2.1).

body: In the mathematical field of graph theory, the Erdős–Rényi models are two closely related models for generating random graphs and the evolution of a random network. These models are named after Hungarian mathematicians Paul Erdős and Alfréd Rényi, who introduced one of the models in 1959. Edgar Gilbert introduced the other model contemporaneously with and independently of Erdős and Rényi. In the model of Erdős and Rényi, all graphs on a fixed vertex set with a fixed number of edges are equally likely. In the model introduced by Gilbert, also called the Erdős–Rényi–Gilbert model, each edge has a fixed probability of being present or absent, independently of the other edges. These models can be used in the probabilistic method to prove the existence of graphs satisfying various properties, or to provide a rigorous definition of what it means for a property to hold for almost all graphs.
title: Erdős–Rényi model

body: [Theorem thm: main left of arXiv:2411.04773, 'Meeting of squared Bessel flow lines and application to the skew Brownian motion'] The process $(U(r)-r,\, r\ge 0)$ is a homogeneous Feller process starting from $0$. For any $r>0$, $\frac{U(r)}{r}$ has distribution ${\mathcal B}(\frac{2-\widehat{\delta}+\delta}{2},\frac{\widehat{\delta}}{2})$. Conditionally on $U(0)=z>0$, the process $U$ stays constant then jumps at time $\mathrm{x}$ where  $\frac{{\mathrm x}}{z}$ has distribution ${\mathcal B}(1,\frac{\delta}{2})$. Conditionally on ${\mathrm x}=x$, $\frac{z-x}{U(x)-x}\sim {\mathcal B}(\frac{2-\widehat{\delta}+\delta}{2},1)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm: main left of arXiv:2411.04773

$$\underbrace{\mathfrak{S}_l\times\cdots\times \mathfrak{S}_l}_{m\text{ times}}:=\{\sigma\in\mathfrak{S}_n:\sigma(i)\equiv i\pmod m\quad\forall1\le i\le n\}$$
is a subgroup of $\mathfrak{S}_n$. 
Denote by $\sim_l\backslash U_{\mathfrak{S}_n}$ the uniform distribution over $\sim_l\backslash\mathfrak{S}_n$.

[Thm 24 of arXiv:2507.08909, 'Annealed almost periodic entropy'] The following hold:
	\begin{itemize}
		\item[a.] (Lower bound) If $Q$ is nonsingular and $O$ is any neighbourhood of $Q$ in $\rmM_{(k+\ell)+}$, then
		\[\frac{\vol_{2kn}T'(n,O)}{v(n)^k} \ge (\det S)^{n - o(n)}.\]

		\[\frac{\vol_{2kn}T'(n,O)}{v(n)^k} \le a^{n + o(n)}.\]

[Lemma 2 of arXiv:2606.24323, 'Conditioning of incoherent sub-dictionaries sampled from a coherent dictionary'] Let $g$ be a real-valued random variable on $\mathcal P([K])$, $S\subseteq [K]$ and $F\subseteq S$ with $\mu(F) = 0$. 
Let $A_F$ consist of all indices outside $S$ that are incoherent to the selected set $F$, that is, $A_F := \{ k \in S^c \mid \mu(F,k)=0\}$, 
then for any $r\in \R$
\begin{align*}
    \P_\mu(g(I) \geq r \mid I\cap S = F) = \P_\mu^{A_F}(g(I\cup F)\geq r).
\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 2 of arXiv:2606.24323

[Definition def:global-minimizer of arXiv:2608.30904, 'Entire monotone solutions of the anisotropic Allen--Cahn equation in dimension 5'] A function $u\in W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^4)$ is a \emph{global minimizer} of
$E_\varepsilon$ if, for every bounded Lipschitz domain
$\Omega\Subset\mathbb R^4$,
\begin{equation}
E_\varepsilon(u;\Omega)\le E_\varepsilon(w;\Omega)
\end{equation}
for every $w$ such that $w-u\in W^{1,2}_0(\Omega).$
title: Global minimizer

body:
[Lemma 8 (Fourth moments for the cross-polytope) of arXiv:2605.11451, '2605.11451'] Let $X\sim \nu_{1,n}$ be uniform on $B_1^n$ and let $i\neq j$. Then
\begin{align}
 \E X_i^4
 &=\frac{24}{(n+1)(n+2)(n+3)(n+4)},\notag\\
 \E X_i^2X_j^2
 &=\frac{4}{(n+1)(n+2)(n+3)(n+4)}.
\end{align}
Consequently, for every $\theta\in\sphere$,
\begin{equation}
 \E\langle\theta,X\rangle^4
 =
 3\,\E X_1^2X_2^2+\bigl(\E X_1^4-3\,\E X_1^2X_2^2\bigr)\sum_{i=1}^n\theta_i^4,
\end{equation}
and the coefficient $\E X_1^4-3\,\E X_1^2X_2^2$ is strictly positive.

body:
[Theoremc 3 of arXiv:2609.02267, 'Locally Conformally Flat Manifolds with Positive Scalar Curvature: Kleinian Groups, Moduli'] Let $(M^{n}, g)$, $n \ge 4$, be a closed, connected, oriented, locally conformally flat manifold with scalar curvature
$\mathrm{Sc}_{g} \ge n(n-1)$, and assume that $(M^{n}, g)$ is not isometric to $(S^{n}, g_{st})$.
View its fundamental group $\pi_1(M)$ as a Kleinian group.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(1)] If $\pi_1(M)$ is elementary, then every smooth map of
nonzero degree $f\colon(M^{n},g)\to (S^{n},g_{st})$ has a
point $p\in M$ at which the pointwise Lipschitz constant of $f$ is
strictly greater than~$1$.
\item[(2)] If $\pi_1(M)$ is infinite (whether elementary or non-elementary),
then for the developing map
$\mathrm{dev} \colon (\widetilde{M}, \tilde g) \to (S^{n}, g_{st})$,
there exists a point $x \in \widetilde{M}$ such that the pointwise Lipschitz constant satisfies
$\mathrm{Lip}_{x}(\mathrm{dev}) > 1$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let U be a connected open subset of C and f : U → C holomorphic and not constant. Then f(V) is open for every open V ⊂ U. More precisely, if z0 is in U and f - f(z0) has a zero of order m ≥ 1 at z0, then for every sufficiently small r > 0 there is δ > 0 such that every w with 0 < |w - f(z0)| < δ has exactly m preimages (counted with multiplicity, in fact m distinct simple preimages when r is small enough) in the disk |z - z0| < r. Consequences: a nonconstant holomorphic function on a connected open set cannot have locally constant modulus, real part, or argument, and an injective holomorphic map has nonvanishing derivative and holomorphic inverse. Connectedness can be replaced by: f is nonconstant on every connected component of U.

[Defn 11 (Compound laws) of arXiv:2605.18751, '\mytitle'] Let $Q$ and $F$ be probability measures on $\N_0$ and $\N$, respectively.
  
  Define
\begin{equation}
  
X=\sum_{i=1}^N J_i
\end{equation}
	where $N$ has law $Q$, and $(J_i)_{i\ge 1}$ is a sequence of i.i.d. random variables with law $F$, each independent of $N$. 
  
  Let $q_n \coloneqq Q(\{n\})$.  Conditioning on $N$ gives
	\[
	\prob(X=k)=\sum_{n\ge0} q_n\,F^{*n}(\{k\}), \quad k\in\N_0, 
	\]
where \(F^{*0}\coloneqq \delta_0\) and \(F^{*n}\coloneqq F^{*(n-1)}*F\) for \(n\ge1\).

\left(\binom r2 -1\right)}}p,
\]
where
\[
\phi'=\beta_{{r\choose2}-2} \phi.
\]

$$\{\mu_t\}_{t>0}\quad:\quad \mu_s\boxplus\mu_t=\mu_{s+t}$$

Let H be a real or complex Hilbert space and a: H × H → K (K = ℝ or ℂ) a sesquilinear form (bilinear in the real case, linear in the first and conjugate linear in the second argument in the complex case) such that: (boundedness) |a(u, v)| ≤ C‖u‖‖v‖ for all u, v ∈ H with C < ∞; (coercivity) Re a(u, u) ≥ α‖u‖² for all u ∈ H with α > 0. Then for every continuous conjugate-linear functional F on H (equivalently every f ∈ H via F(v) = ⟨f, v⟩) there is a unique u ∈ H with a(u, v) = F(v) for all v ∈ H, and ‖u‖ ≤ ‖F‖/α. The solution map F ↦ u is bounded with norm at most 1/α. No symmetry of a is assumed; if a is Hermitian and coercive, the statement is exactly the Riesz representation theorem for the equivalent inner product a. The weaker hypothesis |a(u, u)| ≥ α‖u‖² also suffices. Standard use: for a bounded Lipschitz domain Ω, the form a(u, v) = ∫_Ω (A∇u·∇v̄ + b·∇u v̄ + c u v̄) on H = H_0^1(Ω) is bounded and coercive under uniform ellipticity of A, bounded b, c, and a smallness or sign condition making Re a(u,u) ≥ α‖u‖_{H^1}²; then the weak Dirichlet problem has a unique solution.
H is a Hilbert space (complete)
a is sesquilinear and bounded on all of H × H
a is coercive: Re a(u,u) ≥ α‖u‖² with α > 0, on the whole space H
F is a continuous (conjugate-)linear functional on H

[Proposition 3 of arXiv:2607.16017, 'On large networks of integrate-and-fire neurons with short-term synaptic plasticity'] The invariant probability measure $ \mu_\infty^\alpha ( \d v , \d x) $ has the following properties.
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item Let $\nu^\alpha_\infty( \d v) := \mu^\alpha_\infty(\d v, [0, 1])$ be the first marginal of $\mu^\alpha_\infty$ with respect to $v.$ This measure possesses a Lebesgue density $ \nu^\alpha_\infty ( v) ,$ and it holds that
			\[ \nu^\alpha_\infty(v) = \frac{\gamma(\alpha)}{b(v)+\alpha} \exp \left(-\int_0^v \frac{f(y)}{b(y) + \alpha} \d y \right) \indica{[0, \sigma_\alpha)}(v), \]
			where the normalizing factor $\gamma(\alpha)$ satisfies $\gamma(\alpha) = \int_{\R \times [0, 1]} f(v) \mu^\alpha_\infty(\d v, \d x)$.
		\item Let $M^\alpha(v) := \lim_{t \rightarrow \infty} \E [ X^\alpha_t~|~ V^\alpha_t = v]$. 
			Then
			\[ M^\alpha(v) = 1 - C^\alpha \exp \left( - \frac{1}{\tau} \int_0^v \frac{\d u}{b(u)+ \alpha} \right), \]
            where the constant $C^\alpha$ is given by 
            \begin{equation}
            C^\alpha = U \left( 1 -  (1-U) \int_0^\infty f(\varphi^\alpha_t(0)) \exp \left(-\int_0^t f(\varphi^\alpha_u(0)) \d u \right) e^{-\frac{t}{\tau}} \d t \right)^{-1} .
            \end{equation}
		\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 3 of arXiv:2607.16017

[Definition 20 (joint typical subspace) of arXiv:2609.03736, '2609.03736'] For the operators associated with $(K,L)$, put
$z_n=z_{n,a_n}$ and $q_n=q_{n,a_n}$.
Since $q_n$ is $\mathfrak S_n$-equivariant, it defines the pointwise
multiplier
\begin{equation}
 (\widehat q_nf)(b\mathfrak S_n)
 =bq_nb^{-1}f(b\mathfrak S_n).
 
\end{equation}
Put $E_n=q_n(\CC^m)^{\otimes n}$ and
\begin{equation}
 p_n=z_n\widehat q_n.
 
\end{equation}
The range of $p_n$ is the \emph{joint typical subspace}.  Equivalently,
it is the $z_n$-isotypic summand of
$\Ind_{\mathfrak S_n}^{\mathsf B_n}E_n$, represented inside the full Fourier
model.  Let $\Omega_n$ denote its set of $\mathsf B_n$-types and let
$\Theta_n$ be the map induced by $\mathsf S_{t_n}$ on this summand.

or equivalently
$$
\mathbb{P}_{\operatorname{YM}}^{\operatorname{free}}\left(\mathbf{Hol}(\partial \blacksquare)\in d\mathrm{g}\right)=p_{\upsilon(\blacksquare)}(\mathrm{g})\mu_G(d\mathrm{g}).
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Dfn 20 of arXiv:2507.08909, 'Annealed almost periodic entropy'] A \textbf{partial positive semidefinite} matrix with \textbf{block sizes} $k$, $\ell$ and $m$ is a $5$-tuple
	\[(Q_{11},Q_{12},Q_{22},Q_{23},Q_{33}) \in \rmM_{k+} \times \rmM_{k,\ell}\times \rmM_{\ell+} \times \rmM_{\ell,m}\times \rmM_{m+}\]
	with the property that both of the two-by-two-block matrices
	\[\left[\begin{array}{cc} Q_{11} & Q_{12}\\ Q_{12}^\ast & Q_{22}\end{array}\right] \qquad \hbox{and} \qquad \left[\begin{array}{cc} Q_{22} & Q_{23}\\ Q_{23}^\ast & Q_{33}\end{array}\right]\]
	are positive semidefinite.
	
	A partial positive semidefinite matrix is \textbf{partially nonsingular} if both of those two-by-two-block matrices are nonsingular; otherwise it is \textbf{partially singular}.
	
	We write $\PPSD_{k,\ell,m}$ for the space of partial positive semidefinite matrices with block sizes $k$, $\ell$ and $m$, and $\PPSD^\circ_{k,\ell,m}$ for the further subset of its partially nonsingular members.
title: Definition 20 of arXiv:2507.08909

[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2506.22085, '2506.22085'] For each $T>0$ and $\mu_0,\mu_1$ we have
  $V_T(\mu_0,\mu_1)=\ms V_T(\mu_0,\mu_1)$.\hfill\break
  Let also $\pi^*$ be a minimizer for \emph{(HSP')} and denote by
  $\rho^*= (\rho^*_t)_{t\in[0,T]}$ the corresponding density with
  conjugated momentum $H^*= (H^*_t)_{t\in[0,T]}$ that we recall solve the system of equations \eqref{caneq}.
  Then a minimizer for \emph{(HSP)} is $(\pi^*,\ms J^*)$ where $\ms J^*$ is
  represented by $-D_\mathrm{h}(\rho^*)\nabla\rho^* +
  2\sigma(\rho^*)\nabla H^* $.
  Furthermore, a minimizer to \emph{(MSP)} is provided by $R^*$, the law of
  the time-inhomogeneous Markov diffusion with time dependent
  generator
  \begin{equation}
    
    L^*_t = \nabla\cdot D_\mathrm{s} (\rho^*_t) \nabla 
    +
    \Big\{
    \big[ D_\mathrm{s} (\rho^*_t) -  D_\mathrm{h} (\rho^*_t)\big]
    \frac {\nabla \rho^*_t}{\rho^*_t} 
    + 2 \frac {\sigma(\rho^*_t)}{\rho^*_t} \nabla H^*_t \Big\}\cdot \nabla
  \end{equation}
  and initial condition $R^*_0 =\mu_0$.\hfill\break
  Conversely, if $R^*$ is a minimizer to \emph{(MSP)} then $R^*$ is Markovian,
  $R^*=P(R^*)$ and the family of its 
  single time marginals $(R^*_t)_{t\in[0,T]}$ is a minimizer to \emph{(HSP')}.
  Furthermore, letting $R^*_t=\rho^*_t \,dx$, $t\in[0,T]$, the
  external field $E^*=E^{R^*}$ associated to $R^*$ has the form
  $E^* =\nabla H^*$ and the pair $(\rho^*,H^*)$ solves weakly the
  canonical equations \eqref{caneq}. Finally  $(\pi^*,\ms J^*)$, where $\pi^*$ has density $\rho^*$ and $\ms J^*$ is
  represented by $-D_\mathrm{h}(\rho^*)\nabla\rho^* +
  2\sigma(\rho^*)\nabla H^* $, is a minimizer for \emph{(HSP)}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 9 (Strict anisotropic logarithmic barrier) of arXiv:2609.03916, 'Halfspace Theorems for Anisotropic Minimal Surfaces and Perimeter Minimizers'] There exist constants $C_*=C_*(\Phi)>0$, $a_0=a_0(\Phi)>0$, and
$c_*=c_*(\Phi)>0$ such that, for every $a\in(0,a_0)$, the function
\begin{equation}
  b(x)
  :=-a\log\rho(x)+C_*a^2\big(\rho(x)^{-1}-1\big),
  \qquad \rho(x)\ge1,
\end{equation}
satisfies
\begin{align}
 b&=0 &&\text{on }\{\rho=1\},\\
 b&<0,\qquad \lim_{\rho\to\infty}b=-\infty,
   &&\text{on }\{\rho>1\},\\
 \Phiop[b]&\ge c_*a^2\rho^{-3}>0
   &&\text{on }\{\rho>1\}.
\end{align}
Moreover, $|Db|$ is uniformly small when $a_0$ is chosen sufficiently small.

[Dfn 17 ({\cite[Definition 2.3.1) of arXiv:2605.27974, 'Discrete approximation of semi-Dirichlet forms with non-symmetric perturbations of resista'] {kigami2001analysis}}]
Let $X$ be a set, $\mathcal{F}$ a subspace of $l(X)$ containing all the constant functions on 
$X$, and $\mathcal{E} \colon \mathcal{F} \times \mathcal{F} \rightarrow \R$ a bilinear form. 
Then, $(\mathcal{E},\mathcal{F})$ is called a resistance form on $X$ if the following hold:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[$\mathrm{(RF1)}$]
$\mathcal{E}(g,f)=\mathcal{E}(f,g)$ and $\mathcal{E}(f,f) \geq 0$ for $f,g \in \mathcal{F}$. 
Also, $\mathcal{E}(f,f)=0$ if and only if $f$ is a constant function.
\item[$\mathrm{(RF2)}$]
$\left( \mathcal{F}/ {\sim}, \mathcal{E} \right)$ is a Hilbert space, where 
$\sim$ is an equivalence relation on $\mathcal{F}$ defined by 
$f \sim g$ if $f-g$ is a constant function.
\item[$\mathrm{(RF3)}$]
For any finite subset $V \subset X$ and $f^{\prime} \in l(V)$, there exists some
$f \in \mathcal{F}$ such that $f \lvert_{V} =f^{\prime}$ holds.
\item[$\mathrm{(RF4)}$]
For any $x,y \in X$, we have 
\begin{align}
    R(x,y) \coloneqq \sup \left\{\frac{\abs{f(x)-f(y)}^{2}}{\mathcal{E}(f)} \middle |
    f \in \mathcal{F},f \, \text{is not constant}\right\} < \infty.
\end{align}
\item[$\mathrm{(RF5)}$]
For any $f \in \mathcal{F}$, we have $0 \vee f \wedge 1 \in \mathcal{F}$ and 
$\mathcal{E}(0 \vee f \wedge 1)\leq \mathcal{E}(f)$.
\end{enumerate}
Then, $R$ in $\mathrm{(RF4)}$ is a metric on $X$, called the resistance metric associated 
with $(\mathcal{E},\mathcal{F})$.

In what follows, $(\mathcal{E},\mathcal{F})$ is a resistance form on $X$ and $V$ is a non-empty finite subset of $X$.

[Corollary 7 (Estimate of Extinction Time in  Exponential Ages Distribution) of arXiv:2608.04716, 'Extinction Time Estimate for Subcritical (Binary) Homogeneous Crump-Mode-Jagers Processes'] Consider a birth death process with birth and death rates $\lambda$ and $\mu$.  Assume that $\lambda /\mu<1$ (subcritical case). 
	Assume Malthusian parameter $\alpha=\lambda-\mu$ exists.  We consider a sequence of initial configurations  indexed by $k\in \N$. For each configuration $k$, the initial population is given by a  non-negative, random integer-valued measure $Z_k$ on $\R_+$, where $Z_k(r)$ represents the number of individuals with age in the interval $[0,r]$ at time zero.   

	Let
	\[D:=1-\lambda /\mu.\]
	Let $T_k$ be the extinction time for configuration $k$. Then, as $k\to \infty$, the random variables $$-\alpha  T_k-\log( M_k)-\log(D)$$ converges in distribution to a Gumbel random variable $Z$ with distribution function $\P(Z\leq r)=e^{-e^{-r}}$. In other words, 
	\[\lim_{k\to \infty}\P(-\alpha  T_k-\log( M_k)-\log(D)\leq r)=e^{-e^{-r}}.\]

TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). For the product measure mu_p on {0,1}^E with each coordinate independently open with probability p and an increasing event A depending on finitely many edges, Russo's formula states d/dp mu_p(A) = sum_{e in E} mu_p(e is pivotal for A), where e is pivotal for A at a configuration omega if flipping the state of e changes the indicator of A. When different edges carry different parameters p_e, the analogous statement is d/dp_e mu(A) = mu(e is pivotal for A). This identity converts questions about how quickly an event's probability crosses a threshold into questions about counting or bounding pivotal edges, which is the basic engine behind sharp-threshold theorems when combined with the Margulis-Russo framework and tools such as hypercontractivity, the Benjamini-Kalai-Schramm influence bound, or the OSSS inequality. Russo's formula does not by itself give sharp thresholds; it requires monotonicity of A, since non-monotone events need a more complex signed-pivotal generalization; and it is stated for independent-coordinate measures, so applying it to dependent measures such as the random-cluster model requires a separate Glauber-dynamics-based generalization rather than the naive product-measure formula. Typical failure: Using Russo's formula on a non-monotone event without its signed-pivotal generalization, or applying the plain product-measure version of the formula to a dependent measure such as a random-cluster or Ising Gibbs measure, where the correct analogue requires the generator of an associated Glauber dynamics rather than a simple coordinatewise derivative; both errors produce a derivative formula that looks structurally similar but is simply wrong. Canonical reference: Russo, 1981, Zeitschrift fur Wahrscheinlichkeitstheorie und verwandte Gebiete; Margulis, 1974, Problemy Peredachi Informatsii; Grimmett, Percolation, second edition, 1999, Springer, Chapter 2.

A is a monotone (increasing) event depending on finitely many coordinates

[Prp 21 of arXiv:2608.30763, 'Ultracontractivity of heat semigroups with non-local Robin boundary conditions via two-sid'] Define the operator $L(A, B) = \tilde{L}(A, B) - \lambda_{0}$ in $\mathrm{L}^{2}\left( \Omega \right)$ on the domain 
$D \left( L(A, B) \right) = D ( \tilde{L}(A, B) )$. Then $L(A, B)$ satisfies the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}[i.)]
\item $L(A, B)$ is associated with the form $a(A, B)$, i.e.
$$
a(A, B)(u, \varphi) =  \langle L(A, B)u, \varphi \rangle_{\mathrm{L}^{2}\left( \Omega \right)}
$$
holds for every $u \in D ( L(A, B) )$ and every $\varphi \in D \left( a(A, B) \right)$.
\item $-L(A, B)$ generates the $C_{0}$-semigroup 
$\mathrm{e}^{t\lambda_{0}}\mathrm{e}^{-t\tilde{L}(A, B)}$
on $\mathrm{L}^{2}\left( \Omega \right)$. We write $\mathrm{e}^{-tL(A, B)}$ for 
$\mathrm{e}^{t\lambda_{0}}\mathrm{e}^{-t\tilde{L}(A, B)}$ at every time $t \geq 0$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

        &\mathds{E}[M_n] = \frac{1}{2} \sum_{e \in E} \sum_{\substack{e' \in E\backslash\{e\}:\\\delta_{e'}=\delta_e}} \frac{(n\mathds{E}[d_U^{\textnormal{out}}]-2\delta_e^{\textnormal{tail}})!(n\mathds{E}[d_U^{\textnormal{in}}]-2\delta_e^{\textnormal{head}})!}{(n\mathds{E}[d_U^{\textnormal{out}}])!(n\mathds{E}[d_U^{\textnormal{in}}])!}\\
        &\hspace{1cm}\times \sum_{\substack{\vb*{a} \in \mathds{N}^{\delta_e^{\textnormal{tail}}}:\\\sum_{i=1}^{\delta_e^{\textnormal{tail}}}ia_i = \delta_e^{\textnormal{tail}}}}  \frac{\delta_e^{\textnormal{tail}}!^2}{\prod_{k=1}^{\delta_e^{\textnormal{tail}}} k!^{2a_k} }
        \sum_{\alpha(\cdot) \in R(\vb*{a})} (-1)^{\sum_{\vb*{x} \in \mathds{N}^{\delta_e^{\textnormal{tail}}}} (\sum_{i=1}^{\delta_e^{\textnormal{tail}}} x_i - 1)\alpha(\vb*{x})} \\
     &\hspace{1cm}\times 
    \prod_{\vb*{y} \in \mathds{N}^{\delta_e^{\textnormal{tail}}}} \Bigg( \frac{1}{\alpha(\vb*{y})!} \Big(\frac{n\mathds{E}\big[\prod_{i=1}^{\delta_e^{\textnormal{tail}}} (\mathds{1}_{\{d_U^{\textnormal{out}} \geq 2i\}}\frac{d_U^{\textnormal{out}}!}{(d_U^{\textnormal{out}}-2i)!})^{y_i} \big]\big(\sum_{i=1}^{\delta_e^{\textnormal{tail}}} y_i-1 \big)!}{\prod_{i=1}^{\delta_e^{\textnormal{tail}}} y_i!} \Big)^{\alpha(\vb*{y})} \Bigg)\\
    &\hspace{1cm}\times \sum_{\substack{\vb*{b} \in \mathds{N}^{\delta_e^{\textnormal{head}}}:\\\sum_{i=1}^{\delta_e^{\textnormal{head}}}ib_i = \delta_e^{\textnormal{head}}}}  \frac{\delta_e^{\textnormal{head}}!^2}{\prod_{k=1}^{\delta_e^{\textnormal{head}}} k!^{2b_k} }\sum_{\beta(\cdot) \in R(\vb*{b})} (-1)^{\sum_{\vb*{x} \in \mathds{N}^{\delta_e^{\textnormal{head}}}} (\sum_{i=1}^{\delta_e^{\textnormal{head}}} x_i - 1)\beta(\vb*{x})}\\
     &\hspace{1cm}\times
    \prod_{\vb*{z} \in \mathds{N}^{\delta_e^{\textnormal{head}}}} \Bigg( \frac{1}{\beta(\vb*{z})!} \Big(\frac{n\mathds{E}\big[\prod_{i=1}^{\delta_e^{\textnormal{head}}} (\mathds{1}_{\{d_U^{\textnormal{in}} \geq 2i\}}\frac{d_U^{\textnormal{in}}!}{(d_U^{\textnormal{in}}-2i)!})^{z_i} \big]\big(\sum_{i=1}^{\delta_e^{\textnormal{head}}} z_i-1 \big)!}{\prod_{i=1}^{\delta_e^{\textnormal{head}}} z_i!} \Big)^{\beta(\vb*{z})} \Bigg).
    \end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem 39 (Identification of the Hilbert--Stein and primitive--Fock splittings) of arXiv:2608.12492, 'Weak Limits of Wiener Chaos: Primitive--Fock Classification and Hilbert--Stein Extraction'] Let
\[
 X_{n,a}=I_q(f_{n,a}),
 \qquad
 \sup_n\sum_{a=1}^{d}q!\norm{f_{n,a}}^2<\infty,
\]
choose $R>0$ with
$R^2\ge\sup_n\sum_aq!\norm{f_{n,a}}^2$, and run the spectrally reduced
feedback on $x_{n,a,q}=\sqrt{q!}\,f_{n,a}$ from the zero module.  Along every
subsequence on which the covariance and all the finitely many proper
self-contraction norms converge, one may extract a further subsequence
and choose a sufficiently slow diagonal $J(n)\to\infty$ such that, with
the corresponding active and
residual Wiener polynomials $A_n^{[J(n)]},B_n^{[J(n)]}$,
\[
 (A_n^{[J(n)]},B_n^{[J(n)]})
 \Longrightarrow(A_{\mathrm{FF}},G_{\mathrm{prim}}),
 \qquad X_n\Longrightarrow A_{\mathrm{FF}}+G_{\mathrm{prim}},
 \qquad
 G_{\mathrm{prim}}\indep A_{\mathrm{FF}}.
\]
If $\xi_a=[f_{n,a}]_{\mathcal U}\in\cH_q$, then, in the terminal
primitive--Fock representation,
\begin{align}
 A_{\mathrm{FF},a}
 &=\mathbb U_q^{-1}P_{\cD_q}\xi_a,
 \\
 G_{\mathrm{prim},a}
 &=\mathbb U_q^{-1}P_{\cK_q}\xi_a.
 
\end{align}
The second term belongs to the first Gaussian chaos over $\cK_q$; the
first is the orthogonal sum of all weighted sectors containing at least
two primitive particles.  In particular the split is intrinsic relative
to the represented packet and ultrafilter, and
\begin{equation}
 \Cov(G_{\mathrm{prim}})_{ab}
 =\ip{P_{\cK_q}\xi_a}{P_{\cK_q}\xi_b}_{\cH_q}
 =q!\,\Ulim\ip{p_{n,a}}{p_{n,b}},
 
\end{equation}
where $(p_{n,a})$ is any bounded representative of
$P_{\cK_q}\xi_a$.

body:
[Theorem thm:sine-gordon of arXiv:2607.24705, 'Derangetropy Operators'] Let $w$ be a kernel and
		$\varphi_{w} := A_{w} - \mathrm{id}$ its reaction.
		\begin{enumerate}[label=\normalfont(\roman*), leftmargin=*]
			\item If $f$ solves the diffusive
			equation~(equation eq:flow-diffusion of the paper) with kernel $w$ and integrable
			data, then $F$ solves the local semilinear equation
			\begin{equation}
				\partial_{t}F = D\,\partial_{xx}F + \varphi_{w}(F),
				\qquad
				\varphi_{w}(u) = \int_{0}^{u}\big(w(s) - 1\big)\,ds,
				
			\end{equation}
			and conversely; for the canonical kernel
			$\varphi(u) = -\sin(2\pi u)/(2\pi)$, so the angular variable
			$v = 2\pi F$ solves the overdamped sine--Gordon equation
			$\partial_{t}v = D\,\partial_{xx}v - \sin v$.
			\item For every $F_{0} \in \mathcal{M}$ the
			equation~(equation eq:cdf-equation of the paper) has a unique global solution,
			smooth for positive times, monotone in $x$ with values in $[0,1]$
			and limits $0, 1$ preserved for all time: laws evolve to laws, mass
			and positivity being conserved automatically.
			\item The dynamics is monotone for first-order stochastic
			dominance: $F_{0} \le G_{0}$ pointwise implies
			$F_{t} \le G_{t}$ for all $t$, the diffusive extension of the
			order-preservation of the operators themselves, which is the
			monotonicity of the transport maps $A_{w}$.
			\item As $D \to 0$, solutions converge locally uniformly on
			compact time intervals to the diffusionless flow; for the canonical
			kernel, to the exact solution~(equation eq:exact-solution of the paper).
		\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Reduction and well-posedness on laws

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2511.10535, 'Eigenvalues of Brownian Motions on $\mathrm{GL}(N,\mathbb{C})$'] Let $\rho>0$, $\zeta\in\mathbb{C}$ with $|\zeta|\leq \rho$, and let $B = B_{\rho,\zeta}$ denote a Brownian motion on $\mathrm{GL}(N,\mathbb{C})$, see \eqref{eq.B.SDE.rho.zeta}.  Let $B_0$ be a random matrix in $\mathrm{GL}(N,\mathbb{C})$ independent from the process $B$ and suppose that $B_0$ converges a.s.\ in $\ast$-distribution (see Definition \ref{def.*-dist}) to an operator $b_0$ as $N\to\infty$.

Then for fixed $t>0$, a.s.\ as $N\to\infty$, the empirical law $\mu_{B_0 B(t)}$ of eigenvalues of the Brownian motion $B_0 B(t)$ converges weakly to a deterministic measure $\mu_{b_0,t}$ (see Definition \ref{def:mub0t} and Section \ref{sect.Brown(ian).meas} below). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm 4 of arXiv:2604.03548, 'Degree-preserving conservative processes and a unified approach for their hydrodynamics'] Under Assumptions \ref{assmp:generator_element_basic} and \ref{assumption:second_order_polymonial}, we have $\mathsf{a} \neq 0$, and there exist constants $v_0, v_1, v_2 \in\mathbb R$ such that $\mathrm{Var}_{\nu_\rho}[\eta_0]=v_2\rho^2+v_1\rho+v_0$ for any $\rho \in \overline{\rho} (I^{o})$, satisfying the relations 
\begin{equation*}
v_2= -\mathsf{b}/(2\mathsf{a})-1 ,\quad 
v_1=  -{\mathsf{c}}/{\mathsf{a}} \quad\text{ and }\quad 
v_0= -{\mathsf{d}}/({2\mathsf{a}}), 
\end{equation*}
for $\mathsf{a},\mathsf{b},\mathsf{c}, \mathsf{d}$ given in \textnormal{(A6.2)}.
Moreover, up to constant shifts and scaling (that is, up to an affine transformation $A\eta_0+B$ with constants $A$ and $B$), the marginal distribution of $\eta_0$ is given by either normal, Poisson, gamma, binomial, negative-binomial or the generalized hyperbolic secant distribution where the parameters $v_0,v_1$ and $v_2$ are given by 
$
(v_2,v_1,v_0)=(0,0,1), (0,1,0), (s,0,0),(-1/{\kappa},1,0), (s,1,0)$ or $(s,0,1),
$
respectively, where $s>0$ and $\kappa \in \mathbb N$.

body: [Corollary 2 of arXiv:2506.16484, 'Stochastic Heat Flow is a Black Noise'] We have that $(Z^\eps,\xi^\eps)\Rightarrow (Z,\xi)$ in law as $\eps\to0$, under the product topology of $C(\R^2_{\leq}, M_+(\R^4))\times \mathcal{S}'(\R^2)$, where $Z$ is independent of $\xi$.

In a finite resistor network whose contracted intermediate interfaces yield a series chain of independently wired layer networks, the sum of those wired layer resistances is at most the original effective resistance. Rayleigh monotonicity alone cannot justify the opposite upper bound. On s-a-t and s-b-t with resistances (1,M) and (M,1), respectively, the original resistance is (M+1)/2 and the wired layer sum is 2M/(M+1). Their ratio (M+1)^2/(4M) is unbounded. To upper-bound the original resistance using layer flows, the interface current distributions must match. This does not identify a DGFF limiting law or refute an upper bound constructed using matched flows.
Finite positive-resistance network
Wired layer terminal minima
Contracted quotient is a series chain

[Proposition 70 (Entrance-to-Rees bridge) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] Let \((X,A,Q)\) be a \(\beta\)-controlled critical second-order entrance.
Then its geometricized second level
\begin{equation}
 {\mathbf X}^{(2)}_{s,t}
 :=\left(1,X_{s,t},\tfrac12X_{s,t}^{\otimes2}+A_{s,t}\right)
 
\end{equation}
is multiplicative.  After one deterministic spatial rescaling and a fixed
renormalization of the control, it belongs to
\(\mathfrak C_\beta^{\mathrm{crit}}(T)\).  The collision coordinate \(Q\)
is a trace-class decoration and does not alter the positive critical cost.
The construction commutes with bounded spatial maps, optional evaluation,
and ucp projection limits.

body: In mathematics, the well-ordering theorem, also known as Zermelo's theorem, states that every set can be well-ordered. A set X is well-ordered by a strict total order if every non-empty subset of X has a least element under the ordering. The well-ordering theorem together with Zorn's lemma are the most important mathematical statements that are equivalent to the axiom of choice. Ernst Zermelo introduced the axiom of choice as an "unobjectionable logical principle" to prove the well-ordering theorem. One can conclude from the well-ordering theorem that every set is susceptible to transfinite induction, which is considered by mathematicians to be a powerful technique.
title: Well-ordering theorem

body: [Lemma lma:detection of arXiv:2608.26564, 'Real ideal points, Conway spheres, and left-orderable Dehn fillings'] Let $\xi = (\chi_1, \chi_2) \in V_S(M_1, M_2)$ be a branch-admissible non-realized limiting gluing datum, where each $\chi_i$ is the character of an irreducible representation $\rho_i: \pi_1(M_i) \to SL_2(\mathbb{C})$. Then there exists an irreducible algebraic curve $\mathcal X \subset X(M)$ and an ideal point of its smooth projective model such that the limiting characters on $\pi_1(M_i)$ are $\chi_i$. If the restrictions $\rho_1|_{\pi_1(S)}$ and $\rho_2|_{\pi_1(S)}$ are not conjugate, then this ideal point detects $S$.

[Thm 2 of arXiv:2603.28702, 'Distribution of the magnetization of the critical Ising model on sparse random graphs'] Consider the Ising model on a graph $G\sim G(n,d/n)$ (for $d>1$) at the critical temperature, $\beta_c=\tanh^{-1}(d^{-1})$. Let $\mu_n\in\mathcal{M}_1(\R)$ be the random measure defined as 
$$\mu_n(A):=\PR(m\cdot n^{-3/4}\in A\ |\ G), \ \text{with}\ G\sim G(n,d/n).$$
Then, there exists a random measure $\mu\in\mathcal{M}_1(\R)$ such that $\mu_n\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}\mu$ in the Wasserstein distance associated to $\text{d}_{\text{KS}}$. Moreover, the measure $\mu$ is given by $\mu=\mu^{(X)}$, where for $x\in\R$,
$$\mu^{(x)}(A)=\dfrac{\int_A\exp\left(\frac{x}{\sqrt{2(d-1)}}\cdot u^2-\left(\frac{1}{4(d-1)}+\frac{1}{12}\right)\cdot u^4\right) \ \text{d}u}{\int_\R\exp\left(\frac{x}{\sqrt{2(d-1)}}\cdot u^2-\left(\frac{1}{4(d-1)}+\frac{1}{12}\right)\cdot u^4\right) \ \text{d}u},$$
and $X\sim N(0,1)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

i.e. the limit distribution is uniform on $\{1,\ldots,c\}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:cv:cov of arXiv:2607.20956, 'Sharp moduli of continuity for Gaussian fields and stochastic PDEs via correlation bounds'] Let $Y$ and $Z$ be centered jointly Gaussian random variables. 
Let $C_0 \in [0\,,1]$ and consider the following statements:
\begin{enumerate}[$(a)$]
    \item $\Var(Y|Z) \ge C_0 \Var(Y)$;\smallskip
    \item $|\mathbb{E}[YZ]| \le \sqrt{1-C_0} \, \|Y\|_2 \|Z\|_2$;\smallskip
    \item $\mathbb{E}[YZ] \le \sqrt{1-C_0} \, \|Y\|_2 \|Z\|_2$.\smallskip
\end{enumerate}
We have $(a) \Leftrightarrow (b) \Rightarrow (c)$.
title: Lemma lem:cv:cov of arXiv:2607.20956

Let n >= 2, Omega in R^n open, and let A be a measurable matrix field with lambda|xi|^2 <= A(x)xi.xi and |A(x)xi.eta| <= Lambda|xi||eta| for a.e. x in Omega and all xi, eta (0 < lambda <= Lambda; A need not be symmetric or continuous). Let u in H^1_loc(Omega) be a weak solution of div(A grad u) = 0 in Omega. Then u has a representative that is locally Hoelder continuous: there exist alpha in (0,1) and C, depending only on n and the ellipticity ratio Lambda/lambda, such that for every ball B_R(x0) contained in Omega, (a) ess sup over B_{R/2}(x0) of |u| <= C (average over B_R(x0) of u^2)^{1/2}, and (b) |u(x) - u(y)| <= C (|x-y|/R)^alpha (average over B_R(x0) of u^2)^{1/2} for all x, y in B_{R/2}(x0). Part (a) also holds for subsolutions with u replaced by u^+. In general alpha cannot be taken close to 1, and u need not be Lipschitz; the statement is for scalar equations and fails for systems.

body:
[Lemma lem:reduction of arXiv:2506.06559, 'Bi-infinite incipient cluster in high dimensions'] Let $G$ be a finite connected simple graph, $S \subset V(G)$, $|S| = 3$. 
Assume that $G$ is 3-connected to $S$, all $v \in V(G) \setminus S$ have degree $3$, and all elements of
$S$ have degree at most $2$.
If $x,y\in V(G)\setminus S$, $\{x,y\} \in E(G)$ but $\{x,y\}$ is not strongly H-reducible, then there exists
a subgraph $G'$ of $G$ and a subset $S' \subset V(G')$ such that the following hold.
\begin{itemize}
    \item[(i)] $G'$ has fewer edges than $G$, and $|S'| = 3$.
    \item[(ii)] Either $y \in S'$ and $x \in V(G') \setminus S'$, or vice versa.
    \item[(iii)] $G'$ is simple, connected, all its vertices not in $S'$ have degree $3$, and all 
    $s' \in S'$ have degree $1$ in $G'$.
    \item[(iv)] $G'$ is 3-connected to $S'$.
    \item[(v)] $V(G') \setminus S'$ contains at least $2$ neighbouring vertices.
\end{itemize}

[Lemma 15 of arXiv:2609.02193, 'State-law dynamics of McKean-Vlasov stochastic reaction-diffusion equations on $\mathbb R^'] Let $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$, $\omega\in\Omega_0$, $x\in H$ and $\mu\in P$. Then equation~\eqref{Eq4-trans} with $\eta=\ell^\epsilon_\mu$ and initial datum $x-\epsilon z(\omega)$ has a unique pathwise variational solution
	\begin{align*}
		v_{\ell^\epsilon_\mu}(\cdot,\omega;
		x-\epsilon z(\omega))
		\in
		C([0,T];H)\cap L^2(0,T;V)
		\cap L^p(0,T;L^p(\mathbb R^n))
	\end{align*}
	for every $T>0$. Consequently,
	\begin{align}
		\varphi^\epsilon_H(t,\omega,x,\mu)
		=
		v_{\ell^\epsilon_\mu}
		(t,\omega;x-\epsilon z(\omega))
		+\epsilon z(\theta_t\omega)
	\end{align}
	is well defined. The map
	$(t,\omega,x,\mu)\mapsto\varphi^\epsilon_H(t,\omega,x,\mu)$ is jointly measurable, and, for all $x,y\in H$ and $\mu,\nu\in P$,
	\begin{align}
		\|\varphi^\epsilon_H(t,\omega,x,\mu)
		-\varphi^\epsilon_H(t,\omega,y,\nu)\|^2
		&\leq
		e^{-\bar\gamma t}\|x-y\|^2
		+L_G\int_0^t e^{-\bar\gamma(t-r)}
		\mathcal W_2^2\big(
		\varphi^\epsilon_P(r)\mu,
		\varphi^\epsilon_P(r)\nu
		\big)dr
		\notag\\
		&\leq
		e^{-\bar\gamma t}\|x-y\|^2
		+\big(e^{(L_G-\bar\gamma)t}-e^{-\bar\gamma t}\big)
		\mathcal W_2^2(\mu,\nu).
	\end{align}
	In particular, $(x,\mu)\mapsto\varphi^\epsilon_H(t,\omega,x,\mu)$ is continuous from $H\times P$ to $H$ for every $t\geq0$ and $\omega\in\Omega_0$.

body: [Theorem 10 of arXiv:2609.03793, 'Typical martingale diverges on a co-$\sigma$-porous set'] Let $(S, \zeta)$ be a metric space, $\mathcal B(S)$ its Borel $\sigma$-algebra, and $\mu$ a probability measure on $\mathcal B(S)$. Assume that every non-empty open set in $(S, \zeta)$ has non-zero measure. Then for every non-empty open set $U\subset S$, any martingale $\f$ on $(S, \mathcal B(S),\mu)$ that is $L^p$-bounded for some $p\in[1,\infty]$ converges at some element of $U$ (i.e., the set of convergence points of $\f$ is dense in $S$).

body: [Theo 21 of arXiv:2602.14618, 'Finitary coding and Gaussian concentration\\ for random fields'] For the ferromagnetic nearest-neighbor Ising model in dimension $d\ge2$, Gaussian concentration holds in the uniqueness regime. In the phase coexistence regime $\beta\ge\beta_c(d)$, it fails for every shift-invariant ergodic Gibbs measure. More precisely, for $\beta<\beta_c(d)$, the unique Gibbs measure $\nu_\beta$ satisfies Gaussian concentration, whereas for $\beta\ge\beta_c(d)$ no shift-invariant ergodic Gibbs measure satisfies Gaussian concentration.
title: Theo 21 of arXiv:2602.14618

  $(\mathcal{A}, \varphi^{(0)})$ is a non-commutative probability space and
  $\varphi^{(i)} : \mathcal{A} \rightarrow \mathbb{C}$ are linear functionals
  such that $\varphi^{(i)} (1_{\mathcal{A}}) = 0$, for every $i = 1, \ldots,
  \nu$. The infinitesimal non-commutative distribution of order $n$ of $a \in
  \mathcal{A}$ is the $(n + 1)$-tuple $(\mu_a^{(i)} : \mathbb{C} \langle
  \mathbf{x} \rangle \rightarrow \mathbb{C})_{i = 0}^n$ of linear functionals,
  defined by
  \[ \mu_a^{(i)} (P) = \varphi^{(i)} (P (a)) \text{, \quad for every } P \in
     \mathbb{C} \langle \mathbf{x} \rangle \text{ and } i = 0, \ldots, \nu .
  \]

body: [Lemma lem-lf-resample-i-infty of arXiv:2411.19810, 'Radial conformal welding in Liouville quantum gravity'] Let $\alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{R}$. Suppose $\psi \sim \mathrm{LF}_\mathbb{H}^{(\alpha, i), (\beta, \infty)}$. If $U$ is a deterministic bounded neighborhood of $i$ disjoint from $\mathbb{R}$, then conditioned on $\psi|_{\mathbb{H} \backslash U}$, we have $\psi|_U \stackrel d= h + \mathfrak h + \alpha G_U(\cdot , i)$ where $h$ is a GFF on $U$ with zero boundary conditions, $\mathfrak h$ is the harmonic extension of $\psi|_{\mathbb{H} \backslash U}$ to $U$, and $G_U$ is the Green function of $h$. If instead $U$ is a deterministic neighborhood of $\infty$ bounded away from $i$, then conditioned on $\psi|_{\mathbb{H} \backslash U}$, we have $\psi|_U \stackrel d= h + \mathfrak h + (\frac\beta2 - Q) G_U(\cdot, \infty)$ where $h$ is a GFF on $U$ with zero (resp.\ free) boundary conditions on $\partial U \cap \mathbb{H}$ (resp.\ $\partial U \cap \mathbb{R}$), $\mathfrak h$ is the harmonic extension of $\psi|_{\mathbb{H} \backslash U}$ to $U$ with zero normal derivative on $\partial U \cap \mathbb{R}$, and $G_U$ is the Green function for $h$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Own-work draft; STATUS: proof (unaudited). Independent review pending. No novelty or target-completion claim. For f(x)=a ReLU(w x1+M x2), one observed training input e1 with label y>0, initialization a=0,w=1,M>0, and both layers trained by gradient flow, the equations are a'=(y-aw)w, w'=(y-aw)a, M'=0. The entire training prediction aw and training Gram K=a^2+w^2 are independent of M, while f(e2)=M a(t). The invariant w^2-a^2=1 and positive residual ensure a(t)>0 for every t>0. Against test law uniform on {e1,e2} and single-index teacher g(x)=x1, R(t)=[(aw-1)^2+M^2 a^2]/2 diverges with M at every fixed t>0. Frozen versus nonlinear unseen predictions also differ by M[(y^3/6)t^3+O(t^4)] near zero. This rules out a deterministic population control from training-only quantities without off-sample assumptions. It does not refute standard-Gaussian-initialization bounds and is not a double-descent example.
Unrestricted deterministic initialization, not standard initialization
M>0, y>0
Gradient flow with active gates on e1 and e2
title: Draft: T267 ReLU training Gram control leaves unseen predictions unbounded

\begin{multline*}
\mathbf E_x\big[f_1(\mathbf Z_{t_1}^{n,z})\,f_2(\mathbf Z_{t_2}^{n,z})\,\mathbf 1_{\{\tau_{j-1}^n<t_1\leq\tau_j^n,\tau_{k-1}^n<t_2\leq\tau_k^n\}}\big]\\
\underset{n\to\infty}{\longrightarrow}\mathbf E_x\big[f_1(\bar{\mathbf Z}_{t_1}^z)\,f_2(\bar{\mathbf Z}_{t_2}^z)\,\mathbf 1_{\{\tau_{j-1}<t_1\leq\tau_j,\tau_{k-1}<t_2\leq\tau_k\}}\big],\quad\forall k\geq j+1.
\end{multline*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 7 of arXiv:2606.26619, 'Ergodicity of stochastic reaction-diffusion equations on unbounded domains driven by space'] Suppose that (H2), (H4) and (H5) hold. 
If $\alpha > \frac{L_{\sigma}^4}{8}$, 
then for any $\lambda>0$ satisfying $\frac{\lambda^2}{8}<\alpha - \frac{L_{\sigma}^4}{8}$ and $\frac{\lambda^2}{4}<\alpha$, we have
\begin{align}
  \sup_{t\geq 0}\mathbb{E} [\Vert u(t)\Vert^2_{L^2_{\lambda}}] <\infty ,
\end{align}
for every bounded continuous initial value $f$ on $\mathbb{R}$. 
In particular, there exists a unique invariant measure in $L^2_{\lambda}$. Moreover, the solution is exponentially mixing with respect to the Wasserstein metric  $W_2$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 7 of arXiv:2606.26619

For finite Gaussian networks indexed by n, let X_n~N(0,C_n), P_n be a finite nonempty family of nonempty positively weighted paths, K_n=|P_n|, D_xi,n=min_p sum_v a_npv exp(xi X_nv), and F_n,beta(y)=-(1/beta)log sum_p exp[-beta log(sum_v a_npv exp(y_v))]. Suppose L_n->infinity, max_i(C_n)_ii=O(L_n), and medians of log D_xi,n divided by L_n converge to -lambda(xi) at fixed 0<=a<b. If beta_n>0 and log K_n/(beta_n L_n)->0, then lambda(b)-lambda(a)=-lim_n L_n^(-1) integral_a^b xi E tr[C_n Hess F_n,beta_n(xi X_n)] dxi. This conditional reduction does not evaluate the planar limit or assert pointwise derivative convergence.

\lim_{a \to 0+,\thinspace p \to 0+} a \cdot J(a,p)\ =\ 1\ .

p \cdot \sum_{k=1}^{J(a,p)} \zeta^{(a,p)}_k\

a \to 0+,\  p \to 0 +.

[Lemma Wg of arXiv:2607.05418, 'On the Group Randomness of 0-1 Real Sequences from Binary Linear Codes'] Assume $d^\bot \geq 5.$ Then there exists a subset $\Gamma \subset \Gamma_{\ell,p}^2/\Sigma_p$ with
    $$\sharp\Gamma=\begin{cases}
        0 &(\ell \text{ odd})\\
        (\ell-1)!!(4^{\ell/2}) &(\ell \text{ even})
    \end{cases}$$
    such that
    $$p^{v_\gamma} W_\gamma=\begin{cases}
    \left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^\ell p^{3\ell/2}n^{\ell/2} &(\gamma \in \Gamma)\\
    O_\ell(n^{2\ell-1}) &(\text{otherwise})
\end{cases}.$$
title: Lemma Wg of arXiv:2607.05418

In local coordinates $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ on $U$, the second family of generators is
$$
\partial_{x_i}
+
\sum_{k=1}^r
\partial_{x_i}(f_k)\partial_{t_k},
\qquad
1\leq i\leq n.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 24 (Estimates for the standard replacement) of arXiv:2608.25971, 'Positive \texorpdfstring{$\tau$}{tau}-bi-Ricci curvature and Mean curvature flow with surg'] Fix $0<\eta<1$ and an integer $m_0\geq2$.  After fixing
  $\alpha_0^*$ and the surgery parameters in
  Lemma~\ref{lem:surgery-taubiric-preservation}, the neck quality may be
  improved and the surgery radius decreased, without changing
  $\alpha_0^*$, so that there exist
  \begin{equation*}
  \eps_s>0,\qquad
  k_s\geq m_0+2,\qquad
  L_s\geq L_b,\qquad
  r_s>0,
  \end{equation*}
  and constants $c_s>0$, $C_m<\infty$, $0\leq m\leq m_0$, with the
  following property.

  If surgery is performed on an $(\eps,k,L)$-neck of radius $r$ satisfying
  \begin{equation*}
  \eps\leq\eps_s,\qquad
  k\geq k_s,\qquad
  L\geq L_s,\qquad
  r\leq r_s,
  \end{equation*}
  and if \eqref{eq:incoming-surgery-taubiric} holds on the incoming neck,
  then every changed point satisfies
  \begin{align}
    \widetilde P_{ij}^{(\tau)}
    &\geq
    \alpha_0^*\widetilde H
    |\widetilde\lambda_p-\widetilde\lambda_q|,
    \\
    \widetilde P_{ij}^{(\tau)}
    &\geq c_sr^{-2},
    \qquad
    \widetilde H\geq c_sr^{-1},
    \\
    |\widetilde A|^2-
    \left(\frac1{n-1}+\eta\right)\widetilde H^2
    &\leq
    -c_s\widetilde H^2,
    \\
    r^{m+1}|\widetilde\nabla^m\widetilde A|
    &\leq C_m,
    \qquad
    0\leq m\leq m_0.
    
  \end{align}
  The area removed from each changed neck is at least $c_sr^n$, and the
  replacement may be chosen so that
  \begin{equation}
    \min_{\widetilde M}\widetilde H
    \geq
    \min_MH.
  \end{equation}

  If $0<R\leq1$ and
  \begin{equation}
    r\leq\frac{c_sR}{n+\alpha_2},
  \end{equation}
  then the replacement preserves
  $\CC_\tau(R,(\alpha_0^*,\alpha_1,\alpha_2))$.

body: Let X be the passage time between fixed endpoints and X^L its value after resampling a block L, and let U_L be the event that the geodesic uses an edge of L. If the geodesic avoids L then the original path survives unchanged in the resampled field, so X^L <= X on the complement of U_L. Hence the positive part (X^L - X)^+ vanishes off U_L, and any functional of the form E[1(U_L) f((X^L - X)^+)] with f(0) = 0 equals E[f((X^L - X)^+)] - the indicator carries no information. Combined with exchangeability this gives E[((X^L - X)^+)^k] = (1/2) E[|X^L - X|^k] for every k >= 1.

[Lem 8 of arXiv:2608.22514, 'Diffusion limits of cyclic finite-velocity random motions\\ along vector fields'] For any $f\in C^3_b(\bR^d,\bR)$ and
any
$\eta\in(0,1]$
\ba
\E_{x,\iota}\Big| f(Z^{\e,\delta}_{T_p^\e}) - f(x) - \int_0^{T^\e_p} Af(Z^{\e,\delta}_u)\,\di u\Big|
\leq \eta \E_{\iota} T^\e_p
\ea
uniformly in $x\in\bR^d$ and $\iota\in\{1,\dots,p\}$ for sufficiently small $\e,\delta$.
Consequently,
\ba
\Big|\E\Big[ f(Z^{\e,\delta}_{T_{k+p}^\e}) - f(Z^{\e,\delta}_{T_{k}^\e})
- \int_{T_{k}^\e}^{T_{k+p}^\e} Af(Z^{\e,\delta}_u) \,\di u\     \Big|\rF^{\e,\delta}_{T_{k}^\e} \Big]\Big|
\leq \eta  \E\Big[ T_{k+p}^\e-T_{k}^\e \Big|\rF^{\e,\delta}_{T_{k}^\e} \Big]
\ea
uniformly in  $k\in\mathbb N_0$ for sufficiently small $\e,\delta$.

[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2608.13631, 'The classical discrete laws near the mode:\\ complete local expansions for the negative bi'] Let $t_c$ be the vertex of the quadratic part of $A_1(\,\cdot\,;p)$.  Then
	\begin{equation}
		t_c=-\frac{1+q}{2p}=-\frac qp-\frac12,
		\qquad\text{so}\qquad
		\mu+t_c+\tfrac12=\frac{(r-1)q}{p} ,
	\end{equation}
	and the unit window $\bigl(\mu+t_c-\tfrac12,\ \mu+t_c+\tfrac12\bigr]$ contains exactly one
	integer, $\lfloor(r-1)q/p\rfloor$.  This integer is the upper mode of $\NB(r,p)$; two modes

[Proposition 19 of arXiv:2605.30030, 'Critical exponents for planar random-cluster model with cluster-weight~$q=4$'] There exist constants~$C,c>0$ such that for every~$x,y\in \mathbb R^2$ satisfying~$\dst:=\min\{|x|,|y|,|x-y|, |x+y|\}>0$ and~$0<\delta<\eps<\dst/2$, we have 
\begin{align}\qquad
\Ll|\bc^\delta(\eps)^4\Ll(\widetilde\pi_2^\delta(x,y,\eps)+\widetilde\Delta^\delta(x,y,\eps)\Rr)
-a_\eps(x,y)\eps^{1/2}\left(\tfrac{ |y|^2}{|x|^2|x-y|\,|x+y|}\right)^{1/4}\Rr|&\le   C\pi_1^\delta(\eps,\dst)^4\left(\tfrac{\eps}{\dst}\right)^c + o_\delta(1),
\end{align}
where~$a_{\eps}(x,y)>0$ is a quantity that converges to an absolute constant~$a_0>0$ independent of~$x,y$ as~$\eps$ tends to $0$
and~$o_\delta(1)$ is a quantity converging to~$0$ as~$\delta$ tends to $0$.

[Proposition 9 (Lopatto--Otto Poisson approximation) of arXiv:2608.20101, '\bfseries Largest bulk gap of the complex Ginibre ensemble'] Fix \(\kappa>0\), \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/16)\), and a Borel set
\(A\subset\{z:|z|<1\}\) with \(\sup_{z\in A}|z|<1\). For all large \(n\), let
\(R_{n,\kappa}(a)\) be the unique radius satisfying
\begin{equation}
 K_n(a,a)\,\Pp\{\xi_n^{a,!}(D_{R_{n,\kappa}(a)}(a))=0\}
 =\kappa.
\end{equation}
Let \(\Xi_{n,\kappa}\) be the point process of the retained unit-disk
anchors \(a\), where \(a\in\xi_n\cap D_1\) is retained when
\(d_n(a)>R_{n,\kappa}(a)\). If \(\zeta_\kappa\) is a Poisson process of
intensity \(\kappa\,\mathrm d^2z\), then, for a constant depending on
\(A,\kappa,\varepsilon\),
\begin{equation}
 d_{\mathrm{KR}}(\Xi_{n,\kappa}\cap A,
                  \zeta_\kappa\cap A)
 \le C n^{-1/16+\varepsilon}.
\end{equation}
Consequently, if \(N_{n,\kappa}(A)=\Xi_{n,\kappa}(A)\), then
\[
 N_{n,\kappa}(A)\ \Longrightarrow\ \Pois(\kappa|A|).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Let X be a compact metric space, T : X -> X continuous, and let M(X,T) be the set of T-invariant Borel probability measures with the weak-star topology, a nonempty compact convex metrisable set. Suppose T is ASYMPTOTICALLY h-EXPANSIVE, i.e. its tail entropy h*(T) = lim as eps -> 0 of sup over x of h(T, Gamma_eps(x)) vanishes; this holds in particular when T is h-expansive, and a fortiori when T is expansive. THEN the entropy map mu -> h_mu(T) is upper semicontinuous on M(X,T): whenever mu_k -> mu weak-star inside M(X,T), limsup_k h_{mu_k}(T) <= h_mu(T). CONSEQUENCES: an upper semicontinuous function on a nonempty compact set attains its supremum, so by the variational principle a measure of maximal entropy exists and h_top(T) = max over mu in M(X,T) of h_mu(T); the entropy function is then a bounded, affine, upper semicontinuous function on a Choquet simplex, which is what makes the theory of maximal measures and of symbolic extensions run. WHERE IT FAILS: (i) some hypothesis of this kind is necessary. For a general continuous map the entropy map need not be upper semicontinuous and a measure of maximal entropy need not exist; this is why smoothness matters - Newhouse proved that C^infinity diffeomorphisms of compact manifolds are asymptotically h-expansive and therefore always carry maximal measures, while for finite smoothness there are counterexamples. (ii) The conclusion is strictly one-sided and cannot be improved to continuity even for expansive systems: in a mixing shift of finite type the periodic-orbit measures, all of entropy 0, are weak-star dense, so they converge to the measure of maximal entropy and the entropy map is not lower semicontinuous. (iii) Compactness of X (hence of M(X,T)) is what converts upper semicontinuity into existence of a maximiser; on a noncompact space the existence conclusion fails even when the map is upper semicontinuous. (iv) The implication is stated in one direction only: upper semicontinuity of the entropy map is a strictly weaker property than asymptotic h-expansiveness, so do not run the criterion backwards.
X is a compact metric space and T : X -> X is continuous
M(X,T) carries the weak-star topology and is nonempty (guaranteed by Krylov-Bogolyubov)
h*(T) = 0 (asymptotic h-expansiveness); h-expansiveness and expansiveness are sufficient special cases
h_mu(T) is the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy of the measure-preserving system (X, mu, T)
the existence corollary uses the variational principle, which itself needs only compactness and continuity

Now let eps -> 0 and use h*(T) = 0. [Thm 9 of arXiv:2609.03054, 'The classes of bivariate Schur and Herglotz matrix-valued rational functions: realizations'] Let $G\in \mathbb C^{m \times n}(s,p)$ be a rational matrix valued  function. Then the following conditions are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[\rm (i)]
\item $G$ has no singularities in $\mathbb{GH}$ and the matrix $G(s,p)$ has norm less than or equal to one
for any $(s,p)\in \mathbb{GH}$;
\item $G$ admits a realization of the form 
    $$G(s,p)=  D+  \frac12 {C} \left(s I+ 2A -
    (s^2-4p) P(s I+ 2A)^{-1} P\right)^{-1}B. $$
    with 
    \begin{equation}
\matr{
A+A^*- C^*C  & C^*D+ B\\ D^* C+ B^*  & 
I - D^* D} \geq 0,
\end{equation}
   and $-I\le P \le I$.
   \end{enumerate}
Additionally, if $G\in {\mathbb R}^{m\times n}(s,p)$, then the matrices $A,B,C,D$ and $P$
can be chosen as real.
title: Thm 9 of arXiv:2609.03054

[Definition 1 (Probabilistically weak and strong solutions) of arXiv:2607.22470, 'A Logarithmic Fluctuation Hierarchy for Sequential Interacting Diffusions'] We call
\[
(Y,\mathcal M)
=
\bigl((Y^n)_{n\ge0},(\mathcal M^n)_{n\ge0}\bigr)
\]
a probabilistically weak solution of the limiting logarithmic hierarchy if
there exists a stochastic basis
\[
(\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_t)_{t\in[0,T]},\mathbb P)
\]
such that, on this basis, \(Y\) and \(\mathcal M\) have the following
properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] For every \(n\ge0\), \(Y^n\) is a continuous
\((\mathcal F_t)\)-adapted process with values in \(H^{-\beta,-m}\) and has
weakly continuous paths in \(H^{-\beta_\ast}\). Moreover, for some
\(q\in(0,1/4)\),
\begin{equation}
\sum_{n=0}^\infty
q^n
\mathbb E\sup_{t\le T}\|Y_t^n\|_{H^{-\beta_\ast}}^2
<\infty.
\end{equation}

\item[(ii)] For every \(n\ge0\), \(\mathcal M^n\) is a continuous
\((\mathcal F_t)\)-adapted process with values in \(H^{-\beta,-m}\), and
\(\mathcal M\), viewed as an \(E^{\mathbb N_0}\)-valued random element, is
centered Gaussian. For every \(n\ge0\) and
\(\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\R^d)\),
\[
M_t^n(\varphi):=\langle\mathcal M_t^n,\varphi\rangle
\]
is a continuous \((\mathcal F_t)\)-martingale, and
\begin{equation}
\langle M^n(\varphi),M^k(\psi)\rangle_t
=
\frac{(n+k)!}{n!\,k!}
\int_0^t
\langle
\bar\rho_s,
\nabla\varphi\cdot\nabla\psi
\rangle\,\dd s
\end{equation}
for all \(n,k\ge0\), \(t\in[0,T]\), and
\(\varphi,\psi\in C_c^\infty(\R^d)\).

\item[(iii)] For every \(n\ge0\) and
\(\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\R^d)\), the following identity holds
\(\mathbb P\)-almost surely for all \(t\in[0,T]\):
\begin{align}
\langle Y_t^n,\varphi\rangle
={}&
\langle Y_0^n,\varphi\rangle
+
\int_0^t
\langle Y_s^n,L_s\varphi\rangle\,\dd s\notag\\
&+
\int_0^t
\left\langle
\bar\rho_s,
(K*Y_s^{n+1})\cdot\nabla\varphi
\right\rangle\,\dd s
+
\langle\mathcal M_t^n,\varphi\rangle.

\end{align}
\end{enumerate}

We call \(Y\) a probabilistically strong solution if there exist a stochastic
basis and a process \(\mathcal M\) on it such that \((Y,\mathcal M)\) is a
probabilistically weak solution and \(Y\) is adapted to
the normal filtration generated by
\((Y_0^n)_{n\ge0}\) and \(\mathcal M\).

[Proposition prop:basic of arXiv:2607.22991, 'Mixing times and spectra of non-equilibrium symmetric exclusion processes on general graph'] For any SEP on a connected graph satisfying the non-triviality condition on the heat baths stated earlier,
the steady-state distribution~$\mu$ exists and is unique.  Moreover, if all heat baths are identical
(i.e., the 2-point probability distribution at every vertex~$v$ with $\xi_v>0$ is $h_v=(h(0),h(1))$, 
with $h(0)=1-h(1)\in (0,1)$), then the SEP is reversible w.r.t.\ the steady-state product distribution 
$\mu(\sigma)=\prod_{v\in V} h(\sigma(v))$.

[Theorem thm:F-via-HF of arXiv:2509.08928, 'The near critical random bond Ising model via embedding deformation'] {[CLR1] and [Che20] }  For each fixed $\kappa<1$, there exist constants $\gamma_0=\gamma_0(\kappa)>0$ and \mbox{$C_0=C_0(\kappa)>0$} such that the following alternative holds. Let $F$ be a s-holomorphic function defined in a ball of radius $r$ drawn over an s-embedding $\mathcal{S}$ satisfying the assumption $\textup{Lip}(\kappa,\delta)$ and some $\alpha \in \mathbb{T}$. Then, provided that $r\ge\operatorname{cst}\cdot\delta$ for a constant depending only on $\kappa$, one has the two following alternatives:

For the integration procedure (equation eq:def-I_C of the paper) 
\[
\begin{array}{rcl}
\text{either}\ \max_{\{z:\mathcal{S}(z)\in B(u,\frac{1}{2}r)\}}|F|&\le& C_0r^{-1}\cdot |\operatorname{osc}_{\{v:\mathcal{S}(v)\in B(u,r)\}}I_{\alpha\mathbb{R}}[\overline{\varsigma}F]|,\\[4pt]
\text{or}\ \max_{\{z:\mathcal{S}(z)\in B(u,\frac{3}{4}r)\}}|F|&\ge& \exp(\gamma_0r\delta^{-1})\cdot C_0r^{-1}|\operatorname{osc}_{\{v:\mathcal{S}(v)\in B(u,r)\}}I_{\alpha\mathbb{R}}[\overline{\varsigma}F]|
\end{array}
\]

For the integration procedure (equation eq:HF-def of the paper) 
\[
\begin{array}{rcl}
\text{either}\ \max_{\{z:\mathcal{S}(z)\in B(u,\frac{1}{2}r)\}}|F|^2&\le& C_0r^{-1}\cdot |\operatorname{osc}_{\{v:\mathcal{S}(v)\in B(u,r)\}}H_{F}|,\\[4pt]
\text{or}\ \max_{\{z:\mathcal{S}(z)\in B(u,\frac{3}{4}r)\}}|F|^2&\ge& \exp(\gamma_0r\delta^{-1})\cdot C_0r^{-1}|\operatorname{osc}_{\{v:\mathcal{S}(v)\in B(u,r)\}}H_{F}|
\end{array}
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop odd-kernel of arXiv:2605.13004, 'Orientation in Poisson Cluster Processes via Imaginary Bispectra'] In the setting of Proposition~(prop:sign-symmetrized-family of the paper), assume that $c_{3,1}\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$ and let $c_3^{\mathrm o}$ be the odd part defined there. Then
\[
\mathbb{E}_\theta[\mathcal O_{T,g}]=\theta\,\mu_{T,g},
\]
where
\[
\mu_{T,g}
=
\frac{1}{T}\int_0^T\iint_{\mathbb{R}^2}
g(\tau_1,\tau_2)\,
\1_{\{0\le x_0+\tau_1\le T,\ 0\le x_0+\tau_2\le T\}}
\,c_3^{\mathrm o}(\tau_1,\tau_2)\,d\tau_1d\tau_2\,dx_0.
\]
If $\mathrm{supp}(g)\subset[-H,H]^2$, then, as $T\to\infty$,
\[
\mu_{T,g}=\mu_g+O(T^{-1}),
\qquad
\mu_g:=\iint_{\mathbb{R}^2} g(\tau_1,\tau_2)c_3^{\mathrm o}(\tau_1,\tau_2)\,d\tau_1d\tau_2.
\]
If in addition $\widehat g=\mathrm{i} H_g$ with $H_g$ real-valued and integrable, then
\[
\mu_g
=
\frac{1}{(2\pi)^2}
\iint_{\mathbb{R}^2}H_g(\omega_1,\omega_2)\,\mathrm{Im} B_1(\omega_1,\omega_2)\,d\omega_1d\omega_2.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Odd local contrast for the sign-symmetrized family

body:
[Lemma lem:bounded-ode of arXiv:2606.19763, 'Optimal Sparsification of Gaussian Processes'] Let $F:[0,1]\times\R^N\to\R^N$ be continuous and bounded, where $\R^N$ is equipped with the Euclidean norm.
	For every initial value $\bar{a}_0\in\R^N$, the initial-value problem
	\[
		\bar{a}'(\theta)
		=
		F(\theta,\bar{a}(\theta))\,,
		\qquad
		\bar{a}(0)=\bar{a}_0
	\]
	has an absolutely continuous solution on $[0,1]$.
	Moreover, if $\|F\|_\infty\leq  M$, then every solution satisfies
	\[
		\|\bar{a}(\theta)-\bar{a}(\theta')\|_2
		\leq 
		M|\theta-\theta'|
	\]
	for all $\theta,\theta'\in[0,1]$, and hence $\|\bar{a}'(\theta)\|_2\leq  M$ for a.e.~$\theta\in[0,1]$.

body:
[Definition 1 of arXiv:2608.27166, 'Well-posedness and regularity of stochastic heat equations on moving domains'] An adapted random field $u$ on $Q_{T}$ is called a weak solution of equation \eqref{eq:moving-spde} if
\begin{equation}
u\in L^2(\Omega;C([0,T];L^2(\mathcal O_{\cdot})))
\cap
L^2(\Omega;L^2(0,T;H_0^1(\mathcal O_{\cdot}))),

\end{equation}
and
for every deterministic $\varephi\in C_D^2(Q_{T})$ and every
$t\in[0,T]$, the following identity holds almost surely:
\begin{align}
\int_{\OOt}u(t,x)\varephi(t,x)\,dx
&=
\int_{\OO}u_0(x)\varephi(0,x)\,dx
-\int_0^t\int_{\mathcal O_s}\nabla_xu(s,x)\cdot\nabla_x\varephi(s,x)\,dx\,ds
\nonumber\\
&\quad
+\int_0^t\int_{\mathcal O_s}u(s,x)\partial_s\varephi(s,x)\,dx\,ds
+\int_0^t\int_{\mathcal O_s}f(s,x,u(s,x))\varephi(s,x)\,dx\,ds
\nonumber\\
&\quad
+\int_0^t\int_{\mathcal O_s}g_i(s,x,u(s,x))\varephi(s,x)\,dx\,dw_s^i .

\end{align}

[Lem proofthm3zeroi of arXiv:2605.06488, 'Continuous-state branching processes with L\'evy-Khintchine drift-interaction: Laplace dua'] Let $\Psi=\Sigma-\Phi$, $\hat{\Psi}=\hat{\Sigma}-\hat{\Phi}$ be mechanisms satisfying the assumptions of Theorem~(thm2zero of the paper) together with $\int_0^{1}\frac{\mathrm{d} u}{\hat{\Phi}(u)}<\infty$. If $\overline{\varrho}_{\,\scriptscriptstyle\Sigma,\hat\Phi}<1$ then there exists $x_1\in (0,\infty)$ such that for all $a\in (0,x_1)$, 
$$\mathbb{E}_0[\sigma^{\mathrm{e}0,+}_{a}]\leq \frac{2}{1-\overline{\rho}_{\Sigma,\hat\Phi}}\int_{0}^{a}\frac{\mathrm{d} u}{\hat{\Phi}(u)}<\infty.$$

body:
[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Given an element $a\in A$ of a $C^*$-algebra, define its spectrum as:
$$\sigma(a)=\left\{\lambda\in\mathbb C\Big|a-\lambda\notin A^{-1}\right\}$$
The following spectral theory results hold, exactly as in the $A=B(H)$ case:
\begin{enumerate}
\item We have $\sigma(ab)\cup\{0\}=\sigma(ba)\cup\{0\}$.

\item We have $\sigma(f(a))=f(\sigma(a))$, for any $f\in\mathbb C(X)$ having poles outside $\sigma(a)$.

\item The spectrum $\sigma(a)$ is compact, non-empty, and contained in $D_0(||a||)$.

\item The spectra of unitaries $(u^*=u^{-1})$ and self-adjoints $(a=a^*)$ are on $\mathbb T,\mathbb R$.

\item The spectral radius of normal elements $(aa^*=a^*a)$ is given by $\rho(a)=||a||$.
\end{enumerate}
In addition, assuming $a\in A\subset B$, the spectra of $a$ with respect to $A$ and to $B$ coincide.

[Defi Def:Contigu of arXiv:2608.29013, 'Weighted Homology and Cohomology of Weighted Polyhedra'] Suppose $(K,\mu)$ and $(K',\mu')$ are two weighted simplicial complexes of the same type. Two morphisms $$\varrho_0,\varrho_1: (K,\mu)\rightarrow (K',\mu')$$ are called \emph{contiguous}, denoted by $\varrho_0 \underset{c}{\simeq} \varrho_1$,  
  if there exists a morphism
  $$ F: (K \times [0, 1], \mu \times \mathbf{1}) \rightarrow (K',\mu')\  \text{with}\
  F(x, 0) =\varrho_0(x),\, F(x,1)= \varrho_1(x),\ \forall x\in K.$$
   Here $([0,1],\mathbf{1})$ is a weighted simplicial complex where the weight of every 
   simplex of $[0,1]$ is $1$, and $(K\times [0,1],\mu\times \mathbf{1})$ is the Cartesian product $(K,\mu)$ with
   $([0,1],\mathbf{1})$ (see Definition~(Def:Product-Wt-Complexes of the paper)). 
   Moreover, if $\varrho_0$, $\varrho_1$ and $F$ are all weight-preserving, we say that 
   $\varrho_0$ and $\varrho_1$ are \emph{strongly contiguous}.
title: Contiguous Morphisms

Let X be a normal topological space, meaning that for every pair of disjoint closed sets there exist disjoint open sets containing them respectively. Let A and B be disjoint closed subsets of X. Then there exists a continuous function f from X to the interval [0,1] with f(a) = 0 for all a in A and f(b) = 1 for all b in B. (No T1 axiom is needed for this statement; f separates A and B but its level sets need not be A and B exactly.)

TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). For two independent centered Gaussian fields X, Y indexed by a common finite (or suitably truncated) set T with covariance functions C_X, C_Y, Kahane's interpolation forms Z(t,u) = sqrt(u) X(t) + sqrt(1-u) Y(t) for u in [0,1] and computes d/du E[F(Z(.,u))] for a smooth test function F, obtaining an integral expression involving (C_Y(s,t) - C_X(s,t)) times a mixed second derivative of F, evaluated against the law of Z(.,u). When C_X <= C_Y pointwise (or the relevant difference has a consistent sign) and F is chosen with matching sign of mixed partials, this yields a comparison inequality between functionals of X and Y, an approach that both generalizes Slepian-type comparisons and, in the Gaussian multiplicative chaos literature, is used to show that different regularizations of a log-correlated field, such as the two-dimensional Gaussian free field, converge to the same limiting chaos measure regardless of the approximation scheme, a key technical step in constructing Liouville quantum gravity measures. It does not apply to non-Gaussian fields, it requires the two fields being compared to be independent for the interpolation construction itself, and the sign or convexity conditions on F needed to obtain a clean inequality must be verified case by case rather than assumed. Typical failure: Applying the interpolation to fields that are not independent, or to a family of regularizations whose covariance difference does not have a consistent sign across the whole index set, which is common when comparing regularizations of a log-correlated field near its singular set; either error breaks the monotonicity the interpolation is meant to exploit, and the resulting comparison can go in the wrong direction with no explicit error term to control it. Canonical reference: Kahane, 1986, Annales des Sciences Mathematiques du Quebec; Robert and Vargas, 2010, Comptes Rendus Mathematique; Berestycki, 2017, Electronic Communications in Probability.

Let X have a probability law on R with mean m and finite variance sigma^2, and let mu_t be its free convolution with a semicircle law of variance t. For every t>0 with t>=1024(7+4sqrt(2))sigma^2, the continuous density of mu_t has a unique global maximizer M(t), and M(t)->m as t tends to infinity. If M3=E|X-m|^3 is finite, put B=(sqrt(2)+2)sigma, A=B^2+sigma^2 and K=A(B+sigma)+4(B^3+M3); then |M(t)-m|<=36K/t at those times. For sigma=0 the mode is exactly m. These are sufficient large-time bounds for a global density maximizer, without a compact-support assumption or a claimed optimal transition threshold.
