body:
Let X = (X_1, ..., X_n) have independent coordinates with finite ranges, f a real function of X, and f = sum over S of f_S its Hoeffding (ANOVA) decomposition over subsets S of {1, ..., n}: f_S depends only on X_S, f_empty = E f, and E[f_S | X_T] = 0 unless S is inside T. Put w_S = E[f_S^2] and W_k = sum over |S| = k of w_S, the variance at interaction order k. With R_r the block conditional variances, put D_m = (-1)^(m+1) Delta^m R_0 for 1 <= m <= n, and let H_<m be the functions whose Hoeffding components of order m or more vanish. Then D_m = binom(n, m)^(-1) sum_{k=m}^n binom(k, m) W_k and D_m <= dist_2(f, H_<m)^2 <= binom(n, m) D_m; so D_m = 0 if and only if f lies in H_<m. With nonzero tail, the left inequality is an equality exactly when all the tail mass sits at order n, and the right one exactly when it sits at order m. The same holds with Q_r, the average over |A| = r of E[(f(X) - f(X^(A)))^2], since Q_r = 2 R_r: for m = 1 it reads Var(f) <= (1/2) sum_i E[(f(X) - f(X^(i)))^2].

body: [Lemma distribution_v_i of arXiv:2607.22480, 'Distinguishability threshold for random geometric graphs'] Let $1\leq s< i\leq n$. Then, conditional on the coordinates $\boldsymbol{v}_i(1), \dots, \boldsymbol{v}_i(s-1)$, the value $\boldsymbol{v}_i(s)/r_i(s)$ is distributed as the first coordinate of a uniform random point $\boldsymbol{y}$ on the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^{d-s}\subseteq \mathbb{R}^{d-s+1}$, where $r_i(s)=\sqrt{1-\sum_{k=1}^{s-1} \boldsymbol{v}_i(k)^2}$ is the residual length of the vector $\boldsymbol{v}_i$ after coordinate $s$. In other words, the first $i-1$ coordinates of $\boldsymbol{v}_i$ follow the same distribution as the first $i-1$ coordinates of a uniform random point on the sphere $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$.

[Lemma boundedorthogonal of arXiv:2609.01885, 'The Order of the Non-universal Tree of a Hilbert Space with Respect to the Haar Basis'] Suppose that $(u_0,\ldots, u_{m-1})\in \textbf{T}(C)$ is a family of pairwise-orthogonal vectors. Set $A = \inf_{n<m}\{||u_n||\}$, $B = \sup_{n < m} \{||u_n||\}$, and $C' = \max\{C B, \frac{C}{A}\}$. Then $m \leq 2^{(C')^2-2}$. 

In particular, for every sting $s\in \textbf{T}(C)$ consisting of pairwise-orthogonal vectors, $|s|\leq 2^{C^4-2}$.

[Theorem thm:rigidity of arXiv:2608.30254, 'Exact Recovery Thresholds for Weighted Data Selection\\ in Vector-Valued Linear Regression'] Let the features span $\mathbb{R}^d$ and suppose $\tau(D)=k:=(m+1)d$. Let $c$ be a

uniquely (up to permutation) into $d$ pairwise disjoint blocks
$S=C_1\sqcup\dots\sqcup C_d$ with $|C_j|=m+1$, where each $C_j$ supports a
positive circuit of the dyads whose features span a one-dimensional line
$U_j$, and $U_1,\dots,U_d$ are linearly independent.

[Proposition prop:well_defined_functional of arXiv:2608.22044, 'Structured Learning on Mapper Representations'] Let
$
F:\widetilde{\mathcal R}\to\mathbb R
$
be a functional satisfying
$
F(\mathcal R_1)=F(\mathcal R_2)
\quad
\text{whenever }
\mathcal R_1\sim\mathcal R_2.
$
Then $F$ induces a well-defined functional
\[
\bar F:\mathcal R\to\mathbb R
\]
on the quotient representation space by
$
\bar F([\mathcal R])=F(\mathcal R).
$

[Lemma lem:absorber of arXiv:2609.00889, 'Dominant-Degree Conditions for Ramsey--Tur\'an Factors of Non-Directed Cycle Orientations'] {[LoMarkstrom,CHWY2024]}
Let $H$ be a fixed oriented graph on $h\ge2$ vertices. For every $\eta,\beta>0$ and $t\in\mathbb N$ there are $\xi>0$ and $n_0$ such that the following holds. If $D$ is a digraph with $n\ge n_0$, and $V(D)$ is $(H,\beta n,t)$-closed, then there is a set $A\subseteq V(D)$ with $|A|\le\eta n$ such that, for any set $U\subseteq V(D)\setminus A$ with $|U|\le\xi n$ and $h\mid |A\cup U|$, the digraph $D[A\cup U]$ has an $H$-factor. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 21 (Multivariate Gaussian) of arXiv:2605.14630, '2605.14630'] For $N\geqs1$, let $\R^N$ be equipped with the $\sigma$-algebra $\cB$ of Borel
sets and Lebesgue measure $\6x$. Let $m\in\R^N$ and let $C\in\R^{N\times N}$ be 
a symmetric, positive definite matrix. 
A random variable $X:\R^N\to\R$ is a (multivariate) Gaussian random variable 
with mean $m$ and covariance matrix $C$ if its law is 
\begin{equation}
 
 \mu(\6x) = 
 \frac{1}{(2\pi)^{N/2}\det(C)^{1/2}} \e^{-\pscal{(x-m)}{C^{-1}(x-m)}/2} \6x\;.
\end{equation} 
In that case, we write $X \sim \cN(m, C)$.
title: Multivariate Gaussian

body: The characteristic function of a random variable X is phi_X(t) = E[e^{itX}] for t real (the Fourier transform of its distribution). It satisfies phi_X(0) = 1, |phi_X(t)| <= 1, and phi_X is uniformly continuous. It DETERMINES the distribution (uniqueness theorem: equal characteristic functions imply equal laws, via the Fourier inversion formula), and X, Y independent implies phi_{X+Y} = phi_X phi_Y.
title: Characteristic Function

body: [Theorem thm: sbt of arXiv:2507.04505, 'Heights of butterfly trees'] Let $\pi \sim \operatorname{Unif}(\operatorname{B}_{n,s})$ and $h_n^{\operatorname{B}} = h(\mathcal T(\pi))$. Then $h_n^{\operatorname{B}} \sim 2^{X_n} + 2^{n - X_n} - 2$, where $X_n \sim \operatorname{Binom}(n,1/2)$, while $(\log_2 h_n^{\operatorname{B}} - n/2)/(\sqrt n/2)$ converges in distribution to $|Z|$ as $n \to \infty$, where $Z \sim N(0,1)$. In particular, $\mathbb{E} h_{n}^{\operatorname{B}} = 2(3/2)^n - 2 = c N^\alpha \cdot(1 + o(1))$ with $c=2$ and $\alpha = \log_2(3/2) \approx 0.58496$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm: sbt of arXiv:2507.04505

[Thm 2 of arXiv:2512.03884, '2512.03884'] Let $\alpha$ be a quadratic irrational, and let $D$ be the discriminant of its minimal polynomial. Let $A=\mathbb{Z} + \mathbb{Z}\alpha$, and let $\varepsilon$ be the smallest totally positive unit in the order $\{ \xi \in \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{D}) : \xi A \subseteq A \}$ such that $\varepsilon>1$. Then
\[ c_1(\alpha) = \frac{2\zeta(A,-1)}{D^{1/2} \log \varepsilon} \quad \textrm{and} \quad c_2(\alpha) = \frac{4 \zeta(A,-3)}{9D^{3/2} \log \varepsilon} . \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm MPL of arXiv:2506.01746, '\bf Optimal Bregman quantization: existence and uniqueness of optimal quantizers revisited'] $(a)$ {\em General case}  (see e.g.~[Kav1993],~[Struwe1990]). If $\Lambda:\mathbb{R}^d\longrightarrow\mathbb{R}_+$ ($\Lambda$ for ``landscape'' when $d\!=\!2$) is
a continuously differentiable function satisfying $\displaystyle \lim_{|x|\to +\infty}\Lambda(x)$  $= +\infty$ and if two distinct zeros of $\nabla \Lambda$ are strict local
minima then $\nabla \Lambda$ has  a third zero  which can be in no case a strict  local minimum.

\smallskip
\noindent $(b)$  {\em  Compact case} (see [LambertonP1996],~[Cohort1998],~[LuPag23]). Let $K\!\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be   a
nonempty compact convex set with a nonempty interior $O$, $\mathring{K} = O$. If $\Lambda :K\longrightarrow \mathbb{R}$ is $C^1$
on $O$, $\nabla \Lambda$ admits a continuous extension  on $K$ satisfying $\{\nabla \Lambda=0\}\!\subset \,O$ 
and if, for every small enough $\varepsilon>0$, $(Id-\varepsilon \nabla \Lambda)(O)\!\subset O$, then $\nabla \Lambda$ has at least a third critical point in $K$ which is not a strict local minimum for $\Lambda$ on $K$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Mountain Pass Lemma

body: [Lemma 52 (FIID sparse unique infinite clusters on the symmetric space) of arXiv:2504.02435, 'Poisson-Voronoi percolation in higher rank'] Let $G$ be a connected higher rank semisimple real Lie group with property (T) and let $(X,d_X)$ be its symmetric space. [Lemma 9 (\cite{Meurant,Usmani}) of arXiv:2607.08536, 'Soft edge limit of the Laguerre beta-ensemble at the lower edge'] Let $\ma{M}$ be an $n\times n$ tridiagonal matrix satisfying the assumptions above.
Then the following statements hold:
\begin{align}
u_{i}&= \det \ma{M}_{[1,i-1]} \cdot \prod_{k=1}^{i-1} e_k^{-1}, \qquad\qquad 1\le i\le n,\\
v_{j}&= \det \ma{M}_{[j+1,n]} \cdot \prod_{k=1}^{j-1} e_k \cdot (\det \ma{M})^{-1}, \qquad 1\le j\le n,\\ 
[\ma{M}^{-1}]_{i,j}&=u_{i} v_{j}= \det \ma{M}_{[1,i-1]}\det \ma{M}_{[j+1,n]} (\det \ma{M})^{-1} \prod_{k=i}^{j-1} e_k, \qquad \quad 1\le i\le j\le n,\\
\det \ma{M}&=v_n^{-1} \prod_{k=1}^{n-1}e_k= (d_n u_n-e_{n-1} u_{n-1})\prod_{k=1}^{n-1} e_k.
\end{align}
Note that by convention  the determinant of the empty matrix is equal to $1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [campaign status: candidate_full_solution - author-checked with a scope caveat; NO independent review - the parent that reviewed it had itself supplied two of the argument's steps, so its review does not certify the amended proof; no Lean] van Handel, The strong convergence phenomenon, arXiv:2507.00346v2 (11 February 2026), Section 6.9, pp. 69-70, asks whether strong convergence of a family of random matrices forces the empirical complex-eigenvalue measures of every noncommutative polynomial to converge to the corresponding limiting Brown measure. Problem 6.9 states it for ARBITRARY strongly convergent families - no independence, no independent entries, no freeness of the limit - and that literal generality is what is addressed. CLAIM: no. Fix an irrational theta and reduced approximants p_j/q_j -> theta; with omega_j = exp(2 pi i p_j / q_j) put U_j e_k = omega_j^k e_k, S e_k = e_{k-1} and V_j = e^{pi i / q_j} S. Then V_j U_j = omega_j U_j V_j, U_j^{q_j} = I, V_j^{q_j} = -I, and det(z I - U_j - V_j) = z^{q_j} exactly, so A_j = U_j + V_j is nilpotent and every empirical eigenvalue measure is delta_0, while the Brown measure of u + v for the limiting irrational-rotation pair is Haar measure on the unit circle (Fang, Jiang, Lin and Xu, arXiv:1210.4771, Theorem 12.2 - a literature dependency, not proved here). The same example blocks any universal lower bound on the limiting spectral radius. Conjugating by an independent Haar unitary makes the family random without changing norms, traces, nilpotency or eigenvalues. THE LOAD-BEARING GAP, named by the record itself: the pair converges to a ROTATION-ALGEBRA pair, not a free pair, and the two have different Brown measures, so the citation has to match the limit the construction actually has; the strong-convergence step is recorded as one of three loose ends. WHAT IS NOT REFUTED: the narrower conjectures for independent Ginibre matrices with adjoints and for free limiting families. Yi Han, arXiv:2606.01664 (June 2026), claims the Ginibre case and is COMPATIBLE with this construction. Do not promote a general counterexample to a result about independent matrix ensembles. FULL CONSTRUCTION AND PROOF: the store holds it as the lemma math:probability.free:candidate-strong-convergence-does-not-force-brown-measure, under a title naming neither the problem nor the campaign; this node is what makes it reachable from the problem id.

[Lemma lem:BLPP-seed-linear of arXiv:2608.02772, 'Non-Abelian Hirota-Miwa Equations for the KPZ Universality Class'] Let $H = L^2(\mathbb{R})$.  The seed functions $\psi_{t,z,n}$
and $\phi_{t,w,n}$ defined in
\S(sec:BLPP-kernel-reform of the paper) satisfy the linear problem
(equation eq:dc-clean-linear-d1 of the paper)--(equation eq:dc-clean-linear-S3 of the paper)
and its adjoint
(equation eq:dc-clean-adjoint-d1 of the paper)--(equation eq:dc-clean-adjoint-S3 of the paper)
with $\partial_1 = \partial_t$,
$\partial_2 = -\partial_a$,
$S_3 = e^{\partial_n}$ and constant scalar edge weights
$C_1 = 0$, $\Lambda_1 = 0$,
$C_2 = I$, $\Lambda_2 = 0$.
Explicitly:
\begin{align}
\partial_z \psi_{t,z,n} &= -\psi_{t,z,n+1},
 \\
\partial_t \psi_{t,z,n}
&= \tfrac{1}{2}\partial_z^2 \psi_{t,z,n},

\end{align}
and
\begin{align}
\partial_w \phi_{t,w,n} &= \phi_{t,w,n-1},
 \\
\partial_t \phi_{t,w,n}
&= -\tfrac{1}{2}\partial_w^2 \phi_{t,w,n}.

\end{align}

Let Z be a non-negative random variable with E[Z] > 0. Then Ent(Z) = sup { E[Z * Y] : Y is a random variable such that E[exp(Y)] <= 1 }.
Z >= 0 almost surely
E[Z] > 0

[Lemma lm:g428 of arXiv:2507.08757, 'Strong existence and uniqueness of the tilt-indexed Busemann process in the planar corner '] Let $B$ be a recovering cocycle in an  environment $\omega\in\Omega_0$. Suppose there exists 
  a coalescing family  $\{\pi^u\}_{u\hspace{0.5pt}\in\hspace{0.5pt}\mathbb{Z}^2}$  of   semi-infinite $B$-geodesics  from all initial vertices $u\in\mathbb{Z}^2$. 
  
  Then $A_{\pi^u}(\omega)=B$ for every geodesic $\pi^u$ from this family.

[Theorem 29 (Mean) of arXiv:2605.14206, 'The clumsy coupon collector's problem'] The first moment of $T_{m, p}$ is
  \[
    \E T_{m, p} = m \, H_m + 
      \frac{(1-p)^{-m}}{p}
      \left[
      (p\,m)^2\left(1-p\right)^{m-1}
      +
      \int_0^1 p^3 \, m^2 \left(m-1\right)
      \left(1-p\,x\right)^{m-2} L(x) \, dx
      \right]
  \]
  where $H_m$ is the $m^\text{th}$ harmonic number
  and $L(x) \coloneqq x + (1-x) \log(1-x)$.
  If $p = p_m$ is an $o(1/m)$ sequence then this becomes
  \[
    \E T_{m, p} = m\,H_m
    + p\,m^2 + \frac{1}{4} \, p^2 \, m^3
    + O\left(p^2 \, m^2\right) + O\left(p^3 \, m^4\right).
  \]
  as $m \to \infty$. If $p \sim c/m$ then
  \[
    \E T_{m, p} = m\,H_m + \left(1 + o(1)\right)
      m \left[ c + c^2 \int_0^1 e^{-cx} \, L(x) \, dx\right].
  \]
  If $p = \omega(1/m)$ then
  \[
    \E T_{m,p} = m\,H_m + \frac{(1-p)^{-m}}{p} \left(1
    + O\left(\frac{1}{p\,m}\right)\right).
  \]
  In particular, for $p$ constant,
  \begin{align*}
    \E T_{m,p}
    = m \, H_m
    + \frac{(1-p)^{-m}}{p}&\Bigg\{
      1 + \left(-6p + 5 + \frac{1}{p}\right) m^{-1}\\
    &\phantom{\Bigg\{} {} + \left(45\,p^2 - 62\,p + 8 + \frac{7}{p} + \frac{2}{p^2} \right) m^{-2}
      + O\left(m^{-3}\right)
    \Bigg\}.
  \end{align*}
  \begin{proof}
    The difference $T_{m, p} - T_{m, 0}$ has \textsc{mgf}
    $I_{m, p}(t)$. Corollary~\ref{thm:mgf} implies
    the \textsc{mgf} of $T_{m, p} - T_{m, 0}$
    exists on a neighbourhood of the origin, hence
    $\E [T_{m, p} - T_{m, 0}] = \lim_{t \uparrow 0} I_{m,p}'(t)$.
    With the knowledge 
    \begin{equation}
      
      \frac{\partial}{\partial t} \left( 1 - x \right)^{m \exp(-t) - m}
      = \log\left(\frac{1}{1-x}\right) \, m \, e^{-t}
      \left( 1 - x \right)^{m \exp(-t) - m},
    \end{equation}
    we differentiate the integral expression of
    \eqref{eq:extra term} to find
    \begin{align}
      \notag
      \E \left[T_{m,p} - T_{m,0}\right]
      &= (1-p)^m
      \left[
        1 - \overbrace{\int_0^1 p\, m\left(1-p\,x\right)^{m-1}
        \, dx}^{1 - (1-p)^m} 
      \right]^{-2}\\
      \notag
      &\quad \times \int_0^1 p\,m^2 \left(1-p\,x\right)^{m-1}
      \log\left( \frac{1}{1-x} \right) dx\\
      
      &= \frac{(1-p)^{-m}}{p}
      \int_0^1 (p\,m)^2 \left(1-p\,x\right)^{m-1}
      \log\left( \frac{1}{1-x} \right) dx.
      \intertext{Notice that $L(x) = x + (1-x) \log(1-x)$
      is an antiderivative of $-\log(1-x)$ that
      increases from $L(0) = 0$ to $L(1) = 1$. Hence, by an
      integration by parts,}
      
      &= \frac{(1-p)^{-m}}{p}
      \left[
      (p\,m)^2\left(1-p\right)^{m-1}
      +
      \int_0^1 p^3 \, m^2 \left(m-1\right)
      \left(1-p\,x\right)^{m-2} L(x) \, dx
      \right].
  \end{align}
    Add on $\E T_{m,0} = m \, H_m$ to find our expression for
    the first moment.

    If $p = o(1/m)$ then use the bound $1 \geq (1-p\,x)^{m-2} \geq e^{O(pm)} = 1 + O(p\,m)$,
    uniform in $x$, within \eqref{eq:diff mean}.
    What remains is straightforward: $\int_0^1 L(x) \, dx = 1/4$ and
    \begin{align*}
      \E \left[T_{m,p} - T_{m,0}\right]
      &= \frac{(p\,m)^2}{p\left(1-p\right)}
      + p^2\,m^3\,(1 + O(1/m))\,(1 + O(p\,m))\,\frac{1}{4}\\
      &= p\,m^2 + O\left(p^2\,m^2\right) + \frac{1}{4} \, p^2 \, m^3
      + O\left(p^2 \,m^2\right) + O\left(p^3 \, m^4\right) + O\left(p^3\,m^3\right).
    \end{align*}
    Remove redundant terms to conclude this case.

    If instead $p \sim c/m$ then by dominated convergence we find
    \[
      \E \left[ T_{m,p} - T_{m,0} \right]
      = \left(1+o(1)\right) c\,m
      + \left(1 + o(1)\right) c^2 \, m \int_0^1 e^{-cx} \, L(x) \, dx.
    \]

    Finally assume $p = \omega(1/m)$. 
    The first term in \eqref{eq:diff mean} is negligible because
    \[
      (p\,m)^2 \left(1-p\right)^{m-1} = O\left( p^2 \, m^2\,e^{-pm} \right).
    \]
    Then, to handle the second term, use the Taylor series of
    $\log(1-p\,x)$:
    \begin{align*}
      (1-p\,x)^{m-2} &=
      \exp\left(-p\,x\left(m-2\right) -\frac{(p\,x)^2}{2}\left(m-2\right)
      - \cdots \right)\\

body: Consider a nearly integrable Hamiltonian H(I,theta) = H_0(I) + eps H_1(I,theta) in action-angle coordinates, where H_0 is nondegenerate (its Hessian in I is nonsingular, so the frequency map I -> omega(I) = dH_0/dI is a local diffeomorphism) and H_1 is a sufficiently smooth, classically real-analytic, perturbation. The KAM theorem states that for eps small enough, invariant tori of the unperturbed system whose frequency vector omega(I) is Diophantine (|omega . k| >= c |k|^{-tau} for all nonzero integer vectors k) persist as slightly deformed invariant tori carrying quasi-periodic motion, and the surviving tori occupy a set of measure tending to full measure as eps -> 0. Due to Kolmogorov, Arnold, and Moser.
title: Kolmogorov-Arnold-Moser theorem

  it holds that
  \begin{align} 
    &
    \Bigl( V_{n}, a_{n}^{-1}R_{n}, \rho_{n}, b_{n}^{-1} \dot{\mu}^{\#}_{n}, 
      \mathsf{P}_{n}
      \bigl(
        (c_{n}^{-1} \nu_{n}, \tilde{\mathcal{L}}_{n}^{\nu_{n}}, \tilde{\Phi}_{n}^{\nu_{n}}, \tilde{\Psi}_{n}^{\nu_{n}}) \in \cdot
      \bigr) 
    \Bigr)\\
    \to &

      \mathsf{P} 
      \bigl( 
        (\nu, \mathcal{L}^{\nu}, \Phi^{\nu}, \Psi^{\nu}) \in \cdot 
      \bigr) 
    \Bigr)
  \end{align}
  in the space $\mathfrak{M}(\markedMeasFunct{\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}} \times \tau_{\mathcal{P}}(\tau^{\mathcal{M}^{\mathrm{dis}}} \times \tau_{\mathcal{P}}(\tau^{J_{1}}) \times \fixedFunct{C(\mathbb{R}_{>0}^{2}, \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0})} \times \tau^{C(\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0} \times \mathbb{R}_{>0}, \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0})}))$.
  In particular, $\tilde{\Psi}_{n}^{\nu_{n}} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{d}} \Psi^{\nu}$ in $C(\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0} \times \mathbb{R}_{>0}, \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0})$,
  where the limit is positive with probability $1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:ODE_log_correction of arXiv:2508.18809, '{\bf Critical long-range percolation III: The upper critical dimension}'] Suppose that $a,\gamma>0$ and that $f:(0,\infty)\to (0,\infty)$ satisfies the ODE
\[
  f'= 
  
  \frac{a}{r}(1-C_r (r^{-a}f)^\gamma+\delta_{r})f
\]
where $r\mapsto C_r$ is continuous a continuous function converging to some positive limit $C$ and where $r\mapsto \delta_{r}$
 
 is a
 logarithmically integrable error function. Then
\[
  f(r) \sim (a \gamma C \log r)^{-1/\gamma} r^{a}
\]
as $r\to \infty$.

body:
Let $v, w$ be independent uniformly distributed (Haar) unit vectors in $\mathbb{R}^D$ with $D \ge 3$, and let $\rho = \langle v, w\rangle$. Then $Y = 1 - \rho^2$ has the Beta distribution with parameters $\frac{D-1}{2}$ and $\frac{1}{2}$, and the singular kernel $(1-\rho^2)^{-1/2}$ has finite mean with the exact value $\mathbb{E}[Y^{-1/2}] = \dfrac{\Gamma(D/2)\,\Gamma((D-2)/2)}{\Gamma((D-1)/2)^2} = 1 + O(1/D)$. This is the benchmark that any corresponding estimate for non-Gaussian residual lines has to reproduce, and having the exact Gaussian value makes a wrong intermediate bound visible immediately.
v and w independent and Haar-uniform on the unit sphere in R^D
D >= 3

[Prop 16 of arXiv:2506.17979, '\large\bf A remark on subharmonicity for symmetric Dirichlet forms'] Take $u\in D(\mathscr{E})_{e,\loc}$ and fix an open set $D$. Suppose one of the following holds: 
\begin{enumerate}
\item[{\rm(1)}] ${\bf X}$ is a diffusion process. 
\item[{\rm(2)}] $u\in L^{\infty}(D;{\m})$.
\item[{\rm(3)}] $u\in D(\mathscr{E})_e$. 
\item[{\rm(4)}] $u\in L^{\infty}_{\loc}(D;{\m})$ and 
for any relatively compact 
open sets $U,V$ with $U\Subset V\Subset D$,
there exists $\phi_V\in\mathscr{C}_D$ such that $0\leq\phi_V\leq1$ on $D$, $\phi_V=1$ on $V$ and 
$\1_U\mathbb{E}_{\cdot}[(1-\phi_V)|\tilde{u}|(X_{\tau_U})]\in D(\mathscr{E}_U)_e$. 
\item[{\rm (5)}] $u\in D(\mathscr{E})_{\loc}$, there exists an intrinsic metric ${\sf d}$ in the sense of 
\cite[Definition~4.1]{FLW} such that all open balls with respect to ${\sf d}$ are relatively compact, and 
for any relatively compact open sets $U,V$ with $U\Subset V\Subset D$,
there exists ${\sf d}$-Lipschitz function $\phi_V$ with 
compact support in $D$ such that  $0\leq\phi_V\leq1$ on $D$, $\phi_V=1$ on $V$ and 
$\mathbb{E}_{\cdot}[(1-\phi_V)|\tilde{u}|(X_{\tau_U})]\in D(\mathscr{E}_U)_e$. 
\end{enumerate}
Then \eqref{eq:2.3} holds for $u$.

[Lemma lem:mtfact of arXiv:2608.05089, 'Correlation decay in area-tilted line ensembles'] Suppose that $\Omega$ is a topological space and that $(\nu_N)_{N \in \mathbb{N}}$ are probability measures on $\Omega$
converging weakly to the probability measure $\nu$.
If $f : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ is a bounded continuous function and $A \subseteq \Omega$ is a Borel set
with $\nu(\partial A) = 0$, then
\begin{equation}
    \mu_N(dx) \propto f(x) \ind*{A}(x) \nu_N(dx)
    \qquad \text{converges weakly to} \qquad
    \mu(dx) \propto f(x) \ind*{A}(x) \nu(dx),
\end{equation}
where $\mu_N$ and $\mu$ are normalized to be probability measures.
title: Lemma lem:mtfact of arXiv:2608.05089

Own-work restricted-data theorem, proof unaudited (C006 v2); novelty not established. Fix n,m,d>=1, unit u, labels y_i in {-1,1}, gamma<=r_i<=1 with gamma>0, and x_i=y_i*r_i*u. Let phi(z)=max(z,lambda*z), 0<lambda<1, and f_i=m^-1 sum_j a_j phi(w_j dot x_i). Train BOTH layers simultaneously on average logistic loss with actual step m*eta, eta>0, choosing a derivative in [lambda,1] at zero. Write b_j=w_j dot u, s_j=a_j+b_j, d_j=a_j-b_j; require every s_j(0)!=0. Then all a_j*b_j become positive after finite time; thereafter loss is strictly decreasing and tends to zero. This holds almost surely for iid N(0,sigma^2) initialization of all weights at any sigma>0. An explicit high-probability time bound is as follows. For delta in (0,1) and epsilon in (0,log(2)), define c0=2*eta*lambda*gamma/[max(1,eta)*(1+eta)], c1=eta*lambda*gamma/(1+eta), Pbar=4*sqrt(2)*(m/delta)^(3/2), Bbar=log(2*Pbar)/c0, Kmin=3*lambda*gamma*sigma^2*delta^2/(64*m^2), Fbar=(2*sigma^2/delta)*exp(2*eta*Bbar), T0bar=ceil(Bbar*(1+exp(Fbar))), and Cbar=max(0,log(log(1/epsilon)/Kmin)/(2*c1)). With probability >=1-delta, L_t<=epsilon for every integer t>=T0bar+ceil(n*Cbar/(1-exp(-epsilon))). The same event works for all epsilon. The proof uses exact per-neuron updates s_j^+=(1+k_j)s_j, d_j^+=(1-k_j)d_j, where eta*lambda*gamma*G<=k_j<=eta*G and G is average logistic weight. The cumulative sum of G cannot be finite, since that would bound parameters and hence keep G positive. Ratios contract into |d_j|<=|s_j|/2, fixing all branches and making all margins grow. The probability estimate uses a Gaussian density bound plus Markov and a union bound, not independence between norm and small-ball events. The times can be extremely large; neither Cai et al.'s sharp eta dependence nor convergence for multidirectional data is established. 13149 passing finite exact rational checks support selected algebra only; the analytic theorem remains unaudited. No formal certificate or numerical Gaussian simulation is claimed.
Collinear signed separable data with gamma<=r_i<=1; arbitrary sample count, labels and width.
Literal leaky activation, both layers trained simultaneously, positive arbitrary step and allowed derivative at zero.
Nonzero expanding coordinates deterministically; the quantified Gaussian bound assumes independent equal-variance N(0,sigma^2) coordinates.
Proof (unaudited), C006 v2; no novelty, full-data theorem, sharp Cai rate or formal certificate claimed.

Let X = (X_1, ..., X_n) have independent coordinates with finite ranges, f a real function of X, and f = sum over S of f_S its Hoeffding (ANOVA) decomposition over subsets S of {1, ..., n}: f_S depends only on X_S, f_empty = E f, and E[f_S | X_T] = 0 unless S is inside T. Put w_S = E[f_S^2] and W_k = sum over |S| = k of w_S, the variance at interaction order k. For 0 <= r <= n let R_r be the average over r-element sets A of E Var(f | X_{A^c}). Then R_r = Var(f) - H_{n - r} = sum_{k=1}^n [1 - binom(n - k, r)/binom(n, r)] W_k (the ratio read as 0 when r > n - k), so R_r is nondecreasing in r. If X^(A) keeps X_{A^c} and replaces X_A by an independent draw from its own law, then E Var(f | X_{A^c}) = (1/2) E[(f(X) - f(X^(A)))^2]. In particular n R_1 = sum_i E Var(f | X_{-i}) = sum_k k W_k.

body:
Let Lambda be a compact hyperbolic set for a diffeomorphism f. There exist a neighbourhood U of Lambda and constants C > 0 and delta_0 > 0 such that: whenever a point x and an integer n satisfy f^k(x) in U for 0 <= k <= n and d(f^n(x), x) < delta < delta_0, there is a genuine PERIODIC point p with f^n(p) = p and d(f^k(p), f^k(x)) <= C delta for every 0 <= k <= n. In words, an orbit segment that almost closes up lies uniformly close to an exactly periodic orbit of the same period. This is the standard device for producing many periodic orbits in a hyperbolic set and for approximating invariant measures by measures on periodic orbits.
Hyperbolicity on the compact set, and the whole segment staying in the neighbourhood U.
The period of the produced orbit is exactly n, and closeness is uniform along the segment.

[Theorem 4 (Uniform growing-window hard-edge comparison) of arXiv:2608.27641, 'Hard-Edge Determinant Fields and Second-Moment Universality for Random Matrix Ratios'] For each \(p\geq1\), fix \(L_p<\infty\). Let
\(\left(\Xi_n\right)_{n\geq1}\) be complex random variables satisfying
\[
\E\left[\Xi_n\right]=0,
\qquad
\E\left[\left|\Xi_n\right|^2\right]=1,
\qquad
\E\left[\Xi_n^2\right]=0,
\qquad
\sup_{n\geq1}
\E\left[\left|\Xi_n\right|^p\right]
\leq L_p
\]
for every \(p\geq1\). Suppose that \(A_n\) has independent entries with common law
\(\Xi_n\) and is almost surely invertible for every \(n\). This last condition is automatic under the density assumption imposed in the triangular-array application below.

There exist constants \(c_{\mathrm{win}},c_{\mathrm{cmp}}>0\) and
\(n_0<\infty\), depending only on a finite collection of the bounds
\(\left(L_p\right)_{p\geq1}\), such that, for every
\[
1\leq m\leq n^{c_{\mathrm{win}}},
\qquad
n\geq n_0,
\]
and every Borel set
\(\Omega\subseteq\left[0,\infty\right)^m\),
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
&\Pr\left(
\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_{n,m}^{\mathrm{Gin}}
\in
\Omega\setminus
\partial_{n^{-c_{\mathrm{cmp}}}}\Omega
\right)
-
n^{-c_{\mathrm{cmp}}}
\leq
\Pr\left(
\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_{n,m}\in\Omega
\right)
\leq
\Pr\left(
\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_{n,m}^{\mathrm{Gin}}
\in
\Omega\cup
\partial_{n^{-c_{\mathrm{cmp}}}}\Omega
\right)
+
n^{-c_{\mathrm{cmp}}}.
\end{aligned}

\end{equation}
The constants are uniform over all triangular arrays satisfying the displayed moment and circularity conditions.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:d7d24572a68ce4263098c324d399774708859cfdac59493b76d5d2697bef2a55","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/d7/d7d24572a68ce4263098c324d399774708859cfdac59493b76d5d2697bef2a55.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:cbac8f169ff863a9595053ddefd9aa680d7116085e24b8a5c3f7297ee2ff2704","bundle_entry_key":"scalar-forced-urn-wright-fisher-generator-limit","bundle_id":"population.w336-p0087-checked-attempt-20261010","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability theory","draft":"w336/bundle_004.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.reinforcement:scalar-forced-urn-wright-fisher-generator-limit","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# P0087: stationary synchronization and covariance at f=c*r^2

Status: proof written; w346 KEEP pending. This proves a full stationary-law limit, stationary moments and a scalar generator limit under conditional independence. It does not prove the general network's functional diffusion limit or its initial layer.

Assume a fixed finite irreducible row-stochastic Q, its stationary probability row vector pi, p in [0,1]^d, c>0, r>0, f=c*r^2 and r+f<=1. Update

    Z'=(1-r-f)Z+r X+f p,

with conditionally independent X_i given Z, and P(X_i=1|Z)=(QZ)_i. There is a unique stationary law on [0,1]^d. Its mean is z*=f*((r+f)I-rQ)^(-1)p. Write pbar=pi.p and K=sum pi_i^2. As r decreases to zero, its stationary covariance satisfies

    Cov(Z) -> [K*pbar*(1-pbar)/(2c+K)]*1*1^T.

Proof of existence/uniqueness: the transition is Feller on a compact cube. Couple two states using the same independent uniforms for their Bernoulli coordinates. Because 1-r-f>=0, the weighted L1 distance has expected next value at most (1-f) times its present value; use pi Q=pi. Thus stationary laws are unique and the transition contracts in this Wasserstein distance. Taking expectations yields the displayed mean; the matrix is invertible because its eigenvalues have positive real part.

For synchronization, let D=diag(pi), S=pi.Z, and E_Q(z)=z^T D(I-Q)z=(1/2)sum pi_i Q_ij(z_i-z_j)^2. At stationarity, with Delta=r(X-Z)+f(p-Z),

    2r E[E_Q(Z)] = 2f E[<Z,p-Z>_D] + E[||Delta||_D^2]
                   <= 2f+(r+f)^2 = O(r^2).

Irreducibility makes E_Q(z)>=gamma*||z-1*(pi.z)||_D^2 for some fixed gamma>0: the finite symmetric quadratic form has kernel precisely the constants. Hence E||Z-1*S||_D^2=O(r). Also E[S]=pbar exactly, so z*_i tends to pbar.

The martingale innovation for S has conditional variance r^2 sum pi_i^2 (QZ)_i(1-(QZ)_i); conditional independence is used exactly here. Total variance at stationarity gives

    (2f-f^2) Var(S)=r^2 sum pi_i^2 E[(QZ)_i(1-(QZ)_i)].

Synchronization shows (QZ)_i-S tends to zero in L2. The variables are bounded, so for any subsequential limit V of Var(S), division by r^2 gives 2c V=K*(pbar*(1-pbar)-V). Its solution is unique. Every subsequence has that limit, and synchronization gives the full covariance limit.

For the scalar case Q=(1), stationarity gives the exact variance

    Var(Z)=r^2*p*(1-p)/(2f-f^2+r^2)
          =p*(1-p)/(1+2c-c^2*r^2).

For h in C^3([0,1]), the one-step scalar generator divided by r^2 converges uniformly to

    Lh(z)=c(p-z)h'(z)+(1/2)z(1-z)h''(z).

Indeed E[Delta]=c*r^2(p-z), E[Delta^2]=r^2*z(1-z)+c^2*r^4(p-z)^2, and |Delta|<=r+cr^2. Taylor's remainder, divided by r^2, is bounded by ||h'''||_infinity*r*(1+cr)^3/6, with the additional second-order drift term O(r^2). This identifies the candidate Wright-Fisher generator; path tightness and martingale-problem uniqueness are further steps.

Theorem (full stationary law). Under the same fixed-network assumptions and 0<pbar<1, the joint stationary law of Z converges weakly to Y*1, where

    Y ~ Beta(2c*pbar/K, 2c*(1-pbar)/K).

Proof: write S'=S+f*(pbar-S)+r*eta, where eta=pi.(X-QZ), E[eta|Z]=0, |eta|<=1 and E[eta^2|Z]=sum pi_i^2 (QZ)_i(1-(QZ)_i). For every polynomial h, the stationary Taylor identity divided by r^2 gives

    0=c E[(pbar-S)h'(S)]
      +(1/2)E[sum pi_i^2 (QZ)_i(1-(QZ)_i)*h''(S)] + O(r).

The drift-square contribution is O(r^2), and the third-order remainder is uniformly O(r). The proved L2 synchronization implies that the sum inside the second term differs from K*S*(1-S) by a quantity tending to zero in L1. Every subsequence has a further weakly convergent subsequence of S because [0,1] is compact. If its limiting moments are mu_k, use h(s)=s^k, k>=1, to obtain

    [2c+K*(k-1)]*mu_k = [2c*pbar+K*(k-1)]*mu_(k-1), mu_0=1.

These are exactly the moments of the displayed beta law: iterating gives the product of (2c*pbar/K+j)/(2c/K+j) for j=0,...,k-1, which also follows by integrating the beta density. A probability law on [0,1] is determined by its moments, since polynomials approximate continuous functions uniformly. Hence all subsequential limits agree and S converges weakly. Synchronization gives Z-S*1 tending to zero in probability, so the joint law converges to Y*1. If pbar=0 or 1, positivity of pi forces every p_i to be that endpoint and the unique stationary law is the corresponding point mass.

This proof uses all polynomial moments, not an inference from the first two moments. It proves convergence of stationary laws, not a limit for trajectories begun away from synchronization. Without conditional independence, the innovation variance changes. For example, Q=J_d/d, constant p, and one shared Bernoulli coin across all coordinates preserve a synchronized state and give the scalar beta parameters 2cp and 2c(1-p), rather than 2cdp and 2cd(1-p).

For reproducible finite checks, the exact covariance identity is

    V=B V B^T+r^2*diag(s*(1-s)-diag(Q V Q^T)),
    B=(1-r-f)I+rQ, s=Q z*.

Checks: the scalar exact formula; first four scalar stationary moments; exact polynomial generators; finite-network covariance systems; first four moments of the exact consensus Markov chain for Q=J_d/d at d=2,3,5; a common-coin control that changes the beta variance. body: [Cor coho to compact indep of ambient of arXiv:2605.16921, '${\ASL_n}(\mathbb Z)$ invariant random subsets of $\mathbb Z^n$'] Let $\Gamma$ be a countable group, $(X, \nu)$ an ergodic $\Gamma$-system, $G$ a locally compact second countable group, and $\alpha: \Gamma \times X \to G$ a cocycle. Suppose that $\alpha$ is cohomologous (in $G$) to a cocycle taking values in a compact subgroup, and that $\alpha(\Gamma \times X) \subset H$ for some closed subgroup $H \subset G$. Then $\alpha$ is cohomologous in $H$ to a cocycle taking values in a compact subgroup.

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2608.01081, 'The Optimal Rate in the Averaged Random-Marginal Central Limit Theorem for Log-Concave Mea'] Let $\mu$ and $\nu$ be probability measures on $\R$ with finite first
moments, and let
\[
 Q_\mu(s)=\inf\{t:F_\mu(t)\ge s\},
 \qquad 0<s<1,
\]
with the analogous definition for $Q_\nu$. Then
\begin{equation}
 W_1(\mu,\nu)
 =\int_0^1|Q_\mu(s)-Q_\nu(s)|\,\dd s
 =\int_\R|F_\mu(t)-F_\nu(t)|\,\dd t.
\end{equation}
Moreover, if $h:\R\to\R$ is one-Lipschitz, then
\begin{equation}
 \left|\int h\,\dd\mu-\int h\,\dd\nu\right|
 \le W_1(\mu,\nu).
\end{equation}

an $n$-sample, and let $\widehat i\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_i Z_i$. There is a universal

    n\eta\geq C\log\frac{1}{\eta\delta}
\]

    \end{itemize}

\[
	\eta (L^2(0,1))=1\qquad \text{and}\qquad M_2(|\eta |)<\infty.
\]
Then, there exists a unique minimizer $f^* \in \mathcal{K}$ of the functional 
\[	
	E:L^2(0,1) \to \mathbb{R},\qquad E(f) = \int_{L^2(0,1)}  \|f-g\|^2{\rm d}\eta(g)
\]
and it is characterized by
\[
	 f^* = P_\mathcal{K}\left( \int_{L^2(0,1)}g\,{\rm d}\eta(g)\right).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:near-core of arXiv:2609.02845, 'Degeneracy bounds, stability, and a sharp gap for $B$-colorings'] Let $d$, $\Delta$, and $s$ be integers satisfying
$1\le d\le\Delta$ and $0\le s<\Delta$.  Let $G$ be a
$d$-degenerate graph with $\Delta(G)\le\Delta$.  If
$q_B(G)\ge d\Delta-s$, then there is a vertex $v$ with distinct
neighbors $u_1,\ldots,u_d$ such that
\begin{equation}

 d\bigl(\Delta-d_G(u_1)\bigr)
 +\sum_{j=2}^{d}|N_G(u_1)\setminus N_G(u_j)|
 \le s.
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\[
  \left|\bigcap_{j=1}^{d}N_G(u_j)\right|\ge\Delta-s,
\]
and hence $G$ contains a copy of $K_{d,\Delta-s}$.

body:
The spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint operators (an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors, real eigenvalues tending to 0, ||T|| = max |eigenvalue|, min-max characterisation of eigenvalues) requires self-adjointness or at least normality. Compactness alone gives only the Riesz-Schauder picture: the nonzero spectrum consists of eigenvalues of finite algebraic multiplicity accumulating only at 0, and the set of such eigenvalues may be empty. The standard counterexample is the Volterra operator on L^2([0,1]), (V f)(x) = integral from 0 to x of f(t) dt, which is Hilbert-Schmidt (kernel k(x,t) = 1 for t < x, 0 otherwise) hence compact, but has no eigenvalues at all: V f = lambda f with lambda nonzero forces f to be absolutely continuous with f' = f/lambda and f(0) = 0, so f = 0; and V f = 0 forces f = 0 a.e. Thus sigma(V) = {0}, spectral radius 0, while ||V|| = 2/pi; the singular values of V are 1/((n + 1/2) pi), n >= 0, so V is Hilbert-Schmidt but not trace class, and the moduli of its eigenvalues (all zero) are nowhere near its singular values. Consequences for an auditor: (a) 'compact, so expand in eigenfunctions' is invalid without normality; the right substitute is the Schmidt decomposition in singular values, which always exists; (b) 'compact, so the spectral radius equals the norm' is false; (c) Rayleigh-quotient and min-max formulas for eigenvalues are statements about self-adjoint operators and become statements about singular values otherwise; (d) Mercer-type positivity conclusions require a self-adjoint positive kernel, not just an L^2 kernel.
the operator is compact on a Hilbert space
self-adjointness or normality is what the eigenbasis conclusion needs
for a general compact operator only the Riesz-Schauder conclusions and the singular value decomposition are available
title: Pitfall: Diagonalizing a Compact Operator Needs Self-Adjointness (or Normality)

\end{align*}
We refer to the measures in $P\!_\mathrm{a.i.}$ as finitely atomic measures having the 
affine independence property. Let $C\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be a  convex subset and let
\begin{align*}
G_\mathrm{fin}(C) & \textstyle
:= \{\mu\in P\!_\mathrm{fin} : \int\mathbf{p}\mathrm{d}\mu\in C\},\\

G_\mathrm{a.i.}(C) & \textstyle
:= \{\mu\in P\!_\mathrm{a.i.} : \int\mathbf{p}\mathrm{d}\mu\in C\}.
\end{align*}
Let $Q\subset P$ be a convex set of probability measures. Denoting the components of 
$\mathbf{p}=(p_1,\ldots,p_d)$ by $p_i\colon X\to\mathbb{R}$, $i=1,\ldots,d$, we define
\begin{align*}
Q^\mathbf{p} & \textstyle 
:= \{\mu\in Q : \text{$p_i$ is $\mu$-integrable $\forall i=1,\dots,d$}\,\},\\

G(C) & \textstyle
:= \{\mu\in Q^\mathbf{p} : \int\mathbf{p}\mathrm{d}\mu\in C\}.
\end{align*}
We abbreviate $G_\mathrm{fin}(\mathbf{q}):=G_\mathrm{fin}(\{\mathbf{q}\})$, etc., for singletons 
$\{\mathbf{q}\}$ with elements $\mathbf{q}\in\mathbb{R}^d$.

[Proposition 16 of arXiv:2609.01574, 'A linear bound for Fujita's freeness conjecture'] Let $Z$ be a normal projective variety of dimension $d\geq2$, let $x\in Z$ be a closed point, and let $\mathcal I_x\subset\mathcal O_Z$ be the ideal sheaf of $x$. Let $f\colon Y\to Z$ be the normalized blow-up of $\mathcal I_x$, write $\mathcal I_x\mathcal O_Y=\mathcal O_Y(-E)$ with $E$ effective, and let $H:=-E$. Then 

\begin{enumerate}
\item $H$ is $f$-ample and $F\cdot H^{d-1}>0$ for every prime component $F$ of $E$.
\item $-H^d=\mult_xZ$.
\item $K_Y\cdot H^{d-1}=(d-1)\mult_xZ-2\ebarone(\m_{Z,x})$.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, $\sum_F\ord_F(\m_{Z,x})(F\cdot H^{d-1})=\mult_xZ$, where $F$ runs over the prime components of $E$.

[Theorem 6 of arXiv:2609.02385, 'Kinetic Fokker--Planck Equations with Drifts in a Supercritical Range'] Under Assumption {\bf (${\text{H}}$)}, the Cauchy problem
$$\p_tu=\Delta_vu+v\cdot\nn_xu+b\cdot\nn_vu+f,\quad u|_{t\leq0}=0,$$
admits a unique global weak solution in the sense of Definition \ref{weaksubsol}, within the class of solutions which are bounded and have finite uniformly local kinetic energy on every finite time interval. Moreover, for every $T>0$ and $t\in[0,T]$,
$$\|u\|_{\mL^\infty((0,t)\times\mR^{2d})}\lesssim_{C_T}\|f\|_{\mL_t^{q_0}\mL_z^{\bbp_0}(0,t)},$$
where $C_T$ depends only on $T,d,q_1,\bbp_1,q_0,\bbp_0,\b$ and $\|b\|_{L^{q_1}((0,T+4);L^{\bbp_1}(\mR^{2d}))}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:sec5-continuum-probe of arXiv:2607.18070, 'The Brownian loop-catcher'] Fix finitely many pairs
\((x_i,y_i)\in D^2\), \(1\leq i\leq r\), with \(x_i\ne y_i\);
repetitions of a pair are allowed.  For every
\(0\leq\lambda\leq1\) there is a random compact set \(C\Subset D\), with
at most \(r\) nondegenerate components, such that for every compact
\(E\subset\overline{D}\),
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb{E}_C\!\left[
 \mathbf 1_{\{C\cap E=\varnothing\}}e^{-\lambda m_D(C,E)}\right]
 =\prod_{i=1}^r
   \frac{G_{D\setminus E}(x_i,y_i)}{G_D(x_i,y_i)}.
\end{equation}
Here a numerator is zero if an endpoint belongs to \(E\) or the endpoints
 lie in different components of \(D\setminus E\).
If all pairs share one endpoint, \(C\) can be chosen connected.

[Proposition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Assuming that $a\in A$ is normal, $aa^*=a^*a$, its law corresponds to a probability measure on its spectrum $\sigma(a)\subset\mathbb C$, according to the following formula:
$$tr(P(a))=\int_{\sigma(a)}P(x)d\mu(x)$$
When the trace is faithful we have $supp(\mu)=\sigma(a)$. Also, in the particular case where the variable is self-adjoint, $a=a^*$, this law is a real probability measure.

Own-work draft; T419-C010 v1, proof (unaudited), no novelty claimed; known-theorem application. Let X be any full-row-rank p-by-n real design, Delta a fixed m-by-p matrix, and Z=Delta X+E, where the entries of E are independent N(0,sigma^2), sigma>0. Fix 1<=r<min(m,p), and minimize (1/(2n))||BA X-Z||F^2 over B m-by-r,A r-by-p. Almost surely over E, every second-order stationary point is a global rank-r empirical regression optimum, and every nonglobal critical point has a negative Hessian direction, for every positive definite covariance C=XX^T/n without a condition-number restriction. Writing H=C^(1/2), M=(ZX^T/n)H^(-1), its product is the unique reduced-rank regression estimate M_r H^(-1), with M_r the rank-r singular-value truncation. For iid Gaussian input vectors, full row rank holds almost surely when n>=p. This does not prove that ordinary factor GD from B0=0 and Gaussian A0 reaches an SOSP or has the estimator's statistical risk; those trajectory, stopping and integrability conditions remain to be established.

[Lemma 19 of arXiv:2608.26565, 'A Horizon-Free Extrinsic Penrose Inequality'] Let $\Sigma$ be a connected compact strongly stable minimal capillary surface with
\[
 \langle\nu_\Sigma,\nu_S\rangle=-\tanh t,
 \qquad t\geq0,
\]
and suppose $H_S\geq0$ along $\partial\Sigma$.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \frac12\int_\Sigma|h_\Sigma|^2\,dA
 +\cosh t\int_{\partial\Sigma}H_S\,ds
 \leq2\pi\chi(\Sigma).
 
\end{equation}
In particular, $\Sigma$ is a disk.

[Thm Weak.Win of arXiv:2609.02588, 'Ramsey-type results for Maker-Breaker games'] Let a hypergraph $(X,\mathcal{F})$ and a bias $b\in\mathbb{N}$ be given. If
$$
\sum_{F\in \mathcal{F}} (1+b)^{-|F|} > \frac{b^2}{(1+b)^3} \Delta_2(\mathcal{F}) |X|
$$
holds, Maker (as first player) has a winning strategy for the $(1:b)$ Maker-Breaker game on 
$(X,\mathcal{F})$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Weak Win Criterion,~Theorem 2 in~\cite{beck1982remarks}

body:
[Lemma lem:lapl of arXiv:2607.26169, 'Scaling and partial universality of the height zero probability in the 2D Abelian sandpile'] Let $g : \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ have continuous and bounded partial derivatives of order up to $3$.
Then for any $u \in \mathcal{V}$ we have that
\eqnst{
  \Delta g(u)
  = \sum_{u' \sim u} (g(u) - g(u'))
  = - \frac{1}{4} \Delta^{(c)} g (u) \sum_{u' \sim u} |u - u'|^2
    + O( \| D^3 g \|_\infty \max_{u'\sim u} |u'-u|^3 ), }
where $\Delta^{(c)} g = (\partial_{11} + \partial_{22}) g$ is the (continuous) Laplacian.
title: Lemma lem:lapl of arXiv:2607.26169

[Thm 4 of arXiv:2607.17576, 'How much randomness is needed to symmetrize a random variable?'] Let $\lambda>0$. Let $X\sim \text{Exp}(\lambda)$ be an exponential random variable with the probability density function $f_X(x)=\lambda e^{-\lambda x}\mathbbm{1}_{\mathbb{R}_+}(x)$. Let $Y$ be an absolutely continuous independent symmetrizer of $X$.  Then we have
$$
\Var (Y)\ge \Var(X).
$$
Equality holds if and only if $Y$ is an independent copy of $-X$.

body:
[Prop subseq of arXiv:2606.30517, '\textsc{Convergence towards Ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations with a focus on Diestel--'] Assume that $t_n\in\mathbb R$ and $\lambda_n>0$ for all $n\in\mathbb N$ such that $\lambda_n\to 0$. Then, the following two statements are equivalent:
		\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
			\item  The shifted Poisson point process $\iota_{t_n}(X^{(\lambda_n)})$ converges weakly as $\lambda\downarrow 0$ to a point process on $\mathrm{Lip}_1$ with respect to the topology of $\mathcal M$,  and its limit is nonempty with positive probability.
			\item  The sequence of measures $\lambda_n \iota_{t_n}^*\mu$‌ converges in $\mathcal M$ and its limit is nonzero.
		\end{enumerate}
		If these conditions hold, then:
		\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
			\setcounter{enumi}{2}
			\item  $t_n\to\infty$ and the measure $\nu\coloneqq\lim_n \lambda_n \iota_{t_n}^*\mu$ is supported on $\widehat{\partial E}$.
			\item  The weak limit of $\iota_{t_n} X^{(\lambda_n)}$ is a (marked) Poisson point process on $\widehat{\partial E}$ with intensity measure $\nu$, namely $\Phi\coloneqq(\Theta_i,\Delta_i)_{i \geq 1}$.
			\item  \textsc{[Convergence of Ordered Points]} Assuming that either $E$ is a graph (with the graph-distance metric) or that the delays $(\Delta_i)_{i\geq 1}$ are distinct a.s., if the points $(\Theta_i,\Delta_i)_{i\geq 1}$ are ordered with the same rule as in (def:PPP of the paper), then the joint distribution of the ordered sequence of points $\left(\iota_{t_n}X^{(\lambda_n)}_i\right)_{i\geq 1}$ converges to that of $(\Theta_i,\Delta_i)_{i\geq 1}$ as $n\to\infty$.
		\end{enumerate}
title: \textsc{Converging Subsequences}

[Thm thm 5.1 of arXiv:2411.01847, 'Well-Posedness of Stochastic Chemotaxis System'] Let $(u, v, \tau_m)$ be a local mild solution of system ((main2 of the paper)), with $\tau_m$ defined by
    \begin{align*}
        \tau_m = \inf \{ t > 0 \mid \|u\|_{\Upsilon^u_t} \geq m \}.
    \end{align*}
    Then, for $p\geq 2$, the following It\^{o} formula for $\|u(t)\|_{p}^{p}$ holds $\mathbb{P}$-a.s. for all $t \in [0, \tau_m]$,
    \begin{align}
        &\|u(t)\|_{p}^{p} - \|u_0\|_{p}^{p} +p(p - 1)  \int_0^{t}\|\nabla u^{\frac{p}{2}}(s)\|_2^2 \, ds \nonumber \\
        &= p(p - 1) \chi \int_0^{t} \int_\mathcal{O} u^{p - 1}(s) \nabla u(s) \cdot \nabla G * u(s) \, dx \, ds \nonumber \\
        &\quad + p \int_0^{t} \int_\mathcal{O} u^{p - 1}(s) g(u(s)) \, dx \, ds \nonumber \\
        &\quad + p \sum_{i=1}^\infty \int_0^{t} \int_\mathcal{O} b_i\|u(s)\|_q^{r}|u(s)|^{p} \, dx \, dW^i_s \nonumber \\
        &\quad + \frac{p(p - 1)}{2} \int_0^{t} \|u(s)\|_q^{2r}\int_\mathcal{O} \sum_{i=1}^\infty b_i^2 |u(s)|^{p} \, dx \, ds.
    \end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm thm 5.1 of arXiv:2411.01847

[Lemma lem:integrals of arXiv:2506.23062, 'Shifted Composition IV\@: \\ Toward Ballistic Acceleration for Log-Concave Sampling'] The following hold for sufficiently large $c_0$.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item For $\omega > 0$ and $T_0 \leqslant (T+Ah-1/|\omega|)\wedge t$, $\int_0^{T_0} \exp(-c\,(\Lambda_t -\Lambda_s))\,\mathrm{d} s \lesssim [1-\exp(-|\omega|\,(T+Ah-t))]^{cc_0}/|\omega|$.
        \item For $\omega < 0$ and $T_0 \leqslant (T+Ah-1/|\omega|)\wedge t$, $\int_0^{T_0} \exp(-c\,(\Lambda_t-\Lambda_s))\,\mathrm{d} s \lesssim [\exp(|\omega|\,(T+Ah-t))-1]^{cc_0} \exp(-cc_0|\omega|\,(T+Ah-T_0))/|\omega|$.
        \item For $t \geqslant T_1 \geqslant T_0 \geqslant T+Ah-1/|\omega|$ and $\ell\geqslant 0$ an absolute constant, $\int_{T_0}^t \eta_s^{-\ell} \exp(-c\,(\Lambda_t-\Lambda_s))\,\mathrm{d} s \lesssim {(T+Ah-t)}^{\ell+1}$.
        Moreover, $\int_{T_0}^{T_1} \eta_s^{-\ell} \exp(-c\,(\Lambda_t-\Lambda_s))\,\mathrm{d} s \lesssim (T+Ah-t)^{c'c_0}/(T+Ah-T_1)^{c'c_0-\ell-1}$.
    \end{enumerate}

\begin{equation}
    \max_{s \in \{\mathcal{P},\mathcal{T}\}}\mleft| \mathrm{Var}(X_s(x))-\lambda_2(a,b)\mleft(x+\frac{a+b}{2} \mright)\mright| \le C_{a,b} \mathcal R_2(x),

    \mleft(\dfrac{4e}{x/a}\mright)^{x/a-(5+(a+b)/(2a))},

\end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition 38 of arXiv:2608.05931, 'Effective Lagrangian regularity and the uniqueness threshold for random H\"older velocity '] Suppose $U=\sum_{j=0}^\infty u^j$ satisfies Assumption~\ref{asmp:main for refreshing} for some $\beta>0$. Additionally, suppose that for some $\alpha\in(0,1)$ and $p>1$, we have a constant $K\geq 1$ such that for $n\in\{0,1,2\}$ and all $j\in\N$,
\begin{equation}
\|\nabla^n u^j\|_{L^p_\omega C^0_{t,x}}\leq K 2^{(n-\alpha)j}.
\end{equation}
    Then for all $\eps>\frac{\beta}{p}$ and $A\geq 1$, there exist vector fields $\{u^{j,A}\}_{j \geq 0}$ (on possibly a larger probability space, though coupled to the original $u^j$) also satisfying Assumption~\ref{asmp:main for refreshing} such that for all $j\geq 0$, $n\in\{0,1,2\}$,
\[\|\nabla^n u^{j,A}\|_{C^0_{t,x}} \leq A K 2^{(n-\alpha+\eps)j},
\]
and, letting $U^A:=\sum_{j=0}^\infty u^{j,A}$, there exists $C(\beta,p,\eps)>0$ such that
\[\P(U^A\neq U)\leq C A^{1-p}.\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 38 of arXiv:2608.05931

body: Green-Tao theorem: The sequence of prime numbers contains arbitrarily long finite arithmetic progressions; that is, for every natural number k >= 1 there exist positive integers a and d such that the k numbers a, a + d, a + 2d, ..., a + (k-1)d are all prime. (The progressions are finite: no infinite arithmetic progression can consist only of primes.) The theorem was proved by Ben Green and Terence Tao in 2004; the proof extends Szemeredi's theorem, via a transference principle, from sets of positive density in the integers to subsets of positive relative density inside a pseudorandom set of almost primes.
title: Green–Tao theorem

body:
[Proposition 18 (Structural properties of the Einstein--Navier--Stokes models) of arXiv:2608.31171, '\bf Finite-energy spacetimes with torus symmetry. \\ \Large Cauchy stability of Einstein--'] Consider the system of equations in \autoref{def-prod-areal-flow} under the pressure assumptions~\eqref{hyperbolic-eos-zero}.
Then the following properties hold for sufficiently regular solutions~$(\Phi,\Psi,\zeta)$.
\bei

\item \emph{Hyperbolicity.} \emph{Under the non-vacuum condition $- \Jbb \cdot \Jbb>0$,} the evolution system consisting of~\eqref{eqchi-evol} and either~\eqref{prod-energy-conservation} or~\eqref{energy-dissip-Sigma} is a first-order hyperbolic system of $12+\dim\mathscr E$ nonlinear balance laws with characteristic cones in the causal cone.

\item \emph{Constraint propagation.}  Given a solution of this hyperbolic system, if the constraints~\eqref{eqchi-constr} on $\log\Omega, K_2, K_3$ are satisfied at initial time they propagate to all future times.

\item \emph{Equivalence property.}
Given such a solution $(\Phi,\Psi,\zeta)$, together with the value of the modular parameter~$\tau$ at one spacetime point and the spatial averages of $G,H$ at initial time, one recovers a unique solution $(g,\beta,\zeta)$ of the Einstein--Navier--Stokes equations, specifically a particle-production relaxation flow (\autoref{def-prod-pot}) or dissipated-energy relaxation flow (\autoref{def-diss-en}).
In particular, the wave equation for the lapse~\eqref{eq:waveconffac-NS} below holds.

\item \emph{Particle-number current.}
The convex current derived from the potential~$\chi$ satisfies
\bel{eq:pot-areal-production}
\aligned
\divuntrois\vNumb_\chi
& = \mathfrak d_{\mathscr B}
\quad && \text{(particle-production areal flow),}
\\
\divuntrois\vNumb_\chi & = 0
\quad && \text{(dissipated-energy areal flow),}
\endaligned
\ee
where $\mathfrak d_{\mathscr B} = \zeta_{\alpha\beta}\mathscr B^{\alpha\beta}(\beta,\zeta) \geq 0$.
\eei (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Structural properties of the Einstein--Navier--Stokes models

[Lemma of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Let $T$ and ${\mathcal{C}}$ be as in the proposition. Then $\lambda$ is a Bousfield localization such that the unit is pointwise given by cocartesian edges.
    \begin{proof}
        The first statement is clear as $\lambda$ is left adjoint to the fully faithful inclusion ${\mathcal{C}}(1)\hookrightarrow{\mathcal{C}}$. For the identification of the units, let $x\in{\mathcal{C}}(A)$ and let $\tilde a\colon x\to x'$ be a cocartesian lift of the unique map $a\colon A\to 1$. Then
        \[
            \begin{tikzcd}
                {\textup{Hom}}_{\textup{Un}^\textup{ct}}(x',y)\arrow[d]\arrow[r, "-\circ\tilde a"] & {\textup{Hom}}_{\textup{Un}^\textup{ct}}(x,y)\arrow[d]\\
                {\textup{Hom}}_T(1,1)\arrow[r, "-\circ a"']&{\textup{Hom}}_T(A,1)
            \end{tikzcd}
        \]
        is a pullback by definition of cocartesian edges. As both spaces in the bottom row are contractible, we see that ${\textup{Hom}}(\tilde a,y)$ is an equivalence. Letting $y$ vary, this is precisely the defining property of a unit for our Bousfield localization.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Unnumbered lemma of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'

[Lemma lem:tautilde-unlikely-back of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix a real number $\lambda \in (0,1)$ and a send sequence $\overline{p}$ with $p_0=1$. Let $j_0$ be a
sufficiently large integer.  
Let  
$\Psi_0$ be the initialising state with
$j^{\Psi_0} = j_0$ and $\tau^{\Psi_0} = \tau_0$.  
Let $\mathrm{hls}$ be  
the $\Psi_0$-backoff bounding rule from Definition~(def:backoff-bounding-rule of the paper).
Let $V$ be a volume process from~$\Psi_0$ with transition rule~$\mathrm{hls}$, send sequence~$\overline{p}$ and birth rate~$\lambda$. For any
$t \ge \tau_0$, 
let   $T(t) = \{\tau_0,\ldots,t\}$.
Then  the following  holds for
every $t >  \tau_0$ and
every tuple
$ 
\overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)} = (\psi_{\tau_0},\dots,\psi_{t-1})$  of high-level states 
such that  
$\mathbb{P}( \overline{\Psi}_{T(t-1)} = \overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)}) > 0$, 
$\textup{type}^{\psi_{t-1}} \in \{ \textup{refilling},\textup{stabilising}\}$, 
and 
$\mathcal{M}_{[j-1]}^{\psi_{t-1}}(\tau^{\psi_{t-1}}) \leq 
2j^{44} 
$, where $j=j^{\psi_{t-1}}$.  
\[
\mathbb{P}(\mbox{the transition into 
$\Psi(\mathrm{back}\textnormal{-}\mathrm{exit}(t-1))$ is a back transition }  \mid 
\overline{\Psi}_{T(t-1)} = \overline{\psi}_{T(t-1)}
 )\leq 
 \exp(-\lambda (\log j )^2/202).
\]
title: Lemma lem:tautilde-unlikely-back of arXiv:2602.21315

[Theorem 4 (Interior regularity under Engelbert--Schmidt conditions) of arXiv:2608.29854, '2608.29854'] Assume \eqref{eq:ES}, let $\cV$ be an admissible form domain with
associated operator $A$, let $q:I\to\mathbb R$ be bounded and Borel,
and recall the strongly continuous semigroup $(T_t^q)_{t\ge0}$ from
\Cref{prop:L2-semigroup}. Let $f\in L^2(I,\mu)$.  For every $t>0$, $T_t^qf$ admits a unique
continuous representative, which we identify with $T_t^qf$.
Furthermore, the following statements hold with $u(t,x)=T_t^qf(x)
$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},ref=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item
For every $k\in\N_0$, $\partial_t^ku$ and
$\partial_x\partial_t^ku$ exist on $(0,\infty)\times I$ and are jointly
continuous there. 

\item
For every $t>0$, $\partial_xu(t,\cdot)\in\AC_{\loc}(I)$, and for almost every $x\in I$,
\begin{equation}
  \partial_tu(t,x)
  =
  a(x)\partial_{xx}u(t,x)
  +b(x)\partial_xu(t,x)-q(x)u(t,x).
\end{equation}
For every $k\in\N_0$, the same assertions hold with $u$ replaced by
$\partial_t^ku$.

\item
If $a$, $b$, and $q$ are continuous on $I$, then
\[
  u\in C^{1,2}((0,\infty)\times I)
\]
and \eqref{eq:a.e.-PDE} holds pointwise on $(0,\infty)\times I$.  Moreover,
$\partial_t^ku\in C^{1,2}((0,\infty)\times I)$ for every $k\in\N_0$.
\end{enumerate}
In addition,
$
  u(t,\cdot)\to f
$
in $L^2(I,\mu)$ as $t\downarrow0$.

[Theorem 6 of arXiv:2606.00945, 'Ising model and percolation: from hexagonal lattice to 3-12 lattice'] Fix a bounded $3$-polygon $(\Omega; A, B, C)$. Suppose $\PO$ is the unique conformal map from $\Omega$ onto the equilateral triangle $\rhd$ with three vertices $(1, \tau, \tau^2)$ such that $\PO(A)=1, \PO(B)=\tau, \PO(C)=\tau^2$. 
Suppose $(\Omega_{\312}^{\delta}; A^{\delta}, B^{\delta}, C^{\delta})$ is a family of discrete polygons such that $(\Omega_{\312}^{\delta}; A^{\delta}, B^{\delta}, C^{\delta})$ converges to $(\Omega; A, B, C)$ in the Carathéodory sense as $\delta\to 0$. 
Consider site percolation with $p=1/2$ in $\Omega_{\312}^{\delta, *}$. 
Then the observable $\PO_{\312}^{\delta}$ defined in~\eqref{eqn::perco_observable} converges to $\PO$ uniformly as $\delta\to 0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 6 of arXiv:2606.00945

[Lemma lem:G8 of arXiv:2608.26765, 'Beyond Client Averaging: A Client-Independent Second-Order Stationary-Bias Component in St'] There exists $C_H<\infty$ such that
\begin{align}
  |\nu_h|&\le C_Hs_{\gamma,N},\qquad h=0,\ldots,H,             \\
  |b_{\gamma,N,H}|&\le C_Hs_{\gamma,N},                                \\
  \sum_{h=0}^{H-1}m_h&=Hb_{\gamma,N,H}+O_H(r_{\gamma,N}).                
\end{align}
This lemma uses only the coarse second-moment result (lem:G5a of the paper) and the finite-step displacement estimate; it does not use (lem:G3 of the paper) or any signed third moment.

[Proposition 7 (Exact recovery restricted to used strokes) of arXiv:2604.25470, 'A mathematical analysis of hierarchical Hopfield models'] In the above setting there exists $a=a(\kappa)>0$ such that, if $U\le N_f^{a-\varepsilon}$ for some
	$\varepsilon>0$, the stroke layer recovers every concept's stroke set exactly from its
	clean cue in the sense that, with probability $1-o(1)$,
	\[
	x_\mu(\eta^{(\alpha)})=\mathbf 1\{\mu\in S_\alpha\}
	\qquad\text{for all }\alpha\le P\text{ and all }\mu\in\mathcal U.
	\]
	Moreover, for each fixed $\alpha$, the same conclusion holds without the union over
	$\alpha$ (i.e.\ only for the fixed cue $\eta^{(\alpha)}$).
	
	Since $U:=|\mathcal U|\le PL$, the strict exact-recovery conclusion holds in particular
	whenever
	\[
	PL \le N_f^{a-\varepsilon}.
	\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Exact recovery restricted to used strokes

[Proposition prop:music-chordal-residual of arXiv:2609.03264, 'Certified Spherical MUSIC for 3D Localization under Adversarial Subspace Perturbations'] Let \(Z=\{{\bm z}_1,\ldots,{\bm z}_s\}\) be a configuration for which
$
    G_Z:=\Phi_Z^*\Phi_Z
$
is invertible, and set
\[
    Q_Z:=\Phi_ZG_Z^{-1/2}.
\]
Then \(Q_Z^*Q_Z=I_s\) and
\[
    \sum_{j=1}^s\widetilde q({\bm z}_j)
    =
    \|(I-P_{\widetilde{\mathcal U}})\Phi_Z\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2.
\]
If
\[
    (1-\mu)I_s
    \preceq
    G_Z
    \preceq
    (1+\mu)I_s,\qquad 0<\mu<1,
\]
then
\begin{eqnarray}
    (1-\mu)
    d_{\mathrm{ch}}^2(
        \mathcal U_Z,\widetilde{\mathcal U}
    )
    \leq
    \sum_{j=1}^s\widetilde q({\bm z}_j)
    \leq
    (1+\mu)
    d_{\mathrm{ch}}^2(
        \mathcal U_Z,\widetilde{\mathcal U}
    ),
\end{eqnarray}
where
\[
    d_{\mathrm{ch}}^2(
        \mathcal U_Z,\widetilde{\mathcal U}
    )
    :=
    \|(I-P_{\widetilde{\mathcal U}})Q_Z\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2
    =
    \frac12
    \|P_{\mathcal U_Z}
       -P_{\widetilde{\mathcal U}}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2.
\]

body:
[Theorem 27 of arXiv:2608.05931, 'Effective Lagrangian regularity and the uniqueness threshold for random H\"older velocity '] Suppose $U = \sum_{j=0}^\infty u^j$ satisfies Assumption~\ref{asmp:main for refreshing} for some $\beta >0$ and let $\alpha \in (0,1)$ such that $\alpha + \beta/2 > 1$. Let
    \[p >\frac{ \beta}{\alpha + \beta/2-1} \lor \frac{\beta}{\alpha}\]
    and suppose for some $K \geq 1$, 
     we have that for all $j \in \N,$ and  $n \in \{0,1,2\},$
     \begin{equation*}
         \|\nabla^n u^j\|_{L^p_\omega \continuous^0_{t,x}} \leq K 2^{(n-\alpha)j}.
     \end{equation*}
     Then there exist $\delta(\alpha,\beta,p)>0, \gamma(\alpha,\beta,p)>0$, and a random field $M : \T^d \to [1,\infty)$ such that $\gamma \to \infty$ as $p \to \infty$ and
        \begin{enumerate}
         \item almost surely $\sup_{y \in \T^d} |M(y)| < \infty$; in fact $\E \big[\big(\log \log\big(\sup_{y \in \T^d} |M(y)| + e\big)\big)^{\gamma}\big]<\infty$,
         \item $\E \big[\big(\log\big(\|M\|_{L^p_y} + 1\big)\big)^{\gamma}\big]<\infty$,
         \item and for any $y,z \in \T^d$, any $w \in C^{1/2 + \delta}([0,1])$ with $w_0=0$, if we have any solution $X$ to~\eqref{eq:main refreshing ODE 0}, and any solution $\tilde X$ to 
          \begin{equation*}
         \tilde X_t=z+\int_0^t U(s,\tilde X_s)\,ds+w_t,\qquad t\in[0,1],
         \end{equation*}
         then we have the stability estimate on the time interval $[0,1]$,
         \[\|X - \tilde X\|_{C^{1/2 +\delta}_t} \leq M(y)\big(|y-z| + \|w\|_{C^{1/2+\delta}_t}\big),\]
        and, in the case that $w=0$, the expansion/compression estimate for all $t \in [0,1],$
        \[\frac{1}{M(y)} |y-z| \leq |X_t - \tilde X_t| \leq M(y) |y-z|.\]
     \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 27 of arXiv:2608.05931

[Proposition prop:adaptive of arXiv:2608.23638, 'Replicable Conformal Prediction'] Fix $\alpha\in(0,1)$, $\rho\in(0,1]$, and a score law with density $f$ continuous and positive at $q=F^{-1}(1-\alpha)$; let $\hat f_n$ be any shared pilot with $\hat f_n\to_pf(q)$, $\hat f_n\ge f_0>0$, independent of both calibration samples, and run \textsc{ReCal}{} with $\beta_n=2B_n/(\hat f_n\rho)$, $\hat\kappa{=}1$. Then, with $Z$ standard normal,
(i) $\mathbb{P}[\tau\neq\tau']\to\mathbb{E}[\min(\rho|Z|/2,1)]\le\rho\sqrt{2/\pi}/2<2\rho/5$;
(ii) $\mathbb{E} F(\tau)-\tfrac{k}{n+1}=(1+o(1))\,B_n/\rho$; and
(iii) $\mathbb{P}[F(\tau)\le\tfrac{k}{n+1}+e_n(\delta)+(2+o(1))B_n/\rho]\ge1-\delta-o(1)$.
The width, hence the premium, carries no $\kappa$: the factor $\kappa^{2}$ in Corollary~(cor:protocol of the paper) is a finite-sample certificate, not an asymptotic necessity, and (ii)--(iii) meet Corollary~(cor:sizelb of the paper) within an absolute factor; a $\sqrt{2/\pi}$ width makes (i) exactly $\rho$. (Proof: Appendix~(app:upper of the paper); empirical check: Appendix~(app:exp of the paper).) (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: The plug-in is asymptotically exact, without $\hat\kappa$

such that, whenever $n\ge n_0(L)$, every scalar rooted centered map with
$m\le L\log n$ satisfies
\[
  |\mathcal A_\Gamma|
  \le NC_L^m n^{-g}
  \prod_j\mu_j^{q_j}K^{m_j-q_j}.
\tag{2.6.15}
\]
At a marked root, its pure-Weyl color factor may be retained as $\beta_j^2$
instead of being relaxed using (eq:2.6.10 of the paper).

 $$ \epsilon M  \le l \le M \ \ \text{ and } \ \  \epsilon l \le j \le (1- \epsilon ) l $$
 or 
 $$ (1 + \epsilon ) M \le l \le 2M \ \ \text{ and } \ \  l-M \le j \le M,$$
 we have 
 $$ P \Big( W (1) \cap W (2) \cap \cdots \cap W (9) \Big) \ge P \big( W (1) \big) \Big\{ 1 - C (\log n)^{-\frac{1}{2}} (\log \log n)^{r} \Big\}.$$

body: In mathematics, low-rank approximation refers to the process of approximating a given matrix by a matrix of lower rank. More precisely, it is a minimization problem, in which the cost function measures the fit between a given matrix and an approximating matrix, subject to a constraint that the approximating matrix has reduced rank. The problem is used for mathematical modeling and data compression. The rank constraint is related to a constraint on the complexity of a model that fits the data. In applications, often there are other constraints on the approximating matrix apart from the rank constraint, e.g., non-negativity and Hankel structure.
title: Low-rank approximation

body:
[Theorem thm:lyapunov-stuff of arXiv:2511.10223, 'Stochastic Reaction Networks Within Interacting Compartments with Content-Dependent Fragme'] Let $X$ be a continuous-time Markov chain on a countable state space $\mathbb S$ with generator $\mathcal L$. Suppose there exists a finite set $K\subset\mathbb S$ and a positive function $V$ on $\mathbb S$ such that
\[
    \mathcal LV(x)\le-1
\]
for all $x\in\mathbb S\setminus K$. Suppose further that $X$ is not explosive. Then each state in a closed, irreducible component of $\mathbb S$ is positive recurrent. Moreover, if $\tau_{x_0}$ is the time for the process to enter the union of the closed irreducible components given an initial condition $x_0$, then $\mathbb E_{x_0}[\tau_{x_0}]<\infty$.
\begin{proof}
    See Theorem 7.3 in [Anderson_Cappelletti_Kim_Nguyen_2020].
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 46 (Density of the systematic scan) of arXiv:2608.03353, '\bfseries A Direct Route to Markov Chain Convergence\\[2mm] \Large via Asymptotic Equivale'] Assume \eqref{eq:condexists} and define
\[
  \tau : \XX\times\XX \to (0,\infty), \qquad
  \tau(y \mid x) := \prod_{i=1}^{d} \frac{p\bigl( x \oplus_{i} y \bigr)}{Z_{i}\bigl( x \oplus_{i-1} y \bigr)} .
\]
Then $\tau$ is $\XXA\otimes\XXA$-measurable, strictly positive at every point of
$\XX\times\XX$, and
\[
  T_{\mathrm{sc}}(A \mid x) = \int_{A} \tau(y \mid x)\,\lambda(\dd y)
  \qquad (A \in \XXA,\ x \in \XX) .
\]

	\|\tilde K^*_m\|_{\mathfrak S_q}\le
	\begin{cases}
		C, & m>0,\\

The algorithm is also known as the Von Mises iteration.

PRIVATE AUTHOR-CHECKED DRAFT, no independent review. Let n be even, Z_1, Z_2 independent standard Gaussians, (g_i) independent N(0, sigma^2) with sigma small, and X_i = Z_1 + g_i for i <= n/2, X_i = Z_2 + g_i for i > n/2. Then (a) with probability tending to one as sigma -> 0 there are two near-maximal indices with correlation R = 0 (multiple peaks in Chatterjee's sense with deficit |Z_1 - Z_2| of order one), (b) Var(max_i X_i) -> Var(max(Z_1, Z_2)) > 0, so the field is not superconcentrated relative to its variance scale, and (c) the argmax half is determined by sign(Z_1 - Z_2) and is unchanged under Ornstein-Uhlenbeck noise of size t unless t exceeds a level of order |Z_1 - Z_2|, so the field is not chaotic. Hence any multiple-peaks condition that admits two peaks cannot be equivalent to chaos or superconcentration; this refutes the two-peak reading of Chatterjee's open problem 6 in 'Chaos, concentration, and multiple valleys' and leaves the growing-number version open.

[Openproblem 18 of arXiv:2608.18834, 'The Parabolic Anderson Model's Total Mass at Small Times: Geometry, Fluctuations, and Reno'] If $\rho\leq-1/2$ (i.e., $d-H\geq2H_0-1/2$), does there sometimes exist a scaling function $\msf s$ such that
$\msf s(t)\big(|D|-\msf M_\ka(t)\big)$
converges in probability to a $\ka$-dependent constant as $t\to0$? (Stated as a problem by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Problem 18 of arXiv:2608.18834

body:
Measured 2026-09-05 on the EMIT and OCO-2 stacking pools (70 cells, the pool protocol, full calibration, paired). Given that the long-only gain is the estimation variance the constraint removes at the rows the stack is scored on, the amount of constraint was chosen with the evaluation inputs: a blend w(t) between the simplex and least-squares stacks with t minimising the cross-validated calibration error plus the excess bootstrap variance of the blend at the evaluation rows over the calibration rows, and a per-row version t_i = 1/(1 + kappa v_i/median v) that leans to the simplex where least squares is uncertain. P24 (a) HELD: on EMIT the per-cell blend reads +0.08 vs the simplex and beats least squares on 39 of 40 cells; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 t* is at or above 0.5 on 30 of 30 cells and the blend reads +0.66 vs least squares; (c) REFUTED: the per-row blend vs the per-cell blend is +0.70 on Y2 and -0.14 on EMIT overall; falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT, or than least squares by more than 0.3 on OCO-2) not triggered. Fresh-split replication (P25, split C, SPLIT_SEED 11, the criterion uses no evaluation targets): P25 (a) HELD: on split C the EMIT blend reads +0.63 vs the simplex and beats least squares on 35 of 40 cells; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 the blend reads +0.84 vs the simplex (wins 30 of 30) and +0.65 vs least squares; (c) HELD: t* averages 0.34 on EMIT and 0.67 on OCO-2; falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT, or than least squares by more than 0.3 on OCO-2) not triggered. Bootstrap-size stability (P28, B = 16 against B = 8 on split B): P28 (a) HELD: t*(16) equals t*(8) on 86 pct of the 70 cells and is within 0.2 on 100 pct; (b) HELD: the blend's mean gain against the simplex moves from +0.08 to +0.06 on EMIT and from +0.83 to +0.83 on OCO-2, and the both-endpoints win count on OCO-2 is 30 of 30 at B = 16; falsifier (agreement below 50 pct or a gain moving by more than 0.5) not triggered. Break test: a fixed midpoint t = 0.5 matches the criterion on OCO-2 (+0.96 / +1.01 against +0.83 / +0.84 on the two splits) but loses 1.6 and 4.4 pct on EMIT where the criterion stays at +0.08 and +0.63 - the criterion's value is knowing, without labels, when not to leave the simplex; the EMIT shortfall against the hindsight-best t is the bias-shift term of the risk identity. Scarce calibration (P30, 240 of the calibration rows per cell, split B): P30 (a) HELD: at n = 240 the simplex beats least squares by +14.10 on EMIT (full calibration +8.83); (b) REFUTED: t* averages 0.22 on EMIT and the blend reads -2.61 vs the simplex; (c) HELD: on OCO-2 the blend beats both endpoints on 30 of 30 cells and the simplex reads +2.27 vs least squares (full calibration -0.18); falsifier (blend worse than the simplex by more than 1 on EMIT) TRIGGERED. The observable part of the bias shift (P31): adding t^2 (D_ev - D_cal), the shift in the two bases' mean squared disagreement between the evaluation and calibration rows, to the criterion - P31 (a) REFUTED: the R'-blend reads -0.71 vs the simplex on EMIT split B (R-blend +0.08) and +0.71 on split C (R-blend +0.63); (b) HELD: on OCO-2 the R'-blend is -0.11 vs the R-blend on split B and -0.12 on split C; (c) REFUTED: mean t** 0.39 against t* 0.33 on EMIT, share of the hindsight optimum 0.07 -> -0.62; falsifier (R'-blend worse than the R-blend by more than 0.3 on any corpus or split) TRIGGERED. Per-output mixing weights (P34, the criterion decoupled across outputs): P34 (a) REFUTED: the per-output blend reads -0.41 vs the per-cell blend on EMIT split B and -0.53 on split C; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 -0.02 and -0.08 on split C; (c) REFUTED: on Y2 the share of outputs at t_d = 0 is 0.20 and at t_d >= 0.5 is 0.34; falsifier (per-output worse than per-cell by more than 0.3 anywhere) TRIGGERED. A nearest-neighbour proxy for the bias shift (P35, the simplex's out-of-fold residuals at the nearest calibration rows standing in for its bias at the scored rows): P35 (a) REFUTED: the full-shift blend reads -0.69 vs the R-blend on EMIT split B and -0.12 on split C; (b) HELD: on OCO-2 -0.08 and -0.14 on split C; (c) REFUTED: cross-only vs full on EMIT -0.05 vs -0.62 (split B); falsifier (either variant worse than the R-blend by more than 0.3 anywhere) TRIGGERED. Scarce calibration, the ratio-metric criterion (P41, 240 calibration rows, split B, three-vertex form, registered and R_1 choices side by side): P41 (a) HELD: at n_cal = 240 the R_1 blend reads +1.17 vs the simplex on EMIT (within 1.0; the registered three-vertex blend reads -1.83); (b) HELD: on OCO-2 the R_1 blend beats both endpoints on 30 of 30 cells (at least 25); (c) HELD: R_1 vs the registered blend on EMIT +1.38 (at least +1.0); falsifier (R_1 worse than the simplex by more than 2.0 on EMIT) not triggered. So the P30 caveat is confined to the squared-loss criterion; the criterion in the score's own metric keeps the simplex where it should at scarce calibration.
the members' predictions on the rows to be scored are available (transductive setting); their targets are not
the blend w(t) = (1 - t) w_simplex + t w_leastsquares is linear in t, so the cross-validated and bootstrap predictions of every t come from the two base estimators' predictions; the criterion is the 5-fold cross-validated squared relative error on the calibration rows plus the excess pairs-bootstrap variance (B = 8) of the blend at the evaluation rows over the calibration rows

body:
Lindeberg-Levy form: let X_1, X_2, ... be independent identically distributed random variables with mean mu and finite variance sigma^2 > 0, and let bar X_n = (X_1 + ... + X_n) / n. Then sqrt(n) (bar X_n - mu) / sigma converges in distribution to the standard normal law: P(sqrt(n) (bar X_n - mu) / sigma <= x) -> Phi(x) for every real x. Lindeberg-Feller form: for a triangular array of independent, mean-zero rows with s_n^2 = sum_k Var(X_{n,k}), the normalised sums S_n / s_n converge to N(0, 1) provided the Lindeberg condition holds: for every epsilon > 0, (1 / s_n^2) sum_k E[X_{n,k}^2 ; |X_{n,k}| > epsilon s_n] -> 0.
finite, non-zero variance; with infinite variance the limit, when it exists, is a stable law
independence (identically distributed in the Lindeberg-Levy form, the Lindeberg condition otherwise)

[Definition 4 ({\normalfont Local graphical data}) of arXiv:2604.24684, 'Waning Immunity Fails to Restore a Positive Epidemic Threshold on Power--Law Networks'] Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph, let $v\in V$, and let $U\subseteq N(v)$ be a set of
neighbors of $v$. We define the \emph{local graphical data}
associated with $(v,U)$ to be the $\sigma$-field
\[
\mathcal{G}(v,U)
:=\sigma\!\Big(
N^{\mathrm{rec}}_{v},\,N^{\mathrm{sus}}_{v},\,
(N^{\mathrm{inf}}_{v\to u})_{u\in U},\,(N^{\mathrm{inf}}_{u\to v})_{u\in U},\,
(N^{\mathrm{rec}}_{u},\,N^{\mathrm{sus}}_{u})_{u\in U}
\Big),
\]
where $\sigma(\mathcal{X})$ denotes the smallest sigma-algebra generated by the collection of $\mathcal{X}$.
title: {\normalfont Local graphical data}

[Lemma lem-LF-SLE of arXiv:2411.19810, 'Radial conformal welding in Liouville quantum gravity'] Let $W \in (0, \frac{\gamma^2}2)$ and $\alpha = Q - \frac W{2\gamma}$. 
	    Sample $(\psi, \eta^\mathrm{wp})$ from $\frac1{2\pi(Q-\alpha)} \mathrm{LF}_{\mathbb C}^{(\alpha, 0), (\gamma, 1), (2Q-\alpha, \infty)} \times \mathrm{SLE}_\kappa^\mathrm{wp}(W-2)$. For each connected component $B$ of $\mathbb{C} \backslash \eta^\mathrm{wp}$, let $p_B$ and $q_B$ be the first and last points of $\partial B$ hit by $\eta^\mathrm{wp}$. Let $\tilde \mathcal{W}$ be the collection of all quantum surfaces $(B, \psi, p_B, q_B)/{\sim_\gamma}$, and  endow $\tilde \mathcal{W}$ with the ordering where $(B_1, \psi, p_{B_1}, q_{B_1})/{\sim_\gamma}$ precedes $(B_2, \psi, p_{B_2}, q_{B_2})/{\sim_\gamma}$ if $\eta^\mathrm{wp}$ hits $q_{B_1}$ for the last time before it hits $q_{B_2}$ for the last time. 
	
	    
	    Let $B_\bullet$ be the connected component of $\mathbb{C} \backslash \eta_0^\mathrm{wp}$ containing $1$, and let $\mathcal{B}_\bullet = (B_\bullet, \psi, 1, p_{B_\bullet}, q_{B_\bullet})/{\sim_\gamma}$. Let $ \mathcal{D} \subset \tilde \mathcal{W}$ (resp.\ $\mathcal{W} \subset \tilde \mathcal{W}$) be the ordered collection of elements that come before (resp.\ after) $(B_\bullet, \psi, p_{B_\bullet}, q_{B_\bullet})/{\sim_\gamma}$. Then the joint law of $(\mathcal{D}, \mathcal{B}_\bullet, \mathcal{W})$ is $(1 - \frac{2W}{\gamma^2})^2 {\mathcal{M}}^\mathrm{disk}_{0,2}(W) \times {\mathcal{M}}^\mathrm{disk}_{1,2}(\gamma^2 - W) \times \mathcal{M}^\mathrm{wed}(W)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma lem-LF-SLE of arXiv:2411.19810

body:
[Theorem thm:torsor of arXiv:2607.24705, 'Derangetropy Operators'] For every open interval $I$, the subgroup of $\mathcal{G}$ of
		distortions with continuous positive derivative on $(0,1)$ acts
		freely and transitively on the laws of $\mathcal{D}_{+}$ with support
		$\overline{I}$, and the full group $\mathcal{G}$ acts so on the
		enlargement of $\mathcal{D}_{+}$ by all laws whose restricted
		distribution function is an absolutely continuous homeomorphism with
		absolutely continuous inverse: for two such laws $f, g$ the unique
		$A \in \mathcal{G}$ with $\alpha_{A}f = g$ is
		\begin{equation}
			A = F_{g}\circ Q_{f}.
			
		\end{equation}
		Consequently, for a reference law $f_{0} \in \mathcal{D}_{+}^{2}$
		with support $\overline{I}$, the potential map is the coadjoint
		orbit map $A \mapsto \operatorname{Ad}^{*}_{A}U_{f_{0}}$, and its
		fibers are the cosets of the stabilizer, which by
		Theorem~(thm:fibers of the paper) is the conjugated M\"obius group
		\begin{equation}
			\operatorname{Stab}_{\mathcal{G}}(U_{f})
			= \big\{\, F_{f}\circ M\circ Q_{f} \;:\;
			M \ \text{an increasing M\"obius self-map of } I \,\big\}.
			
		\end{equation}
		For $f, g \in \mathcal{D}_{+}^{2}$ the torsor
		map~(equation eq:torsor-map of the paper) is automatically a $C^{3}$-diffeomorphism
		of $(0,1)$, and the coadjoint formula, which involves only three
		derivatives, extends verbatim to $C^{3}$ distortions with the same
		cocycle law; the orbit-map statement is understood in this extended
		sense, on the $C^{3}$-regular part of the fiber.

body:
[campaign result 2026-09-14, Author-checked, no independent read.] This is an elementary special case recorded alongside Open Problem 14.12 in David Aldous and James Allen Fill's Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs, unfinished monograph (2002, recompiled 2014; official source https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~aldous/RWG/book.html). Let K_n be the complete simple graph with n>=2 vertices and start one particle per vertex. Each particle jumps independently at rate one to a uniformly chosen different vertex; particles merge on meeting. If T_coal is the time until one particle remains, then E[T_coal]=sum_{k=2}^n (n-1)/(k(k-1))=(n-1)^2/n. The discrete-time simple-walk matrix has n-1 nonconstant eigenvalues all equal to -1/(n-1), so its spectral mean hitting-time sum K=sum_{j=2}^n 1/(1-lambda_j) is also (n-1)^2/n. This is an unrefereed campaign result.
Complete graph; rate-one simple walks; one initial particle at every vertex.

body:
Let N take values in {0, 1, ..., m} on a probability space, mu = E[N] > 0 and beta = E[binom(N, 2)] = E[N(N-1)/2]; put x = 2 beta / mu and r = 1 + floor(x). The masses p_r = (r mu - 2 beta)/r, p_{r+1} = (2 beta - (r-1) mu)/(r+1) and p_0 = 1 - p_r - p_{r+1} are nonnegative, p_{r+1} = 0 when r = m, and the law on {0, r, r+1} with these masses has the same mu and beta as N and P(> 0) equal to the optimized bound D. So the bound is sharp for every feasible pair (mu, beta).
N is integer valued with 0 <= N <= m
mu = E[N] > 0

For a finite real martingale M_k with M_0=0 and finite fourth moments, put D_k=M_k-M_{k-1}. Then E M_N^4=sum_{k=1}^N(6 E M_{k-1}^2 D_k^2+4 E M_{k-1}D_k^3+E D_k^4). The cubic term need not vanish: if M_1 is a symmetric sign and conditionally on M_1=1, D_2=-1 with probability 2/3 and 2 with probability 1/3, with reversed signs when M_1=-1, then E[M_1D_2^3]=2 and E M_2^4=27. Dropping that term gives 19.
Finite real martingale with M_0=0
Each M_k has finite fourth moment
No conditional symmetry of D_k is assumed
